items.title: Psychopharmacological advances in neurorehabilitation after traumatic brain injury.
items.abstract: Purpose of review Pharmacotherapy is widely used to manage neuropsychiatric sequelae that may interfere with neurorehabilitation after traumatic brain injury (TBI), despite limited TBI-specific evidence. This review summarizes psychopharmacological evidence from the past 18 months and proposes a three-step approach: deprescribing potentially recovery-limiting medications, characterizing individual neuropsychiatric symptoms, and selecting symptom-targeted treatments to support cognitive, emotional, behavioral, and functional recovery after TBI. Recent findings Methylphenidate shows the most consistent evidence for selected cognitive outcomes, particularly attention and processing speed. Pharmacological approaches to agitation, sleep-wake disorders, depression, fatigue, and posttraumatic headache have been studied, but TBI-specific evidence remains limited or heterogeneous. Sedative, anticholinergic, and cognitive adverse effects, cardiovascular risks, and dependence require consideration in TBI neurorehabilitation. Summary No pharmacological treatment is established as disease-modifying after TBI. Given the limited evidence, psychopharmacotherapy should be individualized, symptom-targeted, and integrated into multidisciplinary TBI neurorehabilitation. Continuous medication review and deprescribing should accompany careful treatment selection and monitoring. Future trials should determine whether symptom improvement translates into better rehabilitation participation, functional independence, and long-term health-related quality of life.

items.title: Cognitive training for mild neurocognitive disorder: a review of recent evidence and emerging directions.
items.abstract: Purpose of review Older adults with mild neurocognitive disorder (MND), also referred to as mild cognitive impairment, exhibit measurable cognitive deficits while maintaining a relatively preserved autonomy, but are at increased dementia risk. Because learning capacity and neuroplasticity remain substantial during this stage, MND represents an important window for intervention. Cognitive training is increasingly studied in this population and encompasses a broad range of interventions designed to enhance cognitive function through either the repeated practice of targeted tasks (process-based approaches) or instruction of specific strategies (strategy-based approaches). Recent findings This review synthesizes recent evidence on cognitive training in MND focusing on: its efficacy and long-term effects; transfer effects to untrained cognitive tasks, everyday functioning, and psychological symptoms; intervention and participant characteristics associated with treatment response; mechanisms of action investigated using functional neuroimaging; and feasibility and implementation outcomes. Summary Cognitive training is promising for MND. It produces reliable short-term cognitive benefits, and although evidence for long-term effects on cognitive and clinical trajectory remain limited, findings from recent studies are encouraging. Future research should prioritize meaningful transfer to everyday functioning, identification of moderators and responders, and the optimization of implementation strategies across intervention types.

items.title: The Role of DEXA Scanning in Secondary Fragility Fracture Prevention.
items.abstract: Fragility fractures are often the first clinical sign of osteoporosis and represent a substantial source of morbidity, mortality, and healthcare expense in older persons. Despite clear evidence supporting secondary fracture prevention, postfracture care often emphasizes the recovery from the injury itself while insufficiently addressing the underlying skeletal disease. As a result, approximately 6% of patients will have a subsequent fragility fracture within 1 year of the initial injury. In addition, without intervention, osteoporosis will progress in these patients resulting in chronic pain, disability, and decreased quality of life. To slow the progression of osteoporosis, along with lowering the risk of secondary fragility fractures, the aim of this review was to assess the use of dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) in postfracture osteoporosis assessment and monitoring with a focus on its integration with pharmaceutical therapy, fall-prevention techniques, and fracture liaison services (FLS). Without the intervention of FLS, less than one-third of patients will initiate osteoporosis medication therapies within the first year of a hip fracture, despite strong guideline recommendations. DEXA-based bone mineral density evaluation enhances clinical risk stratification, promotes the initiation of evidence-based pharmacologic therapy, and improves osteoporosis detection. The use of DEXA within FLS models improved treatment adherence and subsequently reduced the number of secondary fractures. DEXA-guided postfracture care is essential for lowering recurrent fractures and enhancing outcomes for older persons, especially when incorporated into coordinated care pathways.

items.title: Optimising resource use in audiology and speech therapy practice in South Africa: sectoral challenges, adaptive strategies and system-level implications.
items.abstract: Purpose Efficient and contextually responsive resource utilisation is central to sustainable healthcare delivery, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Within South Africa's dual healthcare system, characterised by structural inequities, there is limited evidence on how practitioners operationalise resource use in practice. This study explored challenges associated with productive resource utilisation among audiology and speech therapy practitioners and identified strategies to enhance efficiency and sustainability across sectors. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative design was employed using semi-structured interviews with 92 practitioners across public and private sectors and urban, peri-urban, and rural contexts in four South African provinces (Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal, Western Cape, and Limpopo). Data were analysed thematically using Braun and Clarke's framework, with exploratory inferential analyses examining sectoral differences. Qualitative codes were quantified at participant level to allow descriptive and exploratory statistical comparison across sectors. Findings Four themes emerged. First, public sector resource constraints included equipment shortages (80%), staffing limitations (75%) and budgetary constraints (85%), particularly in rural areas (χ2 = 17.89, p Originality/value This study provides novel insight into how resource optimisation is enacted within a dual healthcare system in an LMIC. It demonstrates how systemic inequities shape decision-making and service delivery, offering contextually grounded strategies to inform health system strengthening, including implications for public-private integration and South Africa's National Health Insurance. By integrating thematic analysis with exploratory quantitative comparisons, the study extends existing literature beyond descriptive accounts of resource scarcity to illustrate how practitioners adapt operationally within structurally unequal healthcare environments.

items.title: Dynamic managerial capabilities: the role of TMT cohesion in the relationship between transformational leadership and TMT efficacy in hospital context.
items.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine, in healthcare institutions, the mediating role of top management team (TMT) cohesion in the relationship between the CEO's transformational leadership (TL) and the efficacy of the TMT, positioning these three elements as dynamic managerial capabilities (DMC) that enable the organisation to better align with its environment. Design/methodology/approach A structural equation model is used based on a survey conducted in public hospitals in the Valencian Community (Spain), with a total of 87 executives from 19 participating hospitals, covering almost all hospitals in the Valencian Community (20 hospitals). Findings The results indicate that TMT cohesion plays an important mediating role in the relationship between TL and TMT efficacy. Practical implications The findings suggest that CEO TL is associated with greater TMT cohesion, which is in turn associated with higher team efficacy. In healthcare organisations, where decision-making involves high professional diversity and uncertainty, cultivating a cohesive leadership climate supports more integrated decision-making and improves management effectiveness and organisational adaptability. Originality/value This study contributes to healthcare leadership research by examining how CEO TL, TMT cohesion and TMT efficacy are interrelated within the public hospital context, and by explaining why CEOs' TL does not always translate directly into higher TMT efficacy. The findings indicate that TMT cohesion plays a mediating role in this relationship. It further conceptualises these constructs as interrelated DMC with distinct but complementary adaptive functions, offering a novel perspective on how their interaction may support organisational adaptability and alignment with environmental demands.

items.title: The influence of caregivers' lived experiences in decision-making processes on care transitions in young-onset dementia.
items.abstract: BackgroundCaregivers of people with young-onset dementia (YOD) hold diverse perspectives on the caregiving trajectory, reflecting the heterogeneity of underlying etiologies and the life stages of these people, who are often in the midst of employment, child-rearing, and other social responsibilities. Post-diagnostic care and services are often suboptimal and caregivers tend to be hesitant to initiate formal care and support services. We refer to movements of persons between different levels of care or physical locations as care transitions.ObjectiveTo improve caregiver support, this study aimed to provide insights into caregivers' perspectives on the decision-making process regarding care transitions and associated barriers and facilitators.MethodsSeventeen interviews with six caregivers of people with YOD were analyzed. Inductive content analysis was used to generate codes, followed by constant comparative analysis to create categories and themes describing caregivers' experiences.ResultsBarriers and facilitators influencing the decision-making process related to the initiation of care transitions were identified at two themes: individual and contextual level. Six categories and 23 sub-categories emerged. Individual-level categories included the character traits of the caregiver, the caregiver's need for support, impacts on the quality of the caregiver's relationship, and the burden experienced by the caregiver. Contextual-level categories included the social environment and the caregivers' experiences with healthcare professionals.ConclusionsCaregivers' decision-making regarding care transitions is shaped by thinking processes, character traits and contextual aspects. Healthcare professionals should strengthen collaboration and communication with caregivers. Acknowledging grief and supporting caregivers'sense of control are essential to providing adequate support.

items.title: Vitamin C and Methylprednisolone Modulate Apoptotic and Transcript Responses in a B-35 Scratch Screening Model.
items.abstract: In vitro mechanical injury platforms using proliferative neuronal cell lines provide accessible systems for preliminary pharmacological screening before progression to differentiated, primary, or in vivo models. We investigated the effects of vitamin C and methylprednisolone, alone or in combination, on cell viability, Annexin V/PI-defined apoptotic cell death, scratch-gap closure, and selected transcript responses in the B-35 rat neuroblastoma cell line. Mechanical injury was induced in confluent B-35 monolayers using a standardized scratch method. Vitamin C, methylprednisolone, or their combination was applied either immediately after injury (0 h) or after a 24 h delay. Scratch-gap closure was quantified by image-based analysis, and IL-4, IL-10, and TUBB3 expression was evaluated by quantitative real-time PCR. Early combined exposure to vitamin C and methylprednisolone was associated with low apoptotic cell fractions, faster scratch-gap closure, and higher IL-4, IL-10, and TUBB3 mRNA levels than either single treatment, whereas delayed treatment showed attenuated responses. These findings describe treatment-associated changes in a simplified B-35 cell-line screening model. They should not be interpreted as evidence of regeneration, pharmacological synergy, neuroprotection, or spinal cord injury therapy. Protein-level validation, proliferation control, and confirmation in differentiated neuronal cultures, primary neuronglia co-cultures, organoid or slice models, and in vivo injury systems are required before mechanistic or translational conclusions can be drawn.

items.title: Effectiveness of rimegepant across multiple acute migraine attacks: A real-world, prospective, multicentric study.
items.abstract: AimRimegepant is an effective acute migraine treatment, with limited evidence regarding its consistency across multiple migraine attacks. The primary aim is to assess rimegepant effectiveness across multiple migraine attacks.MethodsIn this real-world, prospective, multicentric study we assessed participants who treated up to four different migraine attacks with rimegepant 75 mg orally disintegrating tablet. Data was collected every 30 min from migraine onset up to 2 h post dose using an electronic diary. Our primary outcome was 2-h pain freedom across all-treated attacks; secondary outcomes were: consistency of response (percentage of participants who achieved 2-h pain freedom in at least two treated attacks), safety and tolerability.ResultsWe enrolled 191 participants (80.1% females, age 44.8 [43.2-46.5] years, disease duration 28.4 [25.0-31.8] years, 27.7% with chronic migraine, 9.6 [8.9-10.9] baseline monthly migraine days-MMDs). We collected data from 377 migraine attacks (191 first-treated, 110 s-treated, 46 third-treated and 30 fourth-treated). Two-hour pain freedom was achieved in 44.6% (168/377) of treated attacks [39.3-49.6]. After correction for age, timing of rimegepant intake, baseline pain intensity, ongoing preventive treatment, and number of preventive drug classes that previously proved ineffective, 2-h pain freedom was associated with female sex (odds ratio (OR) = 2.3 [1.2-4.3], p = 0.012), no ongoing mAbs treatment (OR = 3.2 [1.6-6.4], p = 0.001), and lower MMDs (OR = 1.05 [1.0-1.1], p = 0.002). Consistency of response was 36.4% [27.3-45.5] (40/110). Participants reporting at least one adverse event were 11.5% (22/191).ConclusionOur study confirms the effectiveness of rimegepant in nearly half of treated attacks and describe the consistency of response in a relatively large real-world population where one out of five participants achieved 2-h pain freedom in all-treated migraine attacks. No new safety signals were identified.

items.title: The Cost-Of-Living Crisis and Suicide Rates.
items.abstract: Background: The cost-of-living crisis may be contributing to suicide rates, but this has not been adequately tested. Aims: We aimed to determine whether the cost-of-living crisis is associated with suicide rates in multiple countries and areas-within-countries. Method: We sourced country- and area-within-country-level monthly suicide data at a minimum from January 1, 2019, to December 31, 2022 (and at a maximum from January 1, 2016, to June 30, 2023), and population denominator and monthly headline consumer price index (CPI) data. We calculated the yearly change in inflation as the percentage change in CPI for one month versus the equivalent month in the previous year. We estimated associations between yearly change in inflation (lagged by one month) and suicide rates for each country and area-within-country, using autoregressive negative binomial regression. We summarized results using weighted means. Results: We obtained data on 1,372,994 suicides from 54 countries. At the country-level, for every 1.0% increase in yearly inflation in the previous month, there was an average 0.2% increase in suicide rates. The association was strongest in those aged 30-49 and 50-69; for every 1.0% increase in yearly inflation in the previous month, there were 0.3% and 0.6% increases in suicide rates for these age-groups, respectively. This pattern held for males in these age-groups, with increases of the same magnitude, and for females aged 50-69, with a 0.8% increase. At the area-within-country-level, the picture was even starker. Limitations: Study limitations include: the ecological design; the single measure of inflation; potential variations in suicide data quality; lack of representation by low-and-middle-income countries (LMICS); lack of availability of sex, age and sex/age breakdowns for some countries and areas-within-countries; and potential issues with multiple testing. Conclusions: There is an association between the cost-of-living crisis and suicide rates internationally. Public and social policies that improve people's circumstances are critical.

items.title: Beyond the hype: why artificial intelligence is not a shortcut to solving mental illness.
items.abstract: More than one billion people worldwide live with a mental health disorder, and rising prevalence continues to outpace the capacity of mental health services. Artificial intelligence, and large language models in particular, have been widely proposed as a remedy. Nevertheless, psychiatry's limited mechanistic understanding of illness processes (compounded by their psychosocial roots) and its reliance on largely subjective clinical assessments limit what any artificial intelligence model can achieve. We examine where artificial intelligence genuinely helps, including large multimodal data-sets and administrative tools such as ambient scribes, and where evidence for direct therapeutic use remains preliminary and safety concerns are real. We also highlight risks posed by artificial intelligence to the research process itself, from hallucinated citations to unverifiable analysis pipelines. Ultimately, whether artificial intelligence comes to augment psychiatric care or hollow it out depends less on model capability than on the choices of stakeholders and policymakers.

items.title: Short-term outcomes, longer-term disability and relapse risk in LGI1-antibody encephalitis.
items.abstract: Leucine-rich glioma-inactivated-1 antibody encephalitis (LGI1-Ab-E) is a common and immunotherapy-responsive form of encephalitis. However, it is not known which immunotherapy regimens improve short-term outcomes, longer-term disability and relapse risk. Further, it is not known if the widely-utilised modified Rankin Scale (mRS) accurately captures quality of life (QoL) in LGI1-Ab-E, complicating disability measurements and interpretation of immunotherapy responses. A multicentre, international, real-world comparative analysis of patients with LGI1-Ab-E. Retrospective data from patient records evaluated short-term seizure and cognitive outcomes, 1-6 year disability, and future relapse risk associations, by integrating demographics, clinical features investigations and exposures to immunotherapies and antiseizure medications (ASMs). Patient- and neurologist-rated QoL assessments were used to establish an evidence-based mRS threshold for defining clinically significant disability. Cox proportional hazard models, Anderson-Gill, and generalised linear mixed-effects models were employed. 181 patients were included, with median age at onset 63 years (range 23 - 92); 122/181 (67%) were male. Short-term outcomes, evaluated at both five and ten weeks post-treatment initiation, identified exposure to immunotherapies associated with seizure resolution (OR = 13.97, 95%CI = 6.10-32.01; p < 0.0001 and OR = 8.53, 95%CI = 4.14-17.55; p < 0.0001, respectively), notably with corticosteroids, plasma exchange and rituximab, but not ASMs, intravenous immunoglobulins or steroid sparing agents. Conversely, seizure recurrence was observed after discontinuation of oral prednisolone, but not other immunotherapies or ASMs (OR = 39.53, 95%CI = 12.70-122.20, p < 0.0001). To evaluate longer-term disability, first, mRS scores were calibrated using QoL assessments: this identified a significant increase in patient-rated disability at mRS score of 2. Hence, using mRS 0-1 as a favourable outcome, we identified worse mRS at nadir associated with greater one-year disability (OR = 2.56, 95%CI = 1.56-4.20, p = 0.0003), and each month of delayed immunotherapy associated with a 16% increased risk of disability (HR = 1.16, 95%CI = 1.06-1.35, p = 0.004). Additionally, absence of immunotherapy associated both with greater one-year disability (OR = 5.67; 95% CI 1.19-26.54, p = 0.03) and a relapsing course (OR = 7.64, 95%CI = 2.51-21.77, p = 0.0002). Both a relapsing course, observed in 38% of patients, and the number of relapses associated with step-wise worsening of disability and QoL-outcomes. Rituximab exposure was the only identified clinical factor associated with reduced future relapse risk, by 93% (HR = 0.07, 95%CI = 0.01-0.48, p = 0.002). Persistent serum LGI1-IgMs, but not LGI1-IgGs, at one-year, associated with future relapses (HR = 11.69, 95%CI = 1.58-145.80, p = 0.02). Distinctive clinical factors and select immunotherapies, particularly intravenous methylprednisolone and plasma exchange, but not ASMs, associated with favourable short-term outcomes, patient-centric longer-term disability and relapses in LGI1-Ab-E. Our findings provide evidence-based disability thresholds, highlight novel prognostic biomarkers, and pragmatically guide LGI1-Ab-E care, pending randomized clinical trials.

items.title: Regular Exercise Moderates Age-Related Cognitive Differences in Midlife Women: Domain-Specific Effects on Processing Speed and Working Memory.
items.abstract: This study examined whether regular exercise moderates age-related cognitive differences in midlife women, including reaction time (RT), executive planning, and working memory. We further investigated whether these effects differ across exercise modalities. This cross-sectional study included ninety-three women (35-63 years) who completed simple RT, working memory, and executive planning tasks. Participants were categorized by exercise regularity and modality. Time-based outcomes were analyzed via Linear Mixed Models; accuracy via Generalized Estimating Equations. Pairwise comparisons utilized Welch's t-tests with FDR correction. Regular exercise moderated age-related slowing in simple RT (β=-3.083, p=0.032). Resistance training participants exhibited faster RTs than those in the non- regular exerciser, aerobic, and other exercise groups. Regarding working memory, the impact of exercise on response speed was significantly moderated by both age and task difficulty (β = -15.91, p < 0.001). Specifically, exercise-related benefits became more pronounced as cognitive load increased, a trend primarily driven by older participants, whereas these effects were less evident in younger cohorts. However, no modality-specific differences were observed. In contrast, executive planning performance was associated with age, with no significant effects of exercise or exercise-related interactions. These findings suggest that regular exercise moderates age-related cognitive differences in midlife women, particularly in processing speed and high-demand working memory. These benefits were domain-specific: modality-specific advantages emerged in simple reaction time, whereas working memory benefits were modality-independent. The notable efficacy of resistance training further highlights the importance of exercise modality. Findings identify midlife as a sensitive window for targeted exercise interventions to preserve cognitive health.

items.title: Aerobic exercise training alters gastrointestinal microbiota and enhances exercise capacity in UM-HET3 mice.
items.abstract: Aerobic exercise attenuates age-related physiological decline, potentially through favorable modulation of gut microbiota diversity. The purpose of this study was to characterize aerobic exercise training (ET)-induced alterations in the gut microbiome of aging, genetically heterogeneous UM-HET3 mice and examine associations between microbial shifts and changes in body composition (body weight, lean mass, and fat mass) and exercise capacity (total work, distance, and duration). Male UM-HET3 mice were assigned to sedentary (SED; n = 16) or ET (n = 17) groups. ET mice trained 5 days per week for 4 weeks at 65% of maximal work output. Body composition and exercise capacity were assessed before and after the intervention. Post-intervention fecal samples were analyzed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing (SED, n = 13; ET, n = 13). ASVs were taxonomically classified using QIIME2 with the SILVA 138.1 reference database. Alpha and beta diversity analyses were conducted in R, and Spearman's correlations assessed relationships between phylum-level abundances and physiological outcomes. ET mice exhibited greater alpha diversity, with a higher median richness (219.5), although differences were not statistically significant. Principal coordinate analysis of beta diversity demonstrated significant separation between groups (P = 0.01), indicating distinct microbial community composition. At the phylum level, ET was associated with modest shifts in gut microbial composition, characterized by higher relative abundances of Firmicutes and Verrucomicrobiota and lower abundances of Bacteroidota and Desulfobacterota compared to SED mice. Collectively, these findings indicate that aerobic exercise training induces distinct shifts in gut microbiota composition in middle-aged UM-HET3 mice despite underlying genetic heterogeneity.

items.title: Adult attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder symptoms are associated with chronic low back pain: a nationwide cross-sectional study of 2113 individuals.
items.abstract: Low back pain (LBP) is a major contributor to reduced quality of life and increasing global healthcare burdens. Recently, adult attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has been associated with chronic pain interference. In this study, we examined the prevalence and characteristics of ADHD symptoms in the general population and their association with LBP. This nationwide cross-sectional observational study included 2,113 participants from a survey of randomly selected residents aged ≥ 20 years. Self-reported ADHD symptoms were assessed using the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS), a screening instrument for possible ADHD in adults. Perceived stress and psychological distress were assessed with the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS) and the Kessler 6-Item Psychological Distress Scale (K6), respectively. Participants were grouped by LBP status as no LBP, acute/subacute LBP, or chronic LBP, and multinomial logistic regression was used to identify the factors associated with each; models with and without the PSS and K6 were compared. A positive ADHD screen was identified in 3.27% of participants, of whom 23.2% reported chronic LBP compared with 11.0% of screen-negative participants. A higher ASRS score was associated with chronic LBP after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.255 per 10-point increase, 95% confidence interval 1.051-1.509, p = 0.010), as were older age, comorbidity burden, smoking, and the PSS and K6 scores. None of the psychosocial measures was associated with acute/subacute LBP. The aOR for the ASRS score fell from 1.548 to 1.255 when the PSS and K6 were added to the model but remained significant. A positive ADHD screen on the ASRS was identified in 3.27% of participants from the general population, and a higher score for self-reported adult ADHD symptoms remained statistically associated with chronic LBP after adjustment for established associated factors, including perceived stress and psychological distress.

items.title: Neuromuscular junction pathology in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and emerging molecular therapeutic strategies.
items.abstract: Traditionally conceptualized as a soma-centric pathology, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal, heterogeneous neurodegenerative disease. The suboptimal outcomes of central nervous system (CNS)-directed therapeutic strategies have necessitated a shift in focus toward the dying-back hypothesis. This hypothesis contends that synaptic disconnection and axonal retraction at the distal neuromuscular junction (NMJ) are early pathological events that may antedate overt motor neuron loss. This review systematically examines the NMJ as an early vulnerable and therapeutically tractable peripheral niche in ALS pathogenesis, rather than merely a downstream consequence of proximal proteinopathy. Evidence from human clinical samples and ALS mouse models, particularly SOD1-G93A mice, collectively supports the early vulnerability of the NMJ, with the temporal precedence of denervation, synaptic retraction, and mitochondrial dysfunction most clearly demonstrated in experimental models. We highlight how the breakdown of the tripartite synapse-comprising the motor terminal, skeletal muscle, and terminal Schwann cells (tSCs)-may disrupt essential neurotrophic signaling and local metabolic homeostasis. Furthermore, we discuss how advancements in humanized in vitro NMJ models and spatial transcriptomics provide unprecedented resolution into localized RNA dysmetabolism and bioenergetic failure. Finally, we evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies specifically designed to stabilize or restore the NMJ, including MuSK agonists and other NMJ-directed approaches. By recontextualizing the NMJ as a critical early site of vulnerability, we propose that targeting the peripheral synaptic microenvironment may offer a promising strategy for modifying the progression of ALS.

items.title: The Cohered GP Training Model: A systematic review and complexity-informed synthesis of general practice training.
items.abstract: General practice (GP) training is central to the development of the primary care workforce but is often described as a bounded educational programme rather than a process shaped by clinical work, workplace culture, and wider service conditions. To examine how GP training is represented in the literature and to develop a complexity-informed conceptual model of GP training. Systematic review and complexity-informed synthesis of studies relating to GP training in primary care contexts. Empirical and conceptual studies were identified through systematic searching and analyzed using thematic synthesis, informed by complex adaptive systems and Cohered Emergent Theory. Three thematic areas were identified: GP-patient interactions, GP-professional interactions, and training intricacies. Four cross-cutting insights emerged: complexity in everyday training, the influence of power and hierarchy, the importance of diversity and adaptability, and the shaping role of wider system pressures. These informed the Cohered GP Training Model, which conceptualizes GP training as a dynamic system in which outcomes emerge from the degree of coherence between trainee formation, educational relationships, patient care encounters, workplace and team ecology, and the wider primary care system. GP training is best understood as a relational and system-embedded process rather than a discrete educational intervention. The model may help explain variation in training quality across settings and offers a conceptual basis for improving training environments and workforce development.

items.title: Induced Volatile Chemistry and Arthropod Predation Across a Tree Diversity Gradient.
items.abstract: Plant volatile organic compounds (VOCs) play a key role in defence against herbivores and in mediating multitrophic interactions. Yet, how surrounding plant diversity modulates these responses in forest trees remains poorly understood. We examined the effects of tree species richness on induced VOC emissions and arthropod predation in Quercus petraea in a biodiversity-ecosystem functioning experiment. Individual branches were repeatedly induced with methyl jasmonate and paired with non-induced controls within the same tree. VOCs were collected using PDMS tubes after the first and last induction rounds and analyzed by TD-GC-MS. Predation was quantified using plasticine caterpillars. Jasmonate induction strongly altered VOC profiles and effects increased after repeated treatments. Tree species richness modulated VOC composition during the first sampling period, particularly affecting sesquiterpenes. Compound-specific analyses revealed that β-Ocimene was negatively associated with predation probability during the second sampling period. However, absolute VOC class emissions did not explain variation in arthropod predation probability, while compound class-level composition showed only weak and inconsistent effects across sampling periods. These results suggest that indirect defence outcomes in terms of predator responses are unlikely to depend on VOC class-level emission strength or broad VOC class composition but may instead be mediated by fine-scale properties of volatile blends.

items.title: ArthroVerse: mapping protein family diversity across arthropod-associated microbiomes.
items.abstract: Metagenomic studies of arthropod-associated microbiomes have generated vast amounts of sequence data, yet the functional and structural organization of these proteins remains largely unexplored. Here, we present ArthroVerse, the first comprehensive database of protein families derived from arthropod-associated metagenomes. Non-redundant protein families were generated after rigorous filtering, deduplication, and clustering. The protein families were further annotated with microbial taxonomy, host associations, protein structural information, and carbohydrate-active enzymes predictions. The resulting dataset integrates both metagenomic and reference genome-derived proteins, enabling systematic exploration of functional diversity, evolutionary relationships, and host-microbe interactions in insect microbiomes. ArthroVerse provides a valuable resource for the study of microbial ecology and arthropod physiology, offering unprecedented insight into the protein landscape of insect-associated microbial communities. ArthroVerse is publicly accessible at https://envofams.org/arthroverse/.

items.title: Cysteine-rich sperm protamines arose independently at least twice on a deeply conserved, intrinsically disordered scaffold in amniotes.
items.abstract: Every amniote must compact and shield the paternal genome, but the chemistry differs. In placental mammals, sperm chromatin is locked by protamine disulfide bridges, and the cysteine-rich form is considered the "mammalian" protamine. Analyzing 46 tetrapod protamine-1 orthologs on a time-calibrated phylogeny, we find it neither confined to eutherians nor of single origin: dasyurid marsupials (Planigale) carry cysteine-bearing protamines nested among cysteine-free marsupials. Ancestral-state reconstruction recovers cysteine-free as the ancestral state (root probability 0.99), with cysteine-bearing protamine arising independently at least twice (eutherian stem and Planigale; three gains, zero losses). Alignment and a gene tree confirm the Planigale proteins are dasyurid PRM1 orthologs whose cysteines occupy homologous positions within the genus, replacing tyrosine or arginine, at sites distinct from eutherian cysteines. All 46 protamines show sequence characteristics consistent with intrinsic disorder and none is folded by three structure predictors; confidence rises with disorder because poly-arginine is modelled as spurious helix, even in alignment-free AlphaFold3. Cysteine-free protamines carry marginally higher charge density across both origins (PGLS beta = + 0.044, p = 0.046) but not robustly; because the gained cysteines derive from tyrosine rather than arginine, and the difference is independent of PRM2, the pattern is consistent with, but not proof of, electrostatic compensation. The disulfide protamine is thus a convergent elaboration on a conserved, disordered polyarginine scaffold, not a mammalian baseline. Because protamine integrity underlies sperm DNA integrity and fertility, this polarity reframes the central question: how ancestral cysteine-free lineages, birds among them, protect the genome without covalent cross-links.

items.title: Turkish Adaptation and Validation of the Penn State Worry Questionnaire for Children (PSWQ-C): Factor Structure, Reliability and Validity.
items.abstract: Worry is a common psychological experience among most people; however, when it becomes excessive and difficult to control, it can lead to psychological distress. The Penn State Worry Questionnaire for Children (PSWQ-C) was developed to objectively measure worry and consists of 14 items that assess excessive, generalized, and uncontrollable worry in children. This study translated the PSWQ-C into Turkish and examined its psychometric properties in a Turkish sample of 171 children aged 8 to 18 (M = 12.05, SD = 3.37). The Turkish version of PSWQ-C showed high reliability by test-retest and also excellent internal consistency results. To examine the validity of the PSWQ-C, we calculated its correlation with the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory for Children, Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale Child Form and Metacognition Questionnaire for Children and Adolescents. Based on the adult version of the PSWQ, two factor models were evaluated: (a) a single-factor model (M1) and (b) a bifactor model (M2) consisting of one general trait factor and method factor for reverse-scored items. The results suggest that the questionnaire measures a single latent construct, worry, although the bifactor model showed the best fit to the data. The methos factor appear to reflect method effect associated with reverse-scored items. Overall, the PSWQ-C demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity and appears to be a useful tool for objectively assessing worry in Turkish children.

items.title: The Potential for Large Language Models in Eating Disorder Care: Opportunities for Education, Detection and Assessment, and Intervention.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are anticipated to transform the eating disorder field, offering new opportunities for education, detection and assessment, and intervention. This paper synthesizes evidence on these emerging opportunities and sets a future research agenda. Early research provides encouraging evidence that LLMs have clinically relevant capabilities in eating disorders. For education, LLMs can provide accurate responses to consumer-facing eating disorder queries, although performance varies by topic complexity. For detection and assessment, LLMs can identify probable diagnoses from vignettes and translate online discourse into risk signals. For intervention, LLMs are capable of providing empathic support and caregiver guidance, but can also generate harmful outputs. LLMs offer opportunities to expand access to eating disorder support. The evidence base, safeguards, and evaluation standards established now will determine whether these tools can be used safely in practice, necessitating the need for further research in clinical settings.

items.title: Olfactory Context Modulates Recognition and Directed Forgetting of Emotional Faces: A Chemosensory-Cognitive Perspective.
items.abstract: Olfaction has privileged access to limbic and memory-related brain regions, yet how ambient odor valence influences memory for emotional faces remains poorly understood. This study examined the effects of pleasant odor, unpleasant odor, and odorless condition on recognition accuracy, reaction time, and directed forgetting of emotional faces. In Experiment 1 (study-recognition, n = 31), unpleasant odor significantly impaired recognition accuracy relative to pleasant odor and odorless condition (ps < .01) and slowed reaction times (p < .01); negative faces were recognized more accurately than positive faces (p < .01). In Experiment 2 (item-method directed forgetting, n = 33), a three-way interaction (p < .05) showed that odor valence selectively modulated directed forgetting depending on face type. Under pleasant odor, positive faces showed a robust directed forgetting effect (p < .01), whereas neutral faces exhibited a marginally reversed effect (p = .052). Under unpleasant odor, neutral faces demonstrated a significant directed forgetting effect (p < .01). No directed forgetting was observed for negative faces across all odor conditions. These findings provide novel behavioral evidence that olfactory contexts do not simply enhance or impair memory globally but selectively tune intentional forgetting in a valence-specific manner, advancing our understanding of how chemosensory environments shape cognitive control over socially relevant emotional information.

items.title: Stakeholder Perspectives on Factors Influencing Mental Health Following Concussion in Youth.
items.abstract: To characterize factors influencing mental health following concussion from the perspectives of youth, their parents, and community stakeholders. Virtual sessions hosted by a tertiary care children's hospital. Youth aged 11-17 years with recent concussion, their parents, clinicians, trainers, coaches, and school personnel. Qualitative study using focus groups (FGs) and group-level assessment (GLA) sessions. FGs used semistructured guides to elicit experiences. GLA followed a six-step process to generate, reflect on, and prioritize shared insights. Thematic analysis was applied to FG transcripts, while GLA themes were collaboratively developed. Themes from both methods were synthesized using card-sort methodology and iterative team review. Thematic synthesis of stakeholder perspectives on factors affecting postconcussion mental health. FG sessions included 20 participants (15 youth, 5 parents); GLA sessions included 32 (10 youth, 9 parents, 13 stakeholders). Five convergent themes emerged: (1) concussion knowledge: education and informed care reassured, whereas limited knowledge, minimization of symptoms, and delays increased distress; (2) support systems: family, peer, school, and clinician support with timely accommodations protected mental health, whereas lack of support, bullying or peer pressure, and pressure to recover quickly hindered recovery; (3) preinjury mental health: previous anxiety or depression heightened risk and complicated recovery; (4) identity and sense of self: adapting expectations and embracing a "new normal" aided adjustment, whereas isolation and role change added strain; and (5) coping strategies: gradual return to activities, self-care, consistent routines, and celebrating progress supported recovery, whereas pressure to "push through" and rushed reintegration were detrimental. These qualitative insights revealed multifactorial influences on postconcussion mental health across individual, family, school, and care contexts. Implications include enhancing stakeholder education, promoting coordinated support across settings, integrating routine mental health assessments, addressing identity and role changes, and encouraging adaptive coping strategies to optimize recovery.

items.title: Temporomandibular Disorder-Related Symptoms and Health-Related Quality of Life among Japanese Adults.
items.abstract: Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are among the most prevalent musculoskeletal conditions affecting the orofacial region. However, their association with preference-based health-related quality of life (HRQOL) has not been fully examined. This study evaluated the association between TMD-related symptoms and HRQOL using a 5-level EuroQol 5-dimensional questionnaire (EQ-5D-5L) in Japanese adults. A cross-sectional analysis was conducted using data from the Japan COVID-19 and Society Internet Survey, which included participants aged 20 to 79 y. TMD-related symptoms were assessed using the Screening Questionnaire for TMD (SQ-TMD) and the TMD Pain Screener (TMD-PS). Regression standardization based on linear regression models, including sociodemographic and health-related covariates, was applied, and mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated. Among the 23,916 participants, the prevalence of TMD-related symptoms assessed using the SQ-TMD and TMD-PS was 19.8% and 6.7%, respectively. The mean EQ-5D-5L score was 0.894 (SD = 0.156). After being standardized for sociodemographic and health-related covariates, TMD-related symptoms were significantly associated with lower EQ-5D-5L scores (SQ-TMD: MD = -0.045 [95% CI, -0.054 to -0.037]; TMD-PS: MD = -0.061 [95% CI, -0.080 to -0.042]; both P < 0.001). The present study suggested that the presence of TMD-related symptoms was significantly associated with lower EQ-5D-5L scores. The observed differences were close to or exceeded the previously reported reference value for the minimally important difference of the EQ-5D-5L in the Japanese population.Knowledge Transfer Statement:This study demonstrates that symptoms of temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are associated with clinically meaningful reductions in health-related quality of life, as measured by the EQ-5D. These findings underscore the substantial individual and societal burden of TMDs and provide evidence to inform prevention strategies, clinical management, and health economic evaluations. Addressing TMDs through public health and clinical interventions may contribute to improved overall well-being.

items.title: Effectiveness of theory-based educational interventions on fertility and childbearing intentions: a systematic review and meta-analysis among Iranian populations.
items.abstract: Declining fertility highlights the need for theory-based educational interventions that shape couples' childbearing intentions. We examined their effectiveness on fertility and childbearing intentions through a systematic review and meta-analysis. Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, SID, Magiran and Google Scholar were searched up to 18 August 2025, following PRISMA guidelines, and two reviewers extracted data. Pooled standardised mean differences (SMD) were estimated with random-effects models in Stata; heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and Cochran's Q. Twelve studies (1118 participants) were included. Interventions significantly increased fertility and childbearing intentions (SMD 0.79; 95% CI 0.48 to 1.09; I2 = 88.5%). Effects were significant at short-term (SMD 0.52; 95% CI 0.15 to 0.90) and long-term (SMD 0.96; 95% CI 0.53 to 1.39) follow-up. The Theory of Planned Behaviour showed the largest effect (SMD 1.01; 95% CI 0.55 to 1.48), whereas multimedia education without a theoretical foundation showed no significant effect (SMD 0.05). Interventions of three, five, and eight sessions showed significant effects, whereas two and four sessions did not. Theory-based interventions, especially those grounded in the TPB, were associated with higher fertility intentions among Iranian couples. Culturally adapted programmes may inform policy, although most studies were small, quasi-experimental and relied on self-reported intention.

items.title: Determining the Relationship Between Loneliness and Social Support in Adolescents Affected by the Earthquake: A Study From Turkey.
items.abstract: This study was conducted to determine the relationship between loneliness and social support in adolescents affected by the earthquake. This descriptive correlational study was conducted in April-May 2023 with 549 adolescents aged 12-18 living in 11 provinces affected by the February 6, 2023, Kahramanmaraş-centered earthquake in Turkey. In this study, the snowball sampling method was used. Data were collected using a Descriptive Information Form, the UCLA Loneliness Scale, and the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support.Statistical analyses included independent t-test, one-way ANOVA with post hoc Tukey HSD and Dunnett's tests, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression analysis. Most adolescents were significantly affected by the earthquake. Their loneliness score was below average, while their perceived social support score was above average. There was a significant negative relationship between loneliness and perceived social support. Key factors influencing loneliness included satisfaction with current living conditions, loss of relatives, and feelings of loneliness post-earthquake. The findings highlight the critical role of social support in reducing loneliness among adolescents affected by the earthquake. Enhancing social support networks and addressing factors such as living conditions and loss experiences are crucial for improving the psychological well-being of disaster-affected adolescents.

items.title: Disaster exposure and women's mental and general health: evidence from longitudinal data.
items.abstract: Disasters can have important consequences for health, yet much evidence is cross-sectional and cannot account for time-invariant individual heterogeneity. To examine the association between reported disaster exposure and women's mental health, psychological distress, and general health using longitudinal Australian data. Data from women aged ≥ 15 years participating in Waves 9-22 of the Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia Survey were analysed. Individual and survey-wave fixed-effects models examined within-person associations between disaster exposure and mental health (MHI-5), psychological distress (Kessler-10), and SF-36 General Health. Sensitivity analyses considered long-term illness and single exposure. Dynamic associations were examined using the Callaway-Sant'Anna multiple-period difference-in-differences estimator with formal pre-trend tests. Reported disaster exposure was associated with modest declines in mental health (β = -0.86, 95% CI - 1.51 to -0.20) and general health (β = -0.83, 95% CI - 1.44 to -0.22). Psychological distress was higher but not statistically significant in the primary model (β = 0.33, 95% CI - 0.04 to 0.70). Sensitivity analyses generally supported the mental and general health findings. Event-study analyses showed no consistent evidence of persistent post-exposure deterioration; however, the MHI-5 joint pre-trend test indicated differential pre-exposure patterns, limiting causal interpretation. Reported disaster exposure was associated with modest within-person declines in women's mental and general health, while evidence for psychological distress was less conclusive. The findings support consideration of women's health in disaster preparedness and recovery planning.

items.title: Artificial intelligence policies in academic primary health care: a review of journals and their publishers.
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of AI tools in academic research has created uncertainty about appropriate use in manuscript preparation, particularly in primary health care where clear guidance is essential for maintaining research integrity across diverse settings. This review aimed to assess the availability and content of AI policies across primary health care journals and their publishers. We identified primary health care journals through searches of SCImago Journal & Country Rank, Google Scholar, and a Google search. After screening for English language, functioning webpages, recent publications, and exclusion of predatory journals, 41 journals were included. Two reviewers independently reviewed journal homepages, author guidelines, submission policies, and editorial policies for AI-related statements at both journal and publisher levels between 18 and 21 July 2025. Of 41 journals assessed, 33 (80.5%) had publicly available AI policies - 21 (51.2%) at journal level and 12 (29.3%) at publisher level. Eight journals (19.5%) had no identifiable public AI policy. All identified policies were permissive toward AI use but varied in requirements across five key areas: disclosure of AI use, acceptable AI tasks, AI authorship considerations, author responsibility, and peer review guidelines. While most primary health care journals have established AI policies, significant gaps remain in accessibility and standardization. The fragmented governance landscape, characterized by inconsistent policy locations and requirements, creates confusion for authors and might compromise research integrity. Standardized, easily accessible AI policies are needed to enable researchers to harness AI's potential while maintaining transparency and scientific rigour essential to primary health care research.

items.title: A 'luxury' health struggle: a qualitative analysis of the socio-economic experiences of university students with celiac disease.
items.abstract: University students with celiac disease (CD) are considered a vulnerable group. The number of qualitative studies examining the challenges faced by this group is limited. The aim of the study was to analyse the social and economic impacts of the CD among university students diagnosed with CD who live away from their families. A qualitative phenomenological design was utilised. Semi-structured, face-to-face interviews were conducted. Data were analysed using Colaizzi's seven-stage strategy. Türkiye. Nine university students (mean age: 22 ± 1·6 years) diagnosed with CD. The students were living independently at home or dormitory in Konya. The qualitative analysis yielded six main themes: 'encountering the disease', 'adapting to the disease', 'living with the disease', 'impact on relationships', 'economic burden' and 'patient expectations'. Participants reported significant challenges regarding social isolation, lack of societal awareness (confusion between gluten and glucose) and food insecurity within university cafeterias and dormitories. The high cost of gluten-free products was identified as a major economic barrier, with the student described CD as a 'disease of the wealthy'. This study highlights that CD is not merely a clinical condition but a complex lifestyle challenge affecting all aspects of a student's educational and social life. Recognising CD from this holistic perspective is crucial for developing effective interventions, including targeted psychological counselling and institutional support mechanisms.

items.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and adverse outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic viral hepatitis.
items.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) are a novel class of anti-diabetic drugs that can treat obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D). T2D and chronic viral hepatitis (CVH) frequently coexist and worsen liver and non-liver outcomes, but effective pharmacological therapies are limited. We aimed to evaluate the effect of GLP-1RA on liver and non-liver complications among patients with T2D and CVH in the United States. Patients with T2D and CVH initiating GLP-1RA were included (2013-2022) in Merative™ Marketscan® Research Databases. Primary outcomes included (1) hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and cirrhosis, and (2) cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and non-liver cancer. Cox proportional hazards models were conducted to estimate hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence interval (CI). A total of 9,499 patients with T2D and CVH were included after 1:4 propensity score matching. Compared with non-GLP-1RA (N=7,366), GLP-1RA use (N=2,133) was associated with significantly lower risks of any liver-related outcomes (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.57-0.87; P=0.001), HCC (HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.31-0.93; P=0.028), cirrhosis (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.56-0.86; P<0.001), CKD (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.53-0.84; P<0.001). A trend toward a lower risk of CVD (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.66-1.03; P=0.089) and non-liver cancer (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.53-1.01; P=0.055) was observed among GLP-1RA users, although the association did not reach statistical significance. GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risks of cirrhosis, HCC, and CKD among patients with T2D and CVH, with nonsignificant trends toward lower risks of CVD and non-liver cancer.

items.title: From Target to Trial: Artificial Intelligence in Psychiatric Drug Development.
items.abstract: Plain Language SummaryHow Artificial Intelligence Could Improve Psychiatric Drug DevelopmentDeveloping new medicines for mental health conditions is difficult, expensive, and often unsuccessful. One reason is that people with the same diagnosis can differ greatly in their underlying biology and in how they respond to treatment. Clinical trials also rely heavily on symptom ratings and can be affected by placebo responses. This editorial explains how artificial intelligence (AI) could help at several stages of psychiatric drug development. AI can help researchers identify promising drug targets, design new treatment molecules, and use biological, brain-imaging, and clinical data to predict treatment response and improve clinical trials. Emerging approaches include digital twins, synthetic control groups, and digital measures of symptoms and behaviour. However, these technologies are still developing and should not be viewed as a solution to all the challenges of psychiatric drug development. Wider use will require representative datasets, strong data governance, transparent and interpretable models, rigorous clinical validation, and appropriate regulation.

items.title: Artificial intelligence early-warning systems for sepsis: From risk scores to bedside action.
items.abstract: BackgroundSepsis remains a leading cause of preventable mortality in critical care. Timely recognition is essential for effective bundle-based management, and artificial intelligence-enabled early-warning systems (AI-EWS) may facilitate earlier detection by converting electronic health record and bedside monitoring data into actionable risk estimates.ObjectiveThis review aimed to synthesize recent advances in the development, validation, and real-world deployment of AI-EWS for sepsis and to identify the factors that determine their clinical benefit at the unit level.MethodsWe conducted a structured narrative review based on a targeted search of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar from database inception to December 2025. Search terms combined artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning with sepsis and early-warning score or prediction. Priority was given to studies addressing prospective performance, clinical implementation, alert fatigue, workflow integration, governance, and regulation.ResultsAI-EWS may identify sepsis risk earlier than traditional scoring systems; however, retrospective discrimination alone does not ensure clinical benefit. Effective deployment depends on prospective calibration, site-specific threshold setting, precision-recall trade-offs, manageable alert budgets, and integration with nurse-centered workflows, standardized order sets, escalation pathways, and feedback loops. Major implementation risks include alert fatigue, data drift, and limited transportability. Silent-mode trials, group-aware recalibration, regular calibration and drift audits, throttle and rollback rules, and auditable change logs can help mitigate these risks.ConclusionAI-EWS should be evaluated as clinical interventions rather than solely as predictive models. Calibrated risk communication, unit-specific operating points, human-centered workflow integration, and accountable governance are essential for achieving safe, equitable, and measurable improvements in sepsis care.

items.title: Association Between Household Iodized Salt Trajectory and High Milk-Enriched Diet with Thyroid Nodules and Goiter in Children: A Prospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Universal salt iodization (USI) policies have achieved remarkable results in preventing iodine deficiency disorders globally. However, concerns regarding its safety have emerged along with rising detection rates of thyroid disorders and shifts in dietary structures. The association between iodized salt consumption and thyroid nodule development remains unclear, and the modifying role of dietary structures is not well understood. This study aimed to examine associations between iodized salt consumption and the incidence of thyroid nodules and goiter, accounting for dietary structures. This prospective cohort study enrolled 8464 school-aged children across 79 schools from 2021 to 2023. Salt exposure and dietary structures were assessed via household sampling and questionnaires. Thyroid nodules and goiter were identified through ultrasonography. Latent class trajectory modeling identified iodized and noniodized salt trajectories, alongside high milk-enriched and low milk-enriched dietary structures. Cox proportional hazards model and logistic regression model were applied to analyze the associations between salt trajectories and dietary structures with thyroid nodules and goiter separately. Two thousand seven hundred and seven (32.0%) participants developed thyroid nodules and 164 (1.9%) had goiter. Two salt trajectories were identified: iodized (7892; 93.2%) and noniodized (572; 6.8%). Iodized salt was associated with lower risks of nodules (hazard ratio [HR], 0.806 [confidence interval or CI: 0.659-0.986]) and goiter (odds ratio, 0.458 [CI: 0.299-0.669]). However, the association with nodules did not persist in region-stratified analyses (HR, 1.114 [CI: 0.745-1.667]). A high milk-enriched diet was consistently associated with reduced nodule risk (HR, 0.867 [CI: 0.787-0.956]) and remained significant in all sensitivity analyses. A significant interaction was observed between dietary structure and salt trajectory (adjusted p for interaction = 0.024). A U-shaped relationship was observed between salt iodine concentration and nodule risk, with an inflection point at 21.3 mg/kg. Iodized salt was associated with lower goiter risk, but its inverse association with thyroid nodules was not observed after region restriction. A high milk-enriched diet was inversely associated with thyroid nodules. These findings support continued USI for goiter prevention and highlight the importance of regional iodine status and dietary patterns when interpreting household salt use and thyroid outcomes in children.

items.title: Dietary Inflammatory Index and cardiorespiratory fitness among older adults living in the community: a cross-sectional analysis.
items.abstract: The optimal dietary recommendation for healthy ageing remains unclear. This study examined the association between the Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) and cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) in Chinese community-dwelling older adults. Data were drawn from the Guangzhou Nutrition and Health Study's 3rd and 4th follow-up visits (2017-2021). DII was calculated from a Seventy nine-item validated FFQ, and CRF was assessed on a cycle ergometer using a submaximal constant work rate protocol. VO2max was estimated via the Åstrand-Ryhming Nomogram with age correction, and relative intensity was expressed as percentage of predicted maximal heart rate (%HRmax). Favourable CRF was defined as sex-specific VO2max in the top quartile or %HRmax < 85 %. Among 906 participants (615 women, 291 men; mean age 65·9 ± 5·4 years), those in the lowest DII tertile (anti-inflammatory diet) had higher VO2max than those in the highest tertile (P-trend = 0·048) and greater odds of favourable CRF (OR 1·81, 95 % CI 1·22-2·70), while no significant associations were observed for %HRmax (P-trend = 0·356; OR 1·31, 95 % CI 0·94-1·84). Associations between lower DII and higher VO2max were stronger among physically active participants (P-interaction = 0·049). Compared with consistently high DII, both transition to a low-inflammatory diet (OR 3·01, 95 % CI 1·20-7·51) and persistent adherence to such a diet (OR 2·49, 95 % CI 1·28-4·87) were associated with favourable CRF. These findings suggest that an anti-inflammatory diet is associated with better CRF in older adults, with potential synergistic benefits from physical activity.Trial registration: This trial was registered at clinicaltrials.gov as NCT03179657.

items.title: Completion of human papillomavirus vaccination and its determinants among adolescents in Southern Ethiopia: a convergent parallel mixed-methods study.
items.abstract: Cervical cancer is the second most common cancer among women in Ethiopia and is primarily attributable to human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. Although HPV vaccination has been introduced, completion of the recommended two-dose schedule remains suboptimal. Existing evidence has largely focused on access and awareness, with limited attention to cognitive, sociocultural, and maternal decision-making factors influencing completion. This study assessed the magnitude and determinants of second-dose or complete HPV vaccination among adolescents in southern Ethiopia using a mixed-methods approach. A community-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among 832 mothers of adolescent girls aged 9-14 years, selected using a multistage sampling method. Data were collected using a semi-structured questionnaire and analyzed with IBM SPSS ver. 23.0. A binary logistic regression model was used to identify factors associated with vaccine completion. Additionally, in-depth interviews were conducted with 12 purposively selected mothers and analyzed thematically to explore perceptions influencing vaccine completion. The proportion of adolescents who completed the HPV vaccination series was 26.3% (95% confidence interval, 23.3-29.3). Factors positively associated with complete vaccination included maternal education at the secondary or higher, shared or autonomous maternal decision-making, prior cervical cancer screening and good knowledge of HPV. Conversely, high information overload and decision fatigue were associated with lower odds of completing the vaccination schedule. Qualitative findings revealed that mothers' decisions were shaped by cultural beliefs, trust in health workers, peer and social media influences, and prior healthcare experience. HPV vaccination completion was low and was associated with interacting cognitive, socio-cultural, and health-system factors. Interventions should move beyond awareness creation to address information burden, strengthen maternal decision-making autonomy, and improve trust through consistent counseling.

items.title: Gender differences among board-certified general surgeons in Israel: demographics, professional advancement, and leadership.
items.abstract: Women remain underrepresented in general surgery leadership and academic roles globally, yet specialty-specific data from Israel are limited. This study examines gender differences among board-certified general surgeons in Israel across demographic, professional, and leadership domains. A cross-sectional, confidential questionnaire was distributed electronically to all board-certified general surgeons registered with the Israeli Surgical Association in 2026. A total of 105 surgeons responded (15.2%). Participants were stratified by gender and compared across demographic characteristics, employment patterns, operative scope, fellowship training, academic activity, and management roles. Of 105 respondents, 78 (74.3%) were men and 27 (25.7%) were women. Women had a longer residency duration (median 7 vs. 6 years, p = 0.024). Women were less likely to hold full-time public hospital positions (63.0% vs. 84.6%, p = 0.029), participate in on-call (44.4% vs. 80.8%, p = 0.0009) or senior on-call duties (7.4% vs. 38.5%, p = 0.003), and had a substantially narrower operative scope (median 3 vs. 5 surgery types, p = 0.0002). Women were significantly more likely to practice breast surgery (48.1% vs. 16.7%, p = 0.002) and less likely to have completed a fellowship (59.3% vs. 84.6%, p = 0.013) or trained abroad (25.9% vs. 62.8%, p = 0.0015). Academic productivity was also lower among women: fewer taught students (74.1% vs. 91.0%, p = 0.044), published articles (29.6% vs. 65.4%, p = 0.002), or held academic appointments (25.9% vs. 50.0%, p = 0.042). Women were less likely to hold any management role (25.9% vs. 51.3%, p = 0.026). Significant gender disparities exist among board-certified general surgeons in Israel across all domains examined. Women bear a systematically different professional burden, with less call coverage, narrower operative scope, fewer fellowships, lower academic output, and reduced leadership representation. These findings highlight structural barriers that persist beyond training completion. Of particular concern is the leadership gap: in the Israeli hospital system, senior positions are long-tenured and turn over infrequently, meaning that generational change in the trainee demographic alone will not close this gap within any reasonable timeframe. Mandatory, policy-level structural intervention is required alongside broader institutional efforts to promote gender equity in Israeli general surgery.

items.title: Insights from the young people who serve on youth advisory councils in Africa: a mixed-methods study.
items.abstract: Youth Advisory Councils (YAC) are increasingly recognized as key mechanisms to promote meaningful youth engagement. Despite the rapidly growing adolescent population in Africa, existing research on youth engagement largely focuses on barriers to youth engagement in non-African contexts. This mixed-methods study expands understanding of youth engagement by examining who participates in YACs in Africa, how YAC members in Africa define meaningful youth engagement, and what factors facilitate their participation. This cross-sectional study draws on quantitative surveys (n = 154) and qualitative interviews (n = 14) with current or past YAC members living in Africa (aged 18-30 years old). Quantitative data were summarized using descriptive statistics and interviews were analyzed thematically. Findings from both sources were triangulated to identify key patterns. Participants resided across 15 countries, and the majority were current YAC members (94.2%). Despite diverse experiences within their roles on advisory councils, YAC members shared a common conceptualization of meaningful youth engagement, including co-creating and valuing youth voices. Further, YAC members voiced that co-creating and valuing youth voices is attainable through two key factors: integrating youth perspectives into organizational frameworks and providing key support. However, many participants' lived experiences as youth advisors fell short of true meaningful youth engagement. Our findings underscore the importance of youth-led engagement in Africa and organizational support to foster meaningful youth engagement, particularly in light of the continent's rapidly expanding youth demographic. Engaging and amplifying the voices of adolescents when developing policies and advocating for solutions is essential for both youth development and social and economic outcomes.

items.title: Evaluation of antibacterial activity of hydroethanolic seed extract of Descurainia sophia against multidrug-resistant Salmonella typhi isolated from typhoid patients: an integrated in silico and in vitro study.
items.abstract: Typhoid fever caused by Salmonella typhi remains a major public health problem, and multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant strains have left few oral treatment options in endemic regions such as Pakistan. Seeds of Descurainia sophia (L.) are used in Unani and folk medicine for febrile illness and contain cardenolides, glucosinolate-derived isothiocyanates and long-chain fatty acids, but their activity against MDR S. typhi and a plausible molecular target have not been examined. We therefore combined in silico and in vitro approaches to evaluate a hydroethanolic seed extract against clinical MDR S. typhi isolates. A library of 14 literature-reported seed compounds was screened by ADMET profiling (admetSAR 3.0), which selected three drug-like cardenolides (helveticoside, evomonoside and strophanthidin); these were docked against DNA gyrase A with moxifloxacin and gemifloxacin as references, and the top-ranked lead, helveticoside, was then examined in a 50 ns all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. The extract was characterised by GC-MS and FTIR and tested against five MDR isolates (MDR-ST1 to MDR-ST5) by disc diffusion and broth microdilution (CLSI M07). GC-MS confirmed 13 of the 14 library compounds (91.4% of total ion chromatogram area), including the three leads; erysimoside was the only compound not detected. Helveticoside (- 9.7 kcal/mol) and evomonoside (- 9.5) showed higher predicted affinities than moxifloxacin (- 7.9) and gemifloxacin (- 8.2); strophanthidin scored - 8.5. In the MD simulation, the helveticoside complex remained stable (ligand RMSD ~ 1.8 Å without dissociation; protein Cα RMSD ~ 2.2-2.5 Å after ~ 15 ns), and 12 residues, including ARG31, SER185 and GLN288, contacted the ligand in > 95% of frames, six of them also present in the docked pose. The extract inhibited all five isolates in a dose-dependent manner (mean zone of inhibition 11.5-17.15 mm at 25-100 mg/mL; 19.3 ± 0.9 mm for moxifloxacin, reported descriptively because the extract is crude), with a geometric mean MIC of 8.4 mg/mL (range 6.25-12.5) and MBC/MIC = 2 for all isolates, consistent with bactericidal activity. FTIR showed functional groups consistent with the major constituent classes.Docking and MD together generate the hypothesis that DNA gyrase A inhibition by cardenolide constituents may contribute to the antibacterial effect of the extract. The MD simulation supports the structural stability of the predicted helveticoside binding mode but does not demonstrate enzyme inhibition, and fatty acids and isothiocyanates in the extract may also contribute. Overall, the crude extract showed in vitro antibacterial activity against MDR S. typhi at high concentrations, and the study provides a testable mechanistic hypothesis that requires bioactivity-guided fractionation, pure-compound testing and target-engagement assays.

items.title: Impaired cortical inhibition in blepharospasm: evidence from reduced short-latency afferent inhibition and shortened cortical silent period.
items.abstract: Blepharospasm (BSP) is a neural network disorder with poorly understood cortical electrophysiological mechanisms. To investigate intracortical excitability and sensorimotor pathways in BSP patients and evaluate the effects of botulinum toxin A (BoNT-A) on cortical activity. Thirty BSP patients and 20 healthy controls underwent single- and paired-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to assess indices including SAI, CSP, SICI, and ICF. Sixteen treatment-naive patients were reassessed one month post-BoNT-A injection. BSP patients showed significantly reduced SAI and shortened CSP compared to controls. Impaired SAI strongly correlated with disease severity scores (BFMDRS and GDSRS: r ranging from 0.514 to0.782, p < 0.01). SICI and ICF showed no group differences. Furthermore, BoNT-A treatment failed to reverse these central cortical abnormalities.Notably, these deficits were recorded from the clinically unaffected abductor pollicis brevis muscle and therefore represent widespread cortical trait markers rather direct evidence of dysfunction within the eyelid circuit itself. BSP is characterized by impaired cortical inhibition that is consistent with cholinergic dysfunction. BoNT-A relieves symptoms peripherally without altering fundamental central cortical excitability.The cortical deficits, recorded from an unaffected limb, indicate a generalised rather than eyelid-specific abnormality.

items.title: Construction of a machine learning model for dual-region typing of norovirus RdRp and VP1 based on genomic k-mer features.
items.abstract: Norovirus (NoV), a major global acute gastroenteritis pathogen, has high genetic diversity. Developing precise, rapid typing methods is crucial for epidemic control and vaccine development. Thus, this study develops a machine learning tool based on Norovirus genomic k-mer (length-k nucleotide fragments) features. It enables rapid, accurate dual-region typing of RdRp (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) and VP1 (major capsid protein) without alignment or segmentation. Using k-mer frequency features with k = 11, the MurmurHash3 algorithm maps the features to a 2²⁰-dimensional space and constructs a hash feature table. A random forest model comprising 500 decision trees is then used. Each tree randomly selects 20 features during node splitting. The model is trained and evaluated using a bootstrap sampling strategy (80% training and 20% out-of-bag estimation), and prediction confidence intervals are outputted. The typing accuracy rates for the RdRp region and VP1 region reached 97.6% and 99.3%, respectively. Analysis of precision, recall, and F1-score for each genotype in the test set showed that all metrics for the 40 RdRp genotypes and 34 VP1 genotypes were ≥ 0.9. Typing accuracy across all length intervals was ≥ 0.96. This study integrates machine learning and bioinformatics to develop a novel norovirus genome analysis tool. It enables precise genotyping despite multi-region interference and reveals hidden genomic information, supporting viral classification and tracing. The feature hashing and ensemble learning strategies overcome traditional dependencies on alignment and annotation, offering a universal, efficient, scalable framework for viral genome identification.

items.title: Pteryxin disarms MRSA by suppressing the CrtN-staphyloxanthin axis and mitigates osteomyelitis-associated bone damage.
items.abstract: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) remains a major public health concern because of its resistance to commonly used antibiotics and its association with severe infections. Staphyloxanthin (STX), a membrane-associated carotenoid pigment, contributes to MRSA virulence by protecting bacterial cells against reactive oxygen species and host immune clearance. CrtN, a dehydrosqualene desaturase, catalyzes an essential step in STX biosynthesis and represents a potential antivirulence target. In this study, an STX inhibition assay identified pteryxin (PTX), a natural coumarin derivative, as an inhibitor of STX production, with an IC50 of 4.826 µg/mL (12.49 µM). At concentrations that did not measurably affect bacterial growth, PTX reduced STX-associated pigmentation, increased susceptibility to oxidative stress and whole-blood killing and altered membrane-associated properties of USA300. Biophysical analyses, including surface plasmon resonance, thermal shift assay, cellular thermal shift assay, and intrinsic fluorescence quenching, supported an interaction between PTX and CrtN. Molecular docking predicted a possible binding mode involving Arg330 and Ser349. PTX also improved survival in a Galleria mellonella infection model and attenuated bacterial burden and bone damage in an early-treatment rat model of MRSA-associated bone infection. These findings support PTX as a potential antivirulence agent that suppresses STX biosynthesis through a CrtN-associated mechanism.
