items.title: Volume Dependence of Helicity-based Eruption Diagnostics in Recurrent Coronal Jets
items.abstract: Abstract Recurrent solar coronal jets originate from the same source region, providing a useful setting for studying the buildup, redistribution, and release of magnetic energy and helicity. However, how these quantities can characterize magnetic evolution and the onset conditions of the eruptions remains unclear. We perform a full three-dimensional (3D) thermodynamic magnetohydrodynamic simulation of recurrent jets driven by converging motions imposed at the bottom boundary. The simulation naturally produces two successive eruptions. The current-carrying helicity H J decreases during the first jet and gradually recovers between the two jets. In contrast, the free magnetic energy E free shows no clear accumulation after its first release. This difference indicates that H J provides information on magnetic evolution beyond that provided by E free . Furthermore, the commonly used helicity ratio H J / H V reaches different peaks near the onset of the two jets and is sensitive to the integration volume. By comparison, the locally normalized quantity H J / Φ closed 2 reaches similar peaks near the onset of both jets and is relatively insensitive to the choice among the tested integration volumes, where Φ closed is the single-polarity magnetic flux of the closed-field domain. These results reveal the local nature of the eruptions and suggest that H J normalized by the square of the closed magnetic flux may be a useful diagnostic of eruptive conditions.

items.title: KMOS spectroscopic follow-up of 16 star cluster candidates in the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy
items.abstract: The Sagittarius (Sgr) dwarf spheroidal galaxy hosts several known globular clusters and numerous additional cluster candidates identified towards its crowded central regions. Establishing the nature of these candidates is difficult because apparent spatial and astrometric structure can arise from the underlying Sgr population. We investigated sixteen Minni stellar-cluster candidates with KMOS spectroscopy to determine whether the observed stars are compatible with Sgr and whether any candidate field shows evidence for a distinct stellar system. We analysed H-band KMOS spectra of 341 targets from the VVVX--GalCen Spectroscopic Survey, deriving radial velocities (RVs) and empirical metallicities. We compared these with an independent Sgr spectroscopic sample and used VVVX photometry and DR3 astrometry to test for localised stellar excesses relative to local control fields. Gaia Of the 341 KMOS targets, 256 (75%) have RVs within the adopted Sgr interval, and their metallicities broadly overlap the Sgr comparison population. No field shows statistically compelling kinematic evidence for a distinct system after accounting for the multiple examined candidates. Minni 329 shows the strongest spatial excess. However, this is not significant after multiple-testing correction and is not accompanied by significant central concentration. The KMOS targets predominantly trace the Sgr population, but Sgr compatibility alone does not confirm the individual candidates as distinct stellar clusters. None of the sixteen fields can be confirmed as a separate stellar system with the present data, although this does not establish that the original candidates are spurious. Deeper imaging and larger spectroscopic samples are required to determine their physical nature.

items.title: The deepest X-ray view of a kiloparsec-scale jet at z=6.1
items.abstract: Context: The mechanism responsible for the high-energy emission observed in kiloparsec scale jets across cosmic time remains poorly understood. The relativistic jet associated with the z=6.1 AGN PSO J030947.49+271757.31 represents the highest z large-scale jet currently resolved in the X-rays and provides a unique laboratory to study the evolution of these structures. Aim: We present a study aimed at constraining the morphology and spectral properties of the kiloparsec-scale jet associated with PSO J030947.49+271757.31. In addition, we intend to investigate the capabilities of future X-ray observatories in the study of extended jets. Methods: We obtained new dedicated observations of PSO J030947.49+271757.31 with the Chandra X-ray Observatory (for a total of 360 ksec combined with archival data). Thanks to the improvement of a factor of sim3 in exposure time compared to previous studies, we spatially resolved the extended X-ray emission into two distinct components and performed spatially resolved spectral analyses of the different regions. Results: We confirmed the presence of extended X-ray emission of PSO J030947.49+271757.31 with significantly improved statistics and identified two separate and slightly resolved components. The X-ray spectrum of the extended emission has a photon index of Γ = 2.25^ +0.45 _ -0.44 , i.e., steeper than that of the core (Γ = 1.86 /L_ and an extended-to-core-luminosity ratio of L_ ̊m ext ̊m core =18%. Using the Chandra image as input, we performed simulations for next-generation X-ray facilities. An AXIS-like mission would increase the detected photon statistics by a factor of sim17 compared to the current Chandra dataset. Conclusions: We resolved the kiloparsec-scale jet associated with this z=6.1 AGN into two main components and constrained its spectral properties. This extended component corresponds to the most distant and one of the most X-ray-luminous large-scale jets currently known. Simulations show that future X-ray missions with arcsecond-scale angular resolution will not only enable significantly more detailed studies of systems such as PSO J030947.49+271757.31, it will also reveal a population of fainter high-redshift jets currently beyond the reach of Chandra .

items.title: Predicting supply chain bottlenecks with real-time data: a bibliometric review of transport and logistics research from 2016 to 2025
items.abstract: Abstract Supply chain bottlenecks are critical constraints that disrupt the smooth flow of goods, often triggering delays that cascade through interconnected processes and weaken overall resilience. In an era of digital transformation, the ability to anticipate such constraints through real-time data and predictive analytics has become increasingly important, yet the existing literature remains fragmented across transportation, logistics, and information systems, leaving conceptual boundaries blurred and practical insights underdeveloped. Addressing this gap, we conducted a bibliometric review of 3638 Scopus-indexed publications from 2016 to 2025, using Bibliometrix and VOSviewer to analyse publication patterns, keyword clusters, and thematic evolution. The findings reveal a strong concentration in intelligent transportation systems, with traffic congestion emerging as the most frequent theme, and four clusters identified around traffic management and detection, congestion and travel-time modelling, data infrastructure and analytics, and short-horizon flow control. A clear shift is observed between 2016–2020 and 2021–2025, marked by the growing prominence of machine learning and deep learning approaches. The study contributes by distinguishing transport-level prediction from supply chain-level bottleneck management. It further proposes a research agenda that emphasises cross-context validation, prediction-to-action integration, and explicit tests of forecast usefulness, thereby offering both theoretical clarity and practical guidance for strengthening supply chain performance.

items.title: Transforming Social Media: A Prophetic Model for Moral and Digital Responsibility
items.abstract: Social media has emerged as one of the most powerful tools of the modern age, capable of serving both constructive and destructive purposes. In today’s interconnected world, it shapes public opinion, influences perceptions, and drives social trends. However, its misuse has become widespread, with talented individuals spending excessive time on unproductive online activities and entire societies increasingly influenced by its addictive nature. The resulting consequences, including adverse effects on mental and physical health, the rise of self-centeredness, and the erosion of genuine human connection, have significantly affected the moral and social fabric of Muslim societies. Moreover, social media has become a channel for immoral trends, indecent content, and anti-Islamic ideologies, posing challenges to faith, identity, and collective consciousness. For the Muslim Ummah, the Prophetic model of communication offers an effective framework for addressing these challenges. Inspired by this model, governments must not only regulate social media but also educate citizens on its beneficial use by enhancing digital literacy, cultivating ethical awareness, and developing a moral framework rooted in truthfulness, integrity, and compassion. Policies may include anti-addiction measures, promotion of educational and humanitarian content, and reward systems to encourage positive digital engagement. Implementing the Prophetic model at the state level can transform social media from a source of societal decline into a force for moral, educational, and communal progress.

items.title: Short-term solar flare forecasting with a hybrid ConvNeXtV2 and transformer–temporal convolutional network
items.abstract: Solar flares are violent energy-release events in the solar atmosphere, accompanied by intense electromagnetic radiation and energetic particles that threaten satellites, radio communications, and power infrastructure, making accurate flare prediction essential for space weather early warning. This paper proposes a deep learning model integrating ConvNeXtV2 with a Transformer–Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) to forecast whether a solar active region will produce a ≥ C-class or ≥ M-class flare within the next 24 h. Using SHARP magnetograms and magnetic parameters from SDO/HMI (2010–2019), ConvNeXtV2 first extracts spatial structural and deep semantic features from the magnetograms; the resulting feature sequences are then fed into the Transformer–TCN module, where the Transformer captures global temporal dependencies and the TCN models local dynamic features of active-region evolution. The two components jointly predict flare occurrence probability, with the True Skill Statistic (TSS) as the primary metric. Under active-region-isolated five-fold cross-validation, the model achieves TSS values of 0.861 ± 0.021 and 0.844 ± 0.041 for the ≥ C-class and ≥ M-class tasks, respectively, and performs at least as well as the strongest baselines retrained on the same data and the same folds. These results indicate that combining ConvNeXtV2 with the Transformer–TCN characterizes both the magnetic field structure of active regions and its dynamic evolution, offering a further option for short-term solar flare forecasting.

items.title: Quantum Omnipresence and the Probability of a Creator: A Standard Quantum Mechanical Derivation
items.abstract: This study examines a proposed connection between zero-energy cosmological models, quantum states, and the conceptual possibility of a purposeful origin of the universe. Within the Indeterminate Null framework, the analysis considers a hypothetical zero-energy, zero-momentum initial state and investigates its mathematical properties using uncertainty relations, the Schr?dinger equation, quantum field theory, and quantum superposition. The study also discusses cosmological fine-tuning arguments and compares two proposed origin scenarios under selected assumptions. A free-particle plane-wave model with zero momentum and energy yields a spatially and temporally constant amplitude, although its physical interpretation depends on normalization, boundary conditions, and the existence of an appropriate spacetime description. The analysis identifies possible conceptual connections between quantum delocalization and the proposed interpretation of omnipresence. The probability comparison remains conditional on assumptions about prior distributions, independence, and physical mechanisms. The findings provide a theoretical framework for further investigation rather than a definitive demonstration of a creator or a unique cosmological origin mechanism. Determinate Null (IN) framework replaces the continuous real-number coordinate domain used in selected physical calculations with a finite discrete set bounded by the Planck length and a de Sitter scale. Building on the photon-gravity construction introduced in earlier work, this paper defines an IN derivative as a forward finite difference, an IN integral as a finite sum, and an associated telescoping Fundamental Theorem. Three applications are examined. First, imposing the resulting ultraviolet and infrared bounds converts the vacuum zero-point-energy expression into a finite quantity, while leaving a large discrepancy with the observed dark-energy density. Second, evaluation of cosmological quantities from a finite Planck-scale starting point avoids evaluation at zero time and permits a discrete recurrence formulation. Third, restricting radial coordinates to values no smaller than the Planck length bounds the Schwarzschild Kretschmann scalar on the proposed domain. These results show how finite-domain discretization removes the specific mathematical divergences considered here. Further justification is required m-field and gravitational problems.

items.title: Observational Evidence of Positive Feedback from Radio Quasars
items.abstract: Abstract Feedback from active galactic nuclei (AGNs) is widely regarded as a key mechanism mediating the coevolution of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) and their host galaxies. Jets constitute a dominant channel of mechanical energy output and are associated with so-called “radio-mode” feedback. However, the net effect of “radio-mode” feedback—whether it suppresses or enhances star formation—remains observationally unresolved. Here we construct a sample of 1784 radio-detected quasars from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), cross-matched with deep radio surveys: Low-Frequency Array (LOFAR) and Very Large Array Sky Survey (VLASS). We trace the star formation rate (SFR) in quasars' host galaxies across the jet lifetime. Our results reveal a statistically significant, monotonic rise-then-decline trend in the SFRs when jets evolve, which is consistent with hydrodynamical simulations predicting that jet-induced compression of the interstellar medium triggers star formation in its early phases. This trend remains statistically robust under rigorous multivariate control for key confounding parameters, including black hole mass, bolometric luminosity, and redshift. Collectively, our findings indicate that AGN radio jets exert positive influence on star formation over most of their evolutionary cycle.

items.title: Extreme Enrichment at Cosmic Dawn: Three Fe II -strong Quasars at z > 6 from the JWST Aether Survey
items.abstract: Abstract We present three outliers on the quasar main sequence at z > 6, as revealed by JWST/NIRSpec integral field unit (IFU) observations from the Aether survey, a program targeting ∼200 quasars at cosmic dawn. The quasars, J0216−5226, J0320−3521, and J1429+5447, exhibit exceptionally strong Fe ii emission and weak H β and [O iii ] lines, indicating rapid chemical enrichment within the first Gyr of cosmic history. Their Fe ii strengths ( R Fe II, λ 4570 ≡ EW Fe II /EW H β ) range between ∼2.5 and 3.6, placing them among the top ∼3% of Sloan Digital Sky Survey quasars at (0 ≲ z ≲ 1). The H α emission lines of J0216−5226 and J1429+5447 imply black hole masses of ∼1–7 × 10 9 M ⊙ with λ Edd ∼ 0.1–0.6, comparable to typical high- z quasars, although virial black hole masses may be systematically overestimated in strong Fe ii emitters. In contrast, J0320−3521 hosts a lower-mass black hole of ∼0.2–2 × 10 9 M ⊙ , suggesting possible super-Eddington rate accretion with λ Edd ∼ 0.5–6.0. The IFU data of J0320−3521 reveal a distinct emission-line region at a projected distance of ∼1.5 kpc, consistent with either an interacting companion or ionized gas associated to the quasar. We further identify a complex environment around J1429+5447, including two candidate companion galaxies or extended ionized gas structures. These quasars with bright emission-line regions, J0320−3521 and J1429+5447, are radio-loud sources, while J0216−5226 remains undetected in radio ( R 5GHz, 3 σ ≲ 4). Together, these results confirm previous findings that highly enriched, rapidly growing black holes were already in place at cosmic dawn. Despite the small sample size, our results further highlight the diversity in environment and radio-jet properties among quasars that otherwise share the same extreme region of the quasar fundamental plane.

items.title: Kirovs_Theory_of_the_Cosmic_Omnipresence_of_Life
items.abstract: The Inevitability of Planetary Systems: The formation of planetary systems is a natural byproduct of stellar-evolutionary physics. Modern astronomy confirms that stellar birth is consistently accompanied by the formation of protoplanetary disks. Consequently, every star possesses a potential spectrum of rocky and gaseous bodies. Statistical Certainty: Under conditions of spatial scale tending to infinity and stellar energy radiating across trillions of galaxies, the number of planets within habitable zones ceases to be a matter of chance. Across an infinite number of trials with a continuous energy flux, the probability of conditions for life approaches certainty (100%). The Energy Catalyst: Stellar energy provides the unceasing thermodynamic push that organizes non-organic matter into complex molecular chains. Space provides infinite physical environments ("laboratories"), while stellar fire provides the time and temperature required for chemical evolution.

items.title: On the difficulty of rational numbers
items.abstract: Abstract Learning rational numbers poses significant challenges in mathematics education. Recent work has suggested introducing rational numbers starting with the easiest format (i.e., fractions, decimals, or percentages). However, difficulty may not only be influenced by the format itself but also by other factors which drive difficulty within formats, such as responses types (e.g., multiple-choice vs. open-ended responses) and problem types (e.g., visualization, mere calculations, or word problems). Yet, conclusive evidence on how response types and problem types drive the difficulty within each of the three different rational number formats is largely missing. To address this gap, we analyzed a large-scale dataset (around 38,000 learners completing more than 7,000,000 problem steps) from an intelligent tutoring system. We found large differences in error rates within each rational number format, ranging from about 22% for problems including visualizations to 69% for word problems. These findings suggest that difficulty is not driven by rational number format alone but also varies substantially with response type and problem type within formats. Thus, instructional sequencing may benefit from considering not only the order in which fractions, decimals, and percentages are introduced, but also variation in problem difficulty within each format. Our findings provide an empirical basis for developing and experimentally testing sequences that progress from relatively easier to more difficult problems, thereby allowing researchers to identify sequencing approaches that are optimal for performance and learning.

items.title: Digital twin creation and residual analysis using CLEAN for radar target emulation
items.abstract: Abstract Radar sensors in advanced driver assistance systems sense the traffic scene identifying reflections occurring in the environment. Clutter contained in the data is caused by multipath and scattering effects leading to signal processing challenges to identify weak targets, which is critical for vulnerable road users. To be able to test a radar for its robustness against clutter, suitable clutter models are required. In this paper, an approach for filtering reflections following the CLEAN algorithm is proposed. By iterative decomposition of processed radar data to a superposition of point sources, reflections are isolated for a replay with a radar target simulator (RTS) to form a digital twin. Field datasets recorded in a parking garage are analyzed for its radar target and clutter statistics. After the analysis, a list of possible point targets for replay with an RTS is available and residual radar cross-section levels are analyzed and compared to Swerling I case.

items.title: PANORAMIC: The Dawn of Massive Quiescent Galaxies. I. Number Density and Cosmic Variance from 1000 arcmin 2 NIRCam Imaging
items.abstract: Abstract We measure the number density and field-to-field variance of massive quiescent galaxies at z ∼ 3–8 using the JWST/NIRCam pure-parallel imaging survey PANORAMIC together with archival observations, covering an area of 0.28 deg 2 (∼1000 arcmin 2 ) in at least six filters. We identify quiescent galaxy candidates at z ≳ 3 with M * ≳ 10 10 M ⊙ , comprising 101 galaxies in a gold sample of high-confidence candidates and 137 in a more inclusive silver sample. We measure their evolving comoving number density, finding (1.5 versus 3.1) × 10 −5 Mpc −3 at z = 3–4 for the gold and silver samples, respectively, and a decline by more than a factor of 20 by z ∼ 6. Comparisons with empirical models and cosmological simulations show that widely used frameworks underpredict the abundance of massive quiescent galaxies at z ≳ 4 by ≳1 dex, indicating that current implementations of early star formation, feedback, and quenching do not produce enough early quenched systems. With 34 independent sight lines, we present the first direct empirical measurement of field-to-field variance for quiescent galaxies at z > 3, finding a high cosmic variance of σ CV ≈ 0.7 ± 0.3. This exceeds predictions from abundance-matched mock catalogs, suggesting that early quiescent galaxies are more strongly clustered, and more likely to be found near one another or in more biased regions, than expected in current galaxy-formation models. Any successful model for the emergence of early massive quiescent galaxies must reproduce both their abundance evolution and their imprint on the large-scale distribution.

items.title: Pathology of the intervertebral disks and other spinal lesions in 31 aging inbred mouse strains.
items.abstract: In a large-scale aging study of 31 inbred strains of mice, a variety of age-related lesions arose in and around the spine (vertebrae, spinal cord, and adjacent connective and muscle tissues), including lesions of intervertebral disks, vertebrae, muscles, soft tissues, nerves, ganglia, and spinal cord that were either sporadic or strain-specific. In most cases, the mice did not present with obvious clinical signs, as many lesions were mild. Lesions included herniated or displaced intervertebral disk fragments, which appeared to be sporadic in most strains but were common in others. Fibro-osseous lesions of bones were a systemic disease in female mice with no effect on disk disease. Rhabdomyosarcomas were common in A/J mice surrounding the vertebrae but also invaded into the spinal canal, sometimes almost transecting the cord. Lymphomas affected all AKR/J mice, sometimes infiltrating into the spinal canal. Muscular dystrophy of the musculature surrounding the spine, due to mutations in the dysferlin (Dysf) gene, was common in A/J and SJL/J mice. Coccygeal hemivertebra was a novel strain-specific lesion only in PL/J mice. Sporadic lesions in and around the spine included hemangiosarcomas, lymphomas (both enlarged lymph nodes and invading in and around the vertebrae), schwannomas, histiocytic sarcomas, poorly differentiated sarcomas, and epidermoid/dermoid cysts. Since these strains have all been sequenced and annotated, polymorphisms in genes known to affect the pathogenesis of some of these lesions will be reported in other publications.

items.title: Muscular = Fake? Testing a Picture-Word Pairing Procedure to Increase Muscle Appearance Satisfaction in Young Men.
items.abstract: When men compare their bodies to those of muscular fitness models, this may result in dissatisfaction with their own muscularity. We tested whether pairing pictures of male muscular-ideal models with synonyms of 'fake' results in an increase in muscle satisfaction and a decrease in self-objectification among young men. Male participants (N = 66, M age = 22.86, SD = 2.14) were randomly assigned to an experimental (n = 32) or control (n = 34) condition of a picture-word pairing procedure. Both conditions showed the same pictures of muscular-ideal models. In the experimental condition these pictures were systemically paired with synonyms of 'fake'; in the control condition these pictures were randomly paired with words related to sports and colours. Participants in the experimental condition showed a modest increase in muscle appearance satisfaction from pre- to posttest whereas control participants did not change. Change in muscle appearance satisfaction was not moderated by internalisation of the appearance ideal. The predicted decrease in self-objectification was not found. The present research provides initial evidence that pairing pictures of male muscular-ideal models with 'fake' can enhance muscle appearance satisfaction in young men. The study was pre-registered at https://aspredicted.org/uy9zp5.pdf.

items.title: Intestinal Methanogen Overgrowth in Parkinson's Disease Reflects Constipation Physiology: A Matched Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Intestinal methanogen overgrowth (IMO) is associated with delayed intestinal transit. Chronic constipation and slow colonic transit are common in Parkinson's disease (PD) and may favor methanogen overgrowth. The goal was to characterize IMO prevalence in PD and compare findings with constipation reference groups. We retrospectively studied patients with PD who underwent hydrogen-methane breath testing at a tertiary center. IMO was defined as peak methane ≥10 ppm. Patients were matched 1:2 to constipation-spectrum comparators by age, sex, body mass index, test substrate, and irritable bowel syndrome status. A separate constipation cohort with objective colonic transit data provided sensitivity comparisons. Among 93 patients with PD, IMO was present in 46.2% and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) in 15.1%. Isolated IMO occurred in 36.6% and IMO + SIBO in 9.7%. IMO prevalence did not differ by substrate, time relative to PD diagnosis or Movement Disorder Society Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale part III motor score (all P > 0.05). IMO prevalence was comparable between PD and the matched chronic constipation population (42.1% vs. 44.7%; P = 0.703) with similar methane burden. Specifically, IMO prevalence in PD was comparable to that in slow-transit constipation (46% vs. 48%), but significantly higher than in normal-transit constipation (46% vs. 29%; adjusted P = 0.038). In this first characterization of IMO in PD, nearly half of patients tested met criteria for IMO-a prevalence comparable to slow-transit constipation and independent of motor severity or disease duration. Prospective studies should determine whether constipation-directed treatment alone or with methanogen-directed therapy improves outcomes in this population.

items.title: Focused Ultrasound for Essential Tremor in Denmark: Results After 1 Year of Follow-Up.
items.abstract: Essential tremor (ET) is the most common hyperkinetic movement disorder. Magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound thalamotomy (MRgFUSTh) has become an established therapy in drug-refractory tremor as one treatment option. Here, we present the results of a large cohort of MRgFUSTh-treated ET patients followed-up 1 year post-ablation. The primary endpoint durability of tremor reduction at 12 months at this timepoint. This was a single-hospital cohort study. Prior to, and 12 months after, treatment, patients were rated according to the Fahn-Tolosa-Marin (FTM) scale, Quality of Life in Essential Tremor (QUEST) scale, Patient Global Assessment of Change (PGIC), as well as general health, well-being, and factors relating to social and everyday activities. Finally, side effects and adverse event data were collected at 12 months. The current cohort comprised 111 patients. Patients showed good response to MRgFUSTh with a mean decrease of 29.5 points in the total FTM-score from pretreatment (95% CI: 26.3; 32.8, P < 0.0001) corresponding to 62.4% (95% CI: 56.4%; 68.5%). This meant a reduction in the FTM-score of 13.8 points (± 5.2 points, 95% CI: 12.79; 14.73, P < 0.00001) or 85.2% (±24.2%, 95% CI: 80.70%; 89.78%) in the treated limb. For QUEST, symptoms improved by 20.9 points (95% CI: 12.1; 29.6, P < 0.0001) corresponding to a relative improvement of 54% (95% CI: 33.2%; 75.5%). Results showed clear and persistent tremor improvements as assessed by both clinicians and patients. © 2026 The Author(s). items.title: Connexin and Pannexin Channels in Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury: Mechanisms of Secondary Injury and Therapeutic Opportunities.
items.abstract: Traumatic spinal cord injury (tSCI) causes immediate mechanical damage followed by a secondary cascade of excitotoxic, oxidative, metabolic, and inflammatory events that expands tissue loss. Connexin (Cx) and pannexin (Panx) channels are increasingly recognized as potential amplifiers of this secondary injury. This focused review summarizes the structural and biophysical properties of these channels that are relevant to the injured spinal cord, their cellular localization, and the experimental evidence linking Cx43 and Panx1 activity to ATP release, calcium dysregulation, neuroinflammation, tissue loss, neuropathic pain, and functional recovery after tSCI. We also review genetic and pharmacologic studies of channel inhibition and discuss the limited but emerging evidence for Cx-mediated signaling in paralyzed skeletal muscle. Evidence is strongest for astrocytic Cx43 hemichannels, whereas the contribution of Panx1 after tSCI remains promising but less completely defined. Throughout, we distinguish findings demonstrated directly after tSCI from mechanisms inferred from other tissues or disease models and identify priorities for translational research.

items.title: Repeated Head Impacts May Compromise White Matter Integrity and Bimanual Coordination in American Football Players.
items.abstract: Repeated head impacts (RHI) in American Football may contribute to subtle white matter (WM) abnormalities and functional deficits even in the absence of clinically diagnosed concussion. Contact athletes would demonstrate tract-specific differences in fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD) compared with noncontact controls, and high-exposure (HE) athletes would show greater within-season diffusion change, worse bimanual coordination, and greater symptom burden than low-exposure (LE) athletes. Prospective cohort study. Level 3. Twenty-two male varsity American Football players and 13 male noncontact controls underwent preseason diffusion tensor imaging. Football athletes were monitored over a single season using helmet-mounted accelerometers and stratified into HE and LE groups. Tract-specific FA and MD were derived using probabilistic tractography. Pre-post SCAT3 symptom and severity checklist data were collected from all football athletes, and pre-post Kinarm Ball-on-Bar (BOB) bimanual coordination data were available for 12 athletes. At preseason, contact athletes demonstrated higher FA in 15 of 16 tracts compared with noncontact controls, with lower FA in the forceps minor. MD was lower in 10 of 16 tracts, higher in the bilateral inferior longitudinal fasciculus, and similar in the corticospinal tract and superior thalamic radiation. Over the season, HE athletes sustained more impacts (P 0.99), and SCAT3 symptom and severity scores remained low with no meaningful between-group differences. In 22 contact athletes, repeated head-impact exposure was associated with preseason WM differences and worsening bimanual coordination across a single season, while longitudinal tract-level DTI and symptom-based clinical measures showed limited between-group change. Objective motor assessment and advanced neuroimaging may help characterize subtle consequences of RHIs that are missed by routine symptom-based tools.

items.title: Genome-wide association study of human papillomavirus infection and persistence in women living with HIV in Rwanda.
items.abstract: We conducted an explorative genome-wide association study (GWAS) in East Africa to identify host genetic variants associated with the acquisition and persistence of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. We genotyped 385 Rwandan women living with HIV and selected host biomarker assay signals from genital swab samples using qPCR. We compared women who cleared HPV over a two-year interval (operationally defined as persistent infection), with those who did not. Exploratory gene-based aggregation analyses of rare and low-frequency variants represented on the genotyping array were also performed. In the primary cluster-stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel analysis, rs13158830 within PPARGC1B exceeded the conventional genome-wide significance threshold for persistent HPV infection. The nearby MIR378A gene-expression assay signal was higher in HPV-positive women but did not distinguish clearance from persistence. We identified an exploratory host genetic association with persistent HPV infection and several additional candidate loci. The lead rs13158830 signal remained evident in Fisher exact testing and PC-adjusted Firth regression, but the small number of carriers produced substantial uncertainty. These findings require replication in independent cohorts. Not applicable.

items.title: Disease-modifying interventions in psychiatry.
items.abstract: Disease-modifying interventions do not just treat the symptoms of the disease but target the underlying disease process and natural course. The construct of disease-modifying treatments has transformed the care of disorders, like rheumatoid arthritis and multiple sclerosis, by shifting the focus to preventing end-organ damage rather than offering symptomatic treatment. As mental illness may have a chronic and progressive course, there is a need to consider whether any of our interventions may be disease-modifying. We, therefore, conducted a search using databases, including MEDLINE, EMBASE and PsycINFO, to identify peer-reviewed papers and grey literature related to the research question: 'Which psychiatric treatments are disease-modifying?' Disease-modifying properties were largely operationalised around end-organ changes, including structural brain changes evident on neuroimaging and cognition, and were reported for conventional psychotropics, as well as for novel pharmaceuticals and non-pharmacological interventions. Lithium and electroconvulsive therapy showed the greatest evidence as disease-modifying interventions. However, to establish this and identify potential other disease-modifying treatments, there needs to be a shift in the focus of psychiatric clinical trials to include primary outcomes that reflect disease progression and not just acute symptom burden. The potential disease-modifying properties of lithium and electroconvulsive therapy should spur the prioritisation of treatment higher up the algorithm, as well as the commencement of disease-modifying therapy as early as possible in the illness course to prevent adverse outcomes.

items.title: How well do dementia risk scores predict dementia? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: In our systematic review and meta-analysis, we aimed to assess the predictive accuracy and clinical applicability of ten dementia risk assessment scores for incident dementia in cohort studies. Three of 10 risk scores had sufficient, comparable data for a meta-analysis. We analyzed the Cardiovascular Risk Factors Ageing and Dementia (CAIDE), Lifestyle for brain health (LIBRA), and Alzheimer's Disease Risk Index (ANU-ADRI) in middle- and older-aged baseline populations with short, medium, and long follow-up durations, starting free from dementia, with or without other health conditions. A total of 29 studies met our inclusion criteria; 13 were included in the meta-analyses. CAIDE performed best, particularly among middle-aged participants at baseline, with longer follow-up periods, yielding pooled areas under the curves (AUCs) of 0.74-0.76. ANU-ADRI showed stable, moderate predictive accuracy with AUCs of approximately 0.65-0.71. The original LIBRA showed the lowest discrimination, with AUCs ranging from 0.51 to 0.60, whereas the modified LIBRA performed better, with AUCs of 0.65-0.67 at short follow-up and a pooled AUC of 0.70 (95% CI 0.66-0.74) at medium follow-up. Dementia risk assessment scales show variable predictive performance across scores, baseline age, and follow-up duration, and may be useful for dementia risk stratification in clinical practice. As a substantial proportion of dementia risk is linked to potentially modifiable factors, identifying high-risk individuals may help guide timely risk-reduction strategies. Further prospective validation is needed across different populations and clinical settings.

items.title: On the precision of timing during joint rushing.
items.abstract: When individuals synchronize their movements during joint actions, they systematically accelerate the prescribed tempo: the so-called joint rushing phenomenon. While research has focused on the resulting drift in accuracy, it remains unexplored whether interpersonal synchronization also affects precision of timing. Pooling together 110 participants from three independent finger-tapping experiments, this study addresses this gap by analyzing the Weber fraction, the standard deviation of the tapping errors relative to interval duration, by comparing Solo and Joint synchronization in sub-second durations. The results revealed that joint synchronization causes a dramatic, duration-scaled degradation of accuracy (rushing), yet imposes only a small, roughly duration-independent cost on precision, whose non-linear profile across durations was overall preserved in both conditions. This pattern suggests that interpersonal synchronization largely affects period correction while overall preserving phase correction, a distinction relevant to current theoretical models of temporal coordination in social behavior. items.title: Shared control-network recruitment and task-dependent brain-behavior associations in bilingual language and rule switching.
items.abstract: Bilingual language control is thought to draw on domain-general cognitive control, yet it remains unclear whether cross-task overlap in neural recruitment is accompanied by similar brain-behavior relationships. Previous connectivity studies have typically estimated functional connectivity (FC) across entire tasks or blocks, obscuring network changes specific to switch trials. We combined hierarchical drift-diffusion modeling, regional activation, and beta-series FC in 126 Chinese-English bilinguals (123 with usable fMRI data) who completed language- and rule-switching tasks. Both tasks reduced drift rates and prolonged nondecision times on switch trials. They also recruited a common 28-region switch-sensitive control core and showed increased switch-related FC within this core and between the core and default mode, subcortical, and cerebellar systems. At the individual-difference level, generalized estimating equations revealed task-dependent brain-behavior relationships: core-within and core-subcortical FC were more positively associated with drift-rate switch cost during language switching than during rule switching. Together, the results identify partial overlap in regional recruitment, similarly directed system-level FC changes, and distinct FC-evidence-accumulation relationships across tasks.

items.title: Microglial NUS1 deficiency drives dopaminergic neurodegeneration through intercellular iron dysregulation in Parkinson's disease models.
items.abstract: The selective loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta is a defining feature of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. NUS1, which encodes neurite outgrowth inhibitor-B receptor (NgBR), was recently identified as a PD risk gene. Here we show that NgBR is highly expressed in microglia, where its deficiency drives progressive PD-like motor deficits and dopaminergic neurodegeneration via the LCN2-SLC22A17 iron-transport axis in mice. NgBR deficiency in mouse and human microglia triggers endoplasmic reticulum stress and PERK-ATF4-NUPR1 signaling, which preferentially induces LCN2-mediated iron efflux over cytokine release. Subsequently, microglia-derived iron-loaded Holo-LCN2, but not iron-free Apo-LCN2, is internalized by SLC22A17, a receptor highly expressed in dopaminergic neurons, leading to iron overload and ferroptosis. Pharmacological inhibition of LCN2-SLC22A17 axis or ferroptosis alleviated dopaminergic neuron loss and PD-like symptoms caused by microglial NgBR deficiency in vitro and in vivo. Our findings identify disrupted intercellular iron homeostasis as a pathological driver of PD and highlight the LCN2-SLC22A17 axis as a potential therapeutic target.

items.title: Chronic progressive demyelination induces a microglial state with lysosomal dysfunction.
items.abstract: Dysfunctional immune responses impair remyelination and contribute to neurodegeneration. While immune and metabolic responses to acute myelin injury are well characterized, myeloid cell adaptations to chronic myelin damage remain poorly understood. Here we performed a comparative analysis of genetic and toxic mouse models of acute and chronic demyelination, which identified a distinct microglial state associated with chronic demyelination, characterized by sustained pro-inflammatory activation, lysosomal lipid sequestration and reduced lipid droplet formation. Transcriptomics profiling further revealed a metabolic program marked by upregulated cholesterol synthesis and diminished sterol efflux. Treatment with a desmosterol mimetic possessing 24-dehydrocholesterol reductase inhibitor activity reversed this microglial state, attenuated pro-inflammatory signaling (including C-C Motif Chemokine Ligand 4 expression), reduced myelin damage and improved motor performance in a mouse model of leukodystrophy. Our findings uncover a pro-inflammatory microglial state characterized by lysosomal dysfunction and increased myelin reactivity, highlighting a novel therapeutic target for chronic demyelinating disorders.

items.title: Use of animal models to understand CNS neuroimmunology - guidance from the International Society for Neuroimmunology White Paper Task Force.
items.abstract: Neuroimmunology is a rapidly expanding field in which many breakthroughs have been fuelled by studies in animal models that capture aspects of human neurological disease. However, the variety of animal models available, with their relative merits and drawbacks, is not well documented in the literature, posing a hurdle for scientists who are venturing into the world of neuroimmunology. Moreover, nuances between animal models, their utility for studying neuroimmunological processes and the variables that affect their associated clinical and pathological outcomes can affect the reproducibility and clinical relevance of findings at the preclinical stage. In this Review, the International Society of Neuroimmunology White Paper Task Force describes animal models that can be used to study neuroimmunological aspects of neurological disease and the intrinsic and extrinsic factors that affect readouts from these models. We provide guidance on how to manipulate these factors to gain insight into neuroimmunology and to control them for improved reproducibility. We also consider the advantages and limitations of available tools, including robust genetic systems, neuroimmunological imaging, functional readouts and omics-based cell profiling. Finally, we discuss how animal models have advanced drug development to treat neuroimmunological diseases and how the same principles can provide insight into a variety of neurological disorders. We aim to provide guidance on how to optimize the use of animal models to gain insight into neuroimmunological mechanisms and support the preclinical drug discovery pipeline.

items.title: Digital Health Interventions for Falls Prevention in Older People.
items.abstract: Implementation of falls prevention programs at scale remains challenging due to resource constraints, clinic dependency and inequitable access. We critically review digital health technologies and map these to the World Falls Guidelines (WFG) risk-stratified pathway, from risk screening to intervention delivery, appraising the evidence, clinical readiness and implementation challenges. Self-managed digital exercise programs have the strongest evidence base, with three trials demonstrating reductions in falls among community-living older people and economic data supporting cost-effectiveness in those with a history of falls. Other technologies demonstrate feasibility, but none has demonstrated falls reduction in adequately powered trials. Implementation evidence is emerging but concentrated in high-income, digitally literate populations. Mapped to the WFG pathway, digital exercise programs are ready for routine implementation; realising broader potential requires regulatory frameworks that set evidence standards for digital products, funding models that support digital care and sustained commitment to equitable access across the diversity of older people.

items.title: The intermediate hippocampus integrates shock-observation and spatial information during observational fear memory in male rats.
items.abstract: Learning where danger lurks by observing others requires linking another individual's distress to one's own representation of space. How the hippocampus implements this mapping is unknown. We recorded Neuropixels activity across the dorsal, intermediate and ventral hippocampus of male rats during contextual fear learning by observation, subsequent rest and recall. Observers showed increased immobility in the context where they had witnessed a conspecific receive footshocks, with substantial inter-individual variability. Pyramidal neurons were recruited by shock observation, with enriched shock-excited cells in the intermediate hippocampus. In the dorsal and intermediate hippocampus, shock-observation responses scaled with baseline place-field firing, revealing a gain-like conjunctive code between observed distress and observer's position. Following learning, shock-context spatial representations were selectively stabilized in the intermediate hippocampus, and post-learning sharp-wave ripples preferentially reactivated shock-context ensembles, especially in animals expressing contextual freezing. These findings identify candidate hippocampal mechanisms by which socially acquired threat information are mapped onto the observer's spatial representation and consolidated into memory.

items.title: Analytical Performance of the Sysmex XF-1600 Flow Cytometer in Routine Clinical Practice.
items.abstract: Flow cytometry systems are increasingly used for the identification and quantification of lymphocyte subpopulations, supporting the diagnosis and monitoring of hematological and immunological conditions. This study aimed to evaluate the analytical performance of the novel Sysmex XF-1600 flow cytometer for lymphocyte subpopulation quantification in peripheral blood, including precision, carryover, and agreement with established laboratory methods. Peripheral blood samples from routine clinical workload were analysed in the hematology laboratory. Analytical performance was assessed by evaluating precision (repeatability and reproducibility) and carryover. Absolute lymphocyte and leukocyte counts obtained using the XF-1600 automated sample preparation and volumetric counting system were compared with the Sysmex XN-series hematology analyser, while lymphocyte subset quantification was compared with the Navios flow cytometer (Beckman Coulter). The XF-1600 showed coefficients of variation below 6% for major lymphocyte populations, including CD3+, CD4+, CD8+, CD19+, and CD16+/CD56+ cells. No carryover was detected. Comparison with the Sysmex XN analyser showed strong correlation for leukocyte and lymphocyte counts (Spearman's ρ = 0.986 and 0.993, respectively). Comparison with the Navios flow cytometer demonstrated high correlation across lymphocyte subpopulations (Spearman's ρ > 0.9 for most parameters). Bland-Altman and Passing-Bablok analyses showed good agreement between methods, although some parameters were not fully interchangeable. The Sysmex XF-1600 flow cytometer demonstrated good analytical performance for lymphocyte subset quantification, with high precision and strong agreement with routinely used laboratory methods. The integration of automated sample preparation and volumetric counting may support standardization of immunophenotyping workflows in clinical laboratories.

items.title: Neurocognitive characteristics of perceptual feedback processing differ in autism.
items.abstract: Autistic individuals often show reduced adaptation to changing environmental demands, but the neurocognitive mechanisms underlying this difference remain unclear. We asked whether it may be explained by reduced sensitivity to external feedback and changes in task difficulty. Autistic and non-autistic adults of either sex, matched for cognitive ability, performed a pitch discrimination task in which their response was immediately followed by feedback. Accuracy was similar between the two groups, yet autistic participants exhibited a markedly reduced feedback-related negativity (FRN), an event-related EEG potential differentiating explicit negative versus positive feedback. They also showed weaker modulation of feedback-evoked EEG responses by perceptual difficulty. Lastly, they showed reduced trial-by-trial behavioral updating of perceptual bias following recent correct and easy trials. These effects were replicated in a follow-up experiment conducted 1-2 years later. When combined they classified autistic and non-autistic participants with about 80% accuracy. Together, our findings indicate that multiple processes for evaluating perceptual decisions and adjusting subsequent behavior differ in autism and likely contribute to slow updating in changing contexts.Significance Statement Autism is associated with reduced adaptation to changing environments in both behavior and neural signals, but the underlying neurocognitive mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we show that autistic individuals exhibit a reduced feedback-related negativity (FRN), an EEG component that is present when receiving negative instead of positive feedback. They also show weaker neural modulation by perceptual difficulty and reduced trial-by-trial behavioral updating of perceptual bias following recent correct and easy trials. These effects were replicated in a follow-up study. When combined, they classified autistic and non-autistic participants with high accuracy. These findings suggest that reduced flexibility in autism is associated with reduced processing of external feedback and task difficulty.

items.title: Emotional Content Enhances Attentional Tracking of Conversations through Context-Sensitive Modulation of Auditory-Language Networks.
items.abstract: Engagement in conversation often requires continuous monitoring of relevant speech in a continuously evolving auditory environment. Emotional salience of semantic content may influence this process, but its role in attentional tracking of continuous speech remains unclear. We address this question using an audiovisual "Cocktail-party" paradigm combined with source-localized magnetoencephalography and encoding-decoding analyses. Participants (18 female, 14 male) selectively attended to one dialogue while ignoring a concurrent distractor dialogue, with both emotional salience and semantic coherence of the conversations manipulated independently. Decoding analyses revealed that negatively valenced, high-arousal, and socially relevant semantic content strengthened neural speech tracking, but only for attended dialogues. This effect depended on semantic structure, emerging earlier in semantically coherent than incoherent dialogues. Encoding analyses further showed latency- and region-specific effects across temporal, parietal, and frontal cortical regions. Emotional salience and coherence jointly modulated mid-latency (100 - 250 ms) responses, whereas late-latency (270 - 450 ms) responses were driven primarily by emotional salience. These findings demonstrate that emotional meaning enhances neural prioritization of attended speech and semantic coherence shapes the temporal dynamics of this enhancement. Together, these results indicate context-sensitive emotional modulation of auditory-language processing during selective listening of continuous speech.Significance Statement Understanding how the brain prioritizes and selectively processes information in naturalistic, continuously evolving audiovisual scenes such as conversations is a central challenge in neuroscience. Here, we show that conversations conveying negatively valenced, high-arousal, and socially relevant content enhance neural tracking of attended speech in a noisy cocktail-party setting. This enhanced tracking depends on the semantic structure of the conversation, emerging earlier for coherent dialogues that are easy to follow. Furthermore, we show that emotional content strengthens mechanisms related to speech comprehension and sharpens segregation of relevant from irrelevant talk. These findings demonstrate that emotional meaning and semantic continuity jointly shape cortical processing of continuous speech, providing new insight into how the brain selects and processes meaningful information during a conversation.

items.title: Object detection through dynamic motor-sensory convergence in freely moving rats.
items.abstract: To detect objects in natural environments, animals must coordinate movement and sensation. This process unfolds dynamically, as perceivers actively shape sensory input through ongoing motor actions in a closed loop. In this study, we use precise tracking of behavioral kinematics to investigate the initial phase of object interaction, asking: what motor-sensory strategies support object detection during natural approach? Using high-speed videography and advanced tracking tools, we tracked whisker and head dynamics as male rats approached and contacted objects. We found that whisker-object interactions converged toward a distinct ratio between changes in whisker angle and curvature, denoted [Formula: see text] In a motor-sensory phase plane this ratio appears as a line, reflecting a regime in which small motor adjustments produce large curvature changes during contact. This motor-sensory ratio cannot stabilize during free-air whisking and thus can serve as a signature for object presence. Rats gradually converged toward this object-dependent mechanical signature across contacts, and proximity to [Formula: see text] predicted subsequent head movements and the termination of object approach. Convergence to [Formula: see text] was invariant to object shape and texture and to whisker's length. Moreover, touch-induced pumps both signaled and reinforced convergence. The results suggest that rats use successful convergence to this object-dependent motor-sensory contingency as a signature of object presence. Object detection thus emerges as a closed-loop dynamical process in which action, mechanics, and sensation jointly shape perceptual inference.Significance Statement How does a rat know it is touching an object with its moving whiskers? We trained freely moving rats to discriminate objects while tracking whisker kinematics at high resolution. We found that the detection phase involved whisker-object interactions that converged toward a distinct ratio between changes in whisker angle and curvature. This ratio can arise mechanically only when whiskers contact an external object, making its attainment a reliable indication of object presence. During object approach, rats steered their exploratory movements to seek this motor-sensory contingency, marking the transition to focused exploration or disengagement. These findings reveal a dynamical, closed-loop mechanism for object detection in freely moving rats.

items.title: Analysis of Muscle Fibre Orientation in the Human Medial and Lateral Pterygoid Muscles Using Diffusion Tensor Imaging: A Methodological Study.
items.abstract: Deep anatomical locations limit functional and morphological evaluation of the medial and lateral pterygoid muscles, which are vital for mandibular kinematics. The lateral pterygoid comprises superior and inferior heads with distinct anatomical and functional characteristics. Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) tractography non-invasively visualises in vivo muscle fibre orientation. This methodological study aimed to quantify 3D fibre orientation of the medial pterygoid and both lateral pterygoid heads using DTI tractography, comparing simulated mandibular rest and 25-mm open-mouth positions. Healthy males (28.4 ± 4.6 years) underwent cephalometric radiography and 3.0-T MRI. T1-weighted and DTI sequences were acquired at both mandibular positions. Target muscles were segmented. MRtrix3 tractograms were reconstructed (fibre orientation distribution [FOD] amplitude cutoffs: 0.02-0.10). Fibre orientations, quantified via vector projection onto coronal and sagittal planes, were statistically compared. Tractography successfully visualised fibre orientation; optimal FOD amplitude cutoffs varied among individuals and muscles. The medial pterygoid showed no significant changes. During mouth opening, seven participants exhibited marked fibre reorientation in the superior head and seven in the inferior head, although the direction and magnitude varied among participants. However, group-level analyses revealed no significant orientation differences for any muscle. DTI tractography enabled in vivo evaluation of medial and lateral pterygoid internal fibre architecture. Between simulated rest and 25-mm open-mouth positions, group-level differences were non-significant in either plane despite variable lateral pterygoid reorientation. Inter-individual variability and FOD cutoff dependence highlight the need for participant- and muscle-specific parameter adjustment. These findings provide a methodological basis for future DTI applications in temporomandibular disorders and masticatory dysfunction.

items.title: Associations between Simple and Complex Executive Function skills and adaptive function in a sample of 3-year-olds enriched for variation in autism and ADHD traits.
items.abstract: Adaptive Functioning-including communication, socialization, and daily living skills-predicts outcomes and quality of life for individuals who are autistic or have ADHD, yet its cognitive underpinnings in early development remain poorly understood. Executive Functions (EFs) are a plausible mechanism linking developmental level or IQ to Adaptive Functioning, but prior work in preschoolers has relied largely on parent-reported EF measures, which are vulnerable to shared method variance with parent-reported Adaptive Functioning. Here, we examine associations between performance-based EF and parent-reported Adaptive Functioning among 3-year-olds enriched for variation in autism and ADHD traits. One hundred and twenty-nine children (109 with a family history of autism and/or ADHD) completed six EF tasks, reduced through factor analysis to scores for Simple EF (pertaining to simple response inhibition, holding information in mind, and applying a rule) and Complex EF (involving complex response inhibition, shifting response in accordance with a new task set, and updating information). Adaptive Functioning was assessed using the Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales-Second Edition. Autism traits, ADHD traits and developmental level were measured using the SRS-2, CBCL-Preschool, and MSEL, respectively. Hierarchical regression models tested whether each EF index was positively associated with Adaptive Functioning, and whether these effects remained after controlling for developmental level, autism traits, and ADHD traits. Both Simple and Complex EF were positively associated with Adaptive Functioning (β = .293, .316). While associations between Simple EF and Adaptive Functioning were accounted for by general developmental level, Complex EF showed associations with Adaptive Functioning above and beyond developmental level, autism, and ADHD traits. EFs in general, and Complex EF in particular, represent a promising, developmentally-sensitive target for early support in the toddler or preschool years, which could positively impact the day-to-day functioning of children with a family history of autism/ADHD, or already showing elevated autism traits.

items.title: Individualized brain mapping for neurosurgical planning.
items.abstract: The need for personalised approaches in neurosurgery arises from marked variations in the distribution and performance of functional networks among individual brains. Functional MRI and diffusion tractography have been widely adopted for neurosurgical planning. However, the way in which neuroimaging results are used clinically remains largely qualitative. This review explores how personalised neurosurgical mapping can move toward quantitative, patient-specific predictions by adopting techniques from the field of neuroscience. Exciting potential comes from extending our largely static measures of network organisation with metrics probing the dynamic nature of information processing in the brain. Such multidimensional approaches show promise to capture aspects of complex behaviour relevant to everyday function beyond the mainstream focus on language and motor skills. Yet, translation of advanced approaches into the clinic faces many challenges. Progress will require validated metrics capturing individually-unique patient profiles, methods for robust multimodal integration, clinically usable analytical tools, and outcomes that better capture real-life performance. By combining spatial, structural and temporal features of brain networks, neuroimaging may evolve from a 'localisation' tool into a platform for personalised neurosurgical prediction, intervention and longitudinal care.

items.title: A Sensorimotor-Interoceptive Model for Sensory Phenomena in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: Neural and Computational Mechanisms.
items.abstract: Classical models of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) grounded in cognitive-affective processes do not fully account for sensory phenomena (SP), including bodily discomfort, incompleteness, and not-just-right experiences that often precede or accompany compulsive behavior. To address this gap, we propose a sensorimotor-interoceptive model for the sources, generation, and maintenance of SP and SP-driven compulsions in OCD. Specifically, the posterior insula may integrate external sensory signals with internal bodily signals within the perceptual module. These integrated signals are subsequently processed by the salience module centered on the anterior insula and anterior cingulate cortex, where heightened error monitoring may assign excessive salience to integrated signals and recruit the supplementary motor area and primary motor cortex to initiate corrective actions. Dysfunction of a cerebellum-centered forward system may then produce persistent mismatches between predicted and actual action outcomes, which are re-entered into the perceptual module and sustain a recurrent feedback loop. The framework therefore conceptualizes SP-driven compulsions as maladaptive attempts to resolve persistent sensory errors. Predictive coding and active inference provide a computational account of these processes. We underscore that this sensorimotor-interoceptive model, intended to complement existing models, provides an account of symptoms in which SP are prominent and may therefore contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of OCD.

items.title: Diaphragm reserve utilisation in motor neurone disease: a novel ultrasound-derived physiological index.
items.abstract: Respiratory involvement is a major determinant of prognosis in motor neurone disease (MND; or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis), yet conventional static respiratory measures provide limited information about how much available diaphragm thickening capacity is recruited during quiet breathing. We evaluated diaphragm reserve utilisation (RU), an ultrasound-derived ratio of tidal diaphragm thickening relative to maximal diaphragm thickening, as a novel physiological descriptor in MND. In a prospective observational study, 38 patients with MND and 20 healthy controls underwent right hemidiaphragm ultrasound to measure thickness at end-tidal expiration, peak tidal inspiration and peak maximal inspiration. Thickening fractions and RU were calculated. Between-group differences in diaphragm ultrasound indices were assessed. Secondary analyses examined relationships between RU, respiratory function and survival. Tidal diaphragm thickening fraction was similar between patients with MND and controls, whereas maximal thickening fraction was lower in MND, resulting in higher RU in MND than controls. This pattern indicates that patients with MND maintained tidal diaphragm thickening while using a greater proportion of their available maximal thickening capacity. Higher RU was also associated with shorter survival, supporting its potential physiological and clinical relevance. Diaphragm reserve utilisation describes the proportion of measured diaphragm thickening capacity recruited during tidal breathing. Patients with MND demonstrated preserved tidal thickening despite reduced maximal thickening capacity, resulting in higher RU than healthy controls. This supports RU as a novel physiological index of relative diaphragm thickening reserve utilisation. The relationship between RU and survival warrants validation in larger prospective cohorts.

items.title: Preoperative Plasma Metabolites Associated With Intracranial In-Stent Restenosis: A Matched Case-Control Discovery-Validation Study.
items.abstract: Intracranial in-stent restenosis (ISR) remains an important complication after intracranial stenting, and validated preoperative biomarkers for subsequent ISR are lacking. In this exploratory study, we aimed to characterize preoperative plasma metabolic profiles associated with subsequent intracranial ISR and to assess their discriminatory performance in the internal validation subset. We conducted a single-center, age- and sex-frequency-matched case-control study of 96 patients with ISR and 96 non-ISR controls selected from 285 eligible patients who underwent intracranial stenting. Untargeted LC-MS metabolomics was performed in a discovery subset (30 ISR and 30 non-ISR), followed by targeted UPLC-MS/MS quantification in the remaining non-overlapping subset (66 ISR and 66 non-ISR). All plasma samples were obtained before stent implantation. Untargeted profiling identified preoperative metabolic differences spanning amino acid/peptide, lipid/membrane, bile acid, and nucleotide/redox domains, with amino acid-related differences prominently represented. Targeted analysis showed lower citrulline, phenylalanine, glycine, isoleucine, glutamine, and valine and higher ornithine and cystine in ISR. Citrulline showed the strongest single-metabolite discrimination (AUC 0.860, 95% CI 0.794-0.926), whereas a citrulline-phenylalanine-ornithine panel achieved an AUC of 0.911 (95% CI 0.865-0.958) and a cross-validated AUC of 0.895. Several metabolites remained associated with ISR after adjustment for clinical covariates. Preoperative plasma metabolic profiles differed between patients who did and did not subsequently develop intracranial ISR. In the targeted stage, lower citrulline together with higher ornithine was the most prominent finding. These associations are hypothesis-generating, and the identified metabolites should be considered candidate biomarkers requiring independent prospective validation before clinical use.

items.title: Dynamic muscle proprioception impairment in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis revealed by tendon vibration.
items.abstract: While recent studies have drawn attention to the potential role of proprioceptive dysfunction in the development of AIS, its precise characterization remains incomplete. Most research has focused on static proprioception, revealing generally mild or inconsistent deficits. By contrast, dynamic muscle proprioception, particularly the ability to encode limb movement kinematics, remains largely unexplored. This study is the first to assess both static and dynamic muscle proprioception within the same body segment in severe AIS. Fifty-one AIS participants and 31 age-matched controls underwent proprioceptive assessment. Static proprioception was assessed using a knee joint position matching task, while dynamic muscle proprioception was evaluated through vibration-induced movement illusions applied to both legs. Leg movements were recorded with a 3D motion-capture system. Static position-matching performance did not differ between AIS participants and controls. By contrast, vibration-induced illusory movements revealed significant group differences: 27% of AIS participants failed to perceive movement illusions in at least one condition versus 5% of controls, and AIS participants reported reduced illusion amplitudes and velocities (p < 0.01) with moderate effect size (partial η2≈0.08). This impairment was most pronounced in single-curve AIS participants, who showed significantly lower illusion amplitudes and velocities than both controls (p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 0.43) and double-curve AIS (p < 0.05, Cohen's d = 0.28), whereas double-curve AIS did not differ from controls. These findings demonstrate a predominant impairment in Ia-mediated movement perception in severe AIS. The greater impairment observed in single-curve AIS indicates that muscle proprioceptive dysfunction may vary across clinical subtypes, supporting the existence of distinct sensory phenotypes in AIS.

items.title: Telmisartan attenuates gentamicin-induced ototoxicity and modulates oxidative stress and RhoA/ROCK-associated signaling in mice.
items.abstract: Gentamicin-induced ototoxicity involves oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and cochlear hair-cell injury. This study evaluated the protective effects of telmisartan and their association with RhoA/ROCK signaling in mice. Male C57BL/6J mice were assigned to normal control, gentamicin control, gentamicin plus fasudil (2 mg/kg), or gentamicin plus telmisartan (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg) groups (n = 10). Auditory function was assessed by auditory brainstem response, while locomotor and gait performance were evaluated using open-field and gait tests. Cochlear oxidative stress, inflammatory biomarkers, RhoA activation, ROCK1/2 mRNA expression, and ROCK-associated protein phosphorylation were assessed using colorimetric assays, ELISA, fluorescence imaging, qRT-PCR, and Western blotting. Hair-cell integrity was evaluated by MYO7A immunofluorescence, quantitative counting, and histopathology. Gentamicin elevated auditory thresholds, prolonged shock-avoidance response latencies, impaired locomotor and gait performance, increased intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, and reduced antioxidant defenses. It also increased iNOS, NF-κB, active RhoA, ROCK1/2 expression, and phosphorylation of ROCK-associated proteins while reducing MYO7A-positive hair-cell density. Fasudil and telmisartan attenuated these alterations, with higher telmisartan doses generally providing greater protection, although responses were not uniformly dose-dependent. Telmisartan also preserved sensory epithelial organization and cochlear hair-cell density. Telmisartan attenuated gentamicin-associated auditory and cochlear injury, with effects associated with reduced oxidative and inflammatory stress and modulation of RhoA/ROCK-related signaling. Further pathway-specific and clinically relevant studies are required.

items.title: Leveling biological Systems: Material organization and scaffolding scientific Advance.
items.abstract: While general calls for more theory in biology are on the rise, less attention has been paid to the practical usefulness of theorizing about biological phenomena. Furthermore, the increased interdisciplinarity needed to address complex biological problems introduces challenges into how we think about knowledge advancement. All too often, consensus for how to bring the resources of different disciplines together into ordered and coherent frameworks can remain elusive. Here, we address these issues as it especially concerns how we should think about the future of the life sciences. We turn to biological neuroscience as a case study, where recent and profound technological changes in this field bring these questions acutely into relief. We argue that conceptual reasoning, the scrutiny of concepts and their roles in structuring scientific endeavors, can enrich biological practice and help understand how new, locally stable knowledge is generated. The centerpiece of this discussion features a renewed look at the concept of levels of organization, a familiar concept in biology that is often assumed, but rarely developed in detail. We describe the roles of this concept in structuring practical scientific reasoning and as a source of 'stable variation' in characterizing and manipulating biological phenomena. Second, we propose supplementing our understanding of knowledge advancement by considering how we scaffold new achievements and insight from the present into the future. We suggest that the features of the levels concept allow accommodating variability and continuity across experimental reasoning in biology, serving as a scaffolding device for fields such as biological neuroscience.

items.title: Method for collecting cerebrospinal fluid from the cisterna magna of anesthetized mice and processing single-animal samples for proteomic analysis.
items.abstract: CSF proteomics in preclinical mouse models holds great potential for biomarker discovery and CNS disease characterization, but low sample volume and protein content limit the applicability of existing protocols. We describe a workflow for cisternal CSF collection and single-animal proteomic analysis in mice, combining: continuous subcutaneous ketamine/xylazine infusion for extended anaesthesia; semi-automated microinjector-based withdrawal at a constant aspiration rate; syringe preloading with protease inhibitors and cold storage to prevent degradation; and bead-based protein enrichment (ENRICH-iST, PreOmics) for dynamic range reduction without sample pooling. The procedure yields 20µl of CSF per animal and was validated in healthy mice and a DSS-induced colitis model, enabling identification and quantification of 502 proteins from single-animal samples. The coefficient of variation in quantified proteins was below 10%, demonstrating adequate reproducibility for comparative proteomic analyses. Bead-based enrichment provided higher protein recovery than immunodepletion without pooling, preserving inter-individual variability. Semi-automated withdrawal reduces operator-dependent variability compared to manual aspiration. The protocol relies exclusively on commercially available equipment, unlike methods requiring custom-built tools. This workflow enables reliable single-animal CSF proteomics in mice, including debilitated animals, applicable to both basic research and preclinical pharmacological settings. Reproducibility is supported by a step-by-step protocol and troubleshooting guide. The proteomics data have been deposited to the ProteomeXchange Consortium via the PRIDE repository (PXD058129) and are publicly available.

items.title: A lipid-related metabolic signature of the dietary index for gut microbiota predicts a lower risk of osteoarthritis.
items.abstract: To identify a metabolic signature linked to the dietary index for gut microbiota (DI-GM) and examine its association with the risk of osteoarthritis (OA), while accounting for genetic predispositions. We analyzed data from 97,569 UK Biobank participants. An elastic net regression model was used to derive a DI-GM-related metabolic signature from circulating metabolites. Cox proportional hazards models evaluated associations of the DI-GM and its metabolic signature with OA risk. A polygenic risk score (PRS) for OA was incorporated to examine joint associations and potential gene-environment interactions. Mediation and Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses were used to explore metabolic pathways potentially mediating the DI-GM-OA association. During a median follow-up of 11.6 years, 12,860 incident cases of all OA and 4,392 cases of knee OA were documented. Higher DI-GM was associated with lower risks of all OA (HR = 0.94, 95%CIs = 0.90-0.98) and knee OA (HR = 0.91, 95%CIs = 0.84-0.99). The DI-GM-related metabolic signature showed stronger inverse associations, with participants in the highest versus lowest tertile having substantially lower risks of all OA (HR = 0.77, 95%CIs = 0.73-0.80) and knee OA (HR = 0.66, 95%CIs = 0.61-0.72). These associations remained robust after mutual adjustment and were consistent across different levels of genetic susceptibility, with joint analyses suggesting that favorable metabolic profiles were associated with attenuated OA risk. Mediation analyses suggested a potential role for lipid-related metabolism in the DI-GM-OA association, with MR providing additional evidence for specific metabolic associations. We identified a robust DI-GM-related metabolic signature that was inversely associated with OA risk. Notably, favorable metabolic profiles were associated with attenuated OA risk among individuals with high genetic susceptibility.
