items.title: Citizen science data as a tool for monitoring moss diversity in Poland: potential and limitations.
items.abstract: In this study, the potential and limitations of iNaturalist for monitoring mosses in Poland (2019-2025) were assessed using 17,451 verified "Research Grade" records. Rarefaction enabled diversity pattern analysis while accounting for sampling effort differences. Observational activity peaked in early-spring (March) and autumn (October). Analysis revealed extreme asymmetry in research effort (Gusers = 0.89): the 12 most active users contributed 65.5% of national records, creating a "super-user effect." Rarefaction corrected this bias, identifying the Pomeranian Voivodeship as having the highest standardized diversity (Srar = 80.9). Citizen science effectively supports specific moss monitoring aspects. Observers documented 151 unique records of the alien moss Campylopus introflexus, representing over 60% of sites recorded during 30 years of traditional floristic research. Despite the "microscope barrier" restricting the database largely to visually identifiable bryophytes (e.g., reducing nearly the entire genus Hypnum to H. cupressiforme; Gtaxa = 0.76), iNaturalist serves as a crucial early-warning system. Ultimately, large-scale citizen scientists datasets provide valuable guidance for identifying priority areas for future bryological research.

items.title: Rethinking the Gut-Bone Axis: Diet, the Gut Ecosystem, and Skeletal Health.
items.abstract: Purpose of review The gut-bone field has expanded beyond its initial focus on the gut microbiota to include microbial metabolism, epithelial barrier integrity, immune and endocrine signaling, and host-microbial interactions. This review uses a functional gut ecosystem framework to integrate these mechanisms and examine how diet and other exposures influence skeletal health. Recent findings No consistent microbial signature of osteoporosis has emerged across populations or experimental models. Instead, recent studies indicate that skeletal responses are associated with functional outputs of the gut ecosystem, including nutrient bioavailability, microbial co-metabolic products, barrier integrity, and host sensing. Gut-derived signals may act directly on bone or be further processed by the host. Diverse interventions, including whole foods, probiotics, postbiotics, and targeted therapies, can converge on these functions. Bone responds to the integrated biological signals generated by the gut ecosystem rather than microbial composition alone. Defining these functions and individual responder phenotypes may provide new approaches for preserving skeletal health.

items.title: Inferring Struggle, Judging Strength: How Inferred Adversity and Sympathy Shape Competence Evaluations of Black Frontline Employees.
items.abstract: How do racial inferences shape third-party evaluations of employee competence? Across four experiments, White U.S. observers judged Black frontline employees as more competent than otherwise comparable White employees in service-failure encounters involving a Black customer. This pattern was consistent with a serial process in which employee race cued greater inferred adversity, which elicited sympathy, thereby elevating competence judgments. Study 1 established the competence difference and its association with lower negative word of mouth. Study 2 showed that behavioral awkwardness attenuated the difference. Study 3 supported the serial indirect pathway, and the supplementary pilot reproduced it without a service failure. Study 4 showed that structural-opportunity information increased inferred adversity for both employees and especially increased sympathy and competence judgments for the White employee, narrowing Black-White differences. The findings identify a context-dependent, normatively complex route through which presumed adversity can produce comparatively favorable yet racialized competence judgments.

items.title: South Australian psychiatrists' view of voluntary assisted dying: A qualitative content analysis.
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo explore the views of South Australian psychiatrists regarding rational suicide, their views and experiences of voluntary assisted dying (VAD) and their reported willingness in discussing end-of-life issues with patients and expressing their views regarding VAD with their colleagues.MethodAn online qualitative survey was designed, piloted and sent via email to all members of the Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists (RANZCP) in South Australia and responses were subject to qualitative content analysis.ResultsA range of views were identified, from agreement with the concept of rational suicide and support for VAD citing respect for autonomy and dignity, through to misunderstanding of the psychiatrist's role, ambivalence and a rejection of VAD, grounded in discomfort in assisting death. Not all those in support of the legislation were willing to be involved in the VAD process and some only wanted very limited involvement.ConclusionsThis study highlights that psychiatrists do not have equal understanding of South Australian VAD legislation. We recommend that a learning module for psychiatrists be designed and delivered by the RANZCP.

items.title: Is the Proust phenomenon fact or fiction? A systematic review and meta-analysis of odor-evoked autobiographical memory.
items.abstract: Odors are widely believed to be the most powerful trigger for autobiographical memory (AM). This meta-analysis provides the first comprehensive meta-analytic test of this claim, known as the Proust phenomenon. Eighteen experimental/quasi-experimental studies were included in this meta-analysis. Olfactory cueing was compared with a variety of cueing modalities, and seven key characteristics of evoked AMs (specificity, vividness, emotional intensity, pleasantness, rarity, evocativeness, and age of AMs) were assessed. Olfactory cues showed a greater effect (advantage) over other cue types for emotional intensity, pleasantness, evocativeness, and age of AMs. Sample size was negatively associated with effect sizes for emotional intensity, pleasantness, and rarity, although the overall effect for rarity was not significant. Higher proportions of females and more recent publication years were each associated with smaller effects for evocativeness and pleasantness, respectively. Subgroup analyses showed that the advantage of olfactory cues for emotional intensity was stronger in within-subject than between-subject designs. Moreover, their advantage in terms of pleasantness was greatest relative to label cues, followed by visual and auditory cues. Although olfactory cues showed an advantage for four characteristics of AMs, these results do not fully confirm the Proust phenomenon. Overall, these findings suggest that the olfactory advantage is selective rather than universal, and future studies should clarify the conditions under which it emerges.

items.title: Odour preferences of children and adults across four diverse cultures in Africa, Asia, Europe, and Oceania.
items.abstract: Odour perception plays a crucial role in various processes, yet the extent to which odour preferences are universal or shaped by cultural and ecological contexts remains debated. While some studies report substantial cross-cultural agreement in odour pleasantness, others highlight considerable variability. To address this question from a novel perspective, we collected data from 394 children and adults (aged 3-81) across four distinct cultures (Hadza, Pakistani, Dani, and Scottish). Participants rated the pleasantness and familiarity of 11 odours (Fish, Garlic, Butter, Ginger, Thyme, Cinnamon, Banana, Peach, Strawberry, Jasmine, Butanol). We observed both variability and agreement in odour pleasantness ratings across cultures, but overall, there was a similar level of agreement across age groups within each culture. Furthermore, the most pleasant odours (Jasmine, Strawberry, Peach) were rated more consistently across cultures than the most unpleasant ones (Fish, Garlic, Butter). Finally, familiarity was strongly and positively associated with pleasantness. These findings suggest that while some universal consensus in odour evaluation exists, ecological and cultural influences, as well as individual differences, may all play a substantial role in shaping olfactory perception.

items.title: Revisiting the interaction between word frequency and predictability in natural reading: Large-scale evidence based on large language models.
items.abstract: Word predictability-that is, the predictability of a word in a sentence based on the preceding context-reliably influences processing of that word. Prior research has consistently reported additive effects of word predictability and frequency, suggesting that contextual influence may operate independently of bottom-up lexical access. We leveraged an ensemble of large language models (LLMs) to derive predictability estimates across six natural reading eye-tracking datasets in English and Chinese. Across both languages, we found that the frequency effect was attenuated with increasing word probability yet remained significant under the high predictability conditions. These findings support the interactive processing account and Chinese Reading Model, which assume that top-down preactivation reduces the demand for bottom-up lexical access, but does not fully replace it. The findings are inconsistent with the independent relationship implemented in some other computational models of eye-movement control. However, such models could readily be extended to accommodate this interaction.

items.title: Large language models for computational social science.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are transforming computational social science. This Review examines how LLMs now serve four distinct research roles: subjects that simulate human behaviour, assistants that automate analysis, collaborators that generate hypotheses and evaluators that audit and improve research quality. We analyse recent advances across sociology, political science, psychology, anthropology, economics and related fields, revealing how LLMs accelerate discovery while creating new methodological paradigms. This transformation arrives as society itself becomes saturated with artificial intelligence agents-making LLMs both our research tools and authentic research subjects. Yet fundamental challenges persist. LLMs struggle with causal inference and raise urgent ethical concerns about privacy and misinformation, and their ability to reproduce social complexity remains uneven and unproven. We identify critical research directions for harnessing LLMs' potential while addressing their limitations. As artificial intelligence reshapes human society, understanding this transformation requires the very tools driving it-a recursive challenge that will define the future of social science.

items.title: Visual attention: Defining the origin of the current terms of engagement.
items.abstract: Our environment bombards the mind with far more visual information than can be processed. Because of this overload of information, our minds focus on only a subset of the visual inputs that land on our retinas. The visual attention mechanisms of the brain select which inputs we process to the level of awareness, store in memory, and act upon. Here I provide an overview of the topics, tasks, and methods that researchers have developed to study visual attention and conclude by discussing continuing controversies. Finally, weaknesses in our understanding of the brain's limited capacity ability to process visual information are identified as potential targets for future study.

items.title: Targeting central thalamus with transcranial ultrasound reduces arousal in healthy volunteers.
items.abstract: Using low-intensity focused transcranial ultrasound stimulation, we test the causal roles of the central thalamus in arousal and the pulvinar in visuospatial attention in the healthy human brain. In a within-subjects, counterbalanced design, 27 healthy volunteers (two females) complete a vigilance task (Psychomotor Vigilance Task) and a visuospatial attention task (Egly-Driver Task) before and after sham, central thalamic, and pulvinar sonication. Targeting the central thalamus slows responses and increases lapses in attention during the vigilance task, indicating reduced arousal. Pulvinar sonication reduces (and slows) responses to visual stimuli presented contralaterally, suggesting a disruption of contralateral visuospatial attention. These results provide causal evidence linking the pulvinar to visuospatial attention and the central thalamus to arousal in the healthy human brain and demonstrate that ultrasound can elicit distinct behavioral changes in healthy volunteers when delivered to close but functionally distinct thalamic regions, underscoring its potential as a tool for noninvasive brain mapping.

items.title: Biomimetic Nanoparticles With Overexpressed Adhesion Proteins for Targeted Delivery of Gambogic Acid in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
items.abstract: Cancer cell membrane coating offers a promising strategy for targeted drug delivery, yet its homotypic targeting mechanism and optimization remain insufficiently understood. This study identifies epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM), rather than Galectin-3, as the pivotal mediator of homologous uptake in hepatocellular carcinoma. Through genetic engineering, HepG2 cells overexpressing EpCAM are generated, and their membranes are used to coat gambogic acid-loaded PLGA nanoparticles. Cellular uptake assays reveal that EpCAM-enriched membranes significantly enhance nanoparticle internalization by homologous cancer cells via clathrin-mediated endocytosis, a process dependent on both clathrin heavy chain and light chain. In vivo biodistribution studies demonstrate that the EpCAM-engineered biomimetic platform markedly improves tumoral drug accumulation and retention, leading to potent antitumor efficacy through BAX/BCL-2-mediated apoptosis without inducing significant systemic toxicity. Mechanistically, this enhanced targeting is attributed to multivalent EpCAM-EpCAM interactions and the preservation of native membrane functionalities, including immune evasion and prolonged circulation. By elucidating the molecular machinery driving membrane-mediated homotypic recognition, this work establishes a rational basis for engineering cell membranes with overexpressed adhesion proteins, thereby enabling a novel and translatable strategy for precision chemotherapy delivery in hepatocellular carcinoma and potentially other epithelial tumors.

items.title: Exploring Genetic and Biological Interconnections Between Neuroticism, Psychological Distress, Insomnia, and C-Reactive Protein: Insights From the UK Biobank.
items.abstract: Psychobehavioral and physical health traits often co-occur. Although previous studies have identified associations between neuroticism, psychological distress, insomnia, and inflammatory biomarkers such as C-reactive protein (CRP), it remains unclear whether there is a genetic basis to these associations, and which biological pathways are involved. This study aimed to explore pleiotropy between psychobehavioural and physical traits and examine underlying biological pathways. To identify shared SNPs, we applied CPASSOC SHet and genomic SEM to GWAS summary statistics from the UK Biobank (Neale Lab; Nneuroticism = 293,006; Ndoctor visits for distress = 358,693; Ninsomnia = 360,738; NCRP = 358,693). Pathway enrichment analyses were done to explore relevant biological pathways based on positional and eQTL annotations. We used colocalization data to evaluate sharing of genetic signals between pairs of traits. Genetic correlations were moderate to high among neuroticism, distress visits, and insomnia, but low between CRP and each psychobehavioral trait. In the multitrait analyses, we did not observe any genomic region with genome-wide significant variants for all traits, although we identified a few regions with markers that reached genome-wide significance in the cross-trait analysis and had p-values < 0.001 for all traits. Enrichment analysis highlighted 8p23.1, a polymorphic inversion region enriched for immune and developmental genes. Colocalization supported multiple shared causal variants among psychobehavioral traits, with limited sharing with CRP. These findings suggest that co-occurrence between psychobehavioral and systemic inflammation traits is only weakly explained by shared common-variant genetics, emphasizing nongenetic mechanisms.

items.title: Are the Mental Health Concerns of Youth Presenting to an Emergency Department More Scute or Severe than Those Waiting for Outpatient Care?
items.abstract: BackgroundMental health patients presenting to the emergency department (ED) are potentially more unwell than those waiting for mental health services on outpatient waitlists. They often receive prioritized mental health follow up care, yet this practice may be unjustified if they do not have greater severity and acuity of mental illness.ObjectiveAdolescent mental health patients from an outpatient waitlist sample are compared to those who attended the ED to seek help but were not admitted to hospital.MethodAdolescents completed intake questionnaires at time of outpatient (regular or post ED) intake visit at a pediatric hospital in Canada. Statistical comparisons between the groups were completed on multiple measures of demographic and clinical features.ResultsThe ED group reported more substance use, higher psychiatric symptom severity scores for ODD, ADHD, and MDD, more recent self-harm, suicidal ideations and suicide attempts and lower general functioning. They also reported more ethnic diversity.ConclusionThe greatest differences were seen on measures of suicide risk acuity and substance use, which suggests outpatient interventions immanently focussed on these targets for ED attenders. Considering the high amount of suicide risk, despite lower acuity, in the outpatient wait list sample, future studies should investigate how to most equitably service these two populations.

items.title: Shared Understanding in Transition: Retired Athletes' Experiences of a Structured Peer-Support Programme.
items.abstract: Retirement from high performance sport can disrupt identity, relationships, daily structure and access to familiar sources of support. Although career assistance and professional services are important components of transition provision, less is known about how retired athletes experience facilitated peer-support programmes. This qualitative study examined how retired Australian Olympic and Paralympic athletes made sense of shared lived experience within the Retired Athlete Peer Support programme, particularly in relation to coping, belonging and social connection. Eight athletes representing six sports participated in semi-structured online interviews after completing six weekly 90-minute group sessions. Reflexive thematic analysis was guided by critical realism, moving between reported experience and plausible relational and organisational explanations. Six interrelated themes were generated: organisational transition rupture, validation as recognition, psychological safety, identity continuity and belonging, coping as recalibration, and restored relational agency. Organisational rupture, including abrupt career endings and limited follow-up, formed the context against which participants interpreted the programme. They attributed its value not to shared athlete status alone, but to experiential recognition interacting with facilitation, clear boundaries and cross-sport relational distance. Participants associated these conditions with greater willingness to disclose, normalisation of transition difficulties, reconsideration of earlier experiences, a reworked connection with athletic identity and greater choice in approaching future relationships. Readiness for peer support varied across stages of retirement. Structured peer support may therefore provide a relational component of integrated transition provision, complementing rather than replacing career assistance, professional wellbeing services or clinical care. Longitudinal and comparative research is needed to examine outcomes, timing and transferability.

items.title: Subacute administration of human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells is associated with neurobehavioral improvement, myeloid immune modulation, and altered HMGB1 dynamics after experimental ischemic stroke.
items.abstract: Cell therapy using human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hUCMSCs) is attracting attention as a promising treatment strategy for ischemic stroke. This study investigated the therapeutic effects and associated biological changes following hUCMSC administration during the subacute phase using a mouse model of permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). Based on our previous findings showing an increase in CD163-positive brain immune cells after hUCMSC administration, we hypothesized that subacute hUCMSC treatment would be associated with changes in myeloid immune responses and high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) dynamics. hUCMSCs were administered intravenously two weeks after MCAO induction. Ischemic brain and systemic immune responses were evaluated at the 3rd, 4th, and 5th weeks post-MCAO using flow cytometry, RT-qPCR, immunohistochemistry, terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick-end labeling (TUNEL), Evans Blue assay, Western blotting, and ELISA. Neurobehavioral outcomes were also assessed during the subacute and chronic phases after MCAO. Subacute hUCMSC administration was associated with improved neurobehavioral outcomes after ischemic stroke. Brain immune-cell analyses showed treatment-associated changes in CD163/CD204 co-expression and intracellular HMGB1 accumulation, while peripheral myeloid populations also exhibited changes in CD163 expression within Ly6C subsets. These findings indicate that neurobehavioral improvement following hUCMSC administration was accompanied by local and systemic myeloid immune changes and altered intracellular HMGB1 dynamics.

items.title: Associations Between Dietary Carotenoids and Cognitive Performance in Older Hispanic/Latino Adults are Stronger in Men and Smokers.
items.abstract: Dietary intake is associated with age-related cognitive decline and neurodegenerative disease. Carotenoids, fruit-and-vegetable-derived nutrients, support brain health through anti-oxidative and anti-inflammatory properties in non-Hispanic White samples. However, their relevance to ethnoracially diverse populations, including the rapidly growing and aging Hispanic/Latin American (H/L) population, remains unclear. We sought to elucidate the relationship between carotenoids, cognition, and inflammation in adult H/Ls. Cross-sectional data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey represented participants (Mage=67.5±5.9y) of Mexican American (n=2,078,580; 42% Spanish-preferring) and Other H/L heritage groups (n=2,244,252; 51% Spanish-preferring). Regression models adjusted for age, education, smoking status, BMI, acute inflammation, and total energy intake examined the relationship between carotenoid intakes (MTotal Carotenoid=9.47±9.05mg), and a cognitive composite score. Inverted mediation tested whether three systemic inflammation indices (i.e., systemic inflammation response index, SIRI; systemic immune-inflammation index, SII; and pan-immune-inflammation value, PIV) mediated these relationships. Regression results reflect sensitivity analyses that removed (n=61) extreme carotenoid intake values identified by Mahalanobis and Cook's distances. Regression models revealed that total carotenoids (β=0.26), α-carotene (β=0.22), β-cryptoxanthin (β=1.0), lutein+zeaxanthin (β=0.21), and lycopene (β=0.19) were significantly (all ps ≤ 0.04) associated with cognitive performance. Ethnicity/Language-stratified analyses demonstrated significant associations between total and individual carotenoids exclusively among English-preferring H/Ls. However, these associations did not remain significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction (all FDR-adjusted ps ≥ 0.09). Significant interactions suggested associations between a-carotene and cognitive performance differed by sex (χ2(1)=7.02; p=0.029) and smoking (χ2(1)=8.33; p =0.018). Post-hoc analyses revealed stronger effects for men (β=0.34) and smokers (β=1.64), respectively (all ps ≤ 0.001). Results did not support mediation effects of the systemic inflammation indices. Findings revealed nuanced associations between carotenoids and cognition among H/Ls, varying by sex and smoking. Future diet-brain health work should prioritize culturally-informed, community-based approaches to address disparities at the intersection of culture, cognition, aging, and diet.

items.title: Design priorities for clinical trials of immunotherapy in psychiatry: What, how, and for whom?
items.abstract: Decades of research into the immunology of depression is now translating into clinical trials, yet variability in study design, intervention target, and chosen endpoints limit comparability and slows translation into clinical practice. This Viewpoint outlines design priorities for immunotherapy trials in psychiatry, centred on a triad of considerations: the right target, the right patient, and the right outcome. Drawing upon findings from the latest clinical trials and existing literature, the novelty of this Viewpoint includes its emphasis on (i) target selection grounded on robust causal evidence from multi-method evidence triangulation; (ii) rigorous immune-based patient selection using repeat testing of blood biomarkers, such as C-reactive protein, to exclude transient immune activation, alongside inflammation-related clinical features; and (iii) prioritisation of clinically relevant and functionally meaningful outcomes that are mechanistically aligned with the target, alongside general severity scales. Together, these elements provide a pragmatic, mechanistically grounded approach to trial design. Strategic alignment across this triad will enhance precision, improve comparability and replication across studies, and accelerate translation of immunotherapy into clinical practice for patients with inflammation-linked depression and other psychiatric disorders.

items.title: Genetic and environmental predictors of seasonality and seasonal affective disorder in individuals with depression.
items.abstract: The etiology and nosological status of seasonal affective disorder (SAD) as a specifier of depressive episodes versus a transdiagnostic disorder are the subject of debate. In this study, we investigated the underlying etiology of SAD and dimensional seasonality by examining their association with latitude and genetic risk for a range of traits, and investigated gene-environment interactions. This study included 12,460 adults (76% female, aged 18-90) with a history of depression from the Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Regression models included predictors for latitude (distance from equator) and polygenic scores for eight traits; major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, anxiety disorders, chronotype, sleep duration, body mass index, vitamin D levels, and educational attainment. Outcomes were SAD status and general seasonality score. SAD was positively associated with latitude (OR[95%CI] = 1.05[1.03-1.06], padjusted < 0.001), and there was nominal evidence of additive and multiplicative interactions between chronotype genetic risk and latitude (OR = 0.99[0.99-0.99], padjusted = 0.381; OR = 0.98[0.97-0.99], padjusted = 0.489). General seasonality score was associated with latitude (IRR = 1.01[1.01-1.01], padjusted 0.001) and genetic risk for major depressive disorder (IRR =1.02[1.01-1.03], padjusted < 0.001), bipolar disorder (IRR = 1.02[1.01-1.03], padjusted = 0.001), anxiety disorders (IRR = 1.03[1.01-1.04], padjusted < 0.001), vitamin D levels (OR = 0.89[0.80-0.95], padjusted = 0.048), and educational attainment (IRR = 0.97[0.96-0.99], padjusted < 0.001). These findings enhance understanding of SAD etiology, highlighting contributions of psychiatric genetic risk and geographic measures on seasonal behavior, and support examining seasonality as a continuous dimension.

items.title: Environment-specific virtual head direction representation in the human anteroventral thalamus during memory-guided spatial orientation.
items.abstract: Knowing which way you are facing is essential for navigation. In animals, a dedicated set of neurons-head direction cells-acts as an internal compass: each cell fires most strongly when the animal faces a particular direction. The anterior thalamus is a key hub for this system. In humans, however, direct electrophysiological evidence for a comparable head direction signal remains limited. To address this gap, we recorded intracranial electroencephalography (EEG) from the anteroventral thalamus (AVT) in patients with epilepsy while they performed a virtual navigation task. We analyzed neural activity during in-place rotation to isolate virtual head direction (vHD) information. Using inverted encoding models applied to multi-band neural activity, we reconstructed continuous vHD within two distinct virtual environments. Critically, the decoders failed to generalize across environments, indicating that the AVT vHD representation is environment specific rather than a fixed, universal map. This encoding was observed in the AVT and was temporally specific to rotation epochs; no significant encoding was detected in the pulvinar, another thalamic subregion not part of the classic head direction network in rodents. Together, these findings suggest that the human AVT carries environment-specific vHD information, bridging a gap between animal models and human navigation and highlighting a potential link to spatial disorientation disorders.

items.title: Beyond Accumulation: The Intuitive Jump Model of Expert Decision Making in Sports.
items.abstract: We propose the intuitive jump model of expert sport decisions, a dual-pathway conceptual framework in which an evidence accumulation route operates alongside a rapid, threshold-based intuitive route. Two studies with elite basketball athletes tested the hypothesis that time pressure induces a qualitative pathway shift rather than merely a boundary collapse. Study 1 (N = 34) examined the model inputs, showing that trial-level cue informativeness (Csensory) from naturalistic videos reliably predicted faster correct responses, providing a behavioral proxy for accumulation efficiency. Using mid-range Csensory stimuli and a heuristic cue validity paradigm, Study 2 (N = 30) contrasted no time pressure versus time pressure conditions. Analyses using an adapted process dissociation procedure revealed a selective dissociation: Time pressure selectively reduced the evidence accumulation contribution (C), whereas the intuitive jump contribution (H) remained statistically invariant. This dissociation provides behavioral evidence for the intuitive jump model's jump mechanism and lays the behavioral groundwork for future mathematical formalizations.

items.title: Spatial aspects of felt presence and the phenomenon of childhood imaginary companions: Peripersonal space, embodied perspective, and continuity of agent propensity.
items.abstract: Felt presence (FP), the sense that another agent is nearby without corresponding sensory evidence, occurs across neurological, psychiatric and non-clinical populations. Prior work links childhood imaginary companions (ICs) to anomalous and presence-related experience; we asked whether this link carries the spatial and perspectival signature predicted by a bodily self-consciousness (BSC) account. In 185 adults without psychiatric or neurological diagnoses (45 with and 140 without a childhood IC history), IC-positive participants retrospectively reported their companion's location, distance and perspective, and all participants completed the Sensed Presence Questionnaire (SenPQ) and a dissociation questionnaire. IC-positive adults scored significantly higher on the SenPQ, supporting the continuity prediction, whereas dissociation scores did not differ significantly between groups. Of the IC-positive participants, 88.9% (40 of 45) recalled their companion from a body-referenced (first-person or mixed first- and third-person) perspective. This offers tentative support for the perspective prediction, because three of the four response options were body-referenced. In 66.7% (76 of 114) of distance estimates for directions in which the companion had appeared, participants placed it within 70 cm of the body, our operational boundary of peripersonal space (PPS). This proportion significantly exceeded one half, offering moderate support for the peripersonal prediction. Companions were most often localized in front of and beside the body, unlike adult FP, which is typically experienced behind or beside the body. The findings provide partial evidence that the IC-presence link reflects the mechanisms proposed by a BSC account.

items.title: Time to jump: Exploring the distribution of noise in evidence accumulation as a function of time pressure.
items.abstract: The diffusion model conceptualizes binary decisions as emerging from continuous evidence accumulation with Gaussian noise. The Lévy-flight model (LFM) extends this by allowing accumulation noise to follow a heavier-tailed distribution, enabling sudden, large jumps in evidence accumulation. The heavy-tailedness is governed by the stability parameter α, with smaller α-values indicating more frequent and larger jumps. We demonstrate through simulation that the LFM can generate near-symmetrical response time (RT) distributions typical under strict deadlines. In Study 1, we explored the influence of intense time pressure on α in a letter-number discrimination task, expecting higher time pressure to entail smaller α-values. Participants (N = 341) were assigned to an accuracy (unlimited RT), implicit deadline (feedback discouraging RTs over 500 ms), or explicit deadline condition (timeout at 500 ms). Given the LFM's intractable likelihood, we used BayesFlow, a framework for simulation-based inference with deep learning. Model comparisons consistently favored the LFM over diffusion model variants-even in the accuracy condition. Importantly, α-values decreased with increasing time pressure and were especially low in the explicit deadline condition, where RT distributions also approached symmetry. Estimating both the LFM and a structurally matched diffusion model, with and without timeout modeling, further showed that accounting for timeout-related RT truncation led to substantially lower diffusion model drift rates, whereas LFM drift rates changed only modestly. Study 2 (N = 160) replicated α's sensitivity to time pressure in a brightness discrimination task. Overall, α responded systematically to temporal constraints across both tasks and timeout modeling specifications.

items.title: Psychiatric disorders and access to assisted suicide: A comparative analysis of selected international experiences and medico-legal critical issues in the Italian context.
items.abstract: Assisted suicide in patients affected by mental disorders represents one of the most controversial issues in contemporary legal medicine, as it requires distinguishing between an autonomous, stable, and competent request for death and an expression of suffering potentially related to the psychiatric disorder itself. The aim of this narrative medico-legal review is to comparatively analyze the international regulation of medically assisted dying in the presence of psychological suffering, with particular attention to the concept of irremediability of mental suffering and to the limits imposed by the Italian legal system. A narrative review of the international medico-legal, bioethical, and legal literature was conducted, integrated with a comparative analysis of the main legislative, jurisprudential, and professional sources relating to assisted suicide and euthanasia in patients with psychiatric disorders. Jurisdictions were selected through purposive, information-oriented sampling to maximize contrast among permissive, autonomy-based, restrictive, and terminal-illness-based regulatory models. The analysis reveals marked international heterogeneity. The Netherlands and Belgium constitute the most developed models of access to medically assisted dying for psychiatric suffering, subject to rigorous procedures for assessing irremediability and decision-making capacity. Switzerland and Germany attribute comparatively greater weight to individual self-determination, although through different normative arrangements. Canada has suspended until 17 March 2027 the eligibility of mental illness as the sole underlying medical condition for medical assistance in dying. Conversely, the United States, Australia, and New Zealand substantially restrict access to patients affected by terminal conditions or diseases severely limiting survival. Despite procedural differences, the main element of divergence among legal systems concerns the definition of irremediable psychological suffering and the methods used to assess decision-making capacity. In the Italian context, Constitutional Court judgments no. 242/2019 and no. 135/2024 confirm that non-punishability of assistance in suicide requires the cumulative satisfaction of strict requirements, including an irreversible disease, suffering considered intolerable, full capacity for self-determination, and dependence on life-sustaining treatments, with verification by the National Health Service and involvement of the territorially competent ethics committee. Subsequent judgment no. 204/2025 further clarified that regional organizational measures cannot modify these substantive prerequisites. Psychiatric illness alone is therefore not currently sufficient to meet the requirements established by the Italian constitutional framework. The comparative analysis suggests that the fundamental medico-legal and ethical issue does not lie exclusively in ascertaining the applicant's autonomy, but rather in the absence of universally shared clinical criteria for defining the irremediability of mental suffering and distinguishing it from residual therapeutic potential. This uncertainty remains the principal limitation to extending medically assisted dying to psychiatric patients.

items.title: Poorer bereavement outcomes among companion animal owners are associated with unexpected death or describing the pet as a partner or soulmate.
items.abstract: To examine whether circumstances surrounding companion animal death and the owner-companion animal relationship were associated with bereavement outcomes. Cross-sectional survey data from 4,902 bereaved companion animal owners were analyzed. Multivariable regression models examined associations of cause of death, euthanasia, presence at death, and owner-reported relationship with the companion animal with grief severity, severe depression, anxiety/insomnia, social dysfunction, and somatic symptoms, adjusting for pet attachment and demographic and loss-related characteristics. Model sample sizes ranged from 4,099 to 4,758. Unexpected death, compared with natural or anticipated death, was associated with greater grief (unstandardized regression coefficient [B] = 2.49; 95% CI, 1.81 to 3.18), severe depression (B = 1.16; 95% CI, 0.59 to 1.73), anxiety/insomnia (B = 0.84; 95% CI, 0.32 to 1.35), social dysfunction (B = 0.97; 95% CI, 0.56 to 1.37), and somatic symptoms (B = 0.48; 95% CI, 0.02 to 0.94). Describing the companion animal as a partner or soulmate versus a best friend was also associated with poorer outcomes across all 5 domains (B = 0.60 to 1.26). Euthanasia was associated with lower grief (B = -0.95; 95% CI, -1.46 to -0.44) and depression (B = -0.76; 95% CI, -1.19 to -0.32). Presence at death was not associated with any outcome. Unexpected death and a partner/soulmate relationship were consistently associated with poorer bereavement outcomes. Veterinary practices should strive to ensure that owners experiencing an unexpected loss receive the same opportunities for follow-up and bereavement support as those whose companion animals undergo euthanasia.

items.title: Operative displacement and the psychology of smart product use.
items.abstract: As smart products gain autonomy, they increasingly perform tasks that consumers used to carry out themselves. This challenges foundational assumptions in consumer psychology that link psychological value to consumers' active participation in product use. This article introduces the concept of operative displacement, a consumption arrangement in which smart products perform the core tasks of product use while consumers move from operative agency (directly executing tasks) to meta-agency (configuring, supervising, evaluating, and selectively intervening). We outline three dimensions of operative displacement: process-outcome decoupling, effort conversion into supervisory load, and attentional recession and relational intensification, along with their psychological consequences and implications for future research.

items.title: Boredom Proneness and Attention-Related Experiences During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
items.abstract: During the SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) pandemic, measures intended to prevent the spread of the virus (e.g., social distancing) constrained individuals' range of available activities, potentially promoting increased engagement in certain attention-related behaviours. We explored this possibility by assessing whether, one year into the pandemic, participants perceived changes in their mind-wandering, dreaming and media use when comparing their experiences at the time of testing to their memory of these experiences before COVID-19 prevention measures were implemented. Given that boredom prone individuals often struggle to effectively engage their attention, we also investigated trait boredom proneness as a possible contributing factor to these perceived changes. Participants perceived increases in many aspects of their mind-wandering and dreaming (e.g., frequency, pandemic-related content) as well as several forms of media use (e.g., smartphone use, media multitasking during work-related tasks). Moreover, those higher in boredom proneness reported greater increases across many of these experiences. Our findings suggest that individuals' attention-related behaviours changed following the onset of the global crisis. They further suggest that adopting adaptive strategies for coping with boredom might have been effective in attenuating these perceived changes, and may be beneficial in the face of other major crises.

items.title: Young Adults' Conspiracy Beliefs, Fear, and Preventive Behaviors During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
items.abstract: This study investigated how COVID-19 conspiracy beliefs are linked with adoption of preventive behaviors over time, and whether fear of COVID-19 is a potential moderator for this relation. A sample of 424 young adults (89.2% females, Mage = 20.89) completed measures assessing COVID-19-related conspiracy beliefs and preventive behaviors during the second wave of the pandemic, at Time 1, and 352 returned six months later, at Time 2, and completed measures assessing their COVID-19 fear and preventive behaviors. Our findings indicated that higher levels of conspiracy beliefs predicted lower adoption of preventive behaviors over time. Participants who reported higher fear of COVID-19 adopted more preventive behaviors at Time 2. The link between conspiracy beliefs and adoption of preventive behaviors was moderated by COVID-19 fear. Participants who reported higher levels of conspiracy beliefs at Time 1 adopted fewer preventive behaviors at Time 2 only if they experienced lower or medium levels of COVID-19 fear, but not if they experienced high levels of fear. By contrast, participants who reported lower levels of conspiracy beliefs at Time 1 adopted more preventive behaviors at Time 2 regardless of their level of COVID-19 fear. Our findings highlight the importance of countering misinformation and relatively high levels of fear in supporting young adults' positive public attitudes towards protective measures during the pandemic.

items.title: Integrating Natural Language Processing in Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services Research Using Normalization Process Theory: Implementation Report.
items.abstract: Anxiety problems are prevalent among autistic children and adolescents and those with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Natural language processing (NLP) is increasingly used to structure information from electronic health records (EHRs), but its implementation within secure child and adolescent mental health services (CAMHS) research environments is less frequently reported. This study documented the specification, governance, integration, and evaluation of an NLP-enabled information extraction workflow within the Oxford Health National Health Service (NHS) Foundation Trust CAMHS research setting for extracting documented anxiety treatment information and outcome-related text from the EHRs of autistic young people and those with ADHD and examined implementation using normalization process theory (NPT). A multidisciplinary team developed a locally deployed NLP pipeline to identify labeled text spans describing presenting problems, medication attributes, psychological therapies, and treatment outcomes in pseudonymized EHR notes. Implementation followed an iterative seven-phase road map: (1) defining research questions, (2) identifying key constructs, (3) codeveloping an annotation schema, (4) training human annotators, (5) resolving annotation discrepancies, (6) large-scale annotation of EHR data, and (7) developing and evaluating the NLP model. NPT was applied throughout to guide implementation and evaluate progress. Quantitative outcomes (data volume processed, annotation reliability, and model performance) and qualitative feedback were collected to assess implementation success. The source cohort comprised 454,127 notes from 5906 patients; 697 (0.2%) randomly selected, manually annotated notes from 302 (5.1%) patients were used for model development and held-out evaluation. Category-specific position-based Krippendorff α values ranged from 0.325 to 0.579 for problem, psychological therapy, and outcome spans and from 0.665 to 0.967 for medication spans. Agreement was highest for medication names, doses, and frequencies and lowest for cognitive problems and treatment outcomes. Held-out macroaveraged F1-score was 0.87 (95% CI 0.86-0.89) across the 4 medication labels and 0.71 (95% CI 0.68-0.73) across the 5 problem labels, psychological therapy labels, and outcome labels; label-specific F1-score ranged from 0.60 to 0.98. Team-generated implementation records indicated that multidisciplinary schema development and clear protocols supported shared understanding and engagement, whereas annotation burden, documentation variability, data access delays, and computing constraints impeded implementation. No major adverse events or harms were reported. This report demonstrates the feasibility of integrating NLP tools into NHS CAMHS research workflows to extract structured information on anxiety treatments from routine clinical records. The NPT framework provided a structured approach for documenting the organizational work, barriers, and adaptations involved. External validation, refinement of less reliable labels, and further evaluation are required before broader use. RR2-10.31234/osf.io/r4gyw.

items.title: Designing fulfilling and productive workdays: Effects of task meaningfulness sequences on daily engagement and performance.
items.abstract: Given the importance of experiencing fulfilling and productive workdays, scholars have focused on ways to boost employees' daily engagement and performance, suggesting this may be accomplished by increasing meaningfulness of their work tasks. However, an alternative approach may be needed in multifaceted work contexts where employees need to complete sets of varied tasks each day, including tasks that lack meaningfulness. To address this issue, we integrate the workday design perspective with research on residual engagement to examine implications of strategically sequencing tasks in terms of their meaningfulness. We theorize that because of a process we refer to as engagement cascade, performing the day's most highly meaningful tasks earlier and in a concentrated manner will tend to produce higher levels of daily engagement relative to sequences in which the most highly meaningful tasks occur later or are disbursed. We use agent-based modeling to formalize the engagement cascade process and generate specific predictions regarding how daily engagement is impacted by different task meaningfulness sequences. Findings from an intensive longitudinal design study with National Aeronautics and Space Administration and Russian Space Agency crew members (Study 1), an experience sampling field experiment with full-time employees (Study 2), and two controlled laboratory experiments with undergraduates (Study 3 and Supplement to Study 3) provide support for our hypotheses. Specifically, the decreasing task meaningfulness sequence engendered higher levels of daily engagement and, in turn, daily performance, relative to the increasing, inverted U-shaped, and U-shaped sequences. items.title: Supporting fidelity of implementation: Evidence from pathways-to-success replications.
items.abstract: Research shows that when teachers implement Pathways-to-Success with fidelity, their students experience more identity-based motivation and hence better academic trajectories. Teachers receive implementation support. We asked if, with this support, first-time implementing teachers can attain fidelity across time, training, and variations in school contexts across four states, 10 years, and 8,456 students (N = 122 schools trained, 116 of these implemented Pathways-to-Success, n = 92 schools with video-based fidelity data). We review the implementation fidelity literature, distinguish fidelity from implementation support and institutional climate, operationalize our state-of-the-art fidelity assessment and the supports we provided, describe results, and implications for scaling. Results reveal first that, on average, first-time implementing teachers implemented with above-threshold fidelity. Second, across years, teachers engaged with training, preparation, and delivery aids despite planned variability in teacher-trainers and teacher-training method (in-person, virtual) and natural variation in school climate, urbanicity, classroom size, and student features (English learner, free or reduced-priced lunch, standardized test proficiency, racial-ethnic composition). Third, implementation support matters. Continuous fidelity evaluation makes dynamic investment in implementation support possible; implying that scaling and sustainability require ongoing rather than proof-of-concept initial fidelity assessment. At the same time, new tools are required to contain costs. We are exploring use of artificial intelligence-based fidelity coding to address this issue. items.title: How grandparental involvement predicts preschoolers' social development in Chinese families.
items.abstract: Grandparents play an important yet understudied role in early caregiving, particularly in Chinese families where grandparental involvement in childrearing is culturally normative. However, prior research has yielded inconsistent findings regarding the developmental effects of grandparental involvement, in part due to limited attention to the multidimensional nature of this concept. Drawing on four-wave longitudinal data from 129 Chinese families with preschoolers (Mage = 48.97 months, SDage = 6.00, 48.8% girls), the present study examined whether the quantity (i.e., frequency and breadth) and quality (i.e., grandparenting behaviors and intergenerational coparenting) of grandparental involvement predicted children's social development. Latent growth curve and structural equation modeling revealed that the quality of grandparental involvement was significantly associated with growth in children's social skills and problem behaviors. In contrast, quantity had no direct associations with child social outcomes but moderated the effects of quality: High-quality caregiving was more beneficial under conditions of lower frequency or broader grandparental engagement. These findings underscore the importance of distinguishing between structural and relational aspects of grandparental involvement and examining their interactive effects. Relevant interventions and policies should focus on promoting emotionally supportive grandparental practices and on designing culturally responsive programs that help families manage the complexities of frequent grandparental involvement. items.title: Family-based treatment for intergenerational diseases.
items.abstract: This article provides a brief overview of family-based treatment for intergenerational diseases. There is no organized protocol within current treatment approaches to address intergenerational diseases within a family. The optimal approach depends on the trajectory of the disease. For problems or diseases that may be present in both parent and offspring during childhood (e.g., obesity and substance use), treatment should target both generations simultaneously. When a disease emerges more slowly and is present only in the parent, as may occur with cancer, the optimal approach may combine treating the parent with prevention in the child. For diseases that develop in later adulthood, such as cognitive impairment, the goal may be to prevent or delay disease in both the parent and child by addressing modifiable health behaviors and risks. The type of treatment may vary by disease, but lifestyle and behavior change are central to preventing or treating many chronic intergenerational diseases. If the problem is due to unhealthy behavior, or the disease can be prevented by changing behavior, treatment should focus on education and behavior change. It is important to recognize that although education is an important first step for health behavior change, education is not always sufficient to improve health and evidence-based behavioral interventions may be needed to modify behavior and improve health. Although lifestyle should be considered as a first step to prevent many chronic diseases, some intergenerational diseases may require pharmacological or surgical interventions. Extensive research on family-based treatment for intergenerational obesity has shown both short- and long-term treatment effects for children and their parents, as well as spillover effects to untreated siblings. Given the rising prevalence of intergenerational chronic disease in the United States, care must shift from an individual-level model of care to coordinated family-based treatment for intergenerational disease within families. Psychologists can help lead this shift through their expertise in behavior change, family systems, intervention development, implementation, and policy. Without this change, the long-term impact on intergenerational disease will remain limited. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: Lewis R. Goldberg (1932-2026).
items.abstract: Lewis R. Goldberg, one of the most influential personality psychologists of the twentieth century, died in Friday Harbor, Washington, at age 94. Best known for advancing the Big Five model of personality and creating the open-source International Personality Item Pool (IPIP), Goldberg helped transform personality psychology by providing a common framework for understanding individual differences and by making research tools broadly accessible. Across a distinguished career at the University of Oregon and the Oregon Research Institute, he championed rigorous assessment, open data sharing, and collaborative science. His contributions earned him multiple lifetime achievement awards and leadership positions in major psychological associations. Remembered for his intellectual curiosity, candor, and outsized presence, Goldberg leaves a lasting legacy in both the science and practice of personality assessment. items.title: Social cognition and parenting among Black caregivers: Linking public regard to racial and emotion socialization.
items.abstract: Among Black families, cultural racism necessitates adaptations in emotion socialization to prepare children for navigating racialized environments. Black caregivers with high negative public regard, or the belief that others view Black Americans negatively, may engage in racial barrier socialization and discourage their children's expression of negative emotions. However, no studies have directly tested associations among negative public regard, racial barrier socialization, and emotion socialization practices. The present study employed a social-cognitive framework to examine direct and indirect associations between negative public regard, racial barrier socialization, and suppressive emotion socialization practices among Black caregivers. It was hypothesized that negative public regard would be associated with higher racial barrier socialization and, in turn, greater use of distress, minimizing, and punitive emotion socialization practices. Black caregivers (N = 100; Mage = 43.57 years, SD = 7.75; 91% female) completed self-report measures of racial identity, racial socialization, discrimination, and emotion socialization. Controlling for child sex, caregiver emotion dysregulation, and prior discrimination experiences, we found a significant indirect effect of negative public regard on minimizing (but not punitive nor distress) emotion socialization through racial barrier socialization. These findings incrementally advance extant literature, which contends that Black caregivers' racial barrier socialization and minimizing emotion socialization may operate in tandem to prepare Black youth for others' negative prejudicial beliefs and anti-Black racism in broader society. items.title: Bidirectional associations between parent-adolescent and peer conflict: The role of parent and adolescent emotions.
items.abstract: The present study examined bidirectional associations between parent-adolescent conflict and peer conflict and tested parent-adolescent emotion contagion as a dyadic mediating mechanism using a 14-day daily diary design with parent-adolescent dyads (N = 156; adolescent Mage = 14.66, SDage = 1.47; 58% female; 34.6% White/European American, 28.2% Hispanic/Latinx, 23.1% African American/Black, 11.5% Asian American, and 2.6% multiracial). Cross-lagged analyses found bidirectional associations between parent-adolescent and peer conflict. Greater parent-adolescent conflict predicted greater peer conflict the following day, and greater peer conflict similarly predicted greater parent-adolescent conflict the next day. Parent-adolescent conflict was also associated with increased adolescent negative emotion, which predicted higher parent negative emotion the following day; increased parent negative emotion, in turn, predicted greater subsequent parent-adolescent conflict. This indirect pathway did not extend to adolescents' peer conflict. Positive emotion did not mediate associations between family and peer conflict. These findings extend spillover-crossover theory by identifying adolescent-to-parent negative emotion contagion as a dyadic process that may sustain parent-adolescent conflict across days. The study suggests that emotion contagion is more evident within the family dyad than as a mechanism linking family and peer conflict. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: An attachment perspective on support and depressive symptoms in adult child-parent relationships.
items.abstract: The adult child-parent relationship is a mutual support resource that promotes well-being across generations. This study takes a dyadic attachment perspective to examine how providing two attachment-based support processes, secure base and safe haven, is associated with one's own and their partner's depressive symptoms in older parents and adult children. A total of 128 adult child-parent dyads (Mparents' age = 69.63; Mchildren's age = 42.02) were recruited. Structural equation modeling was used to assess actor and partner associations of attachment-based support with depressive symptoms. For both generations, secure base provision was associated with lower actor, but not partner, depressive symptoms. Children's safe haven provision was associated with higher depressive symptoms in parents. Moderation analyses indicated that the association between parents' secure base provision and their own depressive symptoms was stronger at lower levels of children's secure base provision. For safe haven support, children's provision was positively associated with their own depressive symptoms only when parents' safe haven provision was low. Secure base provision may help parents maintain role continuity and resilience, associated with lower depressive symptoms. For adult children, providing a secure base may support a balance between responding to parental needs and maintaining personal goals and is associated with lower depressive symptoms. However, high levels of parental safe haven provision may place pressure on children to reciprocate, contributing to higher depressive symptoms. items.title: Emotion regulation in couples' conflict memories: A dyadic examination of relationship quality.
items.abstract: Although conflicts in a romantic relationship are known to impact its quality, how individuals keep emotionally regulating the memory of these conflicts could also be associated with both partners' relationship quality. The present study investigated whether the emotion regulation strategies used during recall of a couple conflict memory were differentially associated with the perceived relationship quality of both partners. A total of 218 participants (109 couples) reported their general emotion regulation strategies and perception of relationship quality. Each participant subsequently described a specific conflict memory within the relationship, and judges independently rated the intensity of the reported conflict. Participants also reported the emotion regulation strategy they still used when recalling the conflict. Emotion regulation strategies involved either actively engaging with negative emotions, accepting them, and deriving meaning from the experience (i.e., integrative emotion regulation) or difficulty in adequately managing the negative emotions when recalling the conflict, leading to an overwhelming experience (i.e., dysregulation). A multilevel model revealed that integrative regulation during retrieval of conflict memories was positively associated with self-perceived relationship quality. In contrast, dysregulation during retrieval of conflict memories was negatively associated with both partners' perceived relationship quality. Importantly, these results remained significant even after accounting for how people generally regulate their emotions in daily life, as well as the intensity of the conflict. Our findings suggest that the emotion regulation used when retrieving a conflict memory may modulate each partner's perceived relationship quality. items.title: Power predicts declines in oppositional behavior over time in newlyweds.
items.abstract: In romantic relationships, people's goals will inevitably diverge from their partner's at times. When these conflicts arise, people often oppose their partner, such as by blaming their partner or making passive-aggressive comments. Given that opposition aims to influence a partner's attitudes or behavior, oppositional behavior is likely tied to people's sense of power in the relationship. However, past theory and research provide competing hypotheses about the nature of this association; specifically, there are reasons to expect that power could either increase or decrease opposition and/or opposition could either increase or decrease power. Further, previous research addressing this association has been cross-sectional, thus preventing conclusions about the temporal association between power and opposition in romantic relationships. A 2-year longitudinal study of newlyweds indicated that a person's feelings of power predicted declines in both their own and their partners' opposition, but a person's opposition did not predict changes in either their own or their partner's feelings of power. These findings lend support to theories of power in romantic relationships that posit that power decreases oppositional behavior. Moreover, they suggest that addressing either or both partners' feelings of power may be a fruitful avenue for reducing romantic couples' oppositional behavior during conflicts. items.title: Is hostility toward women a substantiated risk factor for sexual recidivism? A meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Hostility toward women (HTW; as part of hostile masculinity) is regarded as a risk factor for sexual offending behavior. However, its connection with sexual recidivism is largely unknown. The purpose of this preregistered meta-analytic review is to provide a synthesis of the state of the art on HTW as a risk factor for recidivism in adult male sexual offenders. We postulated that HTW would significantly increase the odds of sexual recidivism in male individuals with a history of sexual offenses. Inclusion criteria were (a) male individuals with a history of sexual offenses, (b) follow-up assessment of reconviction, and (c) assessment of HTW. Log odds ratio effect sizes were calculated and synthesized with a random-effects meta-analytic model. Based on 10 studies (nine unique samples, N = 7,437), we found that HTW significantly increases the odds of sexual recidivism but with only small magnitude (OR = 1.33, 95% confidence interval [1.01, 1.76], p = .046). Between-study heterogeneity was high and not reduced by controlling follow-up time, recidivism rates, or operationalization of HTW. Leave-one-out sensitivity analysis revealed effect significance was dependent on the inclusion of the complete set of eligible studies. Findings are ambivalent. Using a threshold of d > .15 (proposed in Mann et al., 2010), the observed effect size (OR = 1.33; d = .157) meets the suggested criterion marginally. Therefore, the OR should be interpreted cautiously with respect to the substantiation of HTW as a risk factor for sexual recidivism Further research should aim to increase statistical power, examine potential moderators such as antisociality and impulsivity, and encourage the development of more robust diagnostic measures and validated scales to improve the reliability with which HTW is assessed by practitioners in the field. items.title: Judge v. generative artificial intelligence v. hybrid: The public trusts and accepts human and hybrid more than generative-artificial-intelligence-based judicial decision-making.
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) could transform judicial decision-making by assisting or replacing judges. Prior research indicates that laypeople trust and accept human judges more than algorithmic judges. However, little is known about public perceptions of hybrid decision-making-human judges with GenAI support-which will represent the most realistic scenario in future judiciaries worldwide. Building on the organizational trust model, machine heuristic, and Capability-Personalization Framework, we investigated the effect of the type of decision-maker on perceived trustworthiness (ability, benevolence, and integrity) of the decision-maker and acceptance of judgments. We hypothesized higher ability, benevolence, and acceptance and lower integrity for human and hybrid judicial decision-making than for GenAI. Additionally, we postulated lower ability and acceptance for GenAI for emotional than for technical crimes. Across three preregistered online experiments with German adults (most identified as White) from convenience sampling and panel providers (PsyWeb, Prolific), we presented hypothetical crime cases, court proceedings, and judgments. We manipulated the type of decision-maker as between factor with four levels: (a) human judge, (b) hybrid with high human involvement, (c) hybrid with low human involvement, and (d) GenAI. Participants answered questionnaires assessing the decision-maker's trustworthiness and the acceptance of judgment. Results from Experiment 1 (N₁ = 323) demonstrated decreases in ability, benevolence, integrity, and acceptance with decreasing human involvement. Experiments 2 (N₂ = 674) and 3 (N₃ = 772) demonstrated similar trustworthiness and acceptance ratings for human and hybrid conditions, which were significantly higher than ratings for GenAI. GenAI was perceived as less able for emotional than for technical crimes (d = 0.58). Findings provide mixed evidence on the perception of hybrid judicial decision-making but support preferences for human judges. Overall, they warn of losses in trustworthiness and acceptance if GenAI replaced instead of supported judges but highlight the potential of hybrid judicial decision-making. items.title: Teleconsultation for Managing Physiological Risk Factors of Preventable Noncommunicable Diseases in Indonesian Adults: A Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) present a growing public health challenge in Indonesia, where rapid urbanization and suburban lifestyle shifts contribute significantly to morbidity and mortality. Indonesia's vast geography and limited specialized care impede traditional health care delivery. Teleconsultation offers a cost-effective solution to bridge these access gaps, though evidence-based, context-specific interventions remain urgently needed. This study evaluates the effectiveness of a teleconsultation intervention on key physiological NCD risk factors among suburban Indonesian adults. Primary outcomes include changes in blood pressure, fasting blood sugar, body weight, waist-to-hip ratio, total cholesterol, uric acid, and peripheral oxygen saturation. This parallel-group, open-label randomized controlled trial utilizes a 1:1 allocation ratio with blinded outcome assessors and data analysts. Recruitment occurred between February and July 2025. Baseline evaluations measured key physiological parameters alongside validated assessments of dietary intake, physical activity, and digital health literacy. Following a 1-week familiarization phase, participants completed a 10-week intervention delivered via WhatsApp and videoconferencing. Primary outcomes are evaluated at baseline, Week 10, and long-term follow-up. Quantitative data will be analyzed using an intention-to-treat framework with linear mixed-effects models or appropriate nonparametric alternatives. Semistructured interviews will capture qualitative implementation insights using reflexive thematic analysis. A total of 74 participants were recruited and randomized equally into intervention (n = 37) and control (n = 37) groups. Following baseline completion in July 2025, the 10-week intervention ran from August to November 2025, followed immediately by postintervention assessments. Long-term follow-up is scheduled for completion by September 2026. Inferential efficacy results are withheld in this protocol article. This protocol outlines a structured teleconsultation framework targeting preventable NCD risk factors in suburban Indonesian populations. It will provide essential evidence regarding implementation feasibility, acceptability, and potential effectiveness upon project completion.

items.title: Beyond Individual Responsibility: A Qualitative Study of Capability, Motivation, and Opportunity for Self-Management in Early-Onset Type 2 Diabetes.
items.abstract: The purpose of the study was to explore daily experiences of age-specific unmet needs among adults with early-onset type 2 diabetes across the care trajectory. A qualitative descriptive design was used. Participants were recruited from university-affiliated endocrinology clinics and online diabetes communities and via self-referral in Korea. Thirty-five adults (54.3% men) with early-onset type 2 diabetes were included. Interviews (40-90 minutes) were conducted between June 2023 and February 2024 in person (n = 12) or via video calls (n = 23). Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using qualitative content analysis with investigator triangulation. Findings were synthesized using the capability, opportunities, and motivation-behavior model. Capability developed cumulatively through repeated trial-and-error attempts and vicarious experiences, strengthening over time. Opportunity reflected a health care context characterized by early diabetes detection but less focus on prevention and follow-up treatment. Motivation, shaped by illness perceptions, health care provider support, and evolving self-identity, facilitated the link between capability and opportunity. This study identified age-specific educational and support needs among individuals with early-onset type 2 diabetes. Optimal care requires multifaceted strategies, including person-centered coaching, provider training, age-specific education content, supportive services and environments, and tailored public health messaging, to promote self-management. Interdisciplinary collaboration is essential for implementation.

items.title: Shifting the Smoking Cessation Landscape in Southeast Asia: Expert Perspectives and Recommendations.
items.abstract: Most Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) countries have ratified the World Health Organization Framework Convention on Tobacco Control and adopted MPOWER measures, but disparities persist regarding the help available to quit tobacco use, encompassing smoking cessation treatments, clinical practice guidelines, health care professional (HCP) training and policy implementation. This expert review evaluates the smoking cessation landscape across ASEAN, identifies barriers and proposes strategies to enhance cessation efforts. The ASEAN Advisory Board on Smoking Cessation, formed in 2023 with 9 experts from 7 countries, aimed to establish best practices and optimize pharmacological and behavioural interventions through a structured advisory board discussion. Two advisory board meetings in 2023 and 2024, supported by a targeted PubMed literature review, informed 12 recommendations to address gaps in pharmacotherapy access, behavioural support, HCP training and policy implementation. Key opportunities include standardized policies, advocating improved pharmacotherapy access, regulatory frameworks for each country and sharing HCP training resources and expertise. Areas of improvement for each country include integrating cessation services into primary care, expanding digital interventions and developing targeted strategies for high-risk populations, including pregnant women, adolescents and individuals with mental illnesses. Increased regional collaboration is vital for harmonizing policies, practices and HCP training, thus ensuring greater, more equitable access to evidence-based cessation support.

items.title: A Qualitative Study to Explore Delirium Management and Capability Building in Nurses Caring for Older Patients With Complex Care Needs in the Acute Hospital Setting.
items.abstract: Nurse-led strategies are important for preventing delirium and minimising its consequences when it occurs. Expertise in managing behavioural disturbances not only ensures safe care but also provides opportunities to mentor novice nurses. It is, however, important to know more about nurses' experiences caring for people with delirium to improve support for nurses caring for patients with complex care needs. To explore the experience of nursing patients with delirium in the acute hospital setting. Descriptive qualitative study. Nurses from two acute aged health wards in a Sydney metropolitan tertiary hospital participated in a semi-structured interview. Eleven interviews were recorded and transcribed verbatim. Data were qualitatively analysed by directed content analytical method using human factors principles as an interpretative lens. The interaction of multiple human factors was identified under the 'people', 'management' and 'workplace' framework. Participants identified barriers to delirium management, such as inadequate workforce capability and limited opportunities for novice nurses to develop expertise in delirium management, deficiencies in the environment and information technology and inflexible roles within the multidisciplinary team, leading to a high burden of care for nurses. Most had experienced difficulties delivering patient and family-centred care stemming from excessive workloads and a lack of structured mentorship. Our study identified substantial challenges faced by nurses caring for patients with delirium in the acute care setting. It also highlighted the complexity of delirium care and the importance of clinical expertise, skills development and the capacity for nurses to mentor other nurses. Healthcare organizations need to ensure that nurses with expertise in the care of older patients with complex care needs are available to provide comprehensive, patient- and family-centred care and provide mentorship and support to less experienced nurses. Interdisciplinary workforce capability building should be a priority. This study contributes to addressing the multidisciplinary management of patients with delirium in acute settings. The study found that delirium management is complex and requires a multidisciplinary workforce with knowledge, skills and adequate numbers. This research will have an impact on clinicians and health services managers in tailoring the care of patients and supporting the workforce. Adherence to the COREQ Checklist.
