items.title: Molecular Screening of Arthropod-Borne Pathogens in Domestic Cats from Northeast of Mexico: First Report of Infection and Coinfection in the Country.
items.abstract: Cat-associated pathogens transmitted by arthropods are of global public and veterinary health importance. Cats, as well as dogs, have historically coexisted with humans in rural and urban environments. However, studies on microorganisms associated with cats are much less extensive than those on dogs. Therefore, the present study aims to document natural infections of Anaplasma, Bartonella, Ehrlichia, and Rickettsia in cats (Felis catus) using PCR in northeastern Mexico. Blood samples were collected from cats with the support of the Canine and Feline Control Centers and veterinary clinics. Specific pathogens were amplified by PCR, and some positive samples were sequenced. A total of 250 cats were obtained from three municipalities in Nuevo Leon, Mexico. Specific PCR testing showed that 33.6% (84/250) cats tested positive for at least one of the pathogens. The overall natural pathogen infection rates were Ehrlichia with 20.8% (52/250), followed by Anaplasma with 8% (20/250), Bartonella with 3.2% (8/250), and Rickettsia with 1.6% (4/250). Phylogenetic analysis placed the Bartonella sequence within a well-supported B. quintana clade. The partial 16S rRNA sequence obtained from Ehrlichia was conservatively classified as Ehrlichia sp. closely related to E. chaffeensis. These findings document exposure or infection of cats with multiple arthropod-borne bacteria and support continued molecular surveillance using additional discriminatory loci.

items.title: Prolonged Sedentary Behavior and Cardiometabolic Risk in Older Women With and Without Type 2 Diabetes: The SitWise Study.
items.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) significantly increases cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk in women. Sedentary behavior (SB) may confer risks independent of physical activity. This study examined associations between SB accumulation patterns and cardiometabolic risk markers in older women with and without T2D. We hypothesized that prolonged sedentary bouts (≥60 minutes) would correlate with poorer risk profiles. We conducted a cross-sectional study of women aged 60-76 years of similar body mass index with (n = 9) and without (n = 11) uncomplicated T2D. Accelerometers assessed total SB and time in bouts ≥60 minutes. Risk markers included insulin sensitivity (Matsuda Index and glucose infusion rate [GIR]) and skeletal muscle microvascular function (near-infrared spectroscopy-derived oxygen saturation). Linear regression models adjusted for physical activity and T2D status. Each 1-hour increase in sedentary bouts ≥60 minutes corresponded weakly, though not statistically significantly, with decreased GIR (95% confidence interval [CI] [-1.24, 0.07], p = 0.08). Other associations differed by diabetes status: in women with T2D, the Matsuda index increased by 1.65 per hour of prolonged SB (95% CI: [0.45, 2.85], p = 0.02). Conversely, muscle oxygen saturation during exercise showed a T2D-specific decline; for every additional hour in ≥60-minutes bouts, oxygen saturation was lower by -0.74% (95% CI: [-1.25, -0.23], p = 0.02). Prolonged SB was associated with lower insulin sensitivity regardless of diabetes status and with impaired muscle oxygenation during exercise in women with T2D. Future research should determine if targeting SB accumulation patterns can reduce CVD risk in older adults with T2D.Sedentary Behavior in Older Women With and Without Type 2 Diabetes (SitWise); NCT04262128; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04262128.

items.title: Prognostic significance of nucleated red blood cells in trauma patients.
items.abstract: Nucleated red blood cells are early erythroid precursors typically confined to the bone marrow. Their appearance in peripheral blood reflects stress erythropoiesis and has been linked to hypoxia and systemic inflammation. While nucleated red blood cells have prognostic value in sepsis and critical illness, their significance in trauma remains poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of nucleated red blood cells during the first 10 days in the intensive care unit following severe trauma, and their association with 30-day mortality. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study including 1636 adult trauma patients admitted to the Reims Level-1 Trauma Center between January 2019 and March 2025, recorded in the TraumaBase© registry. Nucleated red blood cell counts were measured daily for the first 10 intensive care unit days. K-means clustering identified four nucleated red blood cell phenotypes based on temporal patterns. Outcomes included 10- and 30-day mortality, incidence of acute respiratory distress syndrome, septic shock, mechanical ventilation, and length of stay. Survival analyses used Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, Injury Severity Score, Simplified Acute Physiology Score II, and the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment, and propensity-weighted regression assessed dichotomised nucleated red blood cell status. Nucleated red blood cells were detected in 221 patients (13.5%). Phenotype classification revealed: transient early nucleated red blood cells (phenotype 1), single peak (phenotype 2), multiple intermittent peaks (phenotype 3), and persistent elevation (phenotype 4). Phenotype 2 was associated with reduced 10-day mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 0.06, 95% confidence intervals 0.01-0.46), while phenotype 4 exhibited markedly increased mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 9.6, 95% confidence intervals 2.23-41.4, P < 0.001). Nucleated red blood cell+ patients had higher risks of acute respiratory distress syndrome, septic shock, mechanical ventilation, and 30-day mortality. Kaplan-Meier curves confirmed significant differences in survival across phenotypes (log-rank P < 0.001). Nucleated red blood cell presence, particularly persistent elevation, identifies trauma patients at higher risk of adverse outcomes. Routine, daily nucleated red blood cell monitoring may serve as a simple, low-cost prognostic tool in intensive care unit trauma care. Prospective studies are needed to validate these findings and integrate nucleated red blood cell dynamics into risk stratification.

items.title: Validating Dental Sampling Frames in Rapidly Expanding Cities: Riyadh Case.
items.abstract: Rapid urbanization and the privatization of health markets frequently render administrative registries obsolete, threatening the validity of epidemiological research. Riyadh exemplifies this challenge, where expansion of dental services under Vision 2030 necessitates spatially verified sampling frames. Using Riyadh as a case study, this study aimed to develop and validate a spatially explicit sampling framework to support rigorous, representative facility-based research in fast-changing urban environments. We conducted a comprehensive cross-sectional field census (August 2023-October 2025) across 168 districts in Riyadh. Commercial streets (n = 2,669 segments) were identified using satellite imagery and municipal data. Seven 2-person teams, calibrated via a 2-phase pilot study, surveyed these segments to geolocate private health facilities. Specialized nondental centers (e.g., dialysis, labs) were excluded. To estimate coverage, a quality control team resurveyed a stratified random sample of 10% of street segments by district. After fieldwork, we contacted a random sample of 100 facilities to validate operational status, dental service provision, and coordinates and calculated accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. True counts were estimated using the Rogan-Gladen estimator to correct for misclassification bias. Spatial analyses mapped facility density (per 10,000 population using the 2022 census) and regional differences. Field enumeration identified 876 eligible private facilities, with data collector coverage estimated at 92.2%. Validation confirmed 98% inclusion accuracy. Sensitivity for dental service provision was 96.2%, and specificity was 61.1%. Spatial precision was high, with 97.9% of coordinates validated within 100 meters. Spatial analysis revealed marked clustering of clinics in central and eastern districts, with lower density in southern and western regions. This study established a rigorously validated, comprehensive sampling frame that overcomes limitations of administrative data. It supports representative facility-based research, which reaches only those who attend and complements population-based designs, and documents marked geographic differences in dental care availability that persist when public facilities are included.Knowledge Transfer Statement:This validated spatial framework shows policymakers and planners where private dental facilities are, and are not, located relative to the resident population. That is a measure of horizontal equity in geographic availability only, and the gaps it reveals persist when public facilities are included. Closing them is necessary but not sufficient: improving oral health also depends on affordability, perceived need, and the acceptability of care and on allocating resources according to need.

items.title: Presumed myofibroblastic hepatic sarcoma associated with a retained surgical swab in a 3.5-year-old dog.
items.abstract: A 3.5-y-old spayed female Labrador Retriever was presented with inappetence, weakness, vomiting, and a tense abdomen. Via abdominal ultrasonography, radiography, and diagnostic laparotomy, we identified a hepatic mass. Thereafter, we performed a lobectomy and sent the resected specimen for histologic examination. The dog was euthanized given the lack of clinical improvement and the formation of an intrathoracic soft-tissue mass identified with radiography. Histologically, the thoracic mass was an infiltrative, highly cellular mesenchymal neoplasm. Its spindle cells were arranged in interwoven fascicles and bundles with marked anisocytosis, anisokaryosis, and nuclear atypia, and a high mitotic count. The tumor tissue surrounded large necrotic areas with numerous cotton fibers originating from a retained surgical swab, which had elicited a marked granulomatous inflammatory response. The neoplastic cells uniformly expressed strong cytoplasmic vimentin immunolabeling. Approximately 50% of the neoplastic cells had strong cytoplasmic "tram-track" α-SMA and moderate cytoplasmic calponin immunolabeling. Tumor cells did not have desmin, S100, CD31, factor VIII-related antigen (von Willebrand factor), HepPar1, or IBA1 immunolabeling. The microscopic and immunohistochemical features were consistent with a soft-tissue sarcoma, most likely a myofibroblastic sarcoma. Hepatic myofibroblastic sarcoma related to retained surgical swab has not been reported previously in dogs, to our knowledge, nor has the use of HepPar1 immunohistochemistry to investigate the possible hepatocellular origin of the tumor.

items.title: Organisational Conditions for Healthcare Workers' Wellbeing: The Roles of Leadership, Social Climate and Psychosocial Safety Climate.
items.abstract: To assess a comprehensive model linking servant leadership, health-promoting leadership, workplace social climate, psychosocial safety climate, work conditions and healthcare workers' wellbeing. A cross-sectional survey design. A total of 1563 healthcare workers completed a survey between 2024 and 2025. Structural equation modelling was employed to test the hypothesised relationships. Servant leadership, health-promoting leadership and workplace social climate were positively associated with healthcare workers' perceptions of psychosocial safety climate. Higher levels of psychosocial safety climate were linked to lower cognitive job demands and greater job resources, including job control, supervisor support and colleague support. These work conditions were associated with lower psychological strain and turnover intention, as well as higher job satisfaction and work engagement. Unexpectedly, cognitive job demands were positively related to work engagement, suggesting that cognitively challenging work may be perceived as meaningful and motivating in healthcare settings. Supportive leadership and a positive workplace social climate are important correlates of psychosocial safety climate, which was associated with healthier work conditions and better wellbeing among healthcare workers. In addition, the findings suggest that certain job demands may play a motivational as well as a straining role in healthcare contexts. Strengthening leadership practices and cultivating a supportive workplace social climate help healthcare organisations foster psychosocial safety climate and improve work conditions for healthcare workers. Enhancing these conditions supports healthcare workers' wellbeing and is associated with more sustainable healthcare workplaces. The STROBE checklist. No patient or public contribution.

items.title: Melatonin Mitigates Doxorubicin-Induced Cardiotoxicity by Targeting the USP18/PKM2 Axis Without Compromising Antitumor Efficacy.
items.abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) remains a widely used chemotherapeutic drug, yet its clinical value is constrained by pronounced cardiotoxicity. Although melatonin is known to protect the heart, how it counters DOX-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC), and whether it interferes with chemotherapy, remains unclear. Here we set out to define how melatonin protects the heart during DOX treatment and to test whether this protection holds in tumor-bearing animals. We used acute and chronic DIC mouse models together with a syngeneic melanoma-bearing model, and combined transcriptomic profiling, pharmacological intervention, cardiomyocyte-specific USP18 overexpression and knockout, co-immunoprecipitation, mass spectrometry, ubiquitination assays, and PKM2 inhibitor treatment. Melatonin markedly improved cardiac function, an effect exerted mainly via the MT1/2 receptors. Mechanistically, DOX activated STAT1, which in turn drove myocardial USP18 upregulation. USP18 bound PKM2 and stabilized it through removing K33-linked ubiquitin chains while favoring K27-linked ubiquitination-thereby aggravating cardiac injury. Overexpressing USP18 specifically in cardiomyocytes worsened DIC and abolished the protection conferred by melatonin, whereas deleting USP18 or inhibiting PKM2 reproduced melatonin's benefits. Notably, in bearing melanoma or lymphoma, melatonin relieved DIC without weakening the antitumor activity of DOX. Together, these findings define a previously unrecognized cardioprotective pathway and provide preclinical support for melatonin as a safe adjunct therapy in cardio-oncology.

items.title: Anatomy Museum: An educational resource for community anatomy education.
items.abstract: University Community Outreach Programs play an important role in the education of Health Sciences students by providing experiences that extend beyond traditional classroom learning and strengthen the integration between teaching, research, and social engagement. The Anatomy Outreach Program "Anatomy Museum: a journey towards knowledge of the human body and awareness and preservation of animal life" is an educational initiative designed to promote scientific learning and socio-environmental awareness through the integration of human anatomy, public health, and wildlife conservation themes. The program is structured around guided visits, interactive exhibitions, and experiential educational activities using anatomical specimens. These activities provide opportunities for participants to engage with anatomical concepts while exploring broader discussions related to human health, preventive behaviors, and environmental preservation. Topics addressed during the program include human body systems, the systemic effects of tobacco and alcohol use, and environmental issues associated with wildlife conservation and human impacts on biodiversity. Through a multidisciplinary and dialogical approach, the program encourages reflection on the relationship between scientific knowledge, individual behavior, and social and environmental responsibility. Educational strategies emphasize accessibility and communication with diverse audiences, fostering engagement between academic knowledge and community experience. The Anatomy Outreach Program highlights the role of university-based outreach initiatives as educational spaces that integrate anatomical sciences with public health and environmental awareness, contributing to science communication, community engagement, and socially responsible education.

items.title: Prognostic Impact of FLT3-ITD Allelic Ratio in AML Patients Treated With High-Dose Anthracycline and a FLT3 Inhibitor.
items.abstract: The prognostic value of FLT3 internal tandem duplication (FLT3-ITD) in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) has traditionally been stratified according to the ITD/wild-type allelic ratio (AR) and NPM1 co-mutation status. We evaluated the prognostic impact of FLT3-ITD AR in 459 newly diagnosed AML patients younger than 60 years enrolled in the prospective BIG-1 study, all treated with high-dose anthracycline-based induction. From 2018 onward, midostaurin was added for FLT3-mutated cases. AR was not associated with composite complete remission (81.7% vs. 79.6% in low vs. high AR, p = 0.85), overall survival (OS) (median 7.6 vs. 6.9 years, p = 0.25), relapse-free survival (median 2.0 vs. 1.7 years, p = 0.50), or event-free survival (median 1.4 vs. 1.2 years, p = 0.58). In multivariable analyses, only midostaurin exposure (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.69, 95% CI 0.50-0.95, p = 0.024) and adverse ELN-2022 risk (aHR 1.66, 95% CI 1.18-2.34, p = 0.004) were independently associated with OS. Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation was associated with improved relapse-free (aHR 0.40, 95% CI 0.29-0.55, p < 0.001) and event-free survival (aHR 0.37, 95% CI 0.27-0.51, p < 0.001), but not OS. These results indicate that FLT3-ITD AR has no independent prognostic impact in younger AML patients treated with intensive anthracycline-based chemotherapy and midostaurin in contemporary clinical practice.

items.title: Evidence Synthesis on Fluoride Use in Traditional Communities and Indigenous Populations: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: To synthesize the evidence on the use of fluoride in the prevention of dental caries among Indigenous populations and traditional communities through a systematic literature review. An electronic search was conducted in the PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Latin American and Caribbean Health Sciences Literature (LILACS) databases. The inclusion criteria were experimental studies comparing the effects of fluoride-based interventions on dental caries prevention with no intervention or with other forms of treatment. Publications up to June 30, 2026 were included. Publications in Portuguese, English, and Spanish were included. No restrictions were applied regarding publication date, country, or any other filters. The methodological quality and risk of bias of the included studies were assessed using tools by the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI). No reports involving traditional communities were identified. Eleven articles met the inclusion criteria; all involved Indigenous populations and the use of fluoride varnish (FV). One report performed a comparison between Indigenous and non-Indigenous populations. Interventions included FV with fissure sealant and povidone-iodine, counselling of parents and family groups, community health promotion, provision of dental care to mothers during pregnancy, and implementation of motivational interviewing. Overall, the study findings suggest that the preventive effect of FV may be greater when applied on the sound surface as soon as the tooth emerges after 6 months of age. Two studies showed a low risk of bias. The semiannual application of FV associated with educational guidance prevents dental caries and the certainty of the evidence was moderate to high. Other preventive strategies such as fluoride sealants and povidone-iodine contributed to the effectiveness of caries prevention in Indigenous children. Studies on fluoride use among traditional communities and adolescents, adults, and older adults from Indigenous populations are needed.

items.title: Anemia and high-output cardiac hypertrophy in Tanzania and Haiti: a cross-sectional analysis.
items.abstract: Low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) face a growing burden of cardiovascular disease (CVD) that is not fully explained by traditional risk factors like hypertension. Anemia is highly prevalent in LMICs and may be an important non-traditional CVD risk factor. We evaluated the association between anemia and preclinical CVD, including left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) and other echocardiographic measures, in two diverse LMIC settings. This was a cross-sectional analysis of data from two separate cohorts of adults in Mwanza, Tanzania (n = 999; data collected 2022-2023) and Port-au-Prince, Haiti (n = 3,005; data collected 2019-2021). Participants underwent clinical examinations, laboratory testing, and echocardiography. Models assessing the relationship between anemia and echocardiographic outcomes were adjusted for age, sex, HIV status, blood pressure, and body mass index. Anemia prevalence was 23% in Tanzania and 32% in Haiti. Despite lower blood pressure and BMI among anemic participants, moderate/severe anemia were strongly associated with higher LVMI and LVH in both cohorts. In combined analyses, moderate/severe anemia were associated with LVMI increases of 8.4 g/m² and 29.7 g/m², respectively. Anemia was also associated with echocardiographic changes characteristic of a high-output cardiac state, including increased cardiac and stroke volume indices. Moderate/severe anemia was associated with18.2% of LVH cases in Tanzania and 9.1% in Haiti, and 34.4% among people with HIV. Anemia was independently associated with high-output cardiac hypertrophy in two distinct LMIC populations, underscoring anemia as a potentially modifiable CVD risk factor. Enhanced anemia screening and management could serve as a vital strategy to mitigate the rising burden of CVD in these regions.

items.title: Comparative characterization of OncoPro™ and Wnt-based media reveals distinct phenotypic and pharmacologic states in patient-derived tumor organoids.
items.abstract: Patient-derived tumor organoids (PDTOs) are strongly influenced by culture medium. We compared OncoPro™ (OP) Tumoroid Culture medium with conventional Wnt/R-spondin/noggin (Wnt) medium. This recently developed OP medium offers a standardized, serum-free alternative to Wnt-based formulations. We compared OP and Wnt media across 36 PDTO lines from various malignancies (colorectal, pancreatic, breast, lung, gastric, gastroesophageal junction, biliary head and neck and unknown primary), assessing establishment success. Selected PDTO models were subjected to downstream characterization, including morphological assessment and bulk transcriptomic profiling with comparison to public single-cell RNA sequencing reference datasets (n = 11), whole-exome sequencing (WES) (n = 9), and pharmacological response profiling to a 33-drug panel (n = 3). Adaptation from Wnt medium to OP succeeded in 83.3% (15/18), whereas de novo establishment favored Wnt (33.3% vs 11.1%). Key oncogenic driver alterations were retained across matched organoid cultures, supporting preservation of tumor-relevant genomic features. Transcriptomic profiling confirmed preserved tumor-identity across media, while revealing different epithelial state programs: Wnt upregulated proliferation/stemness-associated genes (e.g. LGR5) and OP enriched adhesion-associated genes and inflammatory/TGF-β programs. In scRNA databases OP signatures preferentially mapped to malignant epithelial compartments in pancreatic cancer, whereas Wnt signatures were linked to non-malignant epithelium. Similarly, in colon cancer OP signature mapped predominantly to the malignant epithelial compartments. Drug (n = 33) screening in pancreatic- and colorectal cancer PDTOs (n = 3) demonstrated consistent medium-dependent shifts: Wnt-grown PDTOs were globally more sensitive in the screened subset, particularly to MAPK-axis inhibitors and apoptosis-sensitizers, while OP-grown PDTOs exhibited relative resistance. Culture medium composition is a key determinant of PDTO phenotype, transcriptome and drug sensitivity. Wnt medium was associated with drug-sensitive states, whereas OP medium was associated with adhesion- and inflammatory-related programs, relative resistance in the screened subset of 33 drugs and closer alignment with malignant epithelial programs in the analyzed pancreatic / colorectal cancer single-cell atlases.

items.title: Towards equity in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander mental health: Policy priorities across Medicare, telehealth and the National Disability Insurance Scheme.
items.abstract: The objective of this Viewpoint is to synthesise our recently published findings on disparities in mental health service use among Indigenous Australians and explore implications for equitable service delivery across Medicare, telehealth and the National Disability Insurance Scheme. This viewpoint summarises findings from linked data analyses across three studies examining mental health service use across Medicare, telehealth and the National Disability Insurance Scheme psychosocial supports among Indigenous Australians in Southeast Queensland. In these studies, key sociodemographic and service predictors were examined to identify gaps in service use. Despite a higher proportion of Indigenous Australians using any Medicare-subsidised mental health services, Indigenous Australians were more likely to use general practitioners and phone-based services and less likely to use psychologists and psychological therapies as compared with non-Indigenous Australians. A substantial proportion had no follow-up after care plans, and long delays were common. Smaller proportions of Indigenous Medicare mental health service users used telehealth. Access to telehealth increased service use among both Indigenous and non-Indigenous Australians; however, there is still a service gap. In the National Disability Insurance Scheme psychosocial support, access was more common in individuals with psychotic disorders, with underrepresentation of other mental health conditions, and those with unstable housing had lower access rates. These findings highlight persistent inequities in Commonwealth-funded specialised mental health care access for Indigenous Australians. Policymakers should prioritise reforms to strengthen the cultural safety and accessibility of federally administered schemes such as the Medicare and the National Disability Insurance Scheme. Service planners and commissioners can address system gaps by commissioning culturally safe service-navigation supports and alternative pathways to psychological therapies.

items.title: Economic Evaluation of an E-Dengue Early Warning System for Proactive Dengue Prevention in the Mekong Delta Region, Vietnam: A Protocol.
items.abstract: Numerous dengue early warning tools have been developed, while few have been successfully integrated into routine surveillance systems. The E-Dengue tool, designed using the "Useful, Usable, and Used" framework, aims to predict dengue epidemics three months in advance in the Mekong Delta Region (MDR) of Vietnam. This protocol outlines the economic evaluation of an early warning system in which E-Dengue alerts prompt proactive dengue prevention and control interventions. An economic evaluation using a societal perspective will be conducted alongside a cluster-randomized controlled trial. Costs and outcomes will be compared between the E-Dengue early warning system and routine practice. The primary outcome measure will be disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) and the secondary outcome measure will be dengue cases. The mean cost of a dengue case will be quantified by conducting a cost of illness substudy that will utilize both hospital billing records and structured surveys of patients and informal caregivers and by evidence synthesis from the literature. The cost-effectiveness of E-Dengue will be assessed over a 2-year time horizon and expressed as the incremental cost per DALY averted and per dengue case averted, respectively, and compared against a prespecified cost-effectiveness threshold. The robustness of the results will be evaluated using one-way and probabilistic sensitivity analyses. Demonstrating that E-Dengue is cost-effective will provide rigorous evidence to support its integration into routine surveillance in the MDR and potentially for it to be scaled up and adapted to other areas of Vietnam and nations with similar conditions. Conversely, if E-Dengue is not cost-effective, the study will provide critical lessons for the design and implementation of future early warning tools. ACTRN12626000402347.

items.title: Towards Cleaner Cities: Stakeholder Solutions for Combating Urban Air Pollution Enforcement Challenges in Ghana.
items.abstract: Air pollution governance research has focused predominantly on Europe, China, and India, with comparatively limited attention to the governance and implementation challenges of air pollution control in Africa. Existing African research has often considered environmental regulation broadly, with less emphasis on the institutional, political, technical, economic, and social barriers that constrain effective air pollution governance. This study applied a systems-based, participatory approach to identify barriers and develop context-specific strategies for strengthening air pollution governance in Ghana. Four future workshops (FWs) were conducted in Takoradi, Kumasi, Tamale, and Accra in 2024, involving 20-35 institutional stakeholders at each site. The FW comprised five phases: preparation, critical analysis, fantasy, implementation, and action. Participants identified and thematically grouped barriers, generated potential solutions, and assessed proposed strategies through SWOT analysis and a desirability-feasibility (DF) prioritization process. Desirability and feasibility were scored by participating groups on a five-point scale and subsequently converted to percentages. Participants identified 59 barriers, which were grouped into seven domains: politics and governance, education and training, technology, funding and economics, institutional collaboration, legal and regulatory frameworks, and sociocultural factors. More than 200 potential solutions were generated and subsequently refined through group deliberation and consensus into 90 actionable strategies. The prioritized strategies addressed multiple interconnected dimensions of air pollution governance, emphasizing stronger institutional coordination, improved regulatory and enforcement capacity, enhanced technical and human-resource capacity, sustainable financing, improved public and stakeholder engagement, and strengthened use of evidence for decision-making. All prioritized strategies achieved at least 60% on both feasibility and desirability, indicating broad stakeholder support for their potential implementation. The findings demonstrate that effective air pollution governance in Ghana requires integrated, multisectoral, and context-specific action rather than isolated technical interventions. The participatory framework provides a practical mechanism for identifying governance barriers, developing locally relevant responses, and prioritizing feasible and desirable actions. In the context of limited dedicated national air pollution policy, the findings can support efforts to strengthen existing air quality management arrangements and inform the development of more coherent governance and implementation strategies. The approach may also be adaptable to other African settings facing similar institutional, resource, and environmental challenges.

items.title: Rethinking the application and adoption of NOVA classification in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs): a Southeast Asian food systems perspective.
items.abstract: Ultra-processed foods have increasingly been associated with chronic disease risk in global analyses. The NOVA classification is positioned to influence dietary guidelines, food manufacturing, and public health policy worldwide. This paper argues that the NOVA classification, when applied without contextual adaptation, may be inappropriate for Southeast Asian food systems. It could misdirect policy interventions aimed at addressing both the double burden of under- and overnutrition. By labelling foods as UPFs, NOVA may obscure the essential role that certain processed foods play in improving nutritional outcomes and advancing public health. An overemphasis on the negative impact of processed and ultra-processed foods risks oversimplifying complex dietary patterns in Asia and other LMICs. It may also undermine nutritional gains achieved over the past four decades.

items.title: Sensitivity and Criterion Validity of ED100K Lifetime Eating Disorder Diagnoses: A Study Using a National Eating Disorder Quality Register.
items.abstract: Epidemiological and genomic studies of eating disorders (ED) require scalable approaches to case ascertainment. The self-report ED100K questionnaire assesses lifetime ED diagnoses, has been translated into several languages, and has been used in large cohort studies, with data shared or planned for sharing through major repositories and the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium. This retrospective diagnostic validation study linked ED100K data from the Eating Disorders Genetics Initiative-Sweden (EDGI-SE), a case-control cohort, with clinician-assigned diagnoses from the Swedish national quality register for EDs (Riksät). In the subset with Riksät-linked specialist care records (n = 6889), the sensitivity of ED100K-derived lifetime DSM-IV diagnoses, DSM-5 anorexia nervosa (AN), and broadly defined binge-eating behavior (BE-BROAD) was evaluated against clinician-interview diagnoses. In the full EDGI-SE cohort (N = 15,699), comprising community-ascertained cases and controls, criterion validity was assessed via associations with ED specialist care. Sensitivity was high for AN (DSM-IV: 0.84, DSM-5: 0.96) and substantially lower for bulimia nervosa (BN; 0.61) and binge-eating disorder (BED; 0.34). Sensitivity for BE-BROAD was high (0.88), exceeding BN and BED. Most individuals with BN or BED in specialist care not identified with corresponding ED100K diagnoses were captured by broader ED100K classifications, including BE-BROAD and DSM-5 diagnoses. All ED100K diagnoses and BE-BROAD were strongly associated with ED specialist care, providing evidence for the criterion validity of ED100K ED diagnoses. The ED100K shows strong sensitivity for lifetime AN and BE-BROAD. Lower sensitivity for BN and BED likely reflects challenges in retrospective self-report (e.g., recalling frequency and duration) and in capturing diagnostic features requiring greater subjective judgment. Broader binge-eating classifications may better capture cases missed by algorithm-based BN and BED diagnoses. EDGI is a registered clinical trial (clinicaltrials.gov ID: NCT04378101).

items.title: Lean Body Mass Accounts for the Sex Dimorphism of the Circulatory System and Aerobic Exercise Capacity in Humans.
items.abstract: Lean body mass (LBM) strongly associates with the capacity to deliver and consume oxygen in pilot studies performed in adults with low LBM. We aimed to test whether LBM generally accounts for the phenotype of the circulatory system and hence its sex dimorphism in humans. Healthy women and men (n = 294, 50% female) matched by age and physical activity throughout the adult lifespan (aged 18-78 years) were included. Body composition (dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry), hemoglobin mass/intravascular volumes (carbon monoxide rebreathing), cardiac structure/function/hemodynamics (ultrasound, continuous blood pressure), and aerobic exercise capacity (cycle ergometry, metabolic cart, power meter) were assessed in standardized conditions. Linear regression analyses assessed the relationship of LBM with study variables in each sex. Sex comparisons were performed in non-LBM-matched (n = 294) and LBM-matched (n = 70) individuals. Lean body mass linearly associated with the majority of hematological, hemodynamic, cardiac, and exercise capacity variables in women and men. The slopes of the regression lines did not differ between sexes, with women falling in the lower and men in the upper range of the overall relationship of LBM with these variables. Accordingly, in non-LBM-matched individuals, marked sex differences were observed in >90% of variables. In LBM-matched individuals, no cardiac-related variable (left ventricular structure and function, blood pressure, systemic vascular resistance, aerobic capacity) differed between women and men. Cardiac structure and function, blood pressure, vascular resistance, and aerobic exercise capacity are statistically accounted for by LBM in humans, irrespective of sex. The sex dimorphism of the circulatory system strongly associates with the metabolically active mass, rather than sex.

items.title: Cardiovascular Risk Prediction in Postmenopausal Women With and Without Chronic Kidney Disease: An Observational Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is an important risk factor for cardiovascular events, yet performance of cardiovascular prediction models are understudied in the CKD population, including women with CKD. To investigate the performance of multiple cardiovascular prediction models, the Framingham, Adult Treatment Panel (ATP) III, ACC/AHA Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE), QRISK3, and PREVENT models, in women with and without CKD. Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study (Women's Health Initiative Biomarker Studies). 21,548 postmenopausal women ages 50-79 without cardiovascular disease, including 1,095 with CKD defined by eGFR < 60 mL/min per 1.73 m2. Model discrimination by C-statistic. Calibration by clinically relevant decision-making thresholds. Included events varied by model: Framingham model outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), angina, or coronary heart disease (CHD) death; ATP III model outcomes included fatal and nonfatal CHD; PCE and PREVENT model outcomes included CHD or ischemic stroke; QRISK3 model outcomes included CHD, stroke, or transient ischemic attack. Number of cardiovascular events varied based on outcome definition. For the non-CKD group, events ranged from 846 (4.1%) for ATP III to 1,435 (7.0%) for QRISK3; for the CKD group, events ranged from 93 (8.5%) for ATP III to 145 (13.2%) for QRISK3. Discrimination by C-statistic ranged from 0.57 for the Framingham model to 0.67 for PREVENT in the CKD group; in the non-CKD group, C-statistics ranged from 0.61 for the Framingham model to 0.71 for QRISK3 and PREVENT. Calibration was generally poor in both CKD and non-CKD groups, with underprediction for women with CKD across most models, as well as underprediction for women without CKD for the PREVENT model. Common cardiovascular risk prediction models have poor discrimination and calibration in women with CKD; the PREVENT model generally underpredicted risk for women with and without CKD. items.title: Tailoring Pain Self‑management for Chronic Pain and Opioid Use Disorder: Qualitative Insights from Patients and Clinicians.
items.abstract: Chronic pain, opioid use disorder (OUD), and opioid misuse (OM) often appear as co-occurring conditions; however, they are infrequently treated simultaneously which may lead to worse health outcomes. A novel way to manage these co-occurring conditions is by using a pain self-management (PSM) approach, which focuses on changing behavior through mechanisms that focus on self-regulation. Behavioral interventions, such as PSM, are a safe and effective approach to chronic pain treatment and have the highest likelihood of impact when they are tailored to the target population and setting. The purpose of this study was to determine how to tailor PSM for patients with co-occurring chronic pain and OUD/OM. Qualitative study, pragmatic clinical trial. Patients with chronic pain and OUD/OM (N = 31) and clinicians/staff (N = 15) from primary care settings in Pennsylvania and West Virginia were interviewed to gather information needed to develop and tailor a PSM intervention. Pain self-management. Interviews were predominantly conducted remotely and addressed thoughts about pain, pain management, and the usefulness of behavioral interventions. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and coded using an inductively developed codebook; upon completion of coding, conventional content and thematic analysis was conducted. Results of participant interviews included key takeaways such as the risks of long-term opioid therapy, lack of pain self-efficacy, and the complex patient-provider relationships that arise during treatment of these co-occurring conditions. Clinicians/staff interviews discussed social determinants of health and stigma that can hinder clinicians from providing proper care. The qualitative findings described from this pragmatic clinical trial allowed for the precise formulation of a PSM intervention that specifically targets patients with chronic pain and OUD/OM and may be relevant to the future development of other psychosocial-based interventions.

items.title: A Discrete Choice Experiment to Understand Hospital Discharge Preferences of Populations with Non-English Language Preference.
items.abstract: Effective hospital discharge communication is crucial to reducing adverse outcomes and readmissions particularly for patients with non-English language preference (NELP). However, little evidence exists on which specific discharge elements are most valued by this population. To quantify preferences for aspects of hospital discharge among hospitalized patients with NELP and examine how demographic and language-related factors are associated with these preferences. A discrete choice experiment (DCE) was conducted in which participants were presented with pairs of hypothetical discharge scenarios. Each scenario was defined by one level per attribute across four discharge communication attributes: family involvement during teaching (none, by phone, or in person), mode of verbal communication (language-concordant clinician, in-person interpreter, phone interpreter, or video interpreter), record of discharge instructions (written in English, written in preferred language, or audio-recorded in preferred language), and type of post-discharge phone contact (call from primary care nurse, call from hospital nurse, or a number for patients to call). Participants selected their preferred scenario across 20 choice sets. Hospitalized Spanish- and Haitian Creole-speaking adults at a single urban safety-net hospital (n = 89). Relative attribute importance and level preferences. Mixed logit models estimated overall and subgroup preferences by language and acculturation measures, with choice simulations generating predicted selection probabilities. Record of discharge instructions held the greatest relative importance (39.9% decision weight; 95% CI 34.0%-44.5%), followed by mode of verbal communication (34.7%; 95% CI 29.0%-39.1%). Overall participants preferred language-concordant providers, audio-recorded and written instructions in their preferred language, and family involvement. Preferences varied within and between demographic and language-related groups. Hospitalized patients with NELP prioritize language-concordant, multimodal discharge communication, particularly written instructions in their preferred language and discharge teaching from language-concordant staff. Health systems should prioritize implementing these strategies to improve the patient-centeredness of transitional care programs.

items.title: Denosumab, clinical fractures, and osteonecrosis of the jaw in hemodialysis patients: a comparative study.
items.abstract: Comparative effectiveness of denosumab versus bisphosphonates for overall fracture risk and medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) in patients on hemodialysis remains unclear. We compared fracture outcomes and MRONJ using linked medical-dental claims. We used the DeSC Healthcare Database to identify patients on hemodialysis with osteoporosis or prior fragility fractures prescribed denosumab or bisphosphonates from March 2015 to August 2022. Separate prevalent-user (ongoing users) and new-user (treatment initiators) cohorts were constructed. The primary outcome was all clinical fractures, including first and subsequent events; secondary outcomes were first clinical, hip, vertebral, and other fractures. The safety outcome was first MRONJ. IPTW-weighted Cox models estimated hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals. Among 2379 prevalent-user and 1024 new-user records, mean age was 79 years, and 30-40% had a history of clinical fractures. In the prevalent-user cohort, denosumab was associated with a lower incidence of all clinical fractures than bisphosphonates. Point estimates for first-fracture outcomes generally favored denosumab but were imprecise. In the new-user cohort, the point estimates were generally similar in direction, but the results were not statistically significant. First MRONJ incidence was 0.31 and 0.65 per 100 person-years in the bisphosphonate and denosumab groups, respectively, without statistical significance. In the prevalent-user cohort, denosumab was associated with a lower incidence of all clinical fractures than bisphosphonates, whereas first-fracture associations and the new-user analysis were imprecise. These findings and the low incidence of MRONJ may inform shared decision-making regarding antiresorptive therapies.

items.title: Psychosocial work environment and the risk of disability pension among 1.2 million individuals with and without psychiatric diagnoses: a Danish nationwide register-based cohort study.
items.abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate whether psychosocial working conditions contribute to the risk of disability pension (DP) before age 45, particularly among younger employees with psychiatric disorders, and to assess whether these associations differ by psychiatric diagnosis status. We used data from the Danish Work Life Course Cohort, including 1,214,772 employees entering the labour market between 1995 and 2015. Psychosocial working conditions were assessed annually using job exposure matrices and included quantitative demands, influence at work, job strain, emotional demands, and work-related violence. Psychiatric diagnoses (ICD-10: F00-F99) and DP were identified from national registers. Cox proportional hazards models were applied using calendar time as the underlying time scale, adjusting for age and covariates. Analyses were stratified by psychiatric diagnostic status and sex, and interactions tested. DP incidence was higher among employees with hospital-registered psychiatric diagnoses (48.4 and 64.2 per 10,000 person-years among women and men) than among those without (5.6 and 5.0). Among employees with psychiatric diagnoses, psychosocial working conditions showed weaker or no associations with DP. In contrast, among those without psychiatric diagnoses, several working conditions were associated with DP, particularly low influence at work (hazard ratio 1.58 (95% CI 1.36-1.83) for women and 1.69 (1.43-2.00) for men). Interaction analyses consistently supported differences in these associations by psychiatric diagnostic status. Psychosocial working conditions were associated with DP before age 45, with more pronounced associations among individuals without psychiatric diagnoses and weaker or no associations among those with such diagnoses.

items.title: Prevalence of depression and associated factors among caregivers of patients with mental illness in Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Caregivers of patients with severe mental illness play a crucial role in patient care but often experience significant emotional stress, resulting in high rates of depression. In Africa, where mental health resources are limited, it is essential to understand the extent of this issue. This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to assess the prevalence of depression among these caregivers and identify contributing factors. Observational studies reporting depression prevalence among caregivers of people with mental illness in African countries were systematically identified through searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, PsycINFO, the Cochrane Library, and African Journals Online (AJOL) from August to October 2025. Eligible studies were independently assessed, and data were extracted using a standardized Microsoft Excel spreadsheet and imported into STATA version 14.0 for analysis. Prevalence estimates were logit-transformed and pooled using a random-effects model and subsequently back-transformed to percentages. Heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q, I², and τ². Subgroup analyses, leave-one-out sensitivity analyses, and random-effects meta-regression analyses were performed. Small-study effects were evaluated using funnel plots, Begg's test, and Egger's regression test. Comparable adjusted odds ratios (AORs) for associated factors were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. This systematic review and meta-analysis, which included 10 studies with 2,709 participants, revealed a concerning prevalence of depression among caregivers of patients with mental illness in Africa. The pooled prevalence of depression was 45.5% (95% CI: 31.1-60.7%), with substantial between-study heterogeneity (I² = 98.0%, p < 0.001). Subgroup analysis by geographic region showed pooled prevalence estimates of 52.7% (95% CI: 36.9-67.9%) in Eastern Africa, 16.3% (95% CI: 2.8-56.9%) in Northern Africa, and 66.2% (95% CI: 59.5-72.3%) in Western Africa. By publication period, pooled prevalence was 46.4% (95% CI: 24.2-70.1%) for studies published in 2011-2017 and 44.9% (95% CI: 25.9-65.6%) for those published in 2019-2024. Factors associated with depression include being female (AOR = 2.41, 95% CI: 1.41-4.12) and poor social support (AOR = 3.16, 95% CI: 1.31-7.60). Depression is highly prevalent among caregivers of people with mental illness in Africa, with female caregivers and those with poor social support experiencing greater odds of depression. These findings highlight the need to integrate caregiver-focused mental health services, including routine depression screening, counseling, and psychosocial support. Strengthening peer and community support systems and improving access to mental health resources may help reduce the psychological burden among caregivers.

items.title: Cohort profile: The China Emotional Development Cohort of Adolescents (CED-A).
items.abstract: The China Emotional Development Cohort of Adolescents (CED-A) is a nationwide prospective cohort study designed to explore the developmental trajectories of emotional problems during adolescence, as well as to examine the impact of contemporary environmental factors and gene-environment interactions. The baseline survey was conducted between December 2023 and January 2025. A total of 15,299 participants were recruited from 8 provinces, including students in Grade One of junior and senior high schools, aged 12-13 and 15-16 years, respectively. Follow-up will be conducted over a period of 3 years, with data collection occurring once each semester, through in-class questionnaires. The dataset includes information on multi-dimensional environmental factors collected annually, as well as assessments of depression and anxiety symptoms conducted biannually. A composite approach using multiple validated scales was applied to enhance the accuracy of screening for these emotional problems. Saliva samples were also collected at baseline for genomic analysis. The first wave of follow-up is currently ongoing, with an anticipated rate of loss to follow-up to be less than 10%. Initial analyses using a composite assessment approach revealed the overall prevalence of 16.2% for depression and 11.5% for anxiety symptoms in Chinese adolescents. This national cohort study will provide important insights regarding longitudinal mechanisms of mental health in Chinese adolescents, as well as early risks for emotional problems by utilizing integrated environmental and biological data. The findings will inform the improvement of targeted screening and prevention strategies. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, TRN: ChiCTR2400086974, Registration date: 16 July 2024.

items.title: Position statement from the Asociación Mexicana de Gastroenterología on the early detection and timely referral of gastrointestinal cancer (esophagus, stomach, and colon) in primary care.
items.abstract: Gastrointestinal cancer, particularly esophageal, gastric, or colon cancer, is a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in Mexico. There are substantial delays in the early identification and timely referral of primary care patients, resulting in more advanced-stage diagnoses and poorer clinical outcomes. Our aim was to issue a position statement from the Asociación Mexicana de Gastroenterología (AMG) to guide primary care physicians in the identification of alarm features, risk stratification, and timely referral of patients with suspected gastrointestinal cancer. A multidisciplinary group of 20 specialists in the fields of gastroenterology, oncology, endoscopy, epidemiology, and public health, from both public and private institutions, developed the position statement through a structured consensus process. Clinical statements were drafted and voted on, they were organized by cancer type (esophageal, gastric, and colorectal), and three clinical algorithms were designed to support decision-making in primary care. Thirteen statements were issued on alarm features, risk factors, recommended diagnostic studies, and risk-stratified referral pathways (urgent, priority, and elective). The role of upper endoscopy and high-quality colonoscopy as diagnostic procedures of choice was emphasized, clearly distinguishing them from population-based screening strategies. This position statement provides a practical, evidence-based, expert consensus-informed guide, adapted to the Mexican healthcare setting, whose aim is to implement prevention strategies, reduce diagnostic delays, improve early detection, and optimize the referral of primary care patients with suspected gastrointestinal cancer.

items.title: Early Initiation of SGLT2 inhibitor and Mortality in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Target Trial Emulation Study.
items.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve outcomes in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), yet the optimal timing of initiation in routine clinical practice remains uncertain. We investigated the impact of early initiation of SGLT2i within 30 days of HFrEF diagnosis on mortality and HF hospitalization. Using Danish nationwide register data from July 2020 to August 2024, adults with incident HFrEF eligible for SGLT2i therapy were identified. A target trial comparing initiation of SGLT2i within 30 days of HFrEF diagnosis versus no SGLT2i initiation during this 30-day period was emulated. The analysis used a clone-censor-weight design with follow-up starting at HFrEF diagnosis. The primary outcome was one-year all-cause mortality, and HF hospitalization was assessed as a secondary outcome. Among 10,346 patients with incident HFrEF, 3268 (31.6%) initiated an SGLT2i within 30 days of HFrEF diagnosis and 7078 (68.4%) did not initiate the treatment during this 30-day window. About 226 deaths occurred among SGLT2i initiators and 637 deaths among non-initiators. Compared with non-initiation, initiation of SGLT2i within 30 days was associated with lower one-year risks of both death (RD -1.1 percentage points; 95% CI (-2.0 to -0.2)) and HF hospitalization (RD -3.4 percentage points; 95% CI (-3.9 to -2.9)). Initiation of an SGLT2i within 30 days of HFrEF diagnosis was associated with lower one-year mortality and HF hospitalization compared with no initiation. These findings support prioritizing early SGLT2i initiation as part of foundational therapy for HFrEF in routine clinical practice.

items.title: A comparative analysis of the EPA's 2005 cancer risk assessment restructuring vs. the historical Crump linearized multistage model.
items.abstract: In 2005, the US EPA finalized its Guidelines for Carcinogen Risk Assessment, transitioning from the 1986 Linearized Multistage (LMS) framework to the Benchmark Dose (). This shift leveraged software to fit empirical curves to biological data, with a focus on chronic animal bioassay cancer studies. This paper conducts a meta-analysis evaluating the "before and after" risk metrics for 28 carcinogens during this transition. These findings demonstrate that for linear extrapolations, the exposure limits generated by the consistently land within a single log-scale factor () of LMS estimates for 89.3% of chemicals (25 of 28). Furthermore, 64.3% of the cohort (18 of 28) exhibits near numerical parity (), with several agents showing equivalence. We show that cases of divergence () are driven by changes in biological inputs (e.g., human vs. animal datasets, multi-organ tumor aggregation) rather than low-dose curve-fitting. While this restructuring offers theoretically improved model data fits for sublinear and threshold carcinogens, the findings indicate that the BMD approach, like the LMS model, is still primarily limited by the use of the few-dose/high-dose NTP protocol. The present findings are in close agreement with previous studies comparing LMS and BMD risk estimates for a wide range of EPA carcinogens.

items.title: Data-Driven Approach to Estimate Ambient Ammonia Concentrations.
items.abstract: The Netherlands experiences significant environmental impacts from reactive nitrogen, particularly ammonia (NH3), whose long-term deposition harms soil, water, and biodiversity. NH3 is emitted mainly from agriculture and its levels can be very high and variable in intensive livestock areas. Although monitoring stations are set up across multiple locations, data gaps may still arise due to issues with measurement instruments. Therefore, there is a need for models that can reliably fill in these missing observations. In this study, we first applied Linear Regression, Random Forest, and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) models to predict one day ahead NH3 concentrations at six sites (De Zilk, Valthermond, Vredepeel, Wekerom, Wieringerwerf, Zegveld) in the Netherlands. All models captured daily NH3 trends, with Random Forest initially performing best (R2 up to 0.59 at Valthermond). Predictions were strongly driven by lagged NH3 values with wind speed and precipitation contributing moderately. After correcting for prediction lag caused by autocorrelation, the linear regression performed best at most sites (with best performance observed at Zegveld with R2 of 0.84) and was used for gap filling. It maintained reasonable accuracy despite sparse observations (every 2-7 days), with most sites (De Zilk, Valthermond, Vredepeel, Wekerom, Zegveld) exhibiting a significant correlation of almost or more than 0.5 even at 7 days measurement gaps. Additionally, we noted that historical data from existing sites could be effectively used to fill gaps at newly established locations that exhibited similar distributions of NH3.

items.title: Epidemiology of Animal Viruses with Emphasis on Prevention: The Growing Importance of Arboviruses
items.abstract: Viral diseases remain a major threat to animal health, livestock production, biodiversity, and, in some cases, public health. Their epidemiological dynamics are determined by complex interactions among the virus, susceptible hosts, vectors, environmental conditions, animal movements, and management practices. Among these diseases, arboviruses are of particular importance because their transmission depends on arthropod vectors and is therefore strongly influenced by vector ecology, climate, host availability, and environmental change. Important veterinary arboviruses include bluetongue virus, African horse sickness virus, West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever virus etc. Changes in temperature, rainfall patterns, land use, vector distribution, and animal movement may modify the geographical and seasonal patterns of arboviral transmission, increasing the risk of emergence and spread into previously unaffected areas. Wildlife and migratory birds may further contribute to the maintenance and dissemination of several arboviruses, creating complex interactions between wildlife, vectors, domestic animals, and humans. A coordinated One Health approach is therefore essential for anticipating emerging viral threats and implementing timely, evidence-based prevention and control strategies. items.title: Balancing Management and Risk in a New European Pyrogeography
items.abstract: Wildfires are an increasingly important challenge across Europe. Climate change is altering the conditions under which fires can ignite and spread, but wildfire risk is also shaped by how landscapes are used, managed, and planned. These choices influence vegetation and fuel availability, landscape structure, and the resilience of ecosystems and communities. Understanding these interactions is therefore important for developing landscapes that are better prepared for a changing climate. Wildfire research draws on multiple disciplines, including ecology, climate science, land-use research, and fire modelling. This broader perspective is referred to as pyrogeography—the study of how fire interacts with climate, vegetation, landscapes, and human activities across space and time. Although wildfire research in Europe is growing, fewer studies combine land-use change, fuel management, ecosystem function, and wildfire modelling to examine how future landscapes can balance multiple objectives. This dissertation addresses this challenge by investigating how land management, future land-use change, and fuel management influence wildfire risk across Europe. The research combines continental-scale assessments with a regional case study. Chapter 2 maps the suitability of three fuel-relevant management strategies—herbivory, mechanical fuel removal, and prescribed burning—across Europe. The results show that opportunities for these strategies vary considerably between regions, highlighting the importance of adapting management to local ecological and social conditions. Chapter 3 examines how wildfire management interacts with biodiversity and carbon storage. It identifies areas where reducing wildfire risk may also help protect important ecosystem functions, as well as areas where fuel management requires careful consideration of potential trade-offs. Chapter 4 focuses on central Portugal and explores how different land-use trajectories influence wildfire susceptibility. The results indicate that continued agricultural abandonment generally increases wildfire susceptibility, whereas renewed agricultural activity can reduce susceptibility by altering vegetation patterns and fuel continuity. Chapter 5 returns to the European scale and simulates how different fuel management strategies perform under alternative land-use and climate futures. Management targeting fine fuels, either alone or combined with other fuel classes, generally produces greater reductions in wildfire behaviour than strategies focused only on coarse fuels. However, responses vary considerably between regions, reinforcing the importance of adapting management to local conditions. Taken together, the findings demonstrate that wildfire in Europe is shaped not only by climate, but also by decisions about how landscapes are managed. Land-use planning, fuel management, and ecological conservation are closely connected, and effective wildfire management requires balancing multiple objectives, including reducing fire risk, conserving biodiversity, storing carbon, and supporting agriculture and forestry. Because these priorities and landscape conditions vary across Europe, management strategies cannot be applied uniformly. The modelling approaches presented in this dissertation do not predict exactly where or how future wildfires will occur. Rather, they provide ways to explore alternative futures, identify potential management opportunities and trade-offs, and examine how different land-use and fuel management pathways may influence wildfire outcomes. By bringing together wildfire science, land-use planning, ecology, and modelling across spatial scales, this dissertation contributes to a more integrated understanding of wildfire management and provides evidence to support the development of landscapes that are better prepared for a changing climate.

items.title: Classical Mechanics
items.abstract: This textbook provides a thorough coverage of classical mechanics. Meant for undergraduate and graduate physics students, it contains discussions on topics beneficial for researchers also. Along with standard graduate-level topics, it highlights and demonstrates the applications of classical mechanics in various areas of physics, astronomy, and astrophysics, thus emphasizing the subject's relevance to current research. Detailed explanations are provided throughout to support self-study and ensure clear understanding of concepts. The text begins with preliminary topics and then proceeds to Lagrange's equation of motion, Hamilton's principle of stationary action, and conservation principles in classical mechanics. It then extends to topics like Hamiltonian formulation of laws of mechanics, two-body central force problem, and restricted three-body problem, among others. Lagrange and Poisson brackets are discussed in exclusive chapters. The book concludes with expositions on Hamilton–Jacobi formulation of dynamics, perturbation theory in Hamiltonian mechanics, dynamics of rigid bodies, and nonlinear dynamics and chaos.

items.title: Scalable high-density tactile arenas for measuring ground-contact forces in freely moving animals
items.abstract: Understanding how animals physically interact with their environment is fundamental to studying movement, sensorimotor control, and neurological function. Yet most behavioral measurement systems primarily capture movement and posture, while direct measurements of contact forces often require specialized instrumentation or involve trade-offs among spatial coverage, resolution, and acquisition speed. Here, we introduce a scalable tactile sensing platform that transforms the surface beneath freely moving animals into a high-resolution contact-imaging instrument. By combining modular sensor arrays with adaptive compressive tactile sampling, the platform provides 16,384 tactile sensing elements at 2-mm pitch across a 512 x 128-mm runway, with nominal 1 kHz acquisition. Rather than exhaustively scanning the entire array, the system concentrates measurements around active contacts, enabling high-speed sensing across an extended behavioral surface. Synchronized overhead video and a camera-assisted analysis pipeline enable paw-resolved measurements of contact loading, stance dynamics, footprint morphology, interlimb weight redistribution, and center-of-pressure trajectories. In a longitudinal rat model of sciatic nerve injury, the platform detected reduced loading of the injured hindlimb and increased loading of the contralateral limb, including changes that conventional gait timing measures underestimated. The modular architecture, together with openly available hardware designs, software and data, provides an accessible framework for studying the mechanical interactions underlying freely moving behavior, with potential applications across neuroscience, injury, and motor recovery research.

items.title: Neuroscience-informed Psychoeducation for Eating Disorders
items.abstract: Eating disorders are serious psychological concerns associated with high levels of physical and psychological comorbidity and elevated premature mortality rates. Despite the severity of these disorders, gaps in clinical care exist and most individuals with eating disorders either do not receive or do not benefit from existing evidence-based treatments. There has been a growing movement to incorporate neuroscience-informed targets into eating disorder treatment; however, to date psychoeducation for eating disorders remains narrowly focused on eating- and weight-related behaviors and less directed towards their underlying mechanisms. Yet, neuroscience-informed psychoeducation (NIPE) can provide vital insights into diagnostic distinctions, patterns of psychiatric comorbidity, risk and maintenance mechanisms, brain-body relations, prognostic course, and therapeutic targets for eating disorders. Further, knowledge of neuroscience can assist in designing the delivery of psychoeducation with the neurobiology of eating disorders in mind by tailoring content to consider the impact of personality and illness stage on the learning process. In this chapter, we highlight the promise of NIPE for eating disorders, provide a case example of NIPE for eating disorders delivered in a clinical setting, and discuss future directions for research in this area. Ultimately, NIPE can be used to bridge the gap between research knowledge and clinical care in eating disorders, thereby enhancing patient self-efficacy, dispelling misconceptions about eating disorders, and enhancing the accessibility of the science for individuals with these serious, yet undertreated disorders.

items.title: Brain synchrony between interacting sibling pairs during real-time cooperation: an fMRI hyperscanning study
items.abstract: Siblings typically represent the longest-lasting social relationships. Second-person neuroscience provides a framework for studying the neural mechanisms of real-time, reciprocal social interactions. Yet, most studies have focused on simplified coordination tasks, limited brain regions, and did not investigate neural dynamics between siblings. In the first study investigating brain synchrony between siblings to date, we used fMRI hyperscanning to simultaneously record brain activity in 50 same-sex healthy young adult sibling pairs while they played a complex collaborative problem-solving Tetris game requiring continuous non-verbal complementary coordination. Brain synchrony was quantified using inter-subject correlation across 36 regions of interest (ROIs) of the social brain atlas. The interacting sibling pairs showed significantly higher brain synchrony than randomly permuted non-sibling pairs in 19 ROIs (FDR-corrected p < .05). These regions were primarily located within the higher-level theory of mind subnetwork (including bilateral temporo-parietal junction, precuneus and dorsomedial prefrontal cortex), and intermediate-level subnetwork (including anterior insula, inferior frontal gyrus). Greater synchrony in the left temporo-parietal junction significantly predicted better cooperative performance, suggesting that shared neural modelling of a partner's intentions supports effective collaboration. Synchrony in frontal and temporal regions was weakly modulated by cooperative and competitive sibling relationship characteristics; however, these effects did not survive correction for multiple comparisons and should be interpreted cautiously (uncorr. p < .05). This study provides first evidence that real-time cooperation between siblings is supported by inter-brain synchrony in core social brain networks. We highlight the value of ecologically valid hyperscanning approaches for investigating neural mechanisms of cooperation in long-term relationships, advancing the field of relational neuroscience.

items.title: Remote sensing applications in solid waste monitoring and management.
items.abstract: The rapid growth of solid waste generation carries significant environmental and public health challenges globally. Traditional waste monitoring methods are not cost-effective and are limited in spatial and temporal scope. Remote sensing, encompassing satellite, aerial, and unmanned platforms, has emerged as a transformative approach to identify, monitor, and manage solid waste sites. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the state-of-the-art in remote sensing applications for solid waste monitoring and management, covering technological developments in the past 2 decades. We examine sensor platforms (optical, hyperspectral, thermal, synthetic aperture radar, light detection and ranging), data processing and machine learning workflows, major application domains (landfill mapping, illegal dumping detection, volumetric assessment, thermal anomaly detection, greenhouse gas monitoring, marine plastic tracking), and integration with geographic information system and IoT (Internet of Things) systems. The present study also evaluates operational successes, methodological challenges, policy implications, and outlines a research roadmap for enhancing the accuracy, scalability, and real-world adoption of remote sensing in waste management.

items.title: National memory path study: Formation of register-based cohorts of persons diagnosed with dementia in Finland in 2019 and 2021.
items.abstract: Aims This study describes the study design and methodology for the formation of novel National Memory Path cohorts, outlined to investigate dementia incidence and health and social service use preceding dementia diagnosis in Finland before and after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, and to enable further national-level analyses. Methods A register-based study was conducted, consisting of all Finnish home-dwelling adults who received a dementia diagnosis in 2019 or 2021. Dementia was defined based on the diagnosis in the Finnish Health Care Registers, or on the prescription of an anti-dementia drug in the Finnish Prescription Centre. Health and social service use within 12 months before the diagnosis included visits to outpatient and inpatient care in primary and secondary healthcare, emergency departments and home care recorded in the Finnish Health Care Registers. Results Altogether, 23,121 and 22,419 persons were diagnosed with dementia in 2019 and 2021, respectively, corresponding to an incidence of 520 and 501 per 100,000 in mean population. The highest number of diagnoses occurred in the 75-84 age group. Within 12 months before the diagnosis, 98% had used health and social services. Outpatient care in primary healthcare was the most often used service, followed by outpatient care in secondary healthcare and emergency department use. Conclusions National health registers enable comprehensive analysis of dementia incidence and service use. Frequent service use prior to the dementia diagnosis creates opportunities for dementia symptom detection across various parts of the health and social care system.

items.title: Grief, adjustment, and acceptance: A qualitative study of mental health, coping, and identity in people with Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser Syndrome (MRKH).
items.abstract: Receiving a diagnosis of Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser Syndrome (MRKH) presents unique challenges. Little is known about MRKH-related mental health, coping, and identity across the lifespan or the role of positive adaptation in individuals' experiences of MRKH. Participants completed interviews on mental health, family planning, sexual well-being, relationships, and healthcare experiences. A reflexive thematic analysis approach was used to analyze the data. Three themes represented experiences of living with MRKH: grief, adjustment, and acceptance. Our analysis reconstructed a common pattern across participants' retrospective accounts, in which experiences of grief were often described in relation to the period following diagnosis, while adjustment and acceptance were frequently reflected in participants' narratives of living with MRKH. Participants' experiences of mental health, coping, and identity differed across the three themes. The results suggest that many people with MRKH demonstrate psychological resilience and describe enhanced well-being alongside experiences of grieving, adjustment, and acceptance.

items.title: Characterizing genetic determinism about body weight: An exploratory study.
items.abstract: Genetic determinism, the belief that genetic factors are the major determinant of a trait, shapes attitudes about body weight. This study explores deterministic beliefs, evaluates potential predictors, and examines associations with weight-related psychosocial outcomes. Data were collected through an online survey of 678 U.S. adults. Items assessed genetic determinism about body weight, demographics, causal attributions for weight, and weight stigma-associated attitudes. Endorsement of genetic determinism was relatively uncommon, with 21% of participants agreeing to some extent with deterministic statements on average. Deterministic attitudes were positively correlated with genetic and environmental attributions for weight and negatively correlated with dietary and physical activity attributions. Predictors included political orientation and an interaction where parents of more children had more deterministic attitudes at higher body weights. Findings highlight nuanced ways genetic determinism beliefs associate with body weight attitudes, suggesting the need for further research into mechanisms and implications for stigma reduction and health behavior.

items.title: The association between pension and mental health of older adults: Evidence from China.
items.abstract: In the context of high coverage of social pension insurance in China, there is a lack of comprehensive empirical research on how different pension levels affect the mental health of older individuals. Drawing on nationally representative data from the 2018 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, this study empirically examines the link between pension and the mental health of older adults in China. Furthermore, a three-step approach and Karlson-Holm-Breen decomposition method were employed to estimate the mediating effect of social activities. The results indicate that pension level is related to older adults' mental health. Further analysis demonstrates that pensions mitigate depressive symptoms among older Chinese adults through increased participation in social activities. The positive association between pension and mental health is more pronounced among older adults without wage income. Our study provides evidence for China's efforts to refine the social pension insurance system and gradually enhance pension benefits.
