items.title: Internalized weight stigma as a mediator between past weight stigma and current healthcare avoidance/comfort in seeking medical care.
items.abstract: Youth may experience weight stigma from medical providers, which can be internalized and reduce quality of life. However, little is known about how early provider-based weight stigma relates to later healthcare behaviors. This study examined whether internalized weight stigma statistically mediated associations between provider-based weight stigma during childhood and adolescence and (1) healthcare avoidance and (2) comfort in seeking care in adulthood. Participants were 488 university students who reported past and current weight stigma in healthcare, internalized weight stigma, healthcare avoidance, and comfort in seeking medical care. Over half experienced provider-based weight stigma during youth and one-third within the past year. Early provider-based weight stigma was associated with greater avoidance and lower comfort, with significant indirect effects through internalized stigma. Findings underscore the lasting associations between early weight-stigmatizing healthcare experiences and adult healthcare engagement, with internalized weight stigma statistically accounting for these associations.

items.title: The Quantitative Psychologist Is Dead, Long Live the Quantitative Psychologist
items.abstract: Much of what quantitative psychologists publish consists of developing statistical methods, implementing them in software, and evaluating them in simulation studies. I argue that artificial intelligence (AI) can already do much of this work, and that its share will only grow. The quantitative psychologist has always been a jack of all trades, combining programming, statistics, and psychological knowledge without being a master of any one of them. AI is now the better jack of all trades. When methods become cheap, value moves to what AI cannot supply and to what it newly makes possible. I describe three directions: collecting trustworthy data from real people, formalizing psychological theory now that computational modeling is within reach of any researcher, and rethinking methodological educationso that students learn to judge the analyses that AI will run for them. Thespecialist role built around producing methods for others will fade, whilequantitative thinking spreads through all of psychology.

items.title: The Map Is Not the Territory: Construct Names, Items, and Responses in Measures of Mentalizing, Epistemic Trust, and Emotion Regulation
items.abstract: Psychology has a measurement problem: different constructs often share the same name, and the same construct is measured under different names. This matters most for constructs theorized as interdependent. In theory, these constructs are defined by name, and their interdependence is posited at that level; in practice, each is measured by a pool of items, often from separate questionnaires, which may overlap or diverge in ways the names do not anticipate. We asked whether construct names correspond to the items that operationalize them, whether items reflect the structure of responses, and whether responses follow the boundaries posited by names or drawn by items. Using reflective functioning, epistemic trust, and difficulties in emotion regulation as a case study, we compared semantic similarities of construct names and items with response correlations in 1,167 emerging adults (aged 18–29, 72% female; item-level analyses preregistered) and 1,068 secondary school students (aged 14–20, 67% female). Construct names best matched their own items in 4 of 11 subscales. Items reflected the structure of responses (r = .62 and .58), also, less closely, across questionnaires (.42 and .37). Responses followed boundaries drawn by items more than those posited by names. A correlation between such measures, usually read as evidence of interdependence, may also arise from items that describe the same experience or from shared method variance. What theory says about a construct thus applies only in part to what its items measure.

items.title: Accidental overdose admissions and premature death: A large population-based data-linkage cohort study in New South Wales, Australia (PAVLOVA 4).
items.abstract: Background and aims People with substance use disorders have reduced life-expectancy; however, risks of premature death from injuries and natural causes following an accidental overdose are not well characterised. This study aimed to estimate risk of premature death (by cause and over time), and disease burden following hospitalised accidental overdose. Design An observational study using the Poisoning And enVenomation Linkage to evaluate Outcomes and clinical Variation in Australia (PAVLOVA) cohort. Setting A population-based data-linkage including admissions from all public and private hospitals in New South Wales, Australia (population ~8 million), 2011-2020. Participants 14 036 individuals [median age 43.5 years, interquartile range (IQR) = 29.4-61.8 years, 46.7% female, n = 6557] with an index non-fatal accidental poisoning, as defined by hospital coding, followed for a median of 3.9 years (IQR = 1.7-6.3). We restricted our analysis to people with accidental poisonings with prescription and illicit drugs that are associated with non-medical use and dependence, including opioids and benzodiazepines. Measurements Standardised mortality ratio (SMR) by cause (natural causes stratified by body system, and external causes stratified by intent and mechanism), SMR over time (post-index poisoning), years of life lost (YLL) by cause, age and sex. SMR and YLL were calculated based on expected values generated using official statistics. Results Of the 14 036 people included, there were 2588 deaths. Death was more likely in individuals with accidental poisoning compared with the general population [SMR = 3.5, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 3.4-3.7]. SMRs were highest for external causes (SMR = 12.8, 95% CI = 11.5-14.1), including accidental poisoning (SMR = 59.5, 95% CI = 51.7-67.3) and suicide (SMR = 10.5, 95% CI = 8.2-12.9). Death was also more likely across all natural causes, particularly infectious (SMR = 7.0, 95% CI = 5.1-8.9) and respiratory diseases (SMR = 6.2, 95% CI = 5.4-6.9). Median YLL per death was 21.2 (IQR = 10.0-35.6) and 15.2 (IQR = 7.2-30.2) for males and females, respectively. The main contributors to YLL were natural causes (64.0%): neoplasms (19.5%), circulatory (12.2%) and respiratory disease (11.1%). The remainder of YLL was from external causes (36.0%): mainly accidental poisoning (22.4%). Summary People in New South Wales, Australia, who experience an accidental overdose appear to have an increased risk of death over subsequent years, but particularly in the first month, compared with the general population; however, accidental poisoning accounts for only 22% of years of life lost, with death from natural causes being much more common.

items.title: Trends in Opioid Prescribing for Nonspecific Low Back Pain After CDC Guidelines and California Prescription Drug Monitoring Programs, 2012-2024.
items.abstract: Objective Nonspecific low back pain (ns-LBP) is a widespread health challenge, and opioids were frequently prescribed upon first LBP presentation in the United States during the opioid epidemic. We assessed temporal changes in quarterly (Q) opioid prescriptions for new-onset ns-LBP from 2012 through 2024 at a California medical center amid evolving voluntary federal recommendations and mandatory state regulations. Methods We analyzed opioid prescription rates (prescription within 6 months of diagnosis) for ns-LBP patients diagnosed in all departments and stratified by emergency department (ED), and we compared high- versus low-dose prescription (≥50 morphine mg equivalents/day). Change point detection identified transitions without policy priors, and interrupted time series regression quantified level changes and trend modifications. Results Of 31 940 ns-LBP patients, 2077 (6.5%) received opioids (mean [SD] age, 51.0 [17.6] y; 45.3% male; 53.7% White). Change points occurred at 2015 Q2 and 2018 Q4. Prescribing odds declined 2.7% per quarter from 2012 Q1 through 2024 Q4 (95% CI, 0.4%-5.0%; P = .02). ED patients (16.5% prescribed opioids vs 5.8% non-ED) showed a 54.2% immediate reduction at 2015 Q2 (95% CI, 18.8%-74.2%; P = .008), declining from 27.4% to 12.2% before plateauing; non-ED patients showed a 42.8% reduction at 2018 Q4 (95% CI, 27.5%-54.9%; P Conclusion Change points coincided with anticipatory adoption of the 2016 Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommendations and 2018 California mandatory drug monitoring implementation. ED settings showed disproportionate reductions at 2015 Q2, consistent with knowledge diffusion of voluntary guidelines in settings with frequent opioid prescribing, while non-ED reductions coincided with immediate regulatory compliance at 2018 Q4. This distinction can guide future policy selection to address environment-specific adoption barriers.

items.title: An Integrated Housing Intervention for People Involved in the Criminal-Legal System: Contributors to Successfully Moving Along the Housing Continuum.
items.abstract: Objectives People impacted by the criminal-legal system face challenges to securing and sustaining permanent housing. This study was designed to deliver an integrated housing, medical, and behavioral health services intervention to individuals with criminal-legal involvement. Methods After a baseline needs assessment, participants were linked to services and completed quarterly study visits for up to 12 months. We used descriptive statistics to assess frequency and multivariate logistic regression to assess correlates of housing status at last follow-up. Results Between June 2019 and November 2023, 187 participants were enrolled in Project CHANGE (Comprehensive Housing and Addiction Treatment Network of Greater New Haven). At baseline, 43% of participants were unstably housed, 37% were homeless, and the remaining resided in a shelter or institution. At the time of last follow-up, 49 participants (26.2%) reported improved housing outcomes, and an additional 121 participants' (64.7%) housing situation did not worsen. In multivariate models, individuals who were older (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 1.1; 95% CI, 1.0-1.1), unstably housed at baseline (AOR = 7.6; 95% CI, 3.8-15.9), and enrolled in the study for longer (AOR = 1.2; 95% CI, 1.1-1.3) had higher odds of being housed at last follow-up, whereas those with high-severity substance use had lower odds of being housed (AOR = 0.3; 95% CI, 0.1-0.6). Conclusions In this comprehensive program, integrated housing and health services were time and cost intensive but were associated with positive housing outcomes. People involved in the criminal-legal system face unique barriers to housing, particularly when compounded by substance use.

items.title: Exploring the role of COVID-19 pandemic preparedness in Norway's Ukrainian refugee crisis response.
items.abstract: Aims The aim of this study was to explore how and in what ways COVID-19 preparedness in Norway shaped the organization and delivery of the country's response to the Ukrainian refugee crisis and identify lessons learned from the overlap of the pandemic and the refugee crisis to strengthen Norway's preparedness for future crises, as perceived by the participants. Methods A qualitative study with in-depth, semi-structured, individual interviews was conducted among 10 individual, civil society, and government actors who worked in relation to both the COVID-19 pandemic and the Ukrainian refugee crisis. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis. Results The following four themes emerged, including both positive and negative consequences of the end of the pandemic overlapping with the beginning of the Ukrainian refugee crisis: (1) pandemic-shaped mindsets and momentum in crisis response, (2) adapting pandemic resources for refugee crisis response, (3) participation and power in crisis decision-making, and (4) lessons learned: continuity is key. Conclusions This study provides an enhanced understanding of how selected Norwegian actors perceived the role of COVID-19 preparedness in the Ukrainian refugee crisis response. Participants identified both strengths, such as the reuse of resources and coordination structures, and challenges related to communication and participation in decision-making. Understanding these experiences may help inform future preparedness planning across overlapping crises.

items.title: Sunscreen use at Danish beaches in 2025 and long-term changes in sun protection related to public advice.
items.abstract: Background National health authorities advise against excessive sun exposure and recently advised the public to increase sun protection factor (SPF) to ⩾30 to reduce sunburns and lower the risk of developing skin cancer. Aim To examine the prevalence of sunscreen use and level of SPF used at Danish beaches on sunny days in 2025, and the development in sunscreen use over time related to recommendations by the European Union and the Danish Health Authorities. Methods : We investigated the prevalence of sunscreen use at beaches in the Copenhagen area during summer 2025 and related the data to sex, age, SPF, time of sunscreen purchase and frequency of sunscreen application. We compared our data to similar investigations performed during the last 35 years. Results The study population was 389 persons, of which 10% were children. Participating men and women had an identical mean age of 34 years. About 70% of men and 90% of women used sunscreen. Mean body SPF was 30 for women and 28 for men. Mean face SPF was 46 for women and 38 for men. Sunscreen use and SPF were independent of age. Newly acquired sunscreens had a higher SPF than sunscreens bought before 2025. We found an exponential rise in SPF related to recommendations by the EU and Danish Health Authorities. Conclusions In the last 35 years, the level of SPF used at the beach has increased exponentially from a median of SPF 4 to SPF 30, with a clear relation to public health recommendations.

items.title: Frequent Social Media Use Associated With Tobacco, Alcohol, and Drug Use Among US High School Students.
items.abstract: Objectives The purpose of this study was to examine the associations between frequent social media use and tobacco, alcohol, and drug use among US high school students in grades 9 through 12. Methods Data from the 2023 national Youth Risk Behavior Survey (N = 20 103) were analyzed to assess the associations between frequent social media use and current tobacco or nicotine use, current alcohol use, current binge drinking, ever marijuana use, ever prescription opioid misuse, and ever select illicit drug use. Frequent social media use was defined as using social media several times a day, about once an hour, or more than once an hour. Quasi-Poisson regression models estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (APRs) comparing substance use behaviors among students with frequent social media use versus infrequent or no social media use, overall and by sex. Models were adjusted for race and ethnicity and grade. Results Compared with students reporting infrequent or no social media use, students with frequent social media use were more likely to report current tobacco or nicotine use (APR = 1.88; 95% CI, 1.25-2.83), current alcohol use (APR = 2.07; 95% CI, 1.54-2.78), current binge drinking (APR = 2.55; 95% CI, 1.45-4.48), and ever marijuana use (APR = 2.09; 95% CI, 1.68-2.60). Associations were observed among female and male students. Conclusions Frequent social media use was associated with several substance use behaviors among US high school students. Future research should examine mechanisms, including type of social media platform used, exposure to substance use-related content, and peer influences, to inform prevention strategies.

items.title: Cross-Sectional Associations of Positive and Adverse Childhood Experiences with Adulthood Awareness of and Participation in Children's Cafeterias (Kodomo Shokudo) in Japan.
items.abstract: Childhood experiences shape social participation in adulthood. However, evidence remains limited regarding how positive childhood experiences (PCEs) and adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) relate to participation in low-threshold, community-based initiatives. This study examined the associations between PCEs and ACEs and adulthood awareness of and engagement in children's cafeterias ( kodomo shokudo ) in Japan. Using nationwide online survey data, PCE and ACE scores were categorized as 0, 1-2, 3-5, and 6-7, and 0, 1, 2, and ≥3, respectively. Outcomes were awareness and past-year engagement. In fully adjusted models, higher PCE and ACE categories were associated with greater awareness (ORs [95% CIs]: 2.11 [1.95-2.29] for PCE 6-7; 2.13 [1.96-2.33] for ACE ≥3). Higher PCE categories were also associated with engagement (1.32 [1.08-1.63] for PCE 6-7), whereas ACE categories were not. Supportive childhood environments may facilitate engagement in flexible community initiatives.

items.title: Respiratory pathogens across rural populations: general practice patients with community-acquired pneumonia, residents, and goat farmers.
items.abstract: Background Residents living near goat farms ( Methods This cross-sectional study included general practitioner (GP)-diagnosed pneumonia patients (PP; n = 108), non-farming rural residents without pneumonia (NFR; n = 200), and goat farm workers (GFW; n = 91). Oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal swabs were collected and analyzed by a multiplex and two additional PCR test targeting in total 12 bacteria, 20 viruses and 1 fungus. Between-group differences in detection were assessed by Fisher's exact tests. Logistic regression analyses were performed to assess associations between pathogen detection and residential proximity to goat farming and other covariates. Results Presence of any of the examined pathogens was highest in the PP group (94.5%), followed by GFW (88.8%), and NFR (70%). The most frequently detected pathogens overall were Haemophilus influenzae, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and rhinovirus. Of these, M. catarrhalis and S. pneumoniae were significantly more often detected in PP, whereas Salmonella spp. and S. aureus were more frequently detected in GFW. Eight pathogens, including Coxiella burnetii, were not detected. Age, season of sampling, smoking and other covariates were significantly associated with certain bacteria and viruses. However, no associations were identified between residential proximity to goat farming and detection of specific pathogens in NFR and PP. Conclusions Respiratory pathogens were detected in nearly all PP, while substantial proportions of positives were also observed in GFW and NFR, likely reflecting (transient) colonization rather than active infection. Detection of the examined pathogens was not associated with residential proximity to goat farms, suggesting that these pathogens do not explain the observed increased pneumonia risk among nearby non-farming residents. As a substantial proportion of the Dutch population (~ 7%) lives within 2,000 m of a commercial goat farm, and goat farming is expanding globally, further research efforts, including microbiologic diagnostics and surveillance, are needed to elucidate the mechanisms underlying the increased pneumonia risk among nearby residents.

items.title: Cariprazine Augmentation and Sustained Remission of Physical Aggression in Clozapine-Treated Treatment-Resistant Schizophrenia: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Persistent aggression may occur in treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) despite long-term clozapine treatment and multiple augmentation strategies. We describe a male patient in his sixties with a decades-long history of schizophrenia who required prolonged psychiatric inpatient care because of recurrent, unpredictable physical assaults toward other patients, staff, relatives, and police. This included treatment at a state forensic psychiatric hospital because of treatment complexity and safety concerns, not forensic legal status. Aggression persisted during adequately monitored high-dose clozapine treatment and several augmentation strategies. The last documented physical assault occurred in October 2021. Cariprazine 1.5 mg/day was initiated in November 2021, primarily for longstanding negative symptoms. Within approximately seven weeks, mood and participation in communal ward activities improved. No further physical assaults were documented during more than 4 years of follow-up. The patient subsequently transitioned to voluntary treatment and supported housing. Later somatic illnesses, temporary interruptions of oral medication, and substantial fluctuations in clozapine serum concentrations were not followed by renewed physical aggression. This case describes a prolonged temporal association between cariprazine augmentation and the absence of recurrent physical assaults, but the single-case design, episodic pretreatment course, concomitant treatment changes, and absence of standardized ratings preclude causal inference.

items.title: A Gamified Mobile Application for Orthodontic Education: Usability Assessment and Impact on Knowledge and Attitude of Dental Students.
items.abstract: Purpose The use of gamification-based educational interventions in dentistry has been proposed as a novel approach to increase cognitive engagement and improve learning; however, evidence regarding the simultaneous effect of these tools on students' knowledge and attitude in the field of orthodontics is limited. This study evaluated the usability of a gamified orthodontic application and compared its knowledge and attitude outcomes with traditional reference-book study. Methods In an experimental study, 80 sixth-year dental students were assigned to the intervention and control groups. The intervention group used a gamified scenario-based application for 1 month. Usability was assessed with the Mobile Health App Usability Questionnaire (MAUQ). Knowledge and attitude scores were measured before and after the intervention, and data were analysed using a mixed linear model. Results The mean usability scores were assessed as satisfactory. Although both groups improved, significant time × group interactions favoured the intervention group for knowledge (p = 0.013) and attitude (p = 0.001). However, the observed effect sizes were small to moderate, suggesting a limited but potentially meaningful educational benefit. Orthodontic course grade showed a positive and significant association with both outcomes (p 0.05). Conclusion Compared with traditional reference-book study, the gamified application was associated with modest improvements in knowledge and attitudes. However, the design did not allow the specific contribution of gamification to be distinguished from other digital-learning effects.

items.title: Epigenetics in Traumatic Brain Injury.
items.abstract: Following traumatic brain injury (TBI), changes in proteins, metabolites, and gene expression are highly dynamic and are influenced by genetic and environmental factors, circadian rhythms, and injury characteristics, including injury type (focal or diffuse), severity (mild to severe), and stage of recovery (acute, subacute, and chronic). These molecular alterations are accompanied by epigenetic modifications that regulate gene expression and contribute to injury progression and recovery. In this review, we integrate and summarize preclinical and clinical studies examining DNA methylation, histone methylation and acetylation, microRNA (miRNA)-mediated regulation, RNA epigenetic modifications, and mitochondrial epigenetic (mitoepigenetic) changes following TBI. Most studies have focused on DNA methylation, histone modifications, and miRNAs in experimental models, providing important insights into cell type-specific epigenetic responses after injury. We also review studies evaluating therapeutic strategies, including DNA methyltransferase and histone deacetylase inhibitors, that target epigenetic mechanisms to improve TBI outcomes.

items.title: Clinical features of mental imagery in substance use disorders: A mixed-methods analysis.
items.abstract: Aims To characterise the frequency, features and content of craving-related mental imagery among people seeking treatment for substance use disorders (SUDs); examine within-session change in self-reported craving following imagery elicitation; and explore perceived links with autobiographical memory, behavioural, cognitive and emotional responses and imagery triggers. Design Mixed-methods observational study incorporating a semi-structured interview and repeated within-session measurement of craving, with quantitative analyses and qualitative content analysis. Setting A single National Health Service adult community drug and alcohol treatment service in South London, United Kingdom. Participants Fifty-five adults meeting Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th Edition (DSM-5) criteria for SUD were recruited between June and December 2019; 33 (60.0%) met criteria for more than one SUD. Measurements The interview assessed craving-related imagery frequency, sensory and affective characteristics, content, autobiographical-memory links, perceived responses and triggers. Craving was measured using the Craving Experience Questionnaire ̶ Strength (CEQ-S11) at baseline, immediately after imagery elicitation and at the end of the interview. Results Fifty-one participants (92.7%) reported craving-related imagery. The predominant modality was visual in 49/51 (96.1%); among 50 participants with complete imagery data, 42 (84.0%) described recurrent imagery and 26 (52.0%) reported experiencing it daily. Forty-seven (94.0%) perceived their image as representing an actual event or as strongly associated with autobiographical memory, usually an amalgamation of multiple memories. The 51 images were classified into five overlapping themes: stages of substance consumption (80.4%), the substance itself (84.3%), imagery features (94.1%), sensory experiences and activation (84.3%) and contextual or setting features (96.1%). Among 211 reported triggers, places (21.8%), people (19.9%) and internal moods (17.5%) were most frequent. Mean CEQ-S11 scores were 39.50 at baseline, 48.70 immediately after imagery elicitation and 36.70 at interview end, with an overall effect of time, F(2, 100) = 5.03, P-value 0.008. Among participants with recurrent imagery, 31/42 (73.8%) reported often or always wanting to use the substance following the image, and 34/42 (81.0%) reported that the image often or always persisted until distraction or substance use. Summary In a mixed-methods study of adults attending a community drug and alcohol treatment service, craving-related mental imagery was commonly reported and was predominantly visual, often recurrent, closely linked to autobiographical memory and associated with perceived urges to use substances.

items.title: Beliefs about emotions, distress tolerance and paranoia across the menstrual cycle in individuals with premenstrual difficulties and controls.
items.abstract: Objectives Premenstrual Disorders are characterized by recurrent symptoms associated with clinically significant distress or impairment. There is limited understanding of psychological processes associated with premenstrual difficulties. This study investigated maladaptive beliefs about emotions, distress tolerance and social-cognitive experiences of paranoia in individuals with premenstrual difficulties and controls across cycle phases. Methods 109 participants provided data at four timepoints across two menstrual cycles. Participants were classified into PSST-defined provisional PMDD, moderate-to-severe PMS and control groups. Psychological outcomes were assessed during perimenstrual (cycle days 1-2) and mid-follicular (cycle days 4-8) phases across two cycles. Differences across assessment timepoints and groups were examined using linear mixed-effects models. Results In the provisional PMDD group, maladaptive beliefs about emotions were higher and distress tolerance lower at perimenstrual assessments than at mid-follicular assessments and controls perimenstrually. Ideas of reference were also higher at perimenstrual assessments than at mid-follicular assessments and controls perimenstrually. Ideas of persecution did not show the perimenstrual increase in either premenstrual difficulties group. Phase-related changes were not consistently observed in the moderate-to-severe PMS group or controls. Mid-follicular maladaptive beliefs about emotions and ideas of reference did not differ significantly between premenstrual difficulties groups and controls; however, distress tolerance remained lower in the provisional PMDD group than in controls. Conclusions The provisional PMDD group showed higher perimenstrual maladaptive beliefs about emotions and ideas of reference, alongside lower distress tolerance. These findings suggest these processes may be relevant to more severe premenstrual difficulties. Prospective daily assessments are needed to clarify the temporal relationships between these processes and symptom severity.

items.title: Arhgef1 Deletion Disrupts Early Cortical Neurogenesis via PAK1 Overactivation and Causes Motor Dysfunction in Adulthood.
items.abstract: Precise regulation of early cortical development is essential for the establishment of normal brain function, and its disruption can contribute to the pathogenesis of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). Impaired motor function is a prominent early manifestation of various NDDs, yet the mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identified ARHGEF1, a Rho family guanine nucleotide exchange factor highly expressed during early corticogenesis, as a novel regulator in embryonic cortical neurogenesis and adult motor function. By Emx1-Cre-mediated forebrain deletion of Arhgef1 in mice (Arhgef1 cKO mice), early cortical neurogenesis is specifically disrupted, leading to reduced deep-layer cortical neurons. Mechanistically, Arhgef1 deficiency overactivates RAC1/CDC42-PAK1-Cofilin signaling in early cortical development, whereas pharmacological PAK1 inhibition within this critical window rescues the genesis of deep-layer cortical neurons. Importantly, Arhgef1 cKO mice exhibit remarkable motor learning and coordination deficits in adulthood, accompanied by altered neuronal morphology in the motor cortex and impaired neuronal activities in motor circuits. In all, we elucidate a critical developmental window when ARHGEF1 governs corticogenesis via negatively regulates PAK1-dependent pathway and further reveal an important role for ARHGEF1 in maintaining normal motor function in adulthood.

items.title: Parkinson Disease Subtype Stability and Eventual Convergence.
items.abstract: Objective Previous research identified distinct Parkinson disease (PD) clinical subtypes of "Motor Only," "Psychiatric & Motor," and "Cognitive & Motor" based on comprehensive, multidomain classification. Whether these subtypes reflect distinct trajectories or progressive disease stages remains unknown. This study aimed to determine the longitudinal stability of PD subtype membership. Methods This study included 250 PD participants with baseline subtype classifications and behavioral evaluations at two timepoints (average interval = 2.51 years), including motor, cognitive, and psychiatric assessments. Latent transition analyses tested the stability of PD subtype membership over time, and logistic regression models examined baseline factors associated with subtype transitions. Available brain autopsy data from 67 participants strengthened analyses by allowing the exclusion of 9 participants with non-PD neuropathologic diagnoses (e.g., Multiple System Atrophy, Progressive Supranuclear Palsy). Results The three baseline subtypes ("Motor Only," "Psychiatric & Motor," and "Cognitive & Motor") persisted at the second timepoint. Individuals in the "Motor Only" subtype at baseline had a high probability of remaining in the same subtype at follow-up (0.91), demonstrating longitudinal stability. Participants in the "Psychiatric & Motor" and "Cognitive & Motor" subtypes remained in the same subtype with probabilities of 0.55 and 0.59, respectively. A fourth "Severe Multidomain" subtype emerged at follow-up, characterized by more pronounced motor, cognitive, and psychiatric dysfunction. 64% of the "Severe Multidomain" group had dementia, compared with ≤ 7% in the other three subtypes. Subsequent analyses indicated that higher baseline Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) sum of boxes was strongly associated with transition to a different subtype. Interpretation These findings suggest that PD subtypes reflect relatively stable subgroups that may eventually converge with development of dementia.

items.title: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Strategies for Central and Peripheral Remyelination.
items.abstract: Myelin sheaths are produced by myelinating glia and provide metabolic support to neuronal axons while accelerating electrical signal conduction. Myelinating glia, which include oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system (CNS) and Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system (PNS), have distinct developmental origins and biological characteristics that profoundly influence their capacity for myelin regeneration following demyelinating insults. In various demyelinating diseases, loss of myelin and myelinating glia resulting from autoimmune disorders, inflammation, or genetic defects causes neurological dysfunction. Beyond removing disease-causing factors, inducing and accelerating remyelination represents a critical therapeutic goal for demyelinating diseases. In this review, we first summarize and compare molecular mechanisms underlying CNS and PNS remyelination, including extracellular signaling pathways, transcriptional regulation, and intercellular communication. We then highlight current treatments and ongoing clinical trials for common demyelination disorders, including neonatal white matter injury, multiple sclerosis, and inherited peripheral neuropathies.

items.title: Global synchrony moderates sad mood and is associated with emotional Stroop interference and somatic symptoms.
items.abstract: Mood-congruent attention in depression has been studied via emotional interference tasks, including tasks comparing responses to sad and happy stimuli. Mood induction offers a way to experimentally induce sad mood in non-clinical samples and examine its association with subsequent emotional interference, including Sad-Happy interference. Previous studies have separately linked resting-state global neural dynamics (synchrony, metastability) to depressive symptoms and attentional processing. However, whether individual differences in baseline global synchrony and metastability relate to how individuals respond to sad mood remains largely unclear. This study therefore examined the relationship between neural dynamics, sadder mood after induction, and Sad-Happy interference. Depressive symptoms also encompass somatic domains alongside cognitive-affective domains, though these are rarely distinguished in neuroimaging studies. We further examined whether baseline neural dynamics and their association with sadder mood and Sad-Happy interference were related to depressive symptoms (total, cognitive-affective, and somatic). Forty-eight non-clinical individuals completed resting-state neuroimaging, mood induction (sad or non-sad), and an emotional Stroop task. We found in a cross-sectional moderated mediation model that sadder mood after induction was associated with greater interference from sad compared to happy stimuli at medium and high levels of global synchrony, particularly in exploratory path models that included somatic symptoms. Findings suggest that individual differences in resting-state global synchrony may be a neural correlate of sadder mood after induction and Sad-Happy interference in non-clinical individuals. This study offers preliminary associations linking neural dynamics, sad mood, emotional interference, and somatic symptoms, providing insights into the role of neural dynamics in emotional and attentional processing.

items.title: Paraganglioma and childhood-onset optic atrophy in a SDHA compound heterozygous patient: an example of dual dominant and recessive inheritance.
items.abstract: SDHA pathogenic variants cause moderate to severe complex II deficiency, which manifests as a mitochondrial disorder in a homozygous/compound heterozygous child, or as hereditary cancer, mostly paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma, in a heterozygous adult. Here, we report the first composite heterozygous SDHA patient (hypomorphic allele p.(Thr508Ile) × null allele p.(Arg451His)) who developed complete congenital optic atrophy and a paraganglioma at the age of 36 yrs. No other germline variants were identified by sequencing panels of genes involved in these two disorders. This raises the question of whether paraganglioma screening should be implemented for carriers of a null SDHA variant.

items.title: Cardiac perception and self-reported interoception in common mental health disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Atypical interoception may represent a transdiagnostic marker for mental health difficulties. Reviews to date exploring the relationships between interoception and mental health have presented mixed findings, with a narrow focus on cardiac measures of interoception. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies that measured the association of cardiac perception and self-reported interoception with common mental health disorders, including anxiety, depression, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and obsessive-compulsive disorder, in clinical and non-clinical samples of adults. A total of 206 effect sizes from 57 articles (total N = 6,652) were eligible for inclusion in random effects meta-analyses. Overall, pooled associations showed no significant association of mental health difficulties with performance on the Heartbeat Counting Task (r = -.042), but a significant, negative association with Heart Rate Discrimination Task performance (r = -.137). Problems in adaptive interoceptive attention (r = -.183) but not sensing (r =.136), or interpretation (r = -.117), were associated with worse mental health symptomology, as was greater maladaptive interoceptive attention (r =.381). Moderator analyses showed that the size of the effect often varied between different mental health disorders, and there was some evidence of overly influential effect sizes as well as wide 95% prediction intervals. Our findings highlight the importance of methodological choices and potential differences between different performance-based tasks of cardiac interoception and different self-reported interoceptive dimensions. Our results show some support for interoception as a transdiagnostic marker for mental health difficulties that can support the development of evidence-based interventions.

items.title: The Canadian underage substance use prevention (CUSP) trial: Amended protocol for a hybrid effectiveness-implementation cluster randomized trial of PreVenture.
items.abstract: Background Adolescent substance use remains a significant public health concern, particularly among youth with elevated personality-based risk profiles. PreVenture is a brief, personality-targeted intervention shown to reduce substance-related behaviours in prior randomized trials. Objective The Canadian Underage Substance Use Prevention (CUSP) trial was designed to evaluate the effectiveness and implementation of PreVenture under routine school conditions. Methods CUSP is a three-arm, parallel-group, hybrid effectiveness-implementation cluster randomized controlled trial in public secondary schools across three Canadian provinces. Schools were randomized to: (1) PreVenture via a Train-the-Trainer model; (2) PreVenture Train-the-Trainer plus Implementation Facilitation; or (3) treatment-as-usual control. Grade 10 students completed baseline screening using the Substance Use Risk Profile Scale (SURPS); those scoring above predefined SURPS thresholds were invited to participate in PreVenture workshops and included in primary analyses. The primary outcome is screening positive for substance-related problems (CRAFFT score ≥ 2). Secondary outcomes include binge drinking, cannabis, illicit drug, and non-medical prescription drug use. Implementation outcomes include fidelity, reach, uptake, acceptability, and sustainability. Conclusions Data collection is complete, but outcome analyses have not yet been conducted. The trial was affected by the COVID-19 pandemic and other implementation challenges, resulting in substantial attrition at both the student and school levels. This protocol documents modifications to the design and analytic plan, also reflected in the updated trial registration (NCT04198974), to ensure transparent reporting of findings. The pre-specified Statistical Analysis Plan, provided as an online supplement, was finalized and accepted by the trial steering committee prior to unblinding. Clinical trial registration number NCT04198974.

items.title: The predictive value of early clinical and electrodiagnostic markers on short- and long-term functional outcomes in Guillain-Barré Syndrome: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Introduction Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS) presents with highly variable recovery trajectories. Early identification of prognostic markers is crucial for optimizing patient management and anticipating severe complications. Method A systematic search of PubMed, EMBASE, and Scopus was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies reporting early clinical or electrodiagnostic predictors of functional outcomes in confirmed GBS patients were eligible. Study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were each performed independently and in duplicate by both authors (PYG and JHW). Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Exploratory meta-analyses were performed using standardized mean differences (SMD) for functional recovery and pooled proportions for mechanical ventilation incidence. Effect sizes were oriented so that a positive SMD consistently denotes poorer functional status in the poor-prognosis group. Functional recovery was additionally stratified a posteriori by outcome assessment timepoint (short-term, 1-4 weeks; long-term, 3-6 months). Results Seven studies (n = 398 patients) were included. High GBS disability scores, reduced MRC sum scores, elevated mEGOS and EGRIS values, and markedly reduced CMAP amplitudes consistently predicted poor functional recovery. In the exploratory pooled analysis, the SMD for functional recovery was 2.33 (95% CI: 0.34-4.32; I 2 = 85.1%; k = 5), and the pooled proportion requiring mechanical ventilation was 0.29 (95% CI: 0.14-0.50; I 2 = 81.4%; k = 5). When stratified by timepoint, the short-term estimate (k = 4) was 2.67 (95% CI: -0.05 to 5.39; I 2 = 86.1%), and only a single study contributed to the long-term stratum (SMD 1.20; 95% CI: 0.84-1.56), precluding pooling. Prediction intervals crossed the null in every analysis. Conclusion Early clinical and electrodiagnostic markers are consistently associated with functional outcomes in GBS across geographically diverse cohorts. However, the pooled estimates are exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than generalizable: they rest on five small studies, exhibit very high heterogeneity, and are not robust to stratification by outcome timepoint. The direction of association should inform structured prognostic frameworks, and confirmatory prospective studies with standardized timepoints are required before pooled estimates can guide individual patient management.

items.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Immunomodulation by Neural Stem Cells in Spinal Cord Injury: From Macrophage Polarization to Therapeutic Plasticity.
items.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) triggers a chronic neuroinflammatory cascade driven by persistent M1 macrophage polarization, creating a hostile microenvironment that inhibits axonal regeneration and perpetuates secondary tissue damage. Neural stem cells (NSCs) offer a promising therapeutic strategy through immunomodulation, reshaping the inflammatory landscape rather than merely replacing lost neurons. This review synthesizes evidence on the molecular mechanisms by which NSCs reprogram the immune response. NSCs suppress TLR4/NF-κB signaling to shift macrophages from a neurotoxic M1 phenotype toward a pro-regenerative M2 phenotype, engage in reciprocal dialogue with T cells and microglia to create a neurogenic niche, secrete neurotrophic factors that upregulate KCC2 and restore GABAergic inhibition, and modulate purinergic signaling to attenuate neuropathic pain. However, the evidence base remains incomplete. Most studies provide correlative rather than causal evidence, and the M1/M2 framework does not fully capture macrophage heterogeneity after SCI, particularly in the chronic phase where foam cells, pro-fibrotic phenotypes, and disease-associated subpopulations emerge. The subacute window is generally associated with superior outcomes, but optimal timing varies with injury severity, model, cell source, transplantation route, and cell dose. Clinical translation remains at an early stage; phase I trials have established feasibility and short-term safety, but most lacked control groups and adequate sample sizes. Adverse effects, including allodynia, tumorigenicity, and immune-related complications, underscore that neural cell transplantation is not inherently safe. Future progress requires adequately powered trials with objective endpoints, biomarker development, refined immunomodulation strategies, and careful monitoring for adverse effects.

items.title: Transcranial Evoked Potentials are Minimally Influenced by Afferent Feedback From Peripheral Muscle Contraction.
items.abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation with electroencephalography (TMS-EEG) investigates cortical reactivity, yet the contribution of sensory feedback from muscle twitches to the recorded signals remains debated. We combined M1 TMS-EEG with electromyography, accelerometry, and peripheral electrical stimulation to dissociate central and peripheral contributions. We compared EEG responses across trials yielding large versus small motor outputs, while peripheral stimulation isolated pure afferent components. Bayesian analysis revealed that larger motor outputs covaried with distinct EEG morphologies uniformly across all time windows-including those too early for peripheral feedback-indicating that spontaneous fluctuations in baseline motor cortex excitability drive both responses. Conversely, isolated muscle contraction produced delayed (> 65 ms), markedly smaller EEG responses with distinct spatiotemporal profiles. We conclude that sensory feedback from muscle twitches contributes minimally to TMS-evoked EEG responses, which instead primarily reflect the baseline excitability state of the stimulated cortex.

items.title: Volatilomics in psychiatric biomarker research: from odor signatures to multiomic integration.
items.abstract: Schizophrenia remains a major challenge in psychiatry, with diagnosis still relying largely on symptom-based assessments and lacking validated biomarkers for early detection, screening, or longitudinal monitoring. Although genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic studies have revealed systemic biological dysregulation involving immune, metabolic, and neurodevelopmental pathways, conventional multiomic approaches face significant translational limitations. They often require blood or tissue sampling and can be costly; although they include both dynamic, state-sensitive and more stable, trait-like signals, their complexity and sampling burden can limit frequent or population-level use. Volatilomics, the study of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted through breath, sweat, and skin, has emerged as a complementary molecular approach that may help address these gaps. VOCs represent dynamic downstream metabolic outputs and may capture rapid, state-dependent biochemical changes. Analytical and machine-learning studies have reported VOC pattern alterations in schizophrenia with promising classification accuracy in small, early-stage discovery cohorts, although independent external validation remains limited. This review examines volatilomics as a promising complementary approach with potential applications in early detection and longitudinal monitoring, and considers how integration with systemic multiomics could contribute to diagnosis, patient stratification, and precision psychiatry.

items.title: Geophagy During Pregnancy in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Review of Cultural Practices and Health Implications.
items.abstract: Geophagy, the intentional consumption of soil and other earth materials, is a common practice among pregnant women in many parts of sub-Saharan Africa. This narrative review aimed to examine the cultural drivers, nutritional implications and health consequences of geophagy during pregnancy, as well as identify potential intervention strategies for mitigating associated risks. Literature retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar was synthesized to examine evidence on geophagy during pregnancy in sub-Saharan Africa. The available evidence indicates that geophagy during pregnancy is influenced by a combination of cultural traditions, social norms, physiological changes and perceived health benefits. While the practice is often associated with attempts to alleviate pregnancy-related symptoms and address nutritional deficiencies, it may contribute to adverse maternal and foetal outcomes through reduced nutrient bioavailability, exposure to toxic elements and increased susceptibility to parasitic infections. Evidence from the reviewed studies also indicates associations between geophagy and maternal anaemia, neural tube defects, low birth weight and preterm birth. Despite these risks, routine screening and culturally appropriate counselling regarding geophagy remain inadequately incorporated into antenatal care services across many settings in sub-Saharan Africa. This review highlights the need for culturally sensitive public health interventions, improved maternal nutrition education and strengthened research efforts to better understand the determinants and health implications of geophagy during pregnancy. Integrating geophagy-related screening and counselling into maternal healthcare programmes may contribute to improved pregnancy outcomes and maternal well-being in the region.

items.title: A license to disperse: climatic niche lability and geographic expansion shape the diversification of Oleaceae.
items.abstract: Patterns of species diversity reflect interactions among ecological, biogeographic, and lineage-specific evolutionary processes. Oleaceae provides a useful comparative system because its five tribes differ markedly in species richness, geographic extent, dispersal history, and genomic background. Using distribution data for 476 species and a time-calibrated phylogeny of 283 Oleaceae species spanning all five tribes, we integrated ecological niche modelling, ancestral-range and climatic-niche reconstruction, diversification-rate analyses, and phylogenetic comparative methods while accounting for uneven tribal sampling. Climatic niche position and breadth evolved heterogeneously across Oleaceae, while major range expansions beyond the reconstructed ancestral Asian region were concentrated in Jasmineae and Oleeae. Climatic niche evolution and speciation rates were not consistently coupled; rather, their relationships with dispersal and diversification were lineage- and climatic-axis-specific. Oleeae showed more coordinated associations among niche evolution, dispersal, and speciation, whereas Jasmineae exhibited a more restricted, axis-specific pattern. The ancient whole-genome duplication (WGD) in Oleeae may have contributed to its distinctive evolutionary trajectory. Overall, our results support a conditional 'license to disperse' framework in which climatic niche lability facilitates geographic expansion, thereby indirectly increasing opportunities for diversification.

items.title: Systematic mapping of monitoring and evaluation in rewilding.
items.abstract: Rewilding is a landscape recovery approach that seeks to enhance the functioning of degraded ecosystems by reinstating natural processes, and it is increasingly being adopted by organizations and landowners. Despite its popularity, there is no accepted way to assess rewilding's impacts, which is due in part to inconsistent monitoring and evaluation. To address this gap, we developed a systematic map of a unique dataset combining academic and gray literature on monitoring and evaluation in rewilding case studies. We mapped definitions of success, study systems, methods of monitoring, and evaluation metrics for rewilding case studies to compare where the different strands of literature overlap and contrast in focus. We found that researchers and practitioners have been focused on different aspects of rewilding and that the limited recording of case study details and lack of robust experimental design make it difficult to pool and compare data. Researchers and rewilding practitioners face challenges in building a robust evidence base from which to evaluate rewilding outcomes. These challenges include resources as well as spatial and time constraints, which all limit the consistency of data gathering among projects. More comparisons across rewilding projects, better standardization of data collection and data recording methods, and increased collaboration between researchers and practitioners could help remedy these limitations. We developed recommendations for how to monitor and evaluate rewilded landscapes to improve data quality and availability. These include the broad adoption of low-cost and scalable survey designs with greater focus on comparisons across sites and continued effort toward open-source data storage.

items.title: A systematic review of deforestation outcomes in potential other effective area-based conservation measures across Latin America.
items.abstract: Recognizing conservation contributions from areas outside protected areas (PAs), including other effective area-based conservation measures (OECMs), is increasingly central to meeting global biodiversity targets. However, little is known about which areas could qualify as OECMs and whether they support forest conservation. Focusing on Latin America, we conducted a systematic literature review following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines synthesizing 93 peer-reviewed studies published through 2024 that assess the effectiveness of OECMs outside formal PA systems in reducing deforestation. First, we identified and classified area-based measures that may qualify as potential OECMs into six types based on their conservation objectives and characteristics: strict biodiversity conservation areas, set-aside areas for ecosystem services, Indigenous peoples' territories, local communities' territories, other managed sustainable-use areas, and ancillary conservation areas. Second, we synthesized the available evidence on their effectiveness in reducing deforestation. Indigenous people's territories were the most frequently evaluated, whereas strict biodiversity conservation areas have received relatively little attention. Methodologically, most evidence relied on nonexperimental comparisons of forest-cover trends; quasi-experimental designs were less common but provide stronger causal inference of conservation effectiveness. Disaggregating outcomes by comparator type revealed important patterns: Indigenous territories most consistently showed reduced deforestation relative to both PAs and non-PAs, whereas local communities' territories showed more favorable outcomes relative to non-PAs than to PAs. Set-aside areas for ecosystem services showed predominantly negative outcomes, largely reflecting weak enforcement. Despite this evidence base, very few of these areas have been formally recognized as OECMs, highlighting a disconnect between available research and reporting under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. Bridging this gap will require stronger causal evidence, broader geographic coverage, and inclusive recognition processes that account for the governance rights of those who manage these territories.

items.title: Fifteen years of change in biodiversity conservation across Latin America and the Caribbean.
items.abstract: Latin America and the Caribbean (LACA) is one of the most biodiverse regions globally, yet it continues to experience accelerated biodiversity loss driven by persistent and emerging anthropogenic pressures. In 2009, the Society for Conservation Biology conducted a regional assessment of conservation challenges; however, the evolution of these dynamics over the following 15 years had not been systematically reassessed. We conducted an updated regional synthesis of biodiversity conservation priorities, perceived threats, and implementation barriers across 25 countries, based on a 2024 survey of conservation professionals (n = 244). Respondents were predominantly experienced practitioners affiliated with academic institutions, nongovernmental organizations, and government agencies. Our findings were consistent with the patterns reported in 2009, with deforestation, habitat fragmentation, industrial agriculture, climate change, and pollution persisting as the most severe threats. However, these traditional drivers are now compounded by the intensification of landscape-scale pressures and a marked shift toward the security-conservation nexus. Respondents explicitly identified organized crime and drug trafficking as primary constraints that compromise both ecosystem integrity and the safety of practitioners. Although conservation tools, such as protected areas and environmental policies, have diversified and improved in many ways, their effectiveness remains limited by a diversification without consolidation trend, characterized by chronic underfunding, corruption, and weak intersectoral coordination. Furthermore, engagement with local communities and citizen science remains predominantly low to moderate, highlighting an enduring gap between policy design and on-the-ground implementation. This study underscores that addressing biodiversity loss in LACA has moved beyond the need for technical solutions; it now requires a fundamental transformation in governance quality, institutional integrity, and state capacity to protect the region's natural heritage and the communities that depend on it.

items.title: Bacterial-fungal cross-kingdom interactions in synthetic consortia: boosting secondary metabolites and sustainable food fermentation.
items.abstract: Bacterial-fungal consortia (BFC) consistently outperform aseptic or single-species cultures in producing high-value secondary metabolites, yet the underlying cross-kingdom interaction mechanisms remain poorly understood. In food fermentations, BFCs enhance process robustness, substrate turnover, and bioactive profiles for sustainable functional foods. In these consortia, bacteria and fungi engage in complex cooperative and competitive interactions, involving signaling molecules, genetic regulation, and metabolic flux redistribution to enhance secondary metabolite yields. Based on the ecological compatibility and molecular communication mechanisms, a synthetic microbiology framework for constructing high-yield BFCs was proposed. This systematic approach included selecting appropriate coculture partners, setting up the BFC, and optimizing cultivation conditions. Functional BFCs can be effectively applied to: food fermentation, improving fermentation efficiency, nutritional value, flavor complexity, and food safety. The review provides an overview of BFCs for secondary metabolite production, with emphasis on their cross-kingdom communication mechanisms. It explores the construction and optimization of BFCs and their applications in food fermentation, identifying future directions for enhancing secondary metabolite yields.

items.title: Energetic costs of catch and release angling in Brook Trout (Salvelinus fontinalis) at two temperatures.
items.abstract: Catch and release (C&R) angling is a common practice in recreational fisheries, which can involve a range of acute stressors for fish that lead to physiological and behavioural impairments. Following a C&R event, energy is expended to fuel recovery, while a cessation in feeding can limit energy intake. While the physiological and behavioural consequences of C&R have been extensively studied, the extent of the bioenergetic impacts has rarely been characterized. This study aimed to assess the energetic impacts of C&R stressors on Brook Trout (Salvelinus fontinalis)-a cold-water salmonid sensitive to temperature perturbations and air exposure. Adult Brook Trout were subjected to simulated angling events (i.e. 30s chase, 30s chase and 10s air exposure) or served as controls at 10°C and 15°C. Respirometry was used to measure energy expenditure through excess post-exercise oxygen consumption (EPOC), while a feeding experiment determined the time to return to feeding. Energy expenditure and reductions in energy consumption were incorporated into a bioenergetics model to predict growth outcomes following captures (i.e. 1, 3, 5) over 30 days. The stressors simulated here resulted in a maximum growth deviation of 4.1% (95% CI [2.8-6.5]) after a single capture and 21.0% (95% CI [14.6-33.4]) after five captures. Across temperatures, Brook Trout experienced higher peak metabolic rates at 15°C, but rapid recovery resulted in similar energetic costs of recovery to 10°C. However, our bioenergetic simulations revealed that prolonged (24 h) elevated daily temperature (15°C) occupancy raised metabolic energy expenditure negating the benefits of a faster resumption of feeding. Nevertheless, the moderate simulated C&R stressors tested here within the optimal temperature range of Brook Trout resulted in relatively small energetic consequences, even with numerous simulated captures. Future research should explore the bioenergetic effects of more intense (but still reasonably common) C&R stressors, including longer air exposure periods, hooking injuries and temperature extremes.

items.title: Influence of a thermohaline front on the trophic ecology of the small pelagic fish Lycengraulis grossidens (Clupeiformes: Engraulidae).
items.abstract: Lycengraulis grossidens is economically important for artisanal fisheries and prey of top predators in the Río de la Plata (RP) (SW Atlantic). In particular, Samborombón Bay (SB)-RAMSAR site and key marine summer feeding area for the species-is strongly affected by climate variability. Diet composition, feeding strategy and dietary shifts related to fish size and to an existing thermohaline front between two SB zones were determined in late austral summer (April). A high incidence of brackish/marine prey was hypothesized, varying ontogenetically and in relation with the front. Trophic incidence exceeded 90%. Neomysis americana (Mysidacea) dominated the diet, followed by decapod larvae, gastropods and teleosts. The feeding strategy was specialist at the population level for N. americana but generalist for other prey. Both nMDS and GLM analyses supported the hypothesis, as N. americana, copepods and gastropods were more consumed in North SB, while teleosts South SB, linked to the thermohaline front affecting prey distribution. Smaller individuals ( 150 mm) increasingly fed on N. americana and gastropods. Unlike previous studies reporting piscivory at larger sizes, SB specimens maintained a zooplankton-based diet, with a strong preference for N. americana. Results highlight the species' trophic plasticity and the influence of environmental and ontogenetic factors. This study provides valuable new information on the trophic ecology of L. grossidens in marine waters after a gap of over 60 years, contributing to a better understanding of its trophic role in highly dynamic estuarine and coastal ecosystems.

items.title: Beyond classical overflow metabolism: Toward a unified mechanistic framework.
items.abstract: Overflow metabolism is traditionally defined as the production of low-energy-yield metabolites despite the availability of more energy-efficient pathways, exemplified by acetate secretion in Escherichia coli, ethanol production in yeast, and lactate formation in mammalian cells. Despite extensive study, the mechanisms underlying overflow metabolism remain incompletely understood. Increasing evidence further demonstrates that overflow-like metabolism is not restricted to carbon excess but also occurs under nutrient limitation, environmental stress, recombinant protein expression, and within microbial communities, indicating that its physiological significance extends far beyond the classical paradigm. Here, we review these diverse manifestations, evaluate the underlying mechanisms of overflow metabolism, and propose adopting a separable, reversible Michaelis-Menten formulation as a unifying conceptual framework. This framework integrates catalytic capacity, substrate saturation, product inhibition, and thermodynamic driving forces into a cohesive explanation. Within this framework, overflow metabolism emerges when substrate influx exceeds the processing capacity of more energy-efficient pathways, resulting in flux redistribution toward alternative routes with distinct energetic, kinetic, and/or proteome-allocation characteristics. By bridging enzyme kinetics, resource allocation, thermodynamics, and microbial ecology, this framework may unify diverse forms of overflow metabolism and provide a predictive foundation for engineering this metabolic behavior in microbial systems.

items.title: How acetate alleviates ammonium inhibition and enhances methane-fed single-cell protein production.
items.abstract: Anaerobic digestion produces methane-rich biogas and ammonium-rich digestate, but their joint conversion into single-cell protein (SCP) requires coordinated carbon and nitrogen utilisation. Here, a methane-fed mixed consortium was operated in a membrane biofilm reactor to determine how acetate regulates carbon-nitrogen coordination under ammonium stress. Ammonium addition impaired nitrogen conversion and protein enrichment without eliminating methylotrophs. Acetate restored these functions, increasing protein content to 61.25 % and the apparent N-based SCP yield from 0.34 to 1.46 g SCP/g N. Nitrogen balances showed greater incorporation of inorganic nitrogen into cellular organic nitrogen with acetate, consistent with the increased metagenomic potential for the glyoxylate shunt and ammonium assimilation. Excess acetate, however, promoted soluble microbial products and extracellular polymeric substances, lowering the apparent carbon-based SCP yield. These findings suggest that acetate improves nitrogen incorporation and protein production in a methane-fed mixed consortium while methane utilisation remains active. Controlled acetate retention in anaerobic digestate may therefore support the joint recovery of waste-derived carbon and nitrogen as microbial protein.

items.title: Molecular detection of pathogens in Rhipicephalus ticks collected from companion animals in Bejaia province, northern Algeria.
items.abstract: Ticks are increasingly recognized as important vectors of pathogens affecting animals and humans worldwide. In northern Algeria, data on tick-borne pathogens (TBPs) in ixodid ticks collected from companion animals are still scarce. This pilot study is the first molecular investigation of TBPs in ixodid ticks collected from companion animals in Bejaia province, bordering the Mediterranean Sea. A total of 100 ticks were collected from 75 dogs, 11 cats, and one tortoise. Rhipicephalus sanguineus was the predominant tick species identified (99/100; 99%; 95% CI: 94.0-100.0), whereas a single tick collected from the tortoise was identified as Hyalomma aegyptium (1/100; 1%; 95% CI: 0-6.0). Ticks were tested for Rickettsia spp., Bartonella spp., Anaplasma phagocytophilum, Ehrlichia canis, Piroplasmida, and Hepatozoon spp. Only Rickettsia spp. (11/100; 11%; 95% CI: 6.1-18.8), Hepatozoon spp. (6/100; 6%; 95% CI: 2.5-12.7) and Piroplasmida (2/100; 2%; 95% CI: 0.1-7.4) were detected. Rickettsia spp. (11/88; 12.5%; 95% CI: 7.0-21.2) and Piroplasmida (2/88; 2.3%; 95% CI: 0.1-8.4) were found only in ticks from dogs, while Hepatozoon spp. was found in both ticks from dogs (3/88; 3.4%; 95% CI: 0.8-9.7) and cats (3/11; 27.3%; 95% CI: 9.2-57.1). Further molecular characterization revealed R. massiliae and R. conorii, as well as H. canis, Babesia vogeli, and Cytauxzoon spp. Phylogenetic analysis supported species identification. These findings highlight the presence of TBPs in ticks from companion animals and their potential relevance to One Health, particularly for zoonotic Rickettsia spp.

items.title: Potent antimicrobial pyridyl-imine derivatives: experimental and computational insights into their biological activity.
items.abstract: Dermatophytic infections remain a persistent therapeutic challenge, particularly due to the increasing resistance to conventional antifungal agents. In search of alternative antifungal scaffolds, a series of 2-pyridyl-imine derivatives (PYE1-PYE11) was synthesized and evaluated for antimicrobial, cytotoxic, and biomolecular interaction properties. All compounds exhibited antimicrobial activity, with the ortho-vanillin derivative PYE10 showing the highest potency, including remarkable activity against Proteus mirabilis (MIC = 0.01 mg/mL) and Trichophyton mentagrophytes (MIC = 0.05 mg/mL). Fluorescence displacement assays provided evidence for PYE10-DNA interactions involving both intercalative and minor-groove-associated binding modes, while human serum albumin binding studies revealed 1:1 complex formation, indicating appreciable interaction with HSA. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations identified favorable and stable binding of the most active compounds within the CYP51B active site, supporting the experimentally observed antifungal activity. Computational thermodynamic analysis indicated that Fe 2 ⁺ chelation is protonation-dependent under physiological conditions. Structure-activity relationship analysis revealed that antimicrobial activity is influenced by the electronic nature of substituents, aromatic planarity, molecular flexibility, and the ability to establish multiple intermolecular interactions. In silico ADMET evaluation demonstrated favorable drug-likeness and pharmacokinetic profiles, highlighting these pyridyl-imine derivatives as promising candidates for further antimicrobial development.

items.title: Citizen science tick observations as a proxy for human exposure: Ecological, behavioural and weather drivers in Finland
items.abstract: Abstract Citizen science is an important source of large-scale data on disease vectors, but observations are influenced by both vector availability and human behaviour. We analysed nearly 300 000 citizen science records of two tick species in Finland ( Ixodes ricinus and Ixodes persulcatus ) using generalized additive models to assess how seasonality, weather, and human activity jointly shape daily tick–human encounter reports. Nonlinear seasonal patterns were observed, with species-specific differences consistent with tick phenology. Human population increased the probability and intensity of reporting, while weekend effects and reduced reporting during rainfall indicated the effects of human activity. Temperature responses differed between species, suggesting that encounter patterns vary according to tick species and environmental conditions. Consequently, citizen science tick observations should not be interpreted as measures of tick abundance alone. Rather, they integrate vector ecology, environmental conditions and human behaviour, allowing elevated encounter risk to be identified based on tick species and weather conditions.

items.title: Population genetic structure of the invasive flatworm Obama nungara in France revealed by mitochondrial and microsatellite markers.
items.abstract: Biological invasions pose a significant threat to biodiversity, yet the processes of introduction and dispersal remain difficult to reconstruct, particularly in soil-dwelling organisms. A multi-marker molecular approach can help overcome this limitation. Here, we examined the genetic structure of the invasive terrestrial flatworm Obama nungara (Geoplanidae) in France using mitochondrial (COI) sequences and newly developed nuclear microsatellite markers, representing the first application of this marker type in an invasive geoplanid flatworm. Analysis of 340 COI sequences, including 169 that were newly generated for this study, revealed that all recent French populations belong to the Argentina 1 lineage, with no evidence of additional primary introductions. Haplotype diversity was low at the local scale. In contrast, microsatellite data revealed moderate genetic diversity and heterozygote deficits in several populations, as well as signatures of recent bottlenecks. Significant genetic differentiation was observed among most populations, with no isolation by distance. These results suggest that the invasion of O. nungara in France was driven by a small number of initial introductions followed by sporadic spread, likely facilitated by horticultural trade. Combining mitochondrial and nuclear markers further reveals a pattern of weakly connected introduction foci rather than a continuous spatial expansion, which reflects the contribution of complementary genetic markers to resolving invasion dynamics across scales.

items.title: The Toxic Legacy of Ammunition Lead (Pb) from Big Game Hunting in Sweden.
items.abstract: In Sweden, a total of 5,880,688 moose (Alces alces), 1,084,671 fallow deer (Dama dama), 173,137 red deer (Cervus elaphus) and 7,911 brown bears (Ursus arctos) were harvested by recreational hunters in 1939-2024. In addition, 1,987,646 wild boars (Sus scrofa) were harvested in 1990-2024. To better understand the the potential for exposure of wildlife to lead (Pb), we estimated the amount of Pb from spent Pb-core hunting bullets in gut piles available to wildlife scavengers. Calculations were based on the number of harvested animals, the proportion of gut piles left in situ, the proportion of hunters using Pb-based ammunition, the number of shots per animal and the amount of Pb in each gut pile. Over the 86-year study period, we estimated that a total of ~ 9,045 kg of Pb from spent hunting ammunition was deposited in gut piles left for scavenging. This amount of Pb, which translates to > 450 million lethal doses for eagles weighing ~ 5 kg (0.02 g of Pb per bird), is likely to have resulted in harmful exposure in a wide range of avian and mammalian scavengers feeding on the gut piles. This source of Pb exposure could be eliminated from the ecosystem if Pb-based hunting bullets were banned.

items.title: Attitudes Toward E-Learning Among Undergraduate Nursing Students in Greece: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Background/objectives E-learning has become an integral component of higher education, including nursing programs that combine theoretical instruction with laboratory and clinical training. This multicenter study investigated undergraduate nursing students' attitudes toward e-learning in Greece and examined the individual, educational, and technology-related factors associated with these attitudes. Methods A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted among 1,148 undergraduate nursing students from all eight public university nursing departments operating in Greece during the study period. Data were collected using the Greek version of the Attitude toward e-Learning Scale among Nursing Students (ALSNS). Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, comparative tests, and Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc analyses. Results Students generally recognized the flexibility and accessibility of e-learning and expressed positive intentions toward using digital educational technologies. However, they remained cautious regarding fully online approaches as a replacement for conventional nursing education and showed a preference for blended learning approaches. More positive attitudes were associated with younger age, university affiliation, higher digital competence, higher family income, and advanced year of study (p < 0.05), whereas gender differences were negligible (Cohen's d < 0.15). Conclusions Undergraduate nursing students viewed e-learning as a valuable complement rather than a replacement for conventional teaching. The findings suggest that blended learning models may be appropriate, integrating digital instruction with face-to-face nursing education while considering differences in students' digital readiness and educational context. Future longitudinal studies should examine whether positive attitudes toward e-learning translate into improved academic outcomes and clinical competence.

items.title: Altered Inhibitory Control Across Subclinical Depression and Major Depressive Disorder: Evidence From Stroop Tasks and Diffusion Modeling.
items.abstract: Inhibitory control deficits are central to cognitive dysfunction in major depressive disorder (MDD), yet how such deficits vary across subclinical depression and MDD remains unclear. Childhood trauma may further contribute to variability in inhibitory control. This study examined behavioral and computational markers of inhibitory control across nonemotional and emotional contexts in healthy, subclinical depression, and MDD groups and explored associations with childhood trauma. Thirty individuals with subclinical depression, 33 patients with MDD, and 36 healthy controls (HCs) completed three Stroop tasks (color-word, emotion, and face-word), during which reaction times (RTs) were recorded. Latent cognitive parameters were estimated using the drift diffusion model (DDM) and diffusion model for conflict tasks (DMCs). Associations between these indicators and childhood trauma were examined. Patients with MDD showed significantly longer RTs than subclinical individuals in emotion and face-word Stroop tasks. Computational modeling revealed prolonged nondecision time in MDD, relative to subclinical depression (color-word Stroop task) and HCs (emotion Stroop task). In the subclinical group, greater childhood trauma was associated with faster RTs in incongruent face-word trials and shorter nondecision time in the color-word Stroop task. Our findings support a possible inverted U-shaped pattern of inhibitory control across depressive severity, with enhanced performance in subclinical depression but poorer performance in MDD. Enhanced inhibitory control in subclinical depression may reflect compensatory adaptation linked to early adversity. These findings provide novel insights into stage-related differences of inhibitory control in depression.
