items.title: Preoperative cognitive training for preventing perioperative neurocognitive disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis and meta-regression of randomised controlled trials.
items.abstract: Although nonpharmacological interventions are recommended for preventing perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), cognitive training has not been explicitly advocated. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis (TSA) and meta-regression tested the hypothesis that preoperative cognitive training, compared with usual care, reduces the incidence of PND. Eight databases and two clinical trial registries were searched for RCTs comparing preoperative cognitive training with usual care. Primary outcomes were postoperative delirium (POD), delayed neurocognitive recovery (DNR), and postoperative neurocognitive disorder. Thirteen RCTs with 1446 patients were identified. Preoperative cognitive training was associated with a lower risk of POD (RR 0.53; 95% CI 0.36-0.77; P = 0.001; low certainty). Subgroup analysis (P for interaction = 0.01) and meta-regression (β1 1.072, 95% CI 0.006-2.138, P = 0.049) suggested an association between training format and treatment effect on POD, with a potentially greater benefit for traditional training. For DNR, the incidence was lower in the training group than in the usual care group (RR 0.66; 95% CI 0.46-0.96; P = 0.03; very low certainty), but this finding was not supported by several sensitivity analyses. No significant differences were detected between subgroups for training format, total duration, or surgery type (P for interaction = 0.06, 0.37, and 0.34, respectively), and meta-regression suggested that overall risk of bias was a potential moderator for DNR (P = 0.045). TSA suggested a potential for false-positive findings, as the cumulative Z-curves did not cross the TSA boundaries, and the required information sizes were not reached for either outcome. Preoperative cognitive training may reduce the incidence of POD, with traditional training showing a potentially greater benefit than digital training. For DNR, the current evidence is insufficient to support a preventive effect of preoperative cognitive training, although a trend toward benefit was observed. These findings are limited by high risk of bias in several included trials and failure to reach the required information sizes in TSA, particularly for DNR, which need to be confirmed in future large-scale RCTs. items.title: The role of hope and its association with quality of life in individuals with chronic pain - insights from a daily diary study.
items.abstract: Hope has been identified as a beneficial factor for enhancing quality of life (QoL), particularly for individuals with chronic disease, including chronic pain. However, significant gaps remain in understanding how hope and QoL intersect and relate to one another. The current study investigated whether daily hope frequency, defined as how often participants felt hopeful each day, can predict next-day QoL among individuals with chronic pain who are using cannabis and opioids to manage pain. This was an observational study, approved by the Institutional Review Board of the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health (Protocol: IRB00009327). Participants (N = 132) using opioids and cannabis for chronic pain completed a baseline survey and 30-day daily diaries assessing hope frequency, QoL, and sleep satisfaction. Participants (mean age = 42.7, SD = 13.9) were predominantly male (58.3%) and Non-Hispanic White (63.6%). Linear mixed-effects models were used to test the lagged effects of daily hope frequency, decomposed into between- and within-person components, on next-day QoL, controlling for baseline variables, daily sleep satisfaction, and previous-day QoL. Intraindividual variabilities were also examined. Higher hope frequency was significantly associated with greater next-day QoL both between participants (i.e., participants with higher average hope reported higher QoL) and within participants (i.e., on days when hope was higher than a participant's own average), even after controlling for previous-day QoL and sleep satisfaction. While higher baseline hope and QoL scores were associated with higher average QoL over the 30-day period, intraindividual variability in hope was not significantly associated with QoL. Our daily diary study found that previous-day hope frequency - both stable individual differences and day-to-day fluctuations - was associated with next-day QoL in individuals with chronic pain who were co-using cannabis and opioids.

items.title: miR-138-5p: From Multidimensional Tumor-Suppressive Regulatory Networks to Nanocarrier-Based Delivery for Solid Tumor Therapy.
items.abstract: MicroRNA-138-5p (miR-138-5p) has been reported to exert tumor-suppressive effects in several solid tumors, and its downregulation has been associated with malignant progression, therapeutic resistance, and poor prognosis. This review summarizes research trends and current evidence on the molecular functions, regulatory networks, and therapeutic potential of miR-138-5p in solid tumors, with particular emphasis on competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) regulation and nanocarrier-based delivery strategies. Bibliometric analysis and CiteSpace visualization were conducted using English-language original articles and reviews retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection from January 2014 to October 2025. Relevant literature was reviewed to examine miR-138-5p expression, biological functions, target genes, signaling pathways, ceRNA networks, and therapeutic strategies. Studies focused exclusively on hematological malignancies were excluded. Bibliometric mapping identified research clusters spanning multiple solid tumor types, cell-cycle regulation, and proliferation, while metabolic reprogramming and therapeutic resistance emerged as relevant research themes. Mechanistic studies suggest that miR-138-5p regulates proliferation, apoptosis, migration, invasion, autophagy, immune-related signaling, and chemosensitivity through diverse targets and pathways. Long non-coding RNA- and circular RNA-mediated ceRNA networks have been proposed as an additional regulatory layer, although their physiological relevance requires further quantitative validation. Preclinical findings, including exosome-mediated delivery of miR-138-5p, suggest potential for replacement therapy; however, challenges involving delivery efficiency, tumor specificity, biosafety, pharmacokinetics, and manufacturing standardization remain. miR-138-5p is a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in solid tumors. Further validation of its context-dependent mechanisms and optimization of targeted delivery strategies are needed to support clinical translation.

items.title: Phenotypic and molecular characterization of ESBL, AmpC, and carbapenemase-producing Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from clinical specimens in Iran.
items.abstract: This study aimed to identify ESBL/AmpC- and carbapenemase-producing Acinetobacter baumannii isolates. In this cross-sectional study, a total of 180 A. baumannii isolates were recovered from clinical samples (2018-2022). Modified Hedge Test (MHT), Disc Potentiation Test (DPT) and Double Disc Test (DDT) methods were used for the recognition of carbapenemase, ESBL and AmpC-producing A. baumannii, respectively. The presence of carbapenemase, ESBL, and AmpC encoding genes was verified using the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) method. The enterobacterial repetitive intergenic consensus-polymerase chain reaction (ERIC-PCR) was employed for differentiating about 80 isolates with high imipenem MIC. out of 180, 44.5%(n = 80),98%(n = 177),17.5%(n = 32),4.5%(n = 8) of isolates were positive in MHT, Metallo-β-lactamase, AmpC and ESBL phenotypic tests, respectively. 44.44% of isolates had MIC ≥ 8 µg/ml for imipenem. CTX(41.5%), TEM(31.5%),OXA23(36.6%),OXA24(53.3%)24 and OXA51(96%) were the most prevalent detected genes. Under the ERIC-PCR fingerprinting method, 5 ERIC types were detected. ESBL/AmpC- and carbapenemase-producing A.baumannii isolates are a serious threat to human public health. Identifying these superbugs is critical for the proper management of relevant infections.

items.title: Exploratory donor-aware analysis of developmental transcriptomic trajectories in 15q13.3-deletion cortical organoids.
items.abstract: This descriptive, hypothesis-generating study examined whether 15q13.3-deletion cortical organoids show developmental transcriptomic differences overlapping retinoic acid (RA)-related gene-expression programs. Signatures derived from early RA exposure and prolonged, 7-day all-trans RA (ATRA) treatment were evaluated in public cortical organoid data from three deletion and 17 control donors. Donors, rather than individual samples, were the units of inference; 16 controls and all three deletion donors had sufficient time points for slope testing. Early human, early mouse, and conserved early RA signatures were not significant. A broad ATRA-derived differentiation score showed a negative deletion-control slope difference (exact P = 0.0083; false-discovery rate = 0.0206), but a non-RA maturation score was also significant. The prolonged score correlated strongly with maturity. Sensitivity analyses adjusting for measured maturation and composition did not identify an RA-specific component; neither the targeted RA program nor the covariate-adjusted joint trajectory test was significant. External and single-cell analyses provided biological context, not independent validation. The findings suggest a developmental/maturation-associated trajectory difference overlapping a broad prolonged ATRA-associated program. The three-donor case group and heterogeneous source models limit stability and generalizability; the results do not establish altered RA signaling, vitamin A deficiency, or retinoid-treatment relevance.

items.title: Disulfiram attenuates paraquat-induced renal injury and fibrosis accompanied by changes in Smad3 and Smad7 gene expression.
items.abstract: Paraquat (PQ) is a highly toxic herbicide that induces renal injury through oxidative stress and progressive fibrosis, contributing to chronic kidney disease. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy for accelerating therapeutic development. This study evaluated the nephroprotective potential of disulfiram (DSF), a clinically approved drug with emerging antioxidant and antifibrotic properties, against PQ-induced renal injury, including its association with changes in the expression of the Smad3 and Smad7 genes. Thirty-five male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to seven groups: Control, Vehicle, DSF20, PQ (1.5 mg/kg), and PQ co-treated with DSF (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg). Renal injury was evaluated using histopathology (H&E, PAS, and Masson's trichrome staining), α-SMA, serum biomarkers (BUN, creatinine, and uric acid), oxidative stress parameters (malondialdehyde [MDA], catalase [CAT], and glutathione peroxidase [GPx]), and Smad3 and Smad7 gene expression determined by qRT-PCR. PQ exposure caused marked renal histopathological injury, increased α-SMA, increased oxidative stress, impaired renal function, and elevated fibrosis, accompanied by increased Smad3 and decreased Smad7 gene expression. DSF co-treatment, particularly at 10 mg/kg, significantly ameliorated these changes by reducing tissue injury, decreasing α-SMA-positive area% and collagen deposition, restoring antioxidant enzyme activity, lowering lipid peroxidation, improving renal function, and altering Smad3 and Smad7 gene expression toward PQ levels. Disulfiram at an optimal dose of 10 mg/kg significantly attenuated PQ-induced renal injury and fibrosis, accompanied by reduced oxidative stress and altered Smad3 and Smad7 gene expression. These findings support the potential of DSF as a repurposed therapeutic candidate for mitigating paraquat-induced renal injury and fibrosis. Further studies evaluating protein-level changes and activation of the TGF-β/Smad signaling pathway are warranted to clarify the underlying molecular mechanisms.

items.title: Leveraging claims data-based small-area estimation to evaluate endoscopy access and the area-level prevalence of being up-to-date with colorectal cancer screening among screen-eligible adults in North Carolina.
items.abstract: Endoscopy remains the most common modality by which screen-eligible adults are up-to-date with colorectal (CRC) screening. For the Area-Level Estimates of Cancer Screening (ALECS) study, we leveraged multi-payor claims data to generate small-area estimates of the prevalence of being up-to-date with colorectal cancer (CRC) screening among continuously insured screen-eligible adults in North Carolina (NC). First, we created bespoke small areas at the intersection of counties and ZIP codes, which enabled linkages with aggregated claims data using patients' residential ZIP codes and counties. Using a 10-year lookback period, we then defined the cohort as near-continuously insured screen-eligible adults age 50-74, who did not have a prior diagnosis of CRC or a total colectomy as of December 2020. Statewide, from 2012 to 2020, 79.8-81.2% of continuously insured screen-eligible adults aged 50-75 were up-to-date (UTD) on CRC screening. In 2020, at the small area level, the mean prevalence of being UTD with CRC screening was 79.6% (Standard Deviation: 9.5). Diagnostic tests of an Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) model indicated a significant degree of spatial dependence of the error terms (I = 0.1540; p<.00001), suggesting the need for spatial models. We thus fit a Conditional Autoregressive (CAR) Bayesian generalized linear model with a logistic link function and Leroux priors, accounting for spatial autocorrelation, and found an inverse association between the minimum distance to access an endoscopy facility and the prevalence of being up to date with CRC screening among continuously insured screen-eligible adults across NC (Point Estimate: - 0.0645; Credible Interval: - 0.1156 - 0.0103).

items.title: Service preservation from matching non-matching socks under stochastic loss
items.abstract: Abstract Socks are produced and replaced at a massive scale, yet their paired use makes them unusually vulnerable to service loss, as the disappearance of a single sock can leave usable wear-capacity stranded and create sockless days even when functional socks remain available. In this study, we examine whether pairing non-matching “orphan” socks can preserve daily sock service under stochastic loss, and how this benefit trades off against perceived social discomfort. We formalize sock ownership as a sequential decision problem under uncertainty in which socks wear out and disappear stochastically during laundering, while public exposure induces a person-specific mismatch penalty. We conducted an in-person study to estimate mismatch sensitivity and diversity preference, linking behavioral heterogeneity to interpretable mixing policies. Using these results, an exact benchmark on small tractable instances, and a simulation-based evaluation of pairing policies, we show that strict matching can appear resource-frugal largely because it generates many sockless days. In contrast, controlled tolerance for mismatch sustains service and reduces stranded wear-capacity across loss regimes. The ecological-cost term is treated as a proportional embodied-cost proxy rather than an independent life-cycle assessment measure, so the environmental interpretation is suggestive and mechanism-based rather than a direct estimate of environmental savings. This study establishes the feasibility and limitations of matching non-matching socks as a simple strategy for preserving service from already-owned garments.

items.title: “We just don’t know why”: students’ epistemic risk taking in the social construction of an explanation of plate tectonics
items.abstract: Abstract Epistemic risk is inherent in the practice of science and can be intimidating for students in classrooms building their science skills. We argue here that science learning must be designed to scaffold epistemic risk that supports students in social knowledge construction. Through the case study of a group of four middle school students and their class working to explain the relationship between earthquakes and volcanoes in relation to the larger theory of plate tectonics, we illustrate students’ engagement in epistemic practices and the scaffolds that enabled them to fully participate in these practices. Our analysis suggests that scaffolding in participant structures, more knowledgeable others, and organizational tools supported students in fully engaging in the epistemic practices of science. Though epistemic risk taking is critical to students’ engagement in epistemic practices, there is a need to attend to the interpersonal and socioemotional influences on students’ epistemic agency, attending to students’ sense of belonging, connectedness, and safety. We advocate for the intentional design of epistemic tools that purposefully include supports for students to navigate epistemic risk.

items.title: Affordance-based designed stools invite dynamic sitting for children: a classroom study
items.abstract: Abstract Children spend much of their day sitting in classrooms, often in prolonged static postures. Sedentary behavior is associated with health risks. This study investigates whether stools designed to afford more dynamic sitting, promote greater postural variety and more frequent posture transitions compared to regular school chairs. We observed the sitting behaviors of 34 children aged 6 to 8 years at the beginning and end of a two-week classroom intervention. Results showed that the stools significantly increased posture diversity and the frequency of posture transitions. The initial effects sustained over time, underlining that the stools facilitated more than a novelty effect as children continued to engage with the affordances provided. Additionally, we observed that the stools encouraged sitting in unconventional postures rarely seen with regular chairs, further supporting their role in promoting posture diversity. These findings highlight the potential of affordance-based designs in classroom environments to foster healthier sitting behaviors.

items.title: 心灵的分岔:从无意识到可观察——心理学流派的六次划线 / The Forking Mind: Six Ways Psychology Drew Its Lines
items.abstract: 中文. 本著作是同一作者"六个核心"系列的第一本科普专著:用六个提问,重读心理学一百五十年的流派史。 核心主张:心理学流派史不是一部"谁取代谁"的进步史,也不是一部"谁都被冤枉"的平反史,而是一部"谁在哪里划线、又把什么划到外面、最后由谁付账"的账本史。每个流派都是一次尝试:先划一条线,再决定记住什么、用什么钟、保哪两项、请谁定价、在哪里设门槛;六核问的是"它在哪一步让出了什么",不是"它对不对"。 结构与证据:6 部分、25 章、附录 A—Q、309 页、25 幅矢量插图、68 个表、约 26 万字。第一部分(1—4)划线的诞生:柏拉图—康德、冯特、布伦塔诺、詹姆斯、构造/机能、格式塔;第二部分(5—11)深度的代价:弗洛伊德、荣格、阿德勒、客体关系、自体/依恋、拉康、神经精神分析、心理测量;第三部分(12—15)可观察的约束:华生、巴甫洛夫、斯金纳、行为疗法、行为主义的遗产;第四部分(16—19)内部的回归:认知革命、皮亚杰/乔姆斯基、认知神经科学、社会认知;第五部分(20—22)意义与时间:人本主义、存在主义、发展心理学;第六部分(23—25)系统与定价:系统/后现代、CBT/正念/积极/文化/进化、六核回望。每章以一个人物或争议开场,以一个核心主提问展开,以一句"它让出了什么"收束。 诚实的纪律:所有结论标注 A/B/C 证据等级(A 可查证/可复算,B 稳定但有争议,C 思辨/开放),结论强度不超过证据强度;有争议的实验(小艾伯特、斯坦福监狱、米尔格拉姆)同时给出原始报告与后来的方法学批评;对人物的临床推测一律标 C。附录 F 是可证伪登记簿(20 条主张,逐条给出"什么会推翻它""怎么查""当前状态");附录 G 是数据缺口与四条边界。 边界:本书不提供临床建议,不裁判疗效;"讲述"这一核心不做"揭穿",只做"定价审计";六核不能替代领域知识,也处理不了权力与制度的全部。它明确让出了临床细节、非西方传统、定量证据与制度史,并在附录 G 逐条列出。 版本:2026-10-25,309 页,25 章,25 图,68 表,附录 A—Q;源码与可复现脚本开源,内容 CC BY 4.0,代码 MIT。 本版说明(2026-10-25)。初版。正文采用四层装置(正文/多想一层/再想一层/给专家的注/动手试试);目录为部分—章—节—子节四级;每章附"案例"与"反例"两个子节,用来防止"让出"变成事后编造。附录 A—Q 依次为:流派×六核对照表、一百五十年时间线、术语表、一百个人名、被埋没与重新发现清单、可证伪登记簿、数据缺口、延伸阅读与主题索引、分支地图、精神病理学的另一条线、被主流漏掉的传统、中国心理学一百年、二十种疗法对照、心理学与 AI、十二个常见误解与练习册、十个实验/十次复现/方法手册、二十对易混概念。 系列 / Series. 同一作者的独立研究系列:九本书(六本学术专著 + 两本通俗读本 + 本书)与九篇论文。入口与外部登记库:https://github.com/lyp0746/knowledge-tradeoffs;源码与可复现脚本:https://github.com/lyp0746/mind-forks。首选预览文件:mind-forks-print.pdf(印刷版)。 English. Abstract (English). This is the first popular-science monograph in the author's six-core series: six questions reread 150 years of psychology. Core thesis: the history of psychological schools is neither a chronicle of replacement nor a rehabilitation of the wronged, but a ledger of who drew which line, what was left outside it, and who paid. Every school is an attempt that first draws a line and then decides what to remember, which clock to use, which two of completeness, composability and transfer to keep, who may set the price, and where to put the threshold; the six cores ask what it gave up, not whether it was right. Structure and evidence: 6 parts, 25 chapters, appendices A–Q, 309 pages, 25 vector figures, 68 tables, about 260,000 Chinese characters. Part I (1–4) the birth of the line: Plato to Kant, Wundt, Brentano, James, structuralism/functionalism, Gestalt; Part II (5–11) the price of depth: Freud, Jung, Adler, object relations, self/attachment, Lacan, neuropsychoanalysis, psychometrics; Part III (12–15) the observable constraint: Watson, Pavlov, Skinner, behaviour therapy, the behaviourist legacy; Part IV (16–19) the return of the interior: cognitive revolution, Piaget/Chomsky, cognitive neuroscience, social cognition; Part V (20–22) meaning and time: humanistic, existential, developmental; Part VI (23–25) systems and pricing: systemic/postmodern, CBT/mindfulness/positive/cultural/evolutionary, and a six-core retrospect. Each chapter opens with a person or a controversy, develops one core question, and closes with one sentence on what the school gave up. Discipline: every claim carries an A/B/C grade (A verifiable/recomputable, B stable but contested, C speculative/open) and no conclusion is stronger than its evidence; contested experiments (Little Albert, Stanford Prison, Milgram) are presented with both the original report and later methodological criticism; clinical conjectures about persons are graded C. Appendix F is a falsifiability ledger (20 claims, each with what would refute it, how to check, and current status); Appendix G lists data gaps and four boundaries. Boundaries: the book offers no clinical advice and does not adjudicate efficacy; the "telling" core audits pricing rather than debunking; the six cores do not replace domain knowledge and cannot handle all questions of power and institutions. It explicitly gives up clinical detail, non-Western traditions, systematic quantitative evidence and institutional history, as listed in Appendix G. Edition: 2026-10-25, 309 pages, 25 chapters, 25 figures, 68 tables, appendices A–Q; source and reproducible scripts open, content CC BY 4.0, code MIT. What this edition is (2026-10-25). First edition. The text uses four reader levels (main text / one layer deeper / one more / expert note / hands-on) and a four-level table of contents (part–chapter–section–subsection). Each chapter adds a "case" and a "counterexample" subsection so that "what it gave up" cannot become a post-hoc story. Appendices A–Q are, in order: a school-by-core table, a 150-year timeline, a glossary, one hundred names, a register of buried-and-recovered ideas, a falsifiability ledger, data gaps, further reading with a thematic index, a map of subfields, a second line in psychopathology, marginalized traditions, a century of Chinese psychology, twenty therapies compared, psychology and AI, twelve misconceptions and a workbook, ten experiments / ten replications / a methods handbook, and twenty confusable concept pairs.

items.title: In What Contexts Do Supporters Provide Positive and Negative Responses to Victims of Nonconsensual Intimate Image Abuse?
items.abstract: Nonconsensual intimate image distribution (NCII) occurs when a person's intimate images or videos are shared or shown to others without their consent. Although NCII victimization is common among young adults and many victims disclose their experiences to others, there is a dearth of research examining the reactions victims receive when they disclose or the factors that might contribute to these reactions. Informed by the broader intimate partner and sexual violence literature, the present study examines supporter, victim, and relational factors that might contribute to social reactions to NCII disclosure. Based on attribution theory and victimization perspective theory, we also hypothesize that these supporter, victim, and relational factors may have primarily indirect effects on social reactions through victim empathy, victim blame, and perceptions of confusion and ineffectiveness in helping. Among a sample of 726 undergraduate students who reported receiving disclosures of NCII, positive and negative social reactions were bivariately associated with several supporter, victim/victimization, and relational factors. Consistent with attribution theory and victimization perspective theories, empathy, victim blame, and feelings of confusion/ineffectiveness about helping mediated associations between a range of victim, supporter, and relational characteristics and social reactions to disclosure. Efforts to modify these perceptions of victims and reduce confusion and ineffectiveness in how to respond to survivors could improve disclosure experiences for NCII survivors.

items.title: Why consumers favour or resist foreign brands: A systematic review of antecedents, mechanisms and moderators
items.abstract: Consumers’ orientations towards foreign brands have been studied through separate constructs, including ethnocentrism, xenocentrism, cosmopolitanism, affinity, animosity and country of origin image, yet no review integrates them around purchase intention as a common outcome. This study presents a systematic literature review of 52 peer reviewed studies published between 2012 and 2026, following PRISMA 2020 and supplemented by umbrella review guidance for the meta analyses and reviews included. Predisposition towards foreign brands (PTFB) is used as an organising label and not as an established construct, and the evidence is structured into an Antecedents Mechanisms Moderators (AMM) framework. Antecedents form three clusters: outgroup oriented dispositions (xenocentrism, cosmopolitanism, affinity), ingroup protective dispositions (ethnocentrism and animosity, with patriotism and nationalism acting as distal drivers through ethnocentrism) and image based perceptions (cognitive and affective country image). Brand attitude, perceived quality and value, and consumer disidentification emerge as the main mediating mechanisms. Product category and involvement, national culture, economic development gaps and demographics are the most consistent moderators. The evidence base is largely cross-sectional, and important gaps remain in digital purchasing contexts, longitudinal and experimental designs, xenocentrism in African and Middle Eastern markets, and links with sustainable consumption. The framework offers researchers a basis for theory testing and gives global brand managers guidance on segmentation, localisation and country image positioning.

items.title: Building environmental engagement: Can bridging social-ecological and learning systems theories be a lever for change?
items.abstract: Abstract Pressing sustainability issues are rooted in human and earth systems interactions that are difficult to address because of their complex, dynamic, and unpredictable nature. Addressing these social-ecological challenges requires systems-level change, which relies on both direct improvements to natural systems and indirect drivers of change, such as educational levers. We aim to provoke more transdisciplinary work between environmental scientists and educators by bringing together key constructs from social-ecological and learning systems theories. Writing from the perspective of educators and social scientists, our objectives are to encourage ecologists and other environmental scientists to (1) recognize that learning systems are essential elements of social-ecological ecosystems and (2) embrace their role as keystones within these learning systems, uniquely positioned to drive interest in the environment and support transformative learning. We suggest potential areas of intersection between social-ecological and learning systems, seeking leverage points for transformative change toward more sustainable communities.

items.title: 自由意志的本体论重构:基于相继耦合原理的二阶自返调控解释
items.abstract: 传统哲学中自由意志与决定论的长期对立,根植于心物二元的实体本体论预设:要么将自由意志设定为独立于因果链的精神实体,要么将其消解为物理因果的副现象,二者始终无法在一元本体论框架内实现自洽统一。后世相容论多停留在语义层面的概念调和,始终未能从本体论层面说明自主选择的存在形态与相对独立性来源。 本文以“认知的本质是前后相继”这一不可证伪的第一原理为逻辑起点,依托存在几何化体系的相继耦合本体论框架,从一阶客观耦合、二阶自返耦合的层级生成规则出发,线性推导出自由意志的本体论本质、运作机制与存在边界。本文证明:自由意志并非独立的精神实体,也非对因果律的突破,而是高阶闭合射线簇演化出的二阶自返调控功能;它以模拟预判、定向选择、偏差修正为核心运作方式,天然具备可错性,其核心价值在于通过纠正认知偏差、实现逻辑序列与本真因果序列的1:1对齐,服务于个体稳态的存续与优化。自由意志具备相对的自主调控空间,但不具备脱离相继因果的绝对自由,其本质是高阶稳态对自身因果链条的自觉校准权。这一界定从根源消解了传统自由意志争论的二元困境,为认知科学、心理学、伦理学等领域提供了统一的本体论基础。 The long-standing opposition between free will and determinism in traditional philosophy is rooted in the substance-ontological presupposition of mind-body dualism: either free will is posited as a spiritual entity independent of the causal chain, or it is reduced to an epiphenomenon of physical causation. Neither approach can achieve self-consistent unity within a monistic ontological framework. Later compatibilist theories mostly remain at the level of semantic conceptual reconciliation, failing to account for the existential form and relative independence of autonomous choice at the ontological level. Taking the unfalsifiable first principle that "the nature of cognition is sequential succession" as its logical starting point, this paper draws on the successive coupling ontological framework of the geometrization of existence system, and linearly deduces the ontological essence, operating mechanism and existential boundary of free will based on the hierarchical generation rules of first-order objective coupling and second-order self-reflexive coupling. This paper proves that free will is neither an independent spiritual entity nor a break from the law of causality, but a second-order self-reflexive regulatory function evolved from high-order closed ray clusters. With simulation and prediction, directional selection, and deviation correction as its core operations, it is inherently fallible. Its core value lies in correcting cognitive biases and realizing 1:1 alignment between logical sequences and real causal sequences, so as to serve the persistence and optimization of individual steady states. Free will has a relative space of autonomous regulation but no absolute freedom independent of successive causality; its essence is the conscious calibration right of high-order steady states over their own causal chains. This definition fundamentally resolves the dualistic dilemma in the traditional debate on free will, and provides a unified ontological foundation for cognitive science, psychology, ethics and other fields.

items.title: Effects of Embodied Cognition Through Arts-Based Strategies in Developing Mathematical Competencies of Grade 7 Learners of Leonarda D. Vera Cruz National High School
items.abstract: This study examined the effects of embodied cognition through arts-based strategies on the mathematical competencies of Grade 7 learners at Leonarda D. Vera Cruz National High School, Unisan, Quezon, Philippines. Grounded in Embodied Cognition Theory and an Input–Process–Output–Outcome framework, the study employed a descriptive quasi-experimental, single-group pretest–posttest design involving 26 Grade 7 learners during School Year 2025–2026. Data were collected using a researcher-developed, validated 20-item competency test and analyzed through mean scores, mean percentage scores (MPS), standard deviations, learning gains, and paired-samples t-tests. The intervention incorporated movement, gestures, artistic expression, and kinesthetic activities to develop three mathematical competencies. Results revealed improvements in using positive and negative numbers to describe directions or opposites (38.46% to 73.63%), locating integers on a number line (41.67% to 91.03%), and performing addition and subtraction of integers (19.78% to 58.24%). The respective learning gains were 35.17, 49.36, and 38.46 percentage points, with a reported overall mean gain of 41.00 percentage points. Statistically significant pretest–posttest differences were observed across all competencies (p < .001). Locating integers demonstrated the greatest improvement, while integer operations remained the most challenging competency. The findings supported the development of a Mathematics 7 lesson exemplar integrating arts-based activities, movement, and formative assessments. Although the absence of a comparison group limits causal interpretation, the results suggest that embodied arts-based instruction is a promising approach to strengthening mathematical understanding. The study aligns with Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education) by supporting learner-centered approaches to foundational numeracy. Its educational sustainability contribution lies in providing a structured instructional resource that may support continued teaching improvement and meaningful Mathematics learning.

items.title: EKSPLORASI DAMPAK PERILAKU BULLYING TERHADAP PERKEMBANGAN SOSIAL-EMOSIONAL SISWA SEKOLAH DASAR DI KOTA TERNATE
items.abstract: Masa sekolah dasar merupakan periode penting dalam perkembangan sosial dan emosional anak karena pada tahap ini siswa mulai membangun hubungan pertemanan, belajar bekerja sama, serta mengembangkan konsep diri melalui interaksi dengan teman sebaya. Apabila pada masa tersebut anak mengalami perlakuan bullying secara berulang, maka pengalaman tersebut berpotensi menghambat perkembangan sosial maupun emosionalnya. Oleh karena itu, penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengeksplorasi bentuk-bentuk perilaku bullying yang terjadi di SD Negeri 25 Kota Ternate serta menganalisis dampaknya terhadap perkembangan sosial dan emosional siswa. Metode penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain deskriptif eksploratif. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara mendalam, observasi, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis dengan teknik reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa bentuk perilaku bullying yang paling dominan di SDN 25 Kota Ternate adalah bullying verbal, diikuti oleh bullying relasional (social bullying) dan bullying fisik. Temuan lain menunjukkan bahwa dari bentuk perilaku bullying tersebut ternyata memberikan dampak yang signifikan terhadap perkembangan sosial dan emosional siswa sekolah dasar di Kota Ternate. Rekomendasi penelitian ini ialah diperlukan upaya pencegahan dan penanganan secara kolaboratif melalui penguatan budaya sekolah yang aman, pendidikan karakter berbasis kearifan lokal, keterlibatan orang tua, serta dukungan kebijakan pemerintah daerah untuk menciptakan lingkungan belajar yang bebas dari bullying.

items.title: Explanatory Beliefs, Psychosocial Factors, and Medication Adherence among Adults Living with Schizophrenia in Zimbabwe
items.abstract: Medication adherence remains an important challenge in the long-term management of schizophrenia, particularly in settings where psychological, social and cultural factors may shape how people understand illness and treatment. Explanatory beliefs, social support and stigma may influence treatment-related behaviours, but evidence from Zimbabwe remains limited. This study examined the associations between explanatory beliefs, psychosocial factors and medication adherence among adults living with schizophrenia receiving outpatient psychiatric care in Zimbabwe. A cross-sectional quantitative study was conducted among 96 adults diagnosed with schizophrenia who were receiving outpatient psychiatric care. Participants completed measures assessing explanatory beliefs, medication adherence, perceived social support and stigma, while demographic and clinical information was also collected. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson’s correlation coefficients and multiple linear regression. Medication non-adherence was common, with 59 participants (61.5%) classified as non-adherent and 37 (38.5%) classified as adherent. None of the explanatory belief domains, psychosocial variables or selected demographic and clinical variables showed a statistically significant correlation with medication adherence. In the multivariable regression model, the overall model was not statistically significant, F(8,87) = 1.58, p = .143, and explained 12.7% of the variance in medication adherence (adjusted R² = .047). Biological explanatory beliefs showed the strongest positive association with adherence (B = 0.498, β = .183, p = .076), although this did not reach statistical significance. The findings indicate that the explanatory and psychosocial variables examined in this study did not adequately explain variation in medication adherence in this sample. The relatively modest explanatory power of the regression model also suggests that other factors not examined here may contribute to medication-taking behaviour. The findings support the value of understanding medication adherence within the wider social and cultural context of psychiatric care, while highlighting the need for studies that directly measure broader dimensions of treatment engagement.

items.title: Between Frustration and Dedication: The Influence of Organizational Constraints and Job Satisfaction on Turnover Intention in a Sample of Indonesian Lecturers
items.abstract: This study aimed to analyze the influence of organizational constraints and job satisfaction on the turnover intention of university lecturers in Indonesia. A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed, with data collected via survey from a sample of 77 Indonesian lecturers selected through convenience sampling. Organizational constraints were measured using the Organizational Constraints Scale (OCS), while job satisfaction was assessed using the Job Satisfaction Survey (JSS), and turnover intention was measured using the Turnover Intention Scale (TIS). Hypothesis testing via multiple linear regression analysis revealed a significant simultaneous effect (R² = 0.35; p ≤ 0.05). Individually, organizational constraints were found to have a significant positive influence on turnover intention, while job satisfaction showed a negative though not statistically significant influence. This study is limited by its sample size and sampling technique; therefore, future research should utilize a larger sample collected through randomized sampling. Furthermore, future studies are encouraged to examine the mediating role of organizational constraints in the relationship between job satisfaction and the turnover intention of lecturers.

items.title: Eyegent: Visual Attention Orchestration on Concepts
items.abstract: Abstract Where a human looks is not random, nor is it merely a reflex to visual salience. It is a decision shaped by goals, constrained by language, and driven by the need to resolve uncertainty. We propose Eyegent , an active vision agent built on this premise: that visual search is best understood as sequential Bayesian inference over semantically grounded hypotheses, with fixations serving as epistemic actions. Given an image and a natural-language query, Eyegent constructs a discrete hypothesis space of candidate segmentation masks, maintains an explicit posterior belief distribution, and selects each fixation to maximise expected information gain—updating beliefs via vision–language model verification and terminating when uncertainty falls below a principled risk threshold. We formalise this process as Bayesian Active Semantic Grounding (BASG), a computational-level account that provides formal guarantees on belief concentration, entropy reduction, and bounded decision risk. The framework is neurobiologically grounded in the large-scale network organisation of the human brain, with the Salience Network identified as the dynamic orchestrator of semantic, inferential, and oculomotor processes. Critically, Eyegent requires no gaze supervision and no task-specific training: it is zero-shot, modular, and built entirely from off-the-shelf components. Evaluated on RefCOCO-Gaze and AiR-D, two benchmarks coupling language-driven visual tasks with human eye-tracking ground truth, Eyegent achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance among zero-shot methods across semantic, spatial, and structural scanpath metrics, and approaches supervised baselines on several dimensions. The result is a system that does not merely predict where humans look, but generates scanpaths for the same reason humans generate them: to find out.

items.title: Critical Thinking and Related Cognitive Processes in Career Decision-Making: A Narrative Literature Review
items.abstract: Career decision-making is a complex process involving the selection of educational and career pathways based on an individual’s values, interests, preferences, and available information. Critical thinking has been proposed as a potentially relevant cognitive competence in this process; however, direct empirical evidence of its role in career decision-making remains limited. This study aimed to synthesize empirical evidence on the relationship between critical thinking, related cognitive processes, and career decision-making. A narrative literature review was conducted using systematic search strategies across major bibliographic databases. Seven studies met the inclusion criteria. Only a small proportion of these studies directly examined critical thinking, whereas most investigated related cognitive constructs, including thinking styles, dysfunctional career thoughts, and other cognitive variables. Overall, the findings suggest that critical thinking and related cognitive constructs may be associated with career decision-making outcomes; however, the available evidence is limited, heterogeneous, and predominantly indirect. These findings highlight the need for further research directly examining critical thinking using validated measures and suggest that fostering critical thinking may represent a promising direction for educational and career guidance.

items.title: Energetic feasibility in ecological systems
items.abstract: Ecological communities can persist for long periods despite strong competition and environmental variability, yet they can also reorganize or collapse abruptly after seemingly modest change. Explaining persistence, diversity, and collapse has produced several major traditions in ecology, including species-interaction models, consumer--resource theory, coexistence theory, feasibility analysis, and stability theory. These approaches are often developed separately, even though they all describe systems that capture energy from the environment, redistribute it through ecological interactions, and lose it through metabolism. Here I propose an energetic framework that helps place these traditions in a common language. The central idea is that ecological communities persist only when external energy supply can support both the maintenance of biomass and the losses associated with internal redistribution, while remaining within finite supply and throughput limits. For flux-based ecological models, this perspective yields an exact aggregate balance identity; for other model classes, the mapping is partial or reduced-form and depends on how the system boundary is defined. This framework clarifies why persistence is conditional on energetic compatibility, why enrichment need not always promote persistence, and how feasibility, coexistence, stability, and early warning signals can be interpreted as related aspects of the same underlying constraint. It also shows how finite supply and throughput can bound energetically compatible community states, while superlinear scaling of internal throughput provides one simple special case that yields transparent reduced-form limits on community size and, with additional assumptions, on ecological complexity. More broadly, the framework offers a physically grounded way to connect historically separate areas of ecological theory.

items.title: Contextualizing Islamic Ecotheology through Sasak, Samawa, and Mbojo Cultural Practices for Nature Conservation in West Nusa Tenggara
items.abstract: How Islamic ecotheological principles acquire culturally specific meanings and expressions in environmental conservation remains insufficiently understood, particularly across ethnocultural communities sharing a broader religious and regional context. This study examines the contextualization of Islamic ecotheology through Sasak, Samawa, and Mbojo cultural values and practices in West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. A qualitative interpretive multi-site design was employed, involving 30 informants equally distributed across the three communities. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, three focus-group discussions involving previously interviewed participants, direct observation, and document analysis. Data were analyzed through thematic interpretation, hermeneutic analysis, and cross-cultural comparison. The findings indicate that khalifah, amanah, mizan, and the prohibition of fasad provide shared ethical orientations emphasizing environmental responsibility and ecological balance. Among the Sasak, awiq-awiq reflects customary arrangements associated with natural-resource protection, while Samawa values, including Larap, Saling Sadu, and Saling Puji, and the Mbojo philosophy of Mori ro Mada provide culturally situated interpretations of collective responsibility. However, empirical evidence supporting specific Samawa and Mbojo conservation functions remains less direct than that supporting Sasak customary arrangements. The study proposes a religious–cultural translation framework comprising normative orientation, cultural interpretation, institutional mediation, and ecological enactment. This framework explains culturally embedded environmental responsibilities without establishing causal relationships or independently measured conservation outcomes.

items.title: A political ecology of reforestation in the Peruvian Andes: a field study of tree species and institutional dynamics
items.abstract: Deforestation is a widespread problem in the Andes Mountains of Peru. Reforestation is an important tool to increase the production of wood and as a means to promote conservation objectives. Since the 1960s, and promoted by government incentives, eucalyptus tree planting has expanded rapidly throughout the region. The benefits of eucalyptus are that it grows quickly, provides fuel for cooking and heating, and is a source of income and employment. Over the past three decades, there has been a shift toward pine plantations, supposedly as a higher-income and less-damaging alternative to eucalyptus. However, there are serious questions about the environmental impacts of both of these introduced species. More recently, the Peruvian government and NGOs have also been supporting reforestation with native tree species as a means to restore fragile and biodiverse Andean ecosystems. The purpose of this research is to critically examine the reforestation efforts in the Andean highlands near Cusco, Peru. The theoretical framework draws on political ecology to assess the ecological, political, economic, and organizational factors that influence the decision to plant trees and whether exotic or native species are chosen. Data for this paper is based on field research conducted in Peru. We interviewed representatives from three levels of the Peruvian government, two environmental NGOs, and businesses that sell and use wood. We also include a case study of an Indigenous agriculturalist community that has extensively reforested areas. The results highlight the dynamics between the various development actors, including the state, NGOs, industry, and rural communities. They reveal a tension between the goals of conservation and human livelihoods and the role of trade-offs. We conclude there is room for a variety of work done by different organizations in different places. We also emphasize that sustainability requires a community-centered approach to development that focuses on strong relationships and capacity building.

items.title: Natural forests are key for bryophyte conservation, while active land-use reveals homogenous communities with low richness, new records, and habitat indicators in the Eastern Amazon
items.abstract: Abstract The implementation of strategies that integrate land use with biodiversity conservation has never been more urgent in the Brazilian Amazon. Here, we compared the effects of land-use types characterized by family farming and low-intensity management systems on the community structure of bryophytes and their lineages (liverworts and mosses) in the Eastern Amazon. We evaluated bryophyte communities across natural forest and three active land-use types: managed forest, agroforestry, and açaí monoculture. We analyzed bryophyte richness, abundance and composition, as well as species associations with each land-use type. Natural forest and active land-use types differed in bryophyte composition, whereas natural forest and agroforestry exhibited similar species richness and abundance. Among active land-use types, no significant differences in bryophyte abundance were observed. Agroforestry and managed forest exhibited similar bryophyte composition, but species richness was lower in managed forest. Açaí monoculture exhibit difference in bryophyte composition between all land-use types. Liverworts and mosses exhibited different responses to the land-use types, with liverworts exhibited similar patterns to the total bryophytes and more sensitive to the habitat change, whereas mosses were more resilient. Thus, liverworts may be a practical group for monitoring the ecological effects of land-use practices, while Cololejeunea surinamensis and Prionolejeunea muricatosserulata showed potential as indicators of natural forest conditions. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of maintaining natural forests and promoting low-intensity land-use systems, particularly agroforestry, to conserve bryophyte community structure in Amazonian landscapes.

items.title: Setting Sweden’s route to Paris: designing policy instruments for climate mitigation in forestry
items.abstract: Abstract The role of forest ecosystems in mitigating climate change has gained increasing prominence in international climate negotiations, particularly within the Paris Agreement and in the strategies and regulations of the European Union. This paper aims to enhance ongoing policy discussions on how Swedish forests can support climate mitigation goals by identifying which policy instruments, incentives, and climate strategies forest stakeholders prioritize, while advancing social science understandings of governance, stakeholder participation, and the socio-political conditions shaping forest management. Specifically, we examined the acceptance of, and perceived need for, alternative policy instruments designed to accelerate the climate transition through three novel mitigation scenarios for Swedish forestry. These scenarios explore the allocation of responsibility for achieving climate targets – whether it rests primarily with the state, the market, or individual landowners. Our findings draw on two participatory workshops involving 27 stakeholders and rightsholders engaged in Swedish forest management. The results reveal significant challenges in management and policy, particularly regarding responsibility for climate mitigation, justice claims, and power sharing. Furthermore, they underscore the need for stronger policy integration across sectors and administrative levels, as well as innovative policy instruments to facilitate the implementation of forest-climate objectives. We call on policy makers to reassess the current forest policy framework, extend policy instruments targeting climate mitigation, and support landowners who are prepared to contribute to the objectives outlined in the Paris Agreement.

items.title: Integrated microbiome and metabolomic analysis reveals associations between vaginal microbiota composition and psychological profiles
items.abstract: The vaginal microbiota plays a key role in women’s health and is increasingly linked to psychobiological processes, although underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study investigated the relationship between vaginal community state types (CSTs), psychological dimensions, and vaginal metabolites in 105 reproductive-aged women. Vaginal microbiota composition was characterised through 16 S rRNA gene sequencing and classified into CSTs; metabolomic profiling was performed using NMR spectroscopy. Participants completed validated questionnaires assessing trait anxiety, emotion regulation, behavioural inhibition/activation, depressive symptoms, perceived stress, and somatisation. Women with polymicrobial CST IV profiles showed significantly lower Behavioural Activation System (BAS)-Reward Responsiveness and BAS-Drive scores, whereas those with Lactobacillus iners -dominated CST III exhibited lower Behavioural Inhibition System (BIS) scores. Limited direct correlations between bacterial taxa and psychological variables emerged, but psychological dimensions strongly correlated with specific vaginal metabolites. Exploratory mediation analyses indicated that aminobutyrate and valine partially or fully mediated the associations between CST IV and BAS dimensions, while phenylalanine partially mediated the relationship between CST IV and BIS inhibition. These findings suggest that the vaginal metabolome may represent a functional interface linking microbial community structure and psychological functioning, supporting a biopsychosocial perspective of vaginal health and the importance of integrating microbiome, metabolomic, and psychological assessments in women’s health research.

items.title: Partitioning patterns of fish and sea urchin herbivory from tropical to temperate reefs
items.abstract: Abstract Herbivory can structure vegetation and affect the states of sunlit ecosystems. On shallow tropical and temperate reefs, herbivory can inhibit macroalgal dominance and promote turf-dominated benthic states. However, standardised comparisons of tropical and temperate herbivory are primarily focussed on fish, leaving the relative contributions of sea urchins poorly understood. Here, we examined thermal realm (tropical vs temperate) and depth (2, 5, 8 and 12-m) effects on relative herbivory patterns and herbivore distributions, using standardised macroalgal assays (N = 1,340) and underwater visual surveys (N = 67 surveys) at 49 sites across six locations spanning approximately 29° of latitude in eastern Australia. Assays were deployed to partition the relative intensity of herbivory using two partitioning treatments: 1) assays were suspended above the benthos allowing only fish consumption (water-column herbivory), and 2) assays were laid flat on the benthos enabling fish and urchin consumption (benthic herbivory). Assay results showed higher fish herbivory on tropical reefs than on temperate reefs, whereas relative benthic herbivory did not differ between thermal realms. Variation in assay consumption across depth was limited. Results from assays and surveys aligned, with higher herbivorous fish abundance on tropical reefs and higher urchin abundance on temperate reefs. Relative patterns in fish and urchin herbivory between thermal realms underscores differences in how herbivory occurs and where in the water-column it predominates, highlighting a key axis of variation for tropicalizing reefs.

items.title: Seed balls with bauxite mining technosol: an alternative forest restoration technique in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest
items.abstract: Abstract This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of technosol, composed of clay cake and organic compost, as a substrate for seed balls using native species from the Atlantic Forest. We investigated how different substrate compositions and the addition of NPK fertilizer influence the emergence, survival, and growth of four native tree species: Senna macranthera , Enterolobium contortisiliquum , Pterogyne nitens , and Anadenanthera peregrina . Seedling emergence and survival were monitored continuously over 190 days, and growth performance was evaluated using logistic growth models. The results showed that, in terms of emergence and survival, treatments without NPK addition yielded the best outcomes, regardless of the proportion of clay cake and organic compost. Growth models revealed that non-pioneer species ( P. nitens and A. peregrina ) performed better under treatments without NPK, while pioneer species ( S. macranthera and E. contortisiliquum ) exhibited higher growth rates in treatments with NPK. These findings emphasize the importance of aligning substrate composition and fertilization with the ecological strategies of different species to optimize restoration outcomes. The use of technosol-based seed balls derived from bauxite mining represents a viable alternative for forest restoration, promoting biodiversity recovery, reducing waste disposal in tailings dams, and contributing to circular economy principles in the mining sector.

items.title: Analysing resource management outcomes: an actor-centred power approach
items.abstract: This paper presents an adapted methodological Interest-Power-Outcome (IPO) framework for analysing environmental resource management outcomes by integrating the Actor-Centred Power (ACP) framework with Qualitative Comparative Analysis (QCA). The framework aims to analyse how actors involved in resource management use their power in pursuit of specific interests, and how their interventions on the ground can either align with or diverge from intended policy outcomes in a resource system. The QCA is applied to the analytical features of actors, interests, power resources, and power application in a given resource management context, regardless of sample size, to provide data-informed outcome analysis for sustainable resource management. The method was pretested through an empirical case study of the mangrove reforestation program, in which 13 local-level cases were comparatively analysed. The results show that 77 % of actors' interest-oriented cases aligned with the policy goal of improving mangrove forest cover; however, the remaining cases are unlikely to achieve the intended outcomes. The analysis further identifies the causes of failed outcomes and provides clear pathways for improving future strategies. The analytical framework is intended to apply to the content-specific cases within broader environmental resource management.

items.title: Implementation Processes and Mediating Factors in Agricultural Support Programmes: Evidence from Zambia's Transition from FISP to CASP
items.abstract: Background: Agricultural input subsidy programmes remain central to food security policy in sub-Saharan Africa, yet persistent implementation failures undermine their effectiveness. Zambia's Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP), a major intervention reaching over one million smallholder households, has faced chronic challenges in timely delivery, equitable targeting, and digital access through its e-voucher system. As Zambia transitions from FISP to the Comprehensive Agriculture Support Programme (CASP), understanding these implementation barriers is critical for designing more effective support. This article examines the implementation processes of FISP in a remote rural context and identifies the institutional, socio-economic, and environmental factors that mediate programme effectiveness. Methods: The study employed a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design. Quantitative data were collected from 300 households (150 FISP beneficiaries and 150 non-beneficiaries) in Kawimbe ward, Mbala District, Northern Province, using structured questionnaires measuring e-voucher functionality, input timeliness, accessibility, targeting fairness, and mediating factors. Qualitative data were gathered through 15 key informant interviews with agricultural officers, agro-dealers, traditional leaders, and cooperative leaders, and 12 focus group discussions stratified by gender and beneficiary status. Data were analysed using logistic regression, hierarchical regression, mediation analysis, and thematic analysis. Results: Implementation failures were pervasive. Only 34% of beneficiaries received inputs on time, with mean delays of 3.4 weeks. E-voucher functionality challenges affected 52% of beneficiaries, and agro-dealer stock-outs affected 55%. Female-headed households comprised only 14% of beneficiaries despite constituting 22% of farming households. Geographic location (distance to agro-dealer) and female-headed household status were significant predictors of late delivery (AOR=1.15 per km, p=0.003; AOR=2.84, p=0.006, respectively). Cooperative membership was protective (AOR=0.42, p=0.014). Thematic analysis revealed five major themes: "The Digital Entitlement Gap," "The Proximity Penalty," "Gendered Exclusion," "Elite Capture and Political Interference," and "The Timeliness-Yield Connection." Conclusion: Implementation failures in FISP reflect systemic transfer entitlement failures that disproportionately affect remote and female-headed households. These findings provide critical evidence for designing CASP with decentralised logistics, multiple delivery channels, gender-sensitive targeting, mobile distribution points, and strengthened community oversight. Addressing these mediating factors is essential for ensuring that agricultural support programmes achieve their intended food security outcomes in remote rural contexts.

items.title: Soil Biogeochemical Cycles and Their Influence on Crop-Environment Dynamics in Changing Climates
items.abstract: Soil biogeochemical cycles regulate nutrient availability, soil organic matter dynamics, greenhouse-gas exchange, and crop productivity, but their functioning is increasingly modified by climate change. This review synthesizes the major processes controlling carbon (C), nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), sulfur (S), and silicon (Si) cycling in agricultural soils and examines how these interconnected cycles influence soil-crop-environment relationships under changing climatic conditions. Warming, drought, excessive soil moisture, altered precipitation, and elevated atmospheric CO2 can modify microbial activity, organic-matter turnover, nutrient mineralization and immobilization, redox conditions, nutrient losses, and greenhouse-gas emissions. Their effects are strongly context dependent and vary with soil texture, pH, organic-matter content, drainage, microbial communities, crop type, and management. The review further evaluates how plant nutrient acquisition, rhizosphere processes, and plant-soil-microbial feedbacks connect biogeochemical cycling with crop performance and environmental outcomes. Conservation agriculture, organic amendments, biochar, and microbial inoculants may improve nutrient retention and soil resilience, but their effectiveness depends on soil, climate, amendment properties, and management history and may involve agronomic or environmental trade-offs. We identify major knowledge gaps concerning interactions among elemental cycles, responses to compound climate extremes, microbial regulation of nutrient transformations, and the transferability of management practices across agroecosystems. Integrating long-term field experiments, process-based modelling, molecular approaches, and high-resolution soil monitoring will be essential for developing climate-resilient nutrient-management strategies.

items.title: Habitat integrity and canopy cover shape small-scale variation in coloration among odonate assemblages in Neotropical streams
items.abstract: Abstract Small aquatic ecosystems, such as Amazonian igarapés, harbor high biodiversity composed of organisms essential for ecosystem functioning. Dragonflies and damselflies (Odonata) are abundant and sensitive to habitat alterations, making them useful indicators of environmental conditions. Their conspicuous diversity and coloration patterns support behavioral strategies and thermoregulation, communication, and protection against solar radiation and water loss. In this study, we evaluated whether environmental gradients influence Odonata species distribution in Eastern Amazonian streams through selection on coloration traits. Specifically, we tested (i) whether local environmental conditions are associated with assemblage-level variation in non-circular coloration traits (Saturation, Value, melanin coverage, and wax-derived pruinescence coverage); and (ii) whether species composition varies along gradients of habitat integrity and canopy cover. We sampled 25 streams and analyzed 213 individuals from 32 species/morphospecies. Using standardized photographs, we quantified body coloration in the HSV colour space (Hue, Saturation, and Value) and estimated melanin and pruinescence coverage. We analyzed community-weighted means of Saturation, Value, melanin coverage, and pruinescence coverage; we used Hue descriptively. Saturation and Value declined with habitat integrity; Value increased with canopy cover, whereas pruinescence coverage decreased. Melanin coverage showed no clear environmental association. More shaded streams unexpectedly supported assemblages with higher Value, and species composition varied with habitat integrity. These findings suggest that distinct coloration components, together with other physiological traits, may help shape fine-scale Odonata community composition along microclimatic gradients. Coloration may complement occurrence and abundance data in environmental assessment, pending experimental validation of the mechanisms involved.

items.title: Regenerative Habitation: Integrating Architecture, Adaptive Furniture, and Productive Landscapes
items.abstract: This preprint defines an implementation-oriented framework for regenerative habitation: the coordinated design of architecture, adaptive furniture, environmental technology, native habitat, diversified food production, and task-specific embodied robotics as one environment for human life and ecological continuity. The design question is how built environments can provide shelter and comfort while making ecological processes and voluntary participation accessible in ordinary life. Shared Cognitive Ecology describes the exchange among environmental information, spatial access, human activity, and ecological change. Environmental Coherence evaluates these relationships across ecological, architectural, material, technological, operational, and human domains. The paper synthesizes research on crop rotation, native urban planting, community gardens, agricultural human-robot collaboration, food life-cycle impacts, and land-use trade-offs. A 2024 review of 55 agricultural human-robot collaboration studies found that 34 met its criteria for robust collaboration and noted limited field and human-factor evidence; a 2025 review mapped 210 studies on agricultural robotics and extended reality. These findings inform design questions, but neither literature establishes performance for a residential or civic habitat. Evidence on land use and life-cycle impacts also establishes limits: food production can increase irrigation demand, material impacts, or habitat pressure. This conceptual synthesis defines a cross-scale model, operating method, measurable evaluation domains, and comparative civic prototype for future study. Ecological literacy, labor reduction, well-being, food output, biodiversity, and human-robot performance remain to be tested through baseline and longitudinal evaluation. Keywords: regenerative habitation; adaptive furniture; shared cognitive ecology; environmental coherence; productive landscapes; native biodiversity; urban agriculture; ecological restoration; human-robot collaboration; embodied robotics; integrated habitat systems

items.title: The Structure of Reality: Recognition, Necessity, and Physical Prediction
items.abstract: A comparison is a physical occurrence. It needs something to compare, an operation that uses both terms, and a state in which its result can matter to what happens next. If the result is measured, the measurement needs a reference. If it is retained, the record needs a carrier. If the operation transfers energy, that energy must appear in the same account. This book asks how much of physical structure is fixed by those demands. Recognition Science begins with the distinctions already exhibited by actual operations and follows their consequences. Its central arguments remove alternatives: a conserved comparison selects a quadratic reading; its residual and reference fix a normalized cost; preservation of additive comparisons, together with a first costly join, fixes golden scaling. A retained linking observation selects three spatial dimensions under its stated realization conditions. Further constructions ask how the resulting source evolves, transfers energy and leaves records. The argument is technical because the alternatives matter. A theorem that selects one cost from a specified class says exactly which other costs fail and why. Changing the class can change the conclusion. A Hamiltonian that acts on a full field carrier establishes more than a finite matrix calculation, while an exact matrix compression remains useful at its own scope. The reader should be able to identify the physical objects, inspect the hypotheses and follow the reason for each conclusion.

items.title: Mobile Learning in Mathematics Education: Trends, Thematic Clusters, Pedagogical Approaches, and Implementation Challenges
items.abstract: Research on mobile learning in mathematics education continues to grow, yet empirical evidence on its actual classroom implementation remains limited. This study aims to comprehensively map the development, knowledge structure, pedagogical approaches, and implementation challenges of mobile learning in mathematics education. The conceptual framework integrates bibliometric analysis and thematic analysis as complementary approaches for understanding the research landscape both quantitatively and qualitatively. The study employed a hybrid review combining bibliometric analysis of 375 publications and thematic analysis of 50 high-quality studies selected from an initial pool of 707 Scopus-indexed records. The findings reveal that mobile learning develops across four main thematic clusters, is dominated by constructivist pedagogical approaches, and faces multi-layered systemic barriers centered on institutional, pedagogical, and individual readiness. Successful implementation is determined by the alignment among technology, instructional design, teacher capacity, and the broader educational ecosystem. These findings provide implications for researchers in identifying future research directions, for educators in designing effective mobile learning environments, and for policymakers in developing comprehensive strategies that support sustainable and equitable mobile learning implementation in mathematics education.

items.title: Ensemble quantile-based deep learning framework for streamflow and flood prediction in Australian catchments
items.abstract: Abstract In recent years, climate extremes such as floods have created significant environmental and economic hazards for Australia. Deep learning methods have been promising for predicting extreme climate events; however, large flooding events present a critical challenge due to factors such as model calibration and missing data. We present an ensemble quantile-based deep learning framework that addresses large-scale streamflow forecasts using quantile regression for uncertainty projections in prediction. We evaluate selected univariate and multivariate deep learning models and catchment strategies. We implement a multistep time-series prediction model using the CAMELS dataset for selected catchments across Australia. The ensemble model employs a set of quantile deep learning models for streamflow determined by historical streamflow data. We utilise the streamflow prediction and obtain flood probability using flood frequency analysis and compare it with historical flooding events for selected catchments. Our results demonstrate notable efficacy and uncertainties in streamflow forecasts with varied catchment properties. Our flood probability estimates show good accuracy in capturing the historical floods from the selected catchments. This underscores the potential for our deep learning framework to revolutionise flood forecasting across diverse regions and be implemented as an early warning system.

items.title: Arabert with Graph Attention for Imbalanced Arabic Sentiment Classification: An Ablation Study of Fusion Strategies
items.abstract: Purpose: This study examines whether combining AraBERT with a Graph Attention Network (GAT) over a semantic text graph improves three-class classification. Design/Methodology/Approach: Experiments were conducted on hotel reviews (HARD, 392,512 texts) and book reviews (LABR, 59,620 texts). Both corpora are imbalanced in almost identical proportions — negative 13.06%, neutral 19.92%, positive 67.01% in HARD, and 13.13%, 19.47%, 67.40% in LABR. A stratified 70/15/15 split preserves these proportions, giving evaluation partitions of 58,878 and 8,944 reviews, respectively. We compared four configurations: AraBERT alone (M1), a frozen encoder feeding the graph network (M2), a fine-tuned encoder whose sentence representation is replaced by the pooled graph states (M3), and a fine-tuned encoder whose pooled graph states are fused with the retained CLS representation (M4). Each configuration was trained with three seeds on a fixed stratified split. Research Limitation: The paired t-test over three seeds does not reach significance in either corpus. Findings: On LABR, M4 obtained the highest F1-Macro (0.6263 ± 0.0036 against 0.6226 ± 0.0036 for M1), and McNemar's test was significant in two of the three seeds. On HARD, the ordering was reversed (0.8337 ± 0.0040 for M1 against 0.8304 ± 0.0028 for M4). M3 did not exceed the baseline, and M2 fell clearly below it. Practical Implication: Establishing a clearer benefit will require a more precise graph, in particular one derived from syntactic parsing rather than lexical matching, and a tighter form of integration than the concatenation used here. Social Implication: Sentiment analysis is a natural language processing technique which seeks to determine whether the expressed sentiment is positive, negative or neutral so that an institution/researcher can gain insights from a large set of unstructured data. Originality/Value: The study isolates the manner of combination rather than the presence of the graph: fusing the pooled graph states with the retained CLS representation improves on the baseline, whereas substituting them for it does not, a distinction not previously separated for Arabic document-level sentiment.

items.title: When to Use t Test, ANOVA, ANCOVA, MANOVA, and MANCOVA: A Step-by-Step Guide for Novice Educational Researchers
items.abstract: Selecting an appropriate statistical test remains a challenge for novice educational researchers, particularly when distinguishing among parametric procedures with different requirements and analytical purposes. This paper provides a practical guide for selecting the t-test, ANOVA, ANCOVA, MANOVA, and MANCOVA in quantitative educational research. The guide begins with hypothesis testing and variable classification, followed by normality assessment and consideration of data transformation before selecting the appropriate statistical procedure. Each test is explained according to its purpose, assumptions, research question, types, decision criteria, and interpretation. The paper emphasizes the necessity of choosing statistical tests based on the research hypothesis structure, number of groups, dependent variables, and covariates, rather than by familiarity with statistical software. The guide is designed to assist novice education researchers to make sound statistical choices and improve the validity and interpretability of their quantitative research results.

items.title: Exploring the Relationship between AI Competency and Professional Identity in Language Education: A Mixed-methods Study
items.abstract: The integration of artifi cial intelligence (AI) in education is increasingly prevalent; however, the implications of AI competency forprofessional identity remain underexplored. Building on Sociocultural Theory and Possible Selves Theory, this convergent mixed-methods study examines the relationship between AI competency and instructor characteristics with professional identity among 111Turkish EFL instructors. Validated scales measuring AI competency and professional identity were administered alongside semi-structured interviews with 12 participants. Quantitative analyses revealed that AI competency signifi cantly predicts professionalidentity (β = .295, p = .002). Prior AI exposure markedly diff erentiated competency levels, while age and teaching experience had nosignifi cant eff ect. Qualitative fi ndings identifi ed three identity trajectories (strengthening, neutrality, and questioning) shaped by beliefs,emotions, institutional support, and instructional experience. We propose a novel interpretive mapping of these trajectories onto thehoped-for, expected, and feared dimensions of professional self-representation, off ering a theoretically parsimonious lens forunderstanding why instructors with equivalent AI competency levels exhibit divergent identity responses. The study highlights theimportance of professional development that goes beyond technical training to include guided, refl ective, and emotionally resonantexploration connecting AI skills with pedagogical values and ethical awareness.
