items.title: Social and psychological factors shaping public views of unconventional climate advocates
items.abstract: Abstract Climate communication faces a messenger challenge: while the urgency of climate crisis demands broad-based public engagement, conventional advocates who are left-leaning environmentalists often struggle to reach diverse audiences due to identity-based barriers and negative stereotypes. This study examines “unconventional advocates”: individuals or groups who advocate for climate action from within social identities not typically associated with environmentalism. Through public intercept interviews with 90 Australians across urban and regional areas, we identified five interrelated social and psychological factors shaping public evaluations of these atypical climate messengers: identification, surprise, group importance, trustworthiness, and legitimacy. Our findings reveal that public views of unconventional advocates are shaped not only by identity alignment, but also by broader stereotype-based expectations, perceived credibility and legitimacy, and the wider socio-political meanings attached to different groups. These findings advance theoretical understandings of social identity, impression formation, and climate communication, while informing practical strategies in climate advocacy to broaden the social base of support for climate action.

items.title: ¿Una tomadura de pelo? Socialización cultural, práctica artística y adhesión a una creencia deslegitimadora sobre la pintura moderna en España
items.abstract: Este artículo analiza la adhesión a la afirmación de que la pintura moderna es una «tomadura de pelo» y que, en muchos casos, podría realizarla un niño. El ítem se conceptualiza como una creencia deslegitimadora compuesta, compatible con juicios sobre habilidad, esfuerzo, intención o autoridad cultural, pero no como una medida inequívoca de negación del estatuto artístico. Se emplean los microdatos del estudio Cultura y estilos de vida del Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas (Estudio 3476, 2024). La muestra comprende 3.493 personas. Se estiman modelos logísticos ordinales anidados y, al incumplirse parcialmente la proporcionalidad, un modelo de probabilidades proporcionales parciales, contrastado mediante sensibilidades. El 34,8 % de la muestra total ponderada expresa acuerdo con la afirmación. La socialización cultural propia y la práctica de pintar, dibujar o esculpir presentan estimaciones no concluyentes; los resultados parentales y religiosos dependen de la especificación. En cambio, una participación más amplia se asocia con menor adhesión, mientras que las posiciones ideológicas de centro y derecha se asocian con mayor adhesión. La desigualdad educativa se atenúa al incorporar participación e ideología. Los resultados describen asociaciones condicionadas, sin demostrar irrelevancia de la socialización ni identificar mediación causal, y delimitan el alcance explicativo de un único ítem compuesto.

items.title: Increased screen exposure predicts faster orienting and prolonged distraction in infancy
items.abstract: Screen exposure is linked with attention difficulties in childhood. Yet, little is known about how different forms of screen exposure relate to specific attentional processes, namely, endogenous and exogenous attention, during infancy, a period characterized by rapid attentional development and increased sensitivity to environmental experiences. The present study addressed this gap by examining the association between screen time, background television exposure, and early attention. A total of 110 typically developing infants aged 9–16 months participated in the study. Infants completed an anti-saccade task and a distractibility task to measure exogenous and endogenous attention. Mothers reported infants’ daily screen time and background television exposure at home. Linear mixed-effects models showed that greater screen time and background television exposure predicted faster orienting to salient stimuli (i.e., heightened exogenous attention) and prolonged distraction (i.e., reduced endogenous attention). When modeled simultaneously, background television exposure remained significantly associated with faster orienting, while increased screen time remained significantly associated with prolonged distraction. These findings suggest that infants’ screen media environments may be differentially associated with specific attentional processes. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of considering both direct and background screen exposure when examining early attention development.

items.title: Developmental paths of reading skills during lower secondary education: associations with literacy-related emotions and psychological well-being
items.abstract: Abstract This study investigates developmental paths of reading fluency and comprehension among adolescents in lower secondary education. Furthermore, we examined the association between these paths, literacy-related emotions and psychological well-being. This longitudinal study’s sample ( n = 1,035, 55% girls) comprised Finnish adolescents (mean age = 13.79, SD = 0.35 at the outset) in Grades 7 and 9. The participants’ reading fluency and comprehension were measured using standardized tests, while literacy-related emotions and psychological well-being were measured via self-reports. Research questions were analyzed using latent profile analysis. Three developmental paths of reading skills were found: (1) low reading comprehension and low and slowly increasing reading fluency (11%), (2) average-increasing reading comprehension and fluency (59%) and (3) high reading comprehension and high-increasing reading fluency (30%). Adolescents on Path 3 reported higher literacy-related enjoyment, hope, and pride and lower literacy-related anger, anxiety, hopelessness, and shame than adolescents on other paths. No differences between paths were found in life satisfaction, but adolescents on Developmental path 1 and 3 reported a higher level of depressive symptoms than adolescents on Path 2, and their symptoms increased faster from Grade 7 to 9. Reading skills continue to develop during adolescence, and the development follows heterogenous paths. A nonlinear connection exists between reading skills and depressive symptoms, which would be important to consider in the efforts to support adolescent reading skills and well-being. The results suggest that both adolescents with particularly low and high reading skills are vulnerable to increased depressive symptoms.

items.title: The perceived utility and scope of ecological momentary assessment and interventions for non-suicidal self-injury: A needs-based dynamic risk perspective
items.abstract: Background Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is characterized by rapid within-person fluctuations in thoughts and urges. Yet, treatments rely on retrospective and static approaches for assessments and interventions. Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) and Ecological Momentary Interventions (EMIs) may enable more dynamic support in real time. This study examined the perceived utility and scope of these new digital modalities from the perspectives of treatment-seeking individuals and mental health professionals. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 30 treatment-seeking individuals engaging in NSSI, after completing a four-week EMA period, and with 14 professionals who used EMA in treatment. Interviews explored experiences with EMA and perspectives on EMIs and were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Three themes were identified. First, EMA and EMIs were perceived as extending therapeutic support by enhancing awareness, reflection, and skill use in daily life. Second, participants emphasized that EMIs must be tailored to changing needs in function of changing risk. This informed the development of a Needs-Based Dynamic Risk and Intervention Model for NSSI, distinguishing needs and interventions through a traffic-light analogy across resilient (i.e., mental health promotion), emerging risk (i.e., vulnerability regulation), and high risk (i.e., behavioral interruption) states. Third, EMIs were viewed as valuable when embedded in blended care and implemented through shared decision-making, balancing system- and user-initiated support. Conclusion Integrating EMA and EMIs into treatment has potential to provide needs-tailored support for individuals who self-injure. Future work should focus on empirically validating the proposed dynamic model and co-designing EMI components that address fluctuating needs in daily life.

items.title: The Hidden Harmony Between Music and Applied Psychology: Theoretical Frameworks, Neurobiological Substrates, and Clinical Innovations
items.abstract: This study looks at the underlying structural and functional connections, termed the Hidden Harmony, between musical creation and applied psychology. Historic studies have seen music mostly as an aesthetic stimulus or a general palliative; however, modern advancements in neuroscience and clinical psychology show that music is a specific, multi-dimensional modulator of human emotion, cognition, autonomic function, and behavior. This thorough study examines how basic music components, that is, tempo, rhythm, harmony, timbre, and melodic contour, fit into real-world psychological models. More especially, we look at how musical mechanics, Neurologic Music Therapy (NMT) and organizational psychology, converge with Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT). This article clarifies the structural design that makes music the best means for psychological reorganization, emotional control, and neurorehabilitation by combining recent empirical meta-analyses, psychophysiological data, and neuroimaging studies. Finally, the article describes the main limits of present approaches and presents a set of open questions and future research views to direct the next generation of quantitative, interdisciplinary studies.

items.title: Bridging local craftsmanship and formal geometry in a rural Colombian classroom
items.abstract: This study evaluates a teaching unit based on an ethnomathematical approach, utilizing the cultural knowledge of crafting reed mats to promote metric and geometric thinking. This qualitative study, following an Action Research model, was conducted with 9 fifth-grade students at IED Euclides Lizarazo (Magdalena, Colombia). The intervention adopted an ethnomathematical didactic approach, structured in two interconnected phases: an ethnographic phase, to systematize the mathematical knowledge of three local artisans; and an educational phase, where the teaching unit was implemented using a parallel and comparative teaching method. The results reveal that, starting from a solid cultural knowledge base, students showed heterogeneous progression. A gap was evidenced between the conceptual understanding of measurement and its procedural execution; however, a group of students achieved advanced formal mathematization in geometry. The majority demonstrated sophisticated strategic-numerical thinking. In this regard, the ethnomathematical approach proved effective in connecting local and academic knowledge within a meaningful context.

items.title: Altered brain-body activity during emotional mental imagery in major depressive disorder
items.abstract: Abstract Major depressive disorder (MDD) has been associated with alterations in emotional processing, brain activity, and autonomic regulation, potentially reflecting impaired coordination between neural and autonomic systems. This study examined whether these alterations are more clearly reflected in distinct measures of brain activity or autonomic nervous system measures (HRV) during emotional mental imagery and investigated associations with mood and cognitive functioning. Therefore, thirty-seven healthy controls and 35 patients with MDD completed an auditory-guided imagery paradigm including positive, negative, neutral, and abstract conditions during EEG and ECG recording. EEG data were analyzed using event-related potentials (ERP), spectral power, and event-related synchronization/desynchronization (ERS/ERD), alongside heart rate variability (HRV) indices derived from ECG. All participants completed mood questionnaires and cognitive assessments. Patients showed higher depressive symptom severity, more negative current mood, and reduced executive performance. Further group differences emerged in alpha, gamma, and delta bands, whereas ERP amplitudes did not differ between groups. Altered neural oscillations were associated with reduced cognitive efficiency and greater depressive symptom severity. HRV measures indicated higher sympathetic nervous system and stress indices in patients, suggesting altered autonomic regulation. Importantly, correlations between delta ERS/ERD activity and HRV indices were observed in healthy controls but not in patients with MDD. These findings suggest that depression-related alterations are more strongly reflected in neural oscillations and autonomic regulation than basic emotional response patterns. Neural and autonomic markers may therefore provide clinically relevant information on cognitive difficulties, stress regulation, and disrupted brain–body interactions in MDD.

items.title: Should Coffee Consumers Not Have Their Habitual Morning Coffee Before Testing Their Cognitive Functions?
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Caffeine could improve cognitive functions, but study protocols usually prohibit drinking coffee before cognitive testing. However, regular coffee consumers may experience withdrawal effects when they cannot drink their habitual coffee, which may impair cognitive performance. Therefore, we tested the effects of overnight coffee abstinence in regular coffee consumers: once allowing to drink their coffee and once not drinking coffee. The cognitive performance was compared with non-regular coffee consumers. METHODS: Thirty regular coffee consumers (RCCs) and 25 non-regular consumers (N-RCCs) took part in this study. RCCs were tested after their habitual morning coffee (c-RCC) and after overnight abstinence (a-RCC); N-RCCs were tested once. A cognitive battery assessed reaction time (RT), processing speed (digit symbol substitution test), working memory, verbal learning/memory and executive function (Stroop). Sleep quality was included as a covariate. RESULTS: Compared to c-RCC, overnight coffee abstinence significantly slowed RTs but did not affect the performance in the other cognitive tasks. In the a-RCC condition, but not the c-RCC condition, the RTs were slower than those of the N-RCCs, while accuracy measures were comparable across groups. Sleep quality did not alter these findings. CONCLUSIONS: Overnight coffee abstinence selectively slowed RT, and no statistical support was found for effects on memory or executive function. This suggests that overnight coffee abstinence protocols may introduce withdrawal-related RT slowing as a confound in habitual consumers, whereas other cognitive domains may not be affected. Allowing habitual consumers to maintain normal coffee intake could reduce this bias, supporting tailored rather than uniform abstinence requirements based on the specific outcomes studied.

items.title: Attendance Information System Success in Mandatory Use Contexts: An Integrated TAM–DeLone and McLean–TPB Framework in Higher Education
items.abstract: Mandatory information systems present a fundamental challenge to IS success theory: institutional enforcement guarantees usage but not acceptance, rendering conventional adoption metrics inadequate in non-voluntary contexts. This study examines the determinants of success of a mandatory mobile attendance application at a single higher education institution, investigating how technical quality dimensions and behavioral factors jointly produce user satisfaction and perceived organizational benefit. An integrated TAM–DeLone and McLean–TPB framework was tested using PLS-SEM on data collected from 140 university lecturers through an online survey. All eight hypotheses were empirically tested; seven were supported. Service quality was the strongest predictor of perceived usefulness (β = 0.399), followed by system quality (β = 0.317) and information quality (β = 0.149). Perceived usefulness (β = 0.592) and social influence (β = 0.368) significantly shaped attitude, while perceived behavioral control exerted no significant effect (β = −0.073, p = 0.299). Attitude strongly predicted user satisfaction (β = 0.825), which in turn predicted perceived net benefits (β = 0.731). This study contributes an empirically tested integrated TAM–DeLone and McLean–TPB model within a mandatory-use IS context. The findings suggest that IS success is mediated principally through psychological mechanisms rather than technical attributes alone, and that user attitude is the ultimate gateway to perceived organizational benefit. Future research may extend this framework to multi-institutional and longitudinal settings, incorporating privacy concern and perceived surveillance as additional constructs.

items.title: Verbal Energy as Value-Oriented Discourse: Shakarim Qudaiberdiuly’s Poetic Language and Its Educational Significance
items.abstract: This study reconceptualizes verbal energy as a discourse-pragmatic effect produced when linguistic form, evaluative positioning, and culturally shared values converge in a literary or public utterance. It examines how Shakarim Qudaiberdiuly (1858-1931), a Kazakh poet and moral philosopher, uses language to orient readers toward reflection, knowledge, civic responsibility, and ethical action. The study addresses three questions: which linguistic resources generate verbal energy; how those resources encode cultural and moral values; and what educational implications follow from their interaction. A purposive micro-corpus of five passages – three poetic excerpts and two historically documented public-address episodes – was analyzed qualitatively. The coding framework combined addressivity, speech-act force, appraisal, conceptual metaphor, repetition, parallelism, and directive positioning. The findings identify four mutually reinforcing mechanisms: direct address constructs an accountable audience; evaluative contrasts organize moral choice; journey, elevation, illness-remedy, and inexhaustible-resource metaphors convert abstract values into actionable images; and rhythmic parallelism increases memorability and collective resonance. Verbal energy is therefore not treated as a measurable physical property of isolated words, but as an interpretive effect arising from patterned language in a specific cultural-historical context. The analysis shows that Shakarim’s discourse links knowledge with healing, thought with movement, and poetic speech with service to the community. Pedagogically, these texts can support culturally responsive teaching when students examine how linguistic choices position an audience and critically discuss the values promoted. The study contributes a replicable framework for connecting Kazakh literary discourse, value education, and linguistic stylistics while distinguishing metaphorical-discursive energy from acoustic energy.

items.title: Rewriting the Divide: Child-Centred Participation and Theoretically Informed and Evidence-Based Intervention Design
items.abstract: Abstract This paper contributes to debates on problematic, dominant criminological narratives by foregrounding children’s own accounts of the support they need to thrive, informing ongoing efforts to support their individual and moral development. Drawing on community-based, participatory focus groups and individual and small-group interviews with 58 children aged 10–17 attending youth centres in Cambridge (UK), the study departs from deficit-oriented, adult-led explanations that frame children primarily through risk, mental disorders, or criminalisation. The findings rework prevailing criminological intervention approaches in two ways. First, using reflexive thematic analysis, the study centres children’s lived knowledge to identify trust, belonging, voice, agency, relational consistency of care, emotional support, and autonomy as central to what makes interventions trustworthy, accessible, engaging, and effective, whilst overly didactic, rigid, or authoritarian approaches were identified as key barriers to participation and effectiveness. These accounts move beyond adult assumptions about children’s needs, showing that effective support is grounded in relational, dialogic, autonomy-supportive environments rather than deficit-oriented models. Second, the paper argues that centring children’s perspectives is necessary but not sufficient: interventions must also be theoretically informed and evidence based. Rather than treating participatory and evidence-informed approaches as competing paradigms, the study offers data supporting their integration, combining child-centred qualitative insight with theoretically specified explanations of behaviour. Implications are discussed for the ongoing development of the school-based SATNAV:Compass youth intervention programme. This reconstruction of recommended intervention design approaches retains the strengths of existing traditions whilst addressing their limitations, offering a direction for future intervention research and practice.

items.title: Mutualistic microbes linked to broader niches but reduced diversification
items.abstract: Mutualistic interactions are widely hypothesized to broaden ecological niches and promote diversification, yet evidence for this relationship at macroevolutionary scales remains limited. Here, we investigate how fungal seed endophytes (Epichloë) influence niche breadth and diversification across over 100 species of the globally-distributed grass genus Poa. Combining global-scale climate, environmental, phylogenetic, and symbiosis data, we construct species distribution models for suites of symbiotic and non-symbiotic plant species, and use phylogenetic comparative methods to assess the influence of these symbionts on niche breadth, niche breadth evolution, and diversification. Endophyte-positive species have ~1.4 times broader primary niche axes (most often associated with temperature tolerances), ~2.5 times larger geographic ranges, and >30 times faster rates of niche breadth evolution than non-symbiotic species. Endophytic plants also have significantly drier climate centroids, consistent with endophyte-mediated drought tolerance, while simultaneously showing constrained niche centroid evolution. Despite pronounced niche expansion, hidden state speciation and extinction models reveal two modes of diversification: endophytes decrease diversification rates in young lineages, and have a neutral effect in older lineages. Together, our results indicate that mutualists can be associated with broader niches without necessarily increasing diversification, highlighting a potential decoupling between niche expansion and diversification. Mutualistic interactions are hypothesized to broaden ecological niches and promote diversification, yet evidence for this relationship remains limited. This study finds that, across Poa grasses, fungal endophytes are associated with broader niches and faster niche breadth evolution, but reduced diversification rates.

items.title: Neotropical puzzles: Assessing the role of spatial arrangement and human induced disturbances on the avian diversity of greenspace patches
items.abstract: Abstract Given the rapid expansion of urbanization, there is an urgent need to understand the drivers of biodiversity decline specially in highly diverse ecosystems such as the Neotropical cities. Specifically, while the influence of ecological factors on biodiversity is well documented, empirical evidence on how specific urban design features such as the spatial arrangement of greenspace patches and sources of anthropogenic disturbance contribute to these patterns remains limited. Here, we assessed how the spatial arrangement of vegetation areas such as lawns, gardens or wooded areas within urban ecosystems (i.e., greenspace patches) relative to their distance to vegetation elements such as trees and shrubs and urban infrastructure and, human disturbances such as pedestrian and pet density associated with avian species richness, abundance, functional diversity and evolutionary distinctiveness by conducting point counts across five cities in the Colombian Andes. Greenspace patches closer to vegetation supported greater bird species richness, abundance and functional diversity. Interestingly, evolutionary distinctiveness was not associated with the ecological variables considered. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of (1) preserving greenspace patches with proximity to surrounding vegetation to maintain biodiversity within urban ecosystems and (2) incorporating taxonomic, phylogenetic and functional dimensions when assessing ecological dynamics as ecological changes may be reflected in certain diversity metrics but not in others. Thus, this study contributes to the understanding of urban biodiversity patterns by identifying key landscape features that support diverse avian communities, offering insights for biodiversity-informed urban planning in rapidly expanding tropical cities.

items.title: Estrategias de competitividad empresarial en sistemas agroforestales sustentables: estudio de cinco fincas del cantón Mocache, provincia de los ríos, Ecuador
items.abstract: La competitividad empresarial de los sistemas agroforestales sustentables depende de la capacidad de integrar la eficiencia productiva, la diversificación de ingresos, la gestión financiera y el aprovechamiento de oportunidades comerciales sin comprometer los recursos naturales. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar estrategias de competitividad aplicables a cinco fincas con sistemas agroforestales del cantón Mocache, provincia de Los Ríos, Ecuador, mediante la integración de literatura científica sobre desempeño económico, sostenibilidad ambiental y gestión de cadenas de valor. Se desarrolló un análisis documental de estudios científicos sobre agroforestería, con énfasis en investigaciones económicas, ambientales y productivas, incluidos estudios realizados en Ecuador. Los hallazgos de la literatura muestran que la diversificación de productos puede ampliar las fuentes de ingresos, aunque sus beneficios dependen de los costos de establecimiento, los requerimientos de mano de obra, el tiempo de retorno de las inversiones y las condiciones de mercado. La evidencia ecuatoriana sobre sistemas agroforestales de cacao indica que es posible incorporar diversidad arbórea sin reducir necesariamente la producción o los ingresos del cultivo principal, pero también identifica desafíos de rentabilidad y trabajo. Asimismo, la cooperación entre productores, el procesamiento y la comercialización conjunta aparecen como alternativas para mejorar la captura de valor, mientras que los beneficios ambientales requieren una evaluación diferenciada de los ingresos privados. A partir de estos hallazgos, se identifican cinco líneas estratégicas para las unidades productivas de Mocache: gestión financiera por componente, diversificación planificada, reducción de pérdidas, diferenciación comercial y fortalecimiento de prácticas sustentables. Se concluye que la competitividad agroforestal no depende exclusivamente de la diversidad de especies, sino de la articulación entre decisiones productivas, financieras, ambientales y comerciales. La priorización de las estrategias en las cinco fincas requiere contrastar estos criterios con información local de costos, producción e ingresos.

items.title: Entropy guided spectral phenological feature engineering using Sentinel-2A data for Pan-Arctic vegetation classification
items.abstract: Arctic vegetation plays a critical role in regulating terrestrial ecosystem structure and function. Existing remote-sensing classification products are often limited in thematic detail and accuracy because of the region’s inaccessibility and the underuse of high-dimensional spectral and phenological information. This study established a Pan-Arctic vegetation classification system comprising Barren Tundra (BT), Sparse Tundra (ST), Cyperaceae Tundra (CT), Graminoid Tundra (GT), Wet Tundra (WT), Grass, and Shrub. A total of 161 homogeneous samples were selected across the Pan-Arctic domain through multi-source consistency filtering and visual verification. These samples were used for spectral–phenological feature development, entropy-based feature evaluation, threshold definition, and model construction. We introduced spectral characteristic information entropy (SCIE) and spectral characteristic information weight coefficients (SCIWC) to characterize spectral information content and relative feature importance. The entropy-guided feature set improved inter-class separability; for example, green-band information helped distinguish BT from ST, whereas red-band information contributed to the separation of CT and GT. Final map accuracy was assessed independently using 761 reference points in Yamal’skiy Rayon, which were not used for feature development or model construction. The classification achieved an overall accuracy of 90.67% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.88. A comparison with CALC-2020 indicated broad spatial consistency, while differences reflected the finer thematic detail and differing class definitions of the two products. These results demonstrate the potential of entropy-guided spectral–phenological feature engineering for fine-scale Arctic vegetation mapping, while further multi-region and multi-year validation is needed to assess Pan-Arctic transferability.

items.title: Vendi information gain for active learning and its application to ecology
items.abstract: Abstract While monitoring biodiversity through camera traps has become an important endeavour for ecological research, identifying species in the captured image data remains a major bottleneck due to limited labelling resources. Active learning—a machine learning paradigm that selects the most informative data to label and train a predictive model—offers a promising solution, but typically focuses on uncertainty in the individual predictions without considering uncertainty across the entire dataset. We study Vendi information gain (VIG) as an active learning policy that selects images based on their impact on dataset‐wide prediction uncertainty, capturing both informativeness and diversity. We applied VIG to two representative datasets in ecological image classification, the Kenya Camera Trap Dataset and the Missouri Camera Trap dataset, and compared VIG against common active learning methods. On both datasets, VIG achieves higher accuracy with fewer labelled examples. We further conducted extensive ablation studies to investigate the effects of the predictive model, batch sizes and other hyperparameters to find relatively robust performance from VIG. VIG has broad applicability beyond ecology, and our results highlight its value for biodiversity monitoring in data‐limited environments.

items.title: Fetish markets and feathers: Analyzing a growing threat to biodiversity in Africa
items.abstract: Abstract Wildlife trade poses a significant threat to global biodiversity and continues to escalate in regions such as West Africa. We investigated birds for sale in the Akodessewa Fetish Market (for belief‐based use) in Lomé, Togo—reported to be among the largest in West Africa—by conducting market surveys and trader interviews during four visits from 2022 to 2024. We used generalized linear mixed‐effects models (GLMMs) to analyze factors influencing species presence and relative abundance in the market. Our findings reveal a >200% increase in market volume and >400% increase in the diversity of birds for sale compared to previous surveys. The market featured 82 species from 38 avian families, including seven globally threatened or near threatened species, and 25 Convention of International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES)‐listed species. At least one‐third of traded species are known to have declining populations. Larger‐bodied species and those with higher estimated abundance were more likely to be offered for sale and in greater quantities. In contrast, species with latitudinal distribution midpoints farther from the market were less likely to be present and, when present, were offered in lower numbers. CITES‐listing was associated with the likelihood of species occurrence, while IUCN conservation status was negatively associated with the number of individuals for sale. Trade likelihood varied among taxonomic families, with hornbills (Bucerotidae) showing the highest probability of appearing in trade, whereas owls (Tytonidae and Strigidae) had the highest number of individuals for sale. All traders in the market originated from neighboring Benin, indicating cross‐border trade operations. Species occurrence and abundance in markets were associated primarily with availability, accessibility, and body size rather than conservation status, with CITES‐listed and threatened species appearing in trade despite nominal regulatory protection. We recommend that policy and legal interventions address regional wildlife trade networks operating as global markets rather than as local traditional practices.

items.title: A multi-scale approach for understanding factors limiting invasive carp distribution in the Ohio River Basin
items.abstract: The spread of aquatic invasive species (AIS) poses a major threat to freshwater biodiversity. Understanding the mechanisms regulating occurrence of invasive species in invaded systems requires a multi-scale approach, as regional dispersal can facilitate arrival while local processes ultimately determine their persistence across a landscape. We used a dynamic multi-scale occupancy model to test hypothesized factors limiting the occurrence of invasive bigheaded carps (bighead carp Hypophthalmichthys nobilis and silver carp H. molitrix) in the Ohio River, USA. Across the basin, invasion has slowed, with limited evidence of upstream advancement of their invaded range in this system. However, once present, silver carp and bighead carp populations tended to persist even in apparently low numbers. Bighead carp occurrence was not correlated with any environmental variables. On the local scale, silver carp exhibit clear habitat and flow preferences, where populations persisted in low velocity off-channel locations especially when flows are too high in the main channel. We found evidence for decreasing detection of both species in mid-reach and upstream pools, potentially because of lower abundance in these reaches. Our results indicated that while silver carp occurred throughout a large range of the Ohio River, fewer sites were occupied in upstream reaches. However, there was indirect evidence that site-level occurrence was increasing in the invasion front. Understanding these multi-scale dynamics can be helpful for developing effective strategies to contain invasive silver carp and bighead carp in the Ohio River and other systems.

items.title: In the synthetic biology era, engineered fungi could mitigate carbon dioxide emissions and enhance environmental resilience
items.abstract: Abstract Over the past two decades, there has been a staggering increase in greenhouse gas emissions, particularly carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) from unrestrained anthropogenic activities, leading to notable environmental shifts. Despite continuous efforts to reduce emissions, the world is not making satisfactory progress, which calls for immediate action to implement alternative strategies to enhance environmental sustainability. The Earth naturally absorbs and stores carbon through various processes, but merely keeping pace with ongoing human activities is no longer sufficient. Land plants and marine prokaryotes absorb CO 2 during photosynthesis and store carbon as biomass. Eukaryotic organisms also represent a valuable resource that can provide insights into the biological fixation and removal of atmospheric CO 2 . Expanding the capacities of Earth’s natural systems offers enormous potential for enhancing carbon sinks and promoting environmental resilience. Although extensive synthetic engineering of plant systems has been conducted to enhance their native carbon fixation pathways, research on microorganisms, especially fungi, has been limited. In this review, we specifically explore the role of soil-borne fungi in carbon management, elucidating their responses to environmental shifts and their potential for climate change mitigation. We place particular emphasis on the role of various fungal guilds in this process, highlighting those that should be prioritized for future synthetic biology applications. We then engage with previous endeavors to address primary challenges in advancing genetic tools for these understudied fungi. Lastly, we discuss how integrating synthetic biology practices into the field of soil-associated fungi can drive advances in long-term carbon storage, enhance degradation of environmental pollutants, and improve nutrient exchange and soil health, contributing to more resilient soil ecosystems and sustainable environmental interventions. Rising carbon dioxide emissions from human activities are driving environmental change and increasing the need for strategies that strengthen natural carbon sinks and ecosystem resilience. While plants and microorganisms play important roles in carbon capture and storage, the potential of soil-associated fungi remains comparatively underexplored, particularly from a synthetic biology perspective. In this Review, we examine the roles of soil-borne fungi in carbon management, their responses to environmental change, and their potential contributions to climate change mitigation. We highlight key fungal guilds that could be prioritized for future synthetic biology applications and discuss current challenges in developing genetic tools for understudied fungi. Finally, we explore how engineering soil-associated fungi could support long-term carbon storage while providing broader environmental benefits, including pollutant degradation, nutrient exchange, and improved soil health. Together, these opportunities position fungal synthetic biology as a promising approach for developing more resilient soil ecosystems and sustainable environmental interventions.

items.title: Advanced forest image classification using generative adversarial network-based data augmentation
items.abstract: The objective of this study was to develop a data augmentation framework that improves forest image classification by addressing limited labeled data, class imbalance, and the high variability of forest scenes caused by differences in vegetation density, illumination, seasonal conditions, and image acquisition perspectives. The generated dataset was intended to enhance model generalization and support the development of reliable forest monitoring applications. A dataset containing multiple forest and vegetation cover categories was expanded using an adaptive conditional generative adversarial network optimized with the Adaptive Jaya Algorithm, together with conventional image augmentation methods such as rotation, flipping, scaling, translation, and brightness adjustment. The images were preprocessed through resizing and Z-score normalization before training an EfficientNet-B0 model for automated feature extraction and classification. The augmented dataset improved class representation, particularly for minority categories, resulting in a classification accuracy of 98.48% . The enhanced dataset reduced overfitting, strengthened feature learning, and improved recognition across diverse forest conditions. All experiments were implemented using Python. The resulting dataset provides a valuable resource for researchers developing robust forest image classification models and supports applications in environmental monitoring, intelligent forest management, and sustainable resource assessment.

items.title: Beyond the Diffusion Coefficient: Propagators and Memory in Cosmic Ray Transport
items.abstract: Abstract Cosmic ray (CR) transport is usually modeled with a single diffusion coefficient, but this description captures only the growth of the variance and not the full transport process. Distinct transport mechanisms can share the same effective diffusion coefficient while producing different particle distributions and approaches to the diffusive limit. This limitation is especially relevant in realistic multiphase, structured, and time-dependent media, and is also reflected in observed environmental variations in CR transport near pulsar wind nebulae, supernova remnants, and molecular clouds. Particle-tracing studies also show clear departures from standard diffusion, including both superdiffusion and subdiffusion. We therefore develop a propagator-based framework centered on P(x, t), the probability distribution of particle positions, or equivalently its Fourier–Laplace transform P(k, s). This object is compact and statistically complete, and naturally exposes memory: the CR flux can depend on earlier gradients when unresolved trapping or phase changes are coarse-grained away. Using the Montroll–Weiss formalism, we show how to measure P(k, s) directly from trajectories, how to recover the associated memory kernel, and how to represent broad kernels efficiently with a Prony expansion. Applied to a multiphase medium, the framework shows that slow regions can regulate escape without dominating the total residence-time budget. We also introduce an accelerated Monte Carlo method for coarse-grained transport, and show that if trapping structures evolve while particles are still sampling them, the static long-time limit need not be reached. This paper provides the foundation for future observational applications, particle-tracing measurements, and CR-MHD closures.

items.title: Multi-dimensional NLTE radiative transfer for a double detonation Type Ia explosion model in the photospheric phase
items.abstract: Abstract Previous radiative transfer calculations have shown that both multi-dimensionality and NLTE (non local thermodynamic equilibrium) effects impact the synthetic observables predicted for Type Ia supernova explosion models. Here we carry out a 2D NLTE radiative transfer simulation in the photospheric phase for a double detonation model with a 1 M⊙ carbon–oxygen core and 0.02 M⊙ helium shell. The predicted observables demonstrate that departures from both spherical symmetry and local thermodynamic equilibrium are significant on scales relevant to comparisons with observations. The NLTE treatment leads to a bluer spectral energy distribution, more slowly declining optical-band light curves, changes to the near-infrared light curve shapes, and differences in the evolution of key spectral features. Although substantial viewing-angle variation is predicted for the model, the scale of the variation is not significantly impacted by NLTE effects up to peak. However, after peak, our 2D NLTE simulation retains a strong viewing-angle dependence in its spectra whereas our simulation of the same ejecta model using an approximate NLTE treatment predicts significantly reduced spectroscopic viewing-angle variation. The NLTE treatment leads to improved agreement with normal Type Ia supernovae, primarily due to the increased ionisation state of the simulation, although the absence of a secondary near-infrared maximum suggests that the ejecta remain over-ionised relative to observations after peak. Despite the improved agreement, many viewing angles still show excessive line blanketing, suggesting that the 0.02 M⊙ helium-shell mass of the current model is too large to reproduce normal Type Ia supernovae over the majority of lines of sight.

items.title: Africa-Papers: A 10-Billion-Token Multi-Domain Academic Corpus for African Foundation Language Models
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) depend fundamentally on the diversity, depth, and factual rigor of their pre-training corpora. However, contemporary foundational pre-training datasets (such as The Pile, S2ORC, and Dolma) exhibit a severe structural omission: African scientific, medical, legal, and agricultural scholarship constitutes less than 0.5% of global pre-training tokens. Consequently, state-of-the-art models suffer from systematic failure modes when reasoning about tropical epidemiology, localized smallholder agro-ecologies, regional economic governance, and indigenous linguistic structures. To resolve this representation deficit and advance African intellectual sovereignty in artificial intelligence, we introduce Africa-Papers, the largest curated multi-domain Pan-African academic pre-training corpus to date. Comprising over 844,807 full-text papers spanning 10.15 billion tokens across 879 Parquet shards, Africa-Papers unifies four primary scientific streams: (1) continental peer-reviewed journals indexed in DOAJ across 31 African nations, (2) the CGIAR CGSpace agricultural repository, (3) African-authored and African-focused STEM/AI preprints on arXiv, and (4) open-access international publications by scholars affiliated with African institutions indexed via OpenAlex. The entire corpus is processed into layout-aware, clean Markdown preserving section hierarchies, mathematical equations, and tabular data, accompanied by exact BPE token counts and a standardized 8-domain taxonomy. We release Africa-Papers openly on the Hugging Face Hub under the AfriSpeech organization to accelerate continual pre-training and domain evaluation for foundation models globally.

items.title: The SAIM Universal Framework: Real-World Applications and Industrial Impact Across Multi-Disciplinary Domains
items.abstract: This report translates the theoretical SAIM Universal Framework into practical engineering and scientific solutions. Moving beyond fundamental physics, we demonstrate how the discovered mathematical laws of error propagation provide direct cost savings, time efficiency, and risk mitigation across five distinct domains: 1. Aerospace & Telecom: Optimizing satellite constellations to avoid high GDOP (Geometric Dilution of Precision) and preventing catastrophic gyroscope failure in microgravity environments (ISS).2. Observational Astronomy: Optimizing multi-million dollar telescope time (JWST, LIGO, DESI) by pre-calculating sky localization errors and sensor requirements.3. Data Science & AI: Applying the square-root law (1/sqrt(N)) to optimize sensor fusion in autonomous vehicles and providing a robust stress-testing method for machine learning algorithms.4. Theoretical Physics: Offering testable predictions for the Hubble Tension (phase transition) and Quantum Cosmology (Model-51 Bounce).5. Civil Engineering & Geodesy: Optimizing the spatial distribution of seismic networks for precise earthquake epicenter localization. This document serves as an impact statement, proving that the SAIM framework is not merely an academic exercise, but a multi-disciplinary toolkit for modern engineering.

items.title: **The Solar System Beyond the Postcard: A Research Paper on Scale, Extremes, and Counterintuitive Physics in Our Planetary System — From the Oort Cloud to Coronal Heating**
items.abstract: --- ## Alternative Titles 1. **Dizzying Worlds: How Scale, Extremes, and Hidden Abundance Make Our Solar System Stranger Than We Imagine**2. **Beyond the Eight Planets: A Scientific Reappraisal of the Solar System's True Extent and Oddities**3. **The Counterintuitive Cosmos Next Door: Scale, Motion, Extremes, and Abundance in Our Planetary System**4. **From 30 AU to 100,000 AU: Reassessing the Solar System's Boundaries, Extremes, and Surprises**5. **What Textbooks Leave Out: A Thematic Review of the Solar System's Most Counterintuitive Features**6. **Dizziness as a Diagnostic: How the Solar System's Strangest Facts Test Our Physical Models**7. **Worlds That Defy Intuition: Volcanoes, Sideways Planets, and Ephemeral Rings in Our Cosmic Neighborhood**8. **The Solar System Reexamined: A Synthesis of Scale, Extremes, Motion, and Hidden Abundance** --- ## Subtitles 1. **A Thematic Review of Four Axes of Counterintuition: Scale, Extremes, Motion, and Abundance**2. **Why the Solar System Extends to 100,000 AU and Why That Matters**3. **From Olympus Mons and Valles Marineris to Io's Volcanoes and the Sun's Coronal Heating Paradox**4. **Retrograde Venus, Sideways Uranus, and the Rotational Oddities That Test Formation Models**5. **Water Ice Everywhere, Transient Rings, and Pluto's Unexpected Geology**6. **Separating Trivia from Diagnostics in Popular Solar System Science**7. **Each Dizzying Fact as a Test of Physical Theory**8. **What Our Planetary System Reveals About the Limits of Intuition and the Frontiers of Understanding** --- ## Detailed Description This paper presents a thematically organized, evidence-based examination of the solar system's most counterintuitive features, using the MSN slideshow "25 dizzying facts about our solar system" (October 2026) as a framing device while substantially deepening its scientific content. Rather than reproducing a list of trivia, the paper organizes its analysis around four axes that defy intuition—**scale**, **extremes**, **motion**, and **hidden abundance**—and argues that each "dizzying fact" is not a curiosity but a **diagnostic**: a case where observation departs from naive expectation, thereby testing a physical model and revealing where understanding remains incomplete. The paper opens by challenging the conventional boundary of the solar system. While textbooks place its edge at Neptune (30 AU), the Oort Cloud extends to approximately **100,000 AU**, meaning that much of what is called "interstellar space"—including the region Voyager 1 entered in 2012—actually lies within the Sun's gravitational domain. Voyager 1, at roughly **125 AU**, will take about **300 years** to reach the Oort Cloud's inner edge and perhaps **30,000 years** to pass beyond it. The paper pairs this with the Sun's mass dominance: **99.8%** of the system's mass, equivalent to more than **330,000 Earths** by mass and **1.3 million Earths** by volume. The **extremes** section examines Mars's **Olympus Mons** (25 km high, roughly three times Everest) and **Valles Marineris** (4,000 km long, over ten times Earth's largest canyon), explaining their scale through the absence of plate tectonics. It then turns to **Io**, the most volcanically active body in the solar system, with eruptions reaching **400 km** altitude, driven by **tidal heating** from orbital resonance with Europa and Ganymede—demonstrating that geological activity requires gravitational mechanisms, not solar proximity. The section culminates in the **coronal heating paradox**: the Sun's photosphere is approximately **5,500°C**, yet its corona reaches **2 million°C**, an inversion that remains one of the major unsolved problems in solar physics. The **motion** section reviews **Venus**, whose **243-Earth-day** rotation exceeds its **225-Earth-day** orbit—making a day longer than a year—and whose retrograde spin may result from a catastrophic collision; **Uranus**, tilted **98 degrees** so that it effectively rolls around the Sun, likely due to early massive impacts; and **Mercury**, with an **88-Earth-day** year, the shortest in the system. The **hidden abundance** section documents the ubiquity of water ice—at Mercury's and the Moon's poles, in Mars's caps, and in subsurface oceans such as Ganymede's, which contains **more water than all of Earth's oceans combined**—with implications for habitability on Europa and Enceladus. It explains that **all four giant planets have rings**, and that ring particles are continuously destroyed and replenished, making rings **transient, dynamic, recently formed** features rather than primordial adornments. It closes with **Pluto's 3,300-meter icy mountains** and evidence of recent geological activity, challenging assumptions about small, distant bodies. The **discussion** argues that these facts function as tests: the Oort Cloud's scale tests formation models and the Sun's gravitational reach; coronal heating tests magnetic energy dissipation in plasmas; Venus's retrograde rotation tests collisional evolution models; Io's volcanism tests tidal heating theory; ring transience tests assumptions about stability; and Pluto's mountains test the limits of radiogenic and tidal heating. The paper concludes that "dizzying" is an apt descriptor—dizziness is equilibrium lost—and that the solar system is not a static diorama but a collection of active, evolving, and frequently surprising systems that continue to destabilize comfortable assumptions after centuries of study. The paper is intended for astronomy students, educators, science communicators, and general readers seeking a rigorous yet accessible synthesis. --- **Keywords:** solar system, Oort Cloud, coronal heating, retrograde rotation, tidal heating, ring dynamics, water ice, Olympus Mons, Valles Marineris, planetary extremes, scale, counterintuition

items.title: Kuaijie Sinology: A Detective-Style Reconstruction of Li Bai's "Quiet Night Thought" through Multi-Dimensional Physical Clues and Optical Investigation
items.abstract: Abstract Based on the "Three-Pairs and Four-Criteria" analytical framework of Kuaijie Sinology, this paper conducts a detective-style physical and spatial reconstruction of Li Bai's famous poem "Quiet Night Thought" (Jing Ye Si). Previous interpretations often place the poem in a traditional "indoor bed" context, lacking empirical verification in physics, astronomy, architecture, and optics. By introducing physical parameters—including astronomical altitude calculations, architectural depth analysis, specular reflection of water, engineering water demand, and the optical refraction of tears—this study constructs an "Eighteen-Link Evidence Chain." We propose a scene reconstruction hypothesis: the poem was composed outdoors by a courtyard well, where the poet sat on a bamboo couch, observing the white illusion formed by the moonlight's specular reflection on the water-soaked ground. This research not only breaks millennium-old textbook interpretations through material and physical premises but also serves as an empirical testament to the unbroken continuity of Chinese civilizational logic across thousands of years. 【摘要】 本文基于“蒯解汉学”三双四通研判体系,对李白千古名篇《静夜思》的创作场景进行物理空间与制度常识的勘察。前人解读多将此诗置于“室内卧床”的传统语境,缺少物理、天文、建筑、光影层面的实勘维度。 本文依托传统营造的工程视角,侧重从建筑物理与人居实景出发,引入天文仰角测算、建筑纵深考据、光影成像原理及工程用水量复原等物质物理参数作为全新研判工具,构建了由物证链与人证链组成的“十八环互证逻辑链”。本文提出场景复原假说:《静夜思》所述场景为李白身处室外庭院井边,倚坐竹榻或胡床,偶见井边洒水映月之白影,叠加人在悲怀垂泪时泪液的光学折射效应,从而触发的望月思乡之情。 本文旨在以物理底座与生活实学,在传统解读上进行迭代并提供实证考据新路径。更为关键的是,此番基于物理维度的推演,反向印证了华夏文明与生存逻辑跨越千年的未曾断绝。

items.title: Teaching Agile Requirements Engineering: A Stakeholder Simulation with Generative AI
items.abstract: Abstract Context: The active involvement of users and customers in agile software development remains a persistent challenge in practice. For this reason, it is important that students in higher education become familiar with good practices in Agile Requirements Engineering during their studies. Objective: Our objective is to support students in learning how to perform requirements analysis by applying agile practices within a stakeholder simulation using AI Personas. At the same time, the approach fosters a critical understanding of the limitations and ethical considerations associated with the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in this context. Method: In our courses, we employ a stakeholder simulation using GenAI, in which students conduct interviews with AI Personas through a provided meta-prompt. Based on the outcomes of these interviews, students apply agile practices (e.g., story mapping or impact mapping) to document requirements. The use of GenAI is subsequently reflected upon in a structured group discussion. Results: Through this approach, students gain practical experience by applying state-of-the art agile practices for requirements elicitation and documentation while simultaneously developing an understanding of the technical and ethical limitations associated with the use of generative AI. Conclusion: We have applied this approach over several terms and found that using a meta-prompt provides flexibility, allowing us to remain independent of specific large language model providers.

items.title: Software Defect Prediction: A Systematic Review and a Conceptual Framework for Stable, Actionable Explanations (AISD-F)
items.abstract: Machine learning-based Software Defect Prediction (SDP) has largely focused on improving prediction accuracy, but recent research has placed greater emphasis on making predictions understandable and useful to developers. This systematic review examines the use of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in SDP and the evidence supporting its reliability in practice. Following PRISMA guidelines, 40 peer-reviewed studies, primarily published between 2020 and 2025, were selected from IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and Scopus. The studies were examined in terms of XAI methods, explanation reliability and stability, dataset quality, and model selection. LIME and SHAP were the most frequently used methods, yet multi-run evaluations showed changes in their feature rankings across configurations, in contrast to the reliability reported by many single-run studies. Data-quality problems, particularly SZZ-related label noise, class imbalance, and multicollinearity, often had a greater effect on prediction reliability than model architecture. The review also found growing use of line-level and just-in-time prediction, although consistent validation at industrial scale remains limited. Within the reviewed corpus, no study provides controlled evidence that XAI explanations improve developers' ability to resolve software defects, and the field currently lacks industrial-scale validation and controlled developer studies of XAI-assisted defect resolution. Based on these findings, this paper proposes the Actionable and Interpretable Software Defect Framework (AISD-F), a conceptual, five-stage modular architecture (not yet empirically validated) that is intended to integrate data quality assurance, hybrid model selection, dual-layer explanation, and CI/CD into a unified research agenda for explainable SDP, rather than a deployment-ready solution.

items.title: Using digital twins as a shared information model for secure software lifecycle management in IoT
items.abstract: Secure software updates are essential for maintaining Internet of Things (IoT) systems throughout their operational lifetime. However, software lifecycle information is typically fragmented across software repositories, deployment services, device management platforms, and runtime monitoring systems, limiting interoperability and end-to-end lifecycle visibility. This paper proposes a Digital Twin (DT)-based information model that uses the DT of each device as a shared information contract throughout the operational stages of the IoT secure software update lifecycle. The proposed model extends the DT with software lifecycle information, enabling deployment intentions, installation status, verification results, and runtime observations to be exchanged through a shared representation across heterogeneous software management components. The approach is realised as an extension of Eclipse Ditto and evaluated in a laboratory set-up for telemedicine gateways that combines a real gateway with fleets of emulated devices. A real security update could be followed revision by revision in the gateway’s DT; queries over the DTs identified vulnerable, updated and failed devices correctly, despite injected installation and verification failures and temporarily offline devices; and new lifecycle information and an additional lifecycle component were introduced without changing the existing ones. The coordination carried out through the DT remained small in comparison with the installation work on the device itself, while the throughput of the DT platform bounded how quickly an update could be assigned across a large fleet.

items.title: Evaluating regression models and machine learning for long-term energy demand forecasting – Germany
items.abstract: Reliable long-term energy demand forecasting underpins energy-system planning and decarbonization policy design, yet most established methods are calibrated for short horizons and may not capture structural change. This study compares four forecasting models: multiple linear regression (MLR), a vector error correction model (VECM), support vector regression (SVR), and an artificial neural network (ANN). Germany’s final energy consumption (FEC) is projected to 2050 from annual data spanning 1992–2021. The SVR and ANN were tuned using particle swarm optimization and Bayesian optimization. Accuracy is assessed using mean absolute error (MAE), mean squared error (MSE), and the coefficient of determination (R²). The SVR achieves the highest test accuracy (MAE = 9.19, R² = 0.974), but its long-term projections substantially exceed the historical range, suggesting extrapolation instability. The ANN attains comparable test accuracy (MAE = 10.05, R² = 0.965) with stronger generalization and more plausible projections, and is therefore adopted for the base-case and scenario analyses. MLR is transparent but less accurate, whereas VECM forecasts are sensitive to the assumed cointegration rank in the small-sample setting. The ANN base-case indicates an approximately 12% decline in FEC by 2050 relative to 2008, driven primarily by fuel substitution and efficiency improvements. Across five decarbonization scenarios, projected 2050 FEC ranges from 1476 to 2195 TWh, demonstrating that transition assumptions dominate long-term forecast uncertainty. Even the most ambitious pathway, approximately 39% below 2008, falls short of Germany’s 45% FEC reduction target for 2045. The results indicate that generalization and extrapolation behavior are as important as predictive accuracy in model selection for long-term energy transition analysis.

items.title: The bidirectional predictive association between methamphetamine use and depression.
items.abstract: Background and aims Co-occurrence of methamphetamine dependence and depression is high, though the direction of this temporal relationship is unclear. We investigated the direction of the temporal relationship between methamphetamine use and depression. Design A longitudinal random-intercept cross-lagged panel model analysis was conducted using 12 contiguous weeks of data from a randomised controlled trial (ACTRN12618000366257). Setting Melbourne, Geelong and Wollongong, Australia. Participants 153 adult participants dependent on methamphetamine. Measurements Each week, days of methamphetamine use in the past week were assessed using the Timeline Followback, and clinically significant symptoms of depression were defined as a score of 4 or greater on the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale depression item. Results Relative to their average, if an individual increased their methamphetamine use in one week, their probability of experiencing clinically significant depressive symptoms increased the following week [estimate = 0.271, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.177-0.365, P Summary There appears to be evidence of a bidirectional relationship between days of methamphetamine use and clinically significant depressive symptoms within a weekly timeframe.

items.title: Picea pan-transcriptomes reveal signatures of complex phylogenetic conflict and adaptation.
items.abstract: Coniferous forests are among the ecosystems most exposed to rapid climate warming, and a well-resolved phylogeny of Picea is essential for understanding the evolutionary processes that have shaped diversification and regional differentiation across the genus. Here, we analysed pan-transcriptomes spanning 37 Picea species from across Northern Hemisphere forests. Our analyses reveal a bipartite pan-transcriptomic architecture in which core genes (9.4%) are associated primarily with fundamental cellular functions, whereas dispensable and private components (90.6% combined) are more strongly associated with ecological differentiation. Species trees inferred from low-copy orthologues resolve four major clades, and approximately 275 loci are sufficient to recover a stable backbone topology. Coalescent analyses indicate pervasive genealogical discordance, with incomplete lineage sorting (ILS) showing the greatest relative importance (27.75%) and gene-flow signals contributing less (7.27%). The most variable gene families (7.4%) further delimit three biogeographically structured regional groups: Qinghai-Tibet Plateau lineages are characterized by genes involved in environmental stress, signalling and low-oxygen responses; East Asian lineages show greater representation of protein metabolism and ubiquitin-mediated regulation; and Holarctic lineages are characterized by photosynthesis, chloroplast function, cell-wall processes and secondary metabolism. Together, these findings link regional gene-family differentiation with the persistence of ancestral polymorphism and provide a phylogenomic framework for understanding spruce diversification and for developing hypotheses relevant to climate-resilient forest conservation.

items.title: HARP: HARmonizing In-Vivo Single-Shell Diffusion MRI Using Phantom-Only Training.
items.abstract: Purpose Combining multi-site diffusion MRI (dMRI) data is hindered by inter-scanner variability, which confounds subsequent analysis. Previous harmonization methods require large, matched or traveling human subjects from multiple sites, which are impractical to acquire in many situations. This study aims to develop a deep learning-based dMRI harmonization framework that eliminates the reliance on multi-site in-vivo traveling human data for training. Methods HARP employs a voxel-wise 1D neural network trained on an easily transportable diffusion phantom. The model learns relationships between spherical harmonics coefficients of different sites without memorizing spatial structures. Results HARP reduced inter-scanner variability levels significantly in various measures. Quantitatively, it decreased inter-scanner variability as measured by standard error in FA (12%), MD (10%), and GFA (30%) with scan-rescan standard error as the baseline, while preserving fiber orientations and tractography after harmonization. Conclusion We believe that HARP represents an important first step toward dMRI harmonization using only phantom data, thereby obviating the need for complex, matched in vivo multi-site cohorts. This phantom-only strategy substantially enhances the feasibility and scalability of quantitative dMRI for large-scale clinical studies.

items.title: Highs and lows: Complex relationships between childhood socio-economic position and adolescent substance use in three United Kingdom birth cohorts.
items.abstract: Background and aims Substance use behaviours frequently commence in adolescence, and socio-economic position (SEP) in childhood is a key predictor of variation in adolescent substance use behaviours; however, the relationship between SEP and substance use may be changing over time. Previous research examined how the construct of SEP has changed over time in the United Kingdom (UK) using latent class analysis; this study extended upon prior work to determine differences in how SEP relates to adolescent substance use over the past 50 years. Methods Observational study using substance use data measuring adolescent smoking, drinking, cannabis and other illicit drug use harmonized across three birth cohorts: the 1970 British Cohort Study (BCS70; n = 8436), Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC; n = 6395) and Millennium Cohort Study (MCS; n = 8548). Substance use outcomes were regressed on previously derived SEP latent classes from these cohorts. Results The most disadvantaged latent class in each cohort were more likely to smoke in all three cohorts, with the smallest odds ratio (OR) observed in the BCS70 [OR = 1.42, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.25-1.61] and the largest in the ALSPAC (OR = 2.86, 95% CI = 1.57-5.22). Conversely, the most disadvantaged class in the BCS70 and MCS were less likely to try an alcoholic drink and drank less frequently; in the MCS, they were also less likely to binge drink (OR = 0.34, 95% CI = 0.22-0.52). Cannabis and illicit substance use were not statistically significantly related to SEP latent classes across cohorts, except in the ALSPAC. Summary In the United Kingdom, certain substance use behaviours appear to be consistently related to socio-economic position over time. Qualitative differences between the cohorts indicate that socio-economic inequalities in adolescent smoking and illicit drug use appear to have peaked in the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children whereas inequalities in drinking appear stronger in the Millennium Cohort Study.

items.title: Government and non-government policy influencers' support for mental health promotion policies in Alberta and Manitoba, Canada.
items.abstract: In Canada, the mental health crisis is an escalating public health concern. Mental health policies, often advocated for and led by government and non-government policy influencers (PIs), are critical in setting the political agenda to improve this issue. Therefore, understanding the views of PIs on mental health-promoting policies may provide insights to policy development priorities. We aim to examine if support for mental health promotion policies varies between Alberta and Manitoba, and between government and non-government PIs. This cross-sectional study was conducted using the 2019 Chronic Disease Prevention Survey, which collects the opinions of Canadian PIs and public on chronic disease prevention topics, including 16 mental health promotion policies. Each policy had a four-point Likert scale of 'strongly oppose' to 'strongly support.' Chi-square tests were performed. A total of 361 PIs participated. PIs were mostly 46 years and older, university graduates, non-visible minority, and had an income of ⩾C$70,000. Overall, policies were well supported by the PIs (>80%). In Manitoba, government and non-government PIs were more aligned in their support. Differences were found between provinces and PI groups around policies targeting disadvantaged populations. Policies aimed at building capacity received the highest support, whereas those promoting engagement and partnerships were the least supported. The lower support for policies targeting specific populations in Alberta signals an opportunity to deepen the discussion about the societal benefits of targeted policies.

items.title: Employment Decisions and Preferences of Physiotherapy Graduates and Students in Canada: An Applied Research Study.
items.abstract: The purpose of this article is to examine recent graduates' employment decisions, students' employment preferences, and factors influencing these choices, so as to inform physiotherapy recruitment. A cross-sectional observational survey was conducted of physiotherapy graduates and students in Manitoba, Canada, informed by the Theory of Planned Behaviour. Quantitative responses were summarized descriptively, and open-text responses were analyzed thematically. Seventy-seven participants completed the survey (40 graduates and 37 students). Forty-eight percent of graduates worked in private practice and 40% in public practice; 68% of students intended to work in both sectors, a pattern we call hybrid employment. Pay was the most frequently selected factor for graduates (78%) and students (100%). Benefits, work-life balance, and patient population also influenced employment choices. Qualitative findings highlighted the role of exposure to practice settings and collaborative work environments in employment choices. Health leaders should consider hybrid employment, total remuneration packages, clinical-placement experiences, and supportive teams when developing recruitment strategies.

items.title: Alcohol use screening, brief intervention and referral to treatment cascade of care in the USA: Variation by alcohol use and socio-demographic characteristics.
items.abstract: Background and aims Screening, brief intervention and referral to treatment (SBIRT) can identify and reduce excessive drinking, reducing the risk of alcohol use disorder (AUD). We estimated the implementation of SBIRT care cascade steps in the United States using national data and quantified differences for key sociodemographic subgroups. Design Cross-sectional analysis of National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH) 2022-2024 data. The SBIRT care cascade was assessed as reported: (1) health care use; and, amongst those with past-year health care use, report of alcohol; (2) use screening; (3) brief intervention (BI) receipt; (4) treatment referral; and (5) treatment receipt. Setting United States. Participants Adults (n = 139 532) stratified across five self-reported alcohol use levels: abstinence or moderate alcohol use, heavy alcohol use, mild, moderate and severe AUD. Measurements Multivariable logistic regression models assessed the likelihood of receiving each cascade step overall, by alcohol use level, and by sociodemographic characteristics (age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, employment, income and insurance). Results About 81% of adults endorsed past-year health care use, of which 69% reported screening for alcohol use. Individuals with severe AUD had the highest screening rates (89%), followed by moderate (84%) or mild (84%) AUD. Only 4% of individuals with heavy alcohol use reported receiving BI, with higher rates among individuals with severe (33%), moderate (17%) or mild AUD (9%). Prevalence of being referred to and receiving treatment increased with AUD severity but remained low overall (3% to 23%). Although women were more likely to use health care than men [marginal prevalence ratio (MPR) = 1.112; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.103-1.121], women were less likely to receive BI (MPR = 0.518, 95% CI = 0.447-0.588). Women with AUD were less likely to be referred to treatment (MPR = 0.621, 95% CI = 0.497-0.744) or receive treatment (MPR = 0.788, 95% CI = 0.618-0.957) than men with AUD. Individuals 50 years old and older were less likely to be screened than younger individuals (MPR = 0.944, 95% CI = 0.925-0.963). Compared with White individuals, Hispanic individuals were less likely to use health care (MPR = 0.946, 95% CI = 0.934-0.958) and Black and Hispanic individuals were less likely to be screened (MPR = 0.883 and 9.913, respectively), in particular if they reported heavy alcohol use (MPR = 0.898 and 0.921, respectively). Summary In the United States, despite wide health care use and high screening rates, there are substantial gaps in the remaining steps of the screening, brief intervention and referral to treatment (SBIRT) care cascade for heavy drinking. Sex and racial differences in receiving SBIRT need to be addressed.

items.title: Effect of Obicetrapib on Glycaemia and New-Onset Diabetes: Pooled Analysis of BROADWAY/BROOKLYN and an Updated Meta-analysis of CETP Inhibitor Trials.
items.abstract: Aims New-onset diabetes (NoD) is a recognised effect of statin therapy potentially influencing acceptance of intensive LDL-C-lowering. In contrast, cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) inhibition has been associated with lower NoD risk in earlier trials. We assessed the effect of the highly selective CETP inhibitor obicetrapib on glycaemia and NoD, contextualised within an updated meta-analysis of CETP inhibitor trials. Methods Individual participant data from the phase 3 BROADWAY and BROOKLYN trials were pooled across 1,700 participants without diabetes at baseline (899 normoglycaemic, 801 prediabetes; 38.8% women), randomised 2:1 to obicetrapib 10 mg or placebo for 52 weeks. The PRISMA-compliant, PROSPERO-registered systematic review identified six eligible trials reporting NoD. Pooled risk ratios were calculated using Mantel-Haenszel fixed-effect models, with prespecified subgroup analyses by baseline glycaemic status and CETPi potency, and trial-level meta-regression. Results Obicetrapib did not increase HbA1c at week 52 vs placebo (LSMD -0.02%, 95% CI -0.04 to 0.00). NoD occurred in 6.4% (obicetrapib) versus 8.5% (placebo) (adjusted OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.47-1.03), directionally consistent across glycaemic strata. Restricted cubic spline analyses identified associations between HDL-C, apoA1 and Lp(a) changes and NoD risk, but not HbA1c change. In the meta-analysis, CETP inhibition was associated with a 16% lower risk of NoD (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.79-0.90; I2 = 0%). Conclusions Obicetrapib did not adversely affect glycaemia and was associated with a numerically lower risk of NoD, consistent with a CETP inhibitor class signal of a modestly lower risk. The PREVAIL trial will provide larger-longer evidence about obicetrapib and NoD.

items.title: Visual-linguistic cues in manual communication: Neural and behavioral responses to Mouthings in sign-naïve perception.
items.abstract: Gesture serves as a foundational modality for conveying event structure, providing critical visual information about transitivity and participant roles. Sign languages integrate manual (hand-based) and non-manual (face, torso, head) articulations to encode complex linguistic information. Among these, mouth movements provide phonological and lexical cues, but their role in sign-naïve individuals remains underexplored. This study investigates how sign-naïve individuals process non-manual markers (mouthings) in unfamiliar signed verbs, to explore how linguistic information is extracted from visual stimuli sharing properties with both gesture and sign language. Using EEG, we examined whether lip-reading functions as a linguistic cue or a general perceptual enhancement in non-signers viewing Austrian Sign Language (ÖGS) and non-ÖGS stimuli. Findings reveal distinct neural signatures for manual signs presented with and without congruent mouthings. An early posterior negativity followed by a late posterior positivity suggests that mouthings facilitate lexical access by providing phonological cues that activate stored lexical representations. Conversely, stimuli without mouthings elicited increased anterior activity, reflecting heightened cognitive control demands. Further, telic verbs, which inherently encode event endpoints, showed earlier and stronger facilitation from congruent mouthings compared to atelic verbs. These findings align with the Event Visibility Hypothesis and reinforce the role of visual cues in linguistic comprehension.
