items.title: Mapping cardiometabolic risk in Cleveland's urban environment: A participatory systems analysis of place-based drivers and the role of Community Health Workers.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) diseases are shaped by place-based social and environmental conditions, yet the dynamic mechanisms linking structural inequities, neighborhood environments, and healthcare systems remain insufficiently understood. This study employed a participatory system dynamics approach, using Group Model Building (GMB), to examine how spatial, social, and institutional processes interact to shape cardiometabolic risk among low-income African American residents in Cleveland, Ohio, and to explore the role of Community Health Workers (CHWs). A community-engaged Group Model Building process engaged residents, Community Health Workers, healthcare providers, public health practitioners, organizational leaders, and academic partners to co-develop a stakeholder-informed causal loop diagram. Across two Group Model Building workshops conducted on November 18, 2023, and February 17, 2024, participants identified drivers of CKM risk and co-developed a stakeholder-informed system map using structured Group Model Building scripts and qualitative workshop data. The systems map depicts CKM risk as emerging from interactions among economic inequality, neighborhood disinvestment, food access, environmental exposures, healthcare fragmentation, screening access, treatment uptake, and disease management. Stakeholders highlighted upstream forces shaping spatial patterns of disadvantage, chronic stress, and healthcare access, contributing to delayed detection and management of risk factors. Three reinforcing dynamics were identified: (1) a limit-to-success dynamic constraining CHW capacity due to insufficient reimbursement; (2) a shifting-the-burden dynamic emphasizing individual responses over structural reform; and (3) a success-to-the-successful dynamic favoring biomedical care over community-based prevention. These findings suggest how cardiometabolic inequities are sustained through interconnected feedback loops and highlight leverage points-including sustainable CHW financing, cross-sector coordination, and neighborhood investment-to inform place-based strategies to reduce inequities.

items.title: Absence of familial adult myoclonic epilepsy-associated intronic repeat expansions in SAMD12, STARD7, and MARCHF6 genes in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy with tremor.
items.abstract: We investigated whether intronic repeat expansions in the SAMD12, STARD7, and MARCHF6 genes are present in individuals with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (JME) and tremor. Given that tremor is a shared feature with familial adult myoclonic epilepsy (FAME), we hypothesized that this phenotype may reflect a common genetic basis involving FAME-associated pentanucleotide repeat expansions. The study included 31 individuals with JME and tremor (17/31 [54.8%] females, mean age at genetic testing = 34.4 ± 13.8 years) and 100 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Genomic DNA was analyzed using repeat-primed polymerase chain reaction and fragment analysis to detect intronic TTTCA repeat expansions in the three established FAME-associated genes. No pathogenic repeat expansions were identified in SAMD12, STARD7, or MARCHF6 among individuals with JME and tremor. The frequency of intronic pentanucleotide repeat expansions did not differ between cases and controls. This is a comprehensive analysis assessing three FAME-associated repeat-expansion loci in a clinically well-characterized cohort of individuals with JME and tremor. Our findings do not support a major contribution of these FAME-associated loci to tremor in this cohort, suggesting that those intronic repeats did not contribute to genetic susceptibility to the tremor in JME. Further studies are required to identify the factors associated with this phenotype.

items.title: Dravet Syndrome Updates: Evolving Insights and Emerging Therapeutics.
items.abstract: Purpose of review This narrative review aims to evaluate current literature on Dravet syndrome, integrating significant new findings into the existing knowledge of pathophysiology and disease course, and highlighting emerging treatments. Recent findings Beyond SCN1A pathogenic variants, recent findings implicate an expanding number of genes and polygenic interactions which may play a role in the pathophysiology of Dravet syndrome. Neuroimmune dysregulation during critical periods of early brain development may be an additional contributing factor. There is increased recognition of neurodevelopmental comorbidities and disease progression over the lifetime, with neurological decline in adulthood suggestive of a possible degenerative process. Emerging and investigational therapies, including gene-modulatory therapies, may provide improvement in seizures and other metrics. Along with an evolving understanding of Dravet syndrome, including its multifactorial disease mechanisms, clinical manifestations beyond seizures, and progression of disease, the advent of novel treatments offers the potential for improved care of patients across the lifespan.

items.title: Improving the clinical trial landscape for Parkinson syndromes in Germany.
items.abstract: Germany has a longstanding tradition of excellence in neuroscience and Parkinson's research, supported by outstanding academic institutions, specialized clinical centers, and a strong scientific community. Building on this strong foundation, the country now has the opportunity to transform its clinical research landscape into a more integrated ecosystem for Parkinson syndromes. Despite major advances in molecular understanding, biomarker development, and therapeutic innovation, important structural, regulatory, financial, and organizational barriers continue to limit the full translational potential of German Parkinson research. Participants in an expert workshop identified identify recurring challenges, including fragmented trial infrastructures, slow and bureaucratic regulatory procedures, insufficient funding for investigator-initiated clinical research, limited integration of patient organizations, and suboptimal patient recruitment pathways. This workshop-derived perspective outlines a strategic framework to elevate Germany from a country with excellent individual centers to a globally competitive and integrated hub for innovative Parkinson clinical research. Key recommendations include transforming the German Parkinson Study Group into a nationally coordinated, service-oriented trial network; establishing centralized digital and regulatory infrastructures; diversifying public and philanthropic funding; implementing platform and observational trial structures; strengthening incentives for participating centers; and enhancing patient engagement through national registries, decentralized trial approaches, real-world data based evidence surveillance, and systematic integration of patient organizations. The authors argue that Germany must move beyond isolated university-based structures toward a nationally coordinated and highly efficient research ecosystem capable of rapidly delivering disease-modifying and precision medicine trials. Such a transformation could strengthen Germany's international position in neurodegenerative disease research and accelerate therapeutic innovation for patients with Parkinson syndromes.

items.title: Neurotrophic regulation of lipid metabolism in Alzheimer's disease: Mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
items.abstract: BackgroundAlzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder in which lipid metabolic dysregulation is increasingly recognized as an important contributor to pathogenesis. Neurotrophic factors (NTFs), beyond their established roles in neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity, may also regulate lipid metabolism.ObjectiveTo summarize current evidence on lipid metabolic dysregulation in AD and evaluate the potential roles of major NTFs in regulating lipid homeostasis.MethodsExperimental, clinical, and translational studies addressing lipid metabolism, neurotrophic signaling, and their interactions in AD were reviewed, focusing on cholesterol, sphingolipid, and fatty acid metabolism and on BDNF, NGF, GDNF, CNTF, and Nrn1.ResultsDisturbances in cholesterol transport, sphingolipid and fatty acid metabolism, and high-density lipoprotein function may promote AD pathology by affecting membrane organization, synaptic plasticity, oxidative stress, insulin signaling, and amyloid-β and tau metabolism. BDNF, NGF, GDNF, CNTF, and Nrn1 may influence lipid-related processes through pathways including PI3K/Akt, AMPK, MAPK, and STAT3. However, evidence strength varies substantially among NTFs, and many proposed interactions are supported mainly by cellular, animal, or non-AD models.ConclusionsNeurotrophic signaling and lipid metabolism may form an interconnected regulatory network relevant to AD pathophysiology. This concept may support future biomarker and therapeutic research, but it should currently be regarded as a hypothesis-generating framework requiring direct validation in human AD and well-characterized AD models.

items.title: Physical activity and brain aging in Sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review of observational studies.
items.abstract: Physical activity may delay cognitive decline, but evidence from Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) remains limited. This review summarizes findings on associations between physical (in)activity and brain aging in SSA, identifies research gaps and limitations, and proposes steps to strengthen research capacity. We searched five databases including PubMed using pertinent keywords. Observational studies conducted in SSA that examined physical (in)activity or related variables such as exercise as predictors and brain aging outcomes such as cognitive impairment or dementia were included. The review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Of 10,880 identified records, 19 studies met the inclusion criteria (18 cross-sectional, 1 longitudinal). Sample sizes ranged from 70 to 5,011 participants. Studies varied in design and assessment of exposures and outcomes. Seven studies reported associations between physical inactivity or lower physical activity levels and less favourable brain aging outcomes, including increased risk of cognitive impairment. Three studies found associations between higher physical activity or physical function and more favourable brain aging outcomes. Nine studies reported no associations between physical (in)activity and brain aging. Overall, the limited number of available studies, most of which were cross-sectional, leaves major gaps in understanding the role of physical (in)activity in brain aging across SSA. The evidence base is methodologically heterogeneous, with inconsistent assessment methods, limited consideration of contextual factors, and lack of longitudinal data, precluding conclusions regarding causality. This highlights the need for longitudinal research within a coordinated research ecosystem in SSA to generate robust evidence that can inform policy and support healthy brain aging across the region.

items.title: Blood Pressure Management Before Intravenous Thrombolysis in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Rethinking Treatment Thresholds.
items.abstract: BackgroundElevated blood pressure (BP) is common after acute ischemic stroke (AIS), but it is unclear if it should be lowered. Lowering elevated BP may compromise the ischemic brain, while the time taken to lower BP may delay or even exclude patients from receiving intravenous thrombolysis (IVT).AimTo review the rationale, guideline recommendations, and clinical evidence informing pre-IVT BP management, with a specific focus on patients presenting with a BP above the current guideline thresholds (BP ≥185/110 mmHg).Summary of reviewCerebral autoregulation is impaired in AIS, both in the core and penumbra, creating vulnerability to harm from both excessive hypertension and BP reduction. Major trials of early or intensive BP-lowering in AIS (INTERACT4, MR-ASAP, and RIGHT-2) have either shown neutral or harmful effects with BP reduction. In the TRUTH study, a cluster-based observational comparison, centers that actively treated elevated BP before IVT achieved higher IVT rates but no better 90-day functional outcome, with a non-significant trend toward worse outcomes in the active-treatment arm. No randomized trial has helped define the optimal systolic BP target, speed of reduction, preferred antihypertensive agent, or balance of risks vs. benefits of BP reduction. prior to IVT.ConclusionsCurrent practice on BP treatment prior to IVT is guided by historical thresholds and expert consensus rather than robust evidence. Major gaps persist with respect to causal associations, individualized treatment targets, and safe BP reduction strategies. Higher quality data are needed to establish evidence-based BP management for patients presenting ≥185/110 mmHg otherwise eligible for IVT, to uniform practice towards improved patient outcomes.

items.title: Combined muscarinic receptor M<sub>1</sub> and M<sub>4</sub> stimulation reverses cocaine-induced attention deficits in male mice.
items.abstract: Background Cocaine use and cocaine use disorder (CUD) are increasing public health concerns that lack effective treatments. CUD is a chronic illness characterized by relapse, altered activity in the prefrontal cortex and neurocognitive symptoms. Pharmacologically stimulating muscarinic acetylcholine receptors M 1 and/or M 4 has been shown to counteract abuse-related effects of cocaine and, independently, to have pro-cognitive effects. Objectives We tested the hypotheses that (1) withdrawal from a subchronic cocaine regimen in mice will negatively impact attention and impulsivity and (2) pharmacological stimulation of M 1 , M 4 , or M 1 + M 4 receptors will blunt or reverse these cocaine-induced impairments. Methods Using a touchscreen rodent continuous performance test, male C57BL/6JRj mice were trained to respond to a target and withhold responses to a non-target stimulus. Mice received 20 mg/kg cocaine for 5 days and 30 mg/kg for 14 days. Then, the effect of treatment with the muscarinic M 1 agonist VU0364572 (3.2 mg/kg) and the M 4 PAM VU0152100 (1.8 mg/kg) was assessed in test probes challenging attention (variable stimulus duration) and impulsivity (variable intertrial interval), respectively. Results Cocaine exposure significantly and consistently impaired measures of attention (discriminability, accuracy), with less consistent effects on impulsivity (false alarm rate, premature responses). Treatment with combined VU0364572 + VU0152100 reversed cocaine-induced attention deficits, while each drug alone had little effect. Conclusions These findings support the hypothesis that targeting M 1 and M 4 receptors can rescue cocaine-induced cognitive symptoms. Because cognitive impairments are thought to contribute to relapse to cocaine use, these results further support M 1 /M 4 receptors as promising targets to treat CUD.

items.title: Weak cross-trophic coupling of multidimensional stability in plankton communities under multiple stressors.
items.abstract: Nutrient enrichment and biological invasions frequently co-occur in freshwater ecosystems, yet it remains unclear whether stability of entire planktonic groups responds uniformly to these combined stressors. To address this question, we conducted a fully factorial mesocosm experiment that crossed three nutrient regimes with two invasive species that impose distinct disturbance pathways. We quantified temporal stability, resistance, resilience, and recovery across functional and compositional facets in zooplankton, phytoplankton, and bacterioplankton communities. Our results revealed highly taxon- and dimension-specific responses. Snail bioturbation significantly reduced the functional resistance of zooplankton under high nutrient conditions. Meanwhile, the functional resistance of bacterioplankton declined with increasing nutrient levels. This suggests that functionally distinct stressors may affect different trophic guilds through distinct mechanisms. Species richness was consistently positively associated with compositional temporal stability, resistance and recovery across all trophic levels, but was negatively associated with resilience, revealing a fundamental trade-off between maintaining community robustness and enabling rapid adaptability. Functional and compositional stability were positively correlated only in the temporal stability dimension, but exhibited negative associations in the resistance and recovery dimensions. This indicates that biomass-related functions and community structure can follow divergent trajectories throughout perturbation and recovery. Most critically, the multivariate analyses and pairwise correlations among trophic levels indicated generally weak cross-trophic coupling, suggesting that, under the conditions of this mesocosm experiment, no single planktonic group provided a consistently reliable proxy for multidimensional whole-community stability. These findings highlight the value of assessing multiple dimensions of ecological stability across trophic groups. Consideration of stability indicators across multitrophic groups may provide complementary information for adaptive lake management as global pressures from nutrient loading and biological invasions continue to intensify.

items.title: Seaweed-based blue carbon potential of eco-engineered coastal structures.
items.abstract: Natural coastal ecosystems hold substantial capacity for blue carbon storage, but habitat replacement with harbour and shoreline infrastructure has severely diminished their potential to mitigate climate change. Enhancement of topographic complexity on coastal infrastructure through eco-engineering can increase biota abundance, such as the standing stock of long-lived seaweeds, thus positively impacting carbon capture and mitigating the carbon footprint of concrete-based infrastructure. However, ecosystem services of eco-engineered structures remain largely unquantified. Here, we assessed the seaweed biomass on a large-scale, eco-engineered seawall and show that topographically complex panels supported up to 19-fold greater blue carbon storage than flat surfaces. However, estimated panel CO 2 emissions exceeded CO 2 captures by 3- to 64-fold, after two years of seaweed growth. No retrofitted panel was realistically expected to achieve carbon neutrality within its 20-year design life, despite seaweed turnover and sequestration supporting long-term blue carbon potential. Predictive calculations, using six topographic designs, four concrete mixtures, two installation scenarios, and two detritus sequestration rates, suggested that the most efficient topography for seaweed growth, produced from low-carbon concrete and integrated during the construction phase, may achieve carbon neutrality within 15-32 years. Less effective or less sustainable scenarios were expected to require 52-277 years until carbon neutrality. An active transition towards low-carbon, integrated designs is necessary to align biodiversity-focused thinking in green infrastructure design with broader principles of sustainability and climate change mitigation.

items.title: Cadmium partitioning and maize accumulation under coal gangue and cattle manure amendments in two contrasting soils.
items.abstract: Assessing Cd behavior in agricultural soils requires consideration of total soil Cd, its operational partitioning, and crop accumulation. A 122-day greenhouse pot experiment evaluated coal gangue, air-dried cattle manure, and their mixtures in two contrasting composite soils: an acidic lower-Cd soil (LS) and a neutral-to-alkaline higher-Cd soil (HS). After cultivation, total soil Cd averaged 0.648 and 1.825 mg kg -1 in LS and HS, respectively, whereas operationally labile Cd concentrations were similar (0.195 and 0.207 mg kg -1 ). Residual Cd accounted for 19.97% of fraction-sum Cd in LS and 57.50% in HS, while mean root-associated, stem, and leaf Cd concentrations were consistently higher in LS. Among grain-bearing amended pots, mixed coal gangue-manure treatments had lower grain Cd concentrations than manure-only treatments in both soils. Mean grain Cd mass decreased from 8.94 to 2.49 μg pot -1 in LS and from 6.92 to 1.50 μg pot -1 in HS for manure-only and mixed treatments, respectively. Grain dry mass was comparable between these treatment groups in LS and slightly lower under mixed treatments in HS, indicating that the lower grain Cd was not attributable solely to biomass dilution. Ten of 18 manure-only grain samples, but none of the 29 mixed-treatment samples, exceeded the 0.10 mg kg -1 reference threshold. Because the unamended planted controls produced no grain at harvest, grain-based comparisons were restricted to grain-bearing amended pots. The contrasting soil and plant responses demonstrate that total soil Cd alone does not adequately represent crop Cd behavior. Integrating soil Cd partitioning with grain Cd concentration and Cd mass provides a more informative basis for evaluating amendment responses in soil-maize systems.

items.title: Conversational AI and the Temporal Ecology of Self-Reflection.
items.abstract: Self-reflection has historically depended on temporal transformations that no one had to arrange: memory faded and reworked what it returned, the standpoint from which the past was met shifted, and other people changed alongside the person reflecting. Conversational AI separates these transformations from the person's own. Transcripts and selective system memory may change technically, yet they persist across the interval without undergoing it as lived time, and a responsive interlocutor answers without the relational time of a history shared with the person. Drawing on cultural psychology's premise that psychological processes unfold in irreversible time and on the phenomenology of time-consciousness, the paper describes the conditions of self-reflection as a temporal ecology of memory, standpoint, other people, and artefacts, related through their differing movement across time. Externalising part of one's past into conversational systems converts regulation that once proceeded tacitly into time work: deciding whether, when, in what order, and how often to return to earlier formulations. Such work draws on attention and judgement; where it is left to defaults, it is performed by those who design and govern the systems. A system that remembers and answers may also lend earlier formulations a witness's authority. The freedom to change, once protected by the coupling of fading and inaccessibility, thus comes to depend on regulatory work distributed between persons and infrastructures, and agency over one's own past, as experienced and as exercised, becomes partly a matter of governance. The paper derives empirical questions and implications for society, wellbeing, education, and personal development.

items.title: Comparative Hippocampal and Serum Metabolomics Reveals Dose-related Metabolic Alterations Consistent with TDMQ20 Intervention in a Cu-Aβ₄₂-induced Mouse Model.
items.abstract: Copper (Cu) dyshomeostasis and metabolic dysfunction have been implicated as key drivers of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Tetradentate monoquinoline 20 (TDMQ20), a Cu chelator, reportedly improves behavioral deficits in AD model mice, but its underlying metabolic mechanism is unclear. Here, we addressed this via untargeted ultra-high performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS) metabolomics in the hippocampus and serum of AD model mice induced by intrahippocampal injection of Cu amyloid-β 42 (Cu-Aβ₄₂) and then treated with TDMQ20 at low (LT, 5 mg/kg) and high (HT, 10 mg/kg) doses. Results showed that AD was associated with tissue-specific metabolic perturbations: hippocampal disorders were enriched in linoleic acid and glycerophospholipid metabolism, while serum perturbations centered on tryptophan, sphingolipid, and purine metabolism, with organic acids, lipids, and benzenoids as core differential metabolite classes. TDMQ20 reversed these abnormalities in a dose-associated manner: LT regulated tryptophan/linoleic acid metabolism in the hippocampus and purine/arachidonic acid metabolism in serum, while HT shifted the hippocampal metabolic profile substantially toward that of the control group. Cross-matrix analysis identified PS (15:0/22:0) and LPC (18:2/0:0) as key lipid metabolites with opposite expression patterns between hippocampus and serum, and four serum endogenous metabolites (pipecolic acid, PGG2, N-sulfo-D-glucosamine, and hex-2-ulose) as exploratory candidate metabolites. TDMQ20 was associated with metabolomic changes in both hippocampus and serum consistent with attenuated oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and membrane lipid remodeling, suggesting preferential central metabolic modulation and dose-associated action. This study provides metabolomic evidence consistent with TDMQ20's potential tissue-resolved regulatory properties and identifies exploratory candidate metabolites for monitoring therapeutic efficacy in AD.

items.title: A New "Asexual Scandal": Independent Evolution of Ancient Planarian Fissiparous Lineages Challenges Phylogenetic Reconstruction Methods.
items.abstract: Phylogenetic methods typically generate bifurcating trees reflecting monophyletic groups formed by populations. However, unexpected topologies sometimes emerge, raising questions about whether they stem from methodological artifacts or biological phenomena. In a recent transcriptome-based study of Dugesia species, asexual populations displayed an unusual phylogenetic pattern: instead of forming monophyletic groups, each individual emerged as a long-branched independent lineage, resulting in a distinctive "ladder-pattern." While such a pattern could result from methodological issues, its exclusive presence in asexual populations suggests a biological explanation-long-term asexuality. Traditionally considered evolutionary dead ends due to reduced genetic diversity and weakened purifying selection, extant long-term asexual lineages challenge these assumptions, being popularly known as "asexual scandals". Here, we test both hypotheses: first, assessing whether the ladder-pattern arises from methodological artifacts, and second, examining expected genomic signatures of prolonged asexuality or hybridization. Using transcriptomic and nuclear marker datasets, we employ state-of-the-art phylogenetic methodologies and intraindividual genetic diversity analyses. Our results confirm that the ladder-pattern is not an artifact. Comparative analyses with other fissiparous planarian lineages support the deep evolutionary history of these asexual populations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that retained ancestral polymorphisms obscure phylogenetic signals. Our findings highlight the limitations of traditional phylogenetic methods in the context of asexuality and underscore the need to renew the models traditionally used in evolutionary studies.

items.title: Modeling association networks from metagenome time series - a proof-of-concept from two contrasting estuaries.
items.abstract: Understanding microbial responses to environmental gradients is important for ecosystem assessment in estuarine environments. Here, we integrated time-series samples and shotgun metagenomics with association network inference, to examine patterns of taxonomic and functional co-variation. We collected and sequenced eDNA from two sediment time series from neighbouring but environmentally contrasting Basque estuaries, and compared the resulting taxonomic and functional association networks, based on Metagenome Assembled Genomes (MAGs) and KEGG Orthologous Groups (KOs), respectively. Networks inferred using 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding data were also included in this comparison. Several topology-based network properties differed strongly between the two sites, although differences were not always consistent when comparing the networks based on MAGs, KOs and metabarcoding. KO-based networks revealed distinct sets of associated Ortholog groups between sites, consistent with known environmental differences. Contrary to our expectations, metabolically related genes rarely formed complete pathway modules in gene networks, likely due to functional redundancy, gene copy number variation, synchronized pathway dynamics, or algorithmic constraints of correlation-based inference. Overall, the results illustrate both the potential and interpretative limitations of metagenome-based time association networks for functional ecosystem assessment, and support their use as hypothesis-generating tools that require further validation across a larger range of sites following environmental gradients.

items.title: Experimental evolution of Chlamydomonas reinhardtii in fluctuating versus constant temperature stress.
items.abstract: Human-driven climate change has amplified the magnitude and reduced the predictability of natural environmental fluctuations. Temperature, a major physiological stressor, is rising in both its mean and the frequency of extremes. Understanding how organisms adapt to shifts in both thermal mean and variability is therefore critical for predicting their performance under future climates. Here, we investigated the standing variation in thermal optima of ten Chlamydomonas reinhardtii strains from a broad geographic sample. We then experimentally evolved one strain for ∼900 generations under three distinct temperature stress conditions: cold, hot and fluctuating. We found that those grown in constant environmental conditions became specialized to their environment of 20°C or 37°C. Contrary to our prediction that adaptation to fluctuating temperatures would compromise fitness at each extreme, those evolved in a fluctuating regime performed comparably to the specialists, suggesting no long-term cost of this generalist phenotype. We also tested the prediction that replicate lines evolved in a fluctuating regime may diverge from one another more than temperature specialists, but found no difference in the amount of among-line variance between growth regimes. Overall, despite our predictions that a fluctuating regime would hinder adaptation, we found a high degree of adaptability even when evolved in a variable environment.

items.title: Impact of Two High-Fiber Dietary Transitions on Fecal Consistency and Microbiota Composition in Captive Dromedary Camels (Camelus dromedarius) With Chronic Recurrent Diarrhea: A Pilot Study.
items.abstract: Dietary fiber is a central driver of gut function in camelids, yet empirical data on how specific fiber sources shape hind-gut ecology remain scarce. This longitudinal pilot study assessed the impact of two sequential high-fiber dietary transitions on fecal consistency and microbiota in five captive dromedary camels (Camelus dromedarius). Over 63 days, straw was offered ad libitum alongside hay; this was followed by a 25-day phased replacement of a lower-fiber concentrate with a high-fiber pellet. Daily fecal scores were recorded, and 98 samples (74 fecal and 24 environmental swab samples) were analyzed using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, with PICRUSt2 used to predict functional profiles from fecal microbiota data. Straw supplementation did not noticeably change group-level fecal consistency, although individual responses were pronounced, with some camels showing increases of up to +2.5 score units. In contrast, high-fiber pellets softened feces at the group level, with a median increase in score of +1.2 and the largest effects observed in two animals. Fecal scores were positively correlated with ambient temperature (Pearson's r up to 0.67). Alpha diversity remained stable or rose slightly during the straw phase but declined transiently during pellet transition, returning to baseline by Day 25. Core hind-gut families (Oscillospiraceae, Rikenellaceae, and Christensenellaceae) persisted throughout; pellet feeding prompted short-lived blooms of Monoglobaceae and Methanocorpusculaceae. Despite taxonomic shifts, functional profiles were dominated by amino-acid, nucleotide, and vitamin biosynthesis, with only modest, reversible increases in polysaccharide-degradation pathways during pellet feeding. Follow-up sampling approximately one year later revealed a relatively stable microbial community during the control period. Collectively, these findings suggest that incremental fiber enrichment may elicit distinct, animal-specific gastrointestinal and microbial adjustments in dromedaries, but metabolic functions remain apparently resilient. These findings suggest individualized dietary management when deploying fiber-based strategies to mitigate diarrhea in captive camelids.

items.title: RNA viruses as drivers of rapid diatom succession within a single bloom event.
items.abstract: Diatoms frequently dominate seasonal phytoplankton blooms and contribute ~40% of marine primary production. Viruses drive phytoplankton mortality and bloom collapse, yet how viruses regulate diatom bloom dynamics is not well resolved. Here, using quantitative metatranscriptomics, we tracked temporal patterns of diatoms and associated viruses at near-daily resolution during the spring bloom in the Gulf of Aqaba, Red Sea. We captured distinct phases and rapid restructuring within both the diatom community and cell-associated virosphere. Diatom transcriptional profiling indicated activation of stress and death pathways prior to taxon-specific demise. RNA viruses emerged as dominant players within the bloom, with fluctuations of putative diatom-infecting RNA viruses across intracellular and extracellular fractions revealing sequential waves of active virus infection that were consistent with virus-mediated diatom mortality. Correlation and codon usage analyses further implicated specific diatom taxa as putative hosts for the identified RNA viruses. Rather than a uniform 'boom and bust', the spring diatom bloom comprised a mosaic of overlapping successional waves of diatom and viral taxa unfolding on daily timescales. These findings support RNA viruses as drivers of diatom turnover, advancing our understanding of how viruses temporally structure diverse diatom assemblages and the biogeochemical trajectory of diatom blooms in marine systems.

items.title: Plant Nutrient Homeostasis In A Rising CO2 World.
items.abstract: The rapid rise in atmospheric CO2 concentration presents a critical paradox for global agriculture: while it stimulates photosynthesis and plant productivity, it simultaneously compromises crop nutritional quality. This decline in quality is linked to a lower concentration of essential macro- and micronutrients in crop edible parts, involving complex regulatory shifts that go beyond the simple growth dilution effect caused by the decoupling between growth and nutrient uptake. In this review, we summarize the current knowledge regarding the impact of elevated CO2 (eCO2) on nitrogen (N) nutrition, among other aspects, discussing how the availability of nitrate (NO3-) or ammonium (NH4+) affects plant growth and N status under eCO2, a long-standing debate in the field. We outline recent advances in the signalling mechanisms regulating NO3- uptake under eCO2 and discuss the interaction between photorespiration and the assimilation of both N sources. Likewise, we address the main effects and regulatory mechanisms associated with eCO2 and the homeostasis of sulphur (S), phosphorus (P) and the micronutrients iron (Fe) and zinc (Zn). Collectively, we intend to provide a comprehensive framework to guide future crop breeding and climate-resilient agronomic management.

items.title: Spatial abilities and wayfinding inclinations in orienteering: Evidence from elite and expert athletes.
items.abstract: Orienteering is a sport based on spatial navigation, the ability to move and reach destinations. Elite athletes, i.e., those competing at the highest level of competition, display distinctive cognitive abilities. However, the practice of this sport at different levels of competition in relation to spatial cognitive abilities and everyday navigation inclinations has not been examined extensively. The current study examines the relationship between different degrees of orienteering practice and a variety of cognitive spatial abilities and inclinations. A total of 122 participants (16-45 years) took part: 32 elites (those competing at national and internation levels), 45 experts (those competing at amateur level) with a similar number of years of experience (≈15) and competitions per year (≈ 27) and 45 non-athletes. Participants completed a series of spatial tasks assessing intrinsic (object-to-object relation based) and extrinsic (subject-to-object relation based), dynamic and static abilities, and everyday navigation strategy questionnaires. The results showed that both elite and experts orienteers performed better in spatial extrinsic tasks, while only elite performed better in spatial intrinsic tasks compared to non-athletes. Both elite and experts had higher everyday navigation inclinations. In the elite group, better championship ranking was associated with lower self-reported spatial anxiety. Overall, these findings support the association between orienteering, a spatial navigation practice, with spatial cognitive abilities and everyday navigation inclinations, showing that for elites these are more object-to-object based.

items.title: Synchronization of the nucleus accumbens-ventral hippocampus reflects cooperative ability and predicts social dysfunction after training in mice.
items.abstract: Abstract Cooperation is a fundamental form of social behavior that promotes collective benefits and group survival. Although considerable progress has been made in understanding cooperation from behavioral and theoretical perspectives, the neural activities underlying cooperative behavior remain incompletely understood. In the present study, we established a cooperative behavioral paradigm in pairs of mice using a Skinner box, with the protocol spanning 22 days. Mice were retrospectively classified into high-, middle-, and low-performance groups based on their performance in the cooperation task. In vivo local field potential recordings from the nucleus accumbens and ventral hippocampus were then conducted in the three groups. High-cooperation mice showed significantly increased delta and low-gamma power in the nucleus accumbens, as well as enhanced delta, theta, beta, and low-gamma power in the ventral hippocampus, compared to low-cooperation mice. Meanwhile, nucleus accumbens-ventral hippocampus coherence within the beta and low-gamma frequency bands was significantly reduced in high-cooperation animals. Behaviorally, high-cooperation mice exhibited social dysfunction as shown by reduced social interaction and more pronounced anxiety-like behaviors compared with low-cooperation mice after training. Collectively, these findings provide early evidence that individual differences in cooperative behavior are associated with distinct patterns of neural oscillatory activity within the nucleus accumbens-ventral hippocampus circuit. Moreover, enhanced cooperative performance was correlated with alterations in social and affective behavior, such as increased social avoidance and anxiety-like behavior. The results suggest that nucleus accumbens-ventral hippocampus oscillatory dynamics may represent a neural correlate of cooperative behavior, and that training-induced differences in cooperative performance are associated with subsequent changes in social and affective functioning.

items.title: Digital Culture, Reflexivity and Care Erosion in Nursing: A Conceptual Model of Reflexive Dissonance Failure.
items.abstract: Aim(s) To examine how digitally mediated social environments may interact with nurses' reflexive capacity, professional values and responses to bias, and to develop Reflexive Dissonance Failure (RDF) as a conceptual model for understanding one possible pathway from ethical dissonance to care erosion. Design Discussion paper. Methods This discussion paper uses a critical conceptual synthesis of interdisciplinary literature from nursing, psychology, sociology, ethics and digital media studies. Literature was purposively selected for conceptual relevance to reflexivity, cognitive dissonance, digital influence, implicit bias, moral disengagement, epistemic injustice, compassionate care and care erosion. The synthesis was used to derive and critically examine the proposed RDF model rather than to estimate effects or claim exhaustive evidence coverage. Results Digital environments may amplify emotionally salient, selective or stereotype-reinforcing content, but they can also support professional learning, peer connection, advocacy and exposure to diverse perspectives. In the proposed RDF model, cognitive dissonance is treated as a potentially protective ethical signal when a judgement or response conflicts with personal, moral or professional standards. Reflexive engagement may support critical reappraisal and adaptive resolution; RDF refers specifically to situations in which this dissonance is absent, suppressed, ignored or maladaptively resolved through denial, justification, distraction or normalisation. These processes may increase vulnerability to moral disengagement, epistemic injustice and care erosion, although direct causal evidence in nursing remains limited. Conclusion RDF is proposed as a testable conceptual model rather than an established causal pathway. It reframes digital influence as one contextual factor that may interact with nurses' ethical agency, reflective capacity, organisational conditions and professional values. The model provides a basis for research on reflexivity, misinformation, bias, compassionate care and equity, while supporting strengths-based educational and organisational strategies for digitally mediated nursing practice.

items.title: Recovery Curves for the PHQ-8 and GAD-7: Clinical Utility and Implementation of Measurement-based Care in a Real-world Outpatient Setting.
items.abstract: Measurement-based care (MBC) relies on repeated outcome assessment and feedback to guide clinical decision-making. Although recovery curves are central to many MBC systems, they have primarily been developed using session-by-session data. This study developed and validated recovery curves for the PHQ-8 and GAD-7 using monthly assessments within a naturalistic outpatient setting. We generated our recovery curves using mixed-effects models with symptom change over four months of treatment as the dependent variable (N = 1124) and cross-validated the results in a second sample (PHQ-8 N = 734; GAD-7 N = 758). Models were evaluated for predictive performance and calibration. We examined additional baseline predictors and evaluated confidence interval thresholds for identifying patients at risk of treatment failure. Predictive performance was strong in the derivation sample (PHQ-8 R² = 0.44; GAD-7 R² = 0.47) and remained robust in validation (PHQ-8 R² = 0.37; GAD-7 R² = 0.40) with acceptable calibration. Baseline symptom severity was the only clinically meaningful predictor of recovery trajectories. A 60% one-sided confidence interval provided the optimal balance of sensitivity and alert frequency, identifying approximately 24-28% of patients as at risk of treatment failure at one month. We conclude that recovery curves for the PHQ-8 and GAD-7 can be effectively derived using monthly assessments and applied in real-world MBC settings.

items.title: Rewriting professional identity: a self-authorship perspective on neurodivergent learners in health professions education.
items.abstract: Professional identity formation in health professions education is often conceptualised as socialisation into established professional norms and values. For neurodivergent learners, however, these norms may reflect assumptions that privilege neurotypical ways of thinking, communicating, and behaving. While professional identity formation has been explored among other minoritised learners, less is known about how neurodivergent learners navigate this process. This study explored how neurodivergent graduates of Australian health professions programs constructed professional identities. Twelve neurodivergent health professionals participated in semi-structured interviews or provided written responses. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, informed by Baxter Magolda's theory of self-authorship. Participants initially encountered narrow archetypes of the "ideal health professional" that were shaped by assumptions about capability, professionalism, and neurotypical behaviour. These expectations generated identity dissonance, concerns about disclosure, and pressure to mask neurodivergent traits. Over time, participants developed greater self-recognition of their strengths, needs, and preferred ways of practising. This enabled them to critically question dominant constructions of professionalism and to rework professional identities in ways that were more authentic, sustainable, and aligned with their values. Rather than simply assimilating into existing norms, participants actively expanded and reshaped understandings of what competent and compassionate healthcare practice can look like. Viewed through the lens of self-authorship, these findings highlight how professional identity formation for neurodivergent learners involves negotiating, resisting, and reconstructing professional norms. In response, educators could move beyond supporting learners to conform to dominant professional archetypes and instead create educational environments that recognise diverse ways of being, foster self-authorship, and broaden understandings of professionalism within the health professions.

items.title: The Interplay Between Depression and Cardiovascular Disease: Mechanisms, Clinical Implications, and Emerging Therapeutic Perspectives.
items.abstract: Purpose of review Depression and cardiovascular disease (CVD) frequently co-occur and contribute substantially to global morbidity and mortality. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the biological, psychological, and clinical mechanisms connecting these two conditions. The aim is to clarify the key pathways underlying their bidirectional relationship and to highlight therapeutic strategies that may improve outcomes in individuals affected by both disorders. Recent findings Recent studies increasingly demonstrate that depression and CVD share multifaceted biological mechanisms, including hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysregulation, systemic inflammation, autonomic imbalance, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and genetic and epigenetic alterations. Immunological activity, particularly cytokine-mediated neuroinflammation, has emerged as a central component linking mood dysregulation with vascular pathology. Behavioral and psychosocial pathways also contribute to cardiovascular risk. Adverse health behaviors, including physical inactivity, poor diet, smoking, substance use, sleep disturbance, and treatment nonadherence, may directly contribute to cardiovascular risk, while psychosocial factors such as chronic stress and social isolation may influence or amplify these behavioral and biological pathways. Additionally, precision-medicine strategies that incorporate genetic, metabolic, and psychosocial profiles are increasingly recognized as important for optimizing individualized care. Depression and CVD are interconnected through a complex web of biological and psychosocial pathways that mutually reinforce disease progression. Understanding these shared mechanisms is critical for improving prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. Integrated, multidisciplinary management, addressing inflammation, autonomic dysfunction, lifestyle factors, and mental health, is essential to reduce morbidity in this high-risk population. Future research should continue exploring biomarkers and personalized interventions to better manage this intertwined comorbidity.

items.title: Sleep deprivation disrupts error awareness and subsequent behavioural regulation.
items.abstract: Study objectives Sleep deprivation is known to impair cognitive performance, yet its effects on error awareness and subsequent behavioural adjustments remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated how sleep loss affects the use of subjective performance evaluation to guide post-error adaptations. Methods Thirty healthy adults completed a novel, gamified error awareness multi-rule Simon task once while well rested and once after one night of total sleep deprivation. On each trial, participants reported both their task response and subjective evaluation of response accuracy. This design allowed us to dissociate objective performance from subjective error awareness and to examine their influence on subsequent behaviour over time. Results Sleep deprivation slowed responses, reduced accuracy, increased missed responses, and decreased the proportion of consciously detected errors, with impairments increasing over time on task. Both objective errors and subjective error judgements were associated with subsequent slowing. When well rested, subjective-error-associated slowing exceeded objective-error-associated slowing. This difference was reduced under sleep deprivation. Specifically, objectively correct responses judged as errors were followed by slowing relative to correctly judged correct responses, and this slowing was attenuated under sleep deprivation. Accuracy showed post-error decreases that were most pronounced following objective errors. Conclusions Together, the findings indicate that sleep deprivation reduces error awareness and is associated with altered post-error behavioural regulation.

items.title: Dentists' Temporomandibular Disorder-Related Education, Knowledge, Attitudes and Behavior: How Do Personal and Educational Experiences Matter?
items.abstract: Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) affect 5%-12% of US adults. The objectives were to assess dentists' TMD-related education, knowledge, attitudes, and behavior and to explore whether TMD-related experiences were associated with these constructs. A total of 296 dentists responded to a survey. Descriptive statistics provided an overview of the results, and Pearson correlation coefficients described the relationships between dentists' TMD experiences, knowledge, attitudes, and behavior. Only 17.2% were satisfied with classroom-based and 10.1% with clinic-based TMD-related education; 29.6% described their classroom-based and 17.8% their clinic-based education about TMD diagnosis positively; 37.7% were confident in their TMD-related knowledge, but 94.1% recognized their limitations when managing TMD. The majority agreed that TMD is a physical/anatomical problem (87.3%), behavioral problem (74.3%), psychosocial problem (71.6%), and that stress plays a role for TMD (93.1%). Most dentists had positive attitudes toward diagnosing TMD (82.8%), felt responsible for treating TMD (63.1%), regularly saw patients with TMD (58.2%), and screened patients for TMD (67%). Concerning treatments utilized, 63.3% used occlusal appliances, while only 23.6% prescribed medications. 43% had experienced TMD themselves. The more persons they knew with TMD, the more treatment-related knowledge they reported (r = 0.26; p < 0.001), the more positive were their attitudes (r = 0.16; p < 0.01), the more comfortable they were treating TMD (r = 0.25; p < 0.001), and the more they cared for patients with TMD (r = 0.34; p < 0.001). TMD-related dental and continuing education should reconsider classroom- and clinic-based TMD training. Personal TMD experiences correlate with more positive attitudes and behavior. This should alert dental educators to the importance of engaging students and dentists in hands-on education.

items.title: The Effect of Leader Knowledge Theft on Employees' Unethical Behavior: The Roles of Perceived Contextual Impunity and Role Ethicality.
items.abstract: Although leader knowledge theft has garnered growing attention, our understanding of its implicit costs remains incomplete. Drawing on social information processing theory and role theory, this study examines the underlying mechanisms and boundary conditions through which leader knowledge theft influences employee unethical behavior. To empirically test this model, we collected three-wave data from 425 full-time employees in China. The results reveal that leader knowledge theft fosters employees' perceived contextual impunity, which subsequently promotes their unethical behavior. Furthermore, employee role ethicality plays a critical moderating role in this process. Specifically, high role ethicality buffers the positive relationship between perceived contextual impunity and unethical behavior. Finally, we discuss the theoretical contributions and practical implications of these findings regarding leader knowledge theft, perceived contextual impunity, and unethical behavior.

items.title: Implicit Self-Death Associations and Symptoms of Depression and Anxiety: A Single-Case Experimental Design.
items.abstract: Death anxiety may operate as a transdiagnostic process underlying anxiety and depressive symptoms. This study used the Death-Implicit Association Task (D-IAT) to index implicit self-death associations (ISDA) and evaluated a brief mindfulness intervention using a concurrent multiple-baseline design with maintenance across four students with prior anxiety/depressive diagnoses. Across 20 daily sessions, D-IAT D-scores and Mini-DASS depression and anxiety scores were collected. Visual analysis suggested reductions in depression and anxiety for several participants, with lower scores often persisting into maintenance. Casewise Tau-b patterns were heterogeneous. Exact randomisation tests showed a significant reduction in anxiety from baseline to intervention ( p = .04), while the reduction in depression was nonsignificant ( p = .08). Neither outcome showed a significant baseline-to-maintenance effect, and D-scores showed no significant reduction. Findings provide partial support for mindfulness-related symptom change but no evidence of corresponding change in ISDA.

items.title: Surveillance of digital marketing strategies for online alcohol sales in Thailand: A comparative study before and after the 2025 selling time extension.
items.abstract: Background Digital alcohol marketing may increase exposure to alcohol-related cues and undermine harm prevention. Changes in alcohol availability may influence online promotion, but before-after comparisons cannot establish policy effects. We compared alcohol marketing posts before and after Thailand's December 2025 extension of legal alcohol sales hours. Methods We conducted a repeated cross-sectional content analysis. Of 1419 eligible Thai-language posts, the main analysis included 1384 posts from Facebook, Instagram and LINE (811 pre-reform; 573 post-reform). AI-assisted coding combined dictionary and contextual rules with manual validation. Modified Poisson models estimated prevalence ratios adjusted for platform and source type, with account-clustered standard errors. All 14 content features were exploratory, with false discovery rate correction. Results Restaurants, pubs and bars contributed 40.7% of pre-reform and 45.9% of post-reform posts, while influencers contributed 17.6% and 11.7%. The higher share from official brand pages disappeared after excluding sponsored posts, which were captured only post-reform. Adjusted estimates indicated higher prevalence of evasive language (aPR 1.12, 95% CI 1.01-1.24) and lower prevalence of urgency (0.84, 0.69-1.01) and fear-of-missing-out (FOMO) messaging (0.87, 0.75-1.02); none remained statistically significant after FDR correction (minimum q = 0.408). Conclusion Posts differed mainly in source composition. Lower urgency and FOMO messaging were compatible with a reduction in the relevance of time-limited purchasing appeals following the extension, but seasonality, concurrent advertising-law changes and retrieval differences prevent attribution to the reform. Longer-term surveillance and stronger comparative designs are needed to evaluate whether changes in alcohol availability are associated with changes in marketing, exposure and alcohol-related outcomes.

items.title: The geopolitical architecture of public health: Integrating political literacy and diplomacy into academic and practical training.
items.abstract: Objective Contemporary public health is increasingly shaped by geopolitical forces including populism, widening inequalities, climate and environmental crises, industrialised disinformation, shifting systems of global power, and the influence of state and non-state actors. Yet these determinants remain insufficiently addressed within traditional public health education and training. Study design This short communication argues for the integration of Geopolitical Health into public health curricula as a practical and logical response to this changing landscape. Methods This communication is a conceptual report which draws on the inclusion of Geopolitical Health within the ASPHER Core Curriculum for Public Health. Results The report highlights the importance of political literacy, strategic communication, systems thinking, ethical negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and public health diplomacy. We further propose simulation-based diplomacy laboratories as a means of translating these competencies into practice. Conclusion Preparing public health professionals to understand and navigate complex political environments is increasingly essential to protecting evidence, equity, public trust, and population health in an era of geopolitical instability and contested public health narratives.

items.title: Global research on urban density and health: A bibliometric analysis of trends, themes, and research priorities.
items.abstract: Urban density is a central concern in urban design and public health, yet evidence on its relationships with health is dispersed across disciplines. This study used bibliometric methods to map the global research landscape on urban density and health, and to identify publication trends, themes, key contributors, and research priorities. A search of the Web of Science Core Collection in May 2025 combined terms for density, health, and urban context. English-language articles and reviews were screened, cleaned, and analysed. Performance analysis and science mapping techniques, including co-authorship, co-citation, and keyword co-occurrence, were conducted using VOSviewer. The dataset comprised 1,670 publications published between 1965 and 2025, with marked growth after 2019. Research output was concentrated in high-income countries, particularly the Global North, with no African country among the most productive contributors. Frequently co-cited sources showed a multidisciplinary field spanning public health, urban design, and physical activity research. Keyword analysis identified nine clusters. Built environment, walkability, and physical activity formed the core. Green space and metabolic health appeared as a distinct but less prominent cluster. These findings show that density-health research has been organised mainly around built environment and movement-related pathways. Psychosocial, environmental exposure, and equity-related pathways remain less integrated. For urban health practice, the findings identify evidence gaps that are relevant to policy and planning. These patterns indicate a need for broader geographical coverage, stronger attention to non-mobility and psychosocial pathways, clearer and more comparable density measures, and deeper cross-disciplinary integration to generate evidence that can better inform healthy densification policies.

items.title: Radiography managers' views on coaching and mentoring as an essential leadership development tool: A qualitative study.
items.abstract: Introduction Providing high-quality radiography services requires motivated and self-sufficient managers. Leadership can be developed through coaching and mentoring, yet few studies have examined these practices in radiography settings. This qualitative study explored the views and perceptions of radiography managers employed in public healthcare institutions regarding the role of coaching and mentoring in facilitating the transition into management and supporting ongoing leadership development. Methods This study was conducted in healthcare institutions in Gauteng Province, South Africa. Radiographers employed as managers of radiography departments were purposively sampled, and data were collected using semi-structured interviews. The data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis approach. Results Twenty-two radiography managers participated. Five themes emerged from the interviews: 1) management preparedness, 2) conceptualization of coaching, 3) conceptualization of mentoring, 4) transition into management positions, and 5) systemic and organizational factors influencing coaching and mentoring. Radiography managers'reflections indicated that they struggled to transition into management roles and that formalized coaching and mentoring programs tailored to radiography managers were needed. Conclusion Radiography managers perceive coaching and mentoring as valuable tools for developing leadership competencies. The managers in this study believed that coaching and mentoring would have eased their transition into management roles. Plain language summary Radiography managers need leadership skills to run services effectively, and coaching and mentoring may help them develop these skills. This study interviewed radiography managers in public healthcare institutions in South Africa about their experiences of moving into management roles and their views on coaching and mentoring. This study found that many managers struggled with the transition to leadership positions and believed that structured coaching and mentoring programs would have helped them develop confidence and management skills. This matters because stronger leadership support may help managers perform their roles more effectively and contribute to high-quality radiography services.

items.title: Health Services Utilization by Individuals With Eating Disorders in Norway: A Nationwide Register-Linkage Study.
items.abstract: Objective This study investigated healthcare utilization by individuals with an eating disorder (ED) stratified by age and ED diagnosis. Method Data were retrieved from the Norwegian Patient Registry (NPR) and the Control and Payment of Health Reimbursements (KUHR). Individuals aged 6-69 years registered with a primary ED diagnosis (ICD-10, F50.0-50.9) between 2015 and 2020 were included. Treatment cycles were defined as a sequence of specialist contacts preceded by and followed by a 48-month lag period. Treatment duration from diagnosis to end-of-treatment was assessed using time-to-event analysis. Results 10,782 individuals were included; 91.8% female. Nearly half (48.3%) were diagnosed with anorexia nervosa (AN; F50.0-50.1), which had the longest median treatment duration (3.1 years), compared with BN (1.6 years) and other EDs (1.3 years). Individuals under 18 were predominantly treated for AN (67.9%). Within 2 years of diagnosis, 29.7% had received inpatient care (median 56 days), while 3.5% received day treatment. Prior to diagnosis, patients had a median of 4.5 GP visits, 62% of which were coded as somatic-related. Discussion Individuals with EDs exhibited substantial utilization of primary and specialised care, with intensive and prolonged specialist care for AN, especially among younger women. Frequent GP consultations highlight primary care as an important setting for earlier ED detection.

items.title: Oleanolic acid-hesperetin co-assembled nanoparticles alleviate neurological injury after ischemic stroke via the PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β axis.
items.abstract: Abstract Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of death and long-term disability, while the current clinically applicable adjunctive neuroprotective strategies face substantial limitations. Oleanolic acid and hesperetin exhibit synergistic antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic activities; however, their poor aqueous solubility and limited bioavailability remain major limitations to their therapeutic development. Oleanolic acid and hesperetin were formulated as co-assembled nanoparticles using an emulsion-solvent evaporation method. A 5:2 mass ratio of oleanolic acid to hesperetin produced primarily spherical nanoparticles with a mean hydrodynamic diameter of approximately 282.6 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.197, and a zeta potential of -12.2 mV. Oleanolic acid-hesperetin nanoparticles displayed minimal hemolysis (0.199%) while maintaining a stable hydrodynamic diameter during 30 days of storage. Spectroscopic analyses and a 50 ns molecular dynamics simulation promoted co-assembly via multiple noncovalent-driven interactions. Oleanolic acid-hesperetin nanoparticles effectively reduced oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion-induced viability loss and apoptosis in HT22 cells. In transient middle cerebral artery occlusion mice, Cy5.5-associated fluorescence was observed in brain tissue, whereas oleanolic acid-hesperetin nanoparticle treatment reduced infarct volume and ipsilesional brain water content, preserved neurons, resulting in improved sensorimotor and spatial cognitive outcomes through day 28. Treatment promoted PI3K and AKT phosphorylation, elevated inhibitory phosphorylation of glycogen synthase kinase 3β at Ser9 and BCL-2 expression, and reduced BAX expression. These findings suggest that oleanolic acid-hesperetin co-assembly offers a promising preclinical formulation approach for multifactorial neuroprotection after ischemic stroke and supports further pharmacokinetic, safety, and pathway-causality studies.

items.title: Sex Differences in the Association Between Child Sexual Abuse and Machine-Based Gambling: Findings from a National Survey.
items.abstract: This cross-sectional study examined the association between child sexual abuse (CSA) and machine-based gambling. Evidence on this association remains limited regarding sex differences. Data came from 27,699 adults aged 18 to 79 in the 2023 Japan COVID-19 and Society Internet Survey (JACSIS). Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) with stabilized weights addressed confounding, and sex-stratified models tested for effect modification. Of 27,699 participants, 2,567 (9.3%) reported CSA before age 18. After IPTW adjustment, CSA was associated with higher prevalence of machine-based gambling (risk difference [RD]: 10.8% points [ppts], 95% confidence interval [CI]: 9.2 to 12.3, p < .001). The risk difference was larger among males (14.0 ppts, 95% CI: 11.3 to 16.7) than among females (8.4 ppts, 95% CI: 6.7 to 10.2, interaction p = .008). CSA showed a lasting association with machine-based gambling in adulthood, and the association concentrated among males. Trauma-informed approaches in gambling treatment and mental health settings should consider CSA history among survivors.

items.title: IgY-Based Immunotherapy Against MDR/XDR/PDR Bacterial Infections: Mechanisms and Experimental Evidence From In Vitro and In Vivo Studies.
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has emerged as one of the greatest threats to global public health, largely driven by the rapid dissemination of multidrug-resistant (MDR), extensively drug-resistant (XDR), and pan-drug-resistant (PDR) bacterial pathogens. The limited antibacterial pipeline, together with the declining effectiveness of conventional antibiotics, highlights the urgent need for alternative therapeutic strategies. Among emerging immunotherapeutic approaches, immunoglobulin Y (IgY), the principal antibody found in egg yolk, has attracted increasing attention because of its high specificity, favorable safety profile, ethical and scalable production, and low propensity to promote antimicrobial resistance. Experimental evidence consistently demonstrates that pathogen-specific IgY exhibits potent antibacterial activity against priority MDR pathogens, including Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Salmonella enterica. Across multiple in vitro and animal studies, IgY reduced bacterial burden, inhibited biofilm formation and bacterial motility, enhanced opsonophagocytic clearance, attenuated inflammatory responses, improved survival, and frequently restored or potentiated the activity of conventional antibiotics. Recent advances in inhalable formulations, nanoparticle-based delivery systems, and combination therapies further expand the translational potential of IgY for managing difficult-to-treat bacterial infections. Therefore, current evidence supports IgY as a promising immunotherapeutic strategy that may complement conventional antimicrobial therapy and, in selected settings, potentially serve as an alternative to antibiotics. Although encouraging preclinical findings have accumulated, additional well-designed clinical trials, standardized manufacturing protocols, and optimized delivery platforms are essential to define the clinical settings in which IgY can safely and effectively be used alone or alongside conventional antimicrobial therapy.

items.title: Bioprospecting perchlorate-reducing bacteria: report of the genera Psychrobacter, Planococcus, Carnobacterium, and Paeniglutamicibacter isolated in Cierva Point, Antarctica, and its contribution to SDG 3.
items.abstract: Perchlorate (ClO4-) is a global contaminant that has been detected in various environmental matrices. ClO4- is considered an emerging pollutant because of its potent endocrine-disrupting effects, which impairs iodine uptake in the thyroid gland, and its high toxicity and persistence. Therefore, the development of technologies for its reduction in ecosystems is imperative; bioremediation is a promising technology for ClO4- reduction. In this study, bacterial strains isolated from marine sediments at Cierva Point, an Antarctic Specially Protected Area (ASPA No. 134), were characterized. The methodology consisted of four stages: i) isolation of the bacterial strains; ii) characterization of isolated strains by morphological, biochemical, and molecular traits; iii) susceptibility tests against NaCl and ClO4-; iv) ClO4- removal assays using a selective electrode. The strains grew at 10 °C for 7 days and tolerated NaCl concentrations up to 30% w/v. All isolates grew at ClO4- concentrations of 10,000 mg/L, and five isolates also grew at 15,000 mg/L. Phylogenetic analysis identified members of the genera Psychrobacter, Planococcus, Carnobacterium, and Paeniglutamicibacter, capable of removing the contaminant in percentages between 40% and 52%. In alignment with UN Sustainable Development Goal 3 on promoting health and well-being, this project supports both ecosystem conservation and public health protection. In conclusion, the bacterial strains isolated from Cierva Point marine sediments, Antarctica, represent valuable resources for the bioremediation of ClO4- contamination, demonstrating significant potential to reduce and mitigate the pollutant in affected ecosystems.

items.title: Copy number variants across the developmental epilepsy-developmental and epileptic encephalopathy spectrum: an Indonesian case series.
items.abstract: Developmental epilepsy (DE) and developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) comprise neurodevelopmental disorders in which epilepsy occurs alongside developmental impairment of varying contributions from the underlying etiology and epileptic activity. Advances in genetic testing, including whole-exome sequencing (WES), whole-genome sequencing (WGS), and chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA), have facilitated the identification of copy number variants (CNVs); however, data on CNV-associated epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders remain limited in Southeast Asia, including Indonesia. This retrospective case series describes the clinical and genetic characteristics of four Indonesian children across the DE-DEE spectrum with pathogenic CNVs identified at a tertiary referral hospital in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Among 48 patients who underwent WES, CNVs were identified in five; four underwent further genetic characterization and were included in this case series, while one patient died before additional testing could be performed. Clinical manifestations included early-onset seizures, developmental delay or intellectual impairment, and abnormal EEG and/or neuroimaging findings. Genetic findings included a 2q24.3 deletion involving SCN1A in a patient with Dravet syndrome and 15q11.2-q13.1 deletions involving UBE3A in three patients with clinical features of Angelman syndrome. Confirmatory testing using WGS or CMA further characterized the identified CNVs. This case series expands the clinical and molecular data on pathogenic CNVs associated with pediatric epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders in an underrepresented Southeast Asian population and illustrates the complementary roles of sequencing and chromosomal analysis in genetic diagnosis.

items.title: Optimal Vitamin C Status is Associated with Better Physical Performance in Men and Women from the EPIC-Norfolk Cohort: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Vitamin C may be important for maintaining skeletal muscle health and preventing sarcopenia, but most previous epidemiological studies have investigated dietary intakes rather than vitamin C status. To address this gap, this study investigated cross-sectional associations between both plasma and dietary vitamin C and muscle strength and physical performance. This study analysed data from over 5000 participants of the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC)-Norfolk cohort (aged 48-92 years). Multivariable linear regression models, adjusted for lifestyle, biological, medical, and dietary covariates, were used to investigate associations between dietary (categorised as quintiles, Qs) and plasma vitamin C (low < 25μmol/L, suboptimal 25 to < 50μmol/L, optimal ≥ 50μmol/L), and handgrip strength (adjusted for height: HGSht), gait speed, and 5-chair-stand time. Least square means for outcome measures were calculated from regression models. Women with optimal versus low plasma vitamin C had higher HGSht (+ 0.54 kg/m2, p = 0.009), and faster gait speed and chair-stand time (+ 0.11m/s, p < 0.001; - 1.03s, p = 0.028, respectively). Men with optimal versus low plasma vitamin C had faster gait speed and chair-stand time (+ 0.05m/s, p = 0.01; - 0.71s, p = 0.026, respectively). Compared with Q1 of dietary intake, women in Q2 and Q5 had faster gait speed (+ 0.04m/s, p < 0.01 for both); women in Q4 and Q5 had faster chair-stand times (- 0.67s, p = 0.002; - 0.57s, p = 0.013, respectively). No associations were found for dietary vitamin C in men. These findings suggest that maintaining optimal plasma vitamin C status could be important for maintaining physical function. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to support our findings.

items.title: Association between voiding dysfunction symptoms and health-related quality of life in primary school children: a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Voiding dysfunction is a common pediatric problem and accounts for roughly one-fifth of visits to pediatric urology clinics. We examined whether voiding dysfunction symptoms were related to health-related quality of life in primary school children. We conducted a cross-sectional correlational study with 498 children aged 8-12 years and their parents from three primary schools in İzmir. Parents completed the Voiding Dysfunction Symptom Score (VDSS), whereas the children completed the Kid-KINDL Health-Related Quality of Life Questionnaire. Sixty children (12%) screened positive on the VDSS. Urgency was the most frequently reported symptom (34.9%), followed by voiding more than seven times per day (18.7%) and daytime incontinence (15.3%). Total VDSS and Kid-KINDL scores showed a weak inverse correlation (r = -0.112, p = 0.012; r2 = 0.013, indicating a small effect size). Before covariate adjustment, children who screened positive on the VDSS had lower total quality-of-life scores than those who screened negative on the VDSS (74.3 ± 12.1; 77.9 ± 12.3). The largest unadjusted difference was in the Family Relationships subdimension (p < 0.05). Neither this difference nor the total-score difference remained significant after Bonferroni correction or adjustment for demographic covariates. The unadjusted findings suggested lower health-related quality of life among children who screened positive on the VDSS, with the clearest difference in Family Relationships. These associations were no longer significant after demographic adjustment. • Among school-aged children, voiding dysfunction is relatively common and has been linked to poorer psychosocial functioning and lower quality of life. • VDSS-positive screening was associated with lower unadjusted quality-of-life scores, especially in Family Relationships, but this association did not persist after covariate adjustment.

items.title: An adversarial deep neural network for identifying non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
items.abstract: BackgroundNon-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is rapidly becoming the most prevalent liver disease worldwide. The accurate identification of NAFLD patients and understand the molecular mechanism of initiating and driving disease progression remain limited.ObjectieThis study aims to develop a robust and accurate computational model for identifying NAFLD patients using mRNA expression profiles, and to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms that drive disease initiation and progression.MethodsWe introduce an adversarial deep neural network (ADNN) to identify NAFLD patients based on mRNA expression profiles, which uses adversarial learning techniques to take advantage of existing mRNA expression profiles in the GEO database. We compare the ADNN model with some traditional machine learning methods, such as random forest (RF), adaptive boosting (AdaBoost).ResultsThe area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of the ADNN model is 0.982, which is much higher than the machine learning models such as RF, SVM and deep neural networks. Meanwhile, by combining the ADNN model with the DeepLIFT algorithm, we calculate the importance score of genes and find that the DeepLIFT algorithm can identify genes that don't differ at the level of mRNA, but interact with other important genes. Such as GSTM1, with the greatest importance score and has no difference between control and NAFLD, but interacts with IGF1 and MEP1B.ConclusionTherefore, the ADNN model can not only identify NAFLD patients from healthy controls, but also help us better understand the disease mechanism of NAFLD.
