items.title: Personal Health Data for Sale: Lessons from the European Union to Strengthen Canadian Privacy.
items.abstract: Personal health data is increasingly recognized as a valuable asset in both the public and private sector, capable of creating numerous advancements in the management and treatment of disease and unlocking profitable market insights. The proliferation of digital health technologies has increased the availability of this data, but the absence of a coordinated public approach to collecting this information in Canada has resulted in a reliance on private data brokers to access potential benefits. While these curated commercial datasets have become essential for public researchers, pharmaceutical companies are by far their largest consumers. In addition, current Canadian privacy law relies on outdated mechanisms of protection which are insufficient against the modern sophistication of data manipulation. This study examines how this regulatory framework fails to uphold ethical obligations to privacy and instead enables pharmaceutical companies to engage in harmful physician and patient profiling practices through their participation in personal health data markets. After detailing the generation and operation of these profiling practices, this study will investigate how the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA)'s reliance on the de-identification of personal data has allowed pharmaceutical companies to identify and target individual physicians and patients through marketing strategies, leading to lower quality prescribing. Finally, this study proposes the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation as inspiration for Canadian modernization efforts and suggests three lessons for reform in order to rebalance private and public benefits, as well as strengthen individual data sovereignty.

items.title: The Sleep-Wake Classification Performance of Pediatric-Trained Machine Learning Algorithms for Raw Accelerometer Data.
items.abstract: Actigraphy sleep-wake classification methods increasingly seek to leverage raw acceleration data and machine-learning-based classification, but performance evaluation in pediatrics is limited. We trained machine-learning models using pediatric data and compared their sleep-wake classification performance with existing algorithms for children. Sixty-five children (46% female, ages 5.3-17.7 years) completed in-lab overnight polysomnography and wore a GENEActiv device on their non-dominant wrist. The acceleration data were converted into 30-second epochs and aligned with physician-scored sleep-wake data from electroencephalography. Eight machine-learning models were trained using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. Epoch-by-epoch analyses generated performance metrics (e.g., balanced accuracy [BA]) and discrepancy analyses provided overall sleep duration bias estimates. The combination of highest performance and least bias was used to rank using Euclidean distance scores - where a lower score represents closer to perfect performance and zero bias. For benchmarking, we included GGIR sleep scoring algorithms and an adult trained random forest classifier. Overall, 560.1 hours of polysomnography and actigraphy data were collected (74.4% of epochs were scored as sleep). The pediatric-trained local-global long-short term memory (LSTM) classifier had the most optimal epoch-by-epoch performance (e.g., BA=0.85, sensitivity=0.88, specificity=0.83, ROC-AUC=0.95, and Cohen's kappa=0.67). These metrics exceeded that of an adult-trained random forest classifier and GGIR-based algorithms. Discrepancy analyses revealed that overall sleep duration was underestimated by an average of 25 minutes using the LSTM classifier with no proportional bias. We trained eight pediatric sleep-wake classifiers that had a strong ability to detect sleep and wake, with the LSTM classifier being most optimal.

items.title: Communicating the Nicotine and Tobacco Risk Continuum: A Scoping Review and Framework for Future Messaging.
items.abstract: The U.S. FDA acknowledges that commercial nicotine and tobacco products (NTPs) exist along a continuum of risk (COR), yet strategies to effectively communicate this concept remain underexamined. This scoping review synthesizes peer-reviewed studies on COR messaging across NTPs to identify promising practices and research gaps. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we searched PubMed, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and Scopus for English-language articles (2014-2024) that empirically tested comparative or modified risk messages across NTPs. Two authors independently screened and extracted data on the conceptualization, operationalization, and effectiveness of COR messaging. We used the Message Impact Framework (MIF) to categorize message effectiveness by message receptivity, precursors to behavior, and behavioral outcomes. Of 531 articles identified, 50 met the inclusion criteria. COR messaging was conceptualized and operationalized inconsistently across studies, with most focusing on binary comparisons (e.g., e-cigarettes/snus vs. cigarettes) rather than communicating the broader COR across multiple NTPs. The operationalization of COR messaging differed in message content (e.g., specific vs. general harm, reduced exposure vs. risk), feature (e.g., audience targeting, message source, numeric information), and delivery (e.g., placement, format). COR messages generally increased the accuracy of risk perceptions of lower-risk NTPs, though effectiveness varied. This scoping review identified practical tactics and key challenges for COR messaging across NTPs, including heterogeneous design, confusion about "complete switching," and unintended "halo effects." We propose a definition of COR messaging and a framework to address the need for a standardized conceptualization and more comprehensive evaluation of its effectiveness in future research.

items.title: Initiatives to Prevent Fatal Drug Overdose Mortality After Incarceration.
items.abstract: There is a direct relationship between fatal drug overdose and individuals who have been involved with the United States criminal legal system. Fatal drug overdose in the United States has reached unprecedented levels in the last decade, disproportionately affecting individuals involved with the criminal legal system and those who experience intersecting social and structural determinants of health. In addition, evidence shows that the immediate post-release period after incarceration is characterized by elevated overdose mortality. However, current policy structures, including the federal Medicaid Inmate Exclusion Policy, fragmented reentry systems, and inconsistent access to medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD), leave justice-involved populations without essential supports during this high-risk transition. This commentary synthesizes national evidence and proposes 3 policy initiatives to reduce post-incarceration overdose deaths: (1) adoption of the Section 1115 Medicaid Reentry Demonstration Waiver to provide prerelease screening, treatment initiation, care coordination, and bridge medication; (2) implementation of statewide carceral-based recovery support programs that integrate peer recovery coaches, trauma-informed care principles, naloxone training, and warm handoffs to community services; and (3) development of low-threshold community harm reduction hubs offering naloxone distribution, same-day and telehealth-enabled MOUD access, housing navigation, and peer support. These initiatives strengthen care continuity and target the transition periods where risk is greatest. Implementing these evidence-informed strategies is both a public health imperative and a critical step toward advancing health equity for criminal legal system-involved populations.

items.title: A critical review of the role of pharmacists in providing care to Indigenous peoples with diabetes mellitus.
items.abstract: Indigenous peoples experience disproportionately higher rates of diabetes mellitus (DM) due to social, historical, and cultural factors. Pharmacists play important roles in DM care, but their involvement in caring for Indigenous peoples with DM is not well documented. This critical review aimed to describe pharmacists' involvement by systematically identifying the roles, barriers, facilitators, interventions, and pharmacists' vision for improving diabetes care for Indigenous peoples. A systematic search utilizing Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines was conducted across seven scientific literature databases and grey literature from inception to May 2026, using keywords related to pharmacists, diabetes, and Indigenous peoples. Data analysis was guided by the Two-Eyed Seeing Framework and the Framework for Diabetes in Canada. Eight studies met the inclusion criteria. The key roles of pharmacists identified included screening, patient education, medication management, and supporting adherence. Barriers to pharmacists' service delivery included mistrust, lack of knowledge of Indigenous languages, and financial issues related to management. Facilitators included family engagement, motivational interviewing, home delivery for prescriptions, and customized information material in the Indigenous language. Recommendations identified to enhance pharmacists' delivery of services included cultural competency, financial support, and increased collaboration with Indigenous peoples and their families. Pharmacists provide care for Indigenous peoples living with diabetes through medication management, education, and counselling. Various facilitators and barriers to the provision of these services were identified, which can be learned from to enhance future care. Further research is required to determine best practices to provide the best possible care in a culturally appropriate manner.

items.title: Epigenetic aging in people with HIV across the life course: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Epigenetic aging algorithms are emerging tools for understanding the biological effects of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). A growing body of literature has applied DNA methylation-based epigenetic clocks in people living with HIV (PWH) across the life course, examining epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) in relation to HIV infection, antiretroviral therapy (ART), comorbidities, and clinical biomarkers (e.g., viral load, CD4 T-cell counts). This systematic review (Prospero: CRD420251126874) summarizes and synthesizes the current evidence on epigenetic aging in PWH across the life course and identifies critical knowledge gaps for future research. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Medline through June 26, 2026. The review followed PRISMA guidelines and assessed studies for risk of bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. We created a narrative synthesis of results and performed a random-effects meta-analysis of HorvathAge EAA. Fifty-five studies met the inclusion criteria. More than half (n = 33) examined EAA in PWH compared to an uninfected control population. We identified heterogeneity in study populations and design, biospecimens profiled, platforms used for DNA methylation analysis, and epigenetic clocks employed. Only 6 studies included participants younger than 18 years and no studies focused exclusively on individuals over 65 years. Only 10 studies examined longitudinal changes in EAA. Thirty-seven papers evaluated associations between EAA and comorbidities. A meta-analysis of HorvathAge EAA across 14 studies found a mean difference of 3.41 years (95%CI 2.22, 4.60) in PWH relative to controls. Current evidence supports accelerated EAA among PWH but highlights substantial methodological heterogeneity and important knowledge gaps. Longitudinal studies of EAA in PWH are needed in populations under 18 and over 65, to clarify the effects of ART, clinical biomarkers, and age-related comorbidities, and determine the clinical utility of epigenetic aging biomarkers.

items.title: Early versus late venous thromboembolism in patients with newly diagnosed high-grade gliomas.
items.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurs in 20-30% and 9.2% of patients with glioblastoma and grade 3 IDH mutant (IDHmut) gliomas respectively, with highest risk during the first months post-surgery. We sought to identify risk factors for early versus late VTE in high-grade gliomas and evaluated the recently proposed 'GliomaPredictVTE' tool. We included 894 patients with newly-diagnosed glioblastoma and grade 3-4 IDHmut gliomas from 2010-2023. Competing-risk analysis estimated VTE cumulative incidence (CumInc), segmented linear regression model identified the change-point between early versus late VTE, and competing-risk regression model identified significant risk factors. GliomaPredictVTE-predicted 6- and 12-month VTE risks were compared to observed CumInc. The estimated 6- and 12-month VTE CumInc was 21.5% and 26.4%, respectively for IDHwt glioblastoma versus 6.3% and 8.3%, respectively for IDHmut gliomas. The VTE CumInc increased rapidly during the first 6 months post-surgery, followed by a more gradual rise thereafter, with a change-point around 6 months. On multivariable analyses, 'Early VTE' (within 6 months post-surgery) was significantly associated with older age, limb weakness, ambulation dependence, and radiotherapy alone; 'Late VTE' (6 months to 5 years) with older age and smoking. GliomaPredictVTE substantially underestimated VTE incidence in our population, with a mean predicted 6- and 12-month risks of 11.0% and 17.4%, versus observed CumInc of 19.9% (p < 0.001) and 23% (p = 0.008), respectively. Distinct risk profiles between early and late VTE support prospective studies of primary prophylaxis in high-risk patients, particularly in the first 6 months post-surgery. GliomaPredictVTE significantly underestimates VTE incidence in this population.

items.title: The mediating role of sleep blood pressure in the association between B-type natriuretic peptide and cardiovascular events: The Nagahama Study.
items.abstract: B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) is a risk marker for not only heart failure but also cardiovascular diseases (CVD). This study investigated the possible mediating role of sleep blood pressure (BP) in the association between BNP and CVD events. Data for 5,751 participants were obtained from the Nagahama Study, a longitudinal cohort study of the general Japanese population. Circulating BNP levels were determined from blood specimens. BP was measured at home in the morning and evening, and three times per night during sleep using a timer-equipped cuff-oscillometric device. During the mean follow-up period of 9.4 years (54,350 person-years), 169 CVD cases were observed (Incidence rate: 31.1 per 10,000 person-year, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 26.7, 36.2). BNP levels ≥40 pg/mL were independently associated with CVD. The sleep BP-adjusted hazard ratio of high BNP for CVD was 1.80 (95% CI: 1.18, 2.74), while the awake home BP-adjusted hazard ratio was 1.92 (95% CI: 1.26, 2.91). Causal mediation analysis indicated a greater mediation rate of sleep SBP (14.3%, 95% CI: -2.8, 31.3) than awake home SBP (5.8%, 95% CI; -2.6, 14.2) in the association between BNP and CVD incidence. Factors associated with log-normalized BNP levels were age, sex, body mass index, sleep SBP, and nocturnal urination frequency. Prognostic significance of BNP for CVD events was partially mediated by BP particularly BP during sleep.

items.title: Improving rates of HIV testing in emergency departments in a health system using clinical decision support.
items.abstract: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) remain a public health priority. The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) recommends comprehensive screening for STIs and HIV, defined as testing for gonorrhoea/chlamydia (GC-CT), syphilis and HIV in persons undergoing STI evaluation. Many patients utilize emergency departments (EDs) for STI evaluation; however, HIV co-testing rates remain low. Electronic Health Record (EHR)-based clinical decision support (CDS) can help providers implement best practices. We assessed the impact of two CDS tools on HIV co-testing rates with GC-CT in freestanding EDs (FSEDs) of a statewide health system. CDS Interventions included Comprehensive STI Order Set made available 1/2024 and a Comprehensive STI Pathway made available 1/2025. We included FSED encounters for adult patients with GC-CT NAAT 1/1/2022-11/21/2025 and measured HIV co-testing rates. Process measures included overall CDS utilization by FSED type (urban Denver sites, Metro; outlying Colorado sites, Outlying; aggregated sites, All Sites). Analysis included statistical process control charts and descriptive statistics. GC-CT testing occurred in 11 087 patient encounters between 1/1/2022 and 11/21/2025. HIV co-testing rates averaged 2.6% 2 years before the intervention (2022-2023). After the first intervention (2024), HIV co-testing rose to 13.1%, with a positive shift in SPC charts across All Sites, Metro and Outlying. After the second intervention (2025), HIV co-testing rose to 18.3%, with greater impacts at Metro FSEDs; positive shifts in SPC charts were seen across All Sites and Metro but not Outlying EDs. EHR-based CDS was effective for increasing HIV co-testing in freestanding EDs.

items.title: Prenatal Exposure to Phthalates and Bisphenols in Association with Hypomineralization of Second Primary Molar.
items.abstract: Hypomineralized second primary molars (HSPM) affect approximately 6.8% of children. Molars affected by HSPM mineralize between 20 wk of gestation and 15 to 17 mo of age. Experimental studies suggest that exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals, including di-2-ethylhexyl phthalate (DEHP) and bisphenol A (BPA), may disrupt enamel formation, but evidence in humans remains limited. This study investigates the association between prenatal exposure to individual phthalates, BPA, and their mixtures and the odds of HSPM in children. It was embedded in the Generation R study, a population-based prospective birth cohort in the Netherlands. Maternal urinary concentrations of BPA and 11 phthalate metabolites were measured each trimester. HSPM was diagnosed at age 6 y based on European Academy of Paediatric Dentistry criteria. Multivariate logistic regression models and Bayesian weighted quantile sum regression were used to assess individual and mixture associations, respectively. Among 1,160 mother-child pairs, 10.2% of children were diagnosed with HSPM. In single-exposure models, higher prenatal concentrations of monobenzyl phthalate (mBzBP) were associated with lower odds of HSPM (odds ratio [OR] = 0.76; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.59 to 0.97). Second-trimester exposure to DEHP metabolites showed a nonsignificant trend toward increased HSPM odds (eg, mEOHP OR = 1.15; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.91 to 1.45). Sex-specific associations were observed: higher BPA and phthalate concentrations were associated with lower likelihood of HSPM in girls (eg, BPA OR = 0.70; 95% CI: 0.50 to 0.98) and higher odds in boys (p-interaction < 0.10). Mixture analyses showed a nonsignificant inverse association for overall prenatal exposure (OR = 0.84; 95% CI: 0.63 to 1.15), with mBzBP contributing most to the mixture. No overall association was observed for DEHP mixture, although sex-specific trends were consistent with single-exposure results. Prenatal exposure to phthalates and BPA may influence HSPM development. These findings highlight the need to consider early-life endocrine-disrupting chemical mixture exposure in HSPM etiology.

items.title: Trends in Oral Health Inequalities among Older Adults in England.
items.abstract: Healthy aging is a global public health priority, and good oral health is essential for this. While studies in the United Kingdom documented social gradients in oral health measures among adults, they were mostly cross-sectional and conducted before major policy and economic changes. One study examined trends over time in inequalities in tooth loss but used only 1 socioeconomic position (SEP) measure and did not focus on older adults. Our study aimed to examine trends in oral health inequalities by a comprehensive range of SEP indicators among older adults in England from 2006-2007 to 2018-2019. Secondary data analyses used both baseline and refreshment samples from waves 3, 5, 7, and 9 of the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA). Oral health outcomes were edentulousness (waves 3-7; 8-y follow-up), self-rated oral health (SROH), and Oral Impacts on Daily Performances (OIDP) (waves 3-9 for both; 12-y follow-up). SEP indicators consisted of education, occupation, household income, and household wealth. Logistic regression with robust standard errors accounting for clustering was used to measure socioeconomic inequalities in oral health over time, controlling for age, sex, and marital status. Odds ratios and predicted probabilities were compared to assess changes in relative and absolute oral health inequalities over 12 y. The prevalence of edentulousness decreased from waves 3 to 7 (data not available for wave 9), while the prevalence of reporting at least 1 oral impact and fair/poor SROH increased from waves 3 to 9. Social gradients were evident across oral health outcomes and for different SEP markers. For all 3 outcomes, relative inequalities remained largely unchanged over the study period. Absolute inequalities slightly narrowed for edentulousness but increased for both SROH and oral impacts. Overall, oral health inequalities among older adults in England have persisted and, in some aspects, widened over these 12 y, highlighting the need for upstream public health strategies to reduce inequalities.

items.title: Connecting Research and Policy to Reduce Risk for Child Maltreatment: A Call to Action.
items.abstract: Over the past five decades since the enactment of the Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act, the field of child abuse and neglect (CAN) has benefitted from extensive research on the correlates and consequences of CAN, intergenerational transmission of risk, and evidence-based interventions. Studies have also shown the benefits of social policies that strengthen the safety net for vulnerable children and families. Despite these achievements, CAN remains a significant global public health problem. In this article, we draw on findings of our recently published book Pathways to Prevention: Connecting Research and Policy to Reduce Risk for Child Maltreatment to explore the challenges of advancing a public health response that prioritizes universal and upstream preventive interventions over targeted programs with limited scope. We call for closer alignment between research, policy, and practice that is grounded in a "blended" prevention model. We encourage readers to take an active role in advocating for more oversight and engagement by federal agencies and policymakers in building a foundation of policies to support family and child needs and prevent CAN.

items.title: Aspects of Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis Empowerment and Pitfalls Among Racial and Ethnic Young Men Who Have Sex With Men.
items.abstract: HIV continues to disproportionately affect men who have sex with men (MSM), particularly Black and Latino populations. With pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) now central to HIV prevention efforts, understanding perceptions of safer sex practices among racial and ethnic minority MSM is essential. This qualitative study conducted three focus groups with 22 Asian, Black, and Latino MSM aged 18 to 29 in Los Angeles County between January and April 2022 to explore how safer sex has evolved since PrEP's Food and Drug Administration approval in 2012. Four themes emerged: (a) shifting definitions of safer sex, (b) sexual autonomy and empowerment, (c) peer perceptions and stigma surrounding PrEP use, and (d) provider judgment and limited knowledge. Participants described PrEP as a source of sexual agency but also highlighted ongoing stigma and discomfort when disclosing PrEP use or engaging with health care providers. Although all participants were active PrEP users, broader access disparities remain, particularly for MSM of color. The recent Food and Drug Administration approval of a biannual injectable PrEP offers a promising opportunity to expand uptake by reducing stigma, enhancing convenience, and improving adherence. These findings underscore the need for culturally responsive messaging, supportive clinical environments, and policy efforts to ensure equitable PrEP access for marginalized MSM. Public health practitioners and providers can use this insight to improve HIV prevention strategies and tailor interventions to the lived experiences of MSM of color.

items.title: Association between preoperative RDW and in-hospital death in trauma patients: A multicenter retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: ObjectiveRed cell distribution width (RDW) is an emerging prognostic marker in trauma. This study aims to investigate the association between preoperative RDW and in-hospital mortality in surgical trauma patients.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study enrolled 34,848 surgical trauma patients sourced from three Chinese medical centers and the MIMIC-IV 2.2 database. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed to evaluate the discriminative ability of preoperative (at-admission) RDW for in-hospital mortality and to determine an optimal cutoff value for patient stratification. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed with a caliper value of 0.01, balancing 18 covariates between the two groups, including demographic characteristics, vital signs, injury severity scores, comorbidities. After PSM, 7,697 pairs were matched. Binary logistic regression was applied to assess the relationship between RDW and in-hospital mortality.ResultsIn-hospital mortality was 3.02% (1,051/34,848). Preoperative RDW showed moderate discrimination for in-hospital mortality, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.777 (95% CI 0.763-0.792). Before PSM, in-hospital mortality was significantly higher in the Pre-RDW > 14.25% group compared to the Pre-RDW ≤ 14.25% group (7.58% vs. 1.11%, P 14.25% was associated with 2.58-fold higher odds of in-hospital death (95% CI 2.17-3.05, P 14.25% indicates a significantly higher risk of in-hospital death.

items.title: Membrane targeted rabies virus labeling system: Brain-wide single-neuron mapping of target-specific and intersectionally defined neuronal circuits.
items.abstract: Abstract Elucidating neural circuit organization at single-neuron resolution is a core goal of modern neuroscience. Brain-wide input connectivity maps underpin the mammalian connectome, but systematic and comprehensive whole-brain input mapping with resolved single-neuron anatomy for defined brain regions remains a formidable technical challenge. Here, we developed a membrane-targeted rabies virus labeling system using mClover3 as the fluorescent reporter, which features high compatibility with fluorescence micro-optical sectioning tomography imaging and enables complete visualization of fine neuronal morphology across the entire brain. Validation in the mouse primary somatosensory cortex barrel field confirms robust full-morphology labeling and faithful reconstruction of brain-wide input neurons, revealing diverse projection patterns with distinct axonal targets. We further generated a dual-recombinase dependent TVA reporter mouse line to enable anatomical interrogation of intersectionally defined neuron populations via EnvA-pseudotyped membrane-targeted rabies virus, allowing specific targeting and single-neuron reconstruction of PV+/vGlut2+ L5b pyramidal neurons in the primary somatosensory cortex barrel field. These neurons exhibited a pathway-conserved population-level projection profile likely representing a subset of pyramidal tract neuron projections, while showing pronounced cellto-cell diversity in axonal target specificity. Overall, this work delivers a robust, versatile toolkit for brain-wide single-neuron mapping of target-specific and intersectionally defined neuronal circuits, with strong potential to advance brain connectomics.

items.title: Psychosocial disability in Australia: Prevalence, functional severity and population projections to 2060 from repeated cross-sectional population surveys.
items.abstract: Background Existing approaches to estimating psychosocial disability - arising from severe mental illness - rely heavily on diagnostic categories and health service utilisation. By neglecting functional-limitation and participation restriction, such approaches limit the utility of current estimates for planning disability supports. This study addresses that gap by estimating the prevalence, functional severity and projected population counts of psychosocial disability in Australia, aligned with the World Health Organization International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health framework. Methods Using a repeated cross-sectional design, we analysed four waves of the nationally representative Survey of Disability, Ageing and Carers (2009, 2012, 2015, 2018). Psychosocial disability was operationally defined as a long-term mental health condition combined with disability, consistent with the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health framework. Survey-weighted prevalence was estimated overall and by functional severity. Pooled age- and sex-specific prevalence rates were then applied to three population growth scenarios to project counts to 2060. Results Prevalence remained stable at 1.0% across all waves, with population counts rising from ~196,600 (2009) to ~243,800 (2018), reflecting demographic growth. People with psychosocial disability were disproportionately middle-aged, Australian-born, socioeconomically disadvantaged and living outside major cities. Under the medium growth scenario, projected counts increase from ~274,000 (2025) to ~410,000 (2060; +50%), with those experiencing profound limitation projected to nearly double (+92%). Conclusion Shifting from diagnosis- to function-based estimation, this study provides a policy-relevant basis for psychosocial disability planning. Rapid growth in the number of profound psychosocial disability underscores the need for early intervention and coordinated psychosocial supports beyond Australia's National Disability Insurance Scheme.

items.title: Mapping the prevalence of Epstein-Barr virus and multiple sclerosis in Middle East and North Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) prevalence has increased to medium-to-high levels in several countries of the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), while Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) exposure as one of the most consistently reported MS risk factors is common throughout the region. This systematic review and meta-analysis descriptively mapped published estimates of MS prevalence and EBV seroprevalence alongside each other in MENA countries. We searched MEDLINE, PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science until 18 June 2022. Observational studies reporting MS prevalence or EBV seroprevalence among healthy MENA populations were eligible. For quantitative EBV synthesis, we restricted analyses to studies reporting VCA-IgG seroprevalence to improve comparability across studies. Studies reporting the prevalence of specific type of MS or those assessing EBV infection by IgA antibodies or non-serological tissues or without a control arm representing general population were excluded. The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools were used to determine the quality of the studies. The heterogeneity of studies was evaluated using I 2 statistics. Results of the fix-effects meta-analysis were presented using prevalence and 95% confidence intervals. Of 4,323 records identified, 131 studies were included. The pooled MS prevalence was 51.02 per 100,000 population, and the pooled EBV VCA-IgG seroprevalence was 75%. In time-stratified analyses, pooled MS prevalence increased from 12 per 100,000 in studies conducted up to 2000 to 58 per 100,000 in studies conducted from 2011 to 2022. Pooled EBV seroprevalence increased from 71 to 75% across the same periods. These findings suggest that the prevalence of both MS and EBV has increased over time, with a more pronounced increase observed for MS. Between-study heterogeneity was extreme for both outcomes (I 2 = 100%), reflecting substantial variation in geography, populations, study methods, diagnostic approaches, and study periods. Published MS prevalence estimates and EBV VCA-IgG seroprevalence estimates showed co-occurring uprising patterns in the available MENA literature. Based on a probable ecological correlation between the increasing prevalence of MS and EBV, the preventive measures against EBV infection may potentially yield favorable outcomes in terms of MS prevention. Future longitudinal, population-based studies with standardized MS ascertainment and age-specific EBV serology are needed.

items.title: Impact of clinical risk factors on white matter microstructure in preterm-born infants: investigation with diffusion MRI and tractography at term-equivalent age.
items.abstract: Premature birth occurs during a phase of intense brain maturation, making white matter (WM) particularly vulnerable to injury. Beyond major lesions, subtle and widespread microstructural alterations also contribute to later neurodevelopmental impairments. We aimed to characterize the impact of key clinical risk factors on global and tract-specific WM microstructure at term-equivalent age (TEA), using 3T-diffusion-MRI data of 111 infants born before 33 weeks of gestation. We implemented a tractography pipeline adapted for use in infants with heterogeneous brain anatomy, including macroscopic abnormalities and lesions, and extracted diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics in sensorimotor tracts: corticospinal tract (CST), superior thalamic radiation (STR), frontal aslant tract (FAT), forceps minor (FMI) and middle cerebellar peduncle (MCP). Associations with risk factors were assessed accounting for age at MRI or global WM microstructure. Tractography succeeded in most infants despite marked anatomical variability and/or overt lesions. Being a male, small for gestational age (SGA) at birth, encountering sepsis and having severe Kidokoro radiological score for WM were associated with altered global WM metrics. At the tract level, CST and STR showed the strongest susceptibility to SGA, prolonged parenteral nutrition, and Kidokoro score. In contrast, associations after adjustment for global WM microstructure suggested that FAT might be less vulnerable than other tracts to extreme prematurity, SGA and invasive ventilation. Findings were partially replicated in infants without macroscopic abnormalities, supporting the presence of WM dysmaturation even in the absence of visible injury. DTI metrics thus provide tract-specific biomarkers of early WM microstructure in preterm infants, which are sensitive to risk factors and could inform targeted prevention and intervention.

items.title: Early-life prolonged hyperthermic seizures alter disease trajectory in the Scn1a(+/-)<sup>tm1Kea</sup> mouse model of Dravet syndrome.
items.abstract: Dravet syndrome (DS) is a catastrophic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy caused most often by de novo loss-of-function mutations in SCN1A, the gene encoding the alpha subunit of the voltage-gated sodium channel (Na v 1.1). Animal models such as the Scn1a(+/-) tm1Kea mouse display relevant DS phenotypes including sensitivity to hyperthermia-induced seizures and later-life spontaneous seizures. Elevating the body temperature of immature Scn1a(+/-) tm1Kea mice reliably triggers seizures. Typically, researchers evoke only short-lasting seizures by hyperthermia, whereas febrile seizures in DS patients are often prolonged and complex. This study aimed to characterize a more clinically relevant model of hyperthermia-induced seizures in F1.Scn1a(+/-) tm1kea mice and clarify how this affects epilepsy progression, severity, and associated comorbidities in mice of both sexes. A prolonged febrile event (PFE) was achieved by placing P17 pups in a warmed-air stream inside a chamber, with stepped body temperature raising up to 41 °C followed by holding for 30 min, before cooling body temperature to 37 °C. While the PFE procedure induced prolonged and recurrent seizures, bulk cortical Na v 1.1 protein abundance remained unchanged across disease progression (P18, P21 and P90). Post-weaning monitoring up to P90 revealed that PFE-exposed F1.Scn1a(+/-) tm1kea mice displayed higher mortality rates and altered survival patterns, with distinct outcomes observed in male and female mice. As adults, PFE-exposed F1.Scn1a(+/-) tm1kea mice displayed increased locomotor and exploratory behavior, whereas PFE-exposed F1.Scn1a(+/+) mice exhibited impaired spatial reference memory. The findings suggest that early-life prolonged hyperthermia-induced seizures influence multiple disease-related phenotypes in this DS model, some of which may exhibit sex-specific differences. The findings extend the range of tools to study DS and provide insights into how a background of prolonged FS may impact later-life outcomes in mice.

items.title: Identifying the Optimal Respiratory Muscle Training Intervention for Heart Failure Patients: A Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
items.abstract: Background Respiratory muscle training interventions have shown promising results in improving functional capacity, quality of life, and prognosis of heart failure patients. However, the optimal respiratory muscle training intervention for rehabilitation remains unclear. Methods A systematic review and network meta-analysis was conducted by searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Library until September 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the effect of respiratory muscle training interventions on maximum inspiratory pressure (MIP), maximum expiratory pressure (MEP), forced vital capacity (FVC), forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV₁), six-minute walk test (6MWT), peak oxygen uptake (VO 2 max), quality of life, and dyspnea. Random-effect network meta-analysis was used to estimate pooled mean differences. Interventions were ranked using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). Results A total of 88 RCTs (5,757 participants) were included. Medium-intensity inspiratory muscle training (IMT) ranked highest for improving MIP (SUCRA: 89.8%). Combined aerobic and resistance exercise was optimal for MEP (SUCRA: 79.3%). Aerobic training showed the greatest benefit for FVC (SUCRA: 94.8%) and FEV₁ (SUCRA: 93.8%). Medium-intensity IMT was most effective for enhancing 6MWT performance (SUCRA: 81.6%). A combination of high-intensity IMT with aerobic training yielded the largest gains in improving VO 2 max (SUCRA: 74.7%), quality of life (SUCRA: 81.4%), and reducing dyspnea (SUCRA: 89.3%). Conclusion Respiratory muscle training interventions provide different benefits across key rehabilitation outcomes in heart failure. Accordingly, rehabilitation strategies may be optimized by aligning exercise modalities with patients' rehabilitation needs, preferences, and clinical profiles, rather than adopting a uniform prescription.

items.title: The evolving role of diamond materials in neuroscience and neuroengineering.
items.abstract: Diamond-based materials are increasingly investigated in neuroscience and neuroengineering because of their tunable surface chemistry, mechanical robustness, electrochemical stability and photostability. This review compares particulate nanodiamonds (NDs), fluorescent NDs, conductive and nanocrystalline diamond electrodes, and NV-containing diamond sensors across neural sensing, imaging, neurochemical monitoring, neural interfacing, regenerative engineering and experimental therapeutic applications. We examine how synthesis, particle size, purity, aggregation, surface chemistry and defect structure influence application-specific performance, biological interactions, biodistribution and safety. Translational potential is assessed according to the available evidence, systemic exposure, technical maturity, manufacturing requirements and regulatory complexity. Localized diagnostic and neurochemical-sensing applications may offer comparatively plausible near-term pathways because they can reduce dependence on systemic delivery. Implantable neural electrodes and retinal interfaces also avoid some systemic barriers but remain predominantly supported by preclinical evidence. ND-based central nervous system (CNS) drug delivery, glioblastoma treatment, neurodegenerative scaffolds and mammalian quantum-neuronal sensing remain at earlier experimental stages. Key barriers include formulation-dependent biocompatibility, sensitivity in complex tissues, blood-brain barrier delivery, long-term biodistribution and clearance, manufacturing reproducibility, GMP-compatible scale-up and regulatory qualification. Although some of these limitations may be reduced through material and process optimization, comparative validation and stronger long-term safety evidence are still required for clinical translation. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Diamond-based materials are increasingly finding their way into neuroscience and neuroengineering by bridging the gap between advanced nanotechnology and living neural systems. This review highlights the versatility of distinct diamond structures-ranging from detonation nanodiamonds and fluorescent defect centers to conductive boron-doped electrodes-across applications like biosensing, neurochemical monitoring, neural interfacing, and targeted therapy.

items.title: A novel and adaptable method to prepare samples for postmortem imaging with artifact reduction.
items.abstract: Background Postmortem MRI enables ultra-high-resolution image acquisition and subsequent biomarker validation. This approach requires that postmortem specimens be suspended in solution, which is not required for in vivo MRI. Susceptibility artifacts occur at surface-air interfaces and around air bubbles that remain in and around the sample, leading to image distortions. New method We set forth our protocol, the Seven Seals Method, whereby we prepare brain specimens for MRI scanning, with special attention to removing artifact-causing air bubbles. This protocol evolved over twenty years of ex vivo imaging experience. The method uses freezer bags to create a custom-shaped container for brain samples with a temporary reservoir pocket that collects air for removal. The protocol provides step by step instructions with diagrams and videos, a history of experimentation, and a troubleshooting guide. Results We have successfully applied this method to whole brains, brain hemispheres and blocked brain specimens, and have prepared samples in a variety of solutions. Comparison with existing methods The strengths of the Seven Seals Method include its high adaptability for shape and size fit, proven air bubble removal techniques, and inexpensive packing materials that do not require the use of a 3D printer. The tailored container minimizes motion and allows for closer proximity of the specimen to the coil elements than when using hard sided plastic containers, which yields better signal-to-noise ratio for structure visualization. Conclusions We anticipate this rigorous protocol will enable other groups to optimize their ex vivo scans for validation studies.

items.title: PPT1-mediated GABA<sub>A</sub>Rα1 depalmitoylation maintains inhibitory synaptic homeostasis and cognition.
items.abstract: GABA A receptors (GABA A Rs), essential for inhibitory neurotransmission, are palmitoylated proteins and their depalmitoylation is catalyzed by palmitoyl-protein thioesterase 1 (PPT1). By generating Gabra1 em1 knock-in mice carrying mutations that disrupt the interaction between GABA A Rα1 and PPT1, we found that the mutant mice exhibited impaired learning and memory, whereas the underlying cellular mechanisms remained largely unclear. Molecular analyses showed that heterozygous (HET) Gabra1 em1 mice (Gabra1 em1 HET) displayed normal GABA A Rα1 protein expression but persistent hyperpalmitoylation of GABA A Rα1. Electrophysiological recordings demonstrated the decreased neuronal excitability, enhanced inhibitory synaptic transmission and impaired hippocampal long-term potentiation (LTP). Behavioral analyses further revealed deficits in learning, memory and social behavior. The homozygous (HOMO) Gabra1 em1 mice (Gabra1 em1 HOMO) exhibited a marked reduction in GABA A Rα1 protein expression, accompanied by enhanced neuronal excitability and excitatory synaptic transmission, but impaired LTP and learning and memory along with a shorten life span. Collectively, these findings indicate that Gabra1 em1 HET mice represent a valuable model for investigating the physiological and pathological roles of protein palmitoylation, as aberrant GABA A Rα1 palmitoylation disrupts neuronal excitability, synaptic plasticity, and cognitive function without altering receptor expression. In contrast, the phenotypes observed in Gabra1 em1 HOMO mice are primarily attributable to the marked reduction in GABA A Rα1 protein expression, which consequently impairs synaptic plasticity and learning and memory. These findings provide new mechanistic insights into the role of protein palmitoylation in neurological disorders and offer a theoretical foundation for the development of precision therapeutic strategies targeting palmitoylation homeostasis.

items.title: CSF1R haploinsufficiency reveals subtle and selective age- and sex-dependent vulnerabilities in cognition and white matter without overt neurodegeneration.
items.abstract: Adult-onset leukoencephalopathy with axonal spheroids and pigmented glia (ALSP) is caused by autosomal dominant mutations in the colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF1R), yet the extent to which CSF1R haploinsufficiency alone drives cognitive and neurobiological dysfunction remains unclear. Here, we performed a longitudinal multi-level characterization of behavioral, neuroimaging, cellular, and molecular phenotypes in male and female Csf1r+/- mice to determine the impact of partial CSF1R loss across aging. Cognitive function was assessed using touchscreen-based tasks probing cognitive flexibility, working memory, selective attention, and extinction learning, given that executive function is mainly compromised in ALSP. Brain microstructure was evaluated by diffusion-weighted MRI, complemented by MALDI mass spectrometry imaging to examine regional phospholipid composition. Cell-type quantification and gene expression analyses were performed to identify potential cellular and molecular correlates. Across most domains and ages, Csf1r+/- mice exhibited preserved cognitive performance and cellular composition. Within this broadly intact framework, subtle, age- and sex-dependent vulnerabilities emerged. Aged females showed reduced fractional anisotropy and neurite density in the corpus callosum and left primary motor cortex, along with region-specific alterations in phosphatidylcholine species. Aged males exhibited increased response persistence at the final extinction session and elevated false alarm rates under maximal attentional load. Notably, these changes occurred in the absence of microglial or oligodendrocyte loss, indicating mild microstructural and circuit-level alterations rather than widespread neurodegeneration. Collectively, these findings indicate that CSF1R haploinsufficiency does not recapitulate the severe phenotype of ALSP but instead reveals selective, sex-specific vulnerabilities in white matter and cognitive function. This profile is consistent with a sensitized state in which additional factors may be required to drive disease progression.

items.title: Common Phenomenal and Neural Substrate Geometry in Visual Motion Perception.
items.abstract: What is a possible physical substrate of the qualitative aspects of consciousness (qualia)? Answering this question is a central goal of consciousness research. Due to their subjective and ineffable nature, finding a quantitative way to characterise qualia from verbal description has thus far proven elusive. To overcome the challenge of expressing subjective experience, recent structural and relational approaches have been proposed from mathematics. Yet, as far as we know, no attempts have been made to evaluate the relationship between a certain structure of qualia and the structure of a candidate underlying physical substrate. Towards this ambitious goal of linking the structures of qualia and physical, we set out to make an empirical first step by focusing on experienced dissimilarity of visual motion in human participants and stimulus-evoked neural population response geometry recorded from mouse primary visual cortex. From human participants (N=171), we obtained dissimilarity ratings of visual motion experiences induced by 48 stimuli, spanning across 8 directions and 6 spatial frequencies. Analysis revealed a human dissimilarity structure that was not well captured by a simple monotonic function of physical motion-direction difference alone nor by a pure orientation-symmetry account. From nine individual mice, we recorded single-neuron activity (n=751) with optical imaging in both awake and lightly anaesthetised conditions (isoflurane 0.6-0.8%). From neuron population responses to a similar set of motion stimuli, we computed a distance matrix that is comparable to our human dissimilarity matrix. Quantitative analyses show structural commonalities between a human dissimilarity structure and mouse neural structure, where a categorical organisation of stimulus direction best explained both. These commonalities were similar in awake and anaesthetised recordings, suggesting that this coarse V1 geometry is relatively insensitive to this type of anaesthesia; future work combining behaviour with causal intervention is required to relate such neural structures to conscious experience. Finally, we list several empirical factors that can be improved to promote our qualia structure approach in the future.

items.title: Diffusion MRI reveals stage-dependent microstructural responses to early ferroptosis inhibition in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.
items.abstract: Background Neurodegeneration drives irreversible disability in multiple sclerosis (MS). Ferroptosis has been implicated in MS and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), but its spatiotemporal dynamics and imaging correlates remain unclear. Methods We combined 7.0 T diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) with histopathological and molecular analyses to evaluate the effects of Liproxstatin-1 (Lip-1) in mice with EAE induced by myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein peptide 35-55 (MOG 35-55 ). Sixty-four female C57BL/6 mice were assigned to control, EAE, early-treatment (Early-Tx; Lip-1 from day 12), and late-treatment (Late-Tx; Lip-1 from day 18) groups. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and tissue analyses were performed at days 20 and 30 post-immunization. Results Early-Tx reduced clinical severity at day 30 (vs. EAE; p Conclusions Ferroptosis-related molecular alterations are associated with stage-dependent inflammatory demyelinating injury in EAE. Early Lip-1 treatment provides greater microstructural protection than delayed treatment. High-field DTI sensitively detects treatment-responsive microstructural injury and may help monitor ferroptosis-related pathology in demyelinating disease.

items.title: Pain mechanisms in trigeminal neuralgia: From peripheral pathology to brain network reorganization and neurosurgical implications.
items.abstract: Objectives Trigeminal neuralgia (TN) involves peripheral neurovascular pathology and may also be associated with maladaptive neuroplastic changes in central nervous system networks. This review synthesizes evidence on peripheral and central pain mechanisms, neuroimaging biomarkers, molecular and transcriptomic correlates, and neurosurgical implications, including emerging neuromodulation strategies. Materials and methods This narrative review drew on topic-oriented searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science conducted between June 27 and July 5, 2026, covering literature published through June 2026. Supplementary targeted searches and reference-list screening were used to identify relevant publications. Evidence was synthesized qualitatively. Results Evidence supports a multilevel model of TN involving peripheral pathology and central neuroplastic changes. Neuroimaging studies report structural and functional alterations in sensorimotor, salience, limbic, and default mode networks, alongside disrupted structure-function coupling. Partial restoration of functional connectivity after neurosurgical treatment has been reported, although outcomes vary. Transcriptomic findings link imaging abnormalities to genes involved in ion channel function, synaptic signaling, neuroinflammation, and energy metabolism but remain hypothesis-generating. Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) may provide short-term analgesic benefit; however, evidence is limited and heterogeneous. Conclusions TN may be understood as a disorder involving interactions between peripheral pathology and central nervous system reorganization. Integrating neuroimaging and molecular evidence may inform future patient stratification and neurosurgical decision-making. Individualized neuromodulation remains investigational and requires further clinical validation.

items.title: Intraoperative and postoperative fluid administration is associated with transfusion in open arteriovenous malformation and aneurysm surgery.
items.abstract: Background Red blood cell transfusion to manage hemodynamic instability or blood loss during and after open cerebrovascular surgery has been associated with postoperative complications, making transfusion avoidance an important quality-improvement target. Iatrogenic hemodilution from liberal crystalloid administration may contribute to perioperative anemia, but its relevance in open aneurysm and arteriovenous malformation (AVM) surgery is poorly defined. We investigated factors associated with receiving intraoperative and postoperative transfusion in these open cerebrovascular procedures and the association between transfusion and early postoperative outcomes. Methods In this single-center retrospective propensity-matched cohort study, patients who underwent open aneurysm or AVM surgery and received an intraoperative or postoperative red blood cell transfusion were matched 1:1 with non-transfused controls. Perioperative variables-including intraoperative and 72-h postoperative fluid administration, estimated blood loss, physiological parameters, comorbidities, and laboratory values-were compared using univariate analysis, and multivariable Firth logistic regression was used to evaluate factors associated with transfusion. To address the temporal relationship between fluid and transfusion, a time-anchored analysis compared pre-transfusion fluids received with fluids received by controls to the same time point. Intensive care unit and hospital length of stay were evaluated. Results Fifty-six patients (28 transfused, 28 controls) were analyzed. Transfused patients received more intravenous fluid in the first 72 postoperative hours (13.1 ± 4.4 vs 9.8 ± 4.6 L, p = 0.009), and transfusion percentage increased across fluid quartiles (21 %, 50 %, 64 %, and 64 %; p for trend = 0.020). Transfused patients also had a higher American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class and longer operative duration. Similarly, in the time-anchored analysis, receiving more fluids was associated with transfusion (adjusted OR 1.28 per L, 95 % CI 1.14-1.45), including after additional adjustment for ASA class (OR 1.23, 95 % CI 1.08-1.40). Intensive care unit and hospital stays were longer among transfused patients, but the differences were not statistically significant. Conclusions Greater fluid administration perioperatively was associated with receiving intraoperative or postoperative transfusion after open aneurysm and AVM surgery. These findings are consistent with, but do not establish, a contribution of iatrogenic hemodilution, and they support prospective evaluation of fluid management.

items.title: Interhemispheric hygroma as a predictor of post-traumatic hydrocephalus after decompressive craniectomy: a phenotype-specific systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Background Post-traumatic hydrocephalus (PTH) is a recognized complication following decompressive craniectomy (DC) for traumatic brain injury (TBI). Subdural hygroma has been implicated as a potential risk factor; however, prior studies have been limited by heterogeneous definitions and lack of distinction between hygroma subtypes. The role of interhemispheric hygroma (IHH) as a specific predictor of hydrocephalus remains unclear. Methods We conducted a systematic review in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. We searched PubMed (MEDLINE), Cochrane, and Scopus from inception to March 2025. We included studies evaluating hydrocephalus following DC for TBI and reporting data on subdural hygroma. We adopted a phenotype-specific approach, focusing on IHH as the primary exposure and clinically significant hydrocephalus (shunt-dependent or clearly defined clinical hydrocephalus) as the outcome. We assessed study quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. We performed the meta-analysis using study-level 2 × 2 data, with fixed-effect and random-effects models for primary and sensitivity analyses, respectively. Results We included 14 studies comprising 1,621 patients in the qualitative synthesis. We included three studies with comparable definitions in the primary meta-analysis, demonstrating a strong association between IHH and hydrocephalus (pooled OR 6.75, 95% CI 3.4-13.41; I 2 = 9.8%). Sensitivity analyses incorporating additional heterogeneous studies confirmed the association, although with a lower effect size and increased heterogeneity. Studies relying on radiological definitions alone were excluded from pooled analysis but showed similar trends. Across studies, incidence of hydrocephalus varied widely depending on outcome definitions. Conclusions Interhemispheric hygroma is strongly associated with the development of clinically significant hydrocephalus following DC. A phenotype-specific analytical approach reduces heterogeneity and improves interpretability compared with prior studies. Recognition of IHH may facilitate early identification of patients at risk for PTH and support more targeted postoperative monitoring and management strategies.

items.title: Effect of circadian-oriented goal-directed sedation on sleep quality and clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.
items.abstract: Background Sleep disruption and circadian rhythm disturbances are common in mechanically ventilated intensive care unit (ICU) patients and are associated with delirium, prolonged ventilation, and poor clinical outcomes. Conventional sedation strategies may further impair sleep architecture and circadian regulation. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the effects of circadian-oriented, goal-directed sedation on sleep quality and clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated ICU patients. Methods This study enrolled 65 mechanically ventilated patients admitted to ICU at Suzhou Ninth People's Hospital between March 2024 and December 2024. Using convenience sampling, 33 patients admitted between March and July 2024 were allocated to the control group and received routine sedation and nursing care, while 32 patients admitted between August and December 2024 were formed the intervention group and received sedation management individualized according to circadian sleep-wake patterns. Sleep quality was assessed on days 1, 3, 5, and 7 after intervention using the Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ) and a portable sleep monitor. Delirium was evaluated by Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU (CAM-ICU). Sedative dosage, duration of mechanical ventilation, length of ICU and hospital stay, , clinical improvement rate, complications, and hospitalization costs were compared between groups. Results Baseline characteristics were comparable between the two groups. Sleep quality improved over time in both groups; however, Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire scores were significantly higher in the intervention group at all assessment points (p Conclusion Sedation management aligned with circadian sleep-wake patterns significantly improves sleep quality, reduces sedative requirements, lowers delirium incidence, and shortens mechanical ventilation duration, demonstrating a favorable safety profile in mechanically ventilated patients.

items.title: Is It a "Hybrid Swarm"? Opportunities for More Informative Terminology in Conservation Genomics.
items.abstract: Hybridization is common in wild taxa, which may cause conservation concerns if hybridization occurs following disturbance or species introductions. High throughput DNA sequencing makes genomic analysis of many individuals feasible, vastly improving and promoting more studies on hybridization. However, more precise genomic identification of hybrids has not always extended to more precise use of terminology to describe hybrid ancestry. For hybridizing species of conservation concern, it is critical to understand hybridization dynamics precisely in order to effectively manage imperiled taxa. We conducted a review of 67 representative journal articles that use the term "hybrid swarm" in reference to hybridization, as variation in the usage of the term makes it difficult to understand which biological processes are being described. We found that "hybrid swarm" is used in several contexts across studies using various methods and numbers of genetic markers, reflecting vastly different statistical power and degrees of evidence for extensive hybridization. We encourage researchers working with genomic datasets to use clearer terminology when describing hybridization outcomes. We elaborate on scenario-specific terminology to strengthen uniformity in hybridization language, which we hope will promote more precise descriptions of hybridization and improve the clarity of future research on hybridization.

items.title: Turtle Herbivory Suppresses Seagrass Function but Reveals Recovery Potential in a Remote Coral Reef Atoll.
items.abstract: Seagrasses are recognised as ecologically and culturally significant habitats across the globe supporting human livelihoods, biodiversity, and carbon storage. In the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, a remote coral reef atoll in the eastern Indian Ocean, seagrasses provide ecosystem services and support culturally, ecologically, and economically important species. However, these meadows have suffered devastating declines, with ongoing green turtle herbivory identified as a key pressure restricting Thalassia hemprichii persistence.To examine how herbivory shapes seagrass traits and function, we compared plots protected from grazing for over two years using exclusion cages against continuously grazed plots across two sites.Seagrass traits at the meadow-scale (shoot density, leaf area and biomass), as well as some functionality (primary production and nutrient storage capacity), were improved with protection from herbivory pressure. Substantial reductions in the belowground biomass in the grazed plots indicate that these seagrasses are operating under severe metabolic constraints. In contrast, some plant-scale traits (photosynthetic rate and growth rate) were not altered despite ongoing herbivory pressure, indicating some capacity for recovery at the individual plant scale.Representing one of the longest turtle exclusion studies in seagrass ecosystems, these results demonstrate that herbivory is driving systemic degradation across multiple biological scales, but these seagrasses currently retain the capacity to recover once grazing pressure is reduced. Synthesis . Tropical seagrass meadows subjected to continuous herbivory pressure can persist in a chronically depleted state. Herbivore exclusion experiments demonstrate that reducing herbivory can unlock the recovery potential of seagrass. These findings highlight the need for nuanced management strategies to safeguard these meadows in a time where seagrasses continue to decline at both localised and global scales, and the global turtle populations are simultaneously on the rise.

items.title: Concentration- and duration-associated transcriptional changes in HepG2 cells following long-term nominal nanomolar PFOA exposure.
items.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) is a persistent environmental contaminant whose transcriptional effects under prolonged low-dose exposure remain insufficiently characterized. We investigated transcriptomic responses in HepG2 cells exposed to nominal PFOA concentrations of 1, 10, or 100nM for 6- or 12-weeks using RNA-seq, differential expression analysis, Gene Ontology enrichment, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). No differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were detected at 1nM PFOA at either time point. At 10nM and 100nM PFOA, respectively, 149 and 183 DEGs were identified after 6 weeks, predominantly downregulated, compared with 10 and 56 DEGs after 12 weeks. The 6-week response included induction of immediate-early genes (FOS, EGR1) and repression of transcriptional and developmental regulators. At 12 weeks, six downregulated genes, including FOS, FOSB, and PLA2G2A, were shared between concentrations, with no shared upregulated genes. GSEA showed negative enrichment of transcriptional and developmental gene sets at both time points, whereas protein folding and stress response gene sets were enriched only at 6 weeks. WGCNA identified one dominant concentration-associated module at 6 weeks and several smaller modules at 12 weeks, most showing preservation across exposure durations. Together, these findings demonstrate concentration- and duration-associated transcriptional differences following prolonged nanomolar PFOA exposure, while the underlying biological mechanisms and potential contributions of culture-associated changes require further investigation.

items.title: Targeted flavour development in chocolate: omics-driven insights into cocoa fermentation.
items.abstract: Cocoa fermentation is the critical microbially driven process that transforms the genetic potential of cocoa beans into the complex flavour precursors essential for high-quality chocolate. Despite its importance, fermentation remains highly variable and poorly controlled, representing a major bottleneck in the production of premium chocolate. This review explores how advanced multi-omics approaches are improving our understanding of cocoa fermentation and flavour formation by linking microbial ecology, metabolite production and sensory outcomes. It highlights the transition of cocoa fermentation from a traditional practice towards a predictive, controllable biotechnological process. Such advances pave the way for the development of tailored starter cultures, optimised fermentation processes, and ultimately, consistent production of targeted flavour development in chocolates with enhanced quality and market value.

items.title: Novel ecological observations of Gobiodon assemblages and an extended species distribution on Nyinggulu Reef, Western Australia
items.abstract: Coral-dwelling gobies (Gobiodon Bleeker 1856) are among the most specialised cryptobenthic reef fishes, living almost exclusively within branching and corymbose corals throughout the Indo-Pacific. Despite extensive research on the ecology of the genus, comparatively little is known about Gobiodon assemblages from Western Australia. Here, we document the diversity, habitat use, host associations, social organisation, and notable behavioural observations of Gobiodon inhabiting shallow Acropora corals at Manimanira (Five Fingers Reef), Nyinggulu Marine Park, during two field seasons in 2025 and 2026. Seven species were recorded: Gobiodon axillaris, G. citrinus, G. histrio, G. oculolineatus, G. okinawae, G. rivulatus, and G. quinquestrigatus. Repeated observations suggested habitat partitioning among dominant species, with G. axillaris occurring primarily on shallow reef flats, while G. oculolineatus and G. quinquestrigatus occupy deeper corals. Host associations differed in several respects from previous reports, including frequent occupancy of Acropora protoeiformis and use of a plating coral by G. citrinus, and mixed-species occupancy of A. acervata. Species also differed markedly in social organisation, from pair-forming species to those forming large social groups. In addition, the confirmed occurrence of G. oculolineatus represents the first documented record from coastal Western Australia, offering a new locality and substantial extension (~3,500 km) to its known distribution. These observations provide the first detailed account of the Gobiodon assemblage from Nyinggulu and establish an important baseline for future studies of coral-associated gobies in this region.

items.title: Ecophysiological assessment of aquatic plants in a Southern Türkiye Lake: heavy metal bioconcentration, phytochemicals, and biological activities.
items.abstract: In the present study, the aquatic macrophytes of Golbasi Lake, located in Hatay Province, the southern part of Türkiye, were investigated for heavy metal pollution. The investigation focused on commonly found macrophytes, such as Ceratophyllum demersum , Lemna minor , and Salvinia natans , to assess cadmium, cobalt, copper, chromium, iron, lead, manganese, nickel, and zinc using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry. Nickel and lead concentrations exceeded the prescribed threshold values. Cadmium, lead, nickel, and zinc concentrations were higher, with copper and iron exceeding the critical values. Among the three species, L. minor showed the greatest accumulation of Cd, Cu, Pb, and Zn, with Cd concentrations approximately 2911% and 300% higher than those in C. demersum and S. natans , respectively. L. minor exhibited the highest total phenolic and flavonoid contents, which were approximately 24.9% and 34.2% higher, respectively, than those of C. demersum . In contrast, S. natans showed the highest DPPH radical-scavenging activity, approximately 14.4% higher than C. demersum . All the extracts showed antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus ; the highest antibacterial activity was observed for L. minor . The present study thus shows the impact of agricultural, industrial, mining, and drainage activities on the Golbasi Lake ecosystem, highlighting the role of aquatic plants as bioindicators for heavy metal detection. The results emphasize the need to remove heavy metals before discharging them into Golbasi Lake and to implement effective environmental management strategies to maintain the balance of nature and the eco-sustainability of the Golbasi Lake ecosystem.

items.title: Spatiotemporal Trends in Suicide: Sociodemographic, Economic, and Environmental Factors.
items.abstract: Suicide is one of the world's leading public health problems, with more than 720,000 deaths annually. Suicide has traditionally been studied from an individual perspective. However, research has increasingly highlighted the influence of community-level factors on suicide risk. This study aimed to (1) analyze the spatial distribution of suicide mortality at the provincial level in Spain (2018-2022); (2) perform stratified analyses by sex and age group; and (3) compare suicide risk across different phases of the COVID-19 pandemic. We used data from the Spanish National Institute of Statistics on 17,809 suicide deaths in 47 peninsular provinces between 2018 and 2022. Covariates included sociodemographic (e.g., aging rate, population density), economic (e.g., unemployment, GDP), and environmental (e.g., temperature) indicators. Bayesian hierarchical spatial Poisson regression models were fitted to estimate suicide risk and identify relevant contextual variables. The general spatial model revealed a higher risk of suicide in provinces with lower population density, higher aging rates, and lower health expenditure. Other covariates such as gross domestic product, unemployment, or temperature were associated with specific sex or age groups. Suicide risk was highest in the northwestern provinces and lowest in the central regions. Stratified analyses showed similar patterns across gender and age groups, and between time periods, with some variations in spatial distribution. This study reveals significant spatial heterogeneity in suicide risk across Spanish regions, influenced by sociodemographic, economic, and environmental factors. These findings underline the importance of regionally tailored suicide prevention policies, especially in aging and low-density areas with low health investment.

items.title: Parenting stress spirals and a gendered labour division over the Christmas holidays.
items.abstract: The Christmas period heightens parental demands and invisible labour, yet little is known about how these processes unfold in daily life. This study used experience sampling data from 293 UK parents over 35 days to examine temporal associations between cognitive labour, emotion suppression, and subjective stress across the holiday season. Dynamic Structural Equation Modelling revealed strong autoregressive stability for all constructs and reciprocal moment-to-moment links between cognitive labour and stress, indicating a self-reinforcing cycle. Cognitive labour and stress also predicted subsequent emotion suppression, suggesting that emotion suppression operates as a situational coping response to mental and stress overload. At the between-person level, social support reduced emotion suppression but did not buffer stress or cognitive labour. Gender differences emerged only for cognitive labour, with mothers reporting higher levels than fathers. Findings highlight the dynamic interplay between invisible labour and stress and underscore the psychological strains parents face during the holidays.

items.title: State-dependent roles of inflammation across pain conditions: insights from human transcriptomics.
items.abstract: Background Inflammation is widely viewed as a driver of pain, yet clinical and transcriptomic studies report conflicting associations. A clearer understanding of how inflammatory processes relate to pain across clinical contexts is essential for improving diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of chronic pain. Methods We analysed whole-blood RNA sequencing from seven human cohorts spanning four pain conditions, including acute, postoperative, chronic localised, and chronic widespread pain in almost 500 blood samples with corresponding pain intensity scores. Using gene-level meta-analyses, pathway enrichment, and immune cell-specific gene ontologies, we tested how inflammatory responses relate to current pain, future pain trajectories, and within-person changes over time. Results Inflammation emerged as one of the strongest biological correlates of pain across all cohorts, yet its association direction depended on the pain state. In acute musculoskeletal and postoperative pain, higher inflammatory activation, which correlated with enhanced neutrophil and macrophage function, was associated with greater pain intensity but also correlated with better subsequent recovery, consistent with an adaptive inflammatory response. In chronic localised pain, this relationship was disrupted and inverted: higher inflammatory activity was linked to lower pain intensity and associated with worse long-term outcomes. In chronic widespread pain, macrophage-related inflammatory activity remained positively associated with both pain severity and persistence, suggesting progression toward a maladaptive immune state. Conclusions These findings indicate that inflammation is not uniformly detrimental in pain but plays distinct roles depending on disease stage and context. Inflammation might support resolution during acute injury yet become dysregulated in chronic and nociplastic pain. Recognising these context-dependent roles could help explain conflicting findings in the literature and guide more precise use of anti-inflammatory therapies.

items.title: Influence of Sex and Fatigue on Velocity Loss as a Set Termination Criterion in the Bench Press.
items.abstract: Purpose To analyze the relationship between the percentage of velocity loss (VL) and the percentage of completed repetitions relative to the maximum possible (%Rep) during a single set to failure, preceded by previous efforts (PE), in the bench press exercise in men and women. Methods Thirty participants (15 men and 15 women) performed 4 protocols (1 week apart) consisting of a set to failure with 60% of one-repetition maximum preceded by a previous effort, consisting of 3 sets at 60% one-repetition maximum. Each protocol differed in the VL attained during the preceding effort: 0% (PEVL0), 20% (PEVL20), 40% (PEVL40), and 60% (PEVL60). The VL-%Rep relationship was assessed using the coefficient of determination (R2) and the standard error of estimate. Results The R2 in the VL-%Rep relationship remained stable for different fatigue levels and sexes (men: R2 = .94-.93; women: R2 = .92-.90, with standard error of estimate values of 7%-9%). Men performed a higher %Rep than women for the same VL, particularly at low-to-moderate VL thresholds. However, prior high fatigue reduced these sex differences. Conclusions The strong and consistent relationship between VL and %Rep observed across all conditions confirms that VL is a robust indicator of the level of effort in bench press, regardless of sex or previous fatigue. However, men completed a greater proportion of repetitions for the same VL, especially under low-to-moderate fatigue. This suggests that, to improve precision when using VL to prescribe or monitor the level of effort, women may require higher VL thresholds to achieve an equivalent relative effort.
