items.title: Cognitive Reserve Reconsidered: Asymmetry Across Proxies Challenges a Domain-General Mechanism.
items.abstract: Cognitive reserve (CR) is a broad framework for explaining why individuals differ in cognitive functioning in the face of aging and neuropathology. One influential mechanistic account proposes that cognitively demanding life experiences such as education, occupational complexity, and cognitively stimulating activities augment a domain-general cognitive capacity that subsequently provides resilience. We refer to this more specific claim as cognitive reserve augmentation (CRA). This narrative and conceptual review evaluates the inferential strength of the evidence for CRA, emphasizing prospective cohort studies as the strongest available observational design for evaluating causal hypotheses. Across meta-analyses, several putative reserve-building experiences show consistent protective associations; however, comparison across prospective cohort studies reveals a striking asymmetry: whereas education, occupational complexity, and cognitively stimulating activities predict reduced risk or delayed clinical diagnosis of dementia, bilingualism-also proposed as a reserve-building cognitive experience-does not. This pattern constrains the assumption that diverse cognitive experiences augment a common reserve mechanism. Life-course evidence further indicates that associations between traditional CR proxies and later cognitive functioning can be substantially attenuated when earlier cognitive ability is measured directly. We argue that these findings are compatible with multiple pathways involving selection, correlated socioeconomic and health factors, domain-specific knowledge and expertise, processing efficiency, and effects on brain and physical health, as well as possible changes in cognitive capacity. Distinguishing among these alternatives requires specifying what experience is proposed to change, which experiences should and should not produce that change, and which outcomes would challenge the proposed mechanism. CR may therefore remain useful as a broad descriptive framework even when evidence for CRA or another specified reserve mechanism is incomplete.

items.title: A behavioral and electrophysiological study on the influence of menstrual cycle, estradiol and progesterone on the social approach-avoidance behavior tendencies of women.
items.abstract: It remains unclear whether women's social approach-avoidance behaviors toward different facial expressions are influenced by their menstrual cycles, estradiol and progesterone levels, or what the underlying electrophysiological mechanisms might be. This study collected data on the levels of estradiol and progesterone, social approach-avoidance behavior and electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings from 27 women with natural menstrual cycles during three phases- early follicular phase, late follicular phase, and mid-luteal phase. The results showed that women in the late follicular phase exhibited a faster approach tendency and a smaller LPP amplitude to happy faces compared to the early follicular phase; women in the mid-luteal phase exhibited a faster approach tendency and a smaller LPP amplitude to fearful faces compared to the late follicular phase. Estradiol levels is positively correlated with the efficiency of approach behavior toward happy faces, while progesterone levels is positively correlated with the efficiency of approach behavior toward fearful faces. The results show that women's social approach-avoidance behaviors are specifically regulated by the menstrual cycle, estradiol and progesterone, and exhibit higher cognitive processing efficiency in the late positive potential (LPP) of the brain. These findings are manifestations in social interactions of the characteristics of women's interest pursuit and self-restraint under the influence of different sex hormones formed during evolution, updating established hormone-behavior links in social emotional contexts.

items.title: Reduction in Fear of Movement Predicts Long-Term Decreases In Functional Disability Among Adolescents With Juvenile Fibromyalgia.
items.abstract: Fear of movement and pain catastrophizing are associated with higher pain intensity and disability in adolescents with juvenile fibromyalgia (JFM), but it is unknown whether treatment-related reductions in these areas predict long-term outcomes. This study reports results of secondary data analyses from a multi-center randomized clinical trial (Fibromyalgia Integrative Training; FIT Teens) in which adolescents with JFM (N=317) received either cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), graded aerobic exercise, or CBT combined with neuromuscular exercise training. In the parent trial, functional disability of youth in all three treatments improved significantly at post-treatment and was maintained over one year. The objective of this study was to assess whether reductions in fear of movement and pain catastrophizing through 3-month follow-up predicted functional disability at 3- and 12-months. A novel latent curve modeling approach was employed to estimate distal outcomes across treatment groups. Results indicated that reductions in pain catastrophizing and fear of movement through 3-month follow-up both significantly predicted functional disability at the 3-month follow-up (p's<.05). However, only a reduction in fear of movement predicted functional disability at 12-months. Results support prioritizing strategies to reduce fear of movement in non-pharmacologic interventions for JFM which are associated with long-term improvements in function. PERSPECTIVE: Results of this study highlight the importance of assessing and addressing fear of movement among youth with widespread musculoskeletal pain. Treatments that include effective ways to improve movement confidence in adolescents with JFM may help optimize their long-term functional outcomes.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of GLP-1 receptor agonists in patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders treated with antipsychotics: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Weight gain and impaired glucose metabolism are common complications of antipsychotic treatment in schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD). While beneficial in other populations, the efficacy and safety of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) in SSD remain unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating GLP-1 RAs versus placebo in SSD patients treated with antipsychotics. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched until January 2026. Random-effects models were used to pool mean differences (MDs), standardized mean differences (SMDs), and risk ratios (RRs), as appropriate. Seven RCTs including 481 participants were included. Compared with placebo, GLP-1 RAs significantly reduced body weight (MD -6.98 kg; 95% CI -10.53 to -3.43), BMI (MD -2.51 kg/m²; 95% CI -3.51 to -1.51), waist circumference (MD -5.05 cm; 95% CI -6.66 to -3.44), HbA1c (MD -0.32 percentage points; 95% CI -0.38 to -0.26), and fasting blood glucose (MD -0.54 mmol/L; 95% CI -0.83 to -0.25). Heterogeneity was substantial for body weight (I²=93%) and BMI (I²=80%). No significant effects emerged for blood pressure or lipid parameters. Psychiatric symptom severity did not differ between GLP-1 RAs and placebo (SMD -0.05; 95% CI -0.36 to 0.25). Gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent with GLP-1 RAs than with placebo, while overall study drop-out did not differ between groups. GLP-1 RAs improve short-term anthropometric and glycemic outcomes in SSD patients treated with antipsychotics. However, the limited number of trials, substantial heterogeneity in weight-related outcomes, and relatively short follow-up warrant cautious interpretation and further large-scale RCTs.

items.title: Disparities in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and severe maternal morbidity: Evidence from a statewide birth cohort.
items.abstract: Objective Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) complicate 15% of pregnancies nationally and are a major contributor to severe maternal morbidity (SMM). We aimed to characterize temporal trends and demographic disparities in HDP incidence and evaluate the association between HDP and SMM in a statewide cohort. Methods This study is a descriptive and regression-based analysis of a retrospective cohort of Wisconsin births from 2017 to 2023. Data were obtained from the Wisconsin Hospital Association (WHA). Subtypes of HDP were identified using ICD-10 codes. Incidence rates of HDP per 10,000 births and average annual percent changes (AAPC) were estimated using Poisson regression and examined across demographic variables. Outcomes measured included SMM incidence, AAPCs, and SMM indicators by HDP. Results Among 388,250 pregnancies, the incidence of nearly all HDP subtypes rose from 2017 to 2023. Severe pre-eclampsia had the highest AAPC (11.8%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 10.6%-13.0%). HDP incidence was highest in urban areas, though the AAPC in preeclampsia was greater in rural areas (8.7%; 95% CI, 7.1%-10.3%; p = 0.004). Black patients experienced higher incidences of HDP, with significant differences in AAPC for HDP overall, chronic hypertension, and severe preeclampsia ( p Conclusion These findings highlight a growing burden of HDP in Wisconsin, with an increase in severe preeclampsia incidence and disparities by geography and race. Targeted interventions in rural areas and for Black patients are needed to improve disparities in HDP incidence and reduce SMM across Wisconsin.

items.title: Mode of conception and pregnancy outcomes at term among low-risk nulliparous patients.
items.abstract: Introduction Available data suggest that assisted reproductive technology (ART) is associated with adverse perinatal outcomes; however, prior studies have been confounded by multifetal gestations, preterm birth, and patient medical comorbidities. There are limited data on pregnancy outcomes among ART-conceived low-risk singleton pregnancies delivering at term. Thus, we aimed to measure the association between mode of conception and mode of delivery among low-risk nulliparous patients delivering singleton gestations at term. Methods Secondary analysis of the ARRIVE trial (NCT01990612), a multicenter randomized, controlled, unmasked, parallel-group trial of nulliparous patients delivering at term, March 2014-August 2017. Pregnancies were categorized by mode of conception as either ART or spontaneous. The primary outcome was cesarean delivery. Secondary outcomes included a composite of perinatal death and severe neonatal complications, and select maternal and neonatal adverse outcomes. Bivariate analyses compared baseline characteristics and outcomes by mode of conception. Primary and secondary outcomes were compared using multivariable logistic regression to generate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sensitivity analyses by type of ART (in vitro fertilization [IVF] vs. ovulation induction [OI] with or without artificial insemination [AI]) and by embryo age were planned. Results Of the 6106 participants in the original trial, 6084 met eligibility criteria: 157 (2.6%) conceived with ART and 5927 (97.4%) did not. Among those with ART, 103 (65.6%) underwent IVF and 54 (34.4%) conceived with OI or AI. Patients undergoing ART were noted to have an older age, differing race/ethnicity, lower body mass index (BMI), more likely to be married, employed full-time, privately insured, and less likely to smoke cigarettes. Cesarean occurred more frequently in those with ART than those spontaneously conceived (29.9% vs. 20.2%; OR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.20-2.40). This remained significant after adjusting for confounders (aOR, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.15-2.45) and was significant in subgroup analysis comparing IVF conception to spontaneous (31.1% vs. 20.2%; aOR, 1.78; 95% CI, 1.12-2.82). Additionally, there was no difference in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (aOR, 1.65; 95% CI, 1.00-2.73), other maternal morbidities, and adverse perinatal composite (aOR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.49-1.67). Conclusions Nulliparas delivering a singleton fetus at term conceived by ART had an increased rate of cesarean delivery, with no difference in hypertensive disorders or pregnancy or neonatal outcomes.

items.title: Delivering psychotherapy when there is no "post": The Healing for Gaza Global Clinic's model for care in conditions of ongoing violence.
items.abstract: Humanitarian responses to war-related trauma frequently prioritize scalable psychosocial activities or medication-adjacent services, while clinically governed psychotherapy remains uncommon in settings shaped by ongoing state violence. When psychotherapy is introduced, it is often without the conditions that make care safe and clinically coherent: stable privacy, continuity, supervised decision-making, culturally grounded formulation, and enforceable boundary governance. Further, in crises, cultural adaptation may be reduced to literal, decontextualized translation rather than interpretation as part of clinical work. This manuscript provides a program description of Healing for Gaza, a hybrid remote and field-based care model developed to extend access to clinically governed psychotherapy and psychiatric care for Palestinians from Gaza amid protracted violence and displacement. The model integrates trauma-informed psychotherapy, psychiatric services, periodic field missions for in-person and community interventions, and a structured training curriculum emphasizing both learning about care for trauma in this setting and countering clinical assumptions anchored in stable settings. In addition, this paper offers an operational account of how Healing for Gaza delivers psychotherapy as a governed clinical process: centralizing triage and coordination; providing clinic-managed communication channels to protect confidentiality in a system reliant on telehealth care; ensuring interpreters and clinicians are trained, consistently assigned, and integrated into supervision; applying workforce safeguards, including structured supervision and debriefing, reflective practices, caseload caps, and access to psychotherapy; and using a mixed-methods monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning framework oriented toward clinical quality and emerging risks. The manuscript concludes with principles that may guide adaptation of this architecture in other humanitarian contexts.

items.title: Moving towards evidence-based screening and investigations in first episode psychosis: A commentary on the ANZJP GRADE Schizophrenia Guidelines.
items.abstract: Physical health assessment and investigations are important considerations during the first episode of psychosis. These activities support diagnostic clarification, monitoring for iatrogenic harms and opportunistic screening to limit the multimorbidity that is often associated with psychotic disorders in the longer term. The recent 'Australian and New Zealand Journal of Psychiatry Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations (GRADE) guidelines for the management of schizophrenia' and the associated systematic review by Warren et al. fill a critical gap by providing evidence-based guidance on which investigations should be routine and when more targeted investigations are warranted. However, the guidance provided has a limited focus on affective psychosis, and its focus on targeted screening for sexually transmitted infections may underestimate the extent to which people experiencing the first episode of psychosis reflect an at-risk group. This commentary explores the relevance of further consideration of sexual health issues and affective psychosis in developing evidence-based guidance for physical health assessment and investigations at the first episode of psychosis.

items.title: Noise, Inequality, and Mental Health. Urban Challenges in the State of Mexico.
items.abstract: Environmental noise is an increasing public health concern, with effects that extend beyond hearing loss to include anxiety and depression. In the Global South, however, evidence remains limited, and most studies focus primarily on objective exposure measures, while subjective dimensions of noise experience remain less explored. This study examines the relationship between sociodemographic characteristics, perceived noise, and mental health in households of the State of Mexico, considering urban-rural differences. Data were collected from a probabilistic, stratified household survey (n = 400). Structural equation modeling (SEM) was applied using the diagonally weighted least squares estimator adjusted with expansion factors, and an exploratory spatial analysis was conducted through IDW interpolation to explore territorial patterns in predicted outcomes. The findings indicate that household size was a significant predictor of perceived noise, with larger households reporting higher levels. Perceived noise was significantly associated with depressive symptoms but not with anxiety, and living in urban municipalities was directly associated with higher levels of depression, independent of perceived noise. Spatial analysis further revealed that patterns of high perceived noise and depression are concentrated in metropolitan areas. Overall, the results suggest that environmental noise is a relevant, though modest, environmental factor associated with mental health in the State of Mexico, particularly in urban contexts, indicating that it merits consideration alongside other urban stressors in planning and public health efforts addressing territorial disparities.

items.title: Unequal Burdens of Health Misinformation: Disparities in Exposure, Susceptibility, and Outcomes.
items.abstract: Health misinformation is a pervasive and inequitable public health challenge with consequences that extend beyond knowledge deficits to influence behavior, healthcare engagement, and psychosocial well-being. This narrative review and critical synthesis examines current evidence on health misinformation disparities, drawing on empirical, theoretical, and policy-relevant literature to characterize differential patterns of exposure, susceptibility, and outcomes across population groups. Exposure and susceptibility are not evenly distributed, as they disproportionately affect populations with intersecting vulnerabilities related to race, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, language, digital access, and health literacy. Evidence demonstrates that susceptibility is shaped by historical and structural factors including medical mistrust, limited health and digital literacy, and algorithmically reinforced social media ecosystems. Meanwhile, age, cognitive style, and sociocultural context further modulate risk. Health misinformation has tangible downstream effects, contributing to vaccine hesitancy, delayed or avoided care, and adverse psychosocial outcomes, including increased anxiety, depressive symptoms, and erosion of trust in healthcare institutions. Cross-national data indicate that disparities are amplified in regions with weaker digital health infrastructure and limited access to timely, multilingual information. Interventions such as debunking, prebunking, media literacy programs, and community-engaged initiatives show the strongest evidence for correcting specific false beliefs whereas evidence for durable translation to behavioral change and sustained health outcomes is more limited and requires further evaluation in equity-diverse populations. Addressing health misinformation through an equity-focused lens is critical for mitigating disparities, restoring institutional trust, and promoting equitable health outcomes across populations.

items.title: Understanding diagnostic challenges and identifying priorities to tackle antimicrobial resistance in conflict zones.
items.abstract: Armed conflict is a key driver of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Diagnostics are critical tools for limiting the impact of AMR where resources are limited. We analyse how conflict shifts the needs and deliverability of AMR diagnostics and identify opportunities to strengthen scope and capacity in these settings with persistent state-delivered health governance and policy. Key priorities include optimisation of robust diagnostic processing, workload and data sharing tools, and procurement policies suitable for resource-limited settings, including linked electronic workload and data-sharing tools with offline options, to support delivery of individual patient care, infection prevention and control, and surveillance.

items.title: Joint associations between 10-year average residential proximity-based pesticide exposures and cardiometabolic markers among women from an agricultural region.
items.abstract: Background Chronic exposure to multiple agricultural pesticides may influence cardiometabolic disease risk. Objective We examined joint associations between long-term, residential proximity-based exposure to seven pesticide classes and cardiometabolic risk factors among women from an agricultural region using complementary mixture methods. Methods Women participating in the Center for the Health Assessment of Mothers and Children of Salinas Maternal Cognition Study completed anthropometric measurements, blood collection, and interviews in 2022-2024. Using participant-reported addresses and California's Pesticide Use Reporting database, we estimated average agricultural use (kg/year) of seven pesticide classes within 1 km of homes in the 10 years preceding outcome assessment. We used quantile g-computation (QGCOMP) and Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) to estimate joint associations with cardiometabolic risk factors and explore the relative contributions of pesticide classes to joint exposure effects. Results Participants (n = 459) were 48.4 ± 5.5 years old at outcome assessment. Using QGCOMP, a joint one-quartile increase in pesticide exposures was associated with higher systolic blood pressure (β = 1.82 mm Hg, 95% CI = 0.38, 3.25), higher pulse pressure (β = 1.59 mm Hg, 95% CI = 0.56, 2.63), and lower HDL cholesterol (β = -1.35 mg/dL, 95% CI = -2.61, -0.10; Impact This study evaluates the cardiometabolic impacts of long-term, residential proximity-based exposure to various agricultural pesticide classes among midlife women from an agricultural region. Using two complementary mixture modeling approaches, we demonstrate robust joint associations between chronic pesticide exposure and adverse cardiometabolic outcomes, specifically higher blood pressure and lower HDL cholesterol. Our findings highlight the relevance of ambient, non-occupational pesticide exposure to cardiometabolic disease risk and underscore the importance of considering correlated exposure mixtures when assessing environmental health risks. To our knowledge, this is the first study to examine long-term, joint exposure to current-use pesticides in association with a wide range of cardiometabolic outcomes.

The influence of combat-related traumatic injury (CRTI), baseline respiratory rate (RR), and physical function/activity on the relationship between SPB and HRV has not been examined previously and was the aim of this study. Short-term HRV was measured using a single-lead electrocardiogram during five minutes of spontaneous breathing, followed by five minutes of SPB (six breaths/minute). We examined the effect modification of SPB on HRV by CRTI (yes/no), RR during spontaneous breathing ( Results A total of 962 male participants (median age: 37.6 years; n = 487 injured, n = 495 uninjured; mean 11years post-injury/deployment) with paired spontaneous-SPB HRV data were included. CRTI, 6MWD and MVPA did not significantly moderate the effect of SPB on HRV, but baseline RR ≥ 15 breaths/minute did, with Root-Mean-Square-Of-Successive-Difference (RMSSD) increasing from 15.57ms to 21.89ms (p Conclusion SPB improves HRV regardless of CRTI status. items.title: Creatine supplementation effects on cognition, sleep, and menopause symptoms in response to six weeks of high-intensity resistance training in perimenopausal females.
items.abstract: Introduction Perimenopause (PERI) women experience cognitive dysfunction, sleep disturbances, and menopause-related symptoms, yet few accessible and time-efficient interventions have been evaluated. Sleep and self-reported menopause symptoms (temperature sensitivity, fatigue, soreness, brain fog, and bloating) were monitored daily using a WHOOP wearable wristband. items.title: Contraceptive method choice by type of intimate partner violence: findings from the 2015 Colombian demographic and health survey.
items.abstract: Background Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a major global health issue and limits women's reproductive autonomy. Despite high IPV and contraception prevalences in Colombia, the link between specific types of IPV and contraceptive methods remains understudied. This study aimed to examine associations between IPV and the type of contraceptive method used by Colombian women. Methods This cross-sectional study used data from the 2015 Colombian Demographic and Health Surveys. The sample included 13,896 ever-partnered women aged 15-49 who were not pregnant, infecund, or used permanent methods. Contraceptive method was categorised as: no contraception, traditional/fertility awareness methods (FAM), intrauterine devices (IUDs)/implants, oral/injectables, and external condoms. Exposure variables included any IPV, physical, sexual and emotional violence, and controlling behaviour in the past 12 months. Adjusted multinomial logistic regressions were conducted, with a significance level of p Results Physical and emotional IPV were associated with higher relative risks of using traditional/FAMs and IUDs/implants, and lower probabilities of using oral/injectables or external condoms. Sexual IPV was associated with higher relative risk and controlling behaviour with lower relative risk of using all contraceptive methods. Conclusions IPV-exposed women were more likely to use long-acting methods that can be used covertly, are less susceptible to partner interference, and require fewer healthcare visits, which may reflect increased contraceptive vigilance. Understanding the impact of IPV on contraceptive methods is necessary to improve women's reproductive autonomy. Integrating IPV screening into family planning services and further research into contraceptive decision-making in abusive relationships is recommended.

items.title: 2026 THS guidelines for the management of hypertension in older adults: Developed by the task force on the management of hypertension of the Taiwan Hypertension Society (THS) and endorsed by the Taiwan Society of Cardiology (TSOC), Taiwan Association of Gerontology and Geriatrics (TAGG), and Taiwan Society of Family Medicine (TSFM).
items.abstract: The 2026 Taiwan Hypertension Society Guidelines for the Management of Hypertension in Older Adults provide an evidence-based framework tailored to the needs of an aging population. Recommendations were developed using PICO-formulated clinical questions, systematic evidence appraisal, and the GRADE approach, integrating evidence from randomized trials, observational studies, and expert consensus. A total of 63 actionable recommendations address diagnostic evaluation, blood pressure measurement and monitoring, lifestyle modification, blood pressure targets, and pharmacological therapy, with input from a multidisciplinary guideline panel and an external interdisciplinary expert committee. The guidelines emphasize age-related characteristics of hypertension, including arterial stiffness, salt sensitivity, frailty, orthostatic hypotension, cognitive vulnerability, atrial fibrillation, and multimorbidity. Standardized blood pressure measurement using validated oscillometric devices and regular out-of-office monitoring are strongly recommended. Blood pressure targets are specified according to age groups and common comorbid conditions. Non-pharmacological interventions, particularly dietary sodium reduction, potassium-enriched salt substitutes, healthy dietary patterns, and physical activity, are encouraged. Pharmacological treatment prioritizes individualized therapy and avoidance of overtreatment, especially in frail older adults. Endorsed by relevant national societies, these guidelines offer a practical approach to improving hypertension management and cardiovascular outcomes in older adults.

items.title: Dioscin attenuates aniline-induced liver injury by targeting the ACOT2-mediated ROS-JAK2/STAT3-CLN5 axis and restoring mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation and lysosomal lipophagy.
items.abstract: Chronic aniline exposure causes prominent hepatotoxicity accompanied by hepatic lipid metabolic disorders and cellular senescence, yet the molecular cascade underlying aniline-triggered liver injury remains unclear. Here, a 90-day chronic aniline intoxication mouse model and an AML12 murine hepatocyte model were established to systematically dissect toxic mechanisms and identify candidate hepatoprotective agents. Adverse outcome pathway analysis revealed lipid metabolic disturbance and cellular senescence as core toxic events, with lipid metabolic disturbance acting as an upstream driver of aniline-induced hepatocyte senescence and injury. Integrated multi-omics analysis showed that acyl-CoA thioesterase 2 (ACOT2), a key rate-limiting enzyme in fatty acid β-oxidation, was markedly downregulated in aniline-damaged livers. Hepatic ACOT2 overexpression restored mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation capacity, alleviated lipid overload, excessive ROS accumulation and hepatic dysfunction, and reduced bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate (BMP) accumulation by suppressing neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis protein 5 (CLN5) expression. Mechanistically, ACOT2 deficiency caused ROS overproduction and activated JAK2/STAT3 signaling. Phosphorylated STAT3 translocated into the nucleus and directly bound the Cln5 promoter, enhancing its transcription. Elevated CLN5 disrupted lysosomal structural integrity and acidification, thereby blocking lipid degradation during lipophagy. Conversely, Cln5 silencing restored lysosomal homeostasis and autophagic flux and reduced hepatic lipid deposition. Virtual screening identified dioscin as a natural small molecule that directly interacts with ACOT2, as confirmed by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation and surface plasmon resonance assays. PPARα-dependent transcriptional regulation contributed to ACOT2 suppression across multiple liver injury models, whereas dioscin restored ACOT2-dependent fatty acid oxidation and conferred broad hepatoprotection against aniline-, CCl 4 -, and APAP-induced liver injury. Collectively, this study reveals, in male mice and murine hepatocyte models, a previously unreported ACOT2-regulated ROS-JAK2/STAT3-CLN5 axis linking impaired mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation, lysosomal dysfunction and defective lipid clearance during aniline hepatotoxicity. These findings further support dioscin as a promising hepatoprotective candidate drug that directly targets ACOT2.

items.title: Time-resolved profiling reveals nonlinear dose-time trajectories of gut microbiota in PM<sub>2.5</sub> and PFOS exposure models.
items.abstract: The gut microbiota is a dynamic ecological system, yet environmental microbiome studies often provide only limited temporal resolution. We characterized gut microbial responses across multiple exposure levels and sampling stages in two independent but complementary mouse models of PM 2.5 inhalation and perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) drinking-water exposure. Time-resolved 16S rRNA gene sequencing, ecological analyses, PICRUSt2-based functional inference, and generalized additive models (GAMs) were integrated to examine temporal succession and nonlinear dose-time relationships. Under unexposed conditions, temporal microbial succession was evident in both models, highlighting the importance of accounting for background community dynamics. Within the PM 2.5 model, community restructuring was most apparent during early-to-intermediate exposure stages, with prominent nonlinear trajectories in Lactobacillus, Prevotella, and the Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio. In the PFOS model, microbial restructuring extended across a longer observation period and involved taxa including Akkermansia, Allobaculum, and UBA7173. PICRUSt2 suggested temporal and dose-associated variation in predicted pathways related to nitrogen metabolism, carbohydrate utilization, and fermentation, although these functions were not directly measured. GAMs identified stage-specific nonlinear response windows in both models. These findings highlight the importance of jointly considering dose and time in environmental microbiome studies and demonstrate the value of time-resolved modeling for detecting microbial response patterns that may be missed by endpoint analyses.

items.title: Source Apportionment and Resistome Signatures of Community and Hospital Effluents in Urban Sewer Networks.
items.abstract: Antibiotic resistance surveillance has traditionally focused on clinical settings, potentially overlooking broader microbial reservoirs in the community. Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) provides a powerful tool for capturing these population-level signals. This study aimed to identify source-specific resistome characteristics and estimate the relative compositional contributions of hospital and residential wastewater to the downstream wastewater treatment plant (WWTP). By integrating droplet digital polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR) with metagenomic sequencing, spatiotemporal dynamics across an urban sewer network were characterized. Bacterial 16S rRNA gene concentrations did not differ significantly between hospital and residential wastewater. Under the specified flow scenarios, hospital wastewater represented a small fraction of the estimated total influent volume. Bayesian source tracking further indicated that residential sources collectively accounted for nearly 80% of the inferred source contribution to the influent antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) profile and 70.9% of the influent microbial community composition, whereas hospital wastewater accounted for only 5.5% of the inferred resistome contribution. These findings show that hospital wastewater contained clinically important resistance genes (e.g., blaKPC-2), whereas the sampled residential references accounted for the largest combined inferred contribution to the influent microbiome and resistome. Together, these results highlight the importance of incorporating community surveillance through wastewater-based approaches within the One Health framework.

items.title: Epidemiology of paediatric traumatology: history, evolution, and perspectives.
items.abstract: Paediatric traumatology sits at the crossroads of orthopaedics, paediatric surgery, and public health. This instructional lecture addresses four questions: what is the global epidemiological burden of acute paediatric trauma? What are the specific features and growing importance of sports-related injuries, both acute and chronic? What are the specificities of paediatric polytrauma assessment and care organisation? How have evolving surgical practises and prevention policies transformed patient outcomes? After a brief historical overview, the article presents global epidemiological data, details acute and overuse sports injuries as a major twenty-first-century challenge, analyses validated polytrauma assessment tools and discusses surgical management trends for long-bone fractures. Future perspectives emphasise multidisciplinary collaboration, SROS-based care pathways, harmonised EPOS training programmes and evidence-based reassessment of surgical thresholds.

items.title: The environmental pollutant benzo[k]fluoranthene alters CD4<sup>+</sup> T-cell subset distribution via AhR signaling.
items.abstract: We examined associations of 16 polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons with aryl hydrocarbon receptor expression in circulating CD4 + T cells. In healthy human controls, BkF showed the strongest association with AhR + CD4 + T cells (r = 0.342, 95% CI 0.130-0.523, P = 0.0021; BH-adjusted q = 0.033); in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus, it did not survive multiplicity correction. In PBMCs from three healthy donors cultured for five days with BkF (3 or 10µg/L) with or without the AhR antagonist CH223191, BkF increased Th2, Th17, cTfh, and Treg populations, decreased naïve CD4 + T cells, and raised the Th1/Th2 ratio, shifts attenuated by CH223191. These findings identify BkF as an immunomodulatory AhR ligand that reshapes CD4 + T-cell subset distribution.

items.title: Erianin Targets Glutathione Reductase to Trigger Immunogenic Cell Death and Sensitize Pancreatic Cancer to PD-1 Blockade.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) responds poorly to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB), largely because of its immunosuppressive and T-cell-excluded tumor microenvironment. While inducing immunogenic cell death (ICD) offers a promising strategy to enhance tumor immunogenicity, redox-targeted ICD inducers with defined molecular targets remain limited in PDAC. Here, a functional screen of natural compounds identified erianin as a potent ICD inducer in PDAC. Erianin triggered canonical ICD hallmarks, including cell-surface calreticulin exposure, extracellular release of HMGB1 and ATP, thereby promoting dendritic-cell maturation, antigen cross-presentation and CD8 + T-cell activation. Target-engagement assays together with genetic perturbation supported glutathione reductase (GSR) as a functionally important erianin target. Erianin decreased the GSH/GSSG ratio, accompanied by increased oxidative stress and preferential activation of the PERK-eIF2α-ATF4-CHOP branch of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress response. Mutational and rescue experiments identified residue ARG-233 as an important residue required for GSR-dependent protection against erianin-induced redox stress and ICD. In syngeneic PDAC models, erianin-treated tumor cells elicited protective antitumor immunity in a tumor-challenge setting, while a therapeutic regimen combining erianin with anti-PD-1 antibody suppressed tumor growth and was associated with increased dendritic-cell activation and enhanced cytotoxic CD8+ T-cell infiltration. These findings define a GSR-associated redox-immune axis that links glutathione metabolism to immunogenic ER stress and provide a rationale for combining erianin with PD-1 blockade in immunologically cold PDAC.

items.title: ERO1A promotes lung cancer progression via HIF1A/EGFR.
items.abstract: Globally, lung cancer has emerged as a formidable public health challenge and is the primary cause of cancer-related deaths. The role of ERO1A in lung adenocarcinoma has been rarely explored. Here, we identified significant overexpression of ERO1A in lung cancer tissues, which correlates with reduced patient survival rates. Silencing ERO1A notably suppressed cell proliferation, clonogenic formation, migration, and invasion in lung cancer cell lines. ERO1A inhibition impairs tumor growth in murine models. RNA sequencing and proteomics analyses following ERO1A knockdown revealed that ERO1A is involved in multiple oncogenic pathways, particularly EGFR and HIF1A. ERO1A modulates HIF1A/EGFR may through H₂O₂. The oncogenes MET, CCND1, and p21 may also be involved in the ERO1A regulation pathway. The upregulation of ERO1A may serve as a valuable diagnostic and prognostic biomarker in lung cancer. The ERO1A-HIF1A/EGFR axis may represent a potential therapeutic target.

items.title: Delayed Risk Perception and Imitative Behavior Drive Epidemic Oscillations and Multistability: A Mathematical Modeling Study.
items.abstract: This study develops a time-delay differential equation model that couples disease transmission with imitation dynamics. Perceived risk is linked to historical prevalence with a discrete time delay τ, to investigate how delay of risk perception shapes protective actions and epidemic evolution. The theoretical analysis reveals that in the absence of delay, the system converges to one of four equilibria. Once τ exceeds a critical threshold, a Hopf bifurcation induces periodic oscillations. Further increasing τ can lead to two distinct dynamical regimes: either bounded periodic solutions persist, or the system undergoes repeated stability switches, with equilibrium and periodic orbits alternating in stability. Under certain delays, multiple stable periodic solutions may coexist. Numerical simulations demonstrate that delay of risk perception critically determines the outbreak trajectory: with short delays, timely protective measures can mitigate epidemic size even under high transmission risk; with long delays, both infection levels and the proportion of individuals adopting protection exhibit persistent oscillations. Notably, in prolonged-delay scenarios, reducing the cost of protection may amplify epidemic fluctuations, causing a sharp rebound in prevalence after transient suppression. Thus, an effective public health strategy should simultaneously lower the cost of protection and shorten delays.

items.title: Compliance with retail public health policies: A systematic review and meta-analysis of tobacco retail studies in the United States.
items.abstract: Objective This review synthesized evidence from United States studies of retail tobacco policy compliance to characterize violation rates and associated factors. Methods We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and Cochrane in March 2025 (updated March 2026) for peer-reviewed English-language United States studies of tobacco retail compliance (data collected 2010-2026) reporting violation rates. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Two reviewers screened and extracted data independently; a third resolved disagreements. Multilevel meta-regression examined factors associated with retailer violation rates. Results Seventy-seven studies (122 policy evaluations) were included. The pooled violation rate was 20.0% (95%CI: 16.0, 25.0%) with extreme between-study heterogeneity (I 2 = 99.97%). Pooled rates were highest for signage (33.0%, 95%CI: 22.0, 44.0%) and age-related policies (24.0%, 95%CI: 21.0, 26.0%), and lowest for promotional restrictions (7.0%, 95%CI: 3.0, 11.0%). Signage policies were associated with higher rates (β = 0.12, 95%CI: 0.04, 0.20) and promotional policies with lower rates (β = -0.24, 95%CI: -0.33, -0.16) than age-related policies. Sixty-seven studies were high quality. Conclusions Reported retailer violation rates should be interpreted in the context of how and where compliance is measured, not as direct estimates of retailer behavior. Residual heterogeneity may reflect unmeasured study and contextual factors.

items.title: AIM2 as a therapeutic target in autoimmunity: balancing inflammasome inhibition with immune homeostasis.
items.abstract: Absent in melanoma 2 (AIM2) is a cytosolic pattern recognition receptor that functions as a critical sensor of double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) of microbial or host origin. Upon DNA recognition, AIM2 assembles into a multiprotein inflammasome complex that drives pyroptotic cell death and maturation of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18. Beyond its canonical role in host defense, aberrant AIM2 activation by self-DNA has been increasingly implicated in the pathogenesis of various inflammatory autoimmune diseases. This comprehensive review synthesizes current understanding of AIM2 biology. We examine the role of AIM2 in different immune cell populations, its effects on multiple downstream signaling pathways, and its complex association with autoimmune diseases such as psoriasis, rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and multiple sclerosis. Finally, we discussed therapeutic prospects and remaining challenges in targeting AIM2 for the treatment of autoimmunity.

items.title: Practical Prevention of Heart Failure Across Stages A and B: A Scientific Statement From the Japanese Heart Failure Society.
items.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a growing health problem in Japan, associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, recurrent hospitalization, impaired quality of life, and increasing healthcare costs. Early prevention before the onset of signs and symptoms has therefore become a major priority in cardiovascular medicine. This scientific statement from the Japanese Heart Failure Society provides practical prevention strategies for patients with HF Stage A and Stage B in Japan. Particular emphasis is placed on biomarker-guided screening using brain (B-type) natriuretic peptide (BNP) and N-terminal pro-BNP (NT-proBNP) to facilitate earlier detection of Stage B (pre-HF) and identification of patients at increased risk of progression to symptomatic HF. The statement summarizes evidence-based management of major cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic disorders associated with HF development, including hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, obesity, coronary artery disease, left ventricular dysfunction, valvular heart disease, and atrial fibrillation. It also addresses disease-specific approaches for optimizing blood pressure, glycemic control, renal protection, lipid management, and weight reduction. Preventive strategies include lifestyle modification, pharmacological therapy, serial reassessment of natriuretic peptide levels, and appropriate use of cardiovascular imaging and timely specialist referral. Because many patients at risk for HF are managed outside specialized cardiovascular centers, practical pathways for collaboration between cardiologists and non-cardiologist physicians are essential. The importance of timely referral, shared risk recognition, and multidisciplinary care is therefore emphasized. Implementation of clinically applicable prevention strategies may help reduce progression to symptomatic HF, facilitate earlier therapeutic intervention, and improve long-term cardiovascular outcomes.

items.title: Serum metabolic characteristics and potential biomarkers of first-episode schizophrenia: An exploratory machine learning-based metabolomics study.
items.abstract: Metabolomics studies in first-episode schizophrenia (FES) remain limited and heterogeneous. This study aimed to characterize the serum metabolomic profile of FES, identify metabolic biomarkers, and develop machine learning-based predictive models. In this exploratory study, serum metabolomic profiles were compared among healthy controls (HCs; n = 10), untreated FES patients (n = 10), and the same patients after second-generation antipsychotics (SGAs) treatment. Candidate biomarkers were evaluated using six machine learning algorithms. Bayesian network analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were further applied to explore the network relationships. Cross-dataset integrative analysis was additionally performed using an external public dataset comprising patients with schizophrenia (n = 30) and HCs (n = 30). Disease-associated candidate biomarkers included PG(16:0/18:1), PC(20:4/15:0), PC(22:5/15:0), PG(18:1/18:1), and PE(16:0/16:0), whereas treatment-associated biomarkers included PG(16:0/18:1), PC(20:4/15:0), PC(22:5/15:0), cholesterol sulfate, DG(20:4/22:4), and Phe-Thr-Asn-Lys. All selected candidate biomarkers achieved Area Under the Curve (AUC) values above 0.9, with performance varying across algorithms. In the Bayesian networks, disease served as a direct parent node of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score and all biomarkers, whereas treatment shared direct edges with the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) score and all biomarkers except cholesterol sulfate, which was indirectly connected via Phe-Thr-Asn-Lys. WGCNA identified metabolite modules significantly associated with disease status (r = -0.88, p < 0.01) and treatment (r = 0.75, p < 0.01). Cross-dataset analysis identified phenylpyruvic acid, SM(d18:1/22:1(13Z)), and 2-octenoylcarnitine as shared differential metabolites with modest-to-moderate discrimination. These exploratory findings reveal potential serum metabolic signatures of FES and provide a basis for the development of objective biomarkers for diagnosis and SGAs treatment monitoring, warranting validation in larger independent cohorts.

items.title: Developmental toxicity of curcumin-mediated silver nanoparticles in the freshwater snails Biomphalaria glabrata.
items.abstract: Curcumin-mediated silver nanoparticles (Curc-AgNPs) are promising biogenic nanomaterials in medical and environmental applications. However, their ecotoxicological impact to non-target aquatic species remains understood. This study assessed the toxicity of Curc-AgNPs in the neotropical freshwater snails Biomphalaria glabrata, considering multiple developmental and post-hatching endpoints, including embryonic mortality, hatching success, developmental progression, heart rate, embryonic cell viability, and mortality of newly hatched snails. Curc-AgNPs (14 ± 4 nm) were synthesized by reducing AgNO 3 with curcumin and characterized by multiples techniques. Curc-AgNPs induced mortality, hatching inhibition, developmental delay, decreased heart rate and cell viability in a time- and concentration-dependent pattern. The cumulative developmental toxicity was confirmed by declining 50% effective concentration (LC50) to embryos (20.96 mg L -1 at 24 h to 1.47 mg L -1 at 168 h) and newly hatched snails (53.7 mg L -1 at 24 h to 37.5 mg L -1 at 120 h). Curc-AgNPs almost completely inhibited snail hatching at concentrations ≥ 1.88 mg L -1 and delayed embryonic development, mainly at gastrula and trochophore stages. Sub-lethal effects were observed in terms of cardiac activity (heart rate reduced by ∼41% at 1.88 mg L -1 ) and reduced cell viability in embryos exposed to Curc-AgNPs at concentration ranging 0.18 to 0.75 mg L -1 . Also, Curc-AgNPs induced higher toxicity in embryos than in newly hatched B. glabrata, indicating that the early developmental stages of gastropod are more susceptible to the toxicity of Curc-AgNPs. Overall, Curc-AgNPs exhibited pronounced embryotoxicity and stage-dependent molluscicidal effects. Although toxic, these concentrations exceed predicted environmental levels, representing hazard, not environmental risk.

items.title: Climate-induced extreme heat associated with suicide risk mediated by poor sleep and emotional dysregulation: A nationally representative panel study from Bangladesh.
items.abstract: Climate change-induced heat exposure is an emerging public health concern with potential mental health consequences, including suicide risk. Yet, in climate-vulnerable low- and middle-income countries the association between heat exposure and suicide risk, and the mediating mechanisms underlying this connection, remain underexplored. Using a nationally representative two-round panel survey from Bangladesh (n=7,492), we empirically examined whether poor sleep quality and emotional dysregulation mediate the relationship between exposure to extreme heat and suicide risk. Risk was assessed using a validated suicide cognitions scale across two seasonal rounds surveying the same individuals. Exposure to days ≥28°C over a two-week period was the lowest temperature threshold significantly associated with elevated suicide risk, with the highest risk detected at ≥35°C. At this 35°C threshold, 29.5% of the total association was mediated through poor sleep quality and 1.8% through emotional dysregulation. Risk was notably higher during the summer, and among less educated and poorer populations. This study provides novel evidence from a climate-vulnerable country on psychosocial mechanisms connecting heat and suicidality. As heat extremes intensify across the Global South, targeted mental health interventions, both infrastructural and psychological, may need consideration in climate adaptation strategies to protect the well-being of at-risk populations.

items.title: Cascade liposomal delivery for glioblastoma through multi-stage biological checkpoints.
items.abstract: Although receptor-targeted liposomes provide promising opportunities for glioblastoma therapy, their clinical translation remains limited by sequential biological barriers encountered after systemic administration. Here, we establish a multi-stage checkpoint framework linking carrier properties with stage-specific transport constraints, including systemic clearance, BBB/BTB heterogeneity, extracellular matrix resistance, and myeloid sequestration. We analyze receptor-mediated transcytosis through a mechanistic triad of ligand engagement, intracellular sorting, and abluminal release, highlighting the binding-site barrier and affinity paradox that restrict effective parenchymal delivery. Successful transcytosis represents only the initial step and we further develop a cascade targeting framework integrating tissue penetration, tumor cell recognition, and intracellular payload availability. Key translational challenges, including tumor microenvironment modulation, Quality by Design (QbD) manufacturing, safety, and companion diagnostics, are critically examined. Future progress will depend on evaluating liposomal platforms according to productive cellular exposure, with bulk accumulation serving only as a supporting measure, and on using quantitative transport profiling and imaging-guided stratification to identify patients whose biological barriers are compatible with specific liposomal designs.

items.title: Beyond treatment selection: Interim hypothesis addition and deletion in confirmatory seamless designs.
items.abstract: Inferentially seamless Phase 2/3 designs can accelerate drug development by combining learning and confirmatory objectives within a single protocol while preserving strict Type I control. Standard multiplicity frameworks for such trials typically assume that the complete set of efficacy hypotheses is fixed at trial initiation. In practice, however, emerging internal or external evidence can motivate the introduction of new confirmatory hypotheses at an interim analysis (IA), for example by adding a new dose that was not initially planned for confirmatory testing. This creates a tension between operational flexibility and rigorous Type I error control, a statistical and regulatory requirement. We extend the conditional error rate (CER) framework to permit hypothesis addition and deletion at an IA while maintaining strong familywise error rate (FWER) control under a closed testing principle. We also derive the conditional covariance structures and reference distributions needed when intersection hypotheses involve a newly introduced component. We compare our CER procedure to (i) an inverse-normal stagewise p-value combination approach and (ii) a straightforward split-α comparator that allocates separate one-sided error to "old" versus newly introduced hypotheses. We evaluate operating characteristics in a two-stage seamless setting with interim best-dose selection and an added dose at the IA. Simulations under the global null and under partial-null configurations support the strong FWER control of the implementation, while sensitivity analyses examine misspecification of the working reference distribution. Across alternative scenarios, the CER procedure can provide meaningful power gains, especially when the newly introduced dose is promising.

items.title: Clinical Outcomes of Long-Acting Lipoglycopeptides in Osteoarticular Infections: A Multidisciplinary Approach Integrating Therapeutic Drug Monitoring and Serum Bactericidal Titre During Dalbavancin Therapy.
items.abstract: Background Osteoarticular infections (OAIs) require multidisciplinary management and prolonged antibiotic therapy. Long-acting (LA) antibiotics may simplify care and enable early discharge, but their use in OAIs remains off-label and data on prolonged regimens are scarce. We evaluated the clinical effectiveness of LA antibiotics and explored the role of therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) and serum bactericidal titres (SBT) as complementary tools to support individualized treatment. Methods Prospective, single-centre observational study including adult patients with OAIs treated with dalbavancin (DAL) or oritavancin (ORI), with a predefined multi-dose regimen, between November 2023-April 2024. TDM and SBT assessments were performed exclusively in dalbavancin-treated patients at predefined time points, and concordance between the two approaches was evaluated. Results Twenty-seven patients were included (median age 62 years; 81.5% male): 22 (81.5%) received DAL and 5 (18.5%) ORI. Fracture-related infections (44.4%) and vertebral osteomyelitis (33.3%) were most frequent. Staphylococci were the predominant pathogens. Clinical cure was achieved in 21/27 patients (77.7%). DAL concentrations generally exceeded PK/PD efficacy thresholds, although greater interindividual variability was observed at later time points. SBT consistently indicated bactericidal activity. Concordance between TDM and SBT was high across time points (78.9-94.7%), particularly in S. aureus infections. Conclusions LA antibiotics facilitate the management of OAIs, allowing early discharge and outpatient treatment. TDM demonstrated that DAL concentrations remained adequate during prolonged regimens, while SBT showed high concordance with TDM and provided complementary functional information. These exploratory findings suggest that combined TDM and SBT may support individualized treatment strategies, warranting confirmation in larger prospective studies.

items.title: Antidepressant use in invasively ventilated patients in intensive care: Frequency of withholding and association with delirium-An observational study.
items.abstract: Objectives The aim of this study was to explore antidepressant use in invasively ventilated patients in intensive care who were able to be given medicines enterally (i.e. via feeding tube). As a secondary observation, we examined whether withholding an antidepressant was associated with positive Confusion Assessment Method - Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) scores. Methods A 12-month (1st Jan 2020 to 31st Dec 2020) retrospective cohort study was conducted in the ICU of a 484-bed tertiary referral hospital. Invasively ventilated patients capable of receiving enteral medicines were included. Results Of invasively ventilated ICU patients prescribed antidepressants prior to admission, 93% had their antidepressants withheld (for part, or all) of their ICU stay and antidepressant withholding was associated with higher odds of a positive CAM-ICU score. Invasively ventilated patients who had an antidepressant withheld were over five times more likely to have had a positive CAM-ICU score during their ICU stay. Availability of a buccal dosage form or a dosage form that could be given enterally did not impact prescribing or administration of pre-existing antidepressants or facilitate swapping to an alternative antidepressant. Conclusions Antidepressant withholding is frequent in invasively ventilated patients in intensive care who were able to be given medicines enterally. An association was identified between antidepressant withholding and positive CAM-ICU scores, warranting further investigation. Given the observed association between antidepressant withholding and positive CAM-ICU scores, review of antidepressants management may be reasonable when managing invasively ventilated patients with positive CAM-ICU scores.

items.title: Risk factors associated with increased mortality in patients with supracondylar amputation secondary to diabetic foot.
items.abstract: Introduction Diabetes is a public health problem that has been increasing in recent years. Infected diabetic foot is established by the presence of inflammatory response data associated with ulcers or tissue loss. Multiple risk factors are associated with diabetic foot and the need for amputation secondary to infection. Patients and methods Retrospective observational cohort study conducted between 2019 and 2024. A total of 403 patients with supracondylar amputation secondary to soft tissue infection due to diabetic foot were included. Demographic, clinical, and biochemical variables were analyzed between deceased and surviving patients. Results A total of 403 patients were included (median age: 58 years, IQR: 50-67; 72.7% male). Overall, in-hospital mortality was 13.4% (54/403), primarily driven by septic shock (44.4%) and decompensated chronic kidney disease (33.3%). Surgical reintervention was required in 11.1% of cases. In multivariable analysis, age (OR=1.06), pre-existing cardiac disease (OR=7.17), bilateral amputation (OR=4.36), Clavien-Dindo complication grade (OR=2.67), and surgical reintervention (OR=6.46) were independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality. Baseline serum albumin exerted a protective effect (OR=0.20). Conclusions In-hospital mortality following supracondylar amputation for diabetic foot is independently associated with acute septic burden, admission hypoalbuminemia, cardiorenal comorbidity, and surgical reintervention, rather than long-term glycemic control. Early identification of this high-risk profile at admission is critical to prioritize prompt infection control and perioperative optimization.

items.title: ART-TMJ: Arthroscopic real-time classification system for temporomandibular joint disorders.
items.abstract: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) Level II arthroscopy offers unparalleled diagnostic and therapeutic capabilities by enabling direct visualization and manipulation of the articular disc and intra-articular structures. This prospective study introduces a novel, evidence-based classification system that integrates clinical findings, radiological imaging, and arthroscopic assessment to improve diagnostic precision and guide personalized treatment planning. A cohort of 160 patients (295 joints) underwent standardized clinical evaluation, MRI, and Level II and III arthroscopy between 2019 and 2024. Patients were stratified into five stages, reflecting combined clinical, imaging, and arthroscopic findings. The cohort was predominantly female (84.6%) with a mean age of 41 years, and 83.8% had bilateral involvement. Arthroscopic findings frequently revealed more advanced joint pathology than clinical and radiological assessments alone (p = 0.005), underscoring the added diagnostic value of direct joint inspection. Patients' outcomes support the treatment algorithm. This integrated classification system bridges existing gaps in TMJ disorder staging by encompassing anatomical, functional, and pathological parameters, thereby facilitating tailored stage-specific interventions ranging from conservative management to advanced arthroscopic procedures and joint reconstruction. By enhancing diagnostic accuracy and treatment alignment, this system serves as a practical tool to optimize outcomes and improve communication among TMJ surgeons in minimally invasive joint surgery.

items.title: Hospital-based surveillance of vaccine-preventable diseases in children: a retrospective study in a Dutch tertiary hospital (2024-2025).
items.abstract: Background Vaccine-preventable diseases (VPDs) are a major cause of morbidity in children, despite established immunization programs. Surveillance of VPDs is essential to inform public health strategies and strengthen national immunization programs. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility of using routinely collected hospital data for in-hospital surveillance of pediatric VPDs. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study at a tertiary hospital in the Netherlands from July 2024 to June 2025, before national implementation of RSV immunization. Children Results We included 99 children (103 VPD episodes; median age 0.6 years), of whom 60% (n = 59) required pediatric intensive care. Most hospitalizations were caused by respiratory infections, particularly RSV (n = 52) and influenza (n = 27). Case ascertainment required integration of multiple data sources, as 45% of children were tested outside the study hospital. Clinical variables were largely complete and vaccination status could be determined for 84% of episodes. Overall, 9% (n = 9) of VPD episodes occurred in fully vaccinated children. Most VPD episodes (76%; n = 78) occurred in children not vaccinated against the specific pathogen, mainly because they were too young or because the pathogen or serotype was not covered by the national immunization program or current guidelines. Conclusions Retrospective hospital-based surveillance of pediatric VPDs is feasible and provides key information to guide efforts to optimize the national immunization program. By capturing disease severity and vaccine preventability, it complements existing surveillance data in the Netherlands.

items.title: Engineering Upd-like to broadly restrict arbovirus infection and vector competence in mosquitoes
items.abstract: The global expansion of mosquito-borne viruses poses a growing threat to public health, yet the endogenous signals that activate antiviral immunity in mosquito vectors remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify Aedes aegypti Upd as an activator of JAK/STAT signaling that restricts arbovirus infection. Loss of Upd increased infection and dissemination of the flaviviruses ZIKV and DENV, as well as the alphavirus SINV, whereas blood meal inducible midgut overexpression reduced ZIKV and SINV infection. Mechanistically, Upd associated with the extracellular region of the Domeless (Dome) receptor, and Upd deficiency markedly reduced STAT phosphorylation and nuclear accumulation in the midgut. Upd expression was transiently induced in the midgut by an uninfected blood meal but remained elevated following ZIKV challenge, linking physiological responses to blood feeding with antiviral defense. In mammal mosquito transmission models, Upd overexpression reduced viral acquisition from infected hosts, whereas Upd deficiency enhanced viral dissemination and increased transmission following systemic infection. Together, these findings identify Upd as an endogenous regulator of mosquito JAK/STAT signaling and provide proof of principle that temporally targeted Upd expression can reduce arbovirus susceptibility and vector competence.

items.title: Social Determinants of Health Screening Tools Used with Immigrant Populations: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Social determinants of health (SDOH) are increasingly recognized as major contributors to health outcomes. Beyond general social challenges, immigrants face additional barriers related to language, immigration status, legal concerns, discrimination, and exclusionary policies. Despite growing interest in SDOH screening, little is known about how existing screening instruments address immigrant-specific factors. Searches of Web of Science, PubMed, CINAHL, and PsychINFO identified peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025. Eligible studies included original research articles focused on immigrant populations and the use of an SDOH screening tool. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts. Data were extracted on screening tool characteristics, SDOH domains assessed, immigrant-specific indicators, language availability, study setting, and tool validation status. The final search yielded 1,155 articles. Eight studies met full inclusion criteria, describing nine screening tools or variants, including adaptations of the Health Leads Social Needs Screening Toolkit, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Accountable Health Communities screening tool, and the Protocol for Responding to and Assessing Patients' Assets, Risks, and Experiences. Most studies occurred in urban primary care settings and primarily served Hispanic/Latinx immigrant populations. Core SDOH domains were well-represented across all tools. While all studies included at least one immigrant-specific measure, these were generally limited to language preference, nativity, legal concerns, and migrant worker status. No adapted or newly developed tool demonstrated formal psychometric validation. Current SDOH screening tools may fail to capture the broader structural factors that shape immigrant health, including immigration-related policies, legal precarity, discrimination, and fear. Significant gaps remain in culturally responsive, psychometrically validated instruments developed with and for immigrant communities.

items.title: Large-scale semantic indexing of Spanish biomedical literature using contrastive transfer learning.
items.abstract: Motivation The exponential growth of biomedical literature has made automatic indexing essential for advancing biomedical research. While automatic indexing has made strides in English biomedical literature, there has been limited research on non-English biomedical texts due to insufficient high-quality training data. Results We propose BERTDeCS, a novel deep learning framework for automatically indexing Spanish biomedical literature using contrastive transfer learning. BERTDeCS utilizes a multilingual BERT (M-BERT) to generate multi-language representations and adapts M-BERT for Spanish biomedical literature domain through contrastive learning. Additionally, BERTDeCS enhances its semantic indexing capabilities on Spanish biomedical literature by leveraging enriched English annotated literature in MEDLINE through transfer learning. Experimental results on Spanish datasets demonstrate that BERTDeCS outperforms state-of-the-art indexing methods, achieving top performance in the MESINESP and MESINESP2 Tasks on medical semantic indexing in Spanish within the BioASQ challenge. Additional experiments on Portuguese provide preliminary evidence that BERTDeCS can transfer to a closely related language sharing substantial lexical and biomedical terminology with Spanish. Availability The source code is available at https://github.com/yourh/BERTDeCS and at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23212468.

items.title: Remote sensing and the EU nature restoration Regulation: monitoring biodiversity indicators for integrated forest management
items.abstract: Implementing the EU Nature Restoration Regulation (EU NRR) requires Member States to monitor multiple indicators of forest biodiversity, yet the role of remote sensing (RS) in this process remains unclear. This review synthesises current evidence on the use of RS for monitoring forest biodiversity indicators defined in the NRR and identifies methodological gaps and operational priorities. Following a systematic review of 222 studies, we evaluate the suitability of different platforms, sensors, and scales of observation. Our results show that RS capabilities are strongly indicator and scale dependent, with no single approach suitable across all indicators. Airborne laser scanning is most effective for capturing forest structural attributes, including uneven-aged forest structure, while satellite multispectral imagery provides consistent, large-scale monitoring of forest connectivity. Tree species composition and diversity can be assessed using multi-sensor approaches, though accuracy declines in mixed and structurally complex forests. In contrast, the common forest bird index cannot currently be monitored using remote sensing, and deadwood indicators are limited by the resolution required for national monitoring. Key challenges include limited availability of repeated high-resolution data, difficulties in detecting high-resolution features, and reduced classification accuracy in complex forest systems. Overall, RS has strong potential to support monitoring when integrated with National Forest Inventories and multi-sensor data streams. Advancing towards operational implementation of RS within the NRR will require harmonised products, improved methods for complex forest conditions, and greater emphasis on temporal monitoring.

items.title: Human–wildlife conflict and farmland transfer under informal land institutions: Evidence from rural China
items.abstract: Abstract Human–wildlife conflict (HWC) affects not only agricultural production but also how farming households adjust access to and use of land. Existing research has focused largely on welfare losses and land‐use responses, while little is known about whether ecological risk is associated with the governance arrangements through which farmland is transferred Drawing on risk and uncertainty theory, we examine the relationship between HWC and informal farmland transfer (IFT) using survey data from 921 land‐transferring households drawn from 3213 surveyed households in Asian elephant range areas of Yunnan Province, China (2022–2024). We employ Probit, Heckman two‐step and IV‐Probit models for analysis. HWC is significantly associated with greater participation in IFT among land‐transferring households. Specifically, HWC increases both the probability and area of informal transfer‐out, but has no significant effect on informal transfer‐in. The effect is context‐dependent: Informal transfer‐out increases among households both near and far from nature reserves and is concentrated among small‐scale farmers, whereas reductions in informal transfer‐in are observed only in specific subgroups, namely households near reserves and households whose head is employed in the public sector. These findings suggest that ecological risk is associated with asymmetric land adjustment, primarily through informal transfer‐out, and that informal arrangements remain an important channel through which households reorganize land commitments under uncertainty. The study extends relational perspectives on HWC by showing that wildlife‐related risk is associated not only with individual land‐use responses but also with socially embedded forms of land reallocation. Policies in ecologically vulnerable regions should improve the flexibility and accessibility of formal land‐transfer institutions and strengthen coordination with wildlife damage compensation and agricultural insurance to support more secure and adaptive land adjustment. items.title: Comparing Population Census Methods for Howler Monkeys ( Alouatta palliata ) in a Fragmented Rainforest
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Accurate population density estimates are important for guiding conservation management practices for threatened animal species. Aims This study tests the efficacy of population census methods at a long‐term study site for the mantled howler monkey ( Alouatta palliatta ), La Suerte Biological Research Station (LSBRS) in Costa Rica. This monkey is a group‐living Neotropical primate with long distance vocalizations that is declining throughout its range. Methods We compared the visual count and long calling acoustic triangulation census methods to determine population count and number of social groups. Results We found 14 monkey groups according to both population census methods, indicating the accuracy of the acoustic triangulation method at determining group number. Visual count data showed that the 1.36‐km 2 study area within a 3‐km 2 forest fragment had a population density of 125.7 individuals/km 2 , one of the highest population densities ever recorded for this species, although mean group size of 11.6 (±4.7 SD) monkeys/group at LSBRS remained within the 10–15 monkeys/group range found at other sites. Discussion The observed mean group size at LSBRS fell within the commonly reported range for the species, suggesting that the acoustic triangulation method alone may provide a reasonably accurate estimate of population density for sites with average monkey group sizes and/or where mean group sizes have previously been quantified using visual count surveys. Recommendations We recommend collecting both types of census data where possible, while suggesting that acoustic triangulation censuses can be used on their own when financial resources are limited. Visual counts are necessary to confirm group number and size, and to enable detailed demographic studies.

items.title: Coastal Climate Change Adaptation: A Review of Engineering, Nature-Based, Governance, and Socio-Economic Adaptation Strategies
items.abstract: Adaptation is becoming a key part of climate policies, including the Paris Agreement, for coastal areas, which host a large proportion of the world's population. Coastal areas are prone to intensive urbanization and tourism, which can exacerbate the threats of sea-level rise, storm intensification, erosion, and saltwater intrusion. Existing reviews have examined engineering, ecological, governance, and socio-economic aspects of coastal system adaptation to climate change, but these studies have generally been limited to a single discipline and offer limited cross-domain information. Such fragmentation can limit their applicability to planners who are interested in context-specific, integrated solutions. This review offers a critical synthesis of engineering, nature based, governance, and socio-economic adaptation approaches used in coastal areas worldwide. The synthesis suggests that no single adaptation pathway performs uniformly well across settings. Rather, the effectiveness of the strategies depends on asset density, ecological and sediment conditions, governance capacity, and the urgency of the hazard. Hard engineering solutions provide a stable short-term solution in urban environments, but they externalize erosion costs and interfere with natural sediment transport. Nature-based solutions provide greater ecosystem and long-term co-benefits but require specific physical conditions to be achieved, which diminishes their transferability. While governance instruments and socio-economic measures help ensure effective, equitable, and sustainable outcomes, they do not directly provide measurable reductions in risk. The review compares the domains to identify points of overlap, interdependencies between strategies, and implementation challenges unique to each domain, and highlights the lack of standardized evidence across domains as an area for future research. This study focuses on integrated, context-adapted solutions that account for physical, ecological, and institutional dimensions to support sustainable and climate-resilient coastal development amid rapid environmental change.

items.title: The promises and perils of satellite Earth observation for just transformations in sustainability
items.abstract: Satellite Earth observation (EO) is considered an essential tool for the ‘Decade of Action’ towards the Sustainable Development Goals. While advocates claim that innovation in satellite EO will bring widespread environmental and societal benefits, satellite EO also raises significant epistemological and ethical challenges. This review examines the use of satellite EO for sustainable development, focusing on use cases related to renewable energy projects, smallholder agriculture programmes, disaster recovery, carbon accounting, water and ocean governance, and environmental activism. We explore the politics behind data capture, access, and use, recognising that satellite EO has ‘world-making’ effects. We find that satellite EO applications can generate unequal material impacts for people and the planet, while consolidating state or private control over natural resources. Yet, we also discuss how EO data can be collected and applied in locally led participatory ways to advocate for sustainability. Critical and reflexive dialogue is therefore needed to support policymakers, practitioners, and communities to realise the potential of satellite EO for just transformations in sustainability.
