items.title: Fear-Specific Technophobia as a Mediator Between Daily Technical Support and Instrumental Versus Hedonic Technology Use in Later Life: Cross-Sectional Survey Study.
items.abstract: Background Population aging and rapid digitalization have intensified concerns about older adults' digital participation. Although access disparities have narrowed, older adults continue to differ from younger groups in how they use digital technologies, with their use skewed toward instrumental rather than hedonic purposes. Technophobia is a salient psychological barrier; yet, its distinct fear dimensions and their links to different forms of technology use remain insufficiently differentiated. Daily technical support (DTS) may provide an important sociotechnical context for understanding these relationships. Objective This study aimed to test how DTS promotes older adults' instrumental and hedonic technology use by reducing multidimensional technophobia (fear of inconvenience, fear of personal failure, and human-machine ambiguity) and whether these mechanisms differ by gender. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among Chinese adults aged ≥55 years recruited via online platforms and offline communities in Nanjing (June-October 2024). A total of 212 valid responses were included (mean age 66.96, SD 6.96, range 55-86 years; 142/212, 68.4% women). Measures assessed day-to-day technical support, 3 dimensions of technophobia, instrumental versus hedonic technology use, and demographic variables. We used partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 5000 bootstrap resamples to test direct, indirect, and moderated mediation effects, reporting 95% bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) CI. Results DTS significantly reduced fear of inconvenience (β=-0.455, 95% BCa CI -0.632 to -0.229; P P =.12) or human-machine ambiguity ( P =.26). Fear of inconvenience and human-machine ambiguity negatively predicted instrumental use (IU; β=-0.215, 95% BCa CI -0.410 to -0.009; P =.05 and β=-0.211, 95% BCa CI -0.389 to -0.001; P =.04). DTS had a positive direct effect on IU (β=0.104, 95% BCa CI 0.009 to 0.203; P =.04) but not on hedonic use (HU; β=0.075; P =.11). The indirect effect of DTS on IU through fear of inconvenience was significant (β=0.097, 95% BCa CI 0.020-0.204). Gender moderated the effect of DTS on fear of inconvenience (β=0.287, 95% BCa CI 0.052-0.518; P =.02), and such conditional indirect effect was significant for men (β=0.098, 95% BCa CI 0.001-0.219) but not for women (β=0.036, 95% BCa CI -0.002 to 0.116). Conclusions DTS was associated with greater instrumental technology use among older adults through lower fear of inconvenience, with a stronger indirect association among men, whereas no comparable pathway emerged for HU. This suggests that gender may shape how older adults benefit psychologically from technical support rather than reflect general differences in support needs. Interventions should move beyond one-size-fits-all approaches by providing targeted, task-oriented support that addresses older adults' specific technological fears and practical barriers.

items.title: Restoring Landscapes: A Structured Dataset of Forest Restoration Projects and Initiatives in Spain
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This dataset provides the first centralized compilation of forest restoration and adaptation projects in Spain, developed within the REFORADAPT project supported by the Biodiversity Foundation of the Spanish Ministry for Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge. The initiative responds to the growing policy momentum around ecosystem restoration and the need for structured, harmonized information to inform planning and decision‐making. Data were collected through a dual approach: a systematic review of European Union and national funding databases (including LIFE, INTERREG, and SUDOE) using forest restoration‐related keywords, complemented by contributions from expert networks and partner organizations. This allowed the identification of both large‐scale projects and small‐scale, community‐led initiatives often absent from official sources. Projects were screened based on titles and abstracts, and relevant metadata were standardized using an Excel template with custom variables on restoration types, goals, and degradation causes. The resulting dataset includes 382 initiatives implemented fully or partially in Spain. Ecological restoration aimed at conserving species and habitats is the most frequently assigned restoration type, representing 18% of all classified entries. In parallel, biodiversity conservation is the most frequently identified goal, occurring in 60% of the projects. Wildfires are the most frequently addressed degradation driver, accounting for 25% of all recorded occurrences. The EU LIFE programme is the most common funding source, present in 28% of the projects. This structured and comprehensive resource offers insights into the diversity, scope, and distribution of restoration efforts across Spain. It provides a valuable foundation for comparative analysis, stakeholder collaboration, and evidence‐based policies to advance forest ecosystem restoration and climate adaptation. The Metadata for this abstract is available in MetaCat in JaLTER at https://doi.org/10.20783/DIAS.JLE.100 , and the complete dataset is available at https://doi.org/10.34810/data2194 .

items.title: Coupled responses of aboveground and belowground net primary productivity stability to nitrogen deposition in grasslands
items.abstract: Abstract The temporal stability of plant net primary productivity (NPP), defined as the ratio of temporal mean productivity to its standard deviation, is crucial for sustaining ecosystem services. Yet, little is known about whether the effects of nitrogen deposition on aboveground NPP (ANPP) stability are coupled with corresponding changes in belowground systems. Here we conducted a global meta-analysis based on 542 multi-year observations from 111 studies to assess the impacts of nitrogen deposition on the stability of ANPP and belowground NPP (BNPP). Nitrogen addition significantly decreased the stability of both ANPP and BNPP in a synchronized manner, reflecting a coupled response resulting from the allocation trade-off between mean ANPP and BNPP and their synchronized increase in variability. Further analysis showed that the declines in both ANPP and BNPP stability were associated with decreased plant species richness under nitrogen addition. Moreover, the negative responses intensified with longer treatment durations and higher nitrogen addition intensity. These findings highlight the importance of considering above- and below-ground interactions in future ecosystem management strategies under global change scenarios.

items.title: Phylogeny of Poaceae tribe Andropogoneae in Australia as a contribution to biological control research on gamba grass ( Andropogon gayanus )
items.abstract: Andropogon gayanus (gamba grass, Poaceae) is a large, tropical grass native to Africa, but introduced as a pasture plant across the tropics worldwide. It is considered invasive in northern Australia, and a research program into the potential of biological control of the species has recently been initiated. Because biological control agents are more likely to pose risks to non-target species closely related to the target weed than to distantly related species, risk management and experimental design in weed biological control require information on the evolutionary relationships of the target weed. Here, we inferred target sequence capture phylogenies of Poaceae tribe Andropogoneae with a focus on Australian lineages of the tribe, combining newly generated and previously published data. Our results place some lineages treated as incertae sedis in the most recent classification of Andropogoneae, including Australian endemics. Clausospicula extensa was retrieved as sister to Chrysopogon, and Spathia neurosa was nested in Dichanthium, but the position of Pseudopogonatherum was inconsistent across our analyses. Our analyses imply that subtribes Apludinae and Anthistiriinae as currently recognised may be non-monophyletic. Only 2 of 25 replicate specimen pairs of the same species failed to group together, confirming a high degree of reproducibility despite differences in bioinformatic approaches between our study and that used for previously published data. The revised phylogeny presented here supports the development of risk assessment plans for biological control and provides additional resources for broader Andropogoneae phylogeny.

items.title: From black plates to backyard animals: Chigger communities associated with wild and domestic hosts and the environment in a rural village setting
items.abstract: Chigger mites (larval Trombiculidae) are obligate ectoparasites, some species transmit Orientia tsutsugamushi , the causative agent of scrub typhus. Despite their public health significance in rural Southeast Asia, relationships between chiggers infesting wildlife, domestic animals and those present in the surrounding environment remain poorly characterised. We hypothesised that agricultural–forest ecotones would support higher chigger occurrence and that murid rodents would be the principal maintenance hosts of chigger communities. We conducted ecological observations of chigger communities associated with backyard chickens (n = 117), free-roaming dogs (n = 22), murid rodents (n = 96), insectivorous bats (n = 24) and environmental black-plate samples (n = 150) within a scrub typhus-endemic rural village in Nan Province, northern Thailand. Host-chigger associations were characterized using bipartite and unipartite network analyses. Twenty-one chigger species were identified, including four previously known to harbour O. tsutsugamushi: Ascoschoengastia indica, Leptotrombidium imphalum, Eutrombicula wichmanni and Walchia kritochaeta. Unfed questing chiggers occurred within the central residential area rather than being restricted to peripheral agricultural-forest interfaces as hypothesised. Murid rodents contributed the greatest chigger diversity, while backyard chickens exhibited unexpectedly high infestation prevalence (54.7%) and mean abundance. Environmental chigger detection rate was 11.3%. Eutrombicula wichmanni was recorded on free-roaming dogs, representing the first documented chigger infestation on dogs in Thailand, and a complete mitogenome was obtained from environmentally collected adults. Network analysis identified distinct rodent- and domestic animal-associated chigger communities, with the environmental chiggers linking both groups, whereas bat-associated chiggers were clearly isolated. These findings reveal complex chigger community structures with distinct ecological partitioning, highlighting the importance of domestic animals, particularly backyard chickens and free-roaming dogs (in addition to rodents) as critical components of peri-domestic transmission cycles. Future studies integrating host-chigger ecology with rickettsial pathogen screening would inform targeted disease surveillance and control programmes in rural endemic communities.

items.title: Biodiversity is a key motivation for European urban green space planning and management
items.abstract: Abstract Many urban green spaces are ecologically degraded. Yet, when designed and managed using ecologically motivated practices, green spaces can support biodiversity. However, many municipalities have not yet adopted strategies to enhance biodiversity. To better understand the importance assigned to biodiversity in public urban green spaces, we interviewed 574 municipalities across 18 European countries. Using a standardized questionnaire, we examined the underlying motivations, management goals and the measures municipalities used to support the public acceptance of biodiverse green spaces. Most municipalities (85%) reported biodiversity as a key motivation in green space planning and management. Many provided staff training (82%) and took action to increase public acceptance (75%) of biodiversity-promoting management. The reported perceptions of municipalities’ ecological condition were mostly positive, but 19% reported declines in the last decade. Differences between municipalities could be linked to regional and structural factors such as the sealed surface of the municipality, highlighting the need for locally adaptable policies for urban biodiversity.

items.title: Morphological variation of the conus arteriosus in Chondrichthyes: Implications for ecology and evolution
items.abstract: Cartilaginous fish have diverse morphological traits that are essential for understanding their evolutionary history and ecological adaptations. However, the conus arteriosus and its valves, key components of the heart and blood circulation, have been underexplored in phylogenetic and ecomorphological contexts. Here, we (1) characterize the morphological diversity and distribution of conal valves across Chondrichthyes, (2) evaluate the phylogenetic signal of valve characters and their potential usefulness for understanding evolutionary relationships, and (3) test whether variation in valve morphology is associated with lifestyle and locomotor demands. Our results show that the number of valves, as well as their distribution along the conus arteriosus, is generally consistent with the pattern observed in previous studies of two to seven rows of valves, with predominantly three series. Novel findings include a higher number of valve rows (up to six) than previously found in sharks and the first detailed descriptions for the orders Torpediniformes and Squatiniformes. Our results indicate that conal morphology is weakly correlated with phylogeny, but is strongly associated with locomotor demands and lifestyle.

items.title: Strengthening Institutional Governance to Counteract Urban-Driven Carbon Emissions in Central Europe: Insights from Economies in the Black Triangle Industrial Zone
items.abstract: Urban expansion and industrial concentration in Central Europe’s historic Black Triangle zone-encompassing Germany, Poland, and the Czech Republic-continue to drive elevated carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions, posing significant challenges to regional climate goals and the downstream ecological stability of the Baltic and North Sea basins. Rapid employment-based urban migration expands built environments, alters land-use patterns, and intensifies energy demand across industrial corridors. This research empirically examines the dynamic long-run impacts of institutional governance, urban migration, and fossil energy consumption on CO2 emissions in three economies across the Black Triangle Industrial zone of Central Europe over the period 1998:Q4 to 2021:Q4. Utilizing the Pooled Mean Group (PMG) estimator within a Panel Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) framework, the long-run empirical results reveal that: (i) strengthening institutional quality significantly abates CO2 emissions, whereas (ii) both fossil fuel consumption and urban migration exert a statistically significant positive effect on long-run carbon emissions. These insights underscore that robust institutional governance is essential to decoupling urban economic growth from environmental degradation. To achieve UN Agenda 2030 targets and mitigate transboundary environmental impacts-including marine resource degradation and eutrophication in connected Central and Northern European catchments-policy interventions must prioritize institutional capacity building, accelerated investments in renewable energy alternatives, and the deployment of smart, green technology-driven transport systems leveraging artificial intelligence and the Internet of Things (IoT).

items.title: Integrating Ecological Fiqh into Transformative Pesantren Education
items.abstract: Environmental crises challenge Islamic educational institutions to translate religious ethics into sustained ecological practice. This study examines how ecological fiqh operates as a pedagogical and institutional mechanism in pesantren education and identifies the conditions that shape its integration. A qualitative multiple-case design was used across ten pesantren in Sumatra and Java. The study analyzed evidence from semi-structured interviews, participatory observations, and curriculum and institutional documents thematically and compared it across cases. Five themes were identified: institutionalization of ecological responsibility, curriculum and pedagogy, internalization of ecological fiqh, institutional capacity and constraints, and resource stewardship. Integration was strongest where Islamic ecological reasoning was connected to experiential learning, repeated routines, student participation, leadership, and material support; where these conditions were weak, practices remained fragmented or extracurricular. Practically, the findings indicate that leaders and educators should align curriculum, teacher development, student responsibilities, and resource-management routines. The study's originality lies in proposing a provisional normative-pedagogical-institutional chain that explains how religious ethics can move from normative meaning to learning, habitual enactment, and environmental stewardship.

items.title: System noise temperature measurements of a 19-element phased array feed
items.abstract: Abstract We present multi-epoch system noise temperature measurements of a 19-element hexagonal room-temperature phased array feed (PAF) using a modified Y-factor method. A Python-based pipeline with iterative channel calibration and maxSNR beamforming is developed to do data reduction, and a covariance-based decomposition scheme is proposed to extract mutual coupling noise temperature \(T_\mathrm{mc}\). Long-term observations from March to June 2026 capture temporal receiver noise drift \textbf{mainly} induced by LNA temperature variations. Within the 1.37–1.47 GHz operating band, the measured beam-equivalent system noise temperature of the PAF is $\sim$73–89 K. \textbf{ The measured \(T_\mathrm{mc}\) baseline ranges from $\sim$2 K to $\sim$8 K, while under thermal loading, the resonant peak of \(T_\mathrm{mc}\) can increase to more than 20 K. The baseline of \(T_\mathrm{mc}\) is consistent with the S-parameter measurements, which show the \(T_{\rm mc}\) of the full array ranges less than 10.7 K. } \textbf{ The baseline fluctuation of \(T_\mathrm{mc}\) most likely arises from the superposition of thermal and non-thermal components of the spatial electromagnetic fields. } A detachable stainless steel shield is deployed to quantify sidelobe spillover noise, and comparative tests show unshielded environmental interference increases receiver noise temperature by over 60 K. The proposed measurements and data processing framework provides a practical reference for noise performance characterization of ground-based radio telescope PAF prototypes.

items.title: A review of error analysis and compensation methods in white-light interferometric surface topography measurement
items.abstract: Surface topography directly affects the functionality and performance of workpieces, while its high-accuracy and repeatable measurement is essential for quality control and precision manufacturing. White-light interferometry, benefiting from the unique advantages of broadband low-coherence light sources, enables high-accuracy measurement while effectively avoiding phase ambiguity and related issues, and therefore plays an important role in surface metrology. However, various error sources in practical measurements can cause deviations from ideal measurement conditions, directly affecting the accuracy and reliability of surface topography reconstruction. Therefore, an in-depth investigation of error mechanisms and the development of effective compensation strategies are essential for ensuring the measurement reliability of white-light interferometry and promoting its application in broader engineering scenarios. This review systematically examines error processing in white-light interferometry. The fundamental principles of white-light interferometry are first described based on an interferometric signal model. The potential error sources and their physical mechanisms are then analyzed in detail, covering environmental vibration, sample characteristics, the batwing effect, and algorithmic errors. Research progress over the past two decades in suppressing these errors is systematically classified and summarized. Based on these developments, future trends in white-light interferometry are further discussed. This review aims to provide a systematic theoretical reference and technical guidance for error analysis and performance improvement in white-light interferometry.

items.title: Non-Axisymmetric Pillar Structures due to Embedded Stars in AGN Accretion Discs
items.abstract: Abstract Gravitationally unstable outer regions of AGN discs may host in situ formation of massive stars whose heating produces localized vertical “pillars” on the disc surface, in the same region that emits the broad lines. Here we investigate the reverberation-mapping signatures that such pillars would produce. We compute velocity–delay maps Ψ(λ, τ), time-evolving emission-line spectra, and continuum reverberation lag spectra for these structures. We model each pillar as a 2D Gaussian perturbation to the disc height under lamp-post irradiation and weight the line response with Cloudy photoionization grids covering the major BLR lines. We show Hα, Mg ii, and C iv as representative examples. A single pillar produces a localized hotspot in Ψ and a clear “S-wave” pattern in the time-evolving spectrum that persists, though diluted, for N ∼ 100 pillars. Emission-line fluxes are suppressed in shadows behind the pillars, but when normalized by Hβ (or by the local continuum) the line-to-Hβ ratios move in opposite directions: Mg ii/Hβ rises while C iv/Hβ drops. This contrast distinguishes pillars from purely kinematic features that would modulate all lines by similar factors. Across scans of the pillar shape and lamp-post height, the pillar models produce an optical continuum reverberation lag spectrum of the observed magnitude. The once-per-orbit modulation grows with sin i from foreshortening, and at sufficiently high inclination the pillar’s body geometrically self-occults its lamp-facing inner slope, adding a sharper near/far contrast. These signatures provide observational diagnostics for detecting in situ star formation in AGN discs through velocity-resolved reverberation mapping campaigns.

items.title: Composition-controlled cutoff-resonance coupling and polarization-selective wave propagation in a four-component magnetized plasma
items.abstract: Abstract This study deals with the propagation of circularly polarized electromagnetic waves in magnetized multicomponent plasmas composed of electrons, deuterium positive ions (D+), hydrogen negative ions (H−), and oxygen negative ions (O−). Based on the cold-fluid approach combined with Maxwell’s equations, the dielectric functions of right-hand circularly polarized (RCP) and left-hand circularly polarized (LCP) waves are obtained analytically. The numerical values of the cutoff frequencies, the reflection, transmission, and absorption coefficients for a finite multicomponent plasma slab are found using electromagnetic boundary conditions. Due to the presence of two kinds of negative ions, three cutoff frequencies of the RCP waves and the propagation and stop bands related to the negative-ion and electron cyclotron resonances are found. In turn, the LCP wave has only one cutoff-controlled propagation boundary. The effects of negative-ion concentrations of hydrogen and oxygen, magnetic field strength, slab thickness, and frequency are studied. Increase in the concentration of the H− ions leads to a shift in cutoff frequencies, changes in the widths of propagation and stop bands, decrease in the gap between the RCP and LCP cutoffs, and improvement of the low-frequency transparency when both RCP and LCP modes are propagating. A remarkable effect is a tendency of the second RCP cutoff towards the H− cyclotron resonance that results in the cutoff-resonance coincidence with an enhancement in absorption of the light negative ions. The cutoff-resonance proximity produces enhanced electromagnetic absorption associated with the resonant response of the light negative-ion population, indicating enhanced wave-ion coupling. The results provide a fluid-level basis for controlling frequency-selective electromagnetic energy deposition in multicomponent plasmas and show how negative-ion composition can tune polarization-dependent propagation and electromagnetic power deposition in the present model. It can be used in plasma diagnostics, ionospheric wave propagation, plasma electromagnetic filters, tunable polarization devices, and ion-selective heating.

items.title: Exploring the potential of Low Gain Avalanche Detectors for low-energy ion spectrometry
items.abstract: Low Gain Avalanche Detectors (LGADs) have emerged as key sensors for High Energy Physics and related applications due to their excellent time resolution and enhanced signal-to-noise ratio. However, their use in low-energy ion spectrometry has generally been limited by gain suppression effects, arising from the high ionization densities produced by such ions within the multiplication layer, which leads to a reduction of the gain and a non-linear detector response with ion energy. In this work, we investigate an alternative detection configuration aimed at mitigating this effect by shifting the region of highest ionization density away from the gain layer. Alpha spectrometry measurements in the energy range 3-9 MeV were performed by irradiating the detector from both the frontside (multiplication layer side) and the backside of the devices. Additionally, potential gain suppression effects when the detected particles are photons were evaluated using an X-ray tube operated at 40 kV, with irradiation from both the front and back sides. The results show that backside irradiation leads to a higher and more uniform gain and a linear relationship between generated charge and alpha particle energy. In particular, a gain of 3-4 is obtained for backside irradiation, while a nearly constant gain of ≈ 2 is achieved for frontside irradiation. In addition, the achieved energy resolution (1%–2%) is comparable to that of standard PiN detectors fabricated under the same conditions. Finally, the gain response to X-rays was found to be very similar to that observed for alpha particles, suggesting that no gain suppression is observed in the studied LGADs for backside irradiation. These findings demonstrate the potential of LGADs for low-energy ion spectrometry, particularly in applications where low deposited energy makes enhanced signal-to-noise ratio a critical advantage.

items.title: Magnetic Field and Electromotive Force of Faraday’s Unipolar Generator
items.abstract: The comparison between the theoretical and experimental results derived from the consideration of a Faraday’s homopolar generator experiment is the topic developed in this work. The theoretical results are based on measurements of the magnetic field and on high-precision measurements of the induced electromotive force (EMF). These magnetic field measurements are confirmed by the theoretical estimations of magnetic field according to the geometric dimensions and the effective magnetic surface-charge density of the magnet used in the experiment. The derivation of these theoretical results is based on Faraday’s view on the one hand and on the special relativity on the other, considering three different cases, namely the case in which the magnet is immobilized and the conductive disk rotates which gives the same results regardless of the theoretical basis used, the case in which the magnet and the conductive disk corotate and the case in which the conductive disk is immobilized and the magnet rotates. Comparing the theoretical results, a discrepancy was found between Faraday’s view and the special relativity. Precise measurements of EMF confirmed Faraday’s view in both cases under consideration. When the magnet and the conductive disk corotate, the theoretical result of Faraday’s view is 20.0 ± mV, the relativistic theoretical result is 16 mV and the measurement result is 19.86 ± 0.02 mV, whereas when the conductive disk is immobilized and the magnet rotates, the theoretical result of Faraday’s view is zero, the relativistic theoretical result is −4 mV, and the measurement result is practically zero.

items.title: Mapping the Evolving Landscape of Ransomware Research: A Bibliometric Analysis for Cybersecurity Advancements
items.abstract: Ransomware is a critical cybersecurity threat that disrupts healthcare, finance, and government by encrypting data and demanding ransom. Although narrative and systematic reviews have examined ransomware from technical, sector-specific, and legal perspectives, quantitative bibliometric mapping remains scarce, and existing studies cover shorter periods and fewer analytical techniques. This study addresses that gap through a bibliometric analysis of 1,386 ransomware-related publications indexed in Scopus from 2007 to 2024, using Scopus, BiblioMagika, VOSviewer, Publish or Perish, and Bibliometrix. It examines publication trends, leading authors, institutions, countries, thematic clusters, and collaboration patterns. Results show a sharp rise in output since 2017, though only seven researchers have published ten or more papers on the topic. Keyword and thematic-map patterns point to early detection techniques, deep learning, data breach analysis, convolutional neural networks, feature selection, machine learning, and artificial intelligence as areas of growing activity, consistent with a shift toward proactive and intelligent defense mechanisms. By mapping the intellectual structure and evolution of ransomware research, this study offers insights for cybersecurity professionals, academics, and policymakers seeking to understand current trends, anticipate future challenges, and design more effective mitigation strategies.

items.title: Evaluating machine-learning models for multiclass classification of LIGO gravitational-wave glitches
items.abstract: Abstract Gravitational-wave detectors are affected by short-duration non-Gaussian noise transients, or glitches, which can obscure astrophysical signals and complicate downstream analyses. We present a systematic benchmark of XGBoost and nine deep tabular architectures for 24-class glitch classification using structured metadata from the Gravity Spy O3 catalogue. The original comparison evaluates predictive performance, random-seed robustness, computational cost, data-scaling behavior, and model-native feature-attribution rankings. We additionally reconstruct a duplicate-aware cohort of 437,753 events and evaluate representative tree-based, fully connected, and attention-based models under frozen grouped-random and chronological protocols. XGBoost achieves the highest grouped-random mean weighted F1 among the three audited representative models, reaching 0.8297 ± 0.0002 with the original nine features. Chronological testing is materially more difficult for all three architectures, and removing absolute timestamp variables does not eliminate the random-to-chronological performance gap; the effects of timestamp removal are also model dependent. Targeted ablations show substantial reliance on signal-strength descriptors and quality factor, whereas restoring bandwidth to the timestamp-free representation produces only modest, architecture- and split-dependent changes. Model-native TreeSHAP and Integrated Gradients rankings exhibit partially aligned but heterogeneous feature orderings. A common permutation-importance analysis supports interpreting this agreement as a protocol-dependent comparative diagnostic rather than as evidence of explanation equivalence or causal feature importance. Controlled operational measurements further show that XGBoost provides the strongest grouped-random predictive performance, while the custom multilayer perceptron has the smallest reconstructed deployment bundle and the lowest measured single-event CPU latency. These results show that random-split performance can overestimate temporal generalization and that model selection depends on the relative importance of predictive performance, deployment footprint, latency, temporal robustness, and interpretability stability.

items.title: The ALMA REBELS Survey: The [C ii ] Luminosity Function of UV-Selected Galaxies at z ∼ 7
items.abstract: Abstract Luminosity functions (LF) are some of the most basic quantities providing insights into galaxy evolution across cosmic time and enabling a direct comparison between observations and simulations. Here, we present the first [C ii] 158 μm LF at z ∼ 7 from a sizeable UV-selected ALMA sample. Our analysis makes use of 27 galaxies with significant [C ii] emission line detections in the epoch of reionization from the REBELS (Reionization Era Bright Emission Line Survey) ALMA Large Program and its pilot programs. We used these line detections and similar from ALPINE to calibrate UV luminosity-$L_\mathrm{[C\, {\small ii}] }$ and stellar mass-$L_\mathrm{[C\, {\small ii}] }$ relations at z ∼ 7. Given the challenge in precisely defining a selection volume for the REBELS sample itself, we rely on published UV LF and stellar mass function (SMF) determinations at z ∼ 7 and three complementary approaches to derive the [C ii] LF. The UV LF-based method provides a lower limit on the [C ii] LF, due to its missing the most dust-obscured systems. Our SMF-based estimate yields a Schechter function with a characteristic luminosity of $L^*_\mathrm{[C\, {\small ii}] }=10^{9.11_{-0.27}^{+0.11}}\, L_\odot$ and a steep faint-end slope. From z ∼ 7 to z ∼ 5, our inferred [C ii] LF shows an evolution of +0.3 dex in normalisation and +0.1 dex in $L^*_\mathrm{[C\, {\small ii}] }$. Our results indicate a general underprediction from models of the abundance of [C ii] emitters at high-redshift and thus potentially the number densities of massive yet UV-faint systems implied by our SMF-based method. Additionally, they suggest that 63% of the star formation rate density occurs in massive [C ii]-bright systems and that ∼60–90% of [C ii] emitters at z ∼ 7 may be missed by bright UV selections. This highlights the importance of surveys focusing on especially massive, UV-faint sources at z > 6.

items.title: GRB 180620A: Detected Signatures of Precessing Magnetars in the Optical Afterglows of Gamma-Ray Bursts
items.abstract: Abstract Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) powered by precessing magnetars have been extensively studied in the X-ray band, whereas clear signatures of such effects in the optical band have not yet been identified. In this work, we present multiwavelength optical observations of the afterglow of GRB 180620A and investigate the physical origin of its unusual optical behavior. The optical light curve exhibits two bumps: the first peaks at ~ 250 s, and the second extends from ~ 10 3 s to ~ 10 4 s. These features are difficult to explain using the standard external shock afterglow model. By analyzing the temporal and spectral properties of GRB 180620A, we find that the second bump likely shares the same physical origin as the contemporaneous X-ray emission, whereas the first bump does not. Based on this interpretation, we perform modeling and show that the first bump can be explained by forward-shock emission with energy injection, while the second bump can be attributed to emission through spin-down of a magnetar with precession which is analogous to the physical mechanism proposed for the X-ray afterglow. Our results suggest that the effects of magnetar precession can also manifest in the optical afterglow, thereby extending investigations for the influence of magnetar precession on GRB radiation to the optical band.

items.title: Electrostatic high-frequency oscillations in partially ionized two-fluid plasmas
items.abstract: Abstract We report the existence of a new electrostatic mode in an electron-neutral collision-dominated, partially ionized plasma, in which electrons and the neutral gas are coupled through collisions to behave as a single electron-neutral (EN) fluid, and positive ions behave as a separate fluid. Interestingly, the EN-ion plasma collectively oscillates with a frequency close to or higher than the ion-plasma oscillation frequency (ωpi), and the corresponding wave mode appears similar to Langmuir waves in classical plasmas. However, when ions form only a stationary background, the EN fluid oscillates at a frequency much lower than ωpi. Estimates suggest that such high-frequency electrostatic modes may be excited in laboratories and in the solar photosphere.

items.title: The Long‐Term Trend of the Equatorial Electrojet Over Indian Sector
items.abstract: Abstract The upper‐atmosphere cooling trend is well documented, while the long‐term trend of the ionospheric electrodynamics remains poorly understood. Using two geomagnetic observation data sets over Indian sector, we analyze the long‐term trend of the monthly‐median equatorial electrojet (EEJ) in 1967–2015 after removing the solar activity and seasonal signals. During 1967–1999, a period of slow geomagnetic‐equator motion, the residual of the EEJ shows a decreasing trend between 09 and 13 LT and an increasing trend between 13 and 16 LT. Following accelerated geomagnetic‐equator motion after 1999, the afternoon enhanced trend is suppressed, whereas the morning decreased trend is strengthened for the full‐period (1967–2015) data set. The semidiurnal‐like pattern in the EEJ long‐term trend is possibly related to the weakened migrating semidiurnal tide (SW2) caused by the enhanced greenhouse gases as reported in previous studies. Our results disentangle the influences of greenhouse gas and geomagnetic secular variation on equatorial ionospheric electrodynamics, and have potential implications for ionospheric climate and weather.

items.title: CochleaNet: deep learning-based image analysis for cochlear connectomics and gene therapy.
items.abstract: With the emergence of gene and optogenetic therapies targeting deafness, the comprehensive analysis of the molecular anatomy and physiology of the cochlea has become ever more important. Here, we introduce CochleaNet, a deep learning-based framework to analyze volumetric imaging data obtained by light-sheet microscopy of decalcified, cleared and fluorescently labeled cochleae. CochleaNet covers the workflow from reconstruction of the cochlea to segmentation of inner hair cells, spiral ganglion neurons and their afferent synapses, to the analysis of tonotopy and specific fluorescent expression patterns. We validated CochleaNet by comparison to manual image analysis, also demonstrating its superiority to prior segmentation methods. We then analyzed different spiral ganglion neuron types and validated different gene therapy products with CochleaNet. Trained on high isotropic resolution mouse data, CochleaNet was also applicable to the cochlea of the gerbil, another relevant animal model, and lower-resolution mouse and marmoset data from a commercially available microscope. We conclude that the combination of light-sheet microscopy and image analysis with CochleaNet paves the way for rapid and reliable quantification of cochlear molecular anatomy and preclinical gene therapy outcomes.

items.title: Antithetical roles of tau in hippocampal long-term synaptic depression in rats versus mice.
items.abstract: Synaptic dysfunction is a primary feature of tauopathies, a group of major neurodegenerative diseases that includes Alzheimer's disease. However, the normal synaptic functions of tau are poorly understood. Since rats provide advantages over mice for understanding human tau, such as expressing six tau isoforms and showing more robust signs of tau pathology, as well as offering a richer behavioural repertoire, we developed a tau knockout (Mapt KO) rat line. We primarily investigated the impact of tau elimination on long-term synaptic depression (LTD)-a form of synaptic weakening that tau mediates in mice. Low-frequency stimulation of hippocampal Schaffer collateral-CA1 synapses revealed a robust enhancement of LTD in Mapt KO rats relative to WT littermates. In contrast, in interleaved experiments, Mapt KO mice exhibited reduced LTD compared to WT littermates, in line with previous reports. Together, our findings demonstrate a species-dependent role for endogenous tau in regulating hippocampal LTD, promoting it in mice yet constraining it in rats. Therefore, the functions of tau are not necessarily conserved in rodents, underscoring the importance of animal model choice.

items.title: Remote Versus In-Person Follow-up Programming After Subthalamic Deep Brain Stimulation for Parkinson's Disease: A Multicenter Randomized Noninferiority Trial.
items.abstract: Background Remote programming of deep brain stimulation may improve access to specialized postoperative care for people with Parkinson's disease, but prospective randomized evidence remains limited. Objective We aimed to determine whether remote follow-up programming after standardized inpatient initiation is noninferior to conventional in-person follow-up programming for motor outcomes during the early postoperative period. Methods In this prospective, randomized, open-label, multicenter noninferiority trial, adults with idiopathic Parkinson's disease who recently underwent bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation implantation at six German centers were randomly assigned 1:1 to conventional in-person follow-up programming or remote follow-up programming through a secure telemedicine platform during the first 90 days after surgery. All participants underwent initial in-person postoperative programming before randomization. The primary outcome was the Movement Disorder Society-Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale Part III score at 90 days in the medication on and stimulation ON state. The prespecified noninferiority margin was 5 points. Results Fifty-two participants were randomly assigned. The per-protocol population included 26 participants in the conventional care group and 22 in the remote programming group. The between-group median difference of the primary endpoint was -2.5 points (95% confidence interval, -9.0 to 2.0), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion. Secondary clinical outcomes and patient-reported outcomes were broadly comparable between groups. Serious adverse events occurred at similar frequencies in both groups, and no deaths occurred. Conclusions Remote follow-up programming after standardized inpatient initiation achieved motor outcomes noninferior to conventional in-person follow-up during the first 3 months, with no clear short-term safety signal. © 2026 The Author(s). items.title: Dimensional and categorical emotional ratings of Russian nouns: The ENRuN-2 database.
items.abstract: Databases with emotional ratings of words are essential for studying emotional information processing in psychology, psycholinguistics, neuroscience, and related disciplines. The emotional content of stimuli is traditionally described within two approaches: dimensional (rating words on continuous scales such as valence and arousal) and categorical (rating associations of words with discrete emotion categories). Databases with emotional ratings of words have been developed for various languages, but only a few integrate both approaches. The present study introduces the first large database with emotional ratings of Russian words, ENRuN-2, which includes 6,708 nouns rated by valence, arousal, and relatedness to five discrete emotion categories: happiness, sadness, fear, anger, and disgust. Ratings were collected from 3,902 native speakers, with data quality procedures yielding a final sample of 2,681 participants. Reliability analyses demonstrated high inter-rater consistency across parameters (mean ICCs = .84-.96) and strong intra-rater stability of ratings. High correlations with existing Russian affective norms (rs = .50-.98) demonstrate the convergent validity of the ratings. Analysis of relationships among emotional parameters revealed that they are mostly nonlinear and consistent with findings from similar databases in other languages, further supporting validity. Gender differences in ratings are negligible, and correlations between them are high; however, male and female ratings diverge substantially for some words. The ENRuN-2 database can be used in a wide array of emotion studies and is freely available on the Open Science Framework ( https://osf.io/sv9mh ).

items.title: Distinct Contributions and Sensorimotor Encoding of PV and FoxP2 Neurons in the External Globus Pallidus during Perceptual Decision-making.
items.abstract: The external globus pallidus (GPe), the central nucleus of the basal ganglia, comprises diverse cell types, including parvalbumin (PV) and forkhead box protein P2 (FoxP2) neurons. Their roles in movement regulation and sensory processing are well established; however, their contribution to perceptual decision-making remains unclear. Using a Go/No-Go visual task in mice, we found that optogenetic activation of either population impaired performance, whereas PV inhibition, but not FoxP2 inhibition, disrupted behavioral accuracy. Electrophysiological recordings showed that PV and FoxP2 neurons differentially encoded visual stimuli, licking movements, and trial outcomes. FoxP2 inhibition produced minimal changes in the spontaneous firing of substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr) neurons. PV inhibition altered spontaneous SNr firing and, together with PV activation, altered task-evoked SNr activity, reducing the preference for reward-predicting stimuli in one subpopulation and unrewarded outcomes in another. These findings reveal the distinct roles of GPe PV and FoxP2 neurons in shaping perceptual decisions and modulating basal ganglia output.

items.title: Neuroplastin Suppresses Seizures by Downregulating Endophilin A1 to Promote Internalization of GluA1-AMPA Receptors: Therapeutic Implications of Arbutin.
items.abstract: Status epilepticus (SE) is a critical neurological disorder characterized by an imbalance between excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmission. α-Amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptors (AMPARs) mediate fast excitatory synaptic transmission, whereas internalization of GluA1-containing AMPARs regulates neuronal excitability. Although neuroplastin (Np) modulates neuronal excitability, its role in GluA1-AMPAR internalization in epilepsy remains unclear. Using single-cell transcriptomics, virtual knockout, in vitro and in vivo epilepsy models, patch-clamp, biochemistry, and behavioral tests, we identified Endophilin A1 (EndoA1) as a key target through which Np regulates GluA1 internalization. In epilepsy models, EndoA1 was upregulated, surface GluA1 levels increased, and receptor internalization was reduced. EndoA1 knockdown decreased the amplitude and frequency of miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents (mEPSCs), promoted GluA1 internalization, prolonged seizure latency, and shortened seizure duration. Np overexpression reduced EndoA1 expression, facilitated GluA1 internalization, and suppressed hyperexcitability, whereas EndoA1 knockdown rescued the Np knockdown-induced phenotype. Network pharmacology and molecular docking studies identified arbutin as an EndoA1-targeting compound that reduced hyperexcitability, mEPSC amplitude, and surface GluA1 in a concentration-dependent manner. These findings establish the Np-EndoA1-GluA1 axis as a key epileptic pathway, whereby Np negatively regulates EndoA1 to promote GluA1-AMPAR internalization and suppress excitability. Arbutin, which targets EndoA1, exerts anti-epileptic effects by modulating excitatory transmission.

items.title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in neurology: biomarkers and clinical implications.
items.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a shared downstream pathogenic mechanism across a wide spectrum of neurological disorders, ranging from primary mitochondrial diseases to conditions including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease, multiple sclerosis, hereditary ataxias and idiopathic inflammatory myopathies. This Review examines the role of mitochondrial biomarkers in improving diagnostic accuracy, patient stratification and monitoring of disease progression and therapeutic response. Primary mitochondrial diseases are presented as proof-of-concept models of impaired oxidative phosphorylation, providing a framework for biomarker identification and validation with translational relevance to other neurological diseases. Mitochondrial biomarkers can be broadly categorized into four domains: fluid biomarkers, reflecting metabolic alterations and stress signalling; genetic biomarkers, capturing mitochondrial DNA integrity and dynamics; multi-omics approaches, integrating transcriptomic, proteomic and metabolomic signatures; and imaging biomarkers, enabling in vivo assessment of structural and functional consequences of mitochondrial dysfunction. Across disorders, these biomarkers reveal shared disturbances in bioenergetics, redox homeostasis, mitochondrial genome maintenance and inflammatory signalling. However, clinical implementation remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, biological variability and reduced disease specificity. Integrated, multimodal biomarker strategies, combined with longitudinal validation, will be essential for supporting precision medicine and guiding the development of therapies to target mitochondrial pathways in neurology.

items.title: Privileged representational axes in biological and artificial neural networks.
items.abstract: How do neurons code information? Recent work emphasizes the geometry and information content of population codes, using measures that are blind to the native tunings (or 'axes') of neural responses. But might these representational axes matter, with some privileged systematically over others? We developed methods to test for alignment of neural tuning across brains and deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs). Across both vision and audition, both brains and DCNNs consistently favoured certain axes for representing the natural world. Moreover, the representational axes of DCNNs trained on natural inputs were aligned to those in perceptual cortices, such that axis-sensitive model-brain similarity metrics better differentiated competing models of biological sensory systems. We further show that coding schemes that privilege certain axes can facilitate task performance, reduce downstream wiring costs and improve generalization. These results motivate a new framework for understanding neural tuning in biological and artificial networks and its computational benefits.

items.title: Interneurons and network activity in the cerebral cortex: a developmental dialogue.
items.abstract: The mammalian cerebral cortex undergoes profound functional changes during early postnatal development. During this period, neurons generate spontaneous electrical activity long before sensory experience, coordinating into distinct patterns of synchronous activity. Traditionally, neuronal activity has been viewed as instructing interneuron development by modulating transcriptional programmes, morphology and connectivity. However, accumulating evidence in rodents reveals that this relationship is bidirectional: cortical interneurons are not merely passive recipients of activity-dependent signals but also active architects of developing network dynamics. They regulate spontaneous activity transitions from gap-junction-mediated synchronous events to large, synaptically driven bursts, and later to sparse firing characteristic of mature circuits. Critically, different interneuron subtypes mature at distinct timelines and orchestrate transitions in network activity. Activity-dependent mechanisms, in turn, regulate interneuron wiring, programmed cell death, diversification and terminal differentiation. This reciprocal dialogue between interneurons and network activity is essential for establishing functional cortical circuits.

items.title: Registered adolescent suicide mortality in Colombia, 2015-2024: a Bayesian spatiotemporal mapping study.
items.abstract: Purpose To describe temporal and geographic variation in registered adolescent suicide mortality in Colombia and its ecological association with multidimensional poverty. Methods This nationwide ecological study analyzed 4,234 presumed suicide deaths at ages 10-19 during 2015-2024 from the national forensic register (INMLCF). Bayesian Poisson models smoothed rates across neighboring departments and years. Aggregate rates combined four sex-age strata. Separate national vital-statistics (DANE) analyses compared suicide-coded deaths with two scenarios including undetermined intent. Results Male-to-female rate ratios (RRs) were 2.00 (95% credible interval [CrI] 1.86-2.15) at ages 15-19 and 1.05 (0.93-1.18) at ages 10-14. Total posterior rates were 4.54 (4.22-4.87) per 100,000 in 2015 and 5.23 (4.86-5.60) in 2024; no adjacent-year change had a 95% CrI excluding zero. Putumayo, Arauca and Amazonas exceeded 10 per 100,000 in 2024. Fifteen INMLCF departments had a probability > 0.95 of rates above the national comparator in all ten years. The pooled Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) RR per standard deviation was 0.84 (0.74-0.94). Including usable DANE undetermined-intent deaths increased the strict count by 22.18%; the expanded pooled MPI RR was 1.04 (0.93-1.17). Conclusion Registered mortality varied by age, sex and department. MPI associations and geographic classifications depended on registration source and case definition. The findings do not establish protection from poverty and support strengthening adolescent surveillance and death classification.

items.title: Sustained antidepressant-like effects of psychedelics through 5-HT<sub>2A</sub>R-β-arrestin signaling.
items.abstract: Psychedelics produce long-lasting antidepressant effects, but their hallucinogenic properties limit clinical use. Using structure-guided design of 5-HT 2A R-β-arrestin-biased agonists, we identified β-arrestin signaling as a critical driver of prolonged antidepressant-like effects in mice. Here we show that the slow-dissociation kinetics of lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD) enable progressive accumulation of 5-HT 2A R engagement during repeated low-dose administration, approaching the receptor occupancy achieved by an acute high dose while avoiding its high peak concentration. This kinetic separation sustains β-arrestin signaling while limiting robust Gα q -mediated Ca 2+ responses. Consistent with this framework, repeated low-dose LSD and repeated low-dose psilocybin pretreatment followed by a high-dose psychedelic challenge produced sustained antidepressant-like behavioral effects in mice. In parallel, these regimens produced no detectable psychedelic-associated behavioral disruption in mice and cynomolgus macaques. Together, these findings uncover the signaling basis of sustained psychedelic efficacy and provide a rational framework for developing nonhallucinogenic psychedelic therapies for psychiatric disorders.

items.title: Identification of candidate markers for the isolation of neuron-specific extracellular vesicles.
items.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are present in biofluids and may be useful biomarkers to non-invasively monitor brain cells, but isolating cell type-specific EVs remains challenging. Here we introduce an approach to immuno-isolate EVs from neurons and glia based on protein surface markers. We first selected transmembrane proteins suitable as cell type-specific EV markers based on gene expression and EV proteomic data. We developed a high-purity EV isolation method and cataloged the proteins present on EVs in human cerebrospinal fluid and plasma. We then computationally identified cell type-specific candidate markers for isolating EVs from neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and microglia. Using ultrasensitive immunoassays against several predicted neuron-specific proteins, we confirmed one marker, NRXN3, as present on EVs in cerebrospinal fluid and plasma. Finally, we developed efficient EV immuno-isolation methods and applied them to isolate NRXN3 + EVs. Our work provides a general methodology for the isolation of cell type-specific EVs, advancing the goal of using EVs to study brain diseases.

items.title: Blood pressure control before and after spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage: a stroke service audit and strategies for improvement.
items.abstract: In a retrospective audit of 89 adults with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) at a tertiary neuroscience centre, fewer than 60% met the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) blood pressure (BP) target in the year before their haemorrhage, despite most carrying a known diagnosis of hypertension. Blood pressure control and antihypertensive prescribing improved after ICH, yet most survivors remained above the European Stroke Organisation (ESO) secondary-prevention target, and the first documented community BP check occurred a median of 62 days after discharge. These findings expose primary- and secondary-prevention gaps spanning the whole care pathway and lend support to a structured, protocolised uptitration pathway after discharge, combining remote BP monitoring with pharmacist- or nurse-led dose escalation.

items.title: Psychological and Neurodevelopmental Correlates of Extreme Demand Avoidance in a Clinical Sample, an Exploratory Study.
items.abstract: Extreme/pathological demand avoidance (EDA) is a behavioral profile characterized by the avoidance of everyday demands, with significant impact on the individuals and those around them. Little is understood regarding the correlates and drivers of EDA; understanding these better may lead to targeted interventions and support strategies. Cross-sectional data from parent-rated measures were analyzed for 63 children referred to a specialist neurodevelopmental clinic in the United Kingdom. The relationship between EDA traits and a number of psychological (intolerance of uncertainty, anxiety, emotional dysregulation [reactivity and dysphoria], cognitive inflexibility, alexithymia [i.e., difficulty identifying emotions]), and neurodevelopmental (autistic and ADHD) traits was tested. No differences in EDA traits were found by diagnostic group (autistic vs. not-autistic) or gender (male and female). Across the whole sample, EDA traits were negatively correlated with age and positively correlated with emotional dysregulation reactivity, ADHD traits, cognitive inflexibility, intolerance of uncertainty and alexithymia. EDA was not associated with autistic traits or anxiety. Path models were used to identify which cognitive and behavioral features predicted EDA scores, once inter-correlations among predictors were controlled for. Only emotional dysregulation, ADHD traits and age predicted EDA-Q scores. Further research is needed to assess how these variables contribute to EDA in larger more diverse samples, capturing potentially unmeasured variables, and exploring possible mediation pathways.

items.title: Closed-Loop Targeted Memory Reactivation During Sleep Spindles Enhances Motor Memory Consolidation.
items.abstract: Sleep spindles are thought to facilitate motor memory consolidation by reactivating recently acquired memory traces during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep, yet most human evidence is correlational. Using a closed-loop targeted memory reactivation (CL-TMR) protocol, this study tested whether auditory cueing time-locked to spindles enhances the consolidation of a newly acquired motor sequence. Twenty-six young adults practiced two eight-element, explicitly known, sequences of finger movements, each paired with a distinct auditory cue. During subsequent NREM Stage 2 and 3 nighttime sleep, a portable deep-learning-based EEG device (Portiloop) detected spindles online and selectively replayed the cue associated with one sequence (TMR condition), while the other served as a within-subject non-reactivated control (non-TMR) condition. Behavioural performance was assessed before and after sleep. Greater overnight improvements in performance were observed for the reactivated as compared to the non-reactivated condition, hence demonstrating enhanced consolidation following spindle-locked CL-TMR. The magnitude of this TMR benefit was positively correlated with the percentage of stimulations delivered during true spindles. Furthermore, a higher percentage of stimulations occurring during spindle trains (i.e., two or more spindles separated by 6 s apart) was associated with reduced gains. These findings provide further evidence that spindle-timed reactivation supports motor memory consolidation in humans and suggest that spindle trains may represent a favourable physiological window for closed-loop interventions.

items.title: Elucidation and reconstitution of the poplar salicortin biosynthetic pathway.
items.abstract: Salicinoids are specialized benzenoid (C 6 -C 1 ) metabolites characteristic of the Salicaceae family. Although salicinoids have long been recognized as effective defense compounds and pharmacologically active constituents in willows and poplars, the biosynthetic pathway underlying their formation remains largely unresolved. Through integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses of black cottonwood (Populus trichocarpa) roots, we identified candidate genes involved in salicinoid biosynthesis belonging to the cytochrome P450 monooxygenase family 92 (CYP92) and the progesterone 5β-reductase/iridoid synthase-like enzyme (PRISE) family of short-chain dehydrogenases/reductases. Co-expression of all identified candidate genes, together with the previously characterized glycosyltransferase gene PtUGT71L1, acyltransferase gene PtACT47, and cinnamic acid-CoA ligase gene PtCNL5, in Nicotiana benthamiana resulted in the production of salicortin, the most abundant salicinoid in poplar. Further characterization of the P450 candidates revealed that two enzymes catalyze ortho-hydroxylation of both aromatic rings of the proposed salicortin precursor, benzyl benzoate, while two other P450s catalyze the subsequent oxidative dearomatization of the benzoic acid-derived ring of benzyl benzoate. The resulting dieneone intermediate is converted by PRISE enzymes via a 1,4-reduction to form the characteristic 1-hydroxy-6-oxocyclohex-2-en-1-carboxylic ester moiety of salicortin. Functional redundancy among the identified CYP92 and PRISE enzymes may reflect the central role of these compounds in plant defense.

items.title: Ten rules for identifying horizontal gene transfers in deep plant phylogenies.
items.abstract: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) is one of the most intriguing aspects of genome evolution, challenging classical views of vertical inheritance. Growing genome availability across the tree of life offers opportunities to discover HGT, yet recent reanalyses suggest many reported cases may not withstand scrutiny. Detecting ancient transfers is especially difficult, as phylogenetic signal erodes over time and analytical choices strongly shape conclusions. Here we propose 10 practical rules for evaluating HGT in deep plant phylogenies, organised around three themes: genomic foundation, rigorous analytical framework, and biological interpretation. A reliable genomic foundation requires excluding contamination, verifying genomic integration, and avoiding biased taxon sampling. Rigorous phylogenetics is essential, as deep phylogenies are sensitive to alignment parameters, substitution model, rooting strategy, and branch support. We illustrate this with three glycosyl hydrolase families: for GH9 and GH32, analytical choices can eliminate apparent HGT signals entirely, while GH18 shows why complex, multi-domain families resist confident inference. Finally, HGT signatures demand cautious, biologically plausible interpretation. Recurrent gene duplication, loss, and domain shuffling commonly produce HGT-like patterns and should always be considered as alternatives. Our rules offer a pragmatic checklist helping authors and reviewers distinguish robust HGT from artefacts, fostering more reliable evidence on HGT in plants.

items.title: Histological description and bone compactness analysis of fossil (Aldabrachelys sp.) and extant Aldabra giant tortoise (Aldabrachelys gigantea) shell bone fragments.
items.abstract: Aldabra Atoll, north of Madagascar and part of the Seychelles Outer Islands, is home to the Aldabra giant tortoise, Aldabrachelys gigantea, the only survivor of several species of giant tortoises that were once widespread on islands across the Western Indian Ocean. Aldabra Atoll preserves an extensive fossil record of giant tortoises, providing a unique opportunity to compare the shell bone microanatomy of extinct and extant forms. This study presents the first detailed histological investigation of fossil Aldabrachelys sp. shell fragments and a preliminary comparison with extant A. gigantea. Additionally, bone compactness is determined. Most fossil specimens exhibit the typical diploe structure of tortoise shell bones, comprising external and internal cortices surrounding cancellous bone, although considerable variation in cortical thickness, vascularization, remodeling, the presence and abundance of Sharpey's fibers, and preservation was observed. In contrast, extant specimens generally display a more homogeneous microanatomy with less distinct regions. This variation is also reflected in the bone compactness. Fossil Aldabrachelys sp. fragments range between 45.1% and 84.9%, and those of extant A. gigantea fragments between 45.8% and 86.1%. The substantial intra- and interfragment variability observed in both histology and compactness complicates the identification of general microanatomical patterns and highlights the importance of considering regional shell variation. Our study establishes a baseline for future investigations of giant tortoise evolution, ecology, and insular adaptation via histological characterization of shell bones.

items.title: Engineering adaptive polysaccharide biomaterials: integrated biotechnology framework for regenerative medicine.
items.abstract: Natural polysaccharides are versatile building blocks for regenerative biomaterials because of their structural diversity, generally favorable biocompatibility and biodegradability, chemical tunability, and capacity for biologically relevant interactions. Advances in biotechnology and materials engineering have expanded their role from primarily structural matrices to multifunctional platforms that can influence cellular, immune, and biochemical processes during tissue repair. This review presents an integrated biological engineering framework linking polysaccharide source and molecular architecture with extraction and purification, chemical functionalization, crosslinking, advanced fabrication, biological recognition, and translational performance. Particular emphasis is placed on structure-function relationships, stereospecific glycan-receptor interactions, immune-instructive biomaterials, protein-mediated cell-material interactions, microbiome-responsive systems, and emerging artificial intelligence-assisted approaches for biomaterial design. The importance of material purity is also critically considered, particularly the potential for residual endotoxin contamination to confound interpretation of immunomodulatory responses and compromise reproducibility. Representative applications in skin, musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, neural, and other regenerative systems illustrate how material composition, scaffold architecture, biofunctionalization, and manufacturing strategy collectively influence biological performance. Finally, challenges associated with scalable manufacturing, batch-to-batch reproducibility, sterilization, storage stability, quality control, regulatory translation, and clinical implementation are examined. By integrating molecular design, biological mechanisms, fabrication, and translational requirements, this review provides engineering principles for the development of adaptive polysaccharide biomaterials and identifies priorities for advancing reproducible and clinically translatable regenerative technologies.

items.title: Coupling irrigation technology upgrades with targeted expansion enables water-efficient and climate-resilient cereal production in China.
items.abstract: Irrigation expansion and water-saving technologies are essential for future water and food security, yet approaches that jointly improve resource conservation, yield stability and investment efficiency remain elusive. Here we integrate 42,190 county-level agricultural records, a nationally representative farmer survey comprising 3,576 observations and 2,230 controlled field experiments on maize, wheat and rice. We show that China's shift towards more efficient irrigation reduced water use by 6.6-13.4% since 2010, but the continuation of historical trends is insufficient to meet national targets or protect yields under future climate change. We identify an optimized investment pathway that combines upgrades in existing irrigated areas with targeted expansion. This crop- and region-specific approach could raise yields by 0.1-10.9% while reducing water use by at least 25.5%, with rice offering the greatest savings potential. This framework provides actionable guidance for strategic irrigation investment in China to support sustainable agricultural intensification.

items.title: Hormesis as a universal cellular strategy for growth.
items.abstract: Our review synthesizes a vast and dispersed literature to demonstrate that subtoxic doses of structurally diverse chemicals can induce a conserved growth-stimulatory (hormetic) response across bacterial, microalgal, plant, and mammalian cells. Stimulation is concentration- and exposure-time-dependent, with higher concentrations inhibiting growth. In eukaryotic models, moderate ROS signaling and activation of DNA-PKcs/Akt, ERK1/2, PI3K/AKT, mTOR, or AURKA accompany growth stimulation, with Cyclin D-CDK4 promoting G1/S transition in mammalian cells. The proliferative DNA-PKcs/Akt response is observed in human hepatic cells, while bacterial examples involve LuxR-dependent signaling and fatty acid β-oxidation. Metabolism rewires, with some microalgae enhancing glycolysis and Krebs cycling, whereas other photosynthetic microorganisms reroute photosynthetic carbon toward lipid or starch storage while downregulating selected carbohydrate-catabolic proteins. Nrf2-driven antioxidants in mammalian cells, carotenoids, and detoxifying enzymes are upregulated, establishing a preconditioned state that can attenuate apoptosis upon subsequent challenge. Within the Catabolic-Anabolic Cycling Hormesis (CACH) model, some time-dependent responses are consistent with an anabolic overshoot following a transient catabolic decline (ATP depletion). This anabolic reprogramming accompanies biofilm formation, altered motility, and, in neoplastic cells, anchorage-independent growth. Thus, cell proliferation is a metabolic strategy shaped by adversity, with functional consequences that depend on cellular context and the endpoint assessed.

items.title: The mediating roles of depression and demoralization daily hassles and behavioral inhibition as predictors of post-MI self-care: the distinct pathways of depression and demoralization.
items.abstract: Effective self-care after myocardial infarction (MI) is essential for secondary prevention, yet many individuals struggle to maintain recommended health behaviors. Daily hassles and psychological distress may interfere with self-care, but the roles of depressive symptoms and demoralization have not been sufficiently examined simultaneously. Although these forms of distress may co-occur, they reflect distinct psychological experiences. Depression is characterized by depressed mood, anhedonia, and related cognitive and motivational symptoms, whereas demoralization centers on perceived inability to cope, helplessness, and loss of meaning or purpose. This cross-sectional study examined the associations of daily hassles and behavioral inhibition (BI) with self-care behaviors after MI and tested whether depressive symptoms and demoralization statistically mediated these associations. Participants were 175 individuals who had experienced MI (mean age = 54.42 years, SD = 12.03; 58% male; 79% married) completed self-report questionnaires assessing self-care behaviors, daily hassles, BI, depressive symptoms, and demoralization. The mean time since MI was 12.08 months (SD = 4.26; range = 6-19 months). Structural equation modeling examined the hypothesized associations and indirect effects. Self-care behaviors were negatively associated with daily hassles, BI, depressive symptoms, and demoralization. Participants generally reported adequate dietary adherence and medication management but lower levels of physical activity. The model showed good fit to the data (CFI = .98, TLI = .95, RMSEA = .08). Depressive symptoms significantly mediated the associations of daily hassles and BI with self-care behaviors (indirect βs = -.09 to -.10, p p < .05). Overall, depressive symptoms and demoralization showed distinct indirect associations with poorer post-MI self-care. The findings highlight the relevance of considering multiple dimensions of psychological distress in psychosocial approaches to secondary prevention.

items.title: The Kessler 6 psychological distress scale (K6) in swedish: a psychometric study of reliability, factor structure and measurement invariance in a large population-based sample.
items.abstract: Background Psychological distress is a major public health concern, and brief, reliable screening instruments are essential for early detection and monitoring. The six-item Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K6) is widely used internationally; however, evidence regarding its psychometric properties in Sweden remains limited. This study examined the reliability, factor structure, and measurement invariance of the Swedish version of the K6 in a large population-based sample. Methods Data were obtained from the Life and Health Survey (2022), conducted in five regions in Mid-Sweden. The study included 31,759 adults aged 18-102 years. Internal consistency was assessed using McDonald's omega total. Structural validity was evaluated using confirmatory factor analysis, comparing a one-factor model, a two-factor model representing depression and anxiety, and a bifactor model comprising a general psychological distress factor and two specific factors representing depression and anxiety. Measurement invariance of one-factor model was examined across age groups and by gender using multigroup CFA, testing configural and metric invariance. Results Internal consistency was high across all demographic groups (McDonald's omega total 0.883-0.899). The one-factor model demonstrated best fit, with acceptable values according to CFI, TLI, and SRMR, but unacceptable according to RMSEA (CFI = 0.996, TLI=0.993, RMSEA=0.069, SRMR=0.020), with standardized loadings ranging from 0.70 to 0.91. The two-factor model showed acceptable fit according to CFI, TLI and SRMR, but unacceptable fit according to RMSEA (CFI=0.989, TLI=0.982, RMSEA=0.109, SRMR=0.040). Standardized factor loadings were high for both factors (Factor 1: 0.78; Factor 2: 0.78-0.91). The correlation between the two latent factors was extremely strong (r=.99). The bifactor model did not converge and therefore could not be evaluated or interpreted further. Configural and metric invariance were supported across the age groups and between men and women. Conclusions The Swedish version of the K6 demonstrates strong reliability and supports a unidimensional structure. Measurement invariance testing supported comparable measurement of psychological distress across age and gender. The scale is suitable for monitoring psychological distress in public health surveys and may also be useful as a brief screening tool in clinical practice. Further research should establish clinically relevant threshold values in a Swedish context. Trial registration Not applicable.

items.title: Can large language models code meaning-making? A multi-model validation of automated autobiographical reasoning scoring in Chinese adolescent narratives.
items.abstract: Autobiographical reasoning (AR) involves drawing self-relevant meaning from personal experiences. It is central to narrative identity research, but manual coding requires substantial time and trained coders. Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for automating other narrative coding tasks, but their capacity for meaning-making judgments that may depend on implicit event-self connections remains untested. We collected autobiographical narratives from 437 Chinese high school students and evaluated three LLMs (GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen-Max) across four prompting strategies (zero-shot, chain-of-thought, 3-shot, 5-shot) using three scoring granularities (binary, ordinal, continuous). The best-performing condition (DeepSeek-V3, zero-shot) achieved Run 1 Cohen's κ = .416; three-run majority-vote accuracy rose from 54.9% for AR-absent texts to 94.4% for moderate-to-high-AR texts, revealing strongly condition-dependent performance. In the fully crossed subset, paired-bootstrap confidence intervals for CoT-minus-zero-shot differences included zero for all three models. Error analysis identified two bias patterns: false negatives concentrated in low-AR texts (OR = 3.99, p < .001) and false positives consistent with over-interpretation of emotional expression. Under the models, prompts, corpus, and scoring rules tested here, general-purpose LLMs cannot replace formal manual AR coding.
