items.title: A web-based spot-the-difference paradigm for studying social information processing in naturalistic visual scenes.
items.abstract: This pilot study introduced and assessed a novel web-based spot-the-difference paradigm for investigating social information processing in naturalistic visual scenes. The task systematically manipulated both the presence versus absence of social elements (i.e., social figures) and the location of the target difference (social vs. nonsocial regions). Participants identified differences via mouse clicks while their eye movements and mouse trajectories were recorded simultaneously throughout the task. In Study 1, behavioral and eye-tracking data supported the task's sensitivity to social salience, as evidenced by differences in accuracy and reaction times for social versus nonsocial target differences, along with consistently greater gaze fixation on social regions regardless of where the target difference appeared. In comparison, mouse-tracking data reflected more goal-oriented behavior, with cursor trajectories more frequently falling within regions containing the target difference. Study 2 further showed that this paradigm was sensitive to individual differences in autistic traits. Participants with higher autistic trait scores exhibited slower responses specifically in social contexts, irrespective of the location of the target difference, suggesting increased cognitive demands during social information processing. However, their gaze and mouse movement patterns remained comparable to those with lower autistic trait scores. Collectively, these findings suggest that this paradigm may provide a scalable and flexible approach for studying social cognition beyond traditional laboratory settings and may help capture the dynamic unfolding of social information processing through integrated multimodal data.

items.title: Spatial-numerical associations survive spatial frequency equalization in an adult unimanual SNARC task.
items.abstract: The origins of spatial-numerical associations (SNAs), such as the SNARC (Spatial-Numerical Association of Response Codes) effect, remain debated. The Brain's Asymmetric Frequency Tuning (BAFT) hypothesis recently proposed that non-symbolic SNAs may arise from hemispheric asymmetries in spatial frequency (SF) processing, rather than reflecting a genuine spatial representation of number. Here we examined whether SNAs persist even in adult human cognition when both SF cues and, crucially, bimanual response confounds are eliminated. Participants performed a Go/No-Go non-symbolic magnitude comparison task, in which lateralized dot-arrays were compared to a central reference. Critically, all stimuli were controlled for low-level visual properties, including luminance and the SF power spectrum, thereby neutralizing potential SF hemispheric asymmetries. In addition, responses were executed using a single central key, removing any contribution of bimanual spatial coding. Results revealed a robust ratio effect, consistent with Weberian numerosity processing. Crucially, a significant SNARC congruency effect emerged in both accuracy and reaction times: relatively smaller numerosities were processed more efficiently when presented in the left visual space, whereas larger numerosities showed a right visual space advantage. Converging evidence from continuous regression analyses further supported this spatial-numerical mapping, showing an asymmetrical advantage for smaller magnitudes in left visual space and larger magnitudes in right visual space. This pattern persisted despite lacking SF asymmetries and bimanual response mappings. Together, these findings weaken the BAFT hypothesis, but only in adulthood, by showing that non-symbolic SNAs cannot be reduced to low-level visual or response-related confounds. Instead, they support a higher-order representation of numerical magnitude likely mapped onto space.

items.title: The SPOT Grid: Naturalistic images with predefined settings, patterns, objects, and textures.
items.abstract: In the natural world, higher-level visual features (e.g., scenes and objects) systematically covary with specific lower-level constituent features (e.g., textures and patterns). This natural covariation makes it difficult to isolate aspects of behavior or brain activity that are specific to a single level of the feature hierarchy. For example, a particular neural or behavioral response may reflect recognition of a "jungle" scene, or it may reflect sensitivity to the lower-level features - leaf textures, dense vertical lines, etc. - that constitute jungle scenes. To address this challenge, we developed a novel approach for partially decoupling higher- and lower-level features in naturalistic images. We employed a Stable Diffusion image generation framework to create a naturalistic image set in which setting-object pairings and texture-pattern pairings are factorially combined, enabling systematic manipulation of higher-level and lower-level image content. To validate our approach, we used state-of-the-art image-processing models to confirm that higher-level features are represented similarly regardless of their lower-level constituents and, conversely, that lower-level features are represented similarly regardless of the higher-level objects/settings they constitute. We then confirmed that human participants can readily and rapidly categorize these features in our generated images. We present the image generation framework and introduce the SPOT (Settings, Patterns, Objects, Textures) Grid, a publicly available stimulus set accompanied by image-specific metrics (upon request: forms.gle/X2HpzRYUGigFS1S27). This resource provides new opportunities for investigating hierarchical visual representations, feature binding, and abstraction across perception, behavior, and the brain.

items.title: Morphological analysis when morphemes are hard to detect: Evidence from infixation and reduplication.
items.abstract: There is substantial psycholinguistic evidence that skilled reading involves morphological analysis, whereby morphologically complex words like teacher are recognised via constituent morphemes {teach}+{-er}. The ability to recognise morphemes is vital as it allows readers to interpret both familiar and unfamiliar words. However, over 50% of the evidence for this claim comes from studies of suffixation in English, where morphemes typically have a relatively consistent surface form across exemplars (clean in cleaner, cleanliness; -ed in walked, jumped). It remains unclear whether morphological analysis is also robust when morphemes lack a consistent surface form. Using the morpheme interference paradigm in Tagalog, we test whether infixes and reduplicants are detected during prelexical processing. Infixes are inserted within a stem and therefore reduce the consistency of its surface realisation (e.g., tawag → t-in-awag 'called'), while reduplicants involve partial or full copying of a stem and therefore lack a consistent surface realisation (e.g., tawag and lundag become tatawag 'will call' and lulundag 'will jump', where ta- and lu- are instances of the same reduplicant morpheme). We found robust morpheme interference effects in both accuracy and RTs. Specifically, nonwords with morphological structure induced significantly lower accuracy and longer RTs than nonwords without. Our findings show skilled readers' acquired sensitivity to these sophisticated morphological structures and motivate refinements to theories of morpheme learning.

items.title: Stimulation uncertainty reveals distinct mechanisms of sensation seeking and impulsivity.
items.abstract: Sensation-seeking is often described as a tendency to pursue novel and stimulating experiences, yet such options are often uncertain as well. This creates a central ambiguity where choices that appear to reflect attraction to stimulation may instead reflect tolerance of uncertain outcomes, or an interaction between the two. Across two experiments, we tested how expected stimulation and stimulation uncertainty shape reward-guided choice. A reanalysis of a previous operant sensation-seeking dataset suggests that stimulation uncertainty explained behaviour better than expected stimulation. Subsequently, we conducted a preregistered online experiment to investigate the joint effects of expected stimulation and stimulation uncertainty and to compare their respective associations with sensation-seeking and impulsivity. Our results indicate that higher sensation-seeking was associated with broader stochastic sampling and lower reward performance, but this was not reducible to random choice or uncertainty tolerance alone. Instead, uncertainty weighting depended on the value assigned to expected stimulation. This profile differed from impulsivity, suggesting that the two traits shape choice through distinct computational routes. By separating expected stimulation from uncertainty, these findings refine accounts of exploratory choice by showing that sensation-seeking shapes not only how much people sample uncertain options, but how stimulation value and uncertainty are jointly weighted during choice.

items.title: Examining reliance patterns on AI advice in medical imaging: a mixed-methods, randomised, crossover experiment.
items.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) holds significant potential to support diagnostic decision making; however, the collaboration between clinicians and AI systems often does not surpass the performance of unaided humans or standalone AI. This study aimed to examine the effect of AI advice on diagnostic decision making among experts and novices, focusing on the occurrence of AI over-reliance and under-reliance and the potential mitigating effect of explainable AI. Methods We used a mixed-methods, randomised, crossover experimental design. Participants (50 task experts [radiologists] and 75 novices [non-radiologist physicians and medical trainees]) were randomly assigned in equal proportions to one of six groups, which determined the order in which the three conditions were presented across the three sessions. In each session, participants read 50 head CT scans with or without the presence of an intracranial haemorrhage, under one of three experimental conditions: control, no AI prediction; basic AI advice, AI prediction without annotations; and explainable AI advice, AI prediction with scan annotations. 80% of cases with basic or explainable AI advice received correct advice, and 20% received incorrect advice. The main outcomes were diagnostic performance (the correct identification of intracranial haemorrhage), confidence in the diagnosis, case reading time, and AI advice usefulness ratings. We defined under-reliance as a final decision that did not align with correct AI advice, and over-reliance as a final decision that aligned with incorrect AI advice. All elements of the project were preregistered and are available on the project's Open Science Framework repository. Findings Data were collected between Feb 16, 2023, and Aug 10, 2023. Both over-reliance on incorrect advice and under-reliance on correct advice occurred. Under-reliance was associated with high uncertainty and, in absolute terms, had a more detrimental effect on diagnostic performance than over-reliance. Correct explainable AI advice reduced under-reliance and improved performance (OR=1·84, p Interpretation The occurrence of both under-reliance and over-reliance highlights the need for efficient counterstrategies beyond classic explainable AI methods to foster appropriate reliance and synergy in AI-supported clinical decision-making. Funding Volkswagen Foundation, Forum for Interdisciplinary Research, and German Federal Ministry of Education and Research.

items.title: Inclusion of a multi-ancestry polygenic risk score into a machine learning weight gain prediction model: an observational analysis from the NIH All of Us Research Program.
items.abstract: Objective Obesity is a public health crisis with few effective preventative treatments limited by challenges in identifying who is at high risk of weight gain. To address this gap, our group has developed machine learning weight gain prediction models with modest predictive power. In this study, we aimed to build upon our prior work by incorporating a multi-ancestry polygenic risk score (MAPRS) into a machine learning model and hypothesized that its inclusion would improve weight gain prediction performance. Materials and methods Adults aged 18-70 years with weight measurements 2 years apart were identified within the NIH All of Us Research Program. Participants with a history of cancer, bariatric surgery, or pregnancy were excluded. XGBoost machine learning models were developed using demographics, vitals, laboratory data, obesity-related comorbidities, and MAPRS. The primary outcome was total body weight (TBW) gain of ≥10% over 2 years. Performance was compared using the area under the curves (AUCs). Results The cohort consisted of 40 205 individuals (mean [SD] age 51.1[13.5] years; 56.1% female; 48.5% White, non-Hispanic), 3806 (9.5%) of whom gained ≥10% TBW over 2 years. Model performance with and without MAPRS was similar, with AUCs of 0.705 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.692-0.718) and 0.697 (0.683-0.710), respectively. Baseline age and MAPRS had the highest variable importance. The best net reclassification index was 0.7%, indicating marginal improvements in risk classification with MAPRS. Discussion Despite the known hereditary components of obesity and the strong association between the MAPRS and weight gain, incorporating a MAPRS did not substantially enhance model performance. Conclusion Further optimization of integrating polygenic risk scores into machine learning weight gain prediction models is needed before they can be applied in the clinical setting.

items.title: Lightweight open-source reasoning large language model for evidence synthesis screening.
items.abstract: Objectives To evaluate performance and efficiency of a lightweight open-source reasoning large language model (LLM) against an expert-derived reference standard for screening scientific publication databases. Materials and methods Two expert reviewers screened subsets of database records across 3 stages: (1) base eligibility ( n = 200), (2) obesity focus ( n = 200), and (3) women of reproductive age focus ( n = 150). The LLM (gpt-oss-20b) screened all records ( n = 20 118). Performance (F1-score and sensitivity [recall]) and efficiency (average screening rate) were assessed. Results Interreader agreement was near-perfect ( κ : 0.99-1.00; all P .001). LLM performance was high: F1-score, 0.83-0.94; sensitivity, 90%-95%; specificity, 86%-99%; accuracy, 89%-94%; precision, 77%-99%; and negative predictive value (NPV), 89%-96%. Conclusion The use of lightweight open-source reasoning LLMs shows promise to support screening in evidence synthesis workflows.

items.title: The accumulation of adverse life events across the life course and their association with mental health and well-being: exploring gender heterogeneity.
items.abstract: Background Most individuals experience multiple adverse life events across their life course, accumulating into cumulative disadvantage with lasting consequences for mental health and well-being. Evidence suggests that women's mental health and well-being is more vulnerable to the negative consequences of single adverse life events, due to gender differences in event perception, available resources, and preferred coping strategies. Until now it's unclear whether these gendered patterns hold when looking at the accumulation of adverse events over a life course. The aim of this study is to examine if the accumulation of adverse life events is associated with depressive symptomatology, life satisfaction, and quality of life with a central focus on gender differences in these relationships. Methods A secondary data analysis was conducted using Wave 3 of the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA). Accumulation of adverse life events was operationalized as the number of different adverse events experienced during the life course, covering 22 life events. Three accumulation scores were calculated: a total score (TCALE) including all adverse events and two separate scores for self-oriented (SOCALE) and other-oriented (OOCALE) adverse events. Associations with depressive symptomatology, life satisfaction, and quality of life were analyzed using logistic and linear regression models. Interaction terms between accumulation scores and gender were included to examine gender differences in these associations. Results Greater accumulation of adverse life events is associated with higher likelihood of depressive symptomatology, lower life satisfaction, and reduced quality of life. Gender moderates the relationships for TCALE, with women being more vulnerable to the accumulation of adverse life events. Although no consistent gender interactions could be found for SOCALE and OOCALE, non-significant trends, for OOCALE, aligned with the patterns observed for the total accumulation score. Conclusion Cumulative life course adversity is a significant risk factor for poorer mental health and well-being, with women showing heightened vulnerability.

items.title: Jail-based opioid treatment implementation, outcomes, and costs: lessons learned from the Massachusetts Justice Community Opioid Innovation Network (MassJCOIN).
items.abstract: Limited access to medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) is a major driver of the opioid overdose crisis. Jails have been slow to implement MOUD treatment, especially agonist medications (methadone, buprenorphine). Massachusetts mandated certain county jails pilot-test delivery of all FDA-approved MOUD treatments, stipulating jails continue MOUD, or initiate it prior to release, and facilitate MOUD continuation in the community post-release. The Massachusetts Justice Community Opioid Innovation Network (MassJCOIN) partnered with seven pilot jails, the Massachusetts Department of Public Health, and community treatment providers to conduct a Type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation study of this carceral MOUD program. Drawing from selected MassJCOIN evidence on MOUD treatment program implementation, outcomes, and costs, we consider how findings can inform more effective, humane public health and clinical responses to treating incarcerated individuals. MOUD treatment in jail improves treatment engagement, reduces recidivism, and saves lives. MOUD program implementation facilitators included: policies and processes to offer universal MOUD access; transformative and adaptive leadership; appropriate staffing capacity and capabilities; proactive prevention of MOUD diversion; and consideration of patient preferences for MOUD treatment and co-occurring mental health conditions. MOUD program success was influenced by the legislative mandate and other major statewide changes and a community-based treatment system conducive to MOUD implementation. MOUD treatment continuity post-release was facilitated by re-entry planning and preparing individuals for post-release risk environments. Site-specific costs of implementing and sustaining MOUD programming provide information for decisions about program design, budgetary needs, and resource allocation. Carceral MOUD programming is a compelling strategy to advance public safety and public health. Lessons learned provide a playbook for broader diffusion of carceral MOUD programs and can help carceral leadership, healthcare providers, and policymakers make carceral healthcare improvements. Within a harm reduction framework, carceral MOUD treatment can provide substantial opportunities to fill gaps in public health prevention efforts and clinical care to reduce opioid overdose and other concomitant risks. Carceral MOUD programming offers ways for carceral systems to work for the common good, garner trust in public institutions, and increase their legitimacy and value as public institutions.

items.title: A Study of Multidisciplinary Perspectives on Lung Cancer Prevention Care for American Indian/Alaska Native People.
items.abstract: Background Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death among American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) people. Lung cancer screening (LCS) remains underutilized among AI/AN people. Multi-disciplinary perspectives can help to inform lung cancer prevention care for this population. Methods We conducted a mixed-methods study with healthcare providers and researchers who intersect with AI/AN care. Participants completed an electronic questionnaire and qualitative interviews about their role(s), perceptions of commercial tobacco use and cessation services, and LCS in AI/AN communities. Survey data were analyzed descriptively. Interview transcripts were analyzed using applied thematic analysis, with final themes organized by Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research domains. Results Multi-disciplinary care providers (n = 21) reported significant gaps in awareness of and access to tobacco cessation and LCS in AI/AN communities. Key themes include tailoring lung health resources to AI/AN cultures and improving access to and awareness of LCS. Ideal programming centers culture and family and applies Indigenous methodologies to optimize resource development. Conclusion Study findings support culturally tailored resources and barrier directed supports to enhance commercial tobacco cessation and LCS in marginalized communities. By working collaboratively within and across disciplines, healthcare systems, and Tribal communities, we can optimize care to promote lung cancer prevention in AI/AN communities.

items.title: Optimizing video review for general surgery residents: a prospective observational study.
items.abstract: Background Surgical video review is increasingly used to support self-reflection and technical skill development. However, little is known about which aspects of video review are the most effective for general surgery residents. We hypothesize that senior residents would find self-review most helpful while junior residents would benefit more from guided review with an attending coach. Methods In this single institution prospective cohort study, residents reviewed hepatocystic triangle dissection videos cropped from laparoscopic cholecystectomy operations captured on OR Black Box where the resident was the primary surgeon during this portion of the case. Over one-hour sessions, residents completed four structured video review modalities: standardized public video, peer video, self-review, and attending coach-guided review. Attending coaches were fellowship-trained MIS faculty with surgical education training. Outcomes included perceived usefulness (5-point Likert-type scale) and modified Objective Structured Assessment of Technical Skills (mOSAT) scores. Results Thirteen residents (5 seniors, 38.5% completed PGY 3-year or more) participated, having completed a mean of 72.2 (SD 36.7) laparoscopic cholecystectomies. Attending coach-guided review was rated most helpful (mean = 4.9/5), followed by self-review (4.2/5), peer video (3.3/5), and standardized public video (2.9/5). Differences across modalities were significant (ANOVA F(3,48)=6.53, p Conclusions Attending coach-guided video review is perceived as most useful by residents at all levels. The time investment of attending coaches appears worthwhile, as both junior and senior residents benefit most from guided expert reflection. Incorporating structured video review sessions with attending coaches could enhance surgical residency training in technical skills, decision-making, and self-assessment.

items.title: Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6)-mediated α-tubulin (K40) deacetylation and microtubule destabilization disrupt autophagosome-lysosome fusion in PBDE-47-induced neurotoxicity.
items.abstract: 2,2',4,4'-tetrabromodiphenyl ether (PBDE-47) is a pervasive environmental brominated flame retardant that accumulates in nervous tissues and induces persistent neurotoxicity. Emerging evidence indicates that PBDE-47 perturbs neuronal autophagy, yet the definitive upstream molecular mechanism remains uncharacterized, hindering the development of effective protective strategies. This study was performed to clarify the toxic regulatory cascade and explore feasible pharmacological interventions using in vivo neonatal rat hippocampal tissue and in vitro PC12 neuronal cell models. Animals were neonatally exposed to PBDE-47 (0.1, 1.0, 10.0 mg/kg·bw), and PC12 cells were treated with PBDE-47 (1, 10, 20 µM) for mechanistic exploration. Results showed that PBDE-47 dose-dependently upregulated histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6), decreased α-tubulin (K40) acetylation, and destabilized neuronal microtubules. Such microtubule structural damage impaired autophagosome retrograde trafficking, blocked autophagosome-lysosome fusion, and eventually caused neuronal loss, synaptic protein reduction, and cognitive impairment. For mechanism validation and rescue experiments, 1 mg/kg·bw paclitaxel (PTX) and 1 mg/kg·bw tubastatin A (TBA) were administered to neonatal rats, whereas 12.5 nmol/L PTX and 10 µmol/L TBA were used for PC12 cell treatment to stabilize microtubules and selectively inhibit HDAC6, respectively. Both pharmacological interventions effectively restored tubulin acetylation, rescued defective autophagic flux, and mitigated PBDE-47-induced neuronal injury, with TBA showing better applicability due to its high blood-brain barrier permeability and biosafety. Behavioral tests in vivo verified that PTX and TBA treatment significantly ameliorated PBDE-47-elicited learning and memory deficits. Collectively, these findings define the HDAC6/microtubule acetylation axis as a core upstream pathway responsible for PBDE-47-triggered autophagic transport failure and neurotoxicity, providing robust experimental evidence and a promising therapeutic target for the prevention of PBDEs-mediated neurological disorders.

items.title: The moderating effects of social norms and attitudes on the relationship between intimate partner violence and depressive symptoms among women in two provinces of Nepal.
items.abstract: Purpose Intimate partner violence (IPV) is often associated with increased depressive symptoms. However, considerable variability exists in this relationship, from null findings to large effect estimates, likely due, in part, to differences in attitudes (thoughts and beliefs), descriptive norms (perceptions of what behaviors occur in a community), and injunctive norms (perceptions of what behaviors are acceptable in a community). In this study, we test the effect of individual- and community-level attitudes and norms on the IPV-depressive symptoms relationship. Methods The sample included 976 married women in 30 communities in Nepal. We measured depressive symptoms with the Patient Health Questionnaire and IPV with items adapted from the Revised Conflict Tactics Scale. We used generalized linear models to test seven moderators: individual-level attitudes (gender-inequitability and acceptability of husband abuse), an individual-level descriptive norms scale, and community-level proxies of injunctive norms (aggregated attitudes) and descriptive norms (aggregated IPV prevalence and descriptive norms scale). Results Descriptive norms significantly moderated the IPV-depressive symptoms relationship at both the individual and community level. The differences in depressive symptoms between women who did and did not experience IPV were stronger where violence was perceived to be less widespread. Individual-level attitudes and community-level injunctive norms proxies were not found to be significant moderators. Conclusion Where IPV is less prevalent (or perceived as such), experiencing IPV may increase depressive symptoms, as the experience deviates from the prevailing norm. Research should continue to refine norms measurement and explore individual and contextual factors that impact the likelihood of negative mental health outcomes to inform prevention and response interventions.

items.title: Assessment of teachers' knowledge, awareness, and response to students with asthma in Greater Cairo schools.
items.abstract: Bronchial asthma remains a significant public health challenge, especially among school-aged children. Schoolteachers are often the initial responders to asthma attacks, making their role vital for early symptom recognition and first aid provision. Therefore, this study aimed to explore the knowledge, awareness, and response of schoolteachers to students with asthma. Between March 2024 and October 2024, a self-administered questionnaire was created on Google Forms and distributed to schoolteachers through WhatsApp groups of private and public schools across different districts in Greater Cairo. The questionnaire consisted of three sections assessing: (1) teachers' experience and demographics, (2) basic knowledge of asthma, and (3) knowledge related to first aid response in an asthma attack. A total of 634 schoolteachers participated in the study. Of these, 361 (57%) reported having previously taught students with bronchial asthma, whereas only 176 (27.8%) had witnessed a student having an acute asthma attack before. A majority of participants (445/634, 70.2%) correctly identified the short-acting beta agonist (SABA) inhaler or nebulizer as appropriate first aid for an acute asthma attack. However, only 187/634 (29.5%) reported knowing the correct technique for using SABA inhalers or nebulizers during an asthma attack. More than half of the participants, 362/634 (57.1%), provided appropriate answers regarding the etiology of the disease, specifically whether it was a contagious disease or not. There was no statistically significant association between teachers' knowledge level and their sociodemographic characteristics. Teachers in Greater Cairo demonstrated fair knowledge and awareness regarding asthma. However, they did not fully understand appropriate first-aid responses, a gap that underscores the need for more asthma education programs.

items.title: Sex-Specific Associations of Small, Vulnerable Newborns With Mental Capital in Early School-Aged Children.
items.abstract: Background Although mental capital is increasingly recognised as a foundation for children's later well-being, its perinatal determinants remain unclear because traditional classifications such as preterm birth and small for gestational age (SGA) capture only partial and overlapping aspects of vulnerability. Objectives Using the integrated small vulnerable newborn (SVN) framework with mutually exclusive categories, we aimed to assess associations between SVN categories and mental capital at ages 6-7 years by sex. Methods We analysed data from six waves of the Adachi Child Health Impact of Living Difficulty (A-CHILD) study, a population-based repeated cross-sectional survey of first-grade students in Adachi City, Tokyo, conducted between 2015 and 2024 (n = 20,928). Caregivers provided gestational week and birthweight from the Maternal and Child Health Handbook, and children were classified into SVN categories (term non-SGA, term SGA, preterm non-SGA, preterm SGA). Mental capital, including behavioural problems, prosocial behaviour, and resilience, was assessed using the parent-reported Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire and Children's Resilience and Coping Scale. Multivariable regression models were fitted, stratified by biological sex. Results Among the 20,928 children, 3402 (16.3%) were term SGA, 1093 (5.2%) were preterm non-SGA, and 227 (1.1%) were preterm SGA. Compared with term non-SGA, term SGA was associated with higher total difficulties scores among girls (standardised β 0.11, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.05, 0.17) but not among boys (β 0.03, 95% CI -0.03, 0.09). Term SGA girls also showed lower resilience (β -0.07, 95% CI -0.12, -0.01). In contrast, preterm non-SGA boys had higher total difficulties scores (β 0.13, 95% CI 0.04, 0.21). There was no evidence that any SVN category was associated with prosocial behaviour in either sex. Conclusions Term SGA tended to be associated with behavioural problems and lower resilience among girls, whereas preterm non-SGA tended to be associated with behavioural problems among boys.

items.title: Substance use profiles predict health outcomes among U.S. adults with diabetes: Implications for primary care screening and intervention.
items.abstract: Aims Substance use is common among adults with diabetes yet remains poorly characterized in terms of co-occurring patterns. This study sought to identify distinct substance use profiles among U.S. adults with diabetes, characterize factors associated with profile membership, and examine their clinical relevance. Methods Data were from the 2022-2023 National Survey on Drug Use and Health (n = 89,889; 6805 with diabetes). Latent class analysis identified substance use profiles. Multinomial logistic regression examined demographic, socioeconomic, and mental health characteristics associated with profile membership. Weighted regression models evaluated associations between membership and health indicators. Results Three profiles emerged: Low/Non-Use (67.6%), Cannabis and Binge Drinking (24.4%), and Polysubstance Use (8.0%). Higher-risk membership was associated with male sex, mental health burden, and urban residence; marriage and college education were protective. Both higher-risk classes were more than twice as likely to report poor self-rated health. Polysubstance Use class members had significantly higher odds of hospitalization (OR = 1.46). Conclusions Substance use among adults with diabetes is heterogeneous and linked to measurably worse health status outcomes including poorer self-rated health and higher hospitalization risk. These findings support routine, risk-stratified screening for substance use and mental health in diabetes care and may help inform targeted interventions.

items.title: Association Between Circadian Rhythm Syndrome and Physical Pain in China.
items.abstract: Purpose Circadian rhythm syndrome (CircS) is a complex syndrome caused by biological rhythm disruption and is closely associated with the onset of numerous diseases. This study aimed to explore the association between CircS and physical pain, providing important clues and a scientific basis for the development of pain prevention strategies. Design A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from the 2011-2018 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). Methods The association between CircS and the risk of developing physical pain was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Cox proportional hazards models. Restricted Cubic Splines (RCS) were employed to examine linear or nonlinear relationships between the number of CircS components and the risk of physical pain events. Assessed the robustness of the results using sensitivity analyses, such as subgroup analyses and interaction analyses. Results The longitudinal study included 5,388 participants, of whom 3,296 experienced pain events during follow-up. Results indicated that participants with CircS had a higher risk of physical pain than those without CircS (hazard ratio: 1.203, 95% confidence interval: 1.113, 1.300, p Conclusions CircS increased the risk of developing physical pain. Addressing circadian rhythm disorders and maintaining metabolic homeostasis were crucial for preventing and delaying the onset of physical pain. Clinical implications This study provides important clues and a scientific basis for the clinical application of "circadian rhythm-pain" management.

items.title: Mesenchymal stem cells: towering ambitions, shaky foundations.
items.abstract: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have been a feature of stem cell research since the early 1990s. Despite long-standing questions concerning the identity, characteristics, physiological functions, and potential therapeutic uses of these cells, MSC studies are now published more frequently than those of any other stem cell type. Over the past decade, this increase in the MSC literature is attributable almost entirely to publications by scientists in China. Reviewing the history and present state of MSC research, we explore why this might be and propose steps that stakeholders in China and other countries might take to address what has become one of the more perplexing developments in contemporary stem cell research.

items.title: Effect of a PRECEDE-PROCEED model-based laughter yoga-supported education program on adolescent bullying: A randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract: Background Peer bullying is a significant public health concern in adolescence. The aim of this study was to examine the effects of a PRECEDE-PROCEED model-based, laughter yoga-supported educational program on peer victimization, bullying perpetration, bullying-related knowledge, and empathy and sympathy among eighth-grade students. Design This randomized controlled trial included 70 eighth-grade students randomized to intervention (n=35) or control (n=35) groups. Data were collected using the Personal Information Questionnaire, the Peer Victimization Scale, the Peer Bullying Scale, the Peer Bullying Information Form, and the Adolescent Measure of Empathy and Sympathy at baseline and post-test. The intervention group received a 6-week health education and laughter yoga program. Data were analyzed using ANCOVA and Quade's ANCOVA. Results At baseline, the groups were comparable on sociodemographic characteristics and on most outcomes. However, the intervention group had significantly lower pre-test scores for PVS total, Terror, Overt Victimization, and Sympathy. These baseline differences were accounted for in the adjusted analyses. At post-test, the intervention group had significantly lower peer victimization and bullying perpetration scores and significantly higher knowledge and empathy-sympathy scores than the control group (p Conclusion The PRECEDE-PROCEED model-based Laughter Yoga Supported Education Program was associated with short-term reductions in peer victimization and bullying perpetration and with short-term improvements in bullying-related knowledge and empathy-sympathy skills. School-based, multicomponent programs that combine educational and emotion-focused strategies may contribute to prevention of bullying. Longer follow-up is needed to assess the sustainability of these effects. Clinical trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07534566.

items.title: Preconception Systemic Inflammation Response Index and Time-to-Pregnancy.
items.abstract: Background Systemic inflammation may affect female reproductive function, but there is relatively little epidemiological evidence regarding the association between pre-pregnancy inflammatory status and fertility. We explore the association between the pre-pregnancy Systemic Inflammation Response Index (SIRI) and the time to pregnancy (TTP) in couples trying to conceive. Method This study included 1739 couples from the National Free Preconception Check-up Project (NFPCP) in Guangzhou. SIRI was calculated as neutrophil count × monocyte count/lymphocyte count from routine complete blood count (CBC) at baseline. Quartile and continuous variable analysis of SIRI was performed, and restricted cubic spline functions were used to evaluate the dose-response relationship. The associations were adjusted for demographic, behavioural, and lifestyle factors. Results In the NFPCP preconception couple cohort, 1182 pregnancy events were observed. In categorical analyses, women in the highest quartile of SIRI (Q4: 0.99, 5.58) had lower fecundability than those in Q2 (FR, 0.79; 95% CI 0.63, 0.98), indicating a longer TTP. The inverse association became more apparent at SIRI levels above approximately 0.89 in spline-based analyses. Sensitivity analyses yielded comparable effect estimates after restricting the analysis to live birth outcomes and excluding women with chronic inflammatory conditions, fertility-related disorders, or antibiotic use, supporting the robustness of the observed association. Conclusions Higher preconception SIRI was associated with longer TTP, and the association remained generally consistent across adjusted and sensitivity analyses. SIRI may have potential value in preconception risk stratification, but further studies are required to confirm its clinical relevance.

items.title: Schaftoside from galgeuntang as a multi-target class I histone deacetylase inhibitor: Integrated molecular docking, dynamics, and systems pharmacology analysis.
items.abstract: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are enzymes that remove acetyl groups from lysine residues of histone proteins, playing a critical role in gene expression regulation. Particularly, Class I HDACs (HDAC1, HDAC2, and HDAC8) are implicated in cancer development and have attracted significant interest as therapeutic targets. However, developing isoform-selective HDAC inhibitors remains challenging. We screened 1625 phytocompounds from the Korean herbal formulation Galgeuntang using the Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology database. After applying drug-likeness filtering, 235 compounds underwent molecular docking against HDAC1, HDAC2, and HDAC8. Schaftoside emerged as the sole candidate engaging all three isoforms, with binding energies of -115.1, -103.8, and -135.5 kcal/mol, respectively. ADMET profiling, quantitative cytotoxicity predictions across multiple cancer cell lines, and in silico gene expression analysis were then performed. One hundred nanosecond molecular dynamics simulations confirmed stable complex formation and PCA-based free energy landscape analysis revealed well-defined conformational minima for each complex. Schaftoside exhibited potent predicted cytotoxicity against hematological and gastrointestinal malignancies (selectivity Index: 8.7-18.6), including the cisplatin-resistant A2780cisR ovarian carcinoma line. In silico transcriptomic profiling predicted downregulation of oncogenic drivers (MYC, STAT3, AKT1) with concurrent upregulation of tumor suppressors (TP53, CDKN1A) and suppression of the HDAC machinery itself. ADMET profiling revealed high aqueous solubility but limited membrane permeability, indicating that structural optimization will be required. Schaftoside therefore constitutes a promising multi-target Class I HDAC inhibitor scaffold, warranting experimental validation through enzymatic assays, histone acetylation analysis, and cell-based cytotoxicity testing.

items.title: Engineering a low cytotoxicity recombinant rabies virus neurotracer via N-gene recoding.
items.abstract: Viral-vector-based tracers have proven invaluable for mapping neural circuits. Rabies virus (RV)-based retrograde trans-monosynaptic tracers have been widely used for depicting the input neural circuit of targeted neuronal populations. However, the cytotoxicity of the RV tracer limits its application. Here, we employed the synthetic attenuated virus engineering technology to recode the N gene of the RV SAD-B19 strain by codon pair deoptimization to generate attenuated RV tracers. The characteristics of the recoded RV tracers were tested both in vitro and in vivo . The full-length recoded N gene abolished viral rescue, whereas the partial recoded N gene supported successful viral recovery. Compared to its parent, the recoded RV trans-monosynaptic tracer exhibited lower cytotoxicity and labeled more input neurons. It can also robustly express proteins to visualize the neuronal morphology and manipulate the neural circuit activity. Collectively, our work generated a new retrograde trans-monosynaptic tool, which complements existing neural circuit tracers. Importance Viral vectors play an important role across multiple fields in biomedicine. In the neuroscience community, rabies virus (RV)-based retrograde trans-monosynaptic tracers have been widely used to map the input neural circuits of targeted neuronal populations. However, the inherent cytotoxicity of RV-based tracers limits their broader application. In this study, we utilized synthetic attenuated virus engineering technology to recode the RV N gene, generating an attenuated neurotracer that will significantly benefit future neuroscience research.

items.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Treatment Failure After Middle Meningeal Artery Embolization for Subdural Hematoma.
items.abstract: Middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) is effective for chronic subdural hematoma (SDH), but failure rates vary and risk prediction tools are lacking. This study developed and validated a machine learning (ML) model to predict MMAE treatment failure for SDH. We conducted an international, multi-institutional retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent MMAE for SDH between 2019 and 2025. The cohort was split into training and test sets, stratified by treatment failure, with all hematomas from each patient assigned to a single cohort to prevent data leakage. Multiple ML algorithms were evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation, with gradient boosting selected as the final model. The primary outcome was treatment failure, defined as rescue surgical evacuation or persistent/recurrent SDH requiring retreatment. Model performance was assessed using area under the curve-receiver operating characteristic. Patients were stratified into low-risk ( 15%) groups using a priori clinically defined thresholds. Among 692 treated hematomas in the test cohort, 64 (9.2%) experienced treatment failure. The gradient boosting model achieved an area under the curve-receiver operating characteristic of 0.856 (95% CI, 0.803-0.902) before calibration and 0.832 (95% CI, 0.766-0.889) after isotonic calibration, with excellent calibration (Brier score, 0.053). The most important predictors were age-platelet interaction, platelet-hemoglobin ratio, platelet count, SDH thickness, and age. Observed treatment failure was 1.6% (95% CI, 0.4%-5.7%) in the low-risk group (n = 124; 17.9%), 6.0% (95% CI, 4.3%-8.4%) in the medium-risk group (n = 516; 74.6%), and 59.6% (95% CI, 46.1%-71.8%) in the high-risk group (n = 52; 7.5%) (P < .001 for trend), a 37.2-fold difference between high- and low-risk groups. This ML model stratified MMAE patients into risk groups with a 37.2-fold difference in treatment failure. High-risk patients had 59.6% failure, whereas low-risk patients had 1.6% failure. Risk stratification may improve patient selection and monitoring.

items.title: Comparison of Life-Space Activities by Driving Engagement Among Older Drivers.
items.abstract: This study aimed to compare the differences in life-space activities among older Japanese drivers based on self-reported driving engagement in relatively difficult situations. This is a cross-sectional cohort study of 12,309 community-dwelling older drivers (mean [SD] age, 72.5 [5.1] years; 54.5% female). Driving engagement was assessed using yes/no questions regarding six driving situations, including rain, dark nights, and unfamiliar roads. Responses to the situations were categorized as "not driving," "driving with anxiety," and "driving without anxiety." The Active Mobility Index (AMI) assessed the life-space and activities from respondents' home. Analysis of covariance showed that driving with anxiety and not driving in some situations were significantly lower AMI scores compared to driving without anxiety (p < 0.05), especially in those who drive ≥ 4 situations. While driving is a correlate of life-space activities in older adults, addressing driving anxiety may help maintain life-space mobility among older drivers.

items.title: Developmental mechanisms contributing to non-linear firing dynamics in spinal motoneurons of the postnatal mouse.
items.abstract: The intrinsic properties of spinal motoneurons support flexible movement, including the maintenance of postural tone. Motoneurons can produce sustained action potential output that outlasts synaptic input, a phenomenon traditionally attributed to persistent inward currents (PICs) mediated by sodium and calcium channels. Using whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology, we examined how specific ion channels contribute to PIC maturation and non-linear firing dynamics that allow motoneurons to sustain their output in fast and slow lumbar motoneurons across postnatal development in mice. PIC amplitude and non-linear firing dynamics increased after weight-bearing in fast but not slow motoneurons. Blocking Na V 1.6 channels reduced PIC amplitude at both pre- and post-weight-bearing stages, whereas L-type calcium channel blockade only reduced PICs after weight-bearing emerged. However, reducing PIC amplitude by blocking these channels, either individually or in parallel, did not abolish sustained firing hysteresis, which may be because PICs are not yet fully established at this stage of postnatal development. Unexpectedly, activation of muscarinic receptors increased PIC amplitude while promoting adaptive firing dynamics, suggesting that PICs alone do not account for sustained firing hysteresis. We also found that pharmacological manipulation of potassium currents mediated by KCNQ and K V 1.2 channels produced substantial changes in firing dynamics. Strikingly, blocking hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channels promoted sustained firing dynamics and led to the emergence of self-sustained firing in fast motoneurons. These results indicate that PICs and non-linear firing dynamics mature together and extend the current framework on non-linear firing dynamics of motoneurons to include additional voltage-gated ion channels. KEY POINTS: Persistent inward currents (PICs) and recruitment-derecruitment hysteresis increase in parallel in fast, but not slow, motoneurons following the onset of hindlimb weight-bearing. Increased expression or function of L-type calcium channels may contribute to enhanced PIC amplitude in fast motoneurons after weight-bearing emerges. Blocking Na V 1.6 or L-type calcium channels did not reduce sustained firing hysteresis in fast motoneurons. KCNQ channels oppose PICs and, together with K V 1.2 channels, shape recruitment-derecruitment asymmetry, thereby modulating firing hysteresis in fast motoneurons. Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channels generate a resting H-current that delays recruitment, modulates firing hysteresis, and prevents the emergence of self-sustained firing in fast motoneurons.

items.title: Availability of resources to apply the 2024 McDonald criteria: A global perspective.
items.abstract: Background The 3rd ECTRIMS Winter School highlighted regional and global disparities in resources needed to implement the 2024 McDonald diagnostic criteria for multiple sclerosis. Objectives To assess the availability of paraclinical tools and regional differences in access reported by neurologists in an online survey. Results The survey was completed by 328 neurologists from 44 countries. Core diagnostic tools, including magnetic resonance imaging and oligoclonal band testing, were widely available. Access to advanced imaging, optic nerve assessment, and laboratory biomarkers varied across regions. Conclusions Variability in access to key paraclinical tests may impact on the implementation of the 2024 McDonald criteria globally.

items.title: The role of physical activity in post-stroke depression among European women and men aged 50 and older.
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo examine the associations between the frequency of moderate-vigorous physical activity and depression among adults aged 50 years or older with a history of stroke.Design and settingCross-sectional study using data from Wave 9 (2021-2022) of the Survey of Health, Aging and Retirement in Europe.ParticipantsA total of 1323 adults aged 50 years or older with a history of stroke, residing in 18 European countries, were included.AnalysisBinary logistic regression models were used to examine associations between the weekly frequency of moderate-vigorous physical activity and depression. Analyses were stratified by sex and adjusted for potential confounders.Main measurementsDepression was assessed using the 12-item European Depression Scale. Weekly moderate-vigorous physical activity frequency was categorized as 1 time per week.ResultsAdjusted results showed that, for men, engaging in moderate physical activity once (odds ratio = 0.60) or more than once a week (odds ratio = 0.49) reduced the odds of depression. For vigorous physical activity, the benefit in men required a frequency of more than once a week (odds ratio = 0.61). Among women, moderate-vigorous physical activity significantly reduced the risk of depression only when performed more than once a week (odds ratio = 0.58 and 0.43, respectively).ConclusionIn individuals aged 50 or older with a history of stroke, the weekly frequency of moderate-vigorous physical activity was associated with lower odds of depression in both sexes. items.title: Modulation of social preference and avoidance of zebrafish conspecifics treated with selected neuroactive compounds.
items.abstract: Social interaction and preference are essential parts of human and animal behavior. Zebrafish are rapidly emerging as a major model organism in neurobehavioral research and, as highly social animals, enable probing of their social preference and its pharmacological modulation. Neuroactive drug effects, however, can also be socially transmittable, thereby indirectly affecting drug-free animal behavior as well. Here, we examine this possibility in adult zebrafish by assessing their social preference for conspecifics treated using a wide range of neuroactive drugs with well established effects in zebrafish. Zebrafish were treated with acute or chronic neuroactive drugs (GBR-12909, fluoxetine, reserpine, caffeine, arecoline, nicotine, cuprizone, ethanol, and atropine), and exposed to target fish in the three-chamber social preference test, scoring time the latter spent in each zone. Overall, we found their overt social preference for conspecifics treated with acute nicotine and GBR-12909, and social avoidance of fish exposed to all other drugs used, except cuprizone and ethanol. These findings confirm altered social preference for central nervous system (CNS) drug-treated zebrafish, but suggest that this preference is nonlinear and does not correlate with anxiolytic or anxiogenic drug profiles. Further research is needed to explore why some CNS drug-evoked behavioral effects render conspecifics socially attractive or aversive to observer zebrafish, and to determine potential practical and translational implications of these findings for neuropharmacology and biological psychiatry.

items.title: Feasibility and apparent safety of functional electrical stimulation-assisted cycling in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and primary lateral sclerosis: a single-arm longitudinal pilot feasibility study.
items.abstract: Functional electrical stimulation-assisted cycling may be relevant in motor neuron disease, but its feasibility and safety in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and primary lateral sclerosis remain unclear. The authors aimed to assess feasibility, apparent safety, and exploratory pre-post clinical changes of a three-week functional electrical stimulation-assisted cycling protocol in ambulatory inpatients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis or primary lateral sclerosis. Fifteen patients were assessed; 11 were enrolled (5 ALS, 6 PLS) and received 15 supervised 30-minute FES-cycling sessions over three weeks in addition to conventional neuromotor rehabilitation. Bilateral eight-channel stimulation targeted quadriceps, tibialis anterior, hamstrings, and gastrocnemius during active or active-assisted cycling. Feasibility outcomes were enrollment, completion, tolerance, adverse events, and pre-post data availability. Clinical outcomes were analyzed descriptively. Eleven of 15 assessed patients were enrolled (73.3%; 5 ALS, 6 PLS). All enrolled participants completed the protocol, no adverse events were documented, and complete pre-post data were available. Exploratory outcomes showed favorable short-term changes in mobility, walking, strength, and spasticity. This protocol appears feasible and apparently safe in selected ambulatory inpatients. Findings are hypothesis-generating and support a prospective controlled feasibility trial before efficacy is tested.

items.title: Disrupting objectification: transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (tDCS) enhances the inversion effect toward sexualized women.
items.abstract: Sexual objectification is associated with viewing women in an object-like manner, often indexed perceptually by a reduced inversion effect for sexualized women relative to men. Prior research has shown that this index can be attenuated through social manipulations; here we investigated whether it can be modulated through neuromodulation. Using a double-blind, between-subjects design, participants ( N = 76) completed a recognition task involving upright and inverted sexualized targets while receiving either anodal transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (tDCS) (10-mins, 1.5 mA, anode at Fp3) or sham/control stimulation (30-secs, 1.5 mA). The sham group exhibited a significantly reduced inversion effect for sexualized women relative to men, a finding interpreted as an index of objectification. Critically, this pattern differed between groups (Orientation × Target × tDCS interaction) and was not observed in the anodal tDCS group: the inversion effect for sexualized women was larger than under sham and did not differ significantly from that for men. This modulation was accompanied by improved recognition of upright sexualized women. These findings provide initial evidence that objectification, as indexed by the inversion effect, can be modulated through neurostimulation. More broadly, the results suggest that the perceptual processes captured by this index are modifiable.

items.title: Temporally differentiated modulation of emotional face processing by attentional resource availability: An ERP study.
items.abstract: The interplay between top-down attentional control and bottom-up emotional capture remains debated, particularly in the late positive potential (LPP) time window. In the present study, we used mass-univariate analysis to examine whether task difficulty itself modulates late-stage emotional processing in an implicit task. In a dual-target rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP) paradigm, perceptual load was manipulated at T1, and at T2, fearful, happy, neutral, or face-absent stimuli were presented in a face-detection task. Emotional differentiation emerged during 148-372 ms and was not influenced by perceptual load, suggesting that emotional features were extracted relatively automatically. During the early LPP (400-600 ms), emotional differentiation was detected under low but not high load, suggesting that inconsistencies in emotion-related LPP effects reported in previous implicit-task studies may stem from differences in task difficulty. During the late LPP (600-800 ms), however, fearful expressions remained distinguishable from neutral expressions even under high load, indicating that resource limitations did not eliminate late emotional differentiation. Together, these findings provide compelling evidence that the availability of attentional resources differentially shapes the processing of emotional information in implicit tasks.

items.title: Distinct profiles of white matter diffusivity in obesity and bipolar disorders: An ENIGMA bipolar disorders study in 2166 individuals.
items.abstract: Background Bipolar disorders (BD) are associated with a wide range of brain white matter abnormalities, but results vary across studies. This heterogeneity likely relates to effects of additional clinical/diagnostic variables, including medications and obesity, on white matter in BD. In this mega-analysis, we studied the links between relevant clinical variables and four diffusivity measures. Methods We obtained diffusion tensor imaging-derived fractional anisotropy (FA), mean, axial, and radial diffusivity (MD, AD, RD) values from 910 individuals with BD and 1256 healthy controls across 16 research sites in the ENIGMA-BD Working Group. We used principal component analysis to detect patterns of covariance across white matter tracts and studied associations between multivariate patterns of white matter alterations and demographic and clinical variables, including body mass index (BMI), medications, and diagnostic information, using mixed regression models. Results Higher BMI was associated with lower PC1 FA and higher PC1 RD; BD was associated with higher PC1 MD, while treatment with antiepileptic medications was associated with lower PC1 FA, higher PC1 MD, and PC1 RD. Conclusions We found FA and MD are weakly associated, providing complementary information, and there are unique associations between specific diffusivity measures and clinical predictors. Treatment with antiepileptics may inflate the statistical effects of BD on white matter. By using all diffusivity measures and accounting for additional clinical factors, we can gain new insights into brain correlates of severe mental illness.

items.title: Striosomes: Small Circuits With a Large Role in Locomotion.
items.abstract: The striosome compartment is a distinct anatomical structure embedded in a labyrinth-like fashion within the mammalian striatum, first identified nearly half a century ago. Although the striosome is a small structure comprising only about 10% to 20% of the total striatal volume, its unique developmental, neurochemical, and projectional characteristics have long suggested specialized and significant functional roles. Furthermore, while clinical evidence has implicated striosomal dysfunction in movement disorders including dystonia and Huntington's disease, their specific involvement in locomotor control has remained a mystery for decades. However, the functional properties of striosomes have begun to become unveiled through the development of genetically modified mouse lines that target striosome-enriched molecules. Accumulating evidence has indicated that striosomes play distinctive roles that differ fundamentally from the canonical direct and indirect pathway models. The striosome inhibits striatal dopamine release and locomotion vigor, potentially biasing subsequent context-dependent action selection. Consequently, the striosome compartment is an indispensable part of the functional anatomy of striatal projection neurons. We hereby describe the anatomy of the striosome compartment and the neuroscience methodologies used for its assessment, emphasizing the emerging roles of the striosome compartment in locomotor control and dopamine regulation.

items.title: Establishment of Standardized Normative Reference Values for Pressure-Based Gait Analysis in the Healthy Korean Population: A Nationwide Multi-Center Registry Study.
items.abstract: Objective Normative gait data for Asian populations remain scarce, and Western reference values may not apply to Koreans. We aimed to establish nationwide reference values for pressure-based gait analysis in healthy Korean adults. Methods Healthy community-dwelling adults (N = 612, aged 20 to 80s) were enrolled at 11 randomly selected centers using quota-based recruitment across 18 sex- and age-stratified cohorts. Spatiotemporal gait parameters, classified into five domains, were recorded on a pressure-based electronic walkway. Gait speed cutoffs were defined at -1.0 and -1.5 standard deviations (SD) below age- and sex-specific means. Age-group differences were evaluated using ANOVA and linear mixed-effects models adjusted for height and study site. Results Gait velocity followed a normal distribution in all strata. In both sexes, older age groups showed lower Pace domain values and higher step length variability, which remained significant after adjustment for height and study site. In contrast, Rhythm domain parameters and asymmetry indices were preserved across age groups. Cutoffs were provided at -1.5 SD for normally distributed parameters and the 7th percentile for non-normally distributed parameters. Conclusions This is the first nationwide multicenter reference dataset for spatiotemporal gait parameters in healthy Korean adults across the full adult age range. These population-specific values provide a practical baseline for interpreting pressure-based gait analysis and for applying gait-based clinical criteria in Korea.

items.title: A Phase 2a randomized trial of once- versus twice-daily remote ischemic conditioning in vascular cognitive impairment (TRIC-VCI).
items.abstract: Introduction Cerebral small vessel disease.(CSVD) is a leading cause of vascular cognitive impairment.(VCI). Remote ischemic conditioning (RIC) is a promising strategy to prevent CSVD progression, but it is unclear what doses of daily RIC are tolerable/adherable for older patients with CSVD-associated VCI. Methods The Trial of Remote Ischemic Pre-conditioning in Vascular Cognitive Impairment (TRIC-VCI; ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT04109963) was a prospective, open-label, randomized controlled trial with blinded endpoint assessment. Participants completing 14-day run-in were randomized to once- or twice-daily RIC for 30 days. RIC consisted of four cycles of blood-pressure cuff inflation to 200 mmHg around an arm for 5 minutes followed by 5-minute deflation using automated devices. Inclusion criteria: ages 60 to 85, CSVD evidence on computed tomography/magnetic resonance imaging, Montreal Cognitive Assessment score 13 to 24, and preserved basic activities of daily living. Outcomes were assessed at 30 and 90 days. The primary outcome was adherence (completing ≥ 80% of sessions). Secondary outcomes included percentage of sessions completed, safety, and pain/discomfort ratings. Exploratory outcomes included changes in white matter hyperintensity (WMH) volume, cognitive tests, and blood biomarkers. We explored trial experiences in a focus group with five patient-caregiver dyads. Results Twenty-two of 23 patients completed run-in and were randomized. Ten of 11.(90.9%) patients in each RIC-group completed ≥ 80% of sessions; median session completion was 96% (interquartile range [IQR]: 89%-100%) for once-daily and 98% (IQR: 93%-100%) for twice-daily RIC. Pain/discomfort ratings were numerically higher with twice-daily RIC (median rating/10: 4.23, IQR.0.98-4.95 vs. once-daily: 1.63, IQR:1.00-3.36, P = 0.60). No patients developed tissue/neurovascular injury or venous thrombosis. Cognitive tests neither changed nor differed significantly between groups; WMH volumes were stable (90-day change from randomization: -0.21.mL, 95% confidence interval:-0.54 to +0.13). Tumor-necrosis-factor alpha and interleukin-1b declined from baseline to 30 days, persisting at 90 days, in both groups. Focus group participants opined the device was easy to use but desired greater portability, generally favored once-daily RIC, and were open to longer treatment courses in future trials. Discussion Patients with CSVD-associated VCI adhered well to once- and twice-daily RIC, with no significant differences in safety or tolerability outcomes. We will incorporate participant feedback into device design and future efficacy trials.

items.title: Environmental microbial communities and host selection shape larval microbiomes.
items.abstract: Ocean warming is altering abiotic environments and biotic interactions experienced by marine organisms, where sensitive early developmental windows occur in biologically complex seawater communities. The impact of these interactions on developmental processes and fitness in hosts is not well understood, but likely contingent on the establishment of a host-associated microbiome. Here, we hypothesize that temperature and microbial exposure during embryogenesis influence larval microbiome assembly and host morphology. Strongylocentrotus purpuratus embryos were raised in low microbial richness (LMR) or high microbial richness (HMR) seawater at ambient (14 °C) or elevated (18 °C) temperature, then collected at 2, 4, and 6 days post-fertilization (dpf) following multiple feedings. Higher microbial diversity was observed in larvae that developed in HMR seawater when compared to LMR. Differences in relative abundances of dominant microbial families between seawater and larvae suggest some degree of host selectivity in microbiome assembly. Temperature did not strongly alter microbiome composition, but both temperature and microbial condition led to differences in larval morphology by 6 dpf, potentially due to enrichment of microbes with chemoheterotrophic functions. By linking how temperature and microbial communities interact with host development, we contribute novel insights into how early-life environmental conditions impact holobiont formation and morphology.

items.title: Artificial selection for enhanced flight propensity in an invasive species (Ceratitis capitata) reveals minimal trade-offs.
items.abstract: Enhanced flight propensity may facilitate range expansions with implications for evolutionary potential, population dynamics, and species invasions. This study investigated artificial selection for flight propensity in a highly invasive agricultural fruit pest, the Mediterranean fruit fly (Medfly), Ceratitis capitata under laboratory conditions. A selection filter was applied for 4-5 generations of C. capitata to select for the fastest (and as a reference group the most lethargic) flyers. Individuals that were able to rapidly overcome a flight barrier were termed "Flyers", while philopatric individuals were referred to as "Non-flyers." Flight propensity was quantified using flight performance measurements, whereas walking speed was used as a measurement of locomotor activity. Reproductive traits, thermal performance (i.e., chill coma recovery and heat knockdown time), and desiccation and starvation resistance were assessed for potential physiological trade-offs that may be associated with increased flight propensity. Flight performance trials showed that Flyers performed significantly better than Non-flyers after 4-5 generations of selection, with only female Flyers showing an increased body mass compared to Non-flyers. Cold stress-resistance was the only trait where Non-flyers outperformed Flyers, while thermal tolerance and fecundity traits remained similar between Flyers and Non-flyers. These findings demonstrated that it may be possible to select for enhanced flight propensity without incurring substantial performance or life-history costs. The ability to improve flight performance with minimal costs could be a key factor contributing to the success of invasive species, such as the Mediterranean fruit fly.

items.title: Partial clonality and the speed of range expansion along an environmental gradient.
items.abstract: Reproductive mode interacts in important ways with patterns of spatial adaptation, such as expansion of species' ranges along environmental gradients. Partial clonality (both asexual/clonal and sexual reproduction) characterizes a broad range of taxa, including important species that structure many terrestrial and marine ecosystems as well as many pathogens, pests, and invasives. We explore the interplay of invasion and local adaptation under partial clonality using an individual-based model, with space modeled as a unidimensional landscape of grid cells. An environmental gradient exists along the direction of expansion, such that the optimal phenotype changes in this direction. We investigate how the fraction of clonal reproduction (rc) and the association between random components of parent and clonal offspring phenotype (ρ) affect the speed of range expansion. We see slower expansion as amount of clonality (rc or ρ) increases, with a sharp drop at complete clonality (rc, ρ = 1), indicating that only a small amount of sexual reproduction suffices for partially clonal populations to show very similar behavior to purely sexual populations-in clear contrast to what has been observed for spatial adaptation across two distinct demes with differing phenotypic optima. Expansion lag load (fitness differences between core and leading-edge sub-populations) is greatest at intermediate environmental gradient steepness, with both gradual and very steep change decreasing this lag load. Thus, clonality may hinder invasion by partially clonal species across an environmental gradient; the reproductive assurance benefits of asexual reproduction may be a better explanation for clonal species expansion in such cases.

items.title: Placental Interdigitation Is Associated with Reproductive Pace across Mammals.
items.abstract: The placenta is a transient organ mainly derived from fetal tissue that is essential for establishing metabolic and immune interactions that support healthy pregnancies in eutherian mammals. Across mammals, placentas show high morphological diversity in both the degree of tissue invasiveness and in the complexity of tissue integration between maternal and fetal tissues. This variation is thought to reflect strong selective pressures on reproductive strategies, balancing maternal investment, offspring development, resource transfer, and reproductive pace. Previous studies have explored the relationship between placental morphology and mammalian life history focusing mainly on placental invasiveness and giving less attention to placental interdigitation. Here, we expand the scope of previous comparative work by analyzing 509 mammalian species to examine how three life history traits (gestation length, interbirth intervals, and relative litter mass) are associated with placental morphology. We also test whether placental morphology covaries with broader multivariate life history structure using phylogenetic principal component analyses (pPCA). We found that, relative to invasiveness, placental interdigitation was more strongly associated with reproductive timing. Labyrinthine placentas were associated with shorter gestation lengths than villous and trabecular placentas, and species with villous placentas were associated with the longest interbirth intervals. Placental invasiveness showed no association with life history variation. Neither invasiveness nor interdigitation was associated with relative litter mass. Our results suggest that, although diverse census timing may have limited the extent of our interpretation, placental interdigitation is associated with reproductive timing (gestation length and interbirth intervals), whereas neither interdigitation nor invasiveness is associated with relative litter mass, an approximate measure of offspring mass produced per reproductive event relative to adult body mass.

items.title: High Frequency Minirhizotron Observations Reveal Diel Patterns of Root Growth Under Water Stress.
items.abstract: Growth and death of vegetation control both the amount of carbon held in living biomass and much of the flow between the atmosphere and soils, the largest terrestrial carbon reservoir. However, long-term field datasets on belowground growth dynamics are rare. Knowledge is lacking on how root growth patterns relate to the environment, fluctuating carbon and water availability, and internal plant physiological control, at both seasonal and diel scales. We imaged roots in a temperate grassland using automated minirhizotrons and interpreting root length density (RLD) automatically twice a day for nine months. From winter to autumn, we always observed some root growth in individual images, but with decreasing net RLD (indicative of net turnover) becoming predominant later in the season. Roots grew day-round except during a period of about one month in spring when root growth was only in daytime. This was a period without rain, during which soil moisture depleted rapidly, but not at its driest point. We discuss potential causes for both overall and short-term growth patterns, particularly the change in drivers of growth from internal storage to new photosynthates, or limits imposed by water availability - both soil moisture and rainfall - under shifting environmental conditions.

items.title: Contact zones as natural laboratories for cryptic speciation: genetic and ecological divergence in the autopolyploid Aster amellus aggregate.
items.abstract: Polyploidy is a major driver of plant evolution and speciation. Autopolyploidy, in particular, plays a key role in the emergence of cryptic lineages that are morphologically similar yet genetically and ecologically distinct. We investigated the extent of genetic exchange and climatic differentiation between diploid (2×) and hexaploid (6×) cytotypes of Aster amellus (Asteraceae) within a narrow contact zone in Central Europe to assess whether reproductive isolation and divergence are maintained where cytotypes occur in close proximity. We implemented a spatially explicit sampling of 735 individuals from 32 adjacent diploid and hexaploid populations located 1-10 km apart. Genetic variation was analysed using nuclear microsatellite markers, and ecological divergence was quantified through hypervolume-based niche analysis. We found strong genetic differentiation between cytotypes, with hexaploids exhibiting higher genetic diversity and occupying a broader climatic space than diploids. Genetic connectivity was high within cytotypes, but sharply reduced between them, and evidence of a recent polyploidization event in one population revealed hexaploid individuals genetically close to the diploid cluster, suggesting recurrent formation of hexaploids. Our findings indicate that reproductive isolation between cytotypes remains effective even at fine spatial scales, maintaining both genetic and ecological divergence despite geographical proximity. Fine-scale sampling reveals that narrow diploid-polyploid contact zones increase the likelihood of detecting early-stage polyploid formation before such signals are obscured by drift or selection, reinforcing their role as key natural laboratories for studying cryptic autopolyploid speciation.
