items.title: Muscle power amplification may enhance sprint performance and broaden the thermal performance of the lizard Sceloporus occidentalis. II: Muscle power and series elastic element properties.
items.abstract: Skeletal muscle is reliant on the myosin ATPase enzyme to power locomotion, making muscle and locomotor performance thermally sensitive. However, muscles performance is often enhanced by elastic tendons, and the power amplification they enable is thought to increase sprint performance and its thermal robustness. The previous study suggests in vivo ankle muscle powers that exceed predicted muscle powers and may contribute to the high thermal robustness of sprint performance in S. occidentalis. Here, we directly measure gastrocnemius muscle power and its thermal sensitivity, compare this to in vivo ankle muscle power to quantify power amplification, and determine the potential for the gastrocnemius muscle-tendon unit (MTU) to store the required elastic strain energy. Peak gastrocnemius muscle power was ∼83, 156 and 371 W kg-1 at 15, 25 and 35°C with Q10 values of ∼1.9-2.4. Peak in vivo muscle power at the ankle was ∼180, 622 and 881 W kg-1, indicating a ∼2.2-, 4.1- and 2.4-fold power amplification, at 15, 25 and 35°C, respectively. The fixed-end compliance of the gastrocnemius was ∼17%, series elastic elements experienced an ∼12% strain, and the muscle fibers stored ∼17 J kg-1. Hence, this species clearly uses power amplification in sprinting at all temperatures, and the high degree of power amplification at 25°C probably increases thermal robustness of sprint performance at 25-35°C. The degree of elastic strain energy storage observed in this MTU is comparable with avian, mammalian and anuran MTUs known to store and utilize elastic strain energy and modestly amplify muscle power.

items.title: Muscle power amplification may enhance sprint performance and broaden the thermal performance of the lizard Sceloporus occidentalis. I: Sprint performance and joint powers.
items.abstract: The maintenance of locomotor performance across temperatures is critical to ectotherm fitness but is limited by the thermal sensitivity of the myosin ATPase enzyme. However, sprint performance in lizards appears more thermally robust than the muscles powering it, potentially due to power amplification by elastic tendons. To explore this, we determined the thermal sensitivity of Sceloporus occidentalis acceleration at 15-35°C, used inverse dynamics to estimate in vivo muscle powers at hindlimb joints and compared these to predicted maximum muscle powers. The Q10 of acceleration was 1.7-2.5, compared with literature Q10 values of 2-3 for muscle power. Maximum in vivo power was ∼180, 622 and 881 W kg-1 at the ankle, ∼127, 393 and 433 W kg-1 at the knee, and ∼41, 176 and 193 W kg-1 at the hip at 15°C, 25°C and 35°C, respectively. Comparison with predicted maximum muscle powers suggest amplifications of ∼2.2, 3.8 and 2.7-fold at 15°C, 25°C and 35°C at the ankle. There was little power amplification at the knee and hip except for a ∼2.4-fold amplification at the knee at 25°C; hip power appeared sub-maximal at 35°C. This is consistent with the limited presence of in-series elastic elements at the knee and, particularly, the hip. These results suggest that power amplification at the ankle is critical to the sprint performance of S. occidentalis and its thermal robustness of 25-35°C, but that there is an additional limit to sprint performance at 35°C that may contribute to the apparent thermal robustness.

items.title: The functional proteome landscape of a cosmopolitan oceanic bacterium.
items.abstract: SAR11 bacteria, the most abundant organisms in the global ocean, are an extensively studied example of streamlining, an adaptation to extremely low nutrient levels. To understand the regulation of gene function in streamlined cells, we developed a proteome map for the SAR11 type strain HTCC1062 under 13 growth conditions. We detected 95% (1284 out of 1354) of the previously predicted proteins from the HTCC1062 genome, corrected 24 predicted coding regions, and discovered 80 previously unannotated proteins, many of which had frame-shifted or overlapping reading frames. HTCC1062 cells expressed almost their entire genome (> 87.7% of predicted proteins) under all growth conditions, demonstrating that they allocate relatively little coding capacity to auxiliary functions that are deployed infrequently in response to environmental challenges. Most proteins involved in fundamental cellular processes were stable. A highly compact genome and relatively stable proteome are critical for the organization of these simple, free-living planktonic cells, providing a unique model for interpreting the cell biology of a larger number of uncultured cell types.

items.title: A sex ratio by incubation temperature reaction norm for the American alligator (Alligator mississippiensis) based on fluctuating thermal regimes.
items.abstract: Environmental conditions during embryonic development wield critical influence on organismal traits. For example, in species with temperature-dependent sex determination (TSD), the incubation temperatures an embryo experiences determines sex. Reaction norms quantifying this relationship are essential tools for predicting how climatic variability will shift population sex ratios. However, existing TSD reaction norms are derived from constant temperature laboratory conditions, leaving open the question of their applicability to natural conditions where incubation temperatures fluctuate. In this study, we developed a TSD reaction norm for the American alligator (Alligator mississippiensis) using fluctuating temperature treatments. We incubated eggs under five fluctuating temperature regimes, determined offspring sex using gonadal gene expression, and used the resulting sex ratios to fit reaction norms based on mean temperature and constant temperature equivalents (CTE). The reaction norms followed the canonical Female-Male-Female pattern of crocodilians. At lower incubation temperatures, our fluctuating-temperature reaction norms closely aligned with that derived from constant temperatures, suggesting that mean temperature and CTE statistics perform reasonably well in this range. However, at higher incubation temperatures, the range most relevant to climate warming projections, our reaction norms diverged substantially from constant temperature reaction norms with upper pivotal temperature estimates differing by up to 1.36°C. Because small thermal shifts at this critical transition can dramatically alter predicted sex ratios, these discrepancies carry real consequences for conservation forecasting. Our results underscore the importance of incorporating ecologically realistic thermal variation into TSD reaction norms and highlight the upper male-to-female transition as a priority for mechanistic study.

items.title: Parental death destabilizes wolf packs despite the benefits of larger pack size.
items.abstract: Cooperative breeding is a fundamental feature of many animal family groups. However, few studies have quantified whether variation in group size meaningfully buffers social and reproductive consequences following parental death. Using 17 years of data from a grey wolf (Canis lupus) population in Oregon, USA, we evaluated how parental death (the death of one or both parents) influenced pack dissolution, reproductive failure and pup recruitment and whether larger pack sizes mitigated these effects. Across 303 pack-years, we recorded 69 parental deaths, 39 pack dissolutions and 112 reproductive failures. Packs that experienced parental death were nearly five times more likely to dissolve (95% CI: 2.12-11.12), nearly 16 times more likely to fail reproductively (95% CI: 5.34-47.26) and recruited 66% fewer pups (95% CI: 49%-78% fewer) than packs in which both parents survived. Larger packs were associated with improved demographic outcomes overall, but these group-size benefits were insufficient to fully offset the elevated risks associated with parental death. Our results show that numerous individuals can provide generalized pack-level demographic resilience but do not functionally replace parental roles, highlighting the importance of evaluating social structure in addition to population size. By clarifying the limits of social buffering in a cooperatively breeding carnivore, this study advances understanding of how social systems respond to parental death.

items.title: Biologging and mechanistic niche modelling reveal thermal dependence of individual lizard movement patterns.
items.abstract: Assessing how variation in thermal physiology and body size influences locomotor performance under ecologically relevant conditions is essential to predicting population vulnerability to climate change. We combined fine-scale animal biologging and individual-level mechanistic niche modelling to unravel animal-environment interactions in ocellated lizards (Timon lepidus) kept in semi-natural mesocosms. We classified mobility states from accelerometer data to describe individual movement patterns. We produced continuous body temperature predictions through individual mechanistic models and used thermal performance curves (TPCs) to assess how body temperature influences locomotor performance. We further tested for evolutionary trade-offs and simulated mobility windows under warming scenarios. Our results provided high-resolution estimates of body temperature across mobility states, revealing how variation in thermal physiology is associated with movement. We found that individuals occupied different positions along a 'specialist-generalist' continuum of thermal strategies: some achieved higher locomotor performance but within narrower thermal ranges, while others displayed broader mobility windows but lower locomotor maxima. On the other hand, body size did not affect movement patterns under current climatic conditions, but warming simulations indicated that larger individuals may experience disproportionately greater increases in mobility under extreme warming. These findings demonstrate that even subtle variations in thermal physiology and body size can translate into differences in locomotor performance and mobility. By integrating physiological, behavioural and microclimatic data, our framework provides a powerful approach for predicting how climate change may reshape the spatial and temporal niches of ectotherms.

items.title: Understanding Nrf2 Function in Manganese Neurotoxicity.
items.abstract: The objective of the present review was to summarize and discuss recent findings on the effects of Mn exposure on Nrf2 signaling in the brain and its relationship with other molecular mechanisms of Mn neurotoxicity. The existing data show that Mn exposure interferes with Nrf2 signaling following a biphasic response model. Upon low-to-moderate dose or following short-term exposure, Mn activates Nrf2 signaling with subsequent upregulation of Nrf2-target antioxidant genes, which limit progression of Mn-induced oxidative stress. Evidence from Nrf2-deficient animal models support the essential role of Nrf2 in counteracting Mn-induced neuronal oxidative stress. In contrast, high-dose and/or long-term Mn exposure down-regulates Nrf2 signaling due to inhibition of SIRT1, REST1, and CYP1B1 expression, as well as upregulation of GSK-3β expression. The observed inhibition of Nrf2 signaling is associated not only with oxidative stress, but is also tightly related to Mn-induced neuroinflammation, pyroptosis, neurodegeneration, endoplasmic reticulum stress, ferroptosis, tau and amyloid-β accumulation, and dysregulated heat-shock protein expression. Although the existing data were derived from laboratory studies and environmentally irrelevant doses, it is assumed that Nrf2 signaling may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for preventing Mn neurotoxicity.

items.title: Optimizing sampling and monitoring of species interactions within Biodiversity Observation Networks.
items.abstract: Optimal monitoring strategies should be designed to efficiently monitor all essential facets of biodiversity. Yet, species interactions are often overlooked in monitoring designs compared to spatial coverage and species richness, partly due to the inherent difficulty of sampling and monitoring interactions compared to species distributions. Here, we used simulations to test the efficiency of monitoring species interactions within Biodiversity Observations Networks (BONs). We tested several methods for designing and optimizing BONs to monitor species interactions and examined efficiency when increasing the number of monitored sites. We showed that the required sampling effort is considerably higher for interactions, especially when considering that interaction realization and detection realistically depend on species abundance. Thus, expectations to monitor a relevant proportion of interactions within a BON should be lower than expectations to monitor its species. However, from a single-species perspective, optimizing monitoring designs based on a known species range proved an efficient strategy to retrieve its interactions, outperforming designs based on total species or interaction richness. Further efficiency gains required detailed knowledge of where realized interactions occurred, highlighting the need for better knowledge of where interactions are likely to take place and integration of factors influencing interaction realization, such as species abundances. Our results were consistent even when the total species range was over- or underestimated by 10%, which shows a tolerance in the precision of the information required for optimization. These findings highlight how attainable levels of information can lead to efficiency improvements when designing BONs. With the right target and optimization strategy, and readily available information, such as species ranges, we can therefore guide observation network designs to monitor species interactions as central biodiversity components.

items.title: Divergent Root and Shoot Trait Strategies Shape Competition-Facilitation Shifts Between Conspecific and Heterospecific Neighbors Under Contrasting Soil Moisture Conditions.
items.abstract: Soil moisture availability is a key driver of plant growth and competitive interactions among plant species. Trait differences among species are expected to influence competitive outcomes, with stronger competition often occurring among functionally similar species due to niche overlap. However, most studies have focused on aboveground traits, whereas belowground traits involved in water acquisition remain less explored. Here, we investigate how above- and belowground traits vary along soil moisture gradients and how they shape plant responses to intra- and interspecific competition. Seedlings of four tropical legume species were grown in a glasshouse for 30 weeks under three soil moisture levels (low, medium, and high) and three neighbor treatments: intraspecific competition, interspecific competition, and no-competition. At harvest, above- and belowground morphological and physiological traits, as well as biomass accumulation, were measured using standardized protocols. Plant performance was strongly influenced by competition and soil moisture. Intraspecific competition increased belowground traits, including specific root length, average root diameter, and root-shoot ratio, particularly under low moisture conditions, and resulted in greater belowground biomass. In contrast, interspecific competition enhanced aboveground traits, including leaf area, average leaf mass, and specific leaf area, leading to higher aboveground biomass and total biomass. Nodule number and nodule dry mass increased with soil moisture, whereas antioxidant enzyme activity was highest under low moisture. Relative interaction index analyses further showed stronger belowground competitive effects under intraspecific interactions and greater aboveground facilitative effects under interspecific interactions. These findings highlight that plant-plant interactions in tropical legumes are highly context-dependent, with neighbor identity and soil moisture together influencing competitive outcomes. Divergent below- and aboveground investment strategies reveal how plants adjust resource allocation, shaping growth performance under changing environmental conditions.

items.title: Air and Water Environmental DNA Enable Detection of a Large Terrestrial Bird: A Case Study of the Southern Cassowary (Casuarius casuarius).
items.abstract: The southern cassowary, Casuarius casuarius , is a large-bodied terrestrial frugivore that plays a critical role in tropical rainforest ecosystems but can be challenging to locate and survey using traditional methods. Across much of its range, populations are threatened by habitat loss, fragmentation and other anthropogenic pressures, and key aspects of distribution and movement remain poorly understood. Environmental DNA (eDNA) offers a non-invasive approach to monitoring elusive species, yet applications for large, mobile terrestrial vertebrates-particularly using air as a sampling medium-remain limited. Here, we develop and validate a highly sensitive, species-specific TaqMan-based eDNA assay to detect the southern cassowary and evaluate its performance using both air and water samples collected in captivity and in the field at sites of known presence. Cassowaries represent a biologically challenging test case for eDNA detection due to their mobility, low local densities and terrestrial ecology. Despite this, we demonstrate that eDNA from both air and water sources provides a practical, non-invasive tool to monitor this keystone rainforest species across landscapes where traditional surveys are logistically constrained. Importantly, this approach provides a scalable method for rapidly assessing cassowary presence, supporting landscape-scale conservation planning and management. Our results highlight the potential of airborne eDNA for detecting large terrestrial vertebrates, with broader implications for biodiversity monitoring.

items.title: Overcoming Alpine Barriers: The First Documented Case of Golden Jackal (Canis aureus) Settlement in a Subalpine Environment.
items.abstract: The golden jackal ( Canis aureus ) continues to expand across Europe, yet fine-scale behavioural data on dispersal-particularly in mountainous regions-remain scarce. Reproducing individuals are recorded further and further to the North and West of the continent, crossing major anthropogenic and natural barriers in the landscape and settling within new habitats. Since jackals are already present or at the doorstep of almost every country on the European mainland, monitoring this range expansion is of great interest to the public and policymakers. The dispersal capacity of jackals is pivotal for their current expansion across Europe. However, research on their movement patterns, particularly natal dispersal, remains limited. Here, we analysed the full dispersal trajectory of a GPS-collared subadult male originating from the Julian Alps (Slovenia). Using T-LoCoH utilisation distributions, Net Squared Displacement modelling and Bayesian movement models, we reconstructed its pre-dispersal behaviour, dispersal phase and subsequent settlement. After several initial exploratory excursions, the young male left its natal home range in mid-November 2023 and travelled a cumulative distance of 170 km (96 km straight-line distance), overcoming natural and anthropogenic barriers along the way. After 11 days, it established a stable home range in the Austrian Malta Valley, where reproduction was later confirmed in spring 2024-the first documented case of successful settlement and breeding by a golden jackal in a subalpine environment. During dispersal, the jackal's step length increased in areas with a higher aggregation index as well as at night, suggesting more extensive movement between consecutive GPS acquisitions in more homogeneous areas and during nighttime. Our study provides the first fine-scale GPS documentation of dispersal, settlement, and subsequent reproduction of a golden jackal in a European subalpine environment. It highlights how both natural and human-dominated landscapes shape movement behaviour during range expansion.

items.title: The Application of Self-Determination Theory to Short-form Video Addiction: The Roles of Psychological Needs and Intrinsic Motivations.
items.abstract: Short-form video applications are widely used worldwide. At the same time, new concerns have been raised owing to excessive and addictive short-form video use, with significant harm to health and well-being. By self-determination theory, the present study aimed to test the effects of satisfaction and frustration of three basic psychological needs (autonomy, competence, and relatedness) in relation to short-form video addiction (SVA) and evaluate the roles of the intrinsic motivations for passing time and entertainment underlying such relationships. The study included 367 Chinese TikTok users (37.1% male) aged 18 to 62 years ( M ± SD = 20.63 ± 4.40 years), who voluntarily completed an anonymous online questionnaire without compensation. All three types of need satisfaction had significant negative associations with SVA, while the three types of need frustration were significantly positively associated with SVA. Entertainment motivation significantly and negatively mediated the relationship between competence/relatedness satisfaction and SVA while significantly and positively mediating the relationship between relatedness frustration and SVA. Motivation for passing time served as a risk-enhancing mediator in the relationship between competence/relatedness frustration and SVA. Therefore, this study identified relatedness frustration and motivation for passing time as the most salient risk factors of SVA. The implications for SVA interventions that focus on psychological needs and intrinsic motivation are also discussed.

items.title: Best Practice International Guidelines on Online Communities of Aphasia Groups.
items.abstract: Purpose We aim to establish best practice guidelines for the design, facilitation, and sustainability of online support groups for people with aphasia (PWA). It explores the benefits, challenges, and psychological considerations of virtual aphasia interventions. Method The recommendations presented were developed through a collaborative consensus process by our writing team, which was informed by a comprehensive review of current literature, insights from international experts, and practical experiences across various settings. This process involved meetings held between June 2023 and April 2025, focusing on the "Community of Practice related to online aphasia support." These discussions examined the types, goals, and key features of online support groups-highlighting person-centered approaches, facilitation skills, and cultural responsiveness-and considered technological, logistical, and funding factors critical for successful implementation. Guided by principles of evidence-based practice and consensus building, the development produced practical recommendations that reflect diverse perspectives and best practices in both face-to-face and online aphasia support. Results Online aphasia support groups enhance accessibility, foster peer support, and promote social participation, contributing positively to psychological well-being. This tutorial identifies common challenges (e.g., technological barriers, engagement difficulties, and resource constraints), offering evidence-based strategies for mitigation. It underscores the importance of tailored facilitator training and sustainable funding models adapted to diverse contexts. Conclusions Online aphasia support groups are valuable tools to improve long-term communication and psychosocial outcomes for PWA. Their success depends on careful planning, skilled facilitation, and inclusive practices. Ongoing research, international collaboration, and adaptable funding strategies are vital to optimize their impact and expand access globally.

items.title: Longitudinal associations between sleep disturbance and disordered eating: the mediating role of emotion dysregulation.

A binary clinically significant disordered eating variable was created by coding participants who met criteria for present, past, or partial remission eating disorder diagnoses on the KSADS-5. items.title: Altered Formant Feedback Elicits Perceptually Detectable Changes in Vocal Femininity.
items.abstract: Purpose This study examined how cisgender (cis) men and transgender (trans) women respond to altered auditory feedback that shifted formants F1 and F2 down with a magnitude derived from empirically observed comparisons of men's and women's vocal tracts. Pairs of words produced with and without altered feedback were presented to blinded listeners to evaluate whether compensatory changes were associated with a change in perceived femininity. The goal was to investigate whether implicit adaptation to auditory feedback could serve as a strategy in gender-affirming voice training (GAVT). Method Twenty cis men and six trans women produced word strings while hearing their speech with F1 and F2 shifted down by roughly the magnitude of the average difference between men's and women's formants. Productions were acoustically measured to determine the magnitude of compensatory formant shifts directly opposing the perturbation. Tokens representing the maximum and median degree of adaptation for each participant and vowel were paired with unshifted tokens and presented to 31 blinded listeners, who were asked to select the most feminine production in each pair. Results Participants exhibited a statistically significant degree of adaptation offsetting the perturbation, averaging 27% of the imposed shift for cis men and 35% for trans women. Listeners selected adapted tokens as "more feminine" with significantly above-chance frequency, roughly 63% of the time. Conclusions Altered auditory feedback elicited measurable, perceptually detectable changes in resonance associated with gendered voice characteristics. These findings suggest that implicit adaptation to altered feedback could complement explicit resonance training in GAVT, although further study of the acceptability of this method to gender-diverse speakers is essential. items.title: It Happened, It's Not My Fault, and I Can Trust Again": Compassionate Imagery to Enhance Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Complex PTSD.
items.abstract: Imagery is a central part of Compassion-Focused Therapy (CFT), which teaches individuals to create affiliative motives and emotions for oneself and others in order to recover from the multiple sequelae of trauma including shame, guilt and fear of trusting others. This case illustration describes the use of imagery during an ongoing 15-month intervention based on CFT and trauma-focused CBT for Sam, a 35-year old male with CPTSD and OCD. Pre-therapy, symptoms included dissociation, nightmares and flashbacks, doubting the abuse, hyperarousal, fear of relying on others and aggressive obsessions. A series of compassionate imagery techniques were used to reduce self-doubt, self-blame, suppressed anger, disgust and an ongoing sense of threat. Large changes were observed in SUDs for trauma memories and dissociation frequency, as well as in conviction in positive beliefs about self and others. PTSD symptoms reduced from severe to non-clinical. This illustrates the potential of CFT to tackle the rational-emotional divide, whereby cognitive techniques often fail to reduce distress underpinned by early traumatic memories.

items.title: Age-Related Differences in Gait Parameters and Their Association With Fall Risk in Older Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: BackgroundFalls are a major cause of morbidity and functional decline among older adults, yet early gait-based markers of fall risk remain unclear.ObjectiveTo examine age-related differences in spatiotemporal gait parameters and their associations with fall risk among older adults.MethodsTwo hundred participants aged 65 years or older were classified into four age groups and two fall-risk levels using a standardized Fall Risk Assessment. Gait parameters were measured with the IB-GAIT system.ResultsWith increasing age, stride length and walking speed decreased, while stance and double support phases increased (ptrend < 0.001). High-risk individuals showed shorter stride lengths, slower walking speeds, and longer stance phases than low-risk counterparts (p < 0.05). Height-adjusted stride length correlated with Fall Risk Assessment components (r = 0.36, p < 0.001), and those in the shortest quartile had over eightfold higher odds of high fall risk.ConclusionHeight-adjusted stride length indicates fall risk.

items.title: Psychiatric, Sociodemographic, and Community Belonging Correlates of Suicidal Ideation in Canada: Findings from the 2022 Mental Health and Access to Care Survey.
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo estimate the prevalence of suicidal ideation among Canadians, identify psychiatric and sociodemographic correlates of past-12-month ideation and its association with community belonging, and compare the out-of-fold predictive performance of logistic regression and random forest models.MethodWe analyzed the nationally representative 2022 Mental Health and Access to Care Survey (analytic n = 8,080; weighted population = 25,828,546). Survey-weighted logistic and multinomial regression used the master weight with 1,000 Fay-adjusted bootstrap replicate weights. Five-fold nested cross-validation compared a sociodemographic-plus-psychiatric logistic model, the same model with belonging added, and a random forest, using out-of-fold discrimination, average precision, Brier scores, and grouped permutation importance.ResultsPast-12-month suicidal ideation was reported by 3.4% (95% CI, 2.9% to 3.9%) and lifetime-only ideation by 7.4% (95% confidence interval (CI), 6.7% to 8.2%). Independent correlates of past-12-month ideation were major depressive episode (MDE) (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 5.80; 95% CI, 3.61 to 9.33), very weak community belonging (aOR = 3.64; 95% CI, 1.88 to 7.04), generalized anxiety disorder (aOR = 2.65; 95% CI, 1.56 to 4.50), bipolar disorder (aOR = 2.43; 95% CI, 1.27 to 4.66), and separation/divorce (aOR = 2.25; 95% CI, 1.22 to 4.17). Adjusted probability rose from 2.0% at very strong to 6.0% at very weak belonging. No interaction was supported. Adding belonging did not improve discrimination (area under the curve (AUC), 0.823 vs. 0.823; difference = 0.000; 95% CI, -0.011 to 0.011); the random forest AUC was 0.843 (difference = 0.020; 95% CI, 0.004 to 0.038).ConclusionsPsychiatric morbidity, separation/divorce, younger age, and very weak community belonging were associated with past-12-month suicidal ideation. Community belonging was independently associated but did not improve cross-validated discrimination, whereas MDE was the most robust correlate.

items.title: Temporal lobe cortical thickness and cognition in paediatric cancer survivors previously treated with chemotherapy.
items.abstract: Long-term neurocognitive outcomes in paediatric cancer survivors treated with chemotherapy remain incompletely characterized, particularly in relation to cortical structure. Prior neuroimaging studies have included limited representation of racial and ethnic minority survivors. We analysed temporal lobe cortical thickness and cognition in paediatric cancer survivors treated with chemotherapy (n = 21; 8-25 years post-chemotherapy; aged 15-34 years) and age-matched controls (n = 21). Cognition was assessed using National Institute of Health (NIH) Toolbox scores. Cortical thickness of nine bilateral temporal regions was derived from T1-weighted 3T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) using FreeSurfer. Group differences and brain-cognition associations were analysed using adjusted regression models with false discovery rate correction. Survivors scored lower on crystallized (p < 0.001), fluid (p = 0.013) and total cognition scores (p = 0.001). They showed reduced temporal lobe cortical thickness (2.62 ± 0.13 vs. 2.74 ± 0.11 mm; p = 0.001), with reductions in seven subregions. Greater thickness was associated with better cognitive performance in 10 of 27 associations, most prominently for crystallized cognition. Fully corrected T-score sensitivity analyses showed crystallized cognition remained lower in survivors (p = 0.044). Paediatric cancer survivors previously treated with chemotherapy showed reduced temporal lobe cortical thickness, which was associated with worse crystallized cognition, suggesting a potential structure-function association.

items.title: Changes in preferred e-cigarette flavor, nicotine concentration, wattage and air valve settings and cigarette consumption during a switching trial.
items.abstract: Aims To characterize changes in preferred e-cigarette (EC) flavor, nicotine concentration, wattage and air valve openness over 12 weeks among adults who smoke and are attempting to switch to ECs, and examine whether these changes are associated with cigarettes smoked per day (CPD). Design Secondary analysis of two arms of a three-arm randomized controlled trial (NCT03113136). Setting Two Midwestern United States cities. Participants 265 adults uninterested in quitting smoking (38% male, 62% female, mean age 40.0 years, 83% white, mean 17 CPD), randomized to lower-wattage EC (n = 132) or higher-wattage EC (n = 133). Measurements Preferred EC flavor (tobacco/tobacco blend, menthol, fruit/sweet), nicotine concentration, wattage, air valve openness (higher-wattage EC only) and CPD were assessed at baseline, 1-week, 4-week, 8-week and 12-week follow-ups. Results Over 12 weeks, mean CPD decreased by approximately 10 cigarettes, from 16.7 to 6.6 in the lower-wattage group and from 17.4 to 7.0 in the higher-wattage group. Most participants preferred fruit/sweet flavors (58.2% at week 12). Throughout the study, participants preferred nicotine concentrations of 12 mg/ml in the lower-wattage group and 6 mg/ml in the higher-wattage group. Preferred nicotine concentrations generally decreased from baseline to week 12 for both groups, though the decrease was statistically significant only in the lower-wattage group. In the higher-wattage group, preferred wattage and air valve openness generally increased from baseline to week 12, with a statistically significant increase observed only for wattage from baseline to week 8 (23.22 W to 27.07 W). In the lower-wattage group, preferred EC settings were not associated with CPD at follow-ups. In the higher-wattage group, menthol flavor preference (vs. tobacco) and higher nicotine concentrations were associated with CPD reductions at follow-ups. Summary Among adults who smoke cigarettes and are switching to e-cigarettes, preferences for e-cigarette settings (flavor, nicotine concentration, wattage and air valve openness) did not change substantially over the first 12 weeks of use. Flavors and nicotine concentration options may support smoking reduction in adults who transition to e-cigarettes.

items.title: Lethal Means and Precipitating Circumstances in Transgender Youth Suicide Mortality.
items.abstract: Purpose Transgender youth experience disproportionately high rates of suicidality, yet little is known about suicide mortality in this population. We characterized suicide lethal methods and precipitating circumstances among transgender youth and compared these factors with matched youth decedents not identified as transgender. Methods This secondary analysis used National Violent Death Reporting System data from 2003 to 2021. The sample included suicide decedents aged 10-24 years identified as transgender ( n = 384) and matched decedents not identified as transgender ( n = 1119). Multinomial and logistic regression models examined differences in lethal means and precipitating circumstances by transgender status. Results The sample included 1503 decedents (mean [standard deviation] age, 18.97 [3.40] years; 78.3% White). Among transgender youth, the most common suicide methods were hanging, strangulation, or suffocation (49.2%), firearm (24.0%), and drug or poison ingestion (18.2%). Compared with decedents not identified as transgender, transgender youth had higher odds of suicide by drug or poison ingestion, hanging, strangulation, or suffocation, and other methods relative to firearm suicide. Transgender youth also had higher odds of multiple mental health diagnoses, prior suicide attempts, child abuse, and disclosure of suicidal intent to a health care worker. Conclusion Transgender youth who died by suicide had distinct patterns of lethal methods and precipitating circumstances, including greater mental health burden and lower likelihood of firearm suicide. These findings highlight the need for tailored suicide prevention strategies and improved gender identity ascertainment in mortality surveillance systems.

items.title: Hematological and biochemical responses to three doses of caffeine during the CrossFit® workout: a randomized, double-blind, crossover trial.
items.abstract: Background This study investigated the effects of three doses of caffeine (CAF) on hematological and biochemical responses during the CrossFit® workout, a protocol known to induce significant physiological fluctuations. Methods In a randomized, double-blind, placebo ( PLA )-controlled crossover trial, 26 moderately trained CrossFit® athletes received acute doses of 3, 6, or 9 mg CAF /kg body mass (BM) , or a PLA, 70 min before a 17-min CrossFit® workout. Results While exercise was the predominant driver of hematological changes, with no CAF-specific modulation of blood cell indices, significant treatment × time point interactions were observed solely for glucose concentration. Specifically, MEDIUM (6 mg CAF /kg BM ) and HIGH (9 mg CAF /kg BM ) CAF doses produced significantly greater post-exercise glucose elevations compared to baseline and PLA visits. Phosphates concentrations increased over time, particularly post-exercise, with no treatment effect retained after excluding baseline visit in the sensitivity analysis. Calcium level dynamics were influenced by temporal factors rather than CAF, and magnesium concentration remained stable. Conclusions These findings suggest that acute CAF ingestion selectively influences post-exercise glucose responses during the CrossFit ® workout, whereas hematological variables and most biochemical markers remain unaffected. Significant post-exercise glucose elevations were observed following the 6 and 9 mg CAF /kg BM conditions compared with baseline and PLA visits , while serum mineral concentrations remained largely stable across treatments. Clinical trials registration NCT03822663.

items.title: Focus on the building, not the blocks.
items.abstract: Objectives Difficulty with word finding is a pervasive symptom in aphasia and a common target of treatment. This review explored whether therapy-induced naming gains induce improvements to everyday (naturalistic) communication. Methods Online databases were searched for naming interventions that also assessed discourse or functional communication, and for studies of therapies that directly treated them. Results Among the studies that found word production gains following therapy, only about half found that the gains generalized to improved discourse or functional communication. However, discourse and functional communication can be improved by therapies that target them, and often improve word finding as well. Conclusions Generalization of rehabilitation is complex and difficult to achieve. If the therapeutic goal in aphasia is to improve everyday communication, then intervention research needs to shift focus from "building blocks" like word production to the building of discourse and functional communication.

items.title: Psychopathological and neuropsychological sequelae in children victimised by intimate partner violence: a clinical case series.
items.abstract: Background: Childhood exposure to intimate partner violence against women (IPVAW) is recognised as a form of maltreatment with lasting emotional, cognitive, and neurobiological consequences. Despite evidence of disruptions in executive functioning, attention, and memory, clinical case-based research remains scarce, particularly during middle childhood. Objective: This study examined psychopathological and neuropsychological sequelae of IPVAW - including witnessing violence and direct psychological, physical, and/or sexual abuse - through a clinical case series. Method: Four children aged 5-9 with documented IPVAW exposure underwent comprehensive clinical and neuropsychological assessment. Results: All children showed significant internalising symptoms, emotional dysregulation, and trauma-related distress. Cognitive profiles revealed selective impairments, especially in executive functioning, attention, and processing speed, while general intelligence was preserved. Greater exposure severity and polyvictimization were associated with more complex symptom patterns. Conclusions: IPVAW exposure is linked to pervasive emotional and cognitive difficulties. Findings underscore the need for early, multidimensional assessments and targeted interventions addressing both psychopathology and neuropsychological consequences.

items.title: Silent scars: psychopathology networks across cumulative childhood trauma exposure and the role of shame about eating.
items.abstract: Background: Childhood trauma is associated with eating disorder (ED) psychopathology and broader transdiagnostic symptoms, yet the role of shame about eating remains overlooked. This study examined psychopathology networks across cumulative childhood trauma exposure, focusing on internal and external shame about eating. Methods: A sample of 624 Romanian adults from the community completed self-report measures of childhood trauma, EDs, shame about eating, mentalisation, alexithymia, post-traumatic stress, depression, anxiety, insomnia, dissociative experiences, and psychotic-like experiences. Participants were grouped according to whether they reported no moderate-to-severe trauma, one trauma domain, or multiple trauma domains. Networks were estimated using Spearman correlations and EBICglasso regularisation. Community structure, expected influence, bridge expected influence, and network comparison analyses were conducted. Results: Across groups, shame about eating was embedded within ED psychopathology. Internal shame was most central in the multiple-domain trauma network, where it showed the highest expected influence and was more central than in the no-trauma network. Interoceptive deficits, PTSD, personal alienation, depression, and alexithymia also showed high centrality and bridge centrality. The multiple-domain network showed a distinct dissociative and psychotic-like experiences community. Conclusion: Shame about eating represents an important but under-recognised component of ED psychopathology, particularly in the context of cumulative childhood trauma exposure, where it shows a distinctive pattern of associations with ED behaviours and other mental health symptoms.

items.title: Diversity of social interactions is related to higher emodiversity among older adults.
items.abstract: Objectives Variability in the emotions that people experience in daily life (emodiversity) is often related to better physical and mental health. However, it is unclear how the diversity of emotional experiences is related to daily interactions in old age. This study examined the social context of diversity in emotions among older adults. Methods In the Swedish Adoption Twin Study of Aging, participants aged 62+ ( N = 144) completed a daily diary for six days, reporting their positive and negative emotions and social interactions with individuals of varying levels of closeness. Results Higher diversity of social contacts across levels of closeness (sociodiversity) was related to higher positive emodiversity. The association of sociodiversity with negative emodiversity was moderated by age. Among adults of older ages, higher sociodiversity was related to lower negative emodiversity. Meeting people from the middle circle of closeness ('close' but not 'very close' ties) was also related to higher positive emodiversity. An interaction with age showed that young-old adults who met close ties experienced higher negative emodiversity. Discussion More sociodiversity in daily interactions is related to higher positive emodiversity. However, the links between social ties and negative emodiversity may differ by age.

items.title: Associations between ADHD behavior and attachment (in)security in middle childhood: A longitudinal study.
items.abstract: Research has consistently suggested an association between ADHD behavior and insecure attachment, yet longitudinal data in middle childhood are largely absent. In particular, the directionality of this association and the role of oppositional defiant disorder (ODD) behavior remain unclear. This longitudinal study therefore examined these links across three annual waves in a Western-European community sample. Data were available for 614 children at Wave 1 (Mage = 10.28, SD = 0.58, range 9-12; 44% boys, 54% girls), 470 at Wave 2 (Mage = 10.28, SD = 0.61, range 10-13; 44% boys, 54% girls), and 385 at Wave 3 (Mage = 12.01, SD = 0.58, range 10-14; 45% boys, 54% girls). ADHD and ODD behavior were rated by mothers using the Child Behavior Checklist; children's attachment was assessed through both explicit (questionnaires) and implicit (secure base script knowledge) measures. Random Intercept Cross‑Lagged Panel Models revealed stable small to moderate between‑child associations between ADHD behavior and attachment (in)security ( β = -0.550 to 0.367), which largely remained significant after controlling for ODD behavior ( β = -0.517 to 0.295). Cross‑lagged effects, reflecting prospective within-child processes, were mostly non‑significant, providing little evidence for bidirectional associations in middle childhood.

items.title: Nutritional transition among women in Bangladesh: analysis of eight waves of population-level data from 1996 to 2022.
items.abstract: Objective To examine trends and determinants of women's nutritional status over the last two decades in Bangladesh, using BMI distribution and BMI-based categories of underweight and overweight/obesity. Design We analysed women's data from the Bangladesh Demographic Health Surveys, conducted between 1996 and 2022. Sociodemographic characteristics, changes in BMI distribution and underweight and overweight prevalence were estimated at national and urban-rural levels. Associated factors were identified using multilevel mixed-effect logistic regression, with survey year as a random intercept. Multinomial regressions were used for the individual survey waves. Setting Nationally representative cross-sectional survey. Participants 90 510 reproductive-aged women. Results There is an epidemiological transition from underweight to overweight by approximately 5 kg/m 2 over the period. The prevalence of underweight women declined by 41·34 %, while overweight/obesity increased by 33·62 %. For urban-rural disparities, the prevalence of underweight was consistently higher among rural women, whereas overweight was more common among urban women. Increased age and higher education had higher odds of being overweight/obese and relatively higher socio-economic status had higher odds of being overweight and lower odds of being underweight. Access to television had mostly higher odds of being overweight. Age, education, socio-economic status and watching television showed consistent risks over time, while other factors showed inconsistent risks at different survey times. Conclusions There was an epidemiological transition in BMI, with a declining trend in underweight and a substantial increase in overweight. Targeted interventions are needed to tackle the persistent undernutrition in rural areas and the rapidly escalating epidemic of overweight/obesity, particularly in urban settings.

items.title: "Staffroom Gist," Institutional Betrayal, and the Paradoxical Role of Schools in Adolescent Suicidal Behavior in Lagos, Nigeria.
items.abstract: Background: Schools are increasingly positioned as platforms for adolescent suicide prevention in low- and middle-income countries, yet institutional cultures may also inhibit disclosure. In Nigerian public secondary schools, punitive discipline, public academic comparison, bullying, and limited counseling provision may interact with stigma and concerns about confidentiality. Aims : To examine how school cultures, confidentiality practices, and institutional trust shape adolescents' willingness to disclose emotional distress and suicidal behavior in school-linked contexts in Lagos, Nigeria, and to identify conditions for safer school-linked prevention. Method: Four focus group discussions were conducted with 32 participants: adolescents, parents and caregivers, teachers and school staff, and child and adolescent mental health professionals. Participants were recruited through ten public secondary schools and three child and adolescent mental health clinics. Audio-recordings were transcribed, translated where necessary, deidentified, and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis informed by socioecological and stigma frameworks. Results: Participants described schools as institutions that could amplify or buffer distress. "Staffroom gist" referred to the informal circulation of students' private disclosures among staff and was associated with anticipated stigma, loss of trust, and pre-emptive silence. Academic shaming, punitive discipline, bullying, and public comparison were described as risk-amplifying, whereas relationally safe adults, credible confidentiality, external partnerships, and functional welfare pathways were viewed as protective. Participants also identified a gap between staff capacity to recognize distress and their ability to respond or refer effectively. Limitations: The findings derive from a purposively selected urban sample and one focus group per stakeholder category. Group discussions may also have constrained disclosure of highly sensitive experiences. Conclusion: School-linked suicide prevention may depend as much on institutional trust, confidentiality, disciplinary culture, and referral capacity as on staff knowledge and case recognition.

items.title: Compassion Fatigue in Emergency Department Nurses: A Cross-Sectional Evaluation of Predictive Models.
items.abstract: Compassion fatigue (CF) is a potential risk for Emergency Department (ED) nurses when workload increases, they experience repeated exposure to trauma or have a long-term emotional burden. A cross-sectional study was conducted to explore the connection between workload, trauma exposure, coping, and compassion satisfaction, and to assess the performance of logistic regression, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine for internal binary classification. The sample included 150 full-time registered ED nurses from three tertiary hospitals, who completed a structured self-administered questionnaire. The analyses encompassed descriptive statistics, group comparisons, multiple linear regression, train-test split (80:20), and stratified five-fold cross-validation. The relationships between workload and trauma exposure were positive (r = 0.75 and r = 0.62, respectively), while the relationships between coping mechanisms and compassion satisfaction were negative (r = -0.52 and r = -0.60, respectively) with CF. The four-predictor regression model explained most of the variance in CF (adjusted R 2 = 0.852), with coping and compassion satisfaction being the strongest negative predictors (β = -0.25; β = -0.35), and trauma exposure and workload being the strongest positive predictors (β = 0.32; β = 0.42). Random Forest outperformed Support Vector Machine (accuracy 83%, ROC-AUC 0.83) and logistic regression (accuracy 80%, ROC-AUC 0.80) in terms of internal classification (accuracy 85%, precision 82%, recall 80%, F1-score 81%, ROC-AUC 0.84). These findings suggest that the following interventions can be used to reduce compassion fatigue among ED nurses: workload management, trauma-informed support, coping, and compassion satisfaction.

items.title: "Stuck in this loop": A qualitative study examining the impact of housing services bureaucracy interactions on people experiencing homelessness who use drugs.
items.abstract: The population of people experiencing homelessness (PEH) across the United States continues to grow as affordable housing stock for low-income renters becomes less available and government-led efforts to increase housing stock and provide subsidized housing lag. A range of community, non-profit, and government organizations have responded to this growth in the population of PEH, alongside the ongoing drug overdose crisis, using a range of both paternalistic and punitive approaches. These state-controlled, as well as public and private non-profit, social services bureaucracies involved in poverty governance have become increasingly hard to navigate and less capable of providing rapid, high-quality aid. This study examines the impact of interactions with this system on PEH who use drugs in Los Angeles County (LAC). Ethnographic participant observation was conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic, between February 2021 and March 2023, at four encampments of PEH in LAC. Semi-structured interviews with 30 PEH who use drugs were also conducted from October 2022 to March 2023. Interviewees described deeply strained interactions with housing and case management social services agents, agencies, and related non-profits that provide these services. They indicated consistent frustration at seeming bureaucratic unpredictability, conflicting and inflexible scheduling, and perceived mistreatment and blame for their situations. The cumulative effect of these interactions on participants and those observed was to diminish feelings of ontological security-defined as social and material constancy, stability of routines, and trust in one's environment-leaving them feeling stuck and with limited agency over their housing trajectories. These outcomes-frustration, mistreatment, and psychological and material insecurity-are situated within a services environment rife with underfunding, employee burnout and turnover, and state failure to adequately resource and monitor agencies. Our results indicate that structural changes to service provision are necessary to reduce worker turnover, provide social stability, and provide autonomy, respect, and flexibility to PEH who use drugs to strengthen ontological security and prevent further harm.

items.title: AbLWR: A Context-Aware Listwise Ranking Framework for Antibody-Antigen Binding Affinity Prediction via Positive-Unlabeled Learning.
items.abstract: Accurate prediction of antibody-antigen binding affinity is fundamental to therapeutic design and the rapid response to evolving pathogens. However, current computational approaches predominantly formulate this as a point-wise regression task. This paradigm struggles to discriminate subtle affinity differences among highly homologous variants and lacks the global context necessary to effectively prioritize top-tier candidates. Furthermore, the field is severely constrained by label sparsity. Although sequence data is abundant, experimentally verified affinities are scarce, leaving a massive pool of unverified antibody-antigen structural interactions unexploited by standard supervised paradigms. We propose AbLWR (Antibody-antigen binding affinity Listwise Ranking), a novel framework that reformulates the conventional affinity regression task as a listwise ranking problem to directly optimize candidate prioritization. To mitigate label sparsity, AbLWR incorporates a Positive-Unlabeled (PU) learning mechanism, leveraging a dual-level contrastive objective and meta-optimized label refinement to distill robust structural representations from vast unlabeled data. To accommodate antigenic variation, we employ a homologous antigen sampling strategy coupled with a Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) module, which explicitly models inter-sample dependencies within training lists to capture subtle affinity nuances. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that AbLWR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art sequence-, structure-, and complex-based baselines. It improves the Full Rank Accuracy (FRA) by approximately 8% compared to the strongest baseline in randomized cross-validation, and exhibits strong robustness in out-of-distribution scenarios involving distinct antigen and antibody clusters. Case studies on Influenza Viruses and Human Interleukin-33 further validate its practical utility. Specifically, AbLWR successfully tracks affinity drops caused by antigenic drift and immediately captures optimal binders in simulated wet-lab screening. Source code and datasets are freely available at https://github.com/Josie-xufan/AbLWR. Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

items.title: A global genomic analysis of Streptococcus equi subsp. z ooepidemicus reveals clade-specific pathogenic and antimicrobial resistance profiles with several mobile genetic elements as key adaptive drivers.
items.abstract: Streptococcus equi subsp. zooepidemicus (S. zooepidemicus) is a zoonotic pathogen affecting various mammals, yet its genomic epidemiology remains poorly understood. To address this, we analyzed 428 S. zooepidemicus strains from six countries (1993-2024). The whole-genome single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) revealed four clades, with genetic diversity driven by lineage rather than host species or geographic origin. The findings support the conclusion that S. zooepidemicus is a host generalist, with horses serving as the primary host. The identified virulence-associated genes (VAGs) showed clade-specific distribution patterns: clade 1 lacked adherence factor genes srtC.2/3/4, clade 2 was enriched for the IgG-degrading enzyme gene ideZ, and clade 4 was enriched for a specific allele of the virulence-associated coupling protein gene virD4. Antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) were detected in 18.2% of strains, and no multidrug resistance was found. ARG prevalence was associated with clade 4, with tetracycline resistance being the most common. Mobile genetic elements (MGEs) are pivotal in shaping the accessory genome profiles: prophages function as the primary carriers of exotoxin genes, while integrative and conjugative elements (ICEs) serve as the main vehicles for ARGs. Notably, the co-localization of the invasion-associated virD4 allele and ARGs was identified on ICESz1, predominantly in clade 4 isolates. In conclusion, the pathogenic potential and resistance profiles of S. zooepidemicus are shaped by specific evolutionary lineages driven by MGEs. These elements act not only as genetic cargo but also as drivers that provide the conjugative machinery to co-disseminate virulence and resistance traits, accelerating the evolution of zoonotic lineages.IMPORTANCES. zooepidemicus is an opportunistic pathogen capable of infecting a wide range of hosts, including humans, often causing severe diseases. This study provides a framework for understanding the evolution of S. zooepidemicus, highlighting that its pathogenic potential and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) profiles are shaped by specific MGE-driven evolutionary lineages. The co-localization of the invasion-associated virD4 allele and ARGs on ICEs indicates that these elements provide both the pathogenic advantage and the conjugative machinery required for horizontal spread in S. zooepidemicus. This suggests that antibiotic selection can promote the transmission of virulent S. zooepidemicus lineages. These findings underscore the need for integrated surveillance strategies to monitor both virulence and AMR traits in S. zooepidemicus within equine populations to benefit public health.

items.title: A plasmid-encoded H-NS protein selectively binds its own plasmid.
items.abstract: H-NS is an abundant nucleoid-associated protein found in Enterobacterales species. Some conjugative plasmids encode H-NS homologs, which are thought to facilitate plasmid maintenance and reduce the fitness costs associated with plasmid carriage. Here, we characterize HppXCROD2, an H-NS homolog encoded by the IncX4 plasmid pCROD2 of Citrobacter rodentium. Our data indicate that HppXCROD2 has a strong preference for binding pCROD2 over the chromosome, or other plasmids. By contrast, chromosomally encoded H-NS displays no preference for plasmid sequence. When expressed from a heterologous plasmid in Escherichia coli, HppXCROD2 showed similar DNA-sequence preference to chromosomally encoded H-NS. Moreover, HppXCROD2 binding to a sequence from pCROD2 was much lower when that sequence was cloned in a laboratory plasmid. Thus, HppXCROD2 preferentially binds DNA in the context of the plasmid where it is encoded, a phenomenon we term "cognate plasmid specificity." We propose that cognate plasmid specificity occurs through recognition of plasmid-specific DNA topology generated by plasmid-encoded topoisomerases. Cognate plasmid specificity may insulate regulation of plasmid genes from the effects of host DNA, while minimizing disruption of host chromosome regulation due to plasmid carriage.IMPORTANCEMany bacteria carry conjugative plasmids, mobile DNA molecules that spread traits such as antibiotic resistance. Some conjugative plasmids encode proteins related to the bacterial DNA-binding protein H-NS. We show that an H-NS-like protein from the IncX4 plasmid pCROD2 binds almost exclusively to the plasmid from which it originates, while largely ignoring the host chromosome. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism that allows plasmids to regulate their own genes with high specificity while minimizing interference with host gene expression.

items.title: Association of Changes in Game Pitch Count, Pitching Velocity, and Arm Injuries in Collegiate Pitchers.
items.abstract: Baseball pitchers experience a high rate of shoulder and elbow injuries. While there have been several factors associated with arm injuries among pitchers, pitch volume and pitch velocity have garnered a great deal of attention. The associations among pitch counts, pitch velocity, and arm injury have not been well studied. To assess the association between changes in game pitch count and arm injuries in collegiate baseball pitchers over 1 summer season. The secondary aim was to assess the association between mean in-game fastball pitch velocity and arm injuries in the same baseball pitchers. Cohort study; Level of evidence, 2. Collegiate pitchers were prospectively followed throughout the summer season for game pitch count, pitch velocity, and arm injuries. Bayesian joint models, including time-to-event Cox regressions and multilevel mixed effects regressions, were performed to assess the associations of interest, while competing risks of release and/or retirement were controlled for. Nonlinear relationships were modeled using natural splines. Change in pitch count and pitch velocity was modeled by the change in each pitcher's mean seasonal pitch count or pitch velocity. A total of 187 pitchers were included in this study and followed for a total of 9890 baseball exposure days. A total of 22 pitchers (12%; 95% CI, 7.5%-17.2%) experienced an arm injury, and 4 pitchers (2%; 95% CI, 0.6%-5.4%) were released, voluntarily retired, or reached their innings limit for the season. There was a nonlinear (parabolic shape) positive association of an increased change in pitch count as compared with the pitcher's mean pitch count and arm injuries. Additionally, there was a nonlinear (parabolic shape) positive association between arm injury hazard and a decrease in fastball pitch velocity when compared with the pitcher's mean fastball pitch velocity. There was an increased risk for shoulder and elbow injuries with an increase in pitch count as compared with a pitcher's mean pitch count over pitch appearances. Additionally, there was an association between arm injuries and decreased pitch velocity as compared with a pitcher's mean pitch velocity.

items.title: What Are the Consequences of Suicide-Related Stigma and How Do We Reduce It? Reflections From Those With Lived Experience.
items.abstract: Background: Suicide-related stigma is an under-researched risk factor for suicide and evidence for interventions specifically designed to reduce suicide-related stigma remains limited. Aims: This study aims to understand the consequences of suicide-related stigma and how it can be reduced. Methods: Thirty adults in Scotland with experience of suicidal thoughts/attempt(s) in the past five years were interviewed in person, by phone, or online via Zoom. Participants were aged 18 to 71 years (M = 28.7 years), 70% were female, and 87% were White. The interviews were analyzed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis. Results: Two themes captured the impact of suicide-related stigma: negative consequences and no impact. Two themes addressed reducing stigma: education and open conversations. These themes represent that within our sample, suicide-related stigma was associated with poor mental health, and it can act as a barrier to help seeking among those who experience suicidal thoughts and attempt(s). Promoting awareness among the public, including having open conversations surrounding suicide were suggested as potential ways to reduce suicide-related stigma. Promoting awareness among the public was also considered to potentially increase help seeking and support for those with suicidal thoughts and decrease suicidal behavior. Limitations: Individuals experiencing high levels of suicide-related stigma may have chosen not to take part in research of this kind. Given that one author conducted all 30 interviews, interpretative biases as a result of working within the suicide prevention and suicide-related stigma field could have been present. Conclusions: The findings of this study could be considered in the development of policy and prevention strategies related to suicide.

items.title: Physical activity during pregnancy and gestational weight gain among nulliparous women: Secondary analysis of the Nulliparous Pregnancy Outcomes Study: Monitoring Mothers-To-Be.
items.abstract: This study examines the longitudinal association between leisure-time physical activity during pregnancy and gestational weight gain (GWG) among nulliparous women. We analyzed data from 8146 nulliparous women enrolled in the Nulliparous Pregnancy Outcomes Study: Monitoring Mothers-To-Be (nuMoM2b). Physical activity was assessed at three visits using questionnaires and categorized by weekly metabolic equivalent (MET)-hours and adherence to guidelines. GWG was evaluated as the rate of weight gain during successive gestational periods and as gain at or above the 75th percentile. Multivariable regression models adjusted for demographic, lifestyle, dietary, and pregnancy-related factors were used to examine overall and time-dependent associations. Women with consistently higher physical activity levels experienced a faster rate of GWG during early pregnancy but a slower rate during later pregnancy. Compared with women reporting <7.5 MET hours/week, those reporting ≥21 MET hours/week had a greater early pregnancy rate of GWG (adjusted mean difference 0.032 kg/week, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.009 to 0.056) but a slower later pregnancy rate (-0.026 kg/week, -0.053 to 0.000). Women who consistently met physical activity guidelines were less likely to have GWG at or above the 75th percentile before delivery (adjusted risk ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.78 to 0.98). Time-updated analyses further showed that higher physical activity during mid-pregnancy was associated with a slower subsequent rate of GWG. Leisure-time physical activity was associated with GWG in a stage-specific manner. These findings highlight the importance of considering gestational timing when evaluating the effects of physical activity on maternal weight gain and support continued promotion of physical activity throughout pregnancy.

items.title: Tobacco Control Policies and Tooth Loss: A Difference-in-Differences Study.
items.abstract: This study estimated the effects of state cigarette taxes, retail cigarette prices, and indoor smoking bans on smoking behavior and tooth loss among US adults. State policy data were merged with individual data from 15 cycles of the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (1995-2012; N = 3,840,519). Covariate-adjusted 2-way fixed effects linear and Poisson models estimated risk differences and risk ratios for contemporaneous and cumulative (10-y average) exposures, complemented by heterogeneity-robust difference-in-differences estimators; the parallel trends assumption was assessed empirically and with causal diagrams. A $1.00 increase in the combined cigarette tax reduced current smoking by 0.35 percentage points (95% CI: -0.56, -0.13) and increased quitting by 0.51 percentage points (95% CI: 0.19, 0.82); the smoking reduction persisted under sustained exposure (10-y average tax: -0.47 percentage points; 95% CI: -0.95, 0.01), and retail prices showed similar effects. In contrast, taxes and prices showed no robust effect on tooth loss. Complete edentulism was unrelated to taxes in every covariate-adjusted specification (current-year tax: 0.08 percentage points; 95% CI: -0.14, 0.31), and loss of ≥6 teeth showed only a weak, statistically nonsignificant protective association that was strongest for cumulative exposure (10-y average tax: -0.44 percentage points; 95% CI: -1.17, 0.30). Indoor smoking bans (restaurant and mall/grocery) were not associated with lower smoking or less tooth loss; point estimates were small and several were positive (e.g., restaurant ban and current smoking: +0.11 percentage points; 95% CI: -0.34, 0.55), and the mall/grocery ban failed a negative control test. Cigarette taxation and pricing remain powerful levers for reducing smoking, but a population-level benefit for tooth loss could not be demonstrated within this 18-y window, and indoor smoking bans showed no robust effect on either outcome; the suggestive association between sustained tax exposure and severe tooth loss warrants evaluation over longer horizons.

items.title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning
items.abstract: Training generalizable embodied agents requires realistic, varied, and simulation-ready indoor environments. Language-guided methods support semantic planning and object-level reasoning, but precise spatial grounding remains difficult. Visual generative models offer rich priors over plausible arrangements, yet their outputs require geometric reasoning to become physically valid 3D scenes. We introduce SceneBloom, an agentic framework that combines visual layout sampling with contract-guided 3D compilation. A hierarchical sampler uses diffusion priors to generate furniture arrangements within functional zones. A compiler then uses relations extracted from each proposal to guide geometric fitting and local pose correction. Across five room types, SceneBloom attains the highest visual quality and physical stability among the compared methods and is the only method with no detected mesh collisions and out-of-bounds objects. Its layouts are also closer to the distribution of real rooms than those of all compared baselines. Object navigation policies trained in these realistic scenes achieve a higher success rate in held-out real scans than those trained on an equal number of real training scans. Code is available at https://github.com/Tinaliu0123/scenebloom.

items.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
items.abstract: Robust reinforcement learning (RL) is critical for reliable real-world deployment, where policies may fail under diverse shifts and disruptions. Existing robust RL algorithms offer a rich set of mechanisms and principles, yet two major barriers limit their broader potential: limited algorithm reusability and an unclear empirical capability boundary. We introduce RobustRLlib, an algorithm-centric library and benchmark that addresses both challenges. It integrates 17 representative robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms under a unified interface for substantially improved reusability, together with an enhanced evaluation platform spanning diverse real-world shifts and advanced humanoid and vision-language-action tasks. Systematic evaluation over 273 perturbation configurations provides an up-to-date capability map of current robust RL algorithms, revealing where they remain effective and where substantial robustness gaps persist. As an open-source, user-friendly platform, RobustRLlib offers a reproducible and extensible codebase for applying existing methods to new problems and developing new robust RL algorithms.

items.title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
items.abstract: Collecting high-quality demonstrations remains a central bottleneck for learning dexterous manipulation. Teleoperation records executable robot actions, but it requires a complete robot setup and places the burden of coordinating many finger joints on the operator. Human demonstrations are easier to collect, but their motions must be estimated and retargeted to the robot, and they do not directly provide robot actions. In this paper, we introduce DexPort, a portable data-collection interface for high-DoF robot hands. It uses the same hand hardware for collection and deployment, avoiding a hand embodiment gap, and records both commanded joint targets and measured joint states. Our key observation is that a small set of skills can support a wide range of dexterous tasks. During collection, the operator moves the hand-held interface to specify the robot wrist motion and selects or adjusts skills that coordinate the finger motion. This removes the need to control each joint independently while retaining behaviors such as precise grasping and in-hand manipulation. We collect demonstrations across several real-world tasks and in unstructured environments without a robot arm. We then use behavior cloning to train visuomotor policies directly on the recorded wrist motions and hand commands, without skill labels. We evaluate across 4 tasks: pick-and-place with diverse objects, screwing with in-hand tool use, drawer stowage which requires simultaneous grasp and pulling, and a bimanual scanning task. We collect over 2,500 demonstrations with our portable device, in both laboratory and in-the-wild settings. Across our tasks, we see an improvement from 11% to 64% when using recorded robot commands instead of states, and an improvement from 36% to 78% for task success when using in-the-wild data.

items.title: Measure Before You Train: Typed Decision Models vs. a Classical Baseline vs. a Generative LLM for Routing a Personal Multilingual Inbox
items.abstract: Personal email agents decide, for every message, what it is, whether it is urgent, whether to draft a reply, create a task, or ignore it. Their error rate is rarely measured: the stored labels were written by the system itself. We present Foyer, a self-hosted personal inbox agent in daily use, and a measurement protocol (stratified sampling, frozen snapshots, thread-grouped splits, pre-registered hypotheses, human labels in the agent's review loop) that yields ground truth before any training. On 739 real Italian/English emails labelled by the owner (231 unbiased, 500 adversarially sampled), we compare nine systems under thread-grouped cross-validation: the production keyword rules, a TF-IDF + logistic-regression baseline, local typed decision models (Tev1, Nimble), a hosted decision model (Nimble v4-max), and hosted generative LLMs (Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma 4 26B/31B). Four results. The production rules score 28% on message type against a 58% majority class: the field shown most prominently carried no information. With ~200 labels, logistic regression has the highest accuracy on every field (type 0.79, urgency 0.74, needs-reply 0.83, is-noise 0.90), though it never predicts the two rarest classes and is statistically tied with Gemma 4 on type; few-shot prompting does not close the gap. The sender's relationship (client, supplier, service) is recovered from other emails of the same contact with 98.6% accuracy where the contact has been seen, and is not inferable from a single message by any model: it belongs in the contact graph, not the prompt. Finally, accuracy is not the product metric: composed into actions, the most accurate system most often ignores emails needing action (18% vs 4% for the best LLM); a cost-chosen threshold on its noise probability halves that rate and makes it the cheapest system.

items.title: Beyond Discrete Tokens: Preserving Numerical Continuity in Medical Vision-Language Models
items.abstract: Objective: To develop a unified vision-language model for prompt-conditioned quantitative ultrasound measurement that addresses the mismatch between continuous measurement targets and discrete token-based numerical prediction. Methods: This article presents HAD-VLM, a hybrid autoregressive-diffusion framework that combines autoregressive text generation with continuous measurement prediction within a shared backbone. Visual prompt tuning adapts the vision encoder to ultrasound images. A diffusion process predicts a five-component representation comprising caliper endpoint coordinates and measurement length. A post-processing strategy combining the proposed coordinate-length consistency mechanism with ensemble prediction is introduced to refine measurement estimates. We evaluate four echocardiographic measurement tasks on EchoNet-LVH, with additional assessments of medical question answering and X-ray vertebral measurement. Results: HAD-VLM achieves mean absolute errors of 1.36, 2.77, 3.05, and 1.16 mm for IVSd, LVIDd, LVIDs, and LVPWd, respectively, reducing errors by 21.4-37.6\% relative to the Vicuna-based autoregressive baseline. It also outperforms fine-tuned Qwen3-VL and direct MLP regression across all four tasks. Medical question answering performance is preserved on the evaluated dataset. For X-ray vertebral measurement, HAD-VLM reduces mean absolute error from 11.4 to 6.7 pixels. Conclusion: Integrating autoregressive language generation with diffusion-based continuous prediction improves quantitative medical image measurement while retaining prompt-conditioned task flexibility. Significance: HAD-VLM provides a unified approach to combining language interaction with anatomically grounded numerical prediction for quantitative medical image analysis.
