items.title: Measuring audience experience across 20 showings of the same theatre performance using customer feedback kiosks and a questionnaire.
items.abstract: Audience experiences can vary both between performances and among spectators, but little is known about how different methods capture this variation across repeated showings of the same production. We therefore examined audience experience across twenty live performances of the same music theatre production. We combined two complementary methods: immediate audience ratings collected through customer feedback kiosks and more detailed post-performance questionnaires. The kiosks recorded 1,887 responses, corresponding to 67% of total attendance, and 458 audience members (16%) completed questionnaires. Overall, the reception was positive, but kiosk ratings varied significantly across performances, indicating that audience-level enjoyment ratings differed from one showing to another. Kiosk and questionnaire responses to the same enjoyment question did not differ significantly at the aggregate level, suggesting that brief kiosk feedback may provide a practical, low-burden measure of audience-level enjoyment. Cluster analysis of questionnaire data identified three descriptive response profiles that differed primarily in overall engagement and ratings of specific artistic elements. These profiles illustrate heterogeneity within the audience of a single production. Qualitative responses from participants whose quantitative ratings were closest to each cluster centroid provided illustrative accounts of the experiences associated with these profiles. These narratives added context to the quantitative findings by showing differences in emotional tone, interpretive emphasis, and personal connection to the performance. Supplementary interviews with the director, artistic director, and an external playwright illustrated both interest in and reservations about incorporating audience data into creative work. Their comments emphasised the potential of empirical findings to support artistic reflection, while also underscoring the importance of how and when feedback is communicated within production teams.

items.title: Programmed DNA breaks drive chromatin reconfiguration and facilitate transcriptional potentiation at neuronal early response genes.
items.abstract: Neuronal activity causes topoisomerase IIβ (TOP2B) to form DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) within the promoters of early response genes (ERGs), such as Fos and Npas4. TOP2B-mediated DSBs facilitate ERG transcription, yet how this occurs is unclear. Using circular chromosome conformation capture (4C-seq), we report here that DSB formation is sufficient to emulate contact profiles observed at the promoters of Fos and Npas4 following neuronal stimulation, including elevated interactions with their cognate enhancers. Despite their purported risk, recurrent DSB cycles progressively potentiate ERG induction in mouse cortical neurons and HEK293T cells, evoking the effects of transcriptional memory. Potentiated ERG inducibility following recurrent DSBs persists through intervening cell cycles, occurs even when DNA repair is likely mutagenic, and correlates with a substantial loss of cis- and a gain of trans-, chromosomal interactions with ERG promoters. Together, these results reveal how activity-induced DSBs impact transcription by regulating chromatin dynamics at ERG promoters.

items.title: Dopamine signaling in the medial accumbens shell constrains the duration of reinforced actions.
items.abstract: Dopamine regulates the frequency of motor actions, but it is unclear whether it similarly regulates the duration of discrete behaviors. Here, we show that dopamine signaling within the medial accumbens shell reinforces actions while simultaneously constraining their duration. When mice hold down a lever to continuously self-stimulate dopamine axons in the medial accumbens shell, hold-downs are rarely longer than 5 s, and higher stimulation frequencies elicit shorter, but more numerous, lever hold-downs. This disengaging property of medial accumbens shell dopamine also applies to consummatory behavior, as mice are quicker to both terminate and reinitiate bouts of licking paired with high-frequency dopamine axon stimulation. Dopamine D1 receptors underpin this disengaging property of dopamine signaling, as we demonstrate a D1 agonist shortens both self-stimulation hold-downs and bouts of consummatory behavior. Altogether, we uncover an anatomically defined role of dopamine, which is to disengage its own reinforcing properties through D1 receptor signaling.

items.title: Neural responses to food-related stimuli following experimental sleep manipulation: A systematic review of task-based neuroimaging studies.
items.abstract: Adequate sleep is essential for physiological, cognitive, and mental functioning. While epidemiological and behavioral studies show that sleep restriction or sleep deprivation is associated with altered responses to food stimuli, the neural mechanisms underlying these effects remain unclear. The preregistered systematic review synthesized evidence from task-based functional magnetic resonance imaging studies examining neural responses to food-related stimuli following experimental sleep manipulations, including sleep deprivation or sleep restriction. Literature searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and American Psychological Association PsycInfo, yielding 11 eligible studies, including nine with adult samples and two with adolescent samples. We extracted the data, assessed the risk of bias, and conducted a qualitative synthesis. Across studies with adult samples, six visual food-cue studies generally reported stronger brain activity following sleep deprivation or sleep restriction, particularly in the striatum, insula, anterior cingulate cortex, and inferior frontal gyrus. Two food valuation studies, including a willingness-to-pay and food-desire task, showed enhanced neural activity in the amygdala and hypothalamus during food valuation. Moreover, one study using a food odor perception paradigm showed that sleep deprivation altered chemosensory and interoceptive processing by enhancing food odor encoding in the piriform cortex. Two adolescent studies reported distinct neural findings. Together, these findings highlight that experimentally induced sleep deprivation or sleep restriction does not uniformly enhance reward-related brain activity; rather, it is associated with task-dependent changes in neural responses to food-related stimuli. However, the limited and heterogeneous evidence limits conclusions regarding common neural mechanisms. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: Dopamine signaling via astrocytic D1 receptors regulates nucleus accumbens synaptic remodeling and cocaine seeking.
items.abstract: D1-type receptor (D1R)-mediated dopaminergic signaling within the nucleus accumbens shell (NAcSh) is essential for forming adaptive circuit changes that embed persistent memories associated with drug seeking and craving. While D1R is expressed in both NAcSh neurons and astrocytes, the specific contribution of astrocytic D1R to drug-related circuit plasticity remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrated in mouse NAcSh slices that D1R agonists increased astrocytic Ca2+ activity, an effect that was attenuated by astrocyte-specific D1R knockdown. Furthermore, selective knockdown of astrocytic D1R in the NAcSh prior to cocaine self-administration inhibited cocaine-induced generation of silent synapses, thereby hampering the associated remodeling of NAcSh circuits. Behaviorally, knockdown of NAcSh astrocytic D1R expedited the extinction of cocaine seeking and reduced cue-induced reinstatement. These results identified astrocytic D1R as a fundamental component of NAcSh dopamine signaling during cocaine experience that remodeled synaptic connections and neural networks underlying drug seeking and relapse.

items.title: Updates in the treatment of eating disorders in 2025: a year in review in Eating Disorders: The Journal of Treatment & Prevention .
items.abstract: A broad range of relevant and diverse studies on the treatment of eating disorders were published in Eating Disorders: The Journal of Treatment & Prevention in 2025. We review novel treatment approaches, including interventions for individuals with complex clinical presentations, integrated primary care models, brief psychological treatments, peer support, and virtually delivered interventions. We also examine clinical, psychological, family, and treatment-related factors associated with treatment outcomes and barriers and facilitators to the implementation of Family-Based Treatment. Moreover, we highlight recent developments in caregiver-focused interventions designed to support and strengthen caregiver skills throughout treatment. With regard to binge-eating disorder, we review evidence supporting guided self-help, together with methodological considerations for strengthening future treatment research. Finally, we synthesize articles addressing adaptation needs for underserved populations, including autistic individuals, racially and ethnically minoritized groups, sexual and gender minority populations, and military-affiliated youth. Overall, the articles published in Eating Disorders: The Journal of Treatment & Prevention in 2025 highlight the growing emphasis on personalized, accessible, and implementation-focused models of care, while underscoring the need for further research to strengthen the evidence base and optimize treatment delivery across diverse clinical settings and populations.

items.title: Intracranial EEG for Detecting Epileptic Activity in Acute Brain Injury: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) has been increasingly explored as part of multimodal neuromonitoring in acute brain injury, yet its diagnostic benefit compared with continuous surface EEG (suEEG) remains uncertain. We have performed a meta-analysis to quantify seizure and rhythmic and periodic pattern detection rates and concordance with suEEG. Secondary objectives were the assessment of correlations with brain injury, safety, and techniques. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched for studies reporting iEEG monitoring in adults with acute brain injury. Epileptic patterns were harmonized to the American Clinical Neurophysiology Society Standardized EEG Nomenclature for Critically Ill Patients (ACNS) 2021 terminology, classifying events as seizures/status epilepticus (SZ/SE) or rhythmic and periodic/ictal-interictal continuum patterns (RPP/IIC). Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale and custom bias domains. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted for (i) pooled proportions and (ii) pooled paired within-patient comparisons. Twelve cohorts (n = 864 participants) with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (n = 343), traumatic brain injury (n = 351), and mixed etiologies (n = 170) were included. Six studies provided paired iEEG-suEEG data (n = 273). Techniques were based on a strip or depth electrode. No severe adverse events were reported. Pooled iEEG versus suEEG incidence rates were respectively: 26% vs. 15% for SZ/SE, 47% vs. 34% for RPP/IIC, and 57% vs. 37% for clinically relevant epileptic activity. Pooled paired analysis demonstrated that iEEG additionally detected SZ/SE in 16.5% of patients [pooled McNemar odds ratio (OR) 3.46 (0.51-23.6); I2 = 63%; p = 0.158] and RPP/IIC in 26% [pooled OR 4.25 (0.19-96.1); I2 = 73%; p = 0.236], while suEEG was negative. Sensitivity analyses for high-risk studies or cohort overlap did not alter the results. Invasive EEG monitoring substantially increased the detection of seizures and RPP/IIC patterns compared with suEEG alone in patients with acute brain injury, serving as a promising monitoring adjunct.

items.title: Feedstock-dependent biochar properties shape short-term soil CO<sub>2</sub> emissions through microbial enzyme-associated processes beyond the effect of soil pH in black soil.
items.abstract: Black soils represent globally important reservoirs of soil organic carbon (SOC), yet the mechanisms regulating short-term carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions following biochar amendment remain poorly understood. Although biochar-induced alkalization has been widely proposed as a key mechanism influencing soil carbon mineralization, whether increased soil pH alone can explain feedstock-dependent CO 2 responses remain unresolved. Here, we investigated the effects of biochars derived from six feedstocks on CO 2 emissions, soil chemical properties, microbial functional traits, and extracellular enzyme activities in a short-term incubation experiment using black soil. Biochar application increased cumulative CO 2 emissions by 9.1%-44.6%, with substantial variation among feedstocks. Biochars increased soil pH, nutrient availability, and the activities of carbon-, nitrogen-, and phosphorus-acquiring enzymes, but the magnitude of these responses varied substantially with feedstock-dependent biochar properties. Cumulative CO 2 emissions were positively associated with β-glucosidase (BG), leucine aminopeptidase (LAP), and acid phosphatase (ACP) activities. Random forest and regression analyses identified soil pH and extracellular enzyme activities as major predictors of CO 2 emissions, with extracellular enzyme activities collectively contributing 52.9% of the relative importance and exhibiting stronger relationships with CO 2 emissions (R = 0.68-0.72) than soil chemical properties alone. Importantly, pH manipulation using NaOH in the absence of biochar failed to reproduce the enhanced enzyme activities and CO 2 emissions observed following biochar amendment, demonstrating that alkalization alone was insufficient to explain the contrasting CO 2 responses among different biochar treatments. These findings indicate that short-term CO 2 emissions following biochar application are shaped by feedstock-dependent biochar properties in association with microbial enzyme-mediated carbon turnover beyond the effect of soil pH. Our results highlight the importance of integrating biochar properties and microbial functional responses when evaluating short-term soil carbon mineralization and the environmental implications of biochar amendment.

items.title: Daphnia magna bioconverts eicosapentaenoic acid continuously and independently of dietary supply.
items.abstract: Freshwater food webs are increasingly exposed to eutrophication and warming, which can shift phytoplankton community composition and reduce the availability of long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids to higher trophic levels. We investigated whether the model freshwater crustacean Daphnia magna can compensate for a dietary lack of eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) through endogenous EPA synthesis from its precursors, and whether this response depends on food quality, temperature, and genetic background. Two D. magna strains, isolated from contrasting temperate regions, were exposed to four diets ranging from edible cyanobacteria-dominated to cryptophyte-enriched communities at 15, 20, and 25 °C. Using deuterium labelling, compound-specific hydrogen isotope analysis, fatty acid quantification and fitness measurements, we assessed EPA bioconversion and its consequences for consumer performance. Cyanobacteria-rich food reduced biomass accrual, delayed reproduction, decreased body size, and lowered offspring production. Despite these pronounced fitness effects, endogenous EPA production remained stable across all dietary treatments. Instead, bioconversion was primarily governed by water temperature, reaching a maximum at approximately 20 °C, and was slightly higher in the cold-adapted strain, consistent with underlying biochemical constraints on metabolic processes. Slight differences between the two strains suggest an important contribution of genetic background in determining EPA biosynthesis. These results indicate that endogenous EPA synthesis in D. magna was not actively regulated but was constantly active and potentially buffered against low dietary EPA levels, but did not fully compensate for poor food quality.

items.title: Healthy default beverage policies: A comprehensive inventory and comparative analysis of enacted and proposed policies across U.S. state and local jurisdictions.
items.abstract: Background Previous evaluations of healthy default beverage (HDB) policies showed inconsistent implementation and enforcement. No study has described and compared implementation and enforcement provisions in enacted and proposed policies to identify gaps impacting policy success. Objective To identify and examine trends in enacted and proposed U.S. local and state HDB policies; compare implementation, enforcement, and equity provisions across policy status and jurisdictional levels; evaluate alignment with Healthy Drinks Healthy Kids (HDHK) recommendations; and illustrate how enacted policies changed during committee review. Design This study identified enacted and proposed local and state policies through systematic searches of policy databases (American Legal Publishing Code Library, Municode, NexisUni, Westlaw), websites, and literature in September 2024. Policies were reviewed for inclusion, and a jurisdiction's final policy version coded for key characteristics. Enacted policy's legislative websites were separately searched for accompanying documents (e.g., committee reports). Main outcome measures The outcomes were number of enacted and proposed policies; frequency of implementation, enforcement, and equity provisions; HDHK recommendations alignment; and committee-required changes to enacted policies. Statistical analyses performed Intercoder agreement was calculated with Cohen's kappa, and descriptive statistics summarized policy contents. As a case-study, accompanying documents from state-level enacted Hawaii and Illinois policies were qualitatively reviewed. Results This inventory included 86 policies (28 local, 58 state) from 2015-2024. After excluding duplicate state-level bicameral policies and counting each re-introduction of a policy across legislative sessions as an additional policy, there were 65 unique policies. Policies were enacted in 28 local jurisdictions and 4 states, and proposed (not enacted) in 14 states. Implementation, evaluation, and enforcement provisions were uncommon across jurisdictions and statuses. Equity provisions appeared only in local policies. No policies completely met HDHK recommendations. Accompanying documents illustrated how the legislative process strengthened or weakened policy provisions in Hawaii and Illinois. Conclusions HDB policies are increasingly enacted across U.S. jurisdictions. Strengthening implementation, enforcement, and equity provisions may enhance policy effectiveness in reducing children's restaurant sweetened beverage intake.

items.title: Intermittent illumination enables reversible carbon buffering by Rhodopseudomonas palustris for enhanced methane recovery from food waste anaerobic digestion.
items.abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) of food waste (FW) is vulnerable to acidification when fermentation outpaces syntrophic oxidation and methanogenesis. To address this temporal imbalance, we introduced Rhodopseudomonas palustris (R. palustris), which can assimilate fermentation-derived volatile fatty acids (VFAs) and store carbon as polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs). Intermittent illumination reduced VFA accumulation and end-cycle H 2 partial pressure, while yielding the highest mean daily methane production (589.0 mL d -1 ) and fraction of carbon recovered as methane (37.2 %). A pure-culture assay showed that PHA accumulated during illumination and declined in darkness, indicating reversible intracellular carbon storage and remobilization. The PHA turnover pattern paralleled reactor methane dynamics, which was consistent with a temporal association between carbon storage and downstream methanogenesis. Intermittent illumination yielded the lowest NADH/NAD + ratio while maintaining high ATP availability. Community analysis revealed a more balanced distribution of functional guilds between the liquid and reactor-wall fractions, while metagenomic analysis indicated functional potential for PHA turnover and methanogenesis. Together, these findings support a carbon-buffering model in which light-dark cycling is associated with transient carbon storage and subsequent remobilization, potentially improving the temporal coupling between acidogenesis and methane formation and enhancing AD stability and methane recovery.

items.title: Metal-organic frameworks-enabled lignocellulose valorization toward medium-chain fatty acids: From sustainable synthesis to integrated catalysis, bioconversion, and separation‬‬‬‬.
items.abstract: Lignocellulosic biomass is a renewable carbon source for medium-chain fatty acid (MCFA) production, but conversion from solid feedstock to recoverable C6-C8 products is limited by biomass recalcitrance, enzyme deactivation, microbial inhibition, and downstream separation. This review critically evaluates metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) as stage-specific materials rather than a universal platform, linking manufacture and stability to biomass conversion, enzyme immobilization, carbohydrate upgrading, chain elongation, product recovery, regeneration, and process economics. Direct studies are distinguished from related-system evidence, mechanistic interpretations, and proposed integrations, with comparisons constrained by material identity, process matrix, and reported endpoints. Key trade-offs concern activity and stability, enzyme protection and substrate access, and adsorption affinity and release. Initial direct studies report enhanced caproate production with MOF-assisted chain elongation, whereas selective and repeated C6-C8 recovery from real chain-elongation broth remains insufficiently demonstrated. The most defensible near-term route is modular, stream-matched use of MOFs rather than a single multifunctional material spanning the biorefinery.

items.title: Spatial patterns, source apportionment, and environmental correlates of soil potentially toxic elements in an arid high-altitude mining area of Wuqia County, Xinjiang, China.
items.abstract: Disentangling mining-related inputs from heterogeneous geological backgrounds remains difficult in arid mining regions. We analyzed eight potentially toxic elements (PTEs; As, Cd, Cr, Cu, Hg, Ni, Pb, and Zn) in 155 surface-soil samples from an arid, high-altitude mining area in Wuqia County, Xinjiang, China. A staged framework combined a self-organizing map (SOM), improved absolute principal component scores-multiple linear regression (APCS-MLR), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) to identify multielement patterns, estimate potential-source contributions, and characterize nonlinear environmental associations. SOM resolved localized Cd-Pb-Zn co-enrichment, with class C3 concentrated near the waste-rock dump and processing plant. APCS-MLR separated five potential-source signals: mining-traffic Cd-Zn, mixed Hg-As deposition/agricultural, Ni parent-material, mixed Cr-Cu parent-material/industrial, and Pb traffic-deposition. In the 105 robust samples used for the final Huber-regression branch, F1 and F4 accounted for mean contributions of 29.7% and 27.5%, respectively. Spatial out-of-fold (OOF) evaluation of downstream LightGBM models identified F1 as the most stable factor (pooled OOF R 2 = 0.36; positive R 2 in all five folds), and its estimated contribution decreased with distance from the mining area. A full-sample, uncertainty-weighted, five-factor positive matrix factorization (PMF) sensitivity analysis recovered one-to-one correspondence with the APCS-MLR structure (cosine similarities, 0.724-0.977); all five profiles matched at cosine similarity ≥ 0.80 in 93% of bootstrap resamples. SHAP associations for F2-F5 remained exploratory because their spatial stability was weak. By separating pattern identification, statistical source apportionment, and association interpretation, the staged evidence chain supports targeted monitoring and improves the robustness of source-oriented environmental assessment in arid mining regions.

items.title: Females shape hunting of vertebrates in wild bonobos.
items.abstract: Hunting and meat consumption are widely considered key drivers of human evolution, and hypotheses about their origins draw on comparisons with our closest living relatives, chimpanzees and bonobos. These comparisons typically set up a behavioral dichotomy in which chimpanzees are characterized by cooperative hunting of arboreal primates by male-dominated parties, whereas bonobo hunts are thought to involve the opportunistic targeting of terrestrial ungulates, primarily by individual females. 1 , 2 , 3 Observations from two habituated bonobo communities at LuiKotale covering 10 years challenge this dichotomy. LuiKotale bonobos hunted both terrestrial ungulates (42%) and arboreal primates (43% of vertebrate prey), with red colobus monkeys comprising the majority of primate prey (77%). Males and females hunted arboreal primates at similar rates, and females accounted for most non-primate captures. Female age affected the hunting frequency of primates and ungulates, with the former being biased to younger and the latter to older females. The prominent role of female bonobos in hunting supports predictions that relate hunting activity to intersexual dominance relations rather than risk aversion, with the dominant sex being more active. Comparing data from neighboring communities revealed differences and suggests that social and environmental parameters affect prey choice by each community in different ways. Together, these findings challenge the assumption that chimpanzee-like, male-biased hunting represents the ancestral condition. They highlight the contribution of females to obtaining vertebrate prey, call for a reassessment of the role of females in hunting and meat sharing, and by extension, the framing of models of early hominin subsistence and social organization.

items.title: Spawning strategy drives divergent stock trends of walleye pollock and Pacific cod under ocean warming in the northwestern Pacific.
items.abstract: Walleye pollock and Pacific cod are cold-water semi-demersal species with similar life histories; however, their long-term catch trends have diverged since the late 1980s along their southern distribution limits in Korea and Japan. This study examined how warming-driven water-column changes differentially affect these species with contrasting spawning strategies (pelagic eggs: pollock; demersal eggs: cod). Using data from 1982 to 2023, spawning-season water-column structure, early life-stage thermal habitat suitability index (HSI), and habitat suitable depth (HSD; HSI ≥ 0.6) were compared with catches across three regional groups (A: Korean East/Japan Sea coast; B: Japanese East/Japan Sea coast; C: Japanese Pacific coast), and lead-lag relationships were assessed by cross-correlation function (CCF) analysis of detrended time series. Surface temperatures increased in all groups under Kuroshio-origin warm currents (A: East Korea Warm Current; B: Tsushima Warm Current; C: Kuroshio Extension), whereas bottom thermal conditions differed depending on regional cold-water masses. Pollock catches declined sharply in all groups after the late 1980s without recovery, even where surface HSI remained suitable. In Group A, pollock HSI declined or remained low in sub-regions, whereas suitable cod habitat persisted and catches increased. In parts of Groups B and C, cod catches declined after the early 2010s; HSD deepened in Group B and was negatively associated with catch five years later in B-1 (r = -0.72, p < 0.001), whereas HSD-catch relationships varied among Group C sub-regions. Contrasting spawning strategies therefore expose early life stages to different water-column layers, whereas catch responses depend on regional oceanographic conditions.

items.title: Dam-induced reshuffling of functional traits in fish communities across the Lower Mekong Basin.
items.abstract: Freshwater ecosystems in the Lower Mekong Basin (LMB) are increasingly affected by anthropogenic pressures such as hydropower development, altered flow regimes, and habitat degradation. While taxonomic declines are documented, the functional reshuffling of fish communities remains poorly understood. To address this gap and assess the temporal shifts in fish traits and identify those most sensitive to environmental change, we applied a trait-based approach using long-term monitoring data from four sites spanning from the upper LMB to the delta. Post-dam, we observed reduced temporal variability at most sites along with strong site-specific patterns in trait dynamics. Notably, migratory species were replaced by non-natives at the upstream site (LPB) and marine-related guilds emerged in Tonle Sap Lake (TLS) but disappeared from the delta. Community-weighted mean (CWM) values decreased for key functional groups, including rhithron residents (G1) at LPB and floodplain-related guilds at TLS. CWM-redundancy analysis identified water level, temperature, dissolved oxygen, total suspended solids (TSS), and total nitrite and nitrate (NO32) as key drivers. Upstream communities (G1 and migratory species, particularly at LPB) were correlated with high water level, dissolved oxygen, and NO32, but low temperature and TSS. Conversely, downstream communities, such as floodplain and marine related guilds, showed the opposite pattern. These findings reveal that post-dam environmental changes reshape the functional organization of the Mekong fish communities. Identifying traits sensitive to long-term environmental variation improves our understanding of how hydrological changes influence the functional composition of fish communities and can guide conservation efforts and environmental flow strategies to sustain functional fish diversity.

items.title: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet.
items.abstract: During interglaciations, the Laurentide Ice Sheet (LIS), which is the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, retreats to Arctic Canada, where it achieves a minimum configuration. The reexpansion of the LIS following this minimum marks the start of the next glaciation. Here, we show that the last remaining remnant of the most recent LIS, Barnes Ice Cap (Baffin Island, Canada), achieved its minimum interglacial dimensions after ~3.6 thousand years ago, before reexpanding ~2000 years ago, marking the onset of the next glaciation. The new LIS reached maximum dimensions in ~1960 CE, after which anthropogenic summer warming resulted in a negative mass balance, ice margin recession, and the termination of the next glaciation. The demise of the next glaciation, despite the ongoing decline in summer insolation, illustrates the influence of anomalous greenhouse gas forcing on climate.

items.title: The evolutionary accessibility of cultural fitness landscapes.
items.abstract: Many human cultural and technological traits have a complex and peculiar structure. They are often characterized by multiple closely interacting parts that can form modules, and change as a result of innovation, collaboration, and social learning. A full understanding of the ways in which such cultural traits evolve requires a model that accounts for the close epistatic interaction of the constituent parts, and for the uniquely cultural processes that act on them. Here, we generalize the concept of 'adaptive landscapes', where populations search a landscape for optimal combinations of components. This generalization accounts for epistatic interactions, and includes processes such as modularization, communication, and collaboration, that are not features of genetic systems but may be quite common features of cultural systems. We show that modularization in combination with collaborative communication of search results is more successful, but sometimes more costly, than searching a full adaptive landscape. However, in many of the circumstances under which technology evolves, a full search of many thousands of possible modules may not be feasible since time, financial, energetic, and environmental constraints are likely to be strong. Under these conditions, our models suggest that there is a critical value for the number of modules to search below which the global optimum is more likely to be reached by searching the full landscape. The value of this threshold depends on the complexity of the technology. Overall, we suggest that analysis of cultural fitness landscapes is likely to be a fruitful avenue for research into technological change especially when combined with elements of human learning and interaction known to be important features of cultural evolution.

items.title: Host-virus interactions dominate fitness and conceal additive genetic variation.
items.abstract: Host-parasite coevolution is expected to generate strong selection for resistance and infectivity that has the potential to erode genetic variation. Despite this, natural populations often retain extensive genetic variation in these traits. Genotype-by-genotype interactions on fitness can generate negative frequency-dependent selection, which helps maintain this variation by preventing any host or pathogen genotype from retaining a permanent advantage. Because these interactions place genetic variance in the interaction term rather than in additive differences among hosts or pathogens, that variance is masked from directional selection and can remain 'cryptic'. Here we combine coevolutionary modelling with large‑scale experimental infection assays to quantify how host-pathogen interactions structure fitness variance in a vertically transmitted virus system, Drosophila melanogaster and sigma virus. Simulations show that coevolution typically erodes additive genetic variance in host and pathogen fitness, concentrating variance in host-virus interaction terms. Consistent with these predictions, experiments spanning 90 host-virus genotype combinations reveal that transmission, viral load, and virulence are overwhelmingly governed by host-virus genetic interactions rather than host or virus main effects. As a result, neither host resistance alleles nor viral genotypes confer consistently higher fitness across genetic backgrounds. Interactions tend to be sex‑specific, further limiting heritable fitness variation. Our results demonstrate that coevolution can substantially mask heritable genetic variation from directional selection by rendering fitness context-dependent. This extensive cryptic genetic variation may be revealed either when ecological or evolutionary conditions shift, or when the process of coevolution itself alters the direction of selection. This demonstrates the need to account for genotype-specific interactions when forecasting evolutionary responses.

items.title: Innovative Standards for Using Nature-Based Solutions in Water Reuse Projects.
items.abstract: Water reuse is increasingly recognized as a key element in sustainable water resource management, yet its implementation faces technical, economic, and social challenges. The Can Cabanyes project in Granollers (Catalonia, Spain) offers a pioneering example of a hybrid water reuse system that combines nature-based solutions with a technical reclamation plant and a distribution network. Over two decades of operation, the system has demonstrated reliable removal of conventional pollutants, pathogens, and certain emerging contaminants while also revealing seasonal patterns linked to temperature-dependent nitrification. Beyond water quality improvements, the project has generated significant ecological and social benefits, including habitat restoration, biodiversity enhancement, and recreational opportunities, all of which contribute measurable positive externalities that outweigh private costs.Drawing from this long-term experience, a set of innovative standards is proposed to guide the replication of hybrid systems. These include integrating green and grey infrastructure, adopting adaptive management practices, implementing rigorous performance monitoring, valuing externalities in economic assessments, and ensuring transparent stakeholder engagement. Together, these principles establish a robust framework for designing resilient and socially accepted water reuse projects. The Can Cabanyes case illustrates how nature-based solutions can be strategically embedded within peri-urban contexts, advancing both environmental sustainability and water security.

items.title: Clonal integration drives divergent assembly of rhizosphere bacteria and fungi in Hydrocotyle vulgaris under cadmium heterogeneity.
items.abstract: Clonal plants enhance their fitness in heterogeneous environments through clonal integration, which enables resource sharing among interconnected ramets. However, how clonal integration shapes rhizosphere microbiome assembly and function remains poorly understood. In this study, we constructed patchy heterogeneous soils with cadmium-polluted and unpolluted substrates to simulate fragmented polluted habitats. Apical ramets were grown in cadmium-polluted soil and basal positions were cultivated in unpolluted soil, with stolons left either intact or severed. Rhizosphere and root-zone soils were sampled, and bacterial and fungal communities were characterized via 16 S rRNA and ITS amplicon sequencing. Our results demonstrated that stolon integration significantly altered rhizosphere microbial composition, with elevated relative abundances of Acidobacteriota, Actinobacteriota and Ascomycota and a reduction in Firmicutes. Beneficial genera Streptomyces and Savoryella were enriched under intact stolon treatments. Bacterial α-richness (Chao1) was significantly higher in the rhizosphere of stolon-intact plants, especially at the basal positions, whereas fungal α- richness showed no significant difference among treatments. Beta-diversity analysis revealed that bacterial communities were more sensitive to stolon integration than fungal communities, with fungal community structural shifts observed only in the basal rhizosphere. Amplicon sequence variant (ASV) analysis showed that intact stolons increased unique bacterial ASVs but reduced unique fungal ASVs in the basal rhizosphere. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that clonal integration differentially regulates the assembly of bacterial and fungal communities in the rhizosphere. This study highlights the distinct ecological roles of bacteria and fungi in plant-soil feedback and emphasizes multi-kingdom assessments of clonal integration under heterogeneous Cd condition.

items.title: Electron transfer to nitrogenase in Paenibacillus polymyxa .
items.abstract: Nitrogenase requires low-potential electrons to reduce N2 to produce ammonia. The direct electron donors to nitrogenase are reduced ferredoxin (Fd) and flavodoxin (Fld). The enzymes that reduce Fd or Fld for N2 fixation mainly include pyruvate-flavodoxin (ferredoxin) oxidoreductase (PFOR), ferredoxin-NADP+ reductase (FNR), Rhodobacter nitrogen fixation protein complex (Rnf), and bifurcating electron transfer flavoprotein complex (Fix). Paenibacillus polymyxa is a model for studies of nitrogen fixation, but the pathways of electron transport to nitrogenase are unknown. In this study, we characterized the electron transport pathway to nitrogenase in P. polymyxa. Deletion analysis showed that among 15 genes encoding Fds, Fld, and Fd-/Fld-reducing enzymes, only cbiW gene and pfoAB operon decreased nitrogenase activity (31% and 37% relative to wild type, respectively). Triple deletion of cbiW and pfoAB led to a reduction of nitrogenase activity by 61%. Elemental analysis and ultraviolet-visible absorption spectroscopy revealed that the purified Fd protein encoded by cbiW is a [2Fe-2S] Fd. The purified Fd protein was able to substitute for Klebsiella NifF (Fld) to transfer electrons from pyruvate to Klebsiella nitrogenase in vitro. The pfoAB operon encodes PFOR, which is composed of two subunits. Klebsiella oxytoca NifJ (PFOR) was able to support nitrogen fixation in the ΔpfoAB mutant. These findings suggest that [2Fe-2S] Fd encoded by cbiW and PFOR encoded by the pfoAB operon constitute an electron transport pathway to Paenibacillus nitrogenase. Gram-positive and facultatively anaerobic Paenibacillus polymyxa is a model diazotroph whose nif (nitrogen fixation) genes encoding nitrogenase have been used for engineering yeast and plants. However, the pathway of electron transfer to Paenibacillus nitrogenase is unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that Fd encoded by cbiW and PFOR encoded by the pfoAB operon constitute an electron transport pathway to Paenibacillus nitrogenase. Fd encoded by cbiW is a [2Fe-2S] Fd, and PFOR encoded by the pfoAB operon is a heterodimer. In contrast, in many gram-negative diazotrophs, [4Fe-4S] Fds are widely used as electron donors to nitrogenase, and PFORs (NifJs) are homodimers. These results suggest that there may be some differences in the mechanisms of electron transfer to nitrogenase between gram-negative and gram-positive bacteria. The identified electron transport components in P. polymyxa will have great potential for use in engineering eukaryotes.

items.title: Expanding the Orchidaceae virome through analysis of public-domain sequencing data.
items.abstract: Orchidaceae is one of the largest plant families and includes species of major ornamental, economic, and ecological importance. Despite this diversity, the viruses associated with orchids remain poorly characterized. The growing availability of high-throughput sequencing data offers new opportunities to explore plant virus diversity across broad taxonomic scales. Here, we conducted a large-scale meta-analysis of orchid-associated viruses by reanalyzing 2,789 publicly available RNA-seq data sets representing 41 genera across 18 subtribes and five subfamilies. We identified sequences corresponding to 163 viruses, including 13 new associations with orchids. Notably, 117 sequences likely represent putative novel species, including tentative new genera within the families Benyviridae, Betaflexiviridae, Phenuiviridae, and Tymoviridae. This analysis also reveals patterns of virus co-occurrence within the orchid virome and uncovers links between viral taxa and orchid life forms. Overall, these findings greatly broaden the known diversity of orchid-associated viruses and offer a comprehensive global framework for understanding their composition, ecological interactions, and potential scope.IMPORTANCEOrchids are among the most diverse plant families, yet little is known about the viruses associated with them. Plant viruses pose significant risks to agriculture and may also threaten orchid conservation, particularly when infected plant material is moved through trade or cultivation. A comprehensive understanding of the orchid virome is therefore essential for improving virus detection, managing diseases, and producing virus-free planting material. In this study, we used large-scale analysis of publicly available RNA-seq data to identify viral sequences associated with orchid-derived transcriptomic data sets and to characterize the diversity of orchid-associated viruses. Our results substantially expand the catalog of viruses associated with Orchidaceae, revealing numerous previously undescribed viruses and candidate virus-orchid associations. By providing a global perspective on the Orchidaceae virome, this work highlights the power of data mining approaches for virus discovery and establishes a foundation for future studies on plant virus ecology, evolution, and surveillance.

items.title: Local Adaptation to the Sex Environment: Reciprocal Sex-Limited Selection in Different Thermal Regimes.
items.abstract: The shared genome prevents independent responses to sex differences in selection. Each sex does not evolve in response to its own sex-specific selection but is influenced by selection on the other sex via the shared genome. We used experimental evolution in Drosophila melanogaster to create separate pools of Chromosome 3s for males (male-limited "ML" chromosomes) and females (female-limited "FL" chromosomes), thereby separating the gene pool, for 15 generations. Viewing each sex as a separate environment, this separation of the genome allows sex-specific adaptation to each sex environment. We performed a reciprocal transplant between the sexes to quantify the strength of local adaptation to each sex. We found each chromosome type was more beneficial in the sex it had been selected for (i.e., local adaptation to sex). Because it has been postulated that sex-differences in selection may depend on how well adapted a population is to the abiotic environment, we performed experimental evolution at two thermal regimes (3 replicate populations each): one benign temperature to which the populations were well-adapted and one novel temperature. Female-specific adaptation was stronger at the benign temperature whereas male-specific adaptation was stronger in the novel temperature. Within chromosome pools, male and female fitness were more positively correlated in the novel compared to the benign conditions. Though males carrying ML chromosomes were typically more fit than males carrying FL chromosomes, they were also more harmful to their female mating partners.

items.title: How metapopulation dynamics shape evolutionary inferences from resurrection ecology.
items.abstract: In the context of global change, such as climate change, resurrection ecology-where ancestors and descendants are phenotyped in a common environment-has recently emerged as a powerful method for characterizing evolution. This approach has been applied across diverse organisms, provided they possess a dormant stage in their life cycle. While limitations have been raised (e.g., the impact of propagule storage on phenotypes), methodological solutions have also been developed. Here, we identify metapopulation dynamics and within-population selection as a potential drivers of evolutionary change in resurrection ecology studies. Using a simple population genetic model, we show how allele frequencies can change with population age. Second, we propose a method to disentangle the evolutionary effects of metapopulation dynamics from those driven by external factors such as climate change. The method is based on the analysis of a set of populations at the initial sampling time and a new, independent set of populations after a given period, moving beyond from the classical "ancestor-descendant" paired approach.

items.title: Duplication, Loss, and Feeding Ecology of Lysozyme Gene Copy Number in Insects.
items.abstract: Lysozymes are ubiquitous enzymes traditionally associated with immune defense via bacterial cell wall degradation. In some insect lineages, particularly Diptera with bacteria-rich diets, these enzymes have been secondarily recruited for digestion, but how widespread this shift is across other insect groups remains unclear. Here we investigate the evolutionary dynamics and functional roles of C-type and I-type lysozymes across 275 insect genomes, inferring patterns of gene duplication and loss and testing associations between lysozyme copy number and dietary habits. Phylogenetic Generalized Least Squares (PGLS) method revealed few significant associations: a weak link between larval detritivory and C-type copy number, and a more consistent one between an omnivorous diet and I-type copy number across life stages. Duplication analysis revealed multiple independent expansions of C-type lysozymes within Brachycera. In Muscoidea, C-type lysozymes were highly expressed in the Musca domestica larval midgut, consistent with digestion, whereas in Blattodea, moderate C-type copy numbers and salivary gland-biased expression in Periplaneta americana adults instead suggest a primarily antiseptic role. I-type lysozymes lack the catalytic residues required for canonical muramidase activity, yet remain conserved throughout Insecta, including in lineages that lost C-type lysozymes, suggesting alternative, non-canonical functions. Together, these findings are more consistent with a predominantly lineage-specific pattern of gene family evolution, largely uncoupled from a single ecological driver, than with a broad, diet-driven adaptive signal. Digestive recruitment of C-type lysozymes may extend beyond the well-characterized cases of Musca domestica and Drosophila melanogaster to additional expanded lineages across Brachycera, although direct functional evidence remains lacking.

items.title: To buzz or to sip: Asymmetric pollination effectiveness hints at the evolutionary transition of floral rewards.
items.abstract: Evolutionary transitions between floral reward types, such as the repeated loss of nectar, are common across angiosperms, yet the ecological mechanisms driving these shifts remain poorly understood. In Pedicularis, the evolutionary loss of nectar is hypothesized to be associated with shifts to buzz pollination. However, empirical comparisons of pollination effectiveness between nectar- and pollen-foraging behaviours within a single transitional system are largely lacking. We investigated Pedicularis alaschanica and its principal pollinator, Bombus friseanus, in the Hengduan Mountains. This plant represents a transitional evolutionary state, as it possesses a beak for specialized pollen delivery but still secretes copious nectar. This novel and unique system allows for a direct comparison of two distinct intraspecific foraging behaviours performed by the same bee species: upright nectar feeding (dorsal contact) versus vibratile pollen collection (ventral contact/buzz pollination). We quantified floral traits, nectar dynamics, single-visit pollen removal and deposition, and assessed the plant's breeding system and natural pollen limitation. We confirmed and quantified the nectar properties of this transitional species, revealing distinct nectar secretion dynamics. While single-visit pollen removal did not differ significantly between the two foraging behaviours, buzz-pollinating visits were significantly more time-efficient and deposited on average more than twice as many pollen grains on stigmas compared to nectar-foraging visits. Breeding system experiments revealed that P. alaschanica is a partially self-incompatible outcrosser, and its natural seed set is not pollen-limited. Our study revealed a marked functional asymmetry in pollen transfer driven by intraspecific behavioral variation among pollinators. In a non-pollen-limited system, the superior per-visit pollen deposition achieved by buzz-pollinating bees likely enhances male siring success. This high effectiveness likely relaxes the selective pressure to maintain metabolically costly nectar. Our findings provide a compelling mechanistic explanation for the repeated evolutionary loss of floral nectar.

items.title: Nocturnal road traffic noise and Sleep during Mid-Adulthood in Urban Settings: Examining Sex and Socioeconomic Differences within the DAS-EP Project.
items.abstract: Sleep is essential for physical and mental health but tends to deteriorate from mid adulthood, particularly among women. Nocturnal road traffic noise is a major environmental stressor that can disrupt sleep. This study aimed to examine the association between nocturnal road traffic noise and sleep health during mid-adulthood and explore potential sex-based differences. We conducted a cross sectional analysis using data from population health surveys (2021-2023) including 1,898 adults aged 40-60 living in urban areas of the Basque Autonomous Community, the Valencian Community, and Barcelona. Nocturnal road traffic noise was assessed using Lnight indicator, defined as the long-term average noise level during the night-time period (23:00-07:00), and estimated using official noise maps. Sleep health was assessed through self-reported measures of sleep duration, overall sleep satisfaction, and sleep quality using the SATED scale, a multidimensional measure of sleep health (Satisfaction, Alertness, Timing, Efficiency, and Duration). A Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) was used to identify covariate adjustment sets and associations were estimated using linear models accounting for the complex survey design. Women generally reported poorer sleep health than men, with lower sleep satisfaction and poorer sleep quality, and sleep quality increased with area-level household income. Noise exposure increased with income at lower levels, while different patterns were observed across regions after €50,000. The association between noise exposure and sleep health varied across regions and sleep health dimensions. In Barcelona, higher noise exposure was associated with greater sleep satisfaction, but this association was not significant in pooled meta analyses. In contrast, higher noise exposure was associated with poorer sleep quality in the Basque Country, with the pooled meta-analysis showing a similar overall pattern. These findings highlight the context-dependent nature of noise-sleep relationships and support the need for targeted public health strategies.

items.title: Altered white matter functional activity and connectivity in pretreatment breast cancer: exploratory associations with affective symptoms.
items.abstract: Resting-state fMRI studies in breast cancer have predominantly focused on gray matter, with limited attention to white matter functional organization. This study investigated white matter functional activity and connectivity before treatment and their associations with anxiety and depressive symptoms. Female patients with breast cancer (BC) were recruited from Zhejiang Provincial Tongde Hospital from November 2023 to December 2025. Amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) and fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (fALFF) were used to compare local white matter functional activity between the BC and healthy control (HC) groups. Seed-based functional connectivity (FC) analysis was then performed to investigate whole-brain white matter FC alterations. Correlations between clinical scale scores and rs-fMRI indices were analyzed. Compared with HCs, patients with BC showed altered ALFF/fALFF in the anterior and posterior corona radiata, internal capsule, posterior thalamic radiation, body of the corpus callosum, pontine crossing tract, left superior cerebellar peduncle, and left superior longitudinal fasciculus. Seed-based analysis revealed decreased FC within the bilateral anterior corona radiata and between the body of the corpus callosum and right anterior corona radiata, and increased FC between the left superior cerebellar peduncle and left posterior thalamic radiation. Higher ALFF in the body of the corpus callosum and reduced FC between this region and the right anterior corona radiata were associated with higher Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale scores at an uncorrected threshold. Neither association survived FDR correction. Patients with BC showed altered white matter functional activity and connectivity before cancer-related treatment, suggesting that pretreatment brain functional alterations may also involve white matter functional organization. The relationship between these white matter changes and anxiety or depressive symptoms remains exploratory.

items.title: Structural constraints and psychosocial eating behaviours associated with dietary quality among reproductive-aged mothers in urban slums of Bangladesh.
items.abstract: Dietary quality among women in urban slums may reflect structural constraints and eating behaviours, yet evidence examining both is limited. This cross-sectional study examined associations of food insecurity, work-time burden, and eating behaviours with dietary quality among 400 mothers aged 15-49 years in 20 urban slums of Dhaka, Bangladesh (two-stage stratified cluster sampling), and explored whether food insecurity moderated the emotional eating-dietary quality association. Dietary quality was assessed using the Bangladesh Healthy Eating Index (BD-HEI; 0-90) from a single 24-h recall, and food insecurity using the Food Insecurity Experience Scale (FIES; 0-8). Multilevel models with slum random intercepts included linear and quadratic food insecurity terms (quadratic term improved fit, p < .001). Mean BD-HEI was 61.5 (SD 15.7), lowest for fruits and milk products. Predicted BD-HEI was 17.3 (95% CI: -24.2 to -10.5) and 18.6 points (-26.7 to -10.4) lower at FIES = 4 and 8, respectively, than at FIES = 0, mostly at low scores, with no statistically significant difference between FIES 6 and 8. Age (β = 0.375) was positively, and emotional eating (β = -0.872 per scale point; 95% CI: -1.696 to -0.048) negatively, associated with BD-HEI; work-time burden and residence duration were not significant after adjustment. The apparent food insecurity × emotional eating interaction was not supported with a quadratic term (joint test χ2(2) = 1.89, p = .389). Findings were similar including implausible energy reporters (n = 427); associations are cross-sectional and the nonlinear analyses data-driven.

items.title: Psychometric Validation of PROMIS Measures in Acute and Chronic Pancreatitis.
items.abstract: Patient-reported outcome (PRO) measures are essential for evaluating symptom burden and quality of life (QoL) in acute and chronic pancreatitis (AP/CP), yet many instruments used in this patient population lack robust psychometric evidence. The Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) offers standardized measures designed for comparability across populations, but their suitability for AP/CP has not been comprehensively evaluated. The objective of this study was to assess the psychometric properties of PROMIS-29, PROMIS-Global Health, and PROMIS Pain Quality scales in individuals with AP/CP and provide an overview of psychometric standards that facilitate selection of PROs for use in clinical research and patient care. Data were drawn from 1,927 participants enrolled in PROCEED, a multi-site longitudinal study across the pancreatitis spectrum, including healthy controls, chronic abdominal pain, acute/recurrent acute pancreatitis and definite CP. Factor models and regressions were used to psychometrically evaluate univariate construct validity, known-groups validity, convergent validity, reliability, structural validity and population invariance. PROMIS measures exceeded all psychometric benchmarks tested. Scores were approximately normally distributed and comprehensively covered the range of each symptom domain. Correlations with other commonly used QoL measures supported convergent validity. PROMIS scores discriminated effectively among diagnostic subgroups and exhibited excellent structural validity and internal consistency reliability. Population invariance assessments indicated that scores are comparable across age, sex, race, and diagnostic subgroups. This study provides strong preliminary evidence that PROMIS measures meet rigorous psychometric standards that supports their use in patient research and care in AP/CP. Their adoption may enhance measurement consistency and support core outcome sets in clinical research and trials of AP/CP.

items.title: A two-layer model of technology lay beliefs and their societal and political consequences: The case of AI.
items.abstract: Modern technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) can contribute to economic and societal prosperity. Yet, independent of their actual effects, consumers, workers, and the public often hold negative beliefs about these technologies, which can contribute to aversion to AI and technological change more broadly. This article examines technology lay beliefs, with AI as the focal case, and proposes an interconnected two-layer model to explain their societal impact. Layer 1 captures general psychological predispositions to technological change that provide a baseline for why technology lay beliefs often emphasize potential losses. Layer 2 captures specific contextual interpretations of AI that amplify or attenuate this baseline. We use this model to organize existing research and discuss the societal and political consequences of technology lay beliefs in the age of AI.

items.title: The psychology behind knowledge hiding: Exploring resource preservation motives and their impact on employee well-being and performance.
items.abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate the phenomenon of knowledge hiding in organizational settings by examining its antecedents and consequences at the employee level. Specifically, the study seeks to uncover the underlying factors that drive individuals to engage in knowledge hiding behavior and to understand the subsequent effects this behavior has on employees. This study employs an exploratory qualitative design. Data were collected through open-ended essays administered via an online research platform, with responses obtained from 50 full-time employees across varied industries. The essays were analyzed using thematic analysis, following open, axial, and selective coding, allowing for the identification of both the antecedents and outcomes of knowledge hiding. The study highlights that personal antecedents such as indispensability, moral disengagement, and concerns over career prospects were associated with knowledge hiding behavior. Similarly, contextual antecedents including task interdependence and the presence (or absence) of ethical leadership were perceived by participants to shape knowledge-hiding behaviors within organizations. Further, the findings suggest that overall knowledge hiding was associated with adverse effects on critical employee outcomes, leading to reduced creative and innovative performance, diminished psychological well-being, and compromised task performance. This study advances the knowledge hiding literature by simultaneously uncovering its personal and contextual antecedents and linking them to multiple employee outcomes. This study also enhances theoretical understanding and offers a more nuanced foundation for future research in organizational behavior and knowledge management. It also advances the conservation of resources theory by examining how resource preservation motivations drive knowledge hiding behaviors in organizational settings.

items.title: Network analysis reveals specific patterns of relationships between connected speech features in subjective cognitive decline.
items.abstract: Subtle language changes occur early in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Early detection of these changes therefore represents a potential tool for the early detection of individuals who could develop the disease. Knowledge on connected speech (CS) in Subjective Cognitive Decline (SCD, a preclinical stage of AD for at least some individuals, characterized by cognitive complaints without objective cognitive deficits), remains limited. In this study, we used network analysis to examine the relationships between CS features extracted with Natural Language Processing techniques. This method allowed us to determine whether the patterns emerging from the SCD CS network (i.e., a network modelling the relationships between CS features) differed from those observed in similar networks constructed for controls and individuals with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI, a prodromal stage of AD for many individuals, characterized by objective cognitive deficits but preserved daily functioning). We found minimal differences between individuals with SCD and controls and individuals with MCI in raw CS features. Nevertheless, our network analysis revealed a stronger relative subdivision of the SCD network into different dimensions (representing linguistic domains), as well as relative reductions in within-dimension density and between-dimension strength compared to the Control and MCI networks. There were also relative differences in how the CS features forming the Semantic conciseness and Lexical and syntactic complexity dimensions associated with other features in the SCD network. Results suggest that network analysis might be more sensitive than other methods to subtle CS differences in SCD and that this population might use distinct CS production mechanisms.

items.title: A failure of food-specific inhibitory control training to affect food choices via a hypothetical food delivery platform.
items.abstract: Inhibitory control training (ICT) is a computerised intervention which requires individuals to repeatedly inhibit a pre-potent motor response to unhealthy food-related cues. In doing so the cues are devalued, which may in turn reduce the choice and/or consumption behaviour towards unhealthy foods. Whilst single-session laboratory evidence suggests ICT may be a promising intervention, online studies show equivocal results. In this pre-registered randomised controlled trial, we administered ICT online (vs a control group) to 512 individuals (47.6% female, mean age = 41.68). Immediately following training participants were asked to make a hypothetical food order from a mock pizza delivery website based on a popular UK chain. Devaluation of pizza, salad, and unhealthy but untrained images was also measured pre- and post-training. Our results demonstrated that ICT (mean = 1270 kcal) did not lead to fewer calories ordered vs the control group (mean = 1287 kcal: t(503.74) = 0.381, p = .703, d = 0.03 [95% CI: -0.14 to 0.21]: BF10 = 0.105), or fewer number of individuals ordering pizza-dishes (X2(1) = 1.93, p = .165; OR = 0.72 [95% CI: 0.47 to 1.11]: BF10 = 0.272). Overall, the findings of this study suggest ICT delivered online is unlikely to be an effective stand-alone intervention for changing food-ordering behaviours, however replication with real world outcomes is necessary.

items.title: Determining the Needs of Spanish-speaking Families That Receive Ambulatory Services in the Division of Developmental-Behavioral Pediatrics (DDBP): The Family Viewpoint.
items.abstract: Previous satisfaction surveys in a Midwestern developmental-behavioral pediatrics clinic showed suboptimal experiences among Spanish-speaking caregivers, particularly regarding visit length and feeling unsafe during encounters. This study sought to gather detailed information about Spanish-speaking families' experiences with ambulatory developmental-behavioral services and to address a gap in the literature on inequitable health care experiences among caregivers of children with developmental-behavioral disorders. We collected descriptive, qualitative data on Spanish-speaking families' experiences with developmental-behavioral ambulatory care using Group Level Assessment (GLA) and Participatory Action Research (PAR) methods. Fifteen Spanish-speaking caregivers participated. Although interpreter services were consistently available and often described as excellent, families reported concerns about interpretation accuracy and consistency. Caregivers also noted that providers sometimes appeared rushed, particularly when language barriers led to delays or shortened encounters with non‑Spanish-speaking clinicians. Families proposed several improvements, including expanding bilingual staffing to enhance comfort and communication, strengthening oversight and training for interpreter services-especially in telehealth-and ensuring interpreters actively engage children during therapeutic sessions. Addressing these concerns through expanded bilingual staffing, improved interpreter quality, and more culturally responsive communication practices may substantially enhance the care experience for Spanish-speaking families and promote more equitable developmental-behavioral services.

items.title: Effectiveness of the internet-based unified protocol transdiagnostic intervention for the treatment of depression, anxiety, and related disorders in a routine primary care setting in Ireland: a pilot pragmatic randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract: The Unified Protocol (UP) is an empirically supported transdiagnostic therapy for emotional disorders. To improve scalability, alternative delivery methods are being developed such as an internet-based version of the UP (iUP) with minimal support. The study examined the effectiveness of iUP and explored users' experiences of the intervention within a primary care setting in Ireland. The study employed a randomised controlled trial design. Participants were assigned to: (a) the iUP or (b) an enhanced waiting list control (eWLC). Randomization followed a 2:1 allocation ratio (iUP n = 60; eWLC n = 29). Depression/anxiety symptoms were assessed at baseline, 4-weeks, 8-weeks and 12-weeks. Participants in the iUP condition also completed a follow-up assessment. Qualitative data regarding participants' experience were also collected. Participants receiving iUP showed statistically significant improvements over the course of treatment, with gains largely retained at follow-up. Although effect sizes suggested a trend for superiority of the iUP, the differences were not statistically significant relative to the eWLC group. Qualitative analyses indicated that participants appreciated the supporters' guidance and the theoretical framework of the intervention, and suggested increased personalization. Benefits included improvements in emotion regulation and awareness.Trial registration ISRCTN18056450 https://doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN18056450.

items.title: Say Less! Backchanneling and HPA-axis Attunement, But Not Semantic Synchrony, Relate to Couples' Relationship Quality Across the Transition to Parenthood.
items.abstract: Language and physiology each carry information about how couples attune, yet are rarely studied together, especially during vulnerable periods such as the transition to parenthood. Semantic synchrony, or shared meaning across partners' speaking turns, is a potential marker of relational functioning that may reflect couples' use of active listening and reflection to validate one another's concerns. Semantic synchrony may also intersect with other dimensions of health-relevant synchrony such as covariation in partners' hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis. The present study examined semantic and HPA-axis/cortisol synchrony in 100 expectant parent dyads during lab-based discussions in pregnancy and at six months postpartum. Results: Semantic synchrony was present across all conversations and was strongest during discussions of conflict. Positive HPA-axis synchrony emerged at both timepoints, but semantic and HPA-axis synchrony were unrelated. Semantic synchrony during discussions about relationship conflict was negatively associated with partners' validation of one another (i.e., communicating sincere understanding), but this association was primarily attributable to couples' backchanneling (e.g., "mmhm," "uh-huh") - brief verbal expressions that communicate understanding without interrupting the speaker. Neither form of synchrony predicted relationship quality at either visit, with one exception: postpartum HPA-axis synchrony marginally predicted couples' relationship quality (P=.04). Moreover, partners' backchanneling during discussions of conflict was positively associated with participants' relationship quality. Together, these findings suggest that it is backchanneling, not semantic synchrony, that is associated with greater validation and relationship quality and may therefore serve as a potential linguistic marker of relational functioning.

items.title: Blinks are strategically coupled with head movements in unconstrained natural gaze behavior.
items.abstract: Blinks are a ubiquitous yet largely unnoticed aspect of human vision, despite causing frequent interruptions of visual input that can amount to up to 10% of waking time. By leveraging a large dataset of unconstrained gaze behavior during two natural tasks, we found a behavioral strategy to limit the impact of blinks: blinks were strategically coupled with head movements, which minimizes information loss due to unreliable visual input during head movements. Specifically, blink probability increased with higher head velocities and showed strong temporal modulation relative to head movement onset: Blink probability was reduced before head movement initiation and then peaked during the head movement. The strength of this coupling was tailored to the individual needs of participants, with participants with higher baseline blink rates showing stronger synchronization. This indicates that blinks are a part of an individually coordinated strategy when orchestrating eye and head movements during unconstrained natural behavior.

items.title: Intrapersonal and interpersonal predictors of posttraumatic growth following the February 6, 2023, Türkiye earthquakes.
items.abstract: The present study examined intrapersonal and interpersonal predictors of posttraumatic growth (PTG) among survivors of the February 6, 2023, Türkiye (Turkey) earthquakes. Specifically, the study focused on loneliness, forms of self-criticism (inadequate self and hated self), self-reassurance, shame, and guilt as potential psychological correlates of PTG. A total of 300 adult earthquake survivors (61.8% women) participated in a face-to-face assessment approximately 2 years after the disaster. Participants completed self-report measures assessing PTG, loneliness, self-criticism, self-reassurance, shame, and guilt. Bayesian correlation and regression analyses were conducted to identify the most parsimonious psychological model of PTG. Results indicated strong evidence for a negative association between loneliness and PTG and very strong evidence for a positive association between self-reassurance and PTG. Associations between PTG and self-critical forms, shame, and guilt were weak or inconclusive. Model comparison demonstrated that a minimal model including loneliness and self-reassurance provided substantially stronger evidential support than more complex models (BF₁₀ = 1,671.34, R² = .086). In the final model, loneliness was negatively associated with PTG (b = -0.13, 95% credible interval [-0.24, -0.02]), whereas self-reassurance was positively associated with PTG (b = 0.36, 95% credible interval [0.16, 0.56]). These findings suggest that posttraumatic growth following large-scale disasters may be most closely tied to the restoration of interpersonal connectedness and the cultivation of affiliative self-regulation, with important implications for community-based and compassion-focused postdisaster mental health interventions. items.title: Enhanced cognitive flexibility with self-determined task choice.
items.abstract: Cognitive control-the ability to regulate one's behavior in accordance with internal goals-is fundamental to adaptive behavior. Despite substantial progress in our understanding of different cognitive control functions supporting goal-directed behavior, most studies rely on externally instructed tasks, whereas in real-world contexts, people often have the autonomy to choose which task to perform. Although research suggests that having the opportunity to choose can enhance a variety of psychological processes (e.g., motivation or learning), it remains unclear whether and how cognitive control differs between instructed and voluntarily chosen tasks. The present study addresses this question using a novel paradigm to investigate how one core function of cognitive control-the flexibility to switch between tasks-differs between self-determined (free-choice) and externally determined (forced-choice) tasks. We reasoned that self-determined task choice may enable individuals to optimize control more effectively (e.g., by switching when control demands are relatively low) and/or may motivate individuals to invest more effort in flexibility-related control processes. Consistent with performance optimization and motivational accounts, switch costs in task performance (in particular, reaction times) were reduced under free-choice compared to forced-choice tasks across multiple experiments. This reduction was driven specifically by shorter reaction times on switch trials in free-choice tasks, suggesting that voluntary task choice takes advantage of control processes that promote cognitive flexibility, such as disengaging from a previous task or reconfiguring a new one. Overall, the present study provides new evidence linking self-determined task choice to improvements in higher order cognitive control functions-specifically, cognitive flexibility. items.title: Correcting for publication bias in multivariate and multilevel meta-analysis: A multivariate step function selection model approach.
items.abstract: Univariate meta-analysis models assume that all effect sizes are independent. This assumption is violated if, for example, two outcomes are reported in a study of interest to the meta-analyst or a study reports multiple experiments administered by the same researchers. The multivariate and multilevel meta-analysis models allow modeling dependent effect sizes. These two models have recently gained in popularity among meta-analysts in psychology, where one of the largest threats to validity of meta-analysis is publication bias where a selective subset of studies remain unpublished. We extend the univariate step function selection model approach, for modeling publication bias, to multivariate and multilevel meta-analyses. We propose strict and relaxed selection models that assign a different publication probability to studies that have only statistically significant outcomes or at least one significant outcome. These two selection models are straightforward approaches for modeling publication bias. Our method can also accommodate more sophisticated alternative selection models, and we discuss possibilities for this. We primarily focus on the method's implementation as a sensitivity analysis where publication probabilities in the selection model are assumed as known but also show how these can be estimated. Simulation studies tailored to two applications show that the proposed method as a sensitivity analysis outperforms the multivariate and multilevel meta-analysis models that do not correct for publication bias. The simulations also show that the publication probability is imprecisely estimated. We offer guidance for applying the proposed method in practice and share R code to facilitate the application of our proposed methodology.
